docs.title: neXtBSW – Neutral Embedded X-Domain Tailorable Basic Software
docs.text:
Hardware-neutral basic software that works across domains and can be tailored to any control unit.

Development release – no safety claim. neXtBSW targets ASIL B as a software safety element out of context, but no release so far is a safety release: every tag is a development release without a safety claim. Read the safety manual before you use neXtBSW in a safety-related control unit; it states what is claimed, what is not, and what the integrator has to do.

neXtBSW is a configurable basic software for 32-bit ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-R microcontrollers (little endian). It is built on Eclipse OpenBSW and FreeRTOS. The focus is the NXP S32K1 family; S32K3, STM32 and TI RM4x are targets too. Application software is attached as Simulink models (AUTOSAR Classic software components) through a generated RTE.

A control unit is described in configuration files, not in code: the MCU derivative, the board and the project each have their own file. Generators derive everything else from them: clock tree, pins, CAN bit timing, memory layout, bootloader values and the RTE. The one thing you pick when you build is the project.

This page is the entry point. It says what is in the repository and how to build it the first time. Everything else is in the documentation.

docs.title: State
docs.text: Configuration, checks and target builds work for S32K1 derivatives with a Cortex-M4F. One example board (an S32K144 board) runs on hardware. Other derivatives and families are at different stages; the table What runs today says exactly how far each one is.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
Path Content external/openbsw Eclipse OpenBSW as a Git submodule, never modified mcudb/<family>/ derivatives: manufacturer facts such as memory regions, peripheral instances, pin functions boards/<board>/ board profiles: what is fitted and how it is wired (board.yaml), hardware only projects/<project>/ projects: what the ECU software uses (project.yaml), ECU description (rte.yaml), CAN database (*.dbc) libs/bsp/, libs/bsw/ neutral driver contracts, device drivers and services; which module exists and how far it is verified: module reference platforms/<family>/ MCU drivers, startup and port of each MCU family ecu/ the ECU application, derived from the OpenBSW reference application bootloader/ UDS bootloader over CAN (ISO-TP), plain C, hardware-independent core swc/ software components as Simulink models, generated code checked in tools/ configuration model (nxconfig), generators (bswgen, rtegen, dbcgen), test runner (test), CAN flash tool (canflash) and more; each tool has its own README doc/ documentation, see below

What each layer does and how the parts fit together: architecture overview.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12
  • CMake 3.28 or newer, Ninja
  • An arm-none-eabi-gcc of major version 11 for target builds. CI uses the freely available xPack GCC 11.3.1; the pinned versions of all tools are in tools/ci/versions.toml, and tools/ci can fetch them.
  • For flashing only: the tool of your debug probe (J-Link, ST-LINK, CMSIS-DAP/DAPLink or XDS110) and, for flashing over CAN, a CAN adapter supported by python-can.

The compiler is found on PATH, or through the environment variable NX_ARM_GCC_BIN pointing at its bin folder. That is a setting of your workstation and is never checked in.

The commands below are written for Windows, where the interpreter of the virtual environment is .venv/Scripts/python. Set PYTHONUTF8=1 there, and keep the path of the checkout short (or enable long paths in Windows): some installed packages and object files otherwise exceed the limit of 260 characters.

docs.title: First build
docs.text:
One-time set-up:

git submodule update --init
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -r tools/requirements.txt -r external/openbsw/libs/bsw/middleware/tools/cpp_generator/requirements.txt
# for the Studio (Qt, its tests, the packer) add (TOOL-63):
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -r tools/requirements-studio.txt

Check a project and build it. buildtest-s32k148-min is a project for an S32K148 without a board behind it; it exists to be built, so it is a good first check of your set-up:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig check projects/buildtest_s32k148_min/project.yaml
cmake --preset buildtest-s32k148-min
cmake --build --preset buildtest-s32k148-min

nxconfig check ends with buildtest_s32k148_min: ok (board buildtest_s32k148, S32K148, 0 warning(s)). It reports every problem with file, line and YAML path; --json gives the same for tools. The configure run checks the project again and runs the generators; the build compiles the application, the bootloader and a bootloader updater, with warnings as errors. Each project has a CMake preset in CMakePresets.json; how to add one for your own project, and what the configure run prints, is in Build and flash.

Flashing needs a board and was not run for this page. Every project has the targets flash-bootloader and flash (through the debug probe) and flash-can (through the bootloader):

cmake --build --preset <preset> --target flash-bootloader
cmake --build --preset <preset> --target flash
cmake --build --preset <preset> --target flash-can

Which probe is used is a board fact; the details are in Build and flash.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
One command runs every host test and the target builds. Nothing in it touches hardware:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group all --jobs 4

--list shows what would run, -k <name> runs a selection. The test list, the groups and how single tests are run are described in tools/test/README.md; what a change has to pass is in CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
I want to … Go to find my way around the documentation doc/README.md take a board from schematic to a running ECU, step by step Guide, starting with Getting started look up a configuration field, a module or a console command Reference understand layers, configuration levels and generators Architecture overview and the binding target picture build, test and submit a change CONTRIBUTING.md read what changed, when and why CHANGELOG.md (German, see Language)

Documentation of a module, tool, board or project lives next to it, for example libs/bsw/e2e/doc/e2e.md, bootloader/doc/README.md or projects/README.md.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text:
neXtBSW is being released under the Apache License 2.0; the LICENSE file is still being prepared. Contributions are accepted under the same licence with a Developer Certificate of Origin, see CONTRIBUTING.md.

Generator output exception: what the neXtBSW generators produce (source code, headers, linker scripts, configuration and documentation) may be used, modified and distributed under terms of your choice, without the obligations of the Apache License 2.0 for the template parts contained in that output. Every generated file carries an SPDX line that points to the exception in NOTICE. The exception does not apply to the generators and templates themselves, which stay under Apache-2.0.

Third-party content in this repository keeps its licence and its headers:

Path Origin Licence ecu/ files derived from the Eclipse OpenBSW reference application (Copyright Accenture) Apache-2.0 mcudb/s32k1xx/sources/hal_nxp/*-pinctrl.h and the mcudb/s32k1xx/*.pinmux.yaml generated from them zephyrproject-rtos/hal_nxp (Copyright NXP) Apache-2.0

Further third-party code (CMSIS, FreeRTOS ports, vendor device headers, pin data) lives in 3rdparty/ and sources/ folders; it keeps the licence headers of its origin, and a README in or next to it names the source.

docs.title: Contributing to neXtBSW
docs.text: Thanks for looking. neXtBSW is a small project with a single maintainer, developed alongside real hardware. This page says how to build it, how to check your change, and what a change has to carry to be accepted. It describes what exists today — where something is still being set up, it says so.

docs.title: Get set up
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Python 3.12, CMake ≥ 3.28, Ninja, and arm-none-eabi-gcc for target builds. The standard is the pinned xPack GCC 11.3.1 that python -m tools.ci setup fetches into the tool cache (versions in tools/ci/versions.toml); another GCC 11 ARM toolchain on PATH or pointed to by NX_ARM_GCC_BIN also works. After changing the compiler, configure an existing build directory once with cmake --preset <name> --fresh: CMake keeps the old compiler path in its cache. Eclipse OpenBSW is a Git submodule and is never modified.

git submodule update --init
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -r tools/requirements.txt \
    -r external/openbsw/libs/bsw/middleware/tools/cpp_generator/requirements.txt
# working on the Studio? its packages are separate since TOOL-63:
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -r tools/requirements-studio.txt

On Windows, always use the interpreter from .venv and set PYTHONUTF8=1.

docs.title: Build and test
docs.text:
One command runs everything — all host tests and both target builds. It is the same command CI runs, and a change is not ready before it is green:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group all --jobs 4

Useful variants while working:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --list            # what would run
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k nxconfig       # a selection
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group target    # only the target builds
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --slow            # including the long mutation runs (~11 min)

If a prerequisite is missing (no toolchain, no submodule), the affected group is skipped and named rather than reported as a failure. Nothing in tools/test touches hardware: no J-Link, no CAN, no serial port, no MATLAB. Details, including how the test list in tools/test/tests.yaml is kept complete, are in tools/test/README.md.

A single target build, for example:

cmake --preset buildtest-s32k148-min
cmake --build --preset buildtest-s32k148-min       # must be warning-free, builds with -Werror

Two build profiles exist on purpose. evalboard-s32k144-demo is the board that really runs; buildtest-s32k148-min is a second derivative that is only built. If the second one breaks, board neutrality is broken — that is the point of having it.

Some console commands exist only in a test build, never in a standard build, because they break the running system on purpose. They are switched on per build folder with a CMake option:

cmake --preset <preset> -B build/<preset>-hftest -DNX_HARDFAULT_TEST_COMMAND=ON   # hardfault udf|bus|sp, to check the fault dump
cmake --preset <preset> -B build/<preset>-gdtest -DNX_GD_ENABLE_COMMAND=ON        # <gd> enable of the gdTmc6200 module

The second one switches on a gate driver through its enable pin: use it only with a person at the board. Which projects offer which command is listed in the console reference.

The other way round, a product image leaves out every test and fault-injection command, also those of the standard build (safety, the fault and shut-down commands of lc, sbc failstart), and refuses the test options above (cmake/NxProductBuild.cmake):

cmake --preset <preset> -B build/<preset>-product -DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=ON
.venv/Scripts/python tools/elfcheck product --app build/<preset>-product/ecu/application/RelWithDebInfo/app.ecu.elf

New hardware-independent code gets a host test. Register models are tested against a simulated device (see libs/bsw/sbcUja113x/test), and a host test is expected to have been checked with deliberately introduced faults, so that it demonstrably fails when the code is wrong.

docs.title: What a change should respect
docs.text:
• external/openbsw is never modified. Fixes for OpenBSW are prepared as upstream patches under doc/openbsw-beitraege/.
  • Generated code is not edited by hand. Change the generator (tools/bswgen, tools/rtegen) or the model.
  • Board facts belong in configuration, not in code. Pins, crystal, fitted parts, memory sizes and CAN instances go into the derivative (mcudb/), the board (boards/<board>/board.yaml) or the project (projects/<project>/project.yaml) — never as a constant in reusable code, in the bootloader or in a tool. The binding target picture is doc/architecture/README.md; its section 11 is the review checklist every change is measured against.
  • Code comments are English, short, and in the style of the surrounding code.

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
Published documentation is written in English. This includes README.md, everything under doc/ apart from the changelog fragments and the internal planning files listed below, module documentation under libs/*/doc/ and the READMEs next to tools, boards and projects. Reason: the software targets an international audience, and its technical vocabulary — AUTOSAR, OpenBSW, the datasheets — is English anyway, so English documentation needs fewer invented translations.

The changelog stays German. CHANGELOG.md is the project's working log, not a product document: it records what was done, why, with which measurements, and how it was verified. It is written and read by the maintainer, and translating it would cost effort without a reader who benefits.

In short:

Content Language README.md, doc/**, module and tool documentation, this page English CHANGELOG.md and the fragments in doc/changelog.d/ German Code comments and identifiers English Commit messages either, German in practice Internal planning files German

Existing German documents are being translated separately; do not translate one as a side effect of another change. When you touch a document, write the new parts in the language the table above calls for.

docs.title: Submitting a change
docs.text:
The repository is not public yet, so there is no issue tracker or pull request queue to point at. Until there is, changes reach the maintainer as patches or as a branch, and the expectations are the same:

  1. One topic per change, with a message that says what changed and why.
  2. .venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group all is green, or the skipped groups are named.
  3. A changelog entry as a fragment doc/changelog.d/<topic>.md, in German, following the style of CHANGELOG.md: what, why, measured values, and how it was verified — on host/mock or on the board. Anything not verified is named as open. Fragments avoid merge conflicts in CHANGELOG.md; see doc/changelog.d/README.md (not published, available on request).
  4. Documentation updated in the same change, if the change makes a document wrong.

Claims about hardware behaviour need to say where they come from. "Works" means it was measured; if it was only run against a mock, say so.

docs.title: Developer Certificate of Origin
docs.text:
neXtBSW is being released under the Apache License 2.0 (the licence decision is made, the LICENSE file and the file-header rollout are still being prepared). Contributions are accepted under the same licence, certified with a Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) — the same lightweight mechanism Eclipse projects use. No copyright assignment and no contributor licence agreement.

Add a sign-off line to each commit, with your real name and an address you can be reached at:

Signed-off-by: Jane Doe <jane@example.org>

git commit -s adds it for you. By signing off you state that you wrote the contribution or otherwise have the right to submit it under the project's licence — the full text is at https://developercertificate.org/.

Please do not contribute material you cannot license this way. That includes code or data derived from documents under a non-disclosure agreement and vendor files whose redistribution terms are unclear; such material is kept out of the open source line on purpose.

docs.title: Not part of the open source project
docs.text: neXtBSW Studio (tools/studio), the desktop tool for configuring projects, is proprietary. It lives in this repository but is excluded from the open source release. Everything the Studio does is available on the command line, and that is what this page and the documentation describe.

docs.title: Security policy
docs.text: neXtBSW contains a UDS bootloader with seed/key access and CSEc key handling. Vulnerabilities in these parts can affect devices in the field, so please report them privately and not in a public issue.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text:
Use GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting: open the repository's Security tab and choose Report a vulnerability. Please do not send reports by e-mail and do not open a public issue or pull request for them.

A useful report names the affected component and version (or commit), the steps or the message sequence that reproduce the problem, and the effect you observed. Do not include real production keys.

neXtBSW is maintained by one person alongside other work. The project makes no response time commitment; reports are handled on a best-effort basis (see below). You will be told when the report is read and, if the project agrees that it is a vulnerability, what happens next. Please keep the report private until a fix or a statement is published.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text:
neXtBSW is versioned according to Semantic Versioning. The rules, including what counts as stable, are in doc/architecture/versioning.md.

Version Support first release candidate (rc1) none: published without a support commitment releases after rc1 best effort: the latest release is looked at first; there is no commitment to fix older versions, no response time and no backports development branch no support

Best effort is not a service level. Anyone who uses neXtBSW in a product remains responsible for its safety and security; see the safety manual for the assumptions of use. The release makes no safety claim.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
In scope:

  • the bootloader (bootloader/): update protocol, flash programming, start-up decision, update image handling;
  • UDS services of the bootloader and of the ECU application (ecu/), in particular security access with seed and key, session handling and the services that write memory;
  • CSEc: key slots, key update, the use of the hardware security module of the S32K1xx family;
  • the generators, where their output weakens one of these (for example a generated key constant or access check).

Not in scope:

  • Eclipse OpenBSW, FreeRTOS and the other third-party parts listed in NOTICE: please report to their projects. If neXtBSW uses them in an unsafe way, that part is in scope.
  • The configuration tools (tools/) as such: they run on the developer's computer and process the developer's own files.
  • Keys of your own product: they are never part of this repository and have to be managed by you.

docs.title: S32K148 build-test board (S32K148 LQFP176)
docs.text:
Build-only profile: no flashing, no debugging, no console, no CAN access. There is no board behind this profile that the project uses; it exists only to be configured, generated and linked.

Second board profile, created with a separate task as a permanent test of board neutrality. It describes the public NXP evaluation board S32K148EVB-Q176 as far as the OpenBSW reference port proves it, with an S32K148 in LQFP176. Hardware description: board.yaml. Project: buildtest_s32k148_min.

Purpose: every change to reusable code must keep building for this profile. Where that fails, or where reusable code would have to change for it, that is a finding with a follow-up task — never a board-specific workaround (guiding principle in the project rules, review questions in doc/architecture/README.md, section 11).

docs.title: What differs from the S32K144 evaluation board
docs.text: Property S32K144 evaluation board this profile derivative, package S32K144, LQFP100 S32K148, LQFP176 (1.5 MB program flash, 252 KB RAM, 8 FTM, 3 FlexCAN) crystal 40 MHz 8 MHz (same 80 MHz system clock, other PLL factors, other CAN bit timing) supply, transceiver, watchdog system basis chip UJA1131 (CAN0, V2, external watchdog) no system basis chip: passive transceivers (canPhyPassive), the MCU's own watchdog, role power_supply unassigned CAN CAN0 (FlexCAN0) used, CAN1 (FlexCAN2) described two buses in use: CAN0 (FlexCAN0, 500 kbit/s) and CAN1 (FlexCAN2, 250 kbit/s) console LPUART2 (PTD6/PTD7) LPUART1 (PTC6/PTC7), the OpenSDA virtual COM port of the EVB pins all present in LQFP100 LEDs and CAN1 on PTE21…PTE25, which exist only in LQFP176 parts SBC, gate driver, cell controller, KL30B switch none; LEDs, a button, an analogue input

docs.title: Fitted parts
docs.text:
Reference Part Function board.yaml entry Source — TJA1051T/3 transceiver of CAN0, mode fixed to normal devices: CAN0_PHY assumed for the build test — TJA1051T/3 transceiver of CAN1 (second bus) devices: CAN1_PHY assumed for the build test

Whether the S32K148EVB really carries these transceivers is not checked (unconfirmed); for the build test only "passive transceiver" matters.

docs.title: Where the values come from
docs.text:
The template is the OpenBSW reference port of the S32K148 EVB (external/openbsw/executables/referenceApp/platforms/s32k148evb). It proves the crystal (8 MHz), CAN0 (PTE4/PTE5), the console (LPUART1, PTC6/PTC7), the button (PTC12), the RGB LED (PTE21/PTE22/PTE23), the safety test pin (PTD31) and the analogue input (ADC0 SE28); every pin function is also checked against mcudb/s32k1xx/S32K148_LQFP176.pinmux.yaml. The port also gives the levels of the button (active high, no internal pull) and of the red LED (active high) and the scaling of the analogue input (5 V full scale, factor 1). What the port does not prove - the levels of the green and blue LED, which it drives as PWM, and the MOT1 group below - is marked [SYN] in board.yaml: a synthetic value of this build-only profile, not a statement about hardware (until then verify: true). Pad numbers are left out.

Two entries are there for the build test, not because of the EVB:

  • CAN1 on FlexCAN2 (PTE24/PTE25), so that a second bus on a second FlexCAN instance is built.
  • A complementary PWM group MOT1 on FTM0 with a synthetic power_stage example, although the EVB has no power stage. PWM groups are optional since an earlier change; the group stays so that the complementary PWM path is built on a second derivative. None of its values is a measurement.

Until a follow-up task the console had to be LPUART2 (PTD6/PTD7), because the board port fixed that instance (finding); since then the profile names the real EVB console.

docs.title: Safety rules
docs.text:
State of these rules: 2026-09-18.

  • Build only. No flashing, no debugging, no console and no CAN access with this profile, because no board exists for it in this project and its values are partly chosen for the build test, not measured. board.debug names a J-Link only so that CMake generates the flash targets; they are not released.
  • Whoever uses the profile for a real S32K148EVB writes a new README for that board first, with its own safety rules and the [SYN] values replaced by values from the EVB documentation.

docs.title: Check and build
docs.text:
.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig check projects/buildtest_s32k148_min/project.yaml
cmake --preset buildtest-s32k148-min
cmake --build --preset buildtest-s32k148-min

In a task worktree use a short build folder instead (Windows path limit), for example:

cmake -S . -B %TEMP%/s32k/bt148 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DNX_PROJECT=projects/buildtest_s32k148_min -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=<.venv python>
cmake --build %TEMP%/s32k/bt148 --config RelWithDebInfo

Legende

  • Reihenfolge: Bootloader vorn (Konvention), Record im letzten Sektor (so legt tools/nxconfig/memory.py ihn heute), der Schlüsselsektor direkt darunter. Die Namen sind die des generierten bl_memory.h (Abschnitt 1); Zahlen hängen vom Derivat ab (Eval Board: Schlüssel bei 0x7E000, 4 KB). Der Anwendungsbereich liegt dazwischen.
  • Das Löschen der Anwendung nimmt weder Schlüssel noch Record mit, das Update des Bootloaders nicht den Schlüssel: deshalb eigene Sektoren (Abschnitt 4, „Key sector“). Der Record-Sektor liegt nicht im Anwendungsbereich (bl_sector_map_ok(), Abschnitt 2).
  • Boot-Request: Magic plus Inversion, 0x10 unter dem Ende des Anwendungs-RAM (Abschnitt 2).

    REQ -- no --> V1("app_image_valid(&checked)<br/>record, compat OK, entry, CRC-32<br/>the only CRC of the start")
    V1 -- invalid --> STAY
    V1 -- valid --> WIN("startup window<br/>10 02 received: stay")
    WIN --> V2("app_image_confirm(&checked)<br/>record read again, compat, entry,<br/>record crc and size = checked")
    V2 -- no --> STAY
    V2 -- yes --> JUMP("hal_jump_to_app()")

    classDef own fill:#ccfbf1,stroke:#0f766e,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    class INIT,REQ,STAY,V1,WIN,V2,JUMP own

Legende

  • Gesamtablauf mit der Anwendung danach: Bild 3, Startablauf. Hier nur die zwei Prüfungen des Bootloaders (Abschnitt 4): die CRC läuft einmal je Start, die zweite Prüfung vor dem Sprung liest den Record erneut und vergleicht ihn mit dem Ergebnis aus bl_init().
  • Die beiden Resets des Watchdog-Schnelltests überspringen das Startfenster (hal_reset_skips_startup_window()).
  • Zwischen den Prüfungen schreibt der Bootloader nichts in den Flash; der Eintritt in die Programmiersitzung hält ihn im Bootloader (Abschnitt 4).

docs.title: Flash-Ablauf über UDS
docs.text:
Die Sequenz (Sitzung, Security Access, Fingerprint, 31 01 FF00, 34/36/37, 31 01 FF01, 11 01) steht als Bild 4, Flash-Ablauf über UDS; Kennungen und Routinen in Abschnitt 4 dieses Dokuments. Nicht wiederholt, damit es nur eine Fassung gibt.

Konformität gegen ISO 14229-1 Kapitel 16 (Programmierablauf, Tabellen 501–503, Anforderungen 16.4.1–16.4.3): iso14229-1-clause16-conformance.md – Zeile für Zeile mit Stand und Test-ID, samt der offenen Punkte, die nur am Board zu belegen sind.

Stand (2026-09-21: Transportschnitt im Kern; davor 2026-09-18, davor; Abschnitt 4 neu und englisch). Zielbild: doc/architecture/README.md Abschnitt 7 (D6: C ohne OpenBSW, HAL je Familie, gleiche Konfigurationsquelle). Verifikation dieses Dokuments: Analyse gegen Code, mcudb und doc/architecture/plattformen.md; Aussagen zu S32K3/STM32 ohne Beleg im Repo sind als Annahme markiert.

docs.title: 2. HAL-Schnitt src/core/bl_hal.h gegen S32K3 und STM32
docs.text:
Der Kern ist familienneutral; was von der Familie abhängt, steht hinter bl_hal.h. Die Tabelle zeigt, was der Schnitt für die R1-Familie (s32k1xx) bedeutet und wo andere Familien eine Entscheidung brauchen. STM32F4 ist umgesetzt S32K3 und Cortex-R4F sind Annahmen.

Funktion s32k1xx (R1) Andere Familien hal_init() Kern bleibt auf dem Reset-Takt FIRC, SOSC für FlexCAN/LPSPI, Hooks, FlexCAN S32K3: FXOSC für CAN, Takt über MC_ME/MC_CGM. STM32: HSI, mit BL_CLOCK_HSE SYSCLK auf HSE, weil bxCAN nur aus PCLK1 läuft hal_millis(), hal_entropy(), hal_reset() SysTick aus BL_CORE_CLOCK_HZ, NVIC_SystemReset Cortex-M-neutral; Cortex-R4F: RTI und Familien-HAL hal_can_send/receive/tx_idle() FlexCAN, Mailboxen im Polling STM32: bxCAN mit einer Sende-Mailbox, FIFO 0, zwei Filterbänke; FDCAN (G4) offen hal_flash_erase_sector(address) FTFC, 4-KB-Sektoren, RAM-Funktion S32K3: 8-KB-Sektoren; STM32F4: ungleiche Sektoren 16/64/128 KB. Die Geometrie ist Daten: bl_sectors.h liefert Start, Größe und Index eines Sektors aus der generierten Tabelle hal_flash_program(address, data, len) Phrase 8 Byte (program_size) BL_PHRASE_SIZE aus mcudb; STM32F4 leitet PSIZE daraus ab hal_boot_request_consume() nur nach Software-Reset (RCM_SRS.SW) STM32: RCC_CSR.SFTRSTF; S32K3: MC_RGM (Annahme) hal_reset_skips_startup_window() true nur für die zwei Resets des Watchdog-Schnelltests (RCM_SRS genau WDOG, WDOG_CS[TST] 2 oder 3); Power-on antwortet false false, solange kein Port eine solche Testfolge zeigt hal_random(out, len) (optional) nicht vorhanden (kein TRNG ohne CSEc) Familie mit Zufallsgenerator definiert sie, der Seed mischt ihn ein hal_app_entry_plausible(start, size) Cortex-M-Regel: Stapelzeiger im App-RAM, Reset-Vektor Thumb Cortex-R4F: feste Weiterleitungstabelle am Anwendungsanfang (E2) hal_jump_to_app(appStart) SysTick/FlexCAN aus, ICER/ICPR, VTOR, MSP STM32: VTOR auf BL_FLASH_START, bxCAN über MCR.RESET still; Cortex-R4F: kein VTOR Startup, Linker FCF bei 0x400 in platforms/s32k1xx/linker.ld STM32: kein FCF, Vektortabelle 0x200; S32K3: IVT/Boot-Header

Reset handler, s32k1xx: bl_system_init() schaltet den MCU-Watchdog aus (WDOG_CS[TST] bleibt für den Schnelltest der Anwendung) und dann den Low-Voltage-Detect-Reset ein (PMC_LVDSC1 = LVDRE, SM-59 von einer früheren Änderung), vor der RAM-Initialisierung. Der Wert kommt aus platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/include/pmc/LowVoltageDetectReset.h; die Datei bl_lvd_s32k1xx.cpp ist die einzige C++-Einheit des Bootloaders.

Record und Boot-Request: Record-Format (app_record_t, Magic „APPV“) und Boot-Request (Magic + Inversion, 0x10 unter dem App-RAM-Ende) gelten für alle Familien. Die Record-Position ist frei (BL_APP_RECORD_ADDR und BL_APP_END getrennt). Bootloader-Bereich, Anwendungsbereich und Record liegen auf Sektorgrenzen, der Record-Sektor nicht im Anwendungsbereich; bl_sector_map_ok() prüft das.

Updater: updater/src/core/bl_update.c ist familienneutral und hält den Ablauf (Stub, übrige Sektoren, Sektor 0, Record; Wiederaufnahme über die Einsprung-Phrase bei Offset 0). Der Abbild-Anfang gehört der Familie (platforms/<familie>/upd_family.h, upd_family_check_image.inc). Gebaut wird der Updater nur, wenn updater/platforms/<familie> existiert; S32K3, STM32 und Cortex-R4F brauchen einen eigenen Port. tools/canflash wählt dieselbe Regel aus der Familie (IMAGE_RULES); eine Familie ohne Regel lehnt canflash blimage/blupdate ab. Der Hook sbcUja113x nutzt bl_spi.h (16 Bit, CPOL 0, CPHA 1); fehlt bl_spi_<familie>.c, bricht devices/sbcUja113x/bootloader.cmake ab.

docs.title: SBC watchdog in the bootloader (bootloader 0.3.11)
docs.text:
%%{init: {'theme':'base','flowchart':{'curve':'basis'},'themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif','fontSize':'14px','background':'#ffffff','primaryColor':'#ffffff','primaryBorderColor':'#64748b','primaryTextColor':'#0f172a','lineColor':'#475569','edgeLabelBackground':'#ffffff','tertiaryColor':'#f8fafc','clusterBkg':'#f8fafc','clusterBorder':'#cbd5e1'}}}%%
flowchart TD
    INIT("sbc_init(configure)<br/>registers read, SBC plausible") --> CFG(("SBC in<br/>bootloader.init?"))
    CFG -- "yes: sbc_init(true)" --> PRJ(("bootloader.sbc_watchdog"))
    CFG -- "no: sbc_init(false)" --> RSDMS(("SDMS?"))
    PRJ -- serve --> SETUP("reason PROJECT<br/>Standby, WMC autonomous, 1024 ms<br/>written twice, read back")
    PRJ -- leave --> SDMS(("SDMS?"))
    SDMS -- "0: no development mode" --> SETUP0("reason SDMS0<br/>same setting as serve")
    SDMS -- "1: development mode" --> LEAVE("reason NONE<br/>watchdog not touched")
    RSDMS -- "0: no development mode" --> SETUPR("reason SDMS0_READ<br/>only the watchdog, same setting<br/>(Standby first if found in Normal)")
    RSDMS -- "1: development mode" --> READ("reason NONE<br/>read only, nothing written")
    SETUP --> NORMAL("Normal mode, V2, CAN active")
    SETUP0 --> NORMAL
    LEAVE --> NORMAL
    SETUPR --> STBY("SBC stays in Standby<br/>V2 and CAN not written")
    SETUP -- "not taken" --> E5("stage 0xE5<br/>no Normal mode")
    SETUP0 -- "not taken" --> E5
    SETUPR -- "not taken" --> E5
    NORMAL --> POLL("bl_device_service() every poll:<br/>trigger every 256 ms")
    STBY --> POLL
    POLL --> JUMP("last trigger right before<br/>hal_jump_to_app(): 1024 ms for the application")

    classDef own fill:#ccfbf1,stroke:#0f766e,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    classDef no fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#b91c1c,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    class INIT,CFG,PRJ,SETUP,SDMS,SETUP0,LEAVE,RSDMS,SETUPR,READ,STBY,NORMAL,POLL,JUMP own
    class E5 no
  • SDMS 0 is always served. After an SBC reset without software development mode the UJA113x watchdog is a timeout watchdog with 128 ms that already runs in Standby (public data sheet UJA113X_SER Rev. 2, Table 7 with 7.2.1, Table 8). Before leave left it alone: without a valid application the SBC reset the ECU over and over, with one the application got only the rest of 128 ms. Since (safety review SBC watchdog 2026-10-06, SDMS0-1 c) the hook serves it whatever the project says; leave takes effect only with SDMS 1.
  • Also when the SBC is only read (bootloader 0.3.11). An SBC that is not in bootloader.init (sbc_init(false)) has the same running watchdog. Since (safety review bootloader 0.3.10 2026-10-07) the hook sets up only the watchdog and serves it: the setting needs Standby (a change of WMC/NWP in Normal mode is a system reset, data sheet 7.2, 7.3.3), serving does not need Normal mode (autonomous in Standby is off while INTN1 is high and a timeout watchdog while an interrupt is pending, Table 8). So the SBC stays in Standby, regulator (V2) and CAN control are not written; an SBC found in Normal mode after an MCU-only reset is put into Standby for the setting and stays there until the application takes over. With SDMS 1 it stays read only.
  • serve differs from leave only with SDMS 1: a watchdog the application left running (MCU-only reset) is set to the fixed setting, i.e. autonomous and therefore off in development mode.
  • Not touched: Forced Normal mode (watchdog off), an SBC that never answers plausibly (stage 0xE4), and an SBC that is only read with SDMS 1.
  • Diagnosis over J-Link: bl_sbc_watchdog (reason 0 none, 1 project serve, 2 SDMS 0, 3 SDMS 0 with the SBC only read; served, triggers, errors, register 0x00 before and after), bl_sbc_diag (registers, stage).
  • The application takes the running watchdog over within 1 024 ms after the jump (AoU-34). The updater builds the hook without the service and still refuses to run unless the SBC watchdog is off (SDMS 1); read only stays read only there.
  • Build: devices/sbcUja113x/bootloader.cmake defines BL_SBC_WATCHDOG_SERVICE (hook) and BL_DEVICE_SERVICE (bl_main.c) for every bootloader with this hook, and BL_SBC_WATCHDOG_SERVE with serve. Host test: bootloader/test/host/test_bl_sbc_watchdog_host.py (tools/test -k bl-sbc-watchdog-host).

Antwortzeiten von Flash-Aufträgen: Ein Auftragsschritt (Sektor löschen, CRC-Stück, Programmierstück, Record) muss in P2* (BL_P2STAR_SERVER_MS, 5 s) passen. Ein Auftrag beginnt mit „response pending“ (0x78); danach schätzt der Kern den nächsten Schritt aus den bisherigen Kosten (Löschen je KB, mal die Größe des nächsten Sektors). Ein 0x78 geht nur, wenn der Schritt hinter P2* enden könnte, und nie früher als BL_PENDING_MIN_GAP_MS (0,3 x P2*, ISO 14229-2) nach dem vorigen. Ein Sektor, der allein länger als P2* braucht, ist nicht abgedeckt; dann muss P2* steigen oder das Löschen unterbrechbar werden.

Zeitbasis des CAN-Transports: bl_transport_poll(nowMs) stempelt alle Frames eines Polls mit dem nowMs dieses Polls und vergleicht N_Cr und N_Bs gegen denselben Wert; ein Stempel hinter nowMs lässt nie einen Timer ablaufen.

docs.title: 3. Kompatibilität mit dem geflashten Bootloader
docs.text:
Wer die Aufteilung im Projekt ändert, ändert Bootloader und Anwendung: ein bereits geflashter Bootloader prüft weiter seine alten Adressen. Bootloader-Bereich, Record-Sektor, App-RAM-Ende und No-Init-Größe eines Boards im Feld daher nur zusammen mit einem Bootloader-Update ändern. Familien-Hooks sind textuell eingebunden (#include "bl_family_image.inc" in app_image.c, upd_family_check_image.inc in upd_check_blob()), damit die Abbilder byte-gleich bleiben; die SHA-256-Vergleiche der einzelnen Änderungen stehen im Changelog.

Abbild geändert → Version geändert. Ein Bootloader im Feld ist nur an seiner Nummer (BL_VERSION_NUMBER, DID 0xF180/0xF189) erkennbar. bootloader/test/image_version.sha256 hält je Nummer den SHA-256 des Abbilds des Referenz-Presets evalboard-s32k144-demo und die GCC-Version. tools/elfcheck blversion <bootloader.hex> vergleicht, der Host-Test bootloader/test/test_bl_image_version.py macht ein geändertes Abbild bei gleicher Nummer rot. Neue Nummer: bl_config.h hochziehen, Demo bauen, tools/elfcheck blversion --add <bootloader.hex>; bestehende Zeilen schreibt es nie um. Ein Bau mit anderer GCC-Version ist nicht vergleichbar (übersprungen).

ändert die Speicheraufteilung (Key-Sektor unter dem Record, die Anwendung endet einen Sektor früher): Bootloader und Anwendung ab gehören zusammen und gehen in einem Bootloader-Update aufs Board. Erweitert den Record hinter dem Kompatibilitätsblock (Abschnitt 4); ein Bootloader vor einer späteren Änderung liest die ersten 56 Byte und ignoriert den Rest.

docs.title: 4. Security access, identification and fingerprint
docs.text:
Key sector. The device key of the security access lives in its own flash sector, BL_KEY_ADDR/BL_KEY_AREA_SIZE of the generated bl_memory.h: the sector below the validity record (eval board: 0x7E000, 4 KB; STM32F446 test layout: sector 2). It is outside the bootloader area, which the updater rewrites completely, and outside the application area, which every download erases, so a provisioned key survives both. The bootloader image itself is the same for every device and holds no key. The key record (NXKY, version, method, length, 32-byte key, CRC-32; 48 bytes, bl_config.h) is written once per chip by tools/canflash/provision.py over the debugger. An erased, half written or foreign record counts as "no key": the security access answers NRC 0x22 and DID 0xF1A1 says why.

Method. Key = HMAC-SHA256(device key, seed), device key = HMAC-SHA256(master key, chip UID). SHA-256/HMAC are implemented in src/core/sha256.c, seed and key in src/core/seedkey.c (own translation units since). The seed (16 bytes) mixes a pool in no-init RAM with the UID, timers (hal_entropy(), hal_millis()) and, where the family has one, the hardware random generator: hal_random() is an optional HAL function with a weak "not available" default in the core; no family defines it yet (S32K1 without CSEc has no TRNG). A counter in no-init RAM keeps a reset from bringing back an earlier seed; failed attempts and a running lockout survive a reset as well.

Identifiers (src/core/uds.c; all but 0xF184 readable in every session without security access):

DID Content Source 0xF180 bootloader identification: numberOfModules 01 (Annex C.1) followed by "<prefix> <version>" BL_VERSION_PREFIX (project, bl_diag.h) + BL_VERSION_NUMBER (bl_config.h) 0xF186 active session UDS state 0xF189 software version number, ASCII BL_VERSION_NUMBER 0xF18C ECU serial number = chip UID (the tester derives the device key from it) derivative uid (bl_security.h) 0xF191 hardware number "<board>/<derivative>", ASCII (a build between sent the 4 bytes of BL_TARGET_ID) BL_HARDWARE_ID (bl_memory.h); BL_TARGET_ID is its CRC-32 0xF1A0 compatibility: record version, target and layout identity, application area, state of the installed record bl_memory.h, record 0xF1A1 security access: format, method, key state (0 missing, 1 present, 2 invalid), seed and key length bl_security.h, key sector 0xF184 application software fingerprint: 4 bytes date (BCD) + 12 bytes tester, programming session only see below

Form der Kennungen. 0xF180 des Bootloaders und 0xF180/0xF181 der Anwendung antworten nach ISO 14229-1 Anhang C.1: ein Byte numberOfModules (hier immer 1) und danach der Kennungstext. Im Flash steht der Text ohne Zählbyte, weil Anwendung (findBootloaderVersion()), Updater (upd_check_blob()) und canflash blimage ihn dort suchen. tools/canflash liest beide Formen (erstes Byte 0x01..0x1F = Modulzahl, ab 0x20 = Text) und meldet, welche es bekam. Ein Tester vor einer späteren Änderung liest die Antwort eines als Text mit Steuerzeichen und verliert den Versionsvergleich von canflash blupdate; ein Arbeitsplatz aktualisiert canflash also vor dem Flashen eines.

Routines (RoutineControl 31 01, programming session with security access):

RID Function Range (ISO 14229-1 Annex F.1) 0xFF00 erase memory: control option 44, address, length eraseMemory, fixed by the standard 0xFF01 check memory: CRC-32, application entry, validity record with fingerprint checkProgrammingDependencies, fixed by the standard 0xF1A0 check compatibility: record version, target and layout identity, application area of the image; a mismatch blocks erase and download system supplier range 0xF000..0xFEFF 0xFF02 the same check under its number before answered for testers from before 0.3.4 reserved by the standard - transition only

Kompatibilitätsroutine verschoben (Bootloader 0.3.4). Bis 0.3.3 war die Prüfung Routine 0xFF02, ein vom Standard reservierter Wert; sie liegt jetzt auf 0xF1A0 im Bereich des Systemlieferanten, derselben Nummer wie DID 0xF1A0. Beide führen dieselbe Prüfung aus. canflash wählt nach der Version in DID 0xF180: 0.3.3 und älter bekommen 0xFF02, neuere 0xF1A0. 0xFF02 ganz zu entfernen ist eine Entscheidung über die Tester im Einsatz (offener Punkt 10 der Konformitätstabelle).

Fingerprint. The tester writes DID 0xF184 (WriteDataByIdentifier, programming session, after security access) before the first erase or download; without it both are refused with NRC 0x22. It lives in uds_t for the session and is dropped with a session change. Since routine 0xFF01 (check memory) writes it into the validity record as a block of its own behind the compatibility block: magic APPF, the 16 bytes, CRC-32 over both (app_record_t, src/core/app_image.h; record 80 bytes, a multiple of the flash phrase, checked at compile time). Reading DID 0xF184 returns the fingerprint written in the running session, otherwise the one of the installed application's record, otherwise NRC 0x22. A record written before or by canflash record, has the block erased and no fingerprint. No FlexNVM is used.

Startentscheidung (Bootloader 0.3.7, 0.3.8). Nur ein Record mit vorhandenem und passendem Kompatibilitätsblock (APP_COMPAT_OK) wird gestartet; ein Record ohne Block (APP_COMPAT_ABSENT) startet nicht mehr (DID 0xF1A0 meldet 0x10, Neuflashen der Anwendung behebt es), weil ein einziges verfälschtes Wort compatMagic sonst die Ziel- und Layoutprüfung übersprungen hätte. Die Entscheidung wird unmittelbar vor hal_jump_to_app() ein zweites Mal geprüft, denn das Ergebnis von bl_init() ist ein RAM-Wort, das ein Tester Minuten in der Extended Session halten kann. Scheitert die zweite Prüfung, bleibt der Bootloader. Der Bootloader läuft ohne MCU-Watchdog (s32k1xx: in bl_system_init() abgeschaltet; HSI Abschnitt 4.13, Safety-Handbuch Abschnitt 4).

Pro Start läuft genau eine CRC-32 über das Abbild (eine zweite Voll-Prüfung kostete am Eval Board etwa 160 ms je Start):

bl_init(): app_image_valid(&checked) vor dem Sprung: app_image_confirm(&checked) Record (Magic, recordCrc, Bereich, Start) ja ja, erneut aus dem Flash gelesen Kompatibilitätsblock (APP_COMPAT_OK) ja ja Anwendungsstart (hal_app_entry_plausible()) ja ja CRC-32 über das Abbild ja, die einzige des Starts; Wert und Größe gehen in checked nein: crc und size des Records müssen checked entsprechen

Das genügt, weil der Bootloader zwischen beiden Prüfungen keinen Flash-Befehl ausgibt: Löschen, Download und Record-Schreiben sind Aufträge der Programmiersitzung, deren Eintritt stayInBootloader setzt; die Extended Session verweigert sie alle (Host-Tests test_extended_session_grants_no_programming_rights, test_flash_is_written_only_by_jobs_of_the_programming_session). Nicht gesehen wird ein Abbildkörper, der ohne Flash-Befehl des Bootloaders geändert wurde (Debugger, Bitfehler); das deckt die ROM-Prüfung SM-14 der Anwendung beim Start (Grenze als Host-Test test_image_changed_without_flash_command_is_left_to_the_application).

docs.title: Conformance with ISO 14229-1 clause 16 (non-volatile server memory programming)
docs.text:
Status (2026-09-22). This is a self-assessment of the neXtBSW boot software (bootloader/) and of the application UDS server (ecu/uds) against clause 16 of ISO 14229-1 (edition 2026), which defines what a programmable server has to support so that a conforming client can reprogram it.

The standard itself is licensed and is not part of this repository (doc/confidential/, excluded by .gitignore). Nothing below quotes it: the rows name the clause, the table and the row, and describe our implementation in our own words. Read this next to the standard, not instead of it.

How to read the status column

Status Meaning met implemented and covered by an automated test named in the evidence column partial the required behaviour exists, but a named part of it is missing or differs; the difference is spelled out open not implemented, or only verifiable on hardware (then: "open, board evidence") n/a the requirement applies to a capability this ECU does not have

Verification. Everything marked "met" is verified on the host (simulated flash and CAN, ISO-TP and UDS driven by udsoncan), never on the board. Evidence is given as <test group of tools/test>: <test method>. Rows that need a measurement or a physical fault injection say so and stay open until a follow-up task covers them on the board.

docs.title: 1. Table 501 — what the boot software must answer while the network is being prepared
docs.text:
The preprogramming step (16.3.1.1) quiesces the vehicle network before anything is flashed. Its rows apply to the boot software whenever the boot software is what answers - after a failed programming attempt, or when a boot request kept the ECU there. When the application is running it answers these rows instead, so both columns matter.

Row (service, parameter, step) Boot software Application Evidence DiagnosticSessionControl, extendedDiagnosticSession (0x03), step (2) — mandatory met. The session grants no rights of its own: security access, fingerprint, erase, download and transfer stay bound to the programming session met (OpenBSW DiagnosticSessionControl) bootloader-host: test_preprogramming_step_of_iso_14229_1_is_answered, test_extended_session_grants_no_programming_rights; app-uds-host: test_write_ram_identifier_only_in_extended_session CommunicationControl (0x28), controlType manufacturer specific (disable non-diagnostic communication), step (7) — mandatory met. controlType 0x00..0x03, communicationType checked against Annex B.1 (message classes 1..3, subnet 0x0 and 0xF). No action is taken and no state is kept: the boot software sends and evaluates no application messages, so the positive response is all the standard asks for met. Here it really switches: the state reaches the ECU as "send" and "evaluate", and the send side acts on it — the diagnostic stack hands every change to the generated COM (rte::setApplicationTxEnabled(), tools/rtegen), which stops writing the cyclic application messages and brings them back in their own phase with the E2E counter one step on. The state is restored when the session ends. Evaluating received application messages (controlType 0x02/0x03) is still only carried. A request naming only network management messages is answered but changes nothing — this ECU has none bootloader-host: test_communication_control_subfunctions_and_negative_responses; app-uds-host: test_communication_control_switches_the_application_messages, test_session_end_restores_communication_and_dtc_updates; rtegen: RteCommControlHostTest ControlDTCSetting (0x85), DTCSettingType = off (0x02), step (5) — mandatory met. On and off are answered; a DTCSettingControlOptionRecord is refused with requestOutOfRange, because without a fault memory there is nothing it could refer to. No action is needed: the boot software updates no DTC status bits partial. The service answers and carries the state, but there is no fault memory yet to freeze. An option record is refused with incorrectMessageLengthOrInvalidFormat rather than requestOutOfRange, because the application declares support for the two byte form only bootloader-host: test_control_dtc_setting_subfunctions_and_negative_responses; app-uds-host: test_control_dtc_setting_freezes_the_status_updates RoutineControl (0x31), manufacturer routine, steps (4) and (6) — optional partial. Step (4) "check programming preconditions" is covered by routine 0xF1A0 (0xFF02 up to boot software 0.3.3): the client declares the target and memory layout of its image and the boot software refuses to erase or download on a mismatch. Step (6) "disable failsafe reaction" does not exist — the boot software runs no failsafe strategy n/a (the application hands over to the boot software before this step matters) bootloader-host: test_bootloader_blocks_programming_after_a_declared_mismatch, test_mismatching_image_is_rejected_before_erasing, test_compatibility_routine_in_the_supplier_range ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22), manufacturer identifiers, step (8) — optional met. 0xF180 boot software identification, 0xF189 software version, 0xF191 hardware number, 0xF18C ECU serial (chip UID), 0xF184 fingerprint, 0xF1A0 compatibility, 0xF1A1 security state. Since an earlier change the identification identifiers carry the numberOfModules byte of Annex C.1 (section 5) met (0xF180, 0xF181, 0xF186, 0xFD00) bootloader-host: test_identification_dids_come_from_one_source, test_target_compatibility_did; bl-security-host: test_uid_and_security_state_are_readable_in_the_default_session LinkControl (0x87), step (9) — optional, required for a bit rate switch n/a. No bit rate switch: the programming event runs at the CAN bit rate of the project, the same one the application uses. Implementing 0x87 would only be needed to speed up a download by switching bit rate mid-event n/a (same reason) —

docs.title: 2. Table 502 — what the boot software must support while the download runs
docs.text:
Row (service, parameter, step) Status Note Evidence DiagnosticSessionControl, programmingSession (0x02), step (1) — mandatory met Answered by the boot software and by the application; the application sets the boot request and resets into the boot software after the positive response has left bootloader-host: test_boot_request_enters_programming_session; app-uds-host: test_programming_session_sets_boot_request_after_response SecurityAccess (0x27), requestSeed (0x01) / sendKey (0x02), step (2) — optional, required for theft/emission/safety related systems met 16 byte seed, key = HMAC-SHA256 over a per-chip device key, attempt counter and lockout survive a reset bl-security-host: test_seed_of_16_bytes_and_hmac_key_unlock, test_wrong_key_and_lockout_of_ten_seconds, test_lockout_and_failed_attempts_survive_a_reset WriteDataByIdentifier (0x2E), fingerprint identifiers, step (3) — optional partial 0xF184 applicationSoftwareFingerprint is implemented and required before the first erase and the first download. 0xF183 and 0xF185 are not (section 5) bootloader-host: test_fingerprint_is_written_and_read_back, test_download_without_fingerprint_is_refused, test_fingerprint_needs_the_programming_session_and_security RequestDownload (0x34), steps (4), (7), (9) — mandatory met Address and length format 0x44, range checked against the application area, maxNumberOfBlockLength from bl_config.h bootloader-host: test_full_flash_cycle_then_app_starts, test_hex_outside_the_application_area_is_refused TransferData (0x36) — mandatory met (host); board evidence open Block sequence counter with repetition of the last block, phrase aligned programming, NRC 0x73 on a wrong counter. Blocks of the full maxNumberOfBlockLength (1026 bytes, 147 CAN frames) are received again since an earlier change: from a separate task on, the CAN transport lost most of them silently when the tick fell inside a poll (section 7). The fix is verified on the host with a clock model of that tick, not yet on the board bootloader-host: test_download_with_maximum_block_length_and_asynchronous_tick, test_transfer_data_of_maximum_length_frame_by_frame, test_wrong_block_sequence_and_range_checks, test_programming_failure_reports_nrc_72 RequestTransferExit (0x37) — mandatory met Refused with requestSequenceError while bytes are still outstanding bootloader-host: test_full_flash_cycle_then_app_starts RoutineControl (0x31), startRoutine (0x01), steps (5), (6), (8), (10), (11) — optional met 0xFF00 erase (step 6), 0xFF01 check memory with CRC-32 and the write of the validity record (step 11), 0xF1A0 compatibility declaration (0xFF02 before a later change). Steps (4), (5), (7) and (8) — downloading an erase or programming routine — do not apply: both routines are permanently in the boot memory partition bootloader-host: test_erase_follows_the_sector_table, test_wrong_crc_does_not_validate, test_check_memory_refuses_an_application_start_of_another_kind ECUReset (0x11), hardReset (0x01), step (12) — mandatory met The response leaves before the reset; 0x03 softReset is accepted as well bootloader-host: test_full_flash_cycle_then_app_starts

Download of an erase or programming routine (steps 4, 7). The standard allows a server to have neither routine in permanent memory and to accept them as a download. This boot software has both permanently, so a client never needs to download them. That is the stricter of the two options and needs no further evidence.

docs.title: 3. Table 503 — what the boot software must support when the event is concluded
docs.text: Row Status Note Evidence ECUReset (0x11), hardReset (0x01), step (1) — mandatory met canflash sends it at the end of every flash run (post_programming_step()); the reset starts the freshly written application and returns the server to the defaultSession, which re-enables communication and DTC status updates app-uds-host: test_canflash_runs_the_full_programming_sequence; bootloader-host: test_full_flash_cycle_then_app_starts

docs.title: 4. 16.4.1 — requirements for servers to support programming
16.4.1.1 State of the pins during a programming session
docs.text: Requirement Status Basis In a programming session the server puts its pins into a defined, low-current state - as far as it can do so without endangering vehicle, server or people partial — open, board evidence Analysis. The boot software is only ever entered through a reset: a power-on reset, or the software reset the application performs after 10 02 (hal_boot_request_consume() reads RCM_SRS.SW). A system reset on Cortex-M returns every peripheral and every pin of the MCU to its reset state — inputs, output drivers disabled — which is the low-current default. The boot software then enables exactly two things: the CAN pins of the bootloader bus and, where the board has one, the SPI of a device hook. It drives no application output. What is not covered: outputs whose level is set outside the MCU — external drivers held by pull resistors, the outputs of the SBC itself, and any load that is switched on by default. Those are board facts and need a current measurement on the board, per board. Eval board S32K144 (2026-09-21, 12 V input, KL30B and power stage off): application idle 63.6 mA, boot software in the programming session without traffic 44.2 mA, during a download 44.3 mA - the programming session draws less than the application. There is also no hook today by which a board could name a safe output state for the programming session; adding one would touch blgen and platforms/, outside this task

docs.title: 16.4.1.2 The boot software itself: protection of its partition and recovery
docs.text: Requirement Status Basis and evidence The boot memory partition is protected against inadvertent erasure met Software address range restriction: app_range_valid() accepts only BL_APP_START .. BL_APP_END, and the erase job additionally clamps the sector range to that window, so no UDS request can reach the boot software, the key sector or anything below the application. bl_sector_map_ok() checks at startup that the areas lie on sector boundaries and that the record sector is outside the application area. The boot software is replaced only by the separate updater application (bootloader/updater), never by the erase/download path the standard warns about. Evidence: bootloader-host: test_bootloader_area_and_record_sector_are_protected, test_hex_outside_the_application_area_is_refused; bl-security-host: test_key_sector_is_outside_every_erase_and_download Recovery after (c) disruption of data link communication met The erase job erases the validity record first, before the first application sector. From that moment the installed application is invalid, so any interruption leaves the ECU in the boot software on the next start. A vanished tester is also caught while the link is up: S3 returns the session to default. Evidence: bootloader-host: test_session_timeout_returns_to_default, test_corrupt_app_is_not_started, test_wrong_crc_does_not_validate Recovery after (a) loss of supplied power and (b) loss of the ground connection (a) met on the eval board; (b) open Eval board S32K144, boot software 0.3.1: supply switched off at 52 % of a download and on again (real power-on reset, RCM_SRS 0x82) - the boot software answers on CAN at once, reports no valid validity record, and a new download completes with a correct check. Before a later change the boot software stayed unreachable on CAN after such a power-on (SBC read before its start-up time). (b) loss of ground was not injected: the debugger, the UART and the CAN adapter would feed the board back. Same mechanism as (c) and simulated as a power loss in the host tests (host_power_loss(), used by the security tests): the record is invalid, the boot software stays and can be reprogrammed. What the host cannot show is a partially programmed flash phrase caused by a supply collapse during a write — that needs the real flash controller and a switched supply on the board Recovery after (d) over- or under-voltage conditions met on the eval board between 6 V and 15 V Eval board S32K144, boot software 0.3.1: the supply was lowered from 12 V to 6.0 V and raised to 15.0 V (upper limit of the test rule) during a download - both downloads completed with a correct check. A brown-out below the reset threshold during a write behaves like (a). The boot software measures no supply voltage and has no undervoltage threshold of its own; it relies on the reset behaviour of the MCU and, on boards with one, of the SBC. Whether the ECU always comes back reprogrammable from a brown-out during a write is a board measurement, per board. bl_board_environment_ok() exists only for the updater (external watchdog off), not as a voltage check

docs.title: 16.4.1.3 Security requirements
docs.text: Requirement Status Basis and evidence A seed and key feature via SecurityAccess protects against inadvertent erasure and unauthorized programming met Seed 16 bytes, key = HMAC-SHA256(device key, seed), device key = HMAC-SHA256(master key, chip UID), so no two chips share a key and the boot software image itself carries none. Failed attempts and the lockout survive a reset. Evidence: bl-security-host: test_device_key_and_record, test_the_uid_decides_the_device_key, test_every_byte_of_the_key_counts, test_repeated_key_and_key_of_an_older_seed_are_refused Field service replacement servers are shipped with the security feature activated met Stricter than asked: a chip whose key sector is erased, half written or holds a foreign record has no security access at all — 0x27 answers conditionsNotCorrect and DID 0xF1A1 says why. An unprovisioned device therefore cannot be programmed over CAN at all, rather than being programmable without a key. Evidence: bl-security-host: test_without_device_key_the_security_access_is_refused_with_a_clear_message, test_damaged_or_foreign_record_counts_as_no_key

docs.title: 5. 16.4.2 — software and data identification, fingerprints (Annex C.1)
docs.text:
Annex C.1 prescribes for the three identification identifiers that the first byte of the record is the number of reported modules; the rest of the structure is manufacturer specific. For the three fingerprint identifiers the whole content is manufacturer specific.

Identifier Status Note Evidence 0xF180 bootSoftwareIdentification met Answered by boot software and application as 01 (numberOfModules) followed by the identification text "<prefix> <version>" of that one module. The text is unchanged and, deliberately, unchanged in flash as well: the byte is put in front of it while the response is built, never stored. That keeps the three places that find a bootloader by searching its flash for the text working - the application, the updater's upd_check_blob() and canflash blimage. Transition: every device flashed before a later change answers the bare text, so canflash reads both forms (parse_identification(), first byte 0x01..0x1F = a module count, 0x20 and above = the first character of a text) and names the old one in its output. Such a device stays readable and flashable; the reverse case, a tester from before a later change against a server, only loses the version comparison of blupdate, so update the tester first bootloader-host: test_boot_software_identification_carries_the_number_of_modules, test_an_ecu_from_before_bl_22_is_read_and_flashed, test_the_two_identification_forms_read_back_the_same, test_identification_dids_come_from_one_source; app-uds-host: test_identification_identifiers_carry_the_number_of_modules, test_canflash_reads_both_forms_of_an_identification; canflash-tool: IdentificationFormTest 0xF181 applicationSoftwareIdentification met Application only, same form as 0xF180: 01 and the application's identification text. It is a constant of the build, not read from flash, so nothing searches for it and the transition costs nothing here app-uds-host: test_identification_identifiers_carry_the_number_of_modules, test_read_identifiers, test_multi_frame_response_and_request_flow_control 0xF182 applicationDataIdentification n/a There is no application data module separate from the application software: one image, one validity record. The identifier would have nothing to report — 0xF183 bootSoftwareFingerprint open (optional) The boot software is not written through the UDS programming path but by the updater application, so no fingerprint is recorded for it. Worth having once bootloader updates are routine — the updater would have to carry it into the record — 0xF184 applicationSoftwareFingerprint met 4 bytes date (BCD) plus 12 bytes tester identification. Required before the first erase and the first download, not merely accepted; written into the validity record by routine 0xFF01, so it survives the reset and can be read back from the installed application bootloader-host: test_fingerprint_is_written_and_read_back, test_fingerprint_survives_the_reset_in_the_record, test_fingerprint_of_the_wrong_length_is_refused, test_download_without_fingerprint_is_refused 0xF185 applicationDataFingerprint n/a Same reason as 0xF182 — Write operations to the identification identifiers are rejected met The boot software's 0x2E accepts 0xF184 and nothing else (requestOutOfRange otherwise); the application's 0x2E accepts 0xFD00 and nothing else bootloader-host: test_unknown_data_identifier_is_refused; app-uds-host: test_write_ram_identifier_only_in_extended_session

docs.title: 6. 16.4.3 / Table 504 — server routine access
docs.text: Routine Status Note Evidence 0xFF00 eraseMemory (standardized) met Control option record 44 plus address and length, checked against the application area and walked sector by sector from the generated sector table. "Response pending" (0x78) follows the timing rules of section 7: P2* only has to cover one sector, and the 0x78 are spaced as ISO 14229-2 asks (before, one was sent before every sector) bootloader-host: test_erase_follows_the_sector_table, test_erase_of_one_byte_erases_exactly_its_sector, test_response_pending_covers_long_sector_erases, test_fast_sector_erases_get_one_response_pending 0xFF01 checkProgrammingDependencies (standardized value, record format of the manufacturer) met CRC-32 over the downloaded image, plausibility of the application entry by the family hook, then the validity record including the fingerprint bootloader-host: test_wrong_crc_does_not_validate, test_application_start_refused_by_the_family_is_not_started 0xF1A0 check compatibility (system supplier range 0xF000..0xFEFF of Annex F.1) met The client declares target identity and memory layout of its image before erasing; after a mismatch the boot software refuses erase and download itself. The same number as DID 0xF1A0, which reads back what the routine compares. The response repeats the identifier of the request bootloader-host: test_compatibility_routine_in_the_supplier_range, test_bootloader_blocks_programming_after_a_declared_mismatch, test_canflash_declares_with_the_new_routine, test_unknown_routine_and_wrong_length; canflash-tool: CompatRoutineTest 0xFF02 (reserved by Annex F.1; formerly another standardized routine) partial (transition) Up to boot software 0.3.3 this was the compatibility check. Since 0.3.4 the boot software still answers it as the same check with the same state, so a tester from before a later change keeps flashing. canflash sends it only to boot software that reports a version below 0.3.4 in 0xF180 (the eval board ran 0.3.1 on 2026-09-22), and after a requestOutOfRange when the target names no version. A conforming tester that uses the reserved value for something else would reach the compatibility check - that is what stays partial until the transition ends (open point 10) bootloader-host: test_former_compatibility_routine_is_still_answered, test_mismatch_declared_with_the_new_routine_is_released_by_the_former, test_an_ecu_from_before_bl_24_is_flashed_with_the_former_routine, test_the_last_version_before_bl_24_gets_the_former_routine, test_without_identification_the_former_routine_follows_a_refusal; bl-update-mutations: six mutations

docs.title: 7. ISO 14229-2 clause 9 — server timing during flash jobs
docs.text:
Clause 16 of part 1 leaves the timing of the programming services to part 2. The rows below are the ones a flash job of the boot software touches; the values are bl_config.h (P2 50 ms, P2* 5000 ms, announced in the response to DiagnosticSessionControl).

Requirement (ISO 14229-2:2021) Status Basis and evidence 9.1.1 / 9.2 Table 4: a request whose final response cannot follow within P2 is answered with NRC 0x78 first, and every further response of that request follows within P2* of the previous one met (host) Every flash job (erase, check, TransferData) starts with a 0x78. Before each further step the core predicts its cost from the steps measured so far (erase per KB and sector size, other steps as the longest of the job; an unmeasured step counts as the longest a step may be) and sends a 0x78 when the step could end beyond P2. Evidence: bootloader-host: test_response_pending_covers_long_sector_erases (4-KB and 128-KB sectors of up to 4.1 s, no pause beyond P2), test_full_flash_cycle_then_app_starts 9.2 Table 4, note b (valid for the programming session by 9.5): consecutive 0x78 of one request at least 0.3 x P2*_Server_Max apart met (host); board evidence open BL_PENDING_MIN_GAP_MS = 0.3 x BL_P2STAR_SERVER_MS, derived in bl_config.h. A step that would need a 0x78 sooner waits for the gap instead; every step fits into P2* behind a fresh 0x78, so waiting is safe. Before a later change the erase job sent one before every sector: every 4 ms on the board (2026-09-21, 45 frames for 41 already blank sectors; a sector with content takes about 42 ms). Evidence: bootloader-host: test_fast_sector_erases_get_one_response_pending, test_response_pending_covers_long_sector_erases (spacing of every 0x78 checked in all five memory layouts) 9.2 REQ 5.19: the server processes a new request right after the transmission of the previous response met (host); board evidence open The CAN transport accepts the next request as soon as the core has released the previous one; the receive timers work on one time base per poll, so a message of any length up to maxNumberOfBlockLength is no longer dropped by a spurious N_Cr timeout. Evidence: bootloader-host: test_transfer_data_of_maximum_length_frame_by_frame, test_download_with_maximum_block_length_and_asynchronous_tick 9.5 REQ 5.25, Table 6: tS3_Server is stopped when a request starts (first frame of a segmented request, or a single frame) and started again when the final response has been transmitted (a 0x78 does not restart it), when the action is complete if no response is sent, or when the reception of a segmented request ends in an error met (host); board evidence open Since an earlier change (boot software 0.3.2): the transport reports a request from its first frame until the core releases it (bl_transport_rx_pending(), CAN: ISO-TP receive state), and uds_poll() holds S3 while that is true, while a job runs and until the response has left the transport. Before, S3 ran from the moment the previous request was complete, also during the reception of the next block and during a long flash job: a block that needed longer than S3 to arrive got NRC 0x24 (STmin 1 ms on a Windows tester), and a job longer than S3 lost the session with its positive response. The link transport implements the same function from the receive state of mcuLink (open point 9). Evidence: bootloader/test/host/test_bl_s3_host.py in three memory layouts - a 1026-byte block over 1.2 x S3 is programmed, S3 starts with the final response and still expires, an N_Cr error restarts it, an erase of 1.2 x S3 keeps the session

docs.title: 8. What is open
docs.text: # Open point Where it belongs 2 ControlDTCSetting carries the state, but there is no fault memory to freeze – 4 16.4.1.1: a hook by which a board can name a safe output state for the programming session (the eval board is measured) blgen/platforms 5 16.4.1.2 (b): loss of the ground connection during a flash write - needs a setup without back-feeding through debugger, UART and CAN ((a) and (d) measured on the eval board) On the board 6 0xF183 bootSoftwareFingerprint for bootloader updates through the updater own task 7 LinkControl (0x87) if a programming event should ever switch bit rate own task, only when the download time demands it 8 The transition window of a separate task: canflash reads both forms of 0xF180/0xF181. It may drop the old one once no device before a later change is left in the field - which is a decision about devices, not about code own task, after the bootloader update of the last device 9 S3 during reception: bl_transport_rx_pending() of the link transport (src/link/bl_transport_link.c, rxActive || rxComplete of mcuLink) is prepared but outside the paths of a separate task; board evidence of the CAN case (download with STmin 1 ms, a block slower than S3) open owner of src/link on the board 10 The transition window of a separate task: the boot software answers the compatibility check under 0xF1A0 and under the reserved 0xFF02, and canflash sends 0xFF02 to boot software below 0.3.4. The boot software may drop 0xFF02 once no tester from before a later change is in use, canflash its half once no device below 0.3.4 is left - two decisions about the field, not about code own task, after the bootloader update of the last device

docs.title: neXtBSW documentation
docs.text:
neXtBSW is a hardware-neutral, configurable basic software for 32-bit ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-R automotive MCUs, built on Eclipse OpenBSW. Applications are attached as Simulink models (AUTOSAR Classic SWC) through a generated RTE.

This page is the map. It tells you where to look; it does not repeat what the linked documents say.

docs.title: Reading paths
docs.text:
R1 is a development release; it makes no safety claim. The safety documents describe the target (ASIL B, safety element out of context) and what is still open.
