docs.title: Where to find what
docs.text:
I want to … Go to know what neXtBSW is, what the repository contains, how to build it the first time ../README.md take a board from schematic to a running ECU, step by step guide/, starting with getting-started.md set up an ECU in your own repository, with neXtBSW pinned to a fixed version guide/customer-project.md look up a configuration field (derivative, board.yaml, project.yaml, rte.yaml) reference/ — generated from the tools/nxconfig schema; rte.yaml: reference/rte.md see which driver and service modules exist and how far each is verified reference/modules.md — generated from libs/ (module manifests, module documentation, test list) see at a glance which modules are confirmed on a board and which only in host tests (mock) figures/07-modulkarte.md — module map and status matrix, generated from the module manifests like reference/modules.md; legend in German until a follow-up task look up a console command: syntax, purpose, the build or module it needs, board rules reference/console.md — generated from the command registration in the code understand how the layers, configuration levels and generators fit together architecture/overview.md see the system in pictures: layers, configuration flow, start-up, UDS flash, ECU states, safety chain, module map figures/ — captions in German until a follow-up task know what comes from OpenBSW and what neXtBSW adds architecture/openbsw.md know which parts follow AUTOSAR and which do not architecture/autosar.md find out which AUTOSAR specification documents exist, where they live and what the current release changed architecture/autosar-standard-set.md — index survey, nothing read in detail look up a binding architecture decision (D1–D15), the review questions, the target repo layout architecture/README.md — the binding target picture understand how an ECU with several MCUs is programmed (one over CAN, the others by it over SPI) architecture/planned.md — planned (after R1), short page see what neXtBSW assures about functional safety, and what it assumes of the integrator safety/concept.md — target ASIL B, safety element out of context see how edge interrupts on digital inputs are to be configured (level, driver, path into the RTE, safety) architecture/pin-interrupts.md — variant A implemented see which safety mechanisms work without software, and what they would cost safety/hardware-mechanisms.md — FTM fault inputs, TRGMUX, comparator; catalogue, none used yet know which static analysis runs, what counts as a deviation and how a new finding stops the CI safety/static-analysis.md — cppcheck with the MISRA add-on and clang-tidy, baseline, deviations see how much of the per-driver glue in the family integration is common, parameter or truly driver-specific architecture/treiber-anbindung-analyse.md — measurement behind know how versions are numbered, what is stable, what support exists, how to report a vulnerability architecture/versioning.md, ../SECURITY.md; third-party notices: ../NOTICE build, test and submit a change ../CONTRIBUTING.md read what changed, when and why ../CHANGELOG.md (repository: CHANGELOG.md) (German, see Language below)

Documentation that lives next to the code it describes stays there and is linked from here, not copied:

Area Document Projects, presets, ECU description, DBC ../projects/README.md Software components (Simulink, AUTOSAR Classic) ../swc/README.md Board profiles ../boards/<board>/README.md Board ports ../ecu/platforms/README.md UDS bootloader ../bootloader/doc/README.md Device drivers and libraries ../libs/bsw/<module>/doc/<module>.md (for example e2e, sbcUja113x) Tools (test runner, CI, flashing, board measurements) ../tools/<tool>/README.md, starting with tools/test Patches sent upstream to Eclipse OpenBSW openbsw-beitraege/README.md

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
Published documentation is written in English. The changelog stays German: it is the working log of this project, written and read by its author, and translating it would cost more than it is worth. The full rule, including what it means for code comments and commit messages, is in ../CONTRIBUTING.md.

All documents under architecture/ are English since an earlier change (2026-09-19); the file names stayed German so that existing references keep working. Some module documents under libs/ are still German and follow as a separate step. Anything new or rewritten is English from the start. Exception until a follow-up task translates them: the short pages under architecture/ for what is planned after R1 (planned.md, non-cortex-m-audit.md, rm4x-quellen.md, stm32-nucleo.md), the short page openbsw-beitraege/README.md and the shortening notes at the head of the shortened pages are German.

docs.title: How this folder is organised
docs.text:
doc/
  README.md        this page — the map
  guide/           task-oriented documentation for users: getting started, how-to guides
  reference/       look-up material, generated from the schema, from libs/ and from the console code
  architecture/    how and why the software is built the way it is, plus binding decisions
  safety/          safety concept, safety manual, analyses and work products (target ASIL B)

guide/, reference/ and architecture/ each have a README.md that says what belongs in it. The split is by what the reader wants (learn, do, look up, understand), not by component, so a page keeps its place as the software grows.

The same pages are built into a documentation website with MkDocs Material (mkdocs.yml in the repository root): search, German/English switcher, Mermaid, navigation along the reading paths above. It takes this folder plus README.md, the module documents next to the code and the tool READMEs, without moving files: one folder per navigation section, each with a README.md as the section index page, and only relative links between documents. The public site is built from the exported tree, so it holds exactly the published pages; how to build it: tools/docgen/website.md.

Not covered here, on purpose:

  • Hardware documents — the datasheets and schematics under hardware/ are manufacturer documents. They are kept locally for development; redistribution is not covered by their terms.
  • neXtBSW Studio — the desktop tool under tools/studio is proprietary and is not part of the open source project, so it has no documentation in this tree.

docs.title: neXtBSW – architecture target picture
docs.text: Status: 2026-09-15, accepted by the maintainer on 2026-09-15 (all proposals D1–D10 in section 10). Readers: the maintainer as architect, the maintainer and contributors. Binding for all tasks; deviations only after consulting the maintainer and with an entry in section 10. Reading versions for outsiders (English, 2026-09-18): overview.md (structure), openbsw.md (relationship to Eclipse OpenBSW), autosar.md (where AUTOSAR fits in). They explain the current state and refer back here; this document remains the binding one. Amended 2026-09-17 (decisions of the maintainer, history in CHANGELOG.md): core profile Cortex-R and D11–D14 (audit non-cortex-m-audit.md) platform rule (section 6), family port at application level (section 8), D7 amended, D15 added (analysis openbsw-naehe.md).

docs.title: 1. Goal and guiding principle
docs.text:
neXtBSW is a universally usable basic software for ARM-based automotive MCUs, put together by configuration (later neXtBSW Studio). Applications are added as Simulink models (AUTOSAR Classic SWC) through a generated RTE.

  • Core profiles: ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-R, 32 bit, little endian (D11). Big-endian derivatives (e.g. TI TMS570) are not part of the target picture; the little-endian assumption (record format, Platform_Types.h, canflash) stays valid.
  • Target families: focus S32K1, specifically also S32K3, STM32 and rm4x (TI Hercules RM4x, Cortex-R4F; proof target LAUNCHXL2-RM46, D13), in principle any automotive MCU with these core profiles.
  • Core and architecture are configuration, just like the board: code distinguishes profiles through the generated architecture (NX_CORE_ARCHITECTURE), never through core names or compiler macros such as __ARM_ARCH (equal to 7 for both Cortex-R4F and Cortex-M4F; implementation).
  • A board is a use case of the architecture, never its yardstick. The S32K144 eval board is the first example and must not trigger any architecture-relevant decisions.
  • One repository: reusable code (drivers, services, generators, bootloader) stays here, even when it is developed on the eval board. What is separated is data: derivative, board, project.

Terms:

Term Meaning Example Family MCU series with shared driver code s32k1xx, s32k3xx, stm32, rm4x Derivative specific chip with package S32K144 LQFP100, STM32G474RE, RM46L852 Board assembled PCB: derivative, crystal, parts, wiring evalboard_s32k144, nucleo_g474re Project one ECU software on one board: functions used, buses, tasks, SWCs evalboard_motor, evalboard_charger Module reusable building block with a manifest (driver, service) sbcUja113x, highSideSwitch, canSystem Role capability that a module provides or needs can_phy, power_supply, watchdog_trigger

docs.title: 2. Starting point: what OpenBSW delivers
docs.text:
The foundation is Eclipse OpenBSW as an unchanged submodule (version v0.1.0-677-g00e3cab1, 2026-08-13).

Carries weight and is used (details in openbsw.md section 2): the platforms posix, s32k1xx (reference S32K148-EVB) and stm32 (Nucleo F413ZH with bxCAN, Nucleo G474RE with FDCAN, so STM32 is not new ground), FreeRTOS or ThreadX, the hardware-independent middleware (async, lifecycle, cpp2can, docan, transport, uds, logger, console, time, util, storage, safety libraries, Ethernet/DoIP/SOME/IP) and a few neutral BSP interfaces (CanPhy, SystemTimer, IFlashDriver, IEepromDriver, IEcuPowerStateController, UartConcept, DigitalInput/Output/OutputPwm, charInputOutput).

Gaps that neXtBSW has to close

Gap in OpenBSW Consequence today No neutral ADC, SPI, I2C, input capture; watchdog and clock only as same-named headers per platform ADC code (AnalogInput) sits in the board configuration, SPI we added ourselves Pin level differs per family (bios::Io on S32K1, Gpio on STM32) Generated pin configuration is family-specific Integration per board by hand: main.cpp, StaticBsp, CanSystem, ISRs, linker script, startup are copied per board (the STM32 port even writes LED and UART registers directly in SystemInit) A second board means copying; board peculiarities creep into the start-up sequence No configuration description, no generators all values in hand-written headers Implementation can only be swapped via same-named headers and CMake targets (static) no checkable contract between interface and implementation

neXtBSW therefore adds: complete MCU interface contracts, device drivers, a configuration model with generators, generated integration, an RTE with Simulink connection, a bootloader and the Studio.

docs.title: 3. Layer model
docs.text:
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | L5  Application: SWCs from Simulink (swc/, projects/<p>/swc)                       |
 +------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | L4  RTE (generated): ports, runnables, tasks, data consistency, BSW service ports  |
 +------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | L3  ECU services (systems): communication (CAN, DoCAN, UDS), state/supply,         |
 |     watchdog manager, NvM, fault memory, console, measurement/calibration          |
 +--------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------+
 | L2  Device drivers/CDD (libs/bsw/<module>) |  Integration (generated per project): |
 |     SBC, gate driver, cell monitoring,     |  main, start-up order, lifecycle      |
 |     smart high-side switch, ...            |  levels, ISR table, role wiring,      |
 +--------------------------------------------+  memory layout                        |
 | L1  MCU abstraction: contracts libs/bsp/<class>,                                   |
 |     implementation platforms/<family>/bsp (OpenBSW or neXtBSW)                     |
 +------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | L0  Hardware: derivative + board                                                   |
 +------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 Cross-cutting: async/RTOS, lifecycle, logger, safety (family-specific parts in platforms/<family>/safety)
 Separate:      bootloader (C, without OpenBSW), own HAL per family, same configuration source

Rules:

  1. Dependencies only point downwards. L2 knows only L1 contracts, L3 only L1/L2 contracts and roles, L5 only the RTE.
  2. No layer knows a board. Board knowledge lives exclusively in configuration data and in the integration code generated from it. Hand-written code under a board name is only permitted for justified exceptions (e.g. working around a PCB defect), as a module of its own with a manifest.
  3. Exchange mechanism:
  4. L1: one implementation per build, selected via the family (static, like OpenBSW). Every contract has a header in libs/bsp/<class> and a contract test (host) that every family implementation must pass.
  5. Above L1: narrow virtual interfaces where several implementations in one build or mocks are needed (models: ISpiDevice in the SBC driver, CanPhy from OpenBSW).
  6. Roles instead of part names. Services request roles, modules provide them. CanSystem needs the role can_phy for a bus; whether a UJA1131, a TJA1044 with STB pin or a dummy fills it is decided by the configuration (section 5).
  7. Hardware-independent code gets host tests with a register model or mock; tests run against their own test profiles.

docs.title: L1 contracts (target)
docs.text: Class Contract Today Digital inputs/outputs DigitalInput/Output (OpenBSW) present, pin level family-specific PWM OutputPwm (OpenBSW) + complementary pairs with dead time pairs as ComplementaryPwm in the board configuration → family ADC new libs/bsp/bspAdc (raw value, conversion, internal channels, resolution from the derivative) only a board copy of the OpenBSW example Input capture new missing SPI ISpiDevice (neXtBSW) present, master only LPSPI I2C new missing CAN controller ICanTransceiver (OpenBSW) FlexCAN, bxCAN, FDCAN present CAN transceiver CanPhy (OpenBSW), readiness via getPhyErrorStatus sbc::Uja113xCanPhy and can::PassiveCanPhy implement it UART UartConcept (OpenBSW) present Flash, EEPROM IFlashDriver, IEepromDriver (OpenBSW) present, FlexNVM only S32K1 Watchdog, reset reason, clock new as a contract (today same-named headers per platform) family-specific System time SystemTimer (OpenBSW) present

docs.title: 4. Configuration levels
docs.text:
Three levels, each with its own schema (schema_version), YAML files, and one shared loader without Qt (tools/nxconfig) used alike by the generators, the command line and the Studio. Values are set exactly once; everything derived is computed by the generator.

 Derivative database        Board                         Project
 (manufacturer facts,       (what is fitted/wired)        (what the ECU uses)
  read-only)                boards/<board>/board.yaml     projects/<p>/project.yaml
 mcudb/<family>/...               |                        + rte.yaml, *.dbc, swc
        \_________________________|___________________________/
                                  v
                    nxconfig: load, link levels, validate
                     (conflicts, limits, missing roles, messages with YAML path)
                                  v
        bswgen (L1 configuration per family) · intgen (integration, memory layout)
        rtegen (RTE, tasks) · dbcgen · blgen (bootloader board part) · a2lgen (later)
                                  v
                build/<project>/generated/...  (not checked in)

docs.title: Responsibility per value
docs.text:
Value Level Reason Flash/RAM size, sector size, peripheral instances, pin mux options, ADC resolution, PLL limits, core (e.g. Cortex-M0+/M4F/M7/M33, Cortex-R4F), interrupt controller (NVIC with priority bits, VIM with channel count and fixed channels) Derivative datasheet, the same for all boards Possible clock sources and asynchronous outputs per peripheral instance, their maximum frequency (s32k1xx PCCn.PCS, instances.<x>.clock with sources, divider, max_hz) Derivative datasheet (manufacturer fact) Chosen clock source per used peripheral instance (peripheral_clocks.<instance>) Project usage decision; without an entry the derivative's default applies Derivative and package, crystal frequency, pin assignment, voltage dividers, ADC reference voltage, fitted parts and their connection (SPI, CS, INT pins), transceiver per CAN connection, pull-ups, debug interface Board property of the PCB Sensor circuit in front of an ADC pin (shunt, gain, reference, pull-up, diode, k_ILIS/R_IS), supply rails, fitted yes/no (adc[].sensor, rails, adc[].fitted) Board property of the PCB; the connected load (NTC characteristic, breakpoint table, adc_loads) is decided by the project Hardware peculiarities of a part that cannot be changed (e.g. MTPNV state of the SBC, missing pull-ups) Board belongs to the assembled PCB Power stage per PWM group: switching times, gate charge, R_DS(on), gate resistors of the PCB, driver propagation delays, V_DS short-circuit threshold (pwm[].power_stage) Board property of the fitted power stage; dead time and dead-time margin (deadtime_margin_ns) are decided by the project Short-circuit detection settings of a gate driver that are chosen over SPI (V_DS thresholds, filter, delay: modules.<device>.short_*) Project a choice of the project like the dead time; the board keeps only what the circuit fixes (R_DS(on), a hard-wired detector in power_stage.short_circuit); nxconfig derives the resulting short-circuit current from both Which peripherals are used, system clock, PWM frequency and dead time, bit rates, CAN IDs, UDS addresses, buses and roles per bus, tasks (number, priority, period, stack), stack sizes per exception mode (Cortex-R), SWCs and connections, monitoring thresholds, memory split bootloader/app/NvM, FlexNVM partitioning, safety outputs, test and expert functions Project decision of the respective ECU software Toolchain path, CAN adapter, serial port, debugger serial number Workstation (local, not checked in) belongs to the computer, not to the project

Consequences for today's entries: pwm.clock_hz is dropped (derived), pwm.frequency_hz/deadtime_ns and safety move into the project, exclusive_groups is dropped in favour of the general conflict check, adc_reference.resolution_bits comes from the derivative.

Separate fact and decision, even within one value. The peripheral clock shows the pattern: which sources and asynchronous outputs a clock switch offers and how fast the output may run is a manufacturer fact and lives in the derivative; which of them is used is decided by the project. So that a project does not have to fill in every value, the derivative names a default (default) that applies as long as the project chooses nothing – backed by evidence like any other derivative value. If there is no evidence for a default, it is left out: a used instance without a project choice is then an error with file, line and YAML path, instead of entering a guessed value. The same pattern applies to future values of this kind (pin pull, filter times, conversion times).

docs.title: Power-stage facts and minimum dead time
docs.text:
A complementary PWM group describes its power stage in the board under pwm[].power_stage (switch, driver, gate, short_circuit; int32 in fixed units ns, nC, mΩ, mV, each group with source/verify; fields in board.md). The project decides pwm.<group>.deadtime_ns and the margin deadtime_margin_ns. tools/nxconfig (powerstage.py) derives:

k_on  = (R_G,int + R_on,board)  / (R_G,int + R_G,test)        R_G,int missing -> 0 (conservative)
k_off = (R_G,int + R_off,board) / (R_G,int + R_G,test)        without resistor data: k = 1

t_off  = (t_d(off) + t_f) * max(1, k_off)                     switch still conducts after the turn-off command
t_on   =  t_d(on)         * min(1, k_on)                      opposite switch starts conducting

t_dead,min = max(0, t_off - t_on)                             switches
           + max(0, t_drv,off - t_drv,on)                     driver propagation delays
           + deadtime_margin_ns                               safety margin (project)

Switching times are entered as the datasheet states them (maximum, otherwise typical); the spread belongs in the margin; scaling to the PCB gate resistance only lengthens the dead time. If deadtime_ns is below the minimum, nxconfig reports it at the YAML path pwm.<group>.deadtime_ns: an error if all facts used have a source and are not verify: true, otherwise a warning; missing facts give a warning with the path, never an assumption. The same facts yield the short-circuit current V_DS,threshold / R_DS(on), the minimum blanking time (t_d(on) + t_r) * max(1, k_on) and the average gate current Q_G * f_PWM.

docs.title: Sensor characteristics on ADC channels
docs.text:
Decisions of the maintainer (all recommendations adopted; fields in board.md and project.md):

  1. Board = circuit, project = load. The board describes the circuit in front of the pin (shunt, amplifier, divider, pull-up) and delivers the quantity at the connector; the project describes the connected load (NTC characteristic, breakpoint table).
  2. Signed integer in fixed units (mV, mA, Ω, 0.1 °C, ‰), no float, at run time too (S32K116 has no FPU).
  3. Kinds. Board adc[].sensor.kind: linear, shunt_amplifier, divider, pullup, highside_is; rails under board.rails. Project adc_loads.<channel>.kind: ntc_beta and table.
  4. Zero-point calibration in operation stays a matter for the application; a BSW service follows later.
  5. Quality at the ADC limits: raw value 0 or full scale, amplifier outside its output range, open pull-up or a board value outside the breakpoints give QLF_ERROR_RANGE (value 32, signal-qualifier.md); a failed conversion QLF_ERROR; otherwise QLF_OK.
  6. No assembly variants in the schema: the board carries the fitted variant; circuits not fitted are marked adc[].fitted: false. scale and sensor both non-trivial is an error (the circuit is stated once); part facts with several users (k_ILIS/R_IS of a high-side switch) are stated once, at the sensor of its IS channel.

tools/nxconfig (sensor.py) derives a rational integer conversion for each used, fitted channel (U = raw · V_REFH / (2^bits − 1), exact as a fraction, then reduced):

x      = min(raw, calc_high)
board  = round((a * x + b) / (c * x + d))       int64, rounds half away from zero; c * x + d > 0 up to calc_high
value  = board | interpolate(points, board)     load: breakpoints ascending in board value, ends held

scale            U * factor + offset_mv                             mV
linear           U * gain_num / gain_den + offset                   unit
divider          U * (r_top + r_bottom) / r_bottom                  mV
shunt_amplifier  (U - U_ref) * 10^6 * gain_den / (gain * R_shunt)    mA   (R_shunt in µΩ)
pullup           R_pu * U / (U_supply - U_diode - U)                 Ω    (calc_high: last code with denominator > 0)
highside_is      k_ILIS * U / R_IS                                  mA
ntc_beta         table from R(T) = R_n * exp(B * (1/T - 1/T_n)) from t_min to t_max in steps of step_ddegc

Checks run over every raw value (int64 intermediates, int32 result, strictly ascending breakpoints, the largest NTC error against max_error_ddegc as a warning); every message with file, line and YAML path. tools/bswgen generates bsp/adc/analogSensorConfiguration.h (nxAdcPhys_<NAME>(raw, &quality), comment with formula and range, "UNCONFIRMED" if a source or verify is missing) and tools/rtegen the targets adc.phys.<NAME> (sint32) and adc.qlf.<NAME>; adc.phys without adc.qlf gives a warning.

docs.title: Validation (minimum scope)
docs.text:
• Pin, timer channel, peripheral instance used at most once; pin function possible according to the derivative.
  • Every requested role filled exactly once (e.g. can_phy for every bus used).
  • Clocks and timings reachable (PLL, bit timing, baud rate, PWM resolution, dead time).
  • Chosen peripheral clocks permitted by the derivative (source, output) and within the output's limit; the instance is actually used by the project.
  • Memory split fits into the derivative; bootloader and app do not overlap.
  • Messages with severity, text and YAML path (basis for Studio live checking).

docs.title: 5. Modules, roles and generated integration
docs.text:
Every reusable module in libs/bsw/<module> (and every L1 implementation) gets a manifest module.yaml:

module: sbcUja113x
kind: device_driver                 # mcu_driver | device_driver | service | library | contract (DOC-14)
requires:
  spi_device: 1                     # L1 contract
provides:                           # roles that a board part of this type can fill
  - can_phy                         # per integrated transceiver
  - power_supply                    # V1/V2, sleep, wake-up sources
  - watchdog_trigger                # external watchdog
  - early_init                      # optional hook before the MCU watchdog test (RCC compensation)
config_schema: schema.yaml          # project parameters (watchdog mode, V2, interrupts, ...)
lifecycle: { level: 1, task: bsp }
cmake_target: sbcUja113x
console: sbc                        # optional, expert functions marked
verification: hardware              # none | mock | hardware, with verification_note (DOC-14)

library (for example e2e, autosarBase) and contract (an L1 interface such as bspSpi) carry only the catalogue fields (module, kind, description, cmake_target, verification); nxconfig and bswgen never treat them as device drivers. The module catalogue doc/reference/modules.md is generated from these manifests.

A module that gives the application readable values declares them in rte, so a new driver becomes connectable through a target <prefix>.<Instance>.<value> without a change to the generator or the Studio:

# libs/bsw/gdTmc6200/module.yaml (excerpt)
rte:
  prefix: gd                        # target gd.<Device>.<value>; left out: the module name in lower case
  access: gate_driver               # generic "reading" contract (below), or the access code of an existing module
  instance: Device
  values:
    faults:  { types: [uint16, uint32], unit: "gd::fault bits, latched until the driver's clearFaults()" }
    enabled: { types: [boolean], unit: DRV_EN switched on by the driver }
    qlf:     { types: [uint8, uint16, uint32], field: quality, unit: "QLF_* of Rte_Qlf.h", qualifier: true }

A new driver uses the generic contract access: reading: the manifest names a header (include), a reading struct (reading) and a reader function (read); the module's family integration defines void ::integration::rte::<read>_<Instance>(<reading>& reading) once per instance (it takes a consistent snapshot itself), and the generated RTE calls it once per task and cycle that reads the instance. Three older access kinds (gate_driver, hall, input_capture) stay code of tools/rtegen; their manifest only states which fields are connectable. instances (default devices) picks the board devices of the module or the board input_capture entries the project uses. At most one value per module may be the qualifier (QLF_*). rte targets are inputs only: nothing switches a device on through them.

The board says which part sits where and which roles it fills there; the project says which of that is used:

# boards/evalboard_s32k144/board.yaml (excerpt, sketch)
devices:
  - name: SBC
    module: sbcUja113x
    part: UJA1131HW/FD/5V/4
    connect: { spi: LPSPI1, pcs: PTE1, int1: PTE12, int2: PTE3 }
    roles: { can_phy: [CAN0], power_supply: true, watchdog_trigger: true }
can:
  - { name: CAN0, controller: FlexCAN0, rx: PTC2, tx: PTC3, phy: SBC }
  - { name: CAN1, controller: FlexCAN2, rx: PTC16, tx: PTC17, phy: { part: SN65HVD1050, module: canPhyPassive } }

# projects/evalboard_motor/project.yaml (excerpt, sketch)
board: evalboard_s32k144
buses:
  - { name: VEH, can: CAN0, bitrate: 500000, dbc: EvalBoard.dbc, node: EVB }
diagnostics: { uds: { bus: VEH, request: 0x7E0, response: 0x7E8 } }
modules:
  SBC: { watchdog: autonomous, v2: on_normal_standby_reset }
tasks:
  - { name: app10ms, priority: 5, period_ms: 10, stack: 2048 }

From this the integration generator (intgen) produces main, platformLifecycleAdd, instances of the systems, the wiring of the roles, ISR binding and priorities as well as the task list. A board without an SBC declares a passive transceiver or one with an STB pin for its CAN connection; power_supply is then filled by an MCU-internal module (low-power modes) or stays empty; no service changes.

Principle: what is generated is wiring, not logic. Logic lives in modules with host tests.

docs.title: Generated binding of a device driver
docs.text:
How a device driver is bound to the system - pins and SPI device, system object, lifecycle registration, safe_off adapter, RTE reader - is generated from its manifest as well (analysis in treiber-anbindung-analyse.md). The manifest describes the wiring, a small trait next to the driver holds the few C++-specific lines, the family provides one binder per connection kind and contract, and tools/bswgen writes the block per instance (integration/moduleBinding.h, family neutral):

# libs/bsw/highSideSwitch/module.yaml (excerpt)
connect:
  in:  { kind: digital_output, safe_off: true }   # safe_off: switched off by the fault handlers, the halt deadman, S1
  den: { kind: digital_output }
  is:  { kind: analog_input }                      # converted with the board channel's characteristic (IO-21)
lifecycle: { level: 1, task: bsp }                 # read: the instance is registered in this level and task
console: instance                                  # component name = console group of the instance
binding:
  include: highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchBinding.h  # the trait, in the module's include directory
  trait: ::highside::HighSideSwitchBinding

Further manifest fields of the binding: connect.<x>.optional: true (the board may leave the connection open; the trait sees Connect::<X>_WIRED; never together with safe_off) and max_instances (checked at the project entry that brings in one instance too many). nxconfig checks every field with a YAML path: a binding needs a device driver with lifecycle in level 1 or 2 and a BSW task, only the contracts the family binders offer (spi_device), RTE access only through the generic reading contract, and the trait header must exist.

Part Where Content Trait libs/bsw/<module>/include/... (the module) System, config<I>()/valid() from the generated instance description I (Param::, Connect::, NAME, PART, COMPONENT, LABEL, PWM_BOUND), Parts<I, B> (pins on the binders B, SPI device), create(), one access struct SafeOff_<connection> per safe_off connection (off, enables, setLock, updateLock), rte() with access: reading, SPI device facts (SPI_FRAME_BITS, SPI_CPOL, SPI_CPHA, SPI_MAX_HZ, SPI_TIMEOUT_US). Contract: tools/bswgen/modules.py, section "binding" Family binders platforms/<family>/port/main/src/integration/ModuleBinders.h digital output/input, ADC channel with characteristic, SPI device on a board bus - one per connection kind and contract, never one per driver Framework .../integration/ModuleBinding.h one generic safe_off adapter SafeOffOutput<Access> for the debug halt guard and the hold of S1, the lock safeOffLock() (S1 latch, and for a PWM-bound instance the degraded group) Generat integration/moduleBinding.h, moduleBindingConfiguration.h, modules.cmake per instance the description, the static_assert on valid() with the YAML path, Parts, storage, the safe_off adapters, addComponents(manager, level); NX_BINDING_TARGETS, NX_BINDING_MODULE_DIRS

The family port includes the generat once (Integration.cpp), calls addComponents() in level 1 (right after bsp) and level 2 (after CAN), puts the generated safe_off adapters into the list of the debug halt guard and the safe state hold (checked against the safe outputs table, NX_SAFE_OFF_OUTPUT_COUNT) and links ${NX_BINDING_TARGETS}; the LPSPI master of the family is linked with the signal kind SPI (NX_USE_SPI), not with the SBC. A new driver with a binding therefore needs no line in the family port (proof: the synthetic fourth driver of tools/bswgen/test/binding).

State (2026-09-30): highSideSwitch is bound this way (lockstep comparison with its former hand-written adapter in test/host/SafeOffEquivalenceHostTest.cpp). Still written by hand in the family port: sbcUja113x (roles can_phy, power_supply, early_init) and gdTmc6200 (a per-instance lock and "keep enable" in an active short; the PWM group as duty source; RTE values with the supervisor's bus verdict). The add_subdirectory of the module directories from NX_BINDING_MODULE_DIRS belongs into the root CMakeLists.txt (today a fixed list there).

docs.title: 6. Platforms and families
docs.text:
Family Foundation neXtBSW addition State s32k1xx OpenBSW platforms/s32k1xx LPSPI, ADC contract, complementary PWM, input capture, FlexIO I2C, derivatives 142/144/146/148 in progress (eval board) stm32 OpenBSW platforms/stm32 (F4 bxCAN, G4 FDCAN) missing contracts (ADC, SPI, PWM, watchdog), further derivatives after a later change s32k3xx no OpenBSW platform yet own platforms/s32k3xx (Cortex-M7), driver source open after a later change rm4x no OpenBSW platform own, OpenBSW-conformant platform platforms/rm4x/{3rdparty,bsp,etlImpl,hardFaultHandler,safety,unitTest,CMakeLists.txt} (Cortex-R4F): startup in ARM state with mode stacks, VIM dispatch, RTI tick, DCAN, F021 flash from RAM; sources open until a follow-up task (D14) audit preparation family board
  • Own family extensions live in platforms/<family>/bsp/<module> in the OpenBSW layout; same-named OpenBSW modules are used, not duplicated. A family without an OpenBSW platform (rm4x) brings its complete platform in platforms/<family>. Binding for this is the platform rule at the end of this section.
  • Vendor libraries and sources (NXP RTD, STM32 HAL/LL, TI HALCoGen register headers, TI F021 flash API) only behind L1 contracts and only after a licence check (for rm4x, D14).
  • Toolchain: generic arm-none-eabi-gcc for all core profiles; core options (-mcpu, FPU) from the derivative database.
  • Startup, vector table or interrupt controller table, linker script (for Cortex-R with stacks per exception mode) and MPU regions are family templates, filled from derivative and project:
Core profile Controller Table Priority, RTOS boundary Jump from the bootloader Cortex-M NVIC vector table (word 0 stack pointer, then Thumb addresses), switchable via VTOR rank → NVIC level; boundary BASEPRI (ARMv6-M: global lock) VTOR to the application entry Cortex-R VIM eight instruction vectors at 0 (ARM state, no VTOR) + VIM channel table (handler per channel) rank → channel order (priority = channel number); boundary: IRQ may call the RTOS, FIQ never fixed forwarding table at the application entry (D12, section 7)

The rank remains a project term (section 4); the mapping onto the controller is derived by nxconfig and the family generator.

docs.title: Platform rule: OpenBSW layout per family (binding)
docs.text:
Decision of the maintainer of 2026-09-17 (decision log: F1/F3, RM46 option A) based on openbsw-naehe.md section 3. Yardstick: OpenBSW has no cross-family platform level – what several platforms need either lives neutrally in libs/ or is kept per platform.

P1 – Layout. Every family is an OpenBSW platform. platforms/<family> has the layout of external/openbsw/platforms/{s32k1xx,stm32}: bsp/<module>, 3rdparty/<rtos-port>, etlImpl, hardFaultHandler, safety, unitTest, CMakeLists.txt; integrated through the hook OPENBSW_PLATFORM.

P2 – Self-containment. platforms/<family> plus libs/ is sufficient. No platform module includes a module of another platform, and none depends on platforms/common. What OpenBSW places per platform (RTOS port, hardFaultHandler, startup, etlImpl, safety, bsp/*) stays per family – even if it then exists more than once.

P3 – platforms/common (the checkable rule). platforms/common contains only modules that have no counterpart in OpenBSW. Check per directory platforms/common/<module>, without discretion:

  1. Is there a module with the same purpose in external/openbsw/platforms/<family>/? → The module belongs per family in platforms/<family>/<module>, not in common.
  2. Is there a module with the same purpose in external/openbsw/libs/ (including libs/3rdparty/)? → It belongs neutrally in libs/bsp or libs/bsw, not in common.
  3. Neither, and the part is neXtBSW's own (bound to the generator or the core profile)? → platforms/common is right.
  4. Every deviation from 1–3 is an exception and is listed with reason and end condition in the list P4. Without an entry there it counts as an error.

P4 – Inventory of platforms/common (list from openbsw-naehe.md section 3, as of 2026-09-17):

Part under platforms/common OpenBSW counterpart Verdict according to P3 cmake/NxCoreArchitecture.cmake – architecture (NX_CORE_ARCHITECTURE) from nxconfig none (OpenBSW's CMake helpers live in the repository root cmake/) stays (C1); moving it to the root cmake/ would be closer to OpenBSW, but is not a must interruptPriority, cortex-m/interruptPriority, cortex-r/interruptPriority – ranks from the project mapped to NVIC levels or VIM channels none (OpenBSW writes the levels as numbers in main.cpp) stays (C4) test/ – build tests per core profile without a board (cortexm0plus, cortexr4f) platforms/<family>/unitTest has a different purpose (module tests of the platform) stays (C5) newlib stubs (_close/_lseek/_read/_write) under platforms/common/newlib none stays; moved there with a separate task (T14) clockCheck – start-up report of the clock check (nxClockCheckReport: one console line, text of the fault codes) none (the OpenBSW clock drivers report nothing; the check nxClockCheck() and its contract clock/nxClockCheck.h are family code and live per family in platforms/<family>/bsp/bspClock, the contract byte-identical in every family) stays (rule 3, placed with a separate task). Only the family-neutral formatting lives here; no family module depends on it (P2) – the integration (port/main, the stm32 build test) links both 3rdparty/freertosPort – selection of the port by architecture yes: OpenBSW selects in platforms/<family>/CMakeLists.txt exception (permanent): only the switch stays central, because it depends on the generated output. The ports themselves live per family: platforms/s32k1xx/3rdparty/freertos_cm0_sysTick, platforms/rm4x/3rdparty/freertos_crx 3rdparty/cmsis/core_cm0plus.h yes: external/openbsw/libs/3rdparty/cmsis (contains only core_cm4.h) exception (temporary): until the header is upstream (C2); after that the copy is dropped Hard fault handler (originally planned for common in a separate task) yes: platforms/<family>/hardFaultHandler (separate for s32k1xx and stm32 in OpenBSW) not into common: assembler handlers stay per family; only the architecture-neutral dump layout with architecture ID and the reader become neutral libs/bsw/faultDump (re-scoped)

P5 – Family port at application level. The hand-written port (so far platforms/<family>/port) lives at application level as in OpenBSW: ecu/platforms/<family> – modelled on referenceApp/platforms/<board>. platforms/<family> thus contains only the MCU level (F1; implementation, then a follow-up task; D7 in section 10 amended accordingly).

P6 – rm4x as proof (RM46 option A). rm4x is built in this layout from the start; the neXtBSW connection (generated output, configuration, RTE) stays separate from it:

platforms/rm4x/
  CMakeLists.txt         integration via OPENBSW_PLATFORM, derivative options from mcudb
  3rdparty/freertos_crx  FreeRTOS port ARM_CRx_No_GIC (PLAT-35) - here, not under platforms/common
  bsp/<module>           bspMcu, bspClock, bspVim, bspRti, bspGio, bspSci, bspDcan, bspF021 (PLAT-36-38)
  etlImpl/               ETL profile of the platform
  hardFaultHandler/      Data Abort, Prefetch Abort, Undefined (ARMv7-R); dump layout from libs/bsw/faultDump
  safety/                MPU, watchdog (DWD/DWWD) and ESM parts of the family
  unitTest/              platform module tests in the OpenBSW way

Additional acceptance criterion of the family: the OpenBSW referenceApp or its unitTest builds for RM46 . The build tests platforms/common/test/cortexr4f may include the port from platforms/rm4x/3rdparty; conversely, platforms/rm4x must not need anything from platforms/common/test.

docs.title: 7. Bootloader
docs.text:
• Stays lean in C without OpenBSW: core (bootloader/core: UDS, ISO-TP, image check) + HAL per family (bootloader/platforms/<family>: flash, CAN, clock, jump) + optional part hooks (bootloader/devices/<part>, e.g. switching on the SBC) + generated board/project part (CAN connection, pins, bit timing, IDs).
  • One source for the memory layout (derivative + project): bootloader linker, app linker, validity record, boot request address, updater and canflash read the same generated values.
  • Family-specific items such as the Flash Configuration Field (S32K1 at 0x400) belong in the family HAL, not in the core.
  • The interface to the application is the application entry, not a vector table. What stands there and how an image is checked for plausibility is decided by the family (hooks in bootloader, updater and canflash): Cortex-M sets VTOR; Cortex-R has no VTOR – the bootloader vectors forward Undefined, SVC, Prefetch Abort and Data Abort through a fixed forwarding table at the application entry (convention versioned like the record format), IRQ/FIQ go through the vector registers of the VIM and need no forwarding. The bootloader itself uses neither SVC nor aborts as long as the table is not in effect (D12, implementation).
  • Compatibility: identifier and record format with a version field; a bootloader already flashed remains updatable.

docs.title: 8. Repository layout (target)
docs.text:
external/openbsw/             unchanged (submodule)
platforms/<family>/           MCU level in the layout of an OpenBSW platform (platform rule P1/P2, section 6):
  bsp/<module>                L1 additions and MCU drivers of the family
  3rdparty/<rtos-port>        RTOS port of the family (freertos_cm0_sysTick, freertos_crx) - never under common
  hardFaultHandler/           fault/abort handlers per family; layout and reader neutral in libs/bsw/faultDump
  etlImpl/ safety/ unitTest/  as in external/openbsw/platforms/<family>, plus CMakeLists.txt (OPENBSW_PLATFORM)
platforms/common/             ONLY neXtBSW's own parts without an OpenBSW counterpart (platform rule P3/P4):
  cmake/                      profile-neutral: architecture from nxconfig (NX_CORE_ARCHITECTURE)
  3rdparty/freertosPort/      only the port selection by architecture (armv6m, armv7m, armv7r);
                              the ports themselves live under platforms/<family>/3rdparty
  test/                       build tests per core without a board (cortexm0plus, Cortex-R4F: PLAT-35)
  cortex-m/                   NVIC interrupt ranks; CMSIS core header as a temporary exception (PLAT-53)
  cortex-r/                   CP15 accesses, VIM channel ranks
libs/bsp/<class>/             L1 contracts (neutral) + contract tests
libs/bsw/<module>/            device drivers and services with module.yaml, host tests (including faultDump)
ecu/                          neutral ECU framework: application, systems, uds, consoleCommands
ecu/platforms/<family>/       port template of the family at the OpenBSW location (PLAT-54, modelled on
                              referenceApp/platforms/<board>): bspConfiguration, safety, main (startUp.S,
                              bootHeader.S, linker script, ISRs, StaticBsp, BspSystem),
                              freeRtosCoreConfiguration - no board value and no derivative value in it
ecu/platforms/<board>/        board port: Options.cmake + board peculiarities and justified exceptions
                              (no port points to another, ecu/platforms/README.md)
bootloader/                   core/, platforms/<family>/, devices/<part>/, updater/
mcudb/<family>/               derivative database (manufacturer facts)
boards/<board>/               board.yaml, documentation, board notes (e.g. safety rules for the board)
projects/<project>/           project.yaml, rte.yaml, DBC, project-specific SWCs
swc/<component>/              reusable components and examples (DemoSwc)
tools/                        nxconfig, bswgen, intgen, rtegen, dbcgen, blgen, canflash, studio, todo
doc/architecture/             this document, decisions

Build: cmake --preset <project> (presets generated from the projects, or generic with -DNX_PROJECT=projects/<p>); board, derivative and family follow from the project configuration. The Studio opens a project through its folder.

On ecu/platforms/ (D7 amended 2026-09-17, F1; previously "ecu/ without platforms/"): ecu/platforms/ stays and is the OpenBSW location for both port levels, like referenceApp/platforms/<board> in OpenBSW.

  • ecu/platforms/<family>/ is the port template of the family (today platforms/<family>/port; move in a separate task, startup templates after that in a separate task). It contains no board value and no derivative value.
  • ecu/platforms/<board>/ contains only the feature switches (Options.cmake, whose target location according to section 9 row 2 is the project) and justified board exceptions. This board folder disappears once the switches are in the project and the integration is generated; until then it is the only place with a board name in the code.
  • After the move, platforms/<family>/ contains only the MCU level – exactly like external/openbsw/platforms/*.
  • Module manifests are found in both port levels (tools/nxconfig/config.py, port_module_dirs).

The layout under platforms/ is thus no longer a neXtBSW invention, but checkably the OpenBSW layout: platform rule P1–P6 in section 6, review question 10 in section 11.
