docs.title: 10. Decisions for acceptance
docs.text:
# Question Proposal D1 Exchange of the MCU drivers static per family (like OpenBSW) + contract tests; virtual interfaces only from L2 upwards D2 Integration generated from module manifests and configuration (section 5) D3 Role model roles (can_phy, power_supply, watchdog_trigger, early_init, …) as the coupling between services and parts D4 Configuration three levels in YAML (ruamel.yaml), schema with pydantic, shared loader tools/nxconfig D5 Derivative database own mcudb from open sources (Zephyr hal_nxp/hal_stm32, CMSIS-SVD), only the fields needed D6 Bootloader C without OpenBSW, HAL per family, same configuration source D7 Repository layout section 8 (including projects/, mcudb/); amended 2026-09-17: ecu/platforms/ stays and carries both port levels – ecu/platforms/<family> (family template, OpenBSW location) and ecu/platforms/<board> (feature switches). The original version "ecu/ without platforms/" no longer applies D8 Language level C++17 as today (GCC 11, OpenBSW-compatible); contracts via static_assert/contract test D9 OpenBSW submodule unchanged; offer neutral contracts (ADC, SPI, watchdog) upstream later D10 Order → → → → the eval board runs after every step (regression test on the board) D11 Core profiles (target picture section 1) ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-R, 32 bit, little endian; big endian (TMS570) explicitly not; the code distinguishes cores through the generated architecture, not through __ARM_ARCH D12 Bootloader ↔ application without VTOR (Cortex-R) bootloader vectors forward Undefined, SVC, Prefetch Abort and Data Abort through a fixed forwarding table at the application entry (convention versioned); IRQ/FIQ through the VIM vector registers (section 7) D13 Family name of the TI Cortex-R derivatives rm4x (TI Hercules RM4x, little endian) D14 Sources for rm4x: derivative headers, flash library, FreeRTOS port open until the licence and source review; candidates according to a separate task: HALCoGen register headers, TI F021 flash API (possibly as a workstation dependency), FreeRTOS GCC/ARM_CRx_No_GIC. None of these sources is used or checked in before the review result is released D15 Platform rule (section 6, P1–P6) Every family in the OpenBSW layout and self-contained; platforms/common only for parts without an OpenBSW counterpart, exceptions only with an entry in P4; family port at application level ecu/platforms/<family>; rm4x OpenBSW-conformant with the acceptance criterion "referenceApp/unitTest builds for RM46"

Acceptance: D1–D10 on 2026-09-15; D11–D13 as proposed and D14 (procedure only; which sources are used is decided after a later change) on 2026-09-17 (audit); D15 and the amendment of D7 on 2026-09-17 (F1/F3, RM46 option A). Implementation: move of the family port, startup in one place, hard fault handler per family, libs/bsw/faultDump, CRx port under platforms/rm4x, CMSIS header upstream. Until these are done the repository deviates from the rule at the places named in P4 and P5; the rule applies to every new placement from now on. The rejected alternatives are in the history of this file.

docs.title: 11. Review questions for reviews and contributor tasks
docs.text:
Every change to reusable code, generators or the bootloader must answer these questions with "yes, without a code change" or justify the exception:

  1. Does it work on a board without an SBC (different or passive CAN transceiver, MCU's own watchdog)?
  2. Does it work with a different crystal and a different system clock?
  3. Does it work with a different derivative of the same family (flash, RAM, instances, package) – and is the way to S32K3/STM32 and to Cortex-R (rm4x) not blocked?
  4. Does it work with two or more CAN buses and different IDs?
  5. Does it work with several tasks and freely chosen priorities?
  6. Is every new value in exactly one configuration level (section 4), and does the generator derive what is derived?
  7. Is there a host test with its own test profile, not just against the eval board?
  8. Does the core logic of the tools stay free of Qt (Studio requirement), and does validation deliver messages with a YAML path?
  9. For device drivers: is the granularity chosen according to treiber-granularitaet.md (generic behaviour or hardware-near per protocol), and are the project parameters in physical units of the function?
  10. For new files under platforms/: does the placement follow the platform rule (section 6) – does platform code live per family in the OpenBSW layout, can platforms/<family> be built with libs/ alone, and does platforms/common contain only parts that have no counterpart in OpenBSW (otherwise an entry in P4)?

docs.title: What the AUTOSAR R25-11 machine-readable models give neXtBSW
docs.text:
Status: 2026-10-01. Verification: mock/analysis (documents read on a workstation, nothing built, nothing flashed). User, 2026-09-23: "later, for the further development of neXtBSW, but no priority". R1 scope requirements basis and AUTOSAR proximity are a must, so this page records what the survey in autosar-standard-set.md could not: the result of actually opening the two models and a few specifications.

Rules of autosar-standard-set.md section 4 apply to every line below: nothing from the release is checked in, nothing is quoted; evidence is document name, release and (where useful) the module and parameter name. Parameter names and numeric limits are facts of an interface and are used as such. The prose descriptions in the files are not, and nothing here reproduces them.

docs.title: 1. Summary
docs.text: Question Answer Can tools/nxconfig or the Studio take over ECUC definitions (as schema, as generated models)? No. The definitions are module-by-module AUTOSAR configuration for AUTOSAR modules we do not have; the ranges are generic (mostly the full 32-bit range); they carry no derivative or board data and no cross-parameter rules. Taking them over would also drag AUTOSAR variant machinery in (decision D4 stays: YAML + pydantic). Is there anything to gain? Yes, three modest things: (a) a name and range cross-check for the parameters that have an AUTOSAR counterpart (diagnostics, NvM, CAN timing, watchdog supervision), (b) a vocabulary map so that an AUTOSAR-aware reader finds our parameter, (c) machine evidence for the claims of the survey page, which were made from the index only. Section 6 lists proposals. Does the survey page hold? Mostly. Four statements needed correction or a footnote (section 3); the main one: Fee, Ea and MemIf still exist in R25-11 and sit on MemAcc, so the memory stack is NvM -> Fee/Ea -> MemAcc -> Mem, not NvM -> MemAcc. E2E and CRC against R25-11 Nothing that touches our P01/P02/P11 implementation changed (section 4).

docs.title: 2. What was opened, and what is in it
docs.text:
Both archives come from the direct-link scheme of autosar-standard-set.md section 1, were unpacked outside the repository and are not checked in. SHA-256 of the downloads of 2026-10-01:

66a7cf67c2190c6ece9c1bba271c02f885d6757e4cfcc3d6ac7f9868db4ba12a  AUTOSAR_CP_MOD_ECUConfigurationParameters.zip
03ff29e16e6d46f7d4c3fc1962c0d347e15a50c3b19bacac54573e2fe738aed2  AUTOSAR_CP_MOD_BSWUMLModel.zip
Model Content Use for neXtBSW ECUConfigurationParameters (one 19 MB ARXML, definitions only) 112 modules, 1920 parameter containers; per parameter short name, type, multiplicity, minimum and maximum, rarely a default, enumeration literals, reference destination and configuration class. No units (only in the description text), no rule between two parameters, no value of a real device name and range cross-check (section 5), vocabulary; no schema takeover BSWUMLModel (84 MB Enterprise Architect repository, a SQLite file) about 2540 interfaces, 165 distinct modules, error classes, client-server operations none for tools/nxconfig or the Studio; at most a reference when a module is implemented (the SWS PDF says the same more readably)

Module sizes relevant to neXtBSW (containers): Dcm 192, Dem 66, Os 41, Rte 47, Com 30, SecOC 23, CanIf 19, WdgM 19, Can 17, Xcp 14, CanTSyn 13, StbM 12, Mcu 9, NvM 9, Wdg 8, CorTst 7, RamTst 7, FlsTst 6, Mem 5, MemAcc 4. The UML model has Mem, MemAcc, MemIf, Fee, Ea, NvM, E2E, SecOC, CanTSyn, Com, and no Fls, Eep, LdCom or hardware test manager.

docs.title: 3. Cross-check of the survey page (what R25-11 changed)
docs.text:
The survey said that no specification had been read. These are the claims of its section 3 and the brief of this task, checked against the ECUC file (and, for E2E/CRC, the PDFs).

Claim Result Fls and Eep removed Confirmed. Neither module exists in the parameter definitions or in the UML model. "Memory stack is now Mem/MemAcc" Needs a footnote. Fee, Ea and MemIf are still there. Fee and Ea reference a MemAcc address area, and the NvM block descriptor points at an Ea or Fee block (choice container). The stack is NvM -> Ea/Fee -> MemAcc -> Mem (MemIf selects between at most two devices). What disappeared are the driver-specific modules that sat below Fee/Ea. For a separate task the relevant shape is Mem's sector batch (erase sector size, write page size, sector count, start address, minimum read size, specified erase cycles, optional burst sizes) and MemAcc's address areas with retry counts and a priority. LdCom merged into Com Confirmed. No LdCom module; Com has a large-data switch on module level and per I-PDU. For a separate task: Com also carries per-signal timeout, first timeout, invalid-data and timeout actions (none, replace, substitute) and the filter algorithms (always, masked-new-differs, new-is-within and others). SecOC and CAN time sync "now in Foundation, no longer in CP" Wrong as worded. The protocol (PRS, RS) moved to Foundation, but SecOC (23 containers) and CanTSyn (13) are still CP modules with CP configuration, and the SWS documents are still in the CP list. What moved is where the wire protocol is specified. HWTestManager obsolete Confirmed, and machine-readable: the ECUC file tags module HTMSS obsolete. The standardised test modules that stay are CorTst (core: ALU, registers, cache, MPU, interrupt, address, memory interface), RamTst (March, Galpat, checkerboard and further algorithms, with block lists), FlsTst. For the safety argument the start-up tests are therefore still expressible with standardised names, only the manager that scheduled them is gone. Mcu, Wdg, Det still there Yes. WdgM (alive, deadline and logical supervision) is the relevant vocabulary for program-flow monitoring.

docs.title: 4. E2E and CRC against R25-11
docs.text: Checked by reading the change histories and the P01/P02 data types of AUTOSAR_FO_PRS_E2EProtocol, AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_E2ELibrary and AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_CRCLibrary (R25-11) against libs/bsw/e2e (basis R22-11). Nothing that touches P01, P02, P11 or the CRC routines in use changed: the state machine rework matters only if E2E_SMCheck is ever implemented (autosar.md section 2.2); profile 22 got a changed interface in R24-11 (not implemented; add it only with the R24-11/R25-11 interface); the P02 configuration type still has an Offset field, so the documented deviation of e2e.md is unchanged; the CRC check values are those of libs/bsw/e2e/test/host/E2eHostTest.c. Not checked: the profile-specific flow charts line by line.

docs.title: 5. Where the ECUC definitions and our configuration overlap
docs.text:
Only the areas where tools/nxconfig (model.py) describes something that AUTOSAR also configures. Read as "consistent" = same name idea and a compatible range; "ours is narrower" = deliberate or a candidate to document; "gap" = a parameter AUTOSAR has that we do not. None of this is a finding against the code: the ranges of an AUTOSAR parameter are generic limits, ours follow the implementation.

Area Ours (model.py) AUTOSAR (module / parameter) Observation Diagnostic session id DiagSession.id 0x01..0x7E Dcm DcmDspSessionLevel 1..126 consistent Session timing p2_ms, p2_star_ms, positive, no upper limit Dcm DcmDspSessionP2ServerMax 0..1 s, ...P2StarServerMax 0..100 s ours has no upper bound (warning, see autosar-ecuc-map.md section 2); an optional warning above 1 s / 100 s would match the standard module, but the wire format of the standard allows more, so not an error Security level DiagSecurityLevel.attempts 1..255, delay_ms, seed_bytes/key_bytes 1..255 Dcm DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay 1..255, ...DelayTime 0..65535 s, ...SeedSize/...KeySize >= 1; at most 31 rows (0..31) consistent; the row cap is a candidate check DTC counter debounce DtcCounterDebounce: failed 1..127, passed -128..-1, steps 1..255, jump values -128..127 Dem DemDebounceCounterBasedClass: failed 1..32767, passed -32768..-1, steps 1..32767, jump values 16-bit; plus DemDebounceBehavior (freeze or reset) and DemDebounceCounterStorage ours is narrower (8-bit counter, deliberate) and should say so; gap: freeze/reset behaviour while the enable condition is off, and storing the counter across power cycles DTC time debounce DtcTimeDebounce: failed_ms, passed_ms positive Dem DemDebounceTimeBasedClass: 0.001..3600 s ours has no upper bound; 3 600 000 ms would be the equivalent DTC attributes aging threshold 1..255, priority 1..255, confirmation_threshold 1..255, DTC number Dem DemAgingCycleCounterThreshold 1..255, DemDTCPriority 1..255, DemDtcValue 256..16 777 214 (3 byte) consistent; the DTC number range is taken from the ISO table in diagdesc.py and stays so Fault memory size DiagFaultMemory.max_entries 1..255, snapshot_records_max, extended_records_max Dem DemMaxNumberEventEntryPrimary 1..255, DemMaxNumberFreezeFrameRecords 0..255, storage trigger (confirmed, FDC threshold, test failed) consistent; gap: an explicit storage trigger CAN bit timing CanUse.bitrate in bit/s, sample_point_percent 50..95, optional sjw_tq, prop_seg_tq Can CanControllerBaudRate in kbit/s (0..2000; FD 0..16000), ...PropSeg 0..384, ...Seg1, ...Seg2, ...SyncJumpWidth 0..255 AUTOSAR configures segment lengths, we derive them from the sample point. The names sjw_tq/prop_seg_tq match. A tool that checks a project against the table of segment limits of a derivative is not covered by ECUC (the limits are in the derivative data) CAN bus off CanBusOff: first_pause_ms, max_pause_ms 0..65535, discard_after 0..255 CanSM CanSMBorTimeL1/...L2 0..65.535 s, CanSMBorCounterL1ToL2 0..255, CanSMEnableBusOffDelay the 16-bit millisecond range of ours is the same span as the standard's seconds with three decimals; the strategies differ (two levels with a counter versus growing pause) NvM block NvmBlockUse: type, length, integrity (qm / asil), write shutdown/change, min_interval_ms; block size at most 0x7FFF NvM NvMBlockDescriptor: block id 2..65535, length 1..65535, management type (native, redundant, dataset), CRC type (8, 16, 32), read retries 0..7, write retries 0..7, write verification, job priority, write-once, write protection ours is narrower by design (always two copies; CRC by integrity class); gaps worth a look for NVM-*: retry counts, write verification, write-once; AUTOSAR reserves block ids 0 and 1 Memory description MemoryRegion: start, size, sector_size or sectors, program_size Mem sector batch: start address, sector count, erase sector size, write page size, minimum read size, specified erase cycles, burst sizes consistent in structure; gap: erase endurance per flash region (we have it only for the emulated EEPROM, eeprom_emulation.endurance) Watchdog derivative LowPowerOscillator frequency range; project/BSW supervision in libs/bsw Wdg WdgInitialTimeout/WdgMaxTimeout 0..65.535 s, trigger mode toggle/window/both; WdgM alive supervision (expected indications, min/max margin, reference cycle), deadline and logical supervision vocabulary for the program-flow monitoring of the safety concept; no data to import E2E use E2eUse: profile, data id, max_delta_counter E2E has no ECUC module of its own in this file (E2E is configured through the transformer and the SWC description) nothing to cross-check

docs.title: 6. Proposals and their state
docs.text: # Proposal State A hand-kept vocabulary map "AUTOSAR: Module.Container.Parameter", marked "borrowed vocabulary, not conformance" (autosar.md section 0) done (autosar-ecuc-map.md) B local cross-check script tools/autosar_xcheck, not run in CI; reads the ECUC ARXML from a path in an environment variable done; first run: 29 mapped parameters, all found, none outside the AUTOSAR limits; correction to section 5: Dcm allows at most 31 security rows (0..31) C optional bounds of section 5 as warnings in tools/nxconfig/diagdesc.py done D take over the ECUC definitions as a generated schema or Studio form source rejected: licence (reproduction only unmodified and for information), no derivative or board data, drags in variant handling; contradicts D4 E ECUC value export from the YAML for customers with an AUTOSAR tool chain not proposed; goes against the standing "no ARXML configuration" line of README.md; recorded so the option is not lost

docs.title: 7. Hints for the open work areas
docs.text:
Taken from section 3 and 5; each is a pointer for the task named, not a requirement.

  • NVM-*: read Mem and MemAcc for the flash side and Ea/Fee for the block layer; the ECUC parameters of section 5 (retries, verification, write-once) are the checklist of what a block manager usually offers. The MemIf device count is at most two, which fits "emulated EEPROM + data flash" without a general device list.
  • COM-*: if a Com-like layer is ever added, follow the R25-11 shape (one module, large data as a switch, signal timeout and invalid-data actions), not the separate LdCom. The qualifier concept of signal-qualifier.md already covers timeout and validity at signal level; compare when that page is next touched.
  • SYS-*/safety: name start-up tests with CorTst, RamTst and FlsTst vocabulary where it fits; do not plan against a hardware test manager. WdgM vocabulary for alive/deadline/logical supervision.
  • Security (SecOC) and time sync: when taken up, read the Foundation PRS for the protocol and the CP SWS for the module; both exist.
  • E2E: see section 4; add P22 only with the R24-11/R25-11 interface.

docs.title: 8. How to repeat the analysis
docs.text: The name and range comparison of section 5 is repeatable with tools/autosar_xcheck (see autosar-ecuc-map.md section 3). The counts of section 2 come from a plain walk of the ARXML tree (xml.etree), the .qea as a SQLite file (t_object, t_package, stereotype module) and pypdf text extraction for the change histories. Not covered: the other CP archives and the template specifications (the ECUConfiguration TPS would be the place if proposal E is ever reopened), the Foundation and Adaptive sets, and every adoption still needs the check against the document itself (autosar-standard-set.md).

docs.title: neXtBSW parameters and their AUTOSAR ECUC counterparts
docs.text:
Status: 2026-10-02 (proposals A to C of autosar-ecuc-evaluation.md section 6). Verification: mock/analysis (cross-check run on a workstation against the R25-11 file, tests on a synthetic excerpt; nothing built, nothing flashed).

Borrowed vocabulary, not conformance (autosar.md section 0). The table says: "if you know the AUTOSAR parameter on the right, this is the neXtBSW parameter on the left". It does not say that a neXtBSW configuration is an AUTOSAR configuration, and it reproduces no AUTOSAR text: only module, container and parameter names (facts of an interface) and numeric limits.

The machine-readable source of this page is tools/autosar_xcheck/map.yaml. A host test checks that every entry of the map appears here and that every model field it names exists; the script tools/autosar_xcheck checks the AUTOSAR side (section 3).

docs.title: 1. The map
docs.text: Result column: the last run against the R25-11 definitions (SHA-256 of the archive in autosar-ecuc-evaluation.md section 2). = same limits, narrower ours lies inside the AUTOSAR limits (deliberate or implementation-driven), no upper bound ours has none where AUTOSAR has one, known an accepted difference.

docs.title: Diagnostics (Dcm)
docs.text:
neXtBSW (YAML path) AUTOSAR Module.Parameter Unit Result diag.yaml sessions[].id Dcm.DcmDspSessionLevel - = (1..126) diag.yaml sessions[].p2_ms Dcm.DcmDspSessionP2ServerMax ms / s no upper bound (AUTOSAR 1 s); warning above 1000 ms diag.yaml sessions[].p2_star_ms Dcm.DcmDspSessionP2StarServerMax ms / s no upper bound (AUTOSAR 100 s); warning above 100 000 ms diag.yaml security[].level Dcm.DcmDspSecurityLevel - = (sub-function 0x01..0x7D is level 1..63) diag.yaml security[].attempts Dcm.DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay - = (1..255) diag.yaml security[].delay_ms Dcm.DcmDspSecurityDelayTime ms / s no upper bound (AUTOSAR 65 535 s) diag.yaml security[].seed_bytes Dcm.DcmDspSecuritySeedSize bytes narrower (1..255) diag.yaml security[].key_bytes Dcm.DcmDspSecurityKeySize bytes narrower (1..255)

The Dcm definition holds at most 31 session rows and 31 security rows (multiplicity 0..31); more is a warning in diag.yaml. (The first version of the evaluation page said 32 for the security rows; the multiplicity is 0..31.)

docs.title: Fault memory (Dem)
docs.text:
neXtBSW (YAML path) AUTOSAR Module.Parameter Unit Result diag.yaml dtcs[].debounce.counter.failed_threshold Dem.DemDebounceCounterFailedThreshold counts narrower (1..127, 8-bit counter) diag.yaml dtcs[].debounce.counter.passed_threshold Dem.DemDebounceCounterPassedThreshold counts narrower (-128..-1) diag.yaml dtcs[].debounce.counter.increment Dem.DemDebounceCounterIncrementStepSize counts narrower (1..255) diag.yaml dtcs[].debounce.counter.decrement Dem.DemDebounceCounterDecrementStepSize counts narrower (1..255) diag.yaml dtcs[].debounce.counter.jump_up Dem.DemDebounceCounterJumpUpValue counts narrower (-128..127) diag.yaml dtcs[].debounce.counter.jump_down Dem.DemDebounceCounterJumpDownValue counts narrower (-128..127) diag.yaml dtcs[].debounce.time.failed_ms Dem.DemDebounceTimeFailedThreshold ms / s no upper bound (AUTOSAR 3600 s); warning above 3 600 000 ms diag.yaml dtcs[].debounce.time.passed_ms Dem.DemDebounceTimePassedThreshold ms / s no upper bound (AUTOSAR 3600 s); warning above 3 600 000 ms diag.yaml dtcs[].aging.threshold_cycles Dem.DemAgingCycleCounterThreshold cycles = (1..255) diag.yaml dtcs[].priority Dem.DemDTCPriority - = (1..255) diag.yaml dtcs[].confirmation_threshold Dem.DemEventConfirmationThreshold cycles = (1..255) diag.yaml dtcs[].number Dem.DemDtcValue - known: the schema allows 0..0xFFFFFF, diagdesc.py checks against the ISO DTC table diag.yaml fault_memory.max_entries Dem.DemMaxNumberEventEntryPrimary entries = (1..255) diag.yaml fault_memory.snapshot_records_max Dem.DemMaxNumberFreezeFrameRecords records narrower (0..254)

Gaps (AUTOSAR parameter exists, neXtBSW has none): debounce behaviour while the enable condition is off (DemDebounceBehavior), storing the debounce counter across power cycles (DemDebounceCounterStorage), an explicit storage trigger (DemEventMemoryEntryStorageTrigger).

docs.title: CAN (Can, CanSM)
docs.text:
neXtBSW (YAML path) AUTOSAR Module.Parameter Unit Result project.yaml can.<Bus>.bitrate Can.CanControllerBaudRate bit/s / kbit/s no upper bound (AUTOSAR 2000 kbit/s nominal); the real limit is in the derivative data project.yaml can.<Bus>.sjw_tq Can.CanControllerSyncJumpWidth time quanta no upper bound (AUTOSAR 255) project.yaml can.<Bus>.prop_seg_tq Can.CanControllerPropSeg time quanta no upper bound (AUTOSAR 384) project.yaml can.<Bus>.bus_off.first_pause_ms CanSM.CanSMBorTimeL1 ms / s = (0..65.535 s) project.yaml can.<Bus>.bus_off.max_pause_ms CanSM.CanSMBorTimeL2 ms / s = (0..65.535 s); strategy differs (growing pause versus two levels) project.yaml can.<Bus>.bus_off.discard_after CanSM.CanSMBorCounterL1ToL2 - = (0..255)

AUTOSAR configures the segment lengths; neXtBSW derives them from the sample point (tools/nxconfig/clock.py).

docs.title: Non-volatile memory (NvM)
docs.text:
neXtBSW (YAML path) AUTOSAR Module.Parameter Unit Result project.yaml nvm.blocks.<Block>.length NvM.NvMNvBlockLength elements / bytes narrower (ours counts elements, the block is limited to 0x7FFF bytes)

Gaps worth a look for the NvM tasks: read and write retries (NvMMaxNumOfReadRetries, NvMMaxNumOfWriteRetries, 0..7), write verification (NvMWriteVerification), write protection (NvMBlockWriteProt), erase endurance per flash region (Mem.MemSpecifiedEraseCycles).

docs.title: 2. Warnings in diag.yaml (proposal C)
docs.text:
tools/nxconfig/diagdesc.py reports, as warnings (never errors, so no existing project breaks), a value above what the AUTOSAR definition accepts: p2_ms > 1000, p2_star_ms > 100 000, time debouncing > 3 600 000 ms, more than 31 sessions or security levels. The wire format of ISO 14229 allows more, so a project above the limit is valid; it is merely not portable to a standard module. The constants sit at the top of diagdesc.py and name the AUTOSAR parameter they come from.

Tests: AutosarUpperLimits and test_time_debouncing_above_one_hour_is_a_warning in tools/nxconfig/test_diagdesc.py.

docs.title: 3. Repeating the cross-check (proposal B)
docs.text:
set NXCONFIG_AUTOSAR_ECUC_ZIP=<download folder>\AUTOSAR_CP_MOD_ECUConfigurationParameters.zip
cd tools
..\.venv\Scripts\python -m autosar_xcheck

The ZIP is read in place (nothing is unpacked or copied). The script prints one line per map entry ([OK], [NARROWER], [UNBOUNDED], [KNOWN], [OUTSIDE], [MISSING]) with names and numbers, never description text, and the SHA-256 of the archive. Exit code 1 means a parameter was renamed or removed in the release (MISSING) or one of our limits left the AUTOSAR limit (OUTSIDE); 2 means no or an unreadable file. Our limits are read from the pydantic model of tools/nxconfig, so they exist in one place. It is not part of CI (the file is not in the repository); the host test tools/autosar_xcheck/test_xcheck.py uses a small synthetic excerpt.

When a new release comes out: download the archive, run the script, fix the map or the model for every MISSING and OUTSIDE, record the release and the SHA-256 in autosar-ecuc-evaluation.md.

docs.title: The AUTOSAR Classic Platform document set: a map, not a reading
docs.text:
Status: 2026-09-23. Survey only. The index was walked and counted; no specification was read for this page beyond the release overview, and nothing here has been checked against the repository. Verification: mock/analysis.

Update 2026-10-01 (second part): the ECUC parameter definitions, the BSW UML model and the E2E/CRC change histories were opened and the statements of section 3 checked against them; the result, with two corrections, is in autosar-ecuc-evaluation.md. Where a statement below was corrected, a note says so. Everything else on this page is still survey level.

Companion page: autosar.md says which parts of neXtBSW follow a published specification and which only borrow the vocabulary. This page says where those specifications are, what else is in the set, and which parts of the current release would touch neXtBSW if we ever go further.

docs.title: 1. Where the documents are
docs.text:
The entry point is https://www.autosar.org/standards/classic-platform. That page carries no direct links to PDFs. It offers two filters into the site's document search:

  • By release — 16 entries, from R25-11 (current) back to Release 2.0. R3.x and older return nothing; the page says so itself.
  • By architecture element — the clickable layer diagram, 19 filters (Application Interfaces, Run Time Environment, System/Memory/Crypto/Communication/Off-board Communication Services, the five hardware-abstraction blocks, the five driver blocks, Microcontroller Abstraction Layer). A few of those links still filter on R24-11, among them "Crypto Services" and "Microcontroller Abstraction Layer" — check the release filter after clicking.

Every file is reachable directly, without the search:

https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/<release>/CP/AUTOSAR_CP_<TYPE>_<Name>.pdf

for example …/standards/R25-11/CP/AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_CRCLibrary.pdf. Foundation and Adaptive use FO and AP in place of CP.

docs.title: 2. What the set contains (R25-11, Classic Platform)
docs.text:
218 items: 212 PDFs, 5 ZIPs, 1 hash file.

Type Count What it is SWS 127 Software Specification — the module behaviour, API and configuration RS 45 Requirements on a module or area, the layer above SWS EXP 21 Explanation — rationale and guidance, e.g. LayeredSoftwareArchitecture TR 11 Technical Report — methodology, VFB, release overview TPS 7 Template Specification — SystemTemplate, ECUConfiguration, SWC template, … ASWS 1 TransformerGeneral

The specifications are grouped into 19 clusters: ReleaseDocumentation, ApplicationInterfaces, BSWGeneral, Communication, Crypto, Diagnostics, General, GlobalTime, IO, Libraries, MCAL, Memory, MethodologyAndTemplates, ModeManagement, RTE, SWArch, Safety, Security, SystemServices.

The non-PDF files are the interesting part for a configurator:

File Why it matters here AUTOSAR_CP_MOD_ECUConfigurationParameters.zip the complete ECUC parameter definitions, machine-readable — the closest thing to a reference schema for what tools/nxconfig does with its own YAML AUTOSAR_CP_MOD_BSWUMLModel.zip the BSW UML model: modules, interfaces, types AUTOSAR_CP_MOD_AISpecification.zip, …Examples.zip standardised application interfaces (port and data type blueprints) AUTOSAR_CP_EXP_ModelingShowCases.zip worked modelling examples AUTOSAR_CP_TR_SpecificationHashes.sha256 checksums for the whole release

Other releases, for scale: CP had 234 documents in R24-11, 229 in R23-11, 226 in R22-11, 219 in R21-11, 217 in R20-11, 231 in R19-11, 232 in R4.4.0. R25-11 also ships 64 Foundation and 63 Adaptive documents; Foundation is a separate page and increasingly holds the protocol specifications (PRS) that the CP documents refer to.

docs.title: 3. What R25-11 changed that would touch us
docs.text:
R25-11 (published 2025-11-27, a minor release, supersedes R24-11) is mostly a clean-up, and the clean-up hits exactly the areas neXtBSW has open work in:

  • The Flash and EEPROM drivers are gone. CP SWS FlashDriver (Fls) and CP SWS EEPROMDriver (Eep) are removed — not deprecated, not released any more. The Memory cluster is now MemoryDriver (Mem), MemoryAccess (MemAcc), MemoryAbstractionInterface, NVRAMManager, MemoryMapping, FlashTest, RAMTest, FlashEEPROMEmulation, EEPROMAbstraction. Anyone reading AUTOSAR for guidance on our storage stack should read Mem/MemAcc, not the Fls/Eep material that most textbooks still describe. Footnote 2026-10-01: the ECUC definitions still contain Fee, Ea and MemIf, and NvM still points at an Ea or Fee block; those two sit on MemAcc. The stack is NvM, Fee/Ea, MemAcc, Mem; only the driver-specific modules below Fee/Ea are gone.
  • LdCom disappears into Com. The COMHandler concept merges large-data COM into Com and adds communication error abstraction and monitoring (data integrity, reception deadline monitoring, data invalidity, range check). CP SWS LargeDataCOM is removed.
  • Secure onboard communication moved to Foundation (FO RS SecureOnboardCommunication), as did the CAN time sync protocol, split into FO PRS TimeSyncOverCANProtocol (protocol) and CP SWS TimeSyncOverCAN (AUTOSAR realisation). Correction 2026-10-01: only the protocol and requirements moved. SecOC and CanTSyn are still Classic Platform modules with their own CP SWS and CP configuration parameters. The same split already applies to E2E, which is why libs/bsw/e2e cites a PRS and an SWS.
  • Removed or obsolete, so not worth planning against: TTCAN driver and interface (removed), the whole V2X branch including Chinese V2X and Wireless Ethernet (obsolete), HWTestManager with its RS and integration guide (obsolete) — the last one is worth knowing because start-up/shutdown hardware tests are a plausible thing to want in a safety context, and AUTOSAR has just stopped standardising it.
  • New: Vehicle Data Protocol (VDPCMRemote, in-vehicle data collection with sampling decoupled from transmission), DDS on the Classic Platform (events/methods/fields over DDS with QoS, new DDS Transformer), reworked MACsec support.
  • The release overview also names known technical deficiencies in individual specifications (LSduRouter, BusMirroring, TimeSyncOverCAN/FlexRay, TransformerGeneral, the SAE J1939 modules, BSWDistributionGuide). Read that chapter before trusting one of those documents.

One cross-check worth recording: the current index contains no FlashDriver and no EEPROMDriver, which confirms the removal from the outside, and it still serves the V2X and HWTestManager PDFs, which confirms that obsolete still means downloadable.

Our own E2E implementation is based on R22-11 documents (libs/bsw/e2e/doc/e2e.md). Checked 2026-10-01 against the R25-11 change histories: nothing relevant for P01, P02, P11 and the CRC routines in use (details in autosar-ecuc-evaluation.md section 4).

docs.title: 4. How to handle these documents here
docs.text:
The specifications are free to download and are copyrighted; the site's terms of use allow reproduction for information only. Treat them like the licensed standards in doc/confidential/:

  • Do not commit AUTOSAR PDFs or ZIPs to this repository, and do not paste specification text into code, comments or documentation.
  • Cite by document name, release and section — AUTOSAR_CP_SWS_CRCLibrary R22-11, section 7.2 — the way libs/bsw/e2e already does.
  • Published check values, API names and numeric constants that we implement are fine to use; that is what the specification is for.

docs.title: neXtBSW and AUTOSAR: what is actually here
docs.text: Status: 2026-09-17, every row below checked against the repository at this commit. Mode management added 2026-09-19, implicit access 2026-09-19.

docs.title: 0. Read this first
docs.text:
AUTOSAR is a registered trademark of the AUTOSAR development partnership and neXtBSW has nothing to do with that partnership. neXtBSW is not AUTOSAR compliant, not AUTOSAR certified, and no conformance has been tested or claimed. It is a hobby basic software that borrows from AUTOSAR where the standard is useful and departs from it where it is not — and this page exists so that a reader who knows AUTOSAR can tell in a few minutes which is which.

The project calls itself "AUTOSAR-like" (README.md). That phrase is meant literally and narrowly: some parts implement a published AUTOSAR specification, some parts use AUTOSAR vocabulary over an implementation of our own, and large parts of AUTOSAR are simply not there. The three columns below say which.

Binding target picture: README.md. Overview of the architecture: overview.md. Where the specifications themselves live, what the document set contains and what the current release R25-11 changed: autosar-standard-set.md. What the machine-readable parameter definitions of R25-11 give the configuration tools (and what they do not): autosar-ecuc-evaluation.md.

docs.title: 1. The short answer
docs.text: Area Follows a published specification Borrows terms and concepts only Deliberately different, or absent Base types Std_Types.h, Platform_Types.h, Compiler.h — names and values as specified, minimal subset — no version-info types, no development-error interface, memory classes are empty macros E2E protection libs/bsw/e2e: profiles P01, P02, P11 and the CRC routines, behaviour per PRS/SWS R22-11 — E2E_SMCheck state machine and the Forward functions not implemented; API types are uint8_t instead of the specified enums; P02 Offset field missing Software components ARXML from Embedded Coder in the r4.0 schema; an application SW component with sender-receiver ports, runnables and timing events; required mode ports with mode switch events; explicit and implicit data access points — no client-server, no multiple instantiation (proposal: a design note (not published, available on request)); modes only from the one ECU mode manager RTE generated Rte_Read_* / Rte_Write_* with Std_ReturnType; Rte_IRead_* / Rte_IWrite_* / Rte_IWriteRef_* with a copy per runnable; Rte_Mode_* with RTE_MODE_*/RTE_TRANSITION_* "RTE", "runnable", "port", "task mapping" generated from an own YAML ECU description, not from a system description or ECU extract; data consistency solved with its own copy-at-task-boundary scheme; mode switches seen per task at its cycle start, not queued Diagnostics ISO 14229 (UDS) over ISO 15765-2 (ISO-TP), both in the bootloader and in the application — no Dcm, no diagnostic extract, no Dem, no DTC memory BSW layering — "BSW", "CDD", "ECU state", "lifecycle levels", layer numbering no AUTOSAR BSW module exists by name; no CanIf, PduR, Com, Dcm, Dem, NvM, EcuM, BswM MCU drivers — — not MCAL: the drivers are OpenBSW's and neXtBSW's own C++ interfaces, and the union-of-all-parameters driver style is rejected on purpose Operating system — tasks, priorities, periods FreeRTOS, not AUTOSAR OS or OSEK Configuration method — "derivative / board / project levels" is our own vocabulary no AUTOSAR methodology: no ECU configuration ARXML, no BSWMD, no EcuC, no system description Conformance — — none. No conformance test suite has been run, and no certification exists or is sought

docs.title: 2. Area by area, with the evidence
2.1 Base types — specification followed, subset
docs.text:
libs/bsw/autosarBase is an interface library with three headers and no source files:

  • Platform_Types.h — boolean, sint8…uint64, *_least variants, float32/float64, VoidPtr, plus CPU_TYPE = CPU_TYPE_32, CPU_BIT_ORDER = LSB_FIRST, CPU_BYTE_ORDER = LOW_BYTE_FIRST. Names, values and meanings are those of AUTOSAR_SWS_PlatformTypes. Since an earlier change the integer types are typedefs of the <stdint.h> types (uint32 is uint32_t, so pointers to both are interchangeable in C and C++); boolean stays uint8_t and is not C99 bool.
  • Std_Types.h — Std_ReturnType, E_OK/E_NOT_OK, STD_HIGH/STD_LOW, STD_ACTIVE/STD_IDLE, STD_ON/STD_OFF. Its own header comment calls it a "minimal subset", and it is: there is no Std_VersionInfoType, no transformer error type and no development-error hooks.
  • Compiler.h — the FUNC, P2VAR, P2CONST, CONST, VAR family for GCC and Clang. Memory classes are ignored by design ("a flat memory model without near/far pointers"), so every macro drops its memclass argument.

Used by the generated RTE and the component code (ecu/rte/CMakeLists.txt links autosarBase into swcComponents and rte); nothing else in the repository uses these types. Note one inconsistency to be aware of: the Platform_Types.h comment says "for 32-bit ARM Cortex-M", while the target picture also covers Cortex-R (README.md section 1, D11). The definitions themselves are correct for both, but the comment is narrower than the intent.

docs.title: 2.2 E2E — specification followed, with documented deviations
docs.text:
libs/bsw/e2e implements profiles P01, P02 and P11 in C99, with the CRC routines (E2E_Crc8 SAE J1850, E2E_Crc8H2F) taken from AUTOSAR_SWS_CRCLibrary R22-11 including their published check values. The header states the basis explicitly: AUTOSAR_PRS_E2EProtocol and AUTOSAR_SWS_E2ELibrary R22-11. Function names (E2E_PxxProtect, E2E_PxxCheck, E2E_PxxMapStatusToSM), the status codes (E2E_P01STATUS_OKSOMELOST, E2E_P_WRONGSEQUENCE, …) and their numeric values are those of the specification; configuration fields use AUTOSAR bit offsets.

Deliberate deviations, all listed in libs/bsw/e2e/doc/e2e.md:

AUTOSAR Here Why Std_ReturnType, enum types uint8_t typedefs with the same values no dependency on Std_Types.h; layout independent of -fshort-enums P01/P02: State->NewDataAvailable, no length explicit length parameter; data == NULL && length == 0 means "no new frame" same shape as P11, and the length is checked for P01/P02 too P02 configuration field Offset absent, header fixed in bytes 0/1 the P02 flow charts never evaluate it Forward functions not implemented not needed for the RTE's CAN frames E2E_SMCheck state machine not implemented the RTE debounces over time instead (doc/architecture/signal-qualifier.md)

The library is real, not decorative: tools/rtegen derives the configuration from DBC signals (E2E_PROFILES, E2E_SYNC_COUNTER_INIT = 1), and ecu/rte/CMakeLists.txt links e2e into the RTE when a project configures can.qualifiers.<message>.e2e. Verification is host-only: 1367 checks in the C host test, a Python reference model over the specification's own examples, a randomised C-versus-Python comparison, and 33 injected mutations all detected (libs/bsw/e2e/doc/e2e.md). One line in that document is stale — it still says the library is "not yet used in the RTE", which was true on 2026-09-15 and is no longer true.

docs.title: 2.3 Software components and RTE — AUTOSAR shape, own generator
docs.text:
The application model is genuinely AUTOSAR Classic in shape. A component is a Simulink model configured with the AUTOSAR Blockset; Embedded Coder emits C and ARXML (swc/<Swc>/generated/{src,arxml}, checked in). The ARXML sits in the http://autosar.org/schema/r4.0 namespace against AUTOSAR_00051.xsd and contains APPLICATION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE, SENDER-RECEIVER-INTERFACE, RUNNABLE-ENTITY, TIMING-EVENT, DATA-RECEIVE-POINT-BY-ARGUMENTS and DATA-SEND-POINTS. The generated component code calls Rte_Read_<Port>_<Element>(&value) and Rte_Write_<Port>_<Element>(value) returning Std_ReturnType — the AUTOSAR API for explicit sender-receiver access (swc/DemoSwc/generated/src/DemoSwc.c).

tools/rtegen reads exactly that subset of the ARXML and generates Rte_Type.h, Rte_<Swc>.h, Rte.c, RteConfig.h/.cpp, RteTasks.h and the task configuration. What the generated RTE offers is Rte_Read/Rte_Write, since an earlier change Rte_Mode, and since an earlier change Rte_IRead/Rte_IWrite/Rte_IWriteRef — grepping the templates for the RTE API surface yields nothing else. There is no Rte_Call, no Rte_Send/Rte_Receive, no Rte_DRead, no Rte_IStatus/Rte_IInvalidate, no Rte_IrvRead/Rte_IrvWrite, no Rte_Switch, no Rte_Pim, no exclusive areas.

Explicitly unsupported (swc/README.md): client-server ports and multiple instantiation (a design for the latter: a design note (not published, available on request)). Arrays, records and calibration parameters have been supported since earlier changes. Mode management exists only in the form described below.

docs.title: Implicit access
docs.text:
Topic As in AUTOSAR Here, and different Component side VARIABLE-ACCESS in DATA-READ-ACCESSS / DATA-WRITE-ACCESSS of the RUNNABLE-ENTITY (Embedded Coder: ImplicitReceive, ImplicitSend, ImplicitSendByRef), read from the component's ARXML; no setting in rte.yaml — API Rte_IRead_<re>_<p>_<o>() returning the value (records and arrays: const pointer), Rte_IWrite_<re>_<p>_<o>(data), Rte_IWriteRef_<re>_<p>_<o>() returning a pointer into the buffer; the component header maps them to Rte_I*_<c>_<re>_<p>_<o> no Rte_IStatus, no Rte_IInvalidate; a read access point on a provided port or a write access point on a required port is rejected Semantics values read stay stable during the whole execution of the runnable; values written are made available only after it terminates the same, realised with one copy per runnable and data element (Rte_Imp_<c>_<re>_<p>_<o>): a wrapper loads every copy before the runnable and publishes the written ones after it. AUTOSAR allows an RTE to share such buffers between runnables of a task; this RTE does not, so the RAM cost is per runnable (listed by tools/schedana) Initial content of a write buffer — the current value of the element, so a runnable that does not write, or writes only part of a record through Rte_IWriteRef, publishes what it found. Runnables of several tasks writing one element implicitly can therefore overwrite a newer value with an older one; rtegen warns Consistency across tasks RTE decides the copies build on the scheme: loaded from the task copy or single-task buffer without a lock, or from the published value of a port used in several tasks under one lock per side of the runnable; the runnable itself never runs under the lock

A component without implicit access points gets byte-identical generated code (checked for every project and every test profile of tools/rtegen).

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
The ECU states of libs/bsw/ecuState are offered as the modes of one mode manager, ecu.mode. What follows the AUTOSAR Classic RTE (SWS RTE, R4.x) and what does not:

Topic As in AUTOSAR Here, and different Component side required port with a MODE-SWITCH-INTERFACE and one MODE-GROUP; MODE-DECLARATION-GROUP with ALPHABETIC_ORDER (default) or EXPLICIT_ORDER, VALUE, ON-TRANSITION-VALUE; MODE-ACCESS-POINTs; SWC-MODE-SWITCH-EVENT with ON-ENTRY, ON-EXIT, ON-TRANSITION — all read from the component's ARXML — API Rte_Mode_<p>_<o>() returning Rte_ModeType_<Group>; RTE_MODE_<Group>_<Mode> and RTE_TRANSITION_<Group> in Rte_Type.h (with #ifndef guards, so an Embedded Coder header may define them first) only the simple form; no enhanced Rte_Mode with previous/next mode, no Rte_Switch, no Rte_SwitchAck Mode manager — one fixed manager, ecu.mode, fed by the ECU state machine. A component cannot be a mode manager (provided mode ports are rejected), and there is no BswM/EcuM mode arbitration Mode group compatibility the groups of manager and user must match the port's group has to name exactly the six ECU states (case ignored); its own values are what Rte_Mode returns, the RTE maps the state number to them Execution of a switch on-exit, then on-transition, then on-entry executables; RTE_TRANSITION_ during the transition; on-entry of the initial mode at start the same order and value, but per task: each task that runs mode switch runnables or reads a mode port in one task keeps its own view of the mode and processes a change at the start of its next cycle, before its periodic runnables. A mode port read in several tasks reads the mode manager directly (like the hand-over of a data port used in several tasks) Mode switch queue a queue of configurable length, every switch processed no queue: the manager publishes only its current state, so a mode shorter than a task's cycle can pass unseen by that task Mode disabling DISABLED-MODE-IREFS on RTE events rejected; a runnable reads the mode with Rte_Mode instead Event to task mapping ECU configuration (RteEventToTaskMapping) the mode switch runnable is listed in rte.yaml tasks[].runnables, like a periodic runnable; a runnable with a mode switch event and a timing or init event is rejected Mode switch runnables and the tools — they are not rows of rte::RUNNABLES but of their own table rte::MODE_RUNNABLES: rte runnables and rte json show one line per event with calls and run time, and tools/schedana adds the worst mode switch per task to the response time

The sender-receiver target ecu.state (the state as a number) is unchanged; an RTE without mode ports is byte-identical to the one before a later change.

Two things are deliberately not AUTOSAR:

  • Where the integration comes from. AUTOSAR would describe the composition, the connections and the task mapping in ARXML (system description, ECU extract, ECU configuration). neXtBSW describes them in its own YAML, projects/<p>/rte.yaml, and connects component ports to board signals by name — dio.in.BUTTON1, adc.phys.MOTOR_NTC, can.qlf.PC_Command, ecu.state. The generator validates direction, data type, existence in the board profile and use by the project, with messages carrying the YAML path.
  • How data consistency is achieved. Instead of IRVs and exclusive areas, rtegen decides per buffer: single-task buffers are accessed directly; a buffer used by several tasks gets one copy per task, read at the task's start and published at its end under a lock; a port whose runnables run in several tasks gets an atomic hand-over under the lock (swc/README.md, "Datenkonsistenz zwischen Tasks"). Implicit access adds a copy per runnable on top of that scheme where the component asks for it. This is a smaller and testable scheme, and it is ours.

Task priorities are also our own: OpenBSW starts each task with its context number as FreeRTOS priority, so the project's priority is a sort key over BSW and application tasks rather than an OS priority (swc/README.md).

docs.title: 2.4 Diagnostics — ISO 14229, not Dcm
docs.text:
Two independent UDS servers exist, both following ISO 14229 over ISO 15765-2:

  • Bootloader (bootloader/src/core/uds.c, isotp.c): plain C, no AUTOSAR and no OpenBSW. Services 0x10, 0x11, 0x22, 0x27, 0x2E, 0x31, 0x34, 0x36, 0x37, 0x3E with the standard negative response codes (0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x22, 0x24, 0x31, 0x33, 0x35, 0x36, 0x37, 0x70, 0x72, 0x73, 0x78, 0x7F). Long operations are chunked and answer 7F xx 78 while they run. DIDs 0xF180, 0xF184 (fingerprint), 0xF186, 0xF189 and 0xF191 are the identifiers ISO 14229-1 defines for these meanings; the routine identifiers 0xFF00/0xFF01/0xF1A0 (0xFF02 before bootloader 0.3.4) and DID 0xF1A0 (target compatibility) are project conventions.
  • Application (ecu/uds): built on OpenBSW's uds, docan and transport libraries. Services 10 01/02/03, 11 01/03, 22 F180/F181/F186/FD00, 2E FD00 and 3E (ecu/uds/include/uds/app/DiagStack.h). Addressing uses OpenBSW's TransportConfiguration::FUNCTIONAL_ALL_ISO14229; timing, block size and separation time come from the project's generated AppDiagConfig.h, so the bootloader answers with the same values.

What is not there: an AUTOSAR Dcm with its ARXML configuration, a Dem with event memory and DTCs, snapshot or extended data records, or an OBD service set. Diagnostics here is a protocol implementation, not the AUTOSAR diagnostic stack.

docs.title: 2.5 BSW modules — vocabulary only
docs.text:
The layer model in README.md section 3 uses AUTOSAR words: BSW, complex device driver, services above drivers, application on top of an RTE. The module names are not AUTOSAR's. A search across libs/, ecu/, platforms/, bootloader/ and tools/ for CanIf, PduR, Dem_, NvM_, EcuM, BswM and Dcm_ returns no hits at all outside the submodule.

What fills those roles instead:

AUTOSAR module Here Com, PduR, CanIf, CanSM tools/dbcgen generates pack/unpack from the project's DBC; libs/bsw/canSystem owns bus state and the transmit gate; the RTE moves signals E2E libs/bsw/e2e — the one place where the specification really is implemented Dcm ecu/uds on OpenBSW's uds library Dem nothing. There is no fault memory and no DTC handling NvM, Fee, Ea nothing. OpenBSW's IEepromDriver exists but EepromDriver::init() is forbidden by project rule, because FlexNVM partitioning is irreversible and the decision is open EcuM, BswM libs/bsw/ecuState plus OpenBSW's lifecycle manager with nine numbered levels Os FreeRTOS WdgM, Wdg OpenBSW's safety libraries plus the MCU watchdog and, where a board has one, the SBC's external watchdog through the watchdog_trigger role

The module manifest module.yaml is a neXtBSW invention with no AUTOSAR ancestry: it declares the module's kind, the L1 contracts it requires, the roles it provides, its configuration schema, its lifecycle level and task, and its CMake target (README.md section 5). It exists for 11 modules today, not for all of them.

docs.title: 2.6 MCU drivers — explicitly not MCAL
docs.text:
The L1 layer is OpenBSW's BSP interfaces plus two of our own (libs/bsp/bspSpi, libs/bsp/bspAdcAccess). No MCAL API appears anywhere: a search for Dio_, Adc_, Spi_, Pwm_, Mcu_Init, Port_Init and Gpt_ returns nothing.

This is a decision, not an omission. treiber-granularitaet.md section 1 names the failure mode it is avoiding: a generic driver whose parameter set is the union of every supported part's capabilities, so that only some parameters apply per instance and no tool can check which combination makes sense — "das ist der MCAL-Fehlschlag". The rule instead is that the boundary runs along the protocol: same behaviour and only numbers differ → one generic behaviour module with the part in its parts: list; own register model or own sequence → a hardware-near driver named after the part family; same behaviour over a different access path → a thin adapter.

docs.title: 2.7 Methodology and tooling — none of AUTOSAR's
docs.text:
There is no AUTOSAR methodology tool chain here. No ECU configuration ARXML, no BSWMD, no EcuC parameter definitions, no system description, no ECU extract, no configuration editor that reads or writes any of them. The configuration is three levels of YAML validated by pydantic models in tools/nxconfig, and the GUI (neXtBSW Studio) edits those.

The only ARXML in the repository is generator output from Embedded Coder, consumed by tools/rtegen as an input description of the component. rtegen parses a deliberately small set of elements and reports anything it cannot resolve; it is not an ARXML tool in the general sense.

docs.title: 3. What is missing, stated plainly
docs.text:
• No AUTOSAR methodology tooling. See 2.7.
  • No complete BSW module list. See 2.5. Memory (NvM) and diagnostic event handling (Dem) are entirely absent, not partially implemented.
  • No conformance evidence. No AUTOSAR conformance test suite has been run against any part of this repository, no certification exists, and none is planned. Where a specification is implemented — the E2E profiles — the evidence is host tests against the specification's own example values and a mutation run, which is a statement about those tests and nothing more.
  • No AUTOSAR Adaptive anything. The vocabulary used here is Classic Platform throughout.
  • Verification level. Every statement on this page is a statement about source code read on 2026-09-17 (verification: mock/analysis). None of it was re-measured on hardware for this document.

docs.title: 4. If you come from AUTOSAR, expect this
docs.text:
You will recognise: the layering, the idea of a component with ports and runnables, Rte_Read/Rte_Write, Rte_IRead/Rte_IWrite/Rte_IWriteRef, Rte_Mode with mode switch events on the ECU states, the base types, the E2E profiles, UDS, and the habit of describing an ECU rather than programming it.

You will not find: ARXML as the configuration language, a BSW module list, a Dcm/Dem pair, an NvM stack, MCAL APIs, AUTOSAR OS, or a conformance statement. Where AUTOSAR would have a standard module, this repository usually has a smaller module of its own with host tests, and the reason is written down in README.md section 10 or in treiber-granularitaet.md.

docs.title: CSEc in neXtBSW: keys, message authentication and secure start
docs.text:
Status: 2026-09-23, proposal, am 2026-10-04 gekürzt; die Abwägungen je Kandidat, die Review-Fragen, die Folgen für andere Aufgaben und die Langfassung der Fragen Q1 bis Q7 stehen in der Versionshistorie dieser Datei (Commit vor). Der Maintainer entschied am 2026-09-23, dass CSEc auf diesem Board gebraucht wird; das Dokument klärt, wofür, wie viele Schlüsselplätze und was das mit der FlexNVM-Partition macht. Es ist die Grundlage für (PGMPART mit Schlüsselraum statt festem FCCOB1/2 = 0).

Reference: architecture target picture, FlexNVM partition state (not published, available on request) safety concept.

Why this is worth care. The number of key slots is written into the chip once, together with the partition. Raising it later needs the CSEc debug authentication with a key that has to exist at that moment, or the device is finished. The eval board is a FS32K144UAVLL, a CSEc part (SDID 0x144F14EA, FEATURES bit 7 set), and it is not partitioned; nothing has been written.
