Reference: architecture target picture (configuration levels section 4, bootloader section 7, review questions section 11), swc/README.md (calibration parameters), tools/a2lgen/README.md (A2L and xcp_master.py), Studio guide (not published, available on request) (model import and <Name>_init.m), safety concept, ISO 26262 gap analysis (not published, available on request) (row 6-40, item 22), tool classification (a2lgen, AoU-28).

The question of the maintainer (2026-09-27): how are parameters and maps given their values, can a versioned calibration database solve that, and how are measurement and calibration signals defined?

Short answer, detailed in the sections below:

  1. One definition per calibration object, one place for its values. The definition (kind, type, axes, unit, limits, safety class) belongs to the component description swc.yaml. The model is checked against it, as ports already are. The values belong to datasets that the project owns.
  2. The calibration database is Git plus a text format plus tools. It is not a server and not a binary store. A dataset is a folder of YAML files, one per component, laid out so that a line diff is a value diff. DCM and CDFX are exchange formats at the edge, not the store.
  3. init_data/ stays the build environment of an imported model and does not become the database. Its constants, types and data stores are what the model needs to compile. The values promoted to calibration parameters move out of it into the dataset. A later neXtBSW init v2 then loads them from the dataset (section 5.4).
  4. Runtime: a calibration segment of its own in flash, with its own validity record (CRC, layout identifier) and a RAM working page in development builds. The segment can be flashed without the application. Production builds read the flash page directly and have no write path.
  5. Measurement: ports stay measurable automatically. Internal model signals are measurable only when the model marks them. BSW values come from the module manifests. DAQ runs per RTE task.

docs.title: 1. Terms
docs.text: Term Meaning here A2L object Calibration parameter value a calibration engineer may change without a new build; the software only reads it CHARACTERISTIC Scalar one value VALUE Array fixed number of values without an axis (today's dim) VAL_BLK Curve (Kennlinie) values over one axis, interpolated or looked up CURVE Map (Kennfeld) values over two axes MAP Axis ascending breakpoints; own (stored with the curve/map) or shared (a separate object used by several curves/maps) AXIS_DESCR with STD_AXIS/COM_AXIS, AXIS_PTS Conversion stored value ↔ physical value (today rational: phys = (n0 + n1·stored)/d); for an enumeration a value table COMPU_METHOD (RAT_FUNC, TAB_VERB) Measurement signal value a tool may read while the software runs MEASUREMENT Dataset (Datensatz) complete set of values of all calibration parameters of one ECU software DCM/CDFX file, HEX of the segment Variant dataset that differs from a base dataset in some values (vehicle, power class, market) – Layout identifier hash over names, kinds, types, dimensions and order of all parameters in the segment; a dataset fits every build with the same layout – EPK identifier of the software build in the image, which a tool compares with the A2L EPK, ADDR_EPK Working / reference page writable RAM copy of the values / flash original SEGMENT + PAGE in IF_DATA XCP

docs.title: 2. Current state
docs.text: Implemented: calibration objects in swc.yaml with extended A2L (K1), datasets and calgen (K2), the calibration segment with start-up check (K3) and plausibility checks (K6). The XCP slave (ecu/xcp), tools/a2lgen (A2L from the ELF, xcp_master.py), swc.yaml parameters: and the Studio parameter editing for C components are older; imported models keep init_data/ as the build environment. Still missing: live values and online calibration in the Studio, FreeMASTER, canflash cal (K4), Simulink round trip (K5), measurement signals and DAQ (K7, K8). Sensor characteristics of the board are configuration, not calibration data (4.5).

docs.title: 3. Requirements and boundary conditions
docs.text:
• Board neutral (architecture section 1). No family-specific overlay hardware is assumed. Sizes and places are project values in memory:. The targets are Cortex-M and Cortex-R, 32 bit, little endian.
  • No FPU on every target (S32K116, architecture section 4). Curves and maps must work in integer or fixed point. float32 stays allowed where the derivative has an FPU.
  • One value, one place (architecture section 4). No number is typed twice: not in the model, not in C, and not in the A2L.
  • No MATLAB where it is not needed. rtegen, a2lgen and the Studio read everything without MATLAB, as they do today with mdata.py.
  • Simulink is the maintainer's working environment. Calibration must fit his workflow: data scripts, Simulink.Parameter, and lookup table blocks.
  • Git is the version control of all project data (customer project, doc/architecture/customer-project.md).
  • ASIL B is confirmed. C and D come later. BSW mechanisms stay separate from driver mechanisms.
  • The bootloader stays compatible: a new record goes behind the existing ones and is never a change of format (app_image.h, rule).

docs.title: 4.1 Kinds
docs.text:
Kind Content Proposal value scalar as today array fixed count without an axis today's dim, renamed. Kept for tables that have no physical axis (e.g. per-cell offsets). curve N values over one axis new map N×M values over two axes new; row = X, column = Y, stored in row-major order (C order) axis shared breakpoint vector new; own object, used by name from several curves/maps (COM_AXIS) text / boolean / enum value with a value table enum new: the value table comes from the type, as for ports (TEXTTABLE)

An axis is either own (axis: {points: 8, …} in the curve, stored in front of the values, STD_AXIS) or shared (axis: SpeedAxis_rpm, COM_AXIS). Shared axes are the normal case for maps over the same operating point. The maintainer's MBDT models build them from Simulink.Breakpoint + Simulink.LookupTable (section 5.4).

Interpolation belongs to the component, not to the calibration layer. A Simulink component uses its lookup block. A C component uses a small library function (nxLookup1D/2D in integer with the same rounding rule as sensor.py, later). The description only states which behaviour the component expects (interpolation: linear | nearest, extrapolation: hold). The generator checks the axis: strictly ascending, and the type range is enough for the differences.

docs.title: 4.2 Types and conversion
docs.text:
• Stored types: the platform types as today (uint8 … sint32, float32, float64, boolean). Axis and values may have different types, with their own conversion each.
  • Conversion: the existing rational form phys = (n0 + n1·stored)/d (generator Fraction, A2L RAT_FUNC) covers lsb/offset. No new conversion kinds. A non-linear conversion is a curve in its own right. Enumerations use value tables.
  • Values in the dataset are physical, as in <Swc>_data.m today. The generator rounds to the grid and reports a deviation above half a step as a warning (already does this).

docs.title: 4.3 Unit, limits, description
docs.text:
Each calibration object gets:

Key Meaning Used by unit physical unit (rpm, mV, degC, -) A2L PHYS_UNIT, Studio, dataset check min, max engineering limits, physical, inside the type range A2L lower/upper limit; dataset check, which refuses values outside; optional run-time check (4.4) description one line A2L long identifier, Studio display optional format (%.3f) A2L format

The type range becomes EXTENDED_LIMITS. A calibration tool then warns inside the type range but outside the engineering limits, and refuses outside the type range.

docs.title: 4.4 Safety class
docs.text:
safety: qm | asil_a | asil_b per parameter (C and D later, same key). What the class causes is defined in section 7.5 :

  • Not writable over XCP in a production build, and not writable at all when the project sets calibration.lock_safety: true.
  • A generated plausibility check against min/max (and monotony for axes) at start-up and after every write. A violation leads to a DEM entry and the component's default reaction; the value is not silently corrected.
  • Listed in a generated report (safety-relevant calibration parameters with limits and dataset value). That report is part of the evidence for Part 6 Annex C of ISO 26262 (calibration data: specified, verified, protected).

docs.title: 4.5 What is not calibration data
docs.text:
• Configuration (board.yaml, project.yaml: ADC sensor tables, PWM frequency, thresholds of the safe supervisor) is fixed at generation time and belongs to a build. A value that must change without a build moves to a component parameter.
  • Coding (variant selection in the field, e.g. by UDS 0x2E) and learned values (adaptation, NvM) are different life cycles. Both may select or correct a calibration value, but they never live in the dataset.
  • Constants of an imported model that no one should change (SYSCONST.HW_REVISION, task time) stay in init_data/ (section 5.4).

docs.title: 5. One source for the definition, one place for the values
5.1 The definition: swc.yaml is the master (E1 a)
docs.text:
Option Result A: Simulink data objects are the master rejected: C components have no Simulink objects (a second path), .sldd is binary, the Studio would need MATLAB for every view, two masters as soon as C components exist B: swc.yaml is the master (extended) chosen: the same pattern as ports (description in swc.yaml, ARXML as the check); no MATLAB to read it; the model is written from it and checked against it C: a separate <Swc>.cal.yaml rejected: as B, but a third file to keep in step

swc.yaml stays the one description of the interface of a component type: ports, runnables and calibration objects. The chain:

swc.yaml parameters:  ──(swc_create / "write to model", MATLAB)──▶  .slx: Simulink.Parameter / LookupTable / Breakpoint
      │                                                                   │ swc_build
      │                                                                   ▼
      │                                                        ARXML (types, dims, compu methods)
      ├──────────── rtegen: check swc.yaml == ARXML (error with YAML path) ◀┘
      ▼
rtegen: Rte_Prm_* storage in the calibration segment, rte::PARAMETERS[] (extended by kind, axes, limits, safety)
      ▼
a2lgen: CHARACTERISTIC/AXIS_PTS/COMPU_METHOD/RECORD_LAYOUT from the ELF tables  +  dataset ──▶ HEX of the segment

The ELF stays the source of addresses: the A2L describes exactly the binary it came from, as today. The extended table rte::PARAMETERS[] has to carry kind and axis references. Alternatively a2lgen reads those two from swc.yaml/the generated RteConfig next to the ELF. That is a detail for the implementation. The rule is: a2lgen never takes a number that the ELF does not confirm.

docs.title: 5.2 Where the values live: the dataset (E2 a)
docs.text:
Option Result 1: keep <Swc>_data.m becomes the default values of the component type (what the MIL test runs with); the Studio migrates it into the first dataset; no place for metadata or variants 2: neXtBSW dataset (YAML) chosen: one value per line, one map row per line, stable order, so a line diff is a value diff; status, author, reason, variant, layout identifier per value or file; MATLAB loader nx_cal_load 3: DCM as the store exchange format only: little room for metadata 4: CDFX as the store exchange format only: ASAM standard, but XML diffs poorly

Sketch of a dataset file:

# projects/<p>/calibration/base/HvsControl.cal.yaml
format: nextbsw-cal 1
component: HvsControl
layout: 3f2a9c1e               # layout identifier this file was written for (checked, not decisive)
values:
  HvsOpModeOnDelay_ms: {value: 200, status: released}
  CellBalThr_mV:       {value: 15, status: checked, note: "measured 2026-10-02 at 25 degC"}
  SpeedAxis_rpm:
    value: [0, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 6000]
  TorqueLimit_Nm:                # map over SpeedAxis_rpm (X) x TempAxis_degC (Y)
    status: draft
    value:
      - [120, 120, 110,  90]     # 0 rpm
      - [120, 118, 108,  88]     # 500 rpm
      # one row per line: a changed cell is a changed line in the diff

docs.title: 5.3 Datasets, variants and who owns them
docs.text:
• A dataset belongs to the project, not to the reusable component: projects/<p>/calibration/<dataset>/, one file per component instance (fits: one file per instance). Today's <Swc>_data.m in swc/<Swc>/ would otherwise give every project that uses a reusable component the same values.
  • Variants as a base plus a delta: calibration/base/ is complete, and calibration/variants/<v>/ contains only the values that differ. The generator resolves them, so a delta never becomes a copy of the whole dataset. Which dataset or variant goes into a build or a segment HEX is a project value (calibration.dataset: base, calibration.variant: 400V). Several variants in one flash image, selected by coding, come later and fit the same model.
  • A dataset must be complete against the layout. A missing value is an error; the default of the component type is not taken silently. The Studio offers "fill from defaults" as an explicit action.

docs.title: 5.4 init_data/ and the calibration database
docs.text:
init_data/ holds copies of the old project's scripts. They define three kinds of content:

Content Example Future place constants the model needs to compile SYSCONST.HW_REVISION, SYSCONST.HVS_CONTROL_TASK_TIME stays in init_data/ types and data stores Simulink.Signal for global data stores, bus objects, enumerations stays in init_data/ (nx:datastores) tuning values thresholds, delays, curves in hvsctrl.* moves into the dataset once promoted to a calibration parameter

So init_data/ does not become the calibration database, and the database does not replace it as a whole. It is the model's build environment and keeps that role. The database takes over the values that are meant to be calibrated. The step between the two is a Studio action "make calibratable" on an imported model:

  1. The Studio lists the variables the model reads from init_data/, marked with where they are used. A variable that feeds a lookup block is proposed as a curve or map with its breakpoints.
  2. The maintainer selects the ones to promote. The Studio adds them to swc.yaml parameters: with type, dimension and axes from the compiled model. Unit, limits and safety class are asked.
  3. MATLAB turns the workspace constant in the model copy into a Simulink.Parameter or LookupTable model argument mapped for AUTOSAR. This is the parameter counterpart of "Ports ins Modell schreiben".
  4. The value goes into the dataset. In the init file the assignment is commented out, not deleted, with a pointer to the dataset, so the history of the old script stays visible.
  5. neXtBSW init v2 gets a section %% nx:calibration that loads the chosen dataset (default: the project's base) with nx_cal_load before the model is compiled. Files marked v1 stay valid.

This keeps the maintainer's accepted rule: the copy in swc/<Name>/ is the master of what it still contains.

docs.title: 6.1 Git is the database
docs.text:
Function of a calibration database Realised by history, who changed what and why Git log/blame over the dataset files; a note per value for the reason branches for experiments Git branches; the Studio names them (cal/<dataset>/<topic>) merge line-based Git merge. The format is built for it: stable order, one value or row per line. A conflict is a real conflict of two values and is shown per object by the Studio (a later merge driver can resolve maps cell by cell) release a value status per object, and a release of the dataset as an annotated tag cal/<project>/<dataset>/vN on a commit where every safety-relevant value is released. The Studio generates the segment HEX and a report with the tag comparison Studio: dataset ↔ dataset, dataset ↔ ECU (upload), dataset ↔ DCM/CDFX access rights repository permissions; for customer projects the customer's own repository (customer-project.md)

No server, no binary store. The "database" is the folder layout, the schema, the checks in tools/nxconfig (or a small tools/calgen), and the Studio.

docs.title: 6.2 Value status
docs.text:
A small set that CDFX can also express, so an export does not lose information:

draft → checked → released. A changed value falls back to draft. A release refuses safety-relevant values that are not released.

docs.title: 6.3 Relation to the software build (EPK, layout identifier)
docs.text:
Two identifiers, because a dataset outlives many builds:

Identifier Content Where EPK of the application build identity (version, Git description, hash) fixed string in the image, EPK/ADDR_EPK in the A2L, also readable over UDS Layout identifier hash over name, kind, type, dimensions, axis references and order of all objects in the calibration segment in the application (expected) and in the header of the segment (present)
  • A dataset fits every build with the same layout identifier. Fixing a bug in the software does not invalidate the calibration.
  • The dataset file records the layout identifier it was written for. The generator reports a stale layout with the objects that were added, removed or changed, and the Studio offers the migration.
  • The application compares the two identifiers at start-up (section 7.3).

docs.title: 6.4 Flow back from an XCP session
docs.text:
1. The engineer calibrates on the RAM working page (Studio, CANape, INCA).
  2. At the end, the Studio uploads the working page, compares it with the dataset, and shows the changes per object in physical values.
  3. The engineer accepts per object. The Studio writes the values into the dataset files with status draft, the author, and an optional reason, and offers a commit on the Git page.
  4. From a third-party tool the same flow goes through a DCM or CDFX export of the session.
  5. To keep the values on the ECU, a segment HEX is built from the dataset and flashed with canflash (7.4). The application itself does not write flash in this concept.

docs.title: 7.1 Memory and page switching (E4 a)
docs.text: Option Result R1: as today (.data) no flashing without the application R2: own segment + RAM working page, switching by copy chosen: needs nothing from the derivative, component code and RTE API unchanged, fits the write mechanism of XcpSystem; the XCP "reference page" becomes a copy action; production build const from flash R3: two pages switched by pointer rejected: one indirection per access, generated component code changes; pays off only when two pages must switch within one cycle R4: hardware overlay possible later as a family option, not board neutral

docs.title: 7.2 Layout
docs.text:
• memory.calibration: {size: 0x2000, region: PFLASH | DFLASH} in project.yaml, checked and placed by tools/nxconfig/memory.py (sector aligned, no overlap, fits). Whether the data flash of an S32K1 is the place is a separate task's question. The concept allows both.
  • Linker: section .nx_cal for all Rte_Prm_* objects, in the order that the layout identifier covers. The RAM copy lies in .nx_cal_ram (development build).
  • Header of the segment: magic CALV, format version, layout identifier, dataset identifier (tag or commit), size, CRC-32 over the values, CRC over the header. It follows the rules of app_image.h: fields never move, and additions are appended.

docs.title: 7.3 Start-up check
docs.text:
1. Header valid, CRC correct, layout identifier equal to the one the application expects → use the segment.
  2. Otherwise the project decides (calibration.on_invalid): defaults: the application uses the default values built into its image (const, costs flash once more) and sets a DTC. refuse: the application does not start its functions and stays reachable over UDS/canflash. Recommended default: refuse for projects with a safety-relevant parameter, defaults otherwise.
  3. The plausibility checks of safety-relevant parameters (4.4) run after 1 and after every XCP write (as built: before the values take effect, section 7.7).

docs.title: 7.4 Flashing a dataset without the application
docs.text:
• canflash cal <segment.hex> writes only the calibration region: the same UDS sequence as for the application (request download to the address of the region, transfer, exit, check routine), with the region in the memory layout that the bootloader already knows from the generated header.
  • The bootloader has to know the region (erase and write only there, and the compatibility check of the CALV record against the application record). That is a bootloader update, so it is done only with the maintainer present . An older bootloader refuses the address, so nothing breaks.
  • The segment HEX is generated from the dataset and the ELF without a build: addresses from the ELF, values from the dataset, header and CRC by the generator.

docs.title: 7.5 Protection in the product
docs.text:
Measure Development build Production build XCP on (project xcp:) off: the production profile has no xcp: section, and nxconfig refuses xcp: in a profile marked release: production Calibration values RAM working page const in the flash segment, no RAM copy, so there is no writable path in memory Safety-relevant parameters writable unless lock_safety not writable (follows from the row above) Integrity CRC at start-up; since an earlier change re-checked in every ROM check pass (7.6) CRC at start-up; since an earlier change re-checked in every ROM check pass (a BSW mechanism, separate from drivers, 7.6) Plausibility after every write at start-up Read-back without the A2L conversion a console command that prints stored parameter values (AoU-28); to be added, since rte shows only signals today –

This is the "disabled in the product" branch of AoU-28. The "interlocked writes" branch is only needed if a customer wants XCP in the vehicle. It stays possible through lock_safety plus seed & key on XCP (not planned).

docs.title: 7.6 Implementation
docs.text:
Stage K3 as built. Details of the code are in ecu/calibration and tools/calseg.

  • Project value (tools/nxconfig, reference doc/reference/project.md):
memory:
  calibration: { region: PFLASH, size: 0x1000, on_invalid: refuse, profile: development }

region is the code flash of memory.flash or a data flash region (the latter refused until the bootloader can write it); size whole sectors; on_invalid refuse (default) | defaults | warn; profile development (default) | production. nxconfig refuses on_invalid other than refuse when a parameter has a safety class other than qm, xcp in the production profile, and defaults in the production profile. - Place and linker. In the code flash the segment follows the first sector of the application, so the vector table stays where the bootloader jumps to. Production: the values are read from the flash segment; development: a RAM working page filled at start-up, and the segment holds the copy. Both profiles give the segment the same bytes. - Header (ecu/calibration/include/calibration/CalibrationSegment.h, 32 bytes, little endian): magic CALV, format 1, layout identifier, dataset identifier, length, CRC-32 over the values and over the header. tools/calseg seal writes it after the link; it stops the build if a parameter lies outside the page. - Start-up check (in RteSystem::init() before the init runnables): erased, magic, format, header CRC, length, layout identifier, values CRC. refuse starts no init runnable and no application task (NvM, fault memory, UDS and console keep running, so a valid image can be downloaded); defaults keeps the values of the build; warn uses the segment. Every result is one log line and a DTC event calibration.segment. - XCP, console, HEX. The RAM working page is the only page the ECU uses; the flash segment is readable over XCP as the reference page. Console cal status and cal values are the read-back path of AoU-28. tools/calseg hex writes the segment HEX of every build and for any dataset (--dataset <project.yaml> [--variant V]). - ROM check. The segment is not on the ROM check list (SM-14); its own CRCs are its reference, re-checked with the same period by calibration::recheckSegment() when the start-up found the segment valid. A failure there is the SM-14 reaction (ROM_CHECK_FAILURE, S1 held); after the power cycle the start-up check applies on_invalid, so the ECU can be flashed again. tools/calseg merge --flip OFFSET:BIT writes a damaged image as a test aid.

docs.title: 7.7 Implementation
docs.text:
Stage K6 as built. The ECU checks every calibration parameter whose safety is not qm (axes take at least the class of the curves and maps that use them). tools/rtegen writes one row per parameter into rte::PARAMETER_CHECKS; a project without such a parameter gets neither table nor code. The rules are the ones the build and tools/calgen check apply (rtegen.value_rules): limits (every stored value inside Rte_Lim_*, NaN fails), ascending (breakpoints strictly rising), form (number of values, element type and axis element counts as in swc.yaml).

  • When: always before the values take effect: at start-up (segment, else image values; failure leads to on_invalid, refuse as soon as a checked parameter exists, and always without a segment) and on every XCP write (a refused write never reaches memory; the master gets ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE; an axis is written as one DOWNLOAD block).
  • No cyclic check (decision): development values change only through XCP, production values are const under the CRC and the ROM check; a cyclic check would only find faults of the RAM working page, which is the RAM test's job.
  • Evidence: one log line per start-up result and per refused write, DTC event calibration.plausibility, console cal check, and RteParameterChecks.md next to RteConfig.h (every checked parameter with class, kind, form, unit, limits, rules and value of the build: the list for the safety case).

docs.title: 8.1 Who decides what is measurable or writable
docs.text:
M1: everything global is measurable M2: explicit list in swc.yaml M3: ports automatic + annotation in the model + BSW manifests Ports yes listed yes, automatic (today's state) Internal model signals only if the coder makes them global; uncontrolled listed by name; breaks on every rename in the model the model marks them (test point or a mapping to static memory); the ARXML carries them; rtegen collects them BSW values – – module manifest (measurements: with name, type, unit) → one generated BSW table Effort for the maintainer none high, duplicate low, in the tool he works in One source no duplicate of the model yes

Recommendation: M3. Calibration objects are always declared in swc.yaml (section 5.1). Measurement follows the place where a signal exists:

  • RTE signals (every port, including BSW signals that are connected to a port) are always measurable, as today.
  • Internal signals of a Simulink model are made measurable in the model: the AUTOSAR code mapping of an internal signal or state to static memory with read-only calibration access (the exact R2024a mapping is to be verified in the implementation). The ARXML then carries them, and rtegen adds them to the table. A signal without this mark cannot be measured, so the model author decides and nothing is typed twice.
  • Internal values of a C component: measurements: in swc.yaml, because there is no model. The code declares them through an RTE macro that places them in the table.
  • BSW (supply voltage, task load, bus state, NvM state): each module manifest names what it offers. The generated BSW table uses the same format as rte::SIGNALS. A project can restrict it (xcp.bsw: [power, can]).

Calibration access is never automatic. Only objects in parameters: are writable. Measurement objects are always read-only.

docs.title: 8.2 The maintainer's name prefixes
docs.text:
The maintainer's models name signals with prefixes that carry type and meaning (b_…, bm_… as in bm_HvsErrorState, st_… as in st_CmcStatus, u_…). The complete table is not written down in the repository. The meaning of u_ in particular has to come from the maintainer (voltage or unsigned). Proposal:

  • The prefix does not decide measurability or calibration access. That would make a rename a change of the interface.
  • It is a checked convention: a table in the workspace (nextbsw.yaml naming.prefixes, prefix → allowed types, display) lets the Studio propose type and display (bm_ → BIT_MASK per bit, st_ → value table, b_ → boolean) and warn when a port's type contradicts its prefix. Without the table nothing is checked. Customers use their own conventions.

docs.title: 8.3 Measurement grid and DAQ
docs.text:
• Events = RTE tasks. Each application task becomes an XCP event (EVENT in the A2L, period from rte.yaml). The sample is taken at the end of the task cycle, so all signals of one task are consistent with each other. This matches the copies at task boundaries the RTE already makes.
  • DAQ lists: dynamic (ALLOC_DAQ/ALLOC_ODT) with a fixed RAM budget as a project value (xcp.daq_bytes). Static lists are not needed.
  • Timestamp: 1 µs or 10 µs from the system timer (SystemTimer), 4 bytes, one per DTO of the first ODT.
  • Bandwidth on classic CAN is the limit. At 500 kbit/s, well below 4000 frames/s are available for all traffic, and each DTO carries 7 bytes. The Studio shows the load of the chosen DAQ lists before the start. CAN FD (64-byte DTO) helps where the bus offers it.
  • Polling (SHORT_UPLOAD) stays for single values and for tools without DAQ.

docs.title: 9. Tools
docs.text: Where What Notes Studio: component page calibration objects (define: kind, axis, unit, limits, safety) for C and Simulink components; "make calibratable" for imported models (5.4) extends MATLAB only for writing into the model Studio: calibration page (new) datasets and variants, table and graph editor for curves and maps (edit cells, a row, or a region; offset or factor on a selection; 2-D plot per row/column and a surface view), status per value, compare two datasets, release (tag + HEX + report) reads/writes only text files, no MATLAB Studio: online live values from DAQ, calibrate the working page, reference/working page, upload/compare/write-back (6.4), flash the segment (canflash cal) needs the runtime of section 7 Import/export A2L (generated), DCM and CDFX (import/export of a dataset, with status in CDFX), Intel HEX/S-record of the segment (flashing, and for tools that take HEX + A2L), <Swc>_data.m (import, migration) converters without Qt in tools/ (core logic free of Qt, as for the later web application) MATLAB nx_cal_load(dataset) → Simulink.Parameter/LookupTable/Breakpoint in the model workspace; nx_cal_save for values tuned in simulation; init v2 section nx:calibration the only MATLAB parts; the dataset reader is also a small subset reader like mdata.py FreeMASTER variable list from the same tables as the A2L no own definition

docs.title: 10. Stage plan
docs.text:
Stage Content State K1 Definition swc.yaml kinds (value/array/curve/map/axis/enum), axes, unit, min/max, safety; rtegen check against the ARXML; a2lgen CURVE/MAP/AXIS_PTS, record layouts, limits, units, COMPU_VTAB, EPK/ADDR_EPK, FUNCTION implemented K2 Dataset format nextbsw-cal 1, calibration/dataset.yaml, base/ and variants/<v>/ (delta), status per value, layout identifier (calgen rebind), release tag cal/<project>/<dataset>/v<N>, nx_cal_load.m implemented (tools/calgen/README.md) K3 Runtime memory.calibration, CALV header, start-up check with on_invalid, production build const and no XCP, segment HEX implemented (7.6) K4 Flashing canflash cal, bootloader checks the CALV record against the application open K5 Simulink curves/maps as model arguments, parameter sync, "make calibratable" for imported models, init v2 open K6 Plausibility generated checks at start-up and after writes, DEM entry, report implemented (7.7) K7 Measurement internal model signals, measurements: for C components and BSW manifests, prefix table (warnings only) open (QM) K8 DAQ events per RTE task, dynamic DAQ, timestamp open (QM) K9 Studio calibration page and map editor, online page, FreeMASTER list open; the Studio display is not evidence (AoU-27)

What matters for ASIL B: the definition with limits (K1), integrity and version check of the segment (K3), the product protection (K3, 7.5) and plausibility where a safety-relevant parameter stays calibratable (K6); a2lgen is qualified or covered by AoU-28 (tool-classification.md), and the dataset release is a defined, verified generation procedure. Variants, DCM/CDFX, the map editor, DAQ and the measurement definition are QM development aids. ASIL C/D would add redundant storage of safety-relevant parameters, for which the segment header leaves room.

docs.title: 11. Decisions
docs.text: # Decision (maintainer, 2026-09-28: all recommendations a) Section E1 The definition of calibration objects is swc.yaml parameters: (extended); the model is written from it and checked against it 5.1 E2 The store is the own YAML dataset nextbsw-cal 1; DCM and CDFX are import/export 5.2 E3 Datasets per project (projects/<p>/calibration/); the component folder keeps only defaults; init_data/ stays the model's build environment and promoted values move into the dataset (init v2) 5.3, 5.4 E4 Own flash segment with a CALV record, RAM working page in development builds, reference page by copying, production build const from flash 7.1 E5 Production build without XCP and with const values, CRC at start-up, on_invalid: refuse when a safety-relevant parameter exists (AoU-28) 7.5 E6 Ports automatic, internal model signals by marking in the model, C components by measurements:, BSW by module manifests; prefixes only as a checked convention (warnings); the complete prefix table is still needed from the maintainer 8.1, 8.2

docs.text: Status: planned (after R1). Die Familie rm4x (TI Hercules RM4x, Cortex-R4F, Little Endian, Nachweisziel LAUNCHXL2-RM46) ist kein Teil von R1. Der Audit mit Fundstellenliste, Messbelegen und Review-Fragen steht in der Git-Historie dieser Datei (Commit vor einer späteren Änderung). Seine Entscheidungen sind verbindlich in README.md: D11 Kernprofile, D12 Bootloader ohne VTOR, D13 Familienname, D14 Quellenverfahren (Abschnitt 10), dazu die Plattformregel (Abschnitt 6).

docs.title: Legende
docs.text:
• Die Grundannahmen halten: ILP32, Little Endian, AAPCS mit VFP; Bootloader-Kern und hardwareunabhängige Module übersetzen für -mcpu=cortex-r4f ohne Meldung; die Toolchain (arm-none-eabi-gcc) genügt.
  • Neutral zu machen war: das Kernmodell in nxconfig (NVIC/BASEPRI), die Architekturerkennung (nie über __ARM_ARCH, es ist 7 für R und M), die Auswahl des FreeRTOS-Ports, Bootloader/Updater/canflash (Image-Anfang ist beim R4F kein Cortex-M-Vektor), FreeRtosAdcLock.h und das Dump-Layout.
  • Unterschiede des RM46: VIM statt NVIC, RTI statt SysTick, Modus-Stacks und Vektoren ab 0 statt VTOR, ARMv7-R-MPU, FreeRTOS-Port ARM_CRx_No_GIC, DCAN statt FlexCAN, F021-Flash-API, XDS110 statt J-Link.
  • Die Quellen- und Lizenzprüfung steht auf rm4x-quellen.md.

Verweise: Zielbild, Plattformen, Bootloader.

docs.title: OpenBSW console commands with a number argument - audit
docs.text:
Safety review 2026-10-01, decision SR-150-1 b: after the finding of a separate task (out set 259 1 wrote output 3, because bios::OutputTester casts the number to the one-byte Output::OutputId before its range check), every console command of OpenBSW that takes a number was checked for the same class of fault. Base: OpenBSW 3b6e702 (submodule external/openbsw) and the neXtBSW copies of OpenBSW commands in ecu/consoleCommands.

What was looked for, per number argument:

  • A - alias by narrowing: the number is checked after a cast to a narrower type (enum, uint8_t, uint16_t), or passed to a narrower parameter after a check on another value - so n + 2^k reaches n past the check.
  • B - unchecked scan result: CommandContext::scanIntToken() returns 0 for a missing or invalid token and only marks the context; a command that acts without looking at the result writes 0 (or element 0).
  • C - scanner wrap: scanIntToken<T>() itself has no overflow detection (wraps modulo 2^bits(T), accepts a sign for unsigned T). Harmless as long as the value that is checked is the value that is used - only a spelling alias, no bypass - but worth an error.

docs.title: Result per tester
docs.text:
Command (class, file) In a neXtBSW image Number arguments Finding Action out set, out get (bios::OutputTester, libs/bsp/bspOutputManager) yes, every project output (uint32_t) A: check after the cast to the one-byte OutputId - set 259 1 writes output 3, get 259 reads it. get also prints and reads when the check failed systems::SafeOffOutputTester refuses every number >= TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_OUTPUTS (and set of safe_off outputs). Upstream: package 13 pwm set, pwm setPeriod (bios::OutputPwmTester, libs/bsp/bspOutputPwm) yes, every project channel, duty, period (uint32_t) A in setPeriod: "wrong channel" is printed but OutputPwm::setPeriod() is still called with the channel narrowed to uint16_t (65536 + k is k). B in set: a missing/invalid duty writes duty 0 (pwm set 1 unmasks the complementary pair MOT1_U at 0 % - low side on), an invalid channel writes channel 0 (the static dummy channel here) systems::CheckedOutputPwmTester runs set/setPeriod only for a complete valid line and a channel in range (host test checked-pwm-tester). Effect of A in neXtBSW today: none (ComplementaryPwm::setPeriod() is BSP_NOT_SUPPORTED). Upstream: package 13 in get (bios::DigitalInputTester, libs/bsp/bspInputManager) yes, every project input (uint16_t) C only: scanned as uint16_t, so 65536 + n reads input n; checked and used as the same value, read only none (read only, no bypass) adc get <start> [<stop>] (bios::AnalogTester, platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspAdc) yes, every project channels (uint32_t) none: both numbers checked as uint32_t before the narrowing to uint16_t, checkEol() before acting none lc level <n> (lifecycle::LifecycleControlCommand, copy in ecu/consoleCommands) development build only (NX_PRODUCT_BUILD removes level) level (uint8_t) B: lc level, lc level x scan as 0 and run transitionToLevel(0) - the full lifecycle shut-down, which cancels the safety cycle and disables the MCU watchdog without the safe state (doc/safety/coexistence.md CX-2) - while the console answers "error". C: lc level 256 is level 0 open: fix in ecu/consoleCommands (not in the paths of a separate task) - context.checkEol() and a check of the scan result before the transition. Mentioned in the upstream issue logger level … (DefaultLoggerCommand, libs/bsw/logger) yes none (names) - none stats, safety … (StatisticsCommand, SafetyCommand, copies in ecu/consoleCommands) yes (safety not in the product build) none - none can send <id> <bytes> (CanCommand, executables/referenceApp/consoleCommands) no (neXtBSW has its own can command in CanSystem.cpp, which parses its tokens itself) id (uint32_t), bytes (uint8_t) B/C upstream: id not checked, bytes wrap at 256, invalid tokens send 0 none here; mentioned in the upstream issue phy get <reg> (Tja1101Tester, platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspTja1101) no register (uint8_t) C (read only) none here; mentioned upstream storage write/fill/read (StorageTester, libs/bsw/storage) no id, value (uint8_t), size B: an invalid id scans as 0 and is written none here; mentioned upstream

Not part of the audit but checked on the way, because the same scanner is used: the number arguments of the neXtBSW commands of the family port (gd, sbc, bcc read/write, sbc failstart, can log, dflash, i2c, hardfault) check the uint32_t value before any narrowing and end with checkEol() - no finding of class A or B. Two notes outside the family port: dem setting <0|1> (ecu/application/src/systems/RteSystem.cpp) scans uint8_t, so dem setting 256 switches the DTC setting off (class C); dem clear <group> passes the uint32_t on unchecked to DemMemory::clear() (which answers "no DTC" for an unknown group).

docs.title: Contribution to OpenBSW
docs.text: Prepared as package 13 in doc/openbsw-beitraege/13-console-tester-ranges (issue text, fix.patch against 3b6e702 for OutputTester.cpp and OutputPwmTester.cpp, PR text, tests); submission by the maintainer (decision 2026-09-17, F4). Once accepted upstream and the submodule is updated, SafeOffOutputTester keeps only its safe_off rule and CheckedOutputPwmTester can be removed.

docs.title: neXtBSW – closeness to OpenBSW: deviations for s32k1xx and the way back
docs.text:
Status: 2026-09-17, Analyse ohne Codeänderung (Nachweis: mock/analysis). Am 2026-10-04 auf Struktur-Vergleich, Abweichungsklassen und Ergebnis gekürzt: das zeilenweise Abweichungsinventar (R, P, T, C, S, E, L), die Momentaufnahme von OpenBSW main vom 2026-09-17, die Folgeaufgaben V1 bis V8, die Fragen F1 bis F8 und die Review-Fragen stehen in der Versionshistorie dieser Datei (Commit vor). Analysierter Stand: Repository c64fd78, Submodul external/openbsw 00e3cab.

Occasion: the maintainer's wish to stay close to OpenBSW instead of moving away from it. The result is the platform rule in README.md section 6 (P1 to P6, decision D15), which also governs the new platform rm4x.

docs.title: 0. Notation
docs.text:
• openbsw:<path> = file in the submodule, repo:<path> = file in this repository.
  • Classification of a deviation: (a) back to OpenBSW (neXtBSW version dropped), (b) extension in OpenBSW style (stays, at the place, with the name and interface OpenBSW would use), (c) submit upstream (bug fix or generally useful addition), (d) necessary and neXtBSW-specific (generator, RTE, configuration levels, board neutrality, bootloader).

docs.title: 1. How OpenBSW is structured, and how neXtBSW cuts it
docs.text:
Level OpenBSW (00e3cab) neXtBSW (c64fd78) MCU drivers of a family openbsw:platforms/<family>/{3rdparty,bsp,etlImpl,hardFaultHandler,safety,unitTest} used unchanged via repo:platforms/s32k1xx/CMakeLists.txt (wrapper + three derivative workarounds); own modules alongside in repo:platforms/s32k1xx/{bsp,hardFaultHandler,3rdparty,startup} Board port openbsw:executables/referenceApp/platforms/<board>/{Options.cmake,bspConfiguration,main,safety,freeRtosCoreConfiguration,threadXCoreConfiguration,ethConfiguration} family template repo:platforms/s32k1xx/port/{bspConfiguration,main,safety,freeRtosCoreConfiguration} + repo:ecu/platforms/<board>/Options.cmake Application openbsw:executables/referenceApp repo:ecu (derived, milestone 1) Neutral interfaces openbsw:libs/bsp/*, openbsw:libs/bsw/bsp additionally repo:libs/bsp/{bspSpi,bspAdcAccess} Services, device drivers openbsw:libs/bsw/* additionally repo:libs/bsw/* (10 modules) Across cores/profiles does not exist: every platform brings its own RTOS port and fault handler (freertos_cm4_sysTick and hardFaultHandler.s exist in s32k1xx and stm32, each as a copy of its own; stm32/hardFaultHandler came with PR #417). CMSIS lives in openbsw:libs/3rdparty/cmsis repo:platforms/common/{cmake,3rdparty/cmsis,3rdparty/freertosPort,interruptPriority,cortex-m,cortex-r,test} Entry point openbsw:CMakeLists.txt, OPENBSW_PLATFORM, BUILD_TARGET_PLATFORM repo:CMakeLists.txt with NX_PROJECT → nxconfig → OPENBSW_PLATFORM = NX_FAMILY Unit tests googletest, openbsw:executables/unitTest, platforms/<family>/unitTest own host tests (C++ + Python runner, tools/test), no googletest

docs.title: 2. Inventory of the deviations, by area
docs.text:
Figures from file comparisons: repo:platforms/s32k1xx/port against openbsw:executables/referenceApp/platforms/s32k148evb: 21 files identical, 38 changed, 57 new; repo:ecu against referenceApp: 33 identical, 11 changed, 38 new. Overrides of OpenBSW targets via CMake are few: bspMcu include directories, etl_profile before ETL, bspCore sources, -include for bspClock and bspInterruptsImpl, an alias for the FreeRTOS port.

Area Deviation Class Root CMake own top level: NX_PROJECT to nxconfig before project(), toolchain from the derivative, OPENBSW_PLATFORM = NX_FAMILY (fits an OpenBSW-layout rm4x), bswgen/rtegen/dbcgen at configure time d / b bspMcu include paths CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR wrong when OpenBSW is not the root project (same bug in platforms/stm32); derivative-neutral mcu.h c + b S32K116 workarounds pllOff() outside PLL_AVAILABLE, NVIC_GetActive on ARMv6-M, cache.cpp without LMEM c, then a Own MCU modules bspLpspi, bspHall, ARMv6-M FreeRTOS port freertos_cm0_sysTick (kept per family, not in common), startup template b Hard fault handler dump location from linker symbols (the fixed 0x2000EC00 is outside the S32K144 SRAM), SP check, FP frame, reader; printf before the jump destroys EXC_RETURN c, location b Safety (safeMemory, safeSystem, safeIo) MPU region count from mcudb (isGlobalEnabled() == 0x201, slot <= SMPU_ENTRYS bugs), ADC reference limits as configuration, role pins instead of board LEDs c, then a / d CAN several buses; Not related to OpenBSW: bootloader/ (D6), tools/, mcudb/, boards/, projects/, swc/.

docs.title: 3. Assessment of the moves to platforms/common
docs.text:
Yardstick: OpenBSW has no cross-family platform level. What several platforms need lives neutrally in libs/ (interfaces, CMSIS, FreeRTOS kernel) or is copied per platform (RTOS port, hardFaultHandler, etlImpl, safety/safeBspMcuWatchdog). An OpenBSW platform is self-contained: platforms/<family> plus libs suffices.

Move Compatible? Result Interrupt ranks by profile under platforms/common yes: no counterpart, bound to the generator keep CMSIS paths by profile, platform hook platforms/<family>/CMakeLists.txt yes: the hook corresponds to OPENBSW_PLATFORM keep FreeRTOS port selection in platforms/common/3rdparty/freertosPort partly: the switch may stay central; the ports themselves stay per family (s32k1xx/3rdparty/freertos_cm0_sysTick, rm4x/3rdparty/freertos_crx) keep the switch, remove the forwarding in s32k1xx FreeRtosAdcLock without core registers yes: contract in libs/bsp keep Hard fault handler to platforms/common no: OpenBSW keeps it per platform assembler handlers per family, only the architecture-neutral dump layout and reader neutral in libs/bsw/faultDump

Do not turn back platforms/common stays for neXtBSW's own parts without an OpenBSW counterpart; everything OpenBSW places per platform stays per family. The binding wording is README section 6 (P1 to P6).

docs.title: 4. State of OpenBSW main and consequences
docs.text: On 2026-09-17 (20 commits since 00e3cab, no release) none of the gaps neXtBSW fills was closed upstream (mpu.h, getBusOffState(), isr_sys.cpp with printf, SystemTimer::updateTicks, clockConfig.cpp, SafeSystem.cpp, startUp.S without .FlashConfig; no S32K144/S32K116, no LPSPI, no ADC contract). Upstream removed the platform library; the submodule was updated to 3b6e702 and all own occurrences replaced (clean-up). Contributions need the Eclipse Contributor Agreement; the maintainer submits them himself. Order of the planned contribution packages, by benefit and effort: MPU regions, FLTCONF, hard fault (printf, fixed location), DWT remainder, CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR, SPLL/ NVIC_GetActive/LMEM, ADC reference limits, .FlashConfig, core_cm0plus.h, monitor context; later derivative-neutral mcu.h, stm32 changes and the SPI/ADC contracts (D9). After acceptance upstream the workaround or copy is deleted (class a).

docs.title: neXtBSW and Eclipse OpenBSW
docs.text:
Status: 2026-09-17, checked against the repository at this commit and against the submodule pointer external/openbsw = 3b6e702.

Eclipse OpenBSW is a project of the Eclipse Foundation, not of neXtBSW. This page describes how neXtBSW uses it. Nothing here is a statement by, about or on behalf of the OpenBSW project, and neXtBSW makes no claim of being endorsed by, certified against or compatible with any particular OpenBSW release. Names and marks belong to their owners.

Binding target picture: README.md, section 2 (what OpenBSW delivers and which gaps neXtBSW closes), section 6 (the platform rule P1–P6) and decision D9. The stocktaking of every place where neXtBSW deviates today is openbsw-naehe.md — this page is the reading version of both.

docs.title: 1. Why OpenBSW at all
docs.text:
OpenBSW brings a working, hardware-near basic software in C++17 with FreeRTOS, reference ports for two MCU families, and middleware that is genuinely hardware independent. That is the expensive half of a BSW and neXtBSW has no reason to write it again. What OpenBSW does not bring is a configuration model: every value lives in a hand-written header, and integrating a board means copying main.cpp, StaticBsp, the CAN system, the ISRs, the linker script and the start-up file. That copying is exactly what neXtBSW replaces.

So the division of labour is: OpenBSW supplies drivers, middleware and structure; neXtBSW supplies the contracts, the configuration model, the generators and everything above them.

docs.title: 2. What neXtBSW takes
docs.text:
Used unchanged from the submodule (external/openbsw, added in CMakeLists.txt:397-408):

Area What Where MCU platforms s32k1xx (reference S32K148-EVB), stm32 (F413ZH bxCAN, G474RE FDCAN), posix external/openbsw/platforms/ RTOS integration FreeRTOS ports, async, lifecycle external/openbsw/platforms/<family>/3rdparty, libs/bsw/async, libs/bsw/lifecycle CAN stack cpp2can (ICanTransceiver, CanPhy), docan (ISO-TP), transport external/openbsw/libs/bsw/ Diagnostics uds — sessions, services, DiagJob, routing external/openbsw/libs/bsw/uds, used by ecu/uds Infrastructure logger, console, time, util, storage, ETL profile, safety libraries external/openbsw/libs/ BSP interfaces CanPhy, SystemTimer, IFlashDriver, IEepromDriver, IEcuPowerStateController, UartConcept, DigitalInput/Output/OutputPwm, charInputOutput external/openbsw/libs/bsp/

The application ecu/ itself started as a copy of executables/referenceApp — OpenBSW intends the reference app to be copied — with Ethernet/lwIP, SOME/IP, DoIP, ThreadX, Rust and the middleware demo left out.

docs.title: 3. What neXtBSW adds, and why
docs.text:
The gaps in OpenBSW and what neXtBSW adds for each (no neutral SPI/ADC contract, no device drivers above the MCU, no configuration description or generators, integration copied per board, no RTE, no bootloader, priorities written as numbers) are the table in README.md section 2; the places in the repository are libs/bsp/bspSpi, libs/bsp/bspAdcAccess, libs/bsw/*, mcudb/, boards/, projects/, tools/{nxconfig,bswgen,rtegen,dbcgen}, bootloader/ and platforms/common/{interruptPriority,cortex-m,cortex-r}.

The deliberate choice: the generated headers carry the OpenBSW file names (bsp/io/io/ioConfiguration.h, bsp/clock/boardClock.h, bsp/can/canBitTimingConfiguration.h and around thirty more), so the OpenBSW drivers that include them stay untouched. neXtBSW changes where the values come from, not who reads them.

docs.title: 4. How the submodule is embedded — and why it stays unchanged
docs.text:
.gitmodules points external/openbsw at https://github.com/eclipse-openbsw/openbsw.git; the checked-out pointer is 3b6e70210034b243dfc26d8d8c253f3be5ee382d.

The embedding is deliberately shallow:

  1. The repository root is its own top-level CMake project. CMakeLists.txt:118 sets OPENBSW_PLATFORM to the family that nxconfig derived from the project, which is the same hook OpenBSW itself uses.
  2. CMakeLists.txt:102-110 prefers platforms/<family>/CMakeLists.txt when it exists and falls back to external/openbsw/platforms/<family> otherwise. For s32k1xx, the own file does add_subdirectory("${OPENBSW_DIR}/platforms/s32k1xx" openbsw/platforms/s32k1xx …) — the OpenBSW platform is used as-is and into the same binary directory, so an existing build sees no difference.
  3. OpenBSW's libs are added wholesale (CMakeLists.txt:408), with EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL: modules are offers, and only what a target links gets built.
  4. Only a handful of OpenBSW targets are touched from outside, all of them listed in openbsw-naehe.md section 2: bspMcu include directories (CMakeLists.txt:419-439, because OpenBSW resolves CMSIS through CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR, which is wrong as soon as OpenBSW is a subproject), the ETL profile ordering (CMakeLists.txt:441), the FreeRTOS port supplied under OpenBSW's expected target name (add_library(freeRtosPort ALIAS nxFreeRtosPort), platforms/common/3rdparty/freertosPort), and the three derivative workarounds in section 6 below.

The submodule is never edited. This is a project rule ("Das Submodul external/openbsw wird nie geändert") and decision D9 in README.md section 10: submodule unchanged, neutral contracts offered upstream later, no fork. The practical reasons:

  • A fork would have to be maintained against every upstream change, and the changes neXtBSW wants are mostly bug fixes that belong upstream anyway.
  • Everything neXtBSW needs can be reached without editing: a generated header under the OpenBSW name, a forced include, a replaced source file, an overridden include path — each visible in one CMake file rather than buried in a diff against a third-party tree.
  • Licensing: ecu/ contains files derived from OpenBSW under Apache-2.0 with the copyright headers preserved (README.md, "Lizenzen"). Keeping the origin clean matters for the planned open-source release (lizenz-und-release.md (not published, available on request)).

Because copies do drift, the copies are tracked rather than trusted: tools/openbswsync with tools/openbswsync/copies.yaml records for every copied file whether it is identical, modified (with a task ID and a reason, both mandatory) or new, plus a hash of the upstream original. Today the list covers two roots — ecu/ against executables/referenceApp (34 identical, 11 modified, 9 new) and platforms/s32k1xx/port against executables/referenceApp/platforms/s32k148evb (21 identical, 39 modified, 7 new). A submodule update that changes an original turns the check red until the change has been reviewed and accepted (python -m tools.openbswsync check / report / accept <path>).

docs.title: 5. The platform rule: staying close on purpose
docs.text:
Until 2026-09-17 neXtBSW was drifting: family-independent things were collected under platforms/common, which OpenBSW does not have at all. The maintainer decided to stay close instead, and the rule is now binding (README.md section 6, P1–P6, decision D15):

  • P1/P2 — every family is an OpenBSW platform: platforms/<family> has the shape of external/openbsw/platforms/{s32k1xx,stm32} and, together with libs/, is self-contained. Duplication between families is accepted; OpenBSW duplicates too (freertos_cm4_sysTick and hardFaultHandler.s exist once per platform there).
  • P3 — platforms/common may only hold parts for which OpenBSW has no counterpart, tested per directory without judgement calls; every exception needs an entry in the P4 list.
  • P5 — the hand-written family port belongs on application level, ecu/platforms/<family>, mirroring referenceApp/platforms/<board>.

Today's state against that rule: platforms/common still contains cmake, 3rdparty, cortex-m, cortex-r, interruptPriority and test, each covered by a P4 entry; the family port is still at platforms/s32k1xx/port (the move is a separate task, open); platforms/rm4x contains only 3rdparty/freertos_crx, which is already at the right place. The rule applies to every new file from now on even where the existing state does not yet match.

docs.title: 6. Own workarounds for OpenBSW defects — and when they go
docs.text:
Each of these is a finding for OpenBSW, not a design decision, and each is meant to disappear once the fix is upstream. They are switched by a derivative fact, never by a board name, and are no-ops on the S32K14x the reference port covers.

In platforms/s32k1xx/CMakeLists.txt (its own comment says exactly this):

# Problem Workaround Goes away when 1 bspCore/src/cache/cache.cpp writes LMEM->PCCCR; a derivative without that cache (S32K11x) has no LMEM block, so the file does not compile the translation unit is replaced by bsp/bspCore/src/cache/cacheUnavailable.cpp when lmem_cache is not in NX_FEATURES the driver is guarded upstream 2 bspClock/src/clockConfig.cpp: pllOff() calls isSpllSysClk()/spllStop() outside the PLL_AVAILABLE guard, so a derivative without SPLL does not compile forced include bsp/bspClock/include/clock/nxSpllUnavailable.h, plus -Wno-unused-function for that one translation unit the guard is fixed upstream 3 bspInterruptsImpl: SYS_GetActive() forwards to NVIC_GetActive(), which ARMv6-M does not have forced include bsp/bspInterruptsImpl/include/interrupts/nxNvicGetActiveUnavailable.h on armv6m ARMv6-M is handled upstream

In the family port, each a corrected copy of an OpenBSW file:

Where Problem upstream neXtBSW today platforms/s32k1xx/port/safety/safeMemory/include/safeMemory/mpu.h 16 regions hard-coded, isGlobalEnabled() compares the whole CESR against 0x201, slot <= reaches one region too far (caused a BusFault on the S32K144, Milestone 1) region count from the generated NX_MPU_REGIONS, static_assert that the generated NRGD code matches, slot < platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/systems/CanSystem.* FlexCANDevice::getBusOffState() applies the setter macro FLEXCAN_ESR1_FLTCONF to ESR1, so the bus reads as permanently bus-off BusStateTransceiver derives the state itself; multi-bus support is neXtBSW's own and stays platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/os/isr/isr_sys.cpp HardFault_Handler calls printf before branching, which destroys EXC_RETURN in LR and moves MSP __attribute__((naked)) with a bare branch to customHardFaultHandler platforms/s32k1xx/hardFaultHandler dump address hard-coded as .equ 0x2000EC00, outside the S32K144's SRAM dump location from linker symbols, stack-pointer check, FP frame, reader after reset platforms/s32k1xx/port/safety/safeSystem/src/safeSystem/SafeSystem.cpp ADC reference fixed at 4800–5200 mV; the eval board's LM4132 delivers 4096 mV VREFH_NOMINAL_MV from the project's configuration platforms/s32k1xx/port/bspConfiguration/src/bsp/SystemTimer/SystemTimer.cpp updateTicks discards the division remainder of the DWT conversion (measured −166 ppm at the board) remainder kept, clock switch without losing time platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/bsp/startUp.S no .FlashConfig section at 0x400; in erased flash that means FSEC = secured section filled with the NXP default values

Two things follow. First, every one of these rows is a reason to contribute rather than to fork. Second, until the fix lands upstream these files are copies that can drift — which is what tools/openbswsync watches.

docs.title: 7. How work flows back
docs.text:
Status: planned (after R1); nothing has been submitted upstream yet. Decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-17 (F4): contributors prepare, the maintainer submits, because contributions need the Eclipse Contributor Agreement signed with the same e-mail address that Git uses. The prepared packages (issue.md in the OpenBSW bug-report template, a minimal fix.patch against upstream main, pr.md, tests.md with the counter-check, einreichen.md) live in doc/openbsw-beitraege/, one folder per package. The first five:

Package Subject 01-mpu-region-count region count per derivative, isGlobalEnabled() on CESR[VLD] only, slot < 02-flexcan-bus-state bus state and error counters by field extraction instead of the setter macro 03-hard-fault-handler printf removed before the branch (naked), dump location from __NOINIT_DATA 04-cmsis-include-path bspMcu CMSIS path no longer through CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR 05-mismatched-tag DiagnosisConfiguration forward-declared as struct (-Wmismatched-tags)

Further packages (DWT remainder, SPLL / NVIC_GetActive / LMEM, configurable ADC reference, .FlashConfig, core_cm0plus.h, monitor context, SPI and ADC contracts) and the S32K116 offer (subject to the licence review) follow the same pattern. Once a package is accepted upstream, the workaround or copy is deleted and the OpenBSW file used unchanged, with a byte comparison of the eval-board image or a justified difference (openbsw-naehe.md section 4).

docs.title: 8. Open points
docs.text:
• The submodule pointer is 3b6e702, while openbsw-naehe.md still describes the state at 00e3cab. Its comparison counts and its "upstream unchanged" checks date from 2026-09-17 against main and should be re-read as historical rather than current.
  • ThreadX and Ethernet/lwIP were left out of ecu/. The maintainer decided (F7) that the way back stays open with at least one build test per option in CI; that task is open, so today the path is untested.
  • platforms/rm4x exists as a directory but is not yet a platform in the sense of P1: only the FreeRTOS CRx port is there. Its acceptance criterion is that OpenBSW's own referenceApp/unitTest builds for RM46.

docs.title: neXtBSW architecture overview
docs.text:
Status: 2026-09-17. Written against the repository, not against intentions: every statement below names the file it can be checked against, and where the code does not yet match the target picture this document says so.

This is the reading version, not a second target picture. The binding document is doc/architecture/README.md — it holds the decision table D1–D15, the responsibility-per-value table and the review questions that every change has to answer. This page explains the shape of the system to someone who has to work with it; when the two disagree, the target picture wins and the difference is a finding, not a variant.

Companion pages: openbsw.md (relationship to Eclipse OpenBSW) and autosar.md (what of AUTOSAR is actually here). Analysis documents that stand behind this one: openbsw-naehe.md, plattformen.md, treiber-granularitaet.md.

docs.title: 1. The one idea
docs.text:
A neXtBSW build has exactly one input the maintainer picks: a project. Everything else — board, derivative, MCU family, core, toolchain flags, clock tree, pin multiplexing, CAN bit timing, task list, memory layout — is read out of configuration files and either derived or generated from them. CMakeLists.txt:21-52 runs tools/nxconfig before project(), because the toolchain itself depends on the answer.

That is the difference to the starting point. Eclipse OpenBSW is a working basic software with hand-integrated reference boards; neXtBSW keeps its drivers and middleware and replaces the hand integration with a configuration model plus generators. What that means in detail is in openbsw.md.

docs.title: 2. Layers
docs.text:
The layer model is defined in README.md section 3. Condensed, with the place in the repository:

Layer Content Where L5 application software components, today Simulink models exported as AUTOSAR Classic SWC swc/<Swc>/, projects/<p>/swc/<Swc>/ L4 RTE generated: ports, runnables, tasks, data consistency, CAN signal qualifiers tools/rtegen → <build>/generated/rte L3 ECU services CAN system, ECU state, diagnostics on CAN, console, safety supervisor libs/bsw/canSystem, libs/bsw/ecuState, ecu/uds, ecu/consoleCommands, OpenBSW middleware L2 device drivers drivers for parts on the board, host-tested, no board names libs/bsw/<module> (10 modules today) L1 MCU abstraction neutral contracts and their per-family implementation libs/bsp/<class>, platforms/<family>/bsp, external/openbsw/libs/bsp L0 hardware derivative plus board described, not coded: mcudb/, boards/

Two rules carry most of the weight and are worth repeating here:

  • Dependencies only point downwards, and no layer knows a board. Board knowledge lives in configuration data and in the code generated from it.
  • Services ask for roles (can_phy, power_supply, watchdog_trigger, early_init), not for part names. Which part fills a role is a board statement. See the manifests libs/bsw/*/module.yaml.

Not in the layer stack, on purpose: the bootloader (bootloader/) is plain C without OpenBSW, with its own HAL per family, and it reads the same memory layout as the application (decision D6, bootloader/doc/README.md).

docs.title: 3. The three configuration levels
docs.text:
Every value is written down exactly once, at the level that owns it. The levels and the full responsibility-per-value table are README.md section 4; this is the short version with the files.

Level File Owns Example Derivative mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml plus <derivative>_<package>.pinmux.yaml manufacturer facts, read-only flash and RAM regions, sector sizes, peripheral instances, possible pin functions, ADC resolution, core and FPU, NVIC priority bits Board boards/<board>/board.yaml what is fitted and wired on the PCB derivative and package, crystal frequency, pin assignment, fitted parts and how they are connected, dividers, sensor circuits in front of ADC pins, debug probe Project projects/<project>/project.yaml plus rte.yaml and *.dbc what this ECU software uses which peripherals are used, system clock, PWM frequency and dead time, bit rates, CAN IDs, UDS addresses, tasks, components and connections, memory split Workstation not checked in belongs to the PC toolchain path (NX_ARM_GCC_BIN), CAN adapter, serial port, debugger serial number

Derivatives present today: mcudb/s32k1xx (S32K116/142/144/146/148 with package pinmux tables), mcudb/stm32 (STM32F446RE, STM32G474RE), mcudb/s32k3xx (S32K344). Boards: boards/{evalboard_s32k144, s32k116evb, nucleo_f446re, buildtest_s32k148}. Projects: projects/{evalboard_s32k144_demo, evalboard_s32k144_charge, s32k116evb_minimal, nucleo_f446re_demo, buildtest_s32k148_min}.

Fact and decision are separated even inside one value. The peripheral clock is the pattern: which sources a clock gate offers and how fast its output may run is a datasheet fact and lives in the derivative; which source is used is a project decision. The derivative may name a default that applies until the project chooses. Without evidence for a default there is none, and a used instance without a project choice is an error with file, line and YAML path — never a guessed value (README.md section 4).

Two projects on one board are the proof that the split works: evalboard_s32k144_demo drives FTM0 as the motor PWM group, evalboard_s32k144_charge uses the same FTM0 for input capture, and the board profile is byte-identical for both (projects/README.md).

tools/nxconfig loads project → board → derivative, validates across the levels and reports every message with file, line and YAML path (tools/nxconfig/checks.py for cross-level checks, clock.py, memory.py, adc.py, sensor.py, powerstage.py, timing.py, can.py, uart.py, diag.py for the computed parts). The core carries no Qt, so the command line, the generators and the Studio all use the same loader.

docs.title: 4. What a generator writes and what a human writes
docs.text:
Generated (into <build>/generated/, never checked in, never edited by hand):

Generator Produces Into tools/nxconfig (cmake command) NX_BOARD, NX_DERIVATIVE, NX_FAMILY, NX_CORE, core options, tool paths generated/nxconfig/project.cmake tools/bswgen the board headers under the names OpenBSW already includes: bsp/io/io/ioConfiguration.h, bsp/io/input/inputConfiguration.h, bsp/io/output/outputConfiguration.h, bsp/clock/boardClock.h, bsp/clock/peripheralClocks.h, bsp/can/canBitTimingConfiguration.h, bsp/adc/analogSensorConfiguration.h, bsp/io/outputPwm/outputPwmConfiguration.h, interrupts/interruptPriorities.h, features/derivativeFeatures.h, mcu/mcuDerivative.h, startup/nxIrqVectors.inc and about twenty more (list in tools/bswgen/bswgen.py, files) generated/board/ tools/bswgen/blgen.py memory layout and the bootloader's board part: bootloader/bl_memory.h, bootloader/bl_memory.ld, memory/memoryLayout.h, plus bootloader/bl_board.h and bl_board.cmake when bootloader/ is configured generated/board/ tools/rtegen Rte_Type.h, Rte_<Swc>.h, Rte.c, RteConfig.h/.cpp, RteTasks.h, Rte_Qlf.h/.m, tasks/async/Config.h, EcuStateConfig.h generated/rte/ tools/dbcgen CanDb.h/.c: pack and unpack of the used CAN messages, called from rtegen generated/rte/

Generated and checked in, because the tool that makes it is not free: the C code and ARXML of a software component, swc/<Swc>/generated/{src,arxml} from tools/swc/swc_build.m under MATLAB. A hash of the model (generated/model.sha256) is compared at configure time, so a stale check-in is reported.

Hand-written today, although the target picture wants it generated:

  • The family port, platforms/s32k1xx/port/{main,bspConfiguration,safety,freeRtosCoreConfiguration} — start-up, linker script template, StaticBsp, BspSystem, the systems, the ISR table. Since an earlier change it carries no board name and no derivative value, but it is still written rather than generated.
  • The module composition, platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/integration/Integration.cpp. Its own header comment says it plainly: wiring and values come from configuration, the composition per module is still written by hand.
  • The board port, ecu/platforms/<board>/Options.cmake — the feature switches. This is the only place left that carries a board name in code; it disappears when the switches move into the project.

The generator that the target picture calls intgen (main, lifecycle order, ISR table, role wiring, task list; README.md sections 4 and 5) does not exist yet — tools/ has nxconfig, bswgen with blgen, rtegen, dbcgen, and no intgen and no a2lgen. Likewise, module.yaml manifests exist for 11 modules (libs/bsp/bspAdcAccess, libs/bsw/{canPhyPassive,canSystem,ecuState,gdTmc6200,hallDecoder,highSideSwitch, sbcUja113x} and three under the family port), not yet for every module — libs/bsw/e2e, libs/bsw/autosarBase, libs/bsw/bccMc33771 and libs/bsp/bspSpi have none.

The governing principle stays: what is generated is wiring, not logic. Logic lives in modules with host tests.

docs.title: 6. Build sequence
docs.text:
cmake --preset <project> (presets in CMakePresets.json; without one, -DNX_PROJECT=projects/<p>). In order, from CMakeLists.txt:

  1. Before project() — tools/nxconfig cmake <project> writes generated/nxconfig/project.cmake. Configuration errors abort here with FATAL_ERROR (line 43). The file sets NX_FAMILY, NX_DERIVATIVE, NX_BOARD, NX_CORE, NX_CORE_ARCHITECTURE, NX_MCPU, NX_MFLOAT_ABI, NX_MFPU, the debug probe and the flash tools.
  2. Platform of the family (lines 102-110): if platforms/<family>/CMakeLists.txt exists it is used, otherwise external/openbsw/platforms/<family>. OPENBSW_PLATFORM is set to NX_FAMILY (line 118).
  3. Family port must exist at platforms/<family>/port/CMakeLists.txt, else abort (lines 112-117).
  4. Board options: include(${ECU_PLATFORM_DIR}/Options.cmake) — the feature switches, and a consistency check that the board port does not claim another family (lines 120-124).
  5. project() with the toolchain file cmake/toolchains/NxArmNoneEabi-gcc.cmake, one file for all cores.
  6. Generators at configure time, so every OpenBSW library finds the headers before the first compile: bswgen → generated/board (line 152), then rtegen (which calls dbcgen) → generated/rte (line 185). blgen runs when bootloader/ is configured.
  7. Subdirectories: family platform, OpenBSW libs, the FreeRTOS port chosen by architecture (platforms/common/3rdparty/freertosPort), the neXtBSW modules the project selected, ecu, ecu/uds, bootloader.

Build with cmake --build --preset <project>; the target build is warning-free with -Werror. Host tests and target builds together: .venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group all (list in tools/test/tests.yaml).

docs.title: 7. Start-up sequence on the device
docs.text:
After reset the bootloader runs first (bootloader/src/core/bl_main.c): it checks the validity record, the CRC over the whole image and the plausibility of the application entry, waits 200 ms for a 10 02 request, and otherwise jumps into the application. The parameter of the jump is the application entry, not a vector table — what stands there is a family decision (bootloader/doc/README.md; Cortex-M sets VTOR, Cortex-R has no VTOR and uses a fixed forwarding table, decision D12).

In the application, platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/main.cpp:

  1. integration::earlyInit() — the early_init role of the project's modules (for example the SBC reset counter compensation).
  2. safety::MemoryProtection::init(), then the safety shell: supervisor into limp home, MCU watchdog fast test (deliberately causes two resets), watchdog enabled.
  3. integration::preBspInit(), then platform::staticBsp.init().
  4. hardfault::reportAndClearDump() — reports a hard fault from before the last reset, once.
  5. app_main() (ecu/application/src/main.cpp) → app::run() (ecu/application/src/app/app.cpp): console UART up, then FreeRTOS starts and startApp() runs.

startApp() fills the lifecycle manager and transitions through the levels (ecu/application/src/app/app.cpp:176-215):

Level Components 1 platform modules (platformLifecycleAdd), runtime, safety, ecu state management 2 platform modules of level 2 (CAN) 3 uds — diagnostics on CAN, in the CAN task, only with PLATFORM_SUPPORT_UDS 8 sysadmin 9 rte — runnables in the application tasks

Nine levels total (MaxNumLevels = 9). The RTE is deliberately last: application code starts only after the basic software is up.

docs.title: 8. Where today differs from the target picture
docs.text: The full list of 31 board couplings with target location and task ID is README.md section 9. What shapes the repository right now: the composition in the family port is hand-written (values inside it are generated); the family port still sits at platforms/s32k1xx/port instead of ecu/platforms/<family> (rule P5); platforms/common still holds items that rule P3 sends elsewhere, each with an entry in the P4 list; and not every module has a manifest or a contract suite that each family implementation must pass. None of this is a variant of the architecture; all of it is work in the task list.
