docs.title: Your own ECU repository
docs.text:
A production ECU project lives in a repository of its own and references neXtBSW at a fixed version. The route, from an empty folder to a built image:

%%{init: {'theme':'base','flowchart':{'curve':'basis'},'themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif','fontSize':'14px','background':'#ffffff','primaryColor':'#ffffff','primaryBorderColor':'#64748b','primaryTextColor':'#0f172a','lineColor':'#475569','edgeLabelBackground':'#ffffff','tertiaryColor':'#f8fafc','clusterBkg':'#f8fafc','clusterBorder':'#cbd5e1'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    S1("1 repository + pin") --> S2("2 .venv") --> S3("3 board.yaml") --> S4("4 project.yaml")
    S4 --> S5("5 check, generate, build") --> S6("6 tests + CI") --> S7("7 git") --> S8("8 update")
    S8 -. next release .-> S1
Step You do Command 1 repository, submodule, pin file git submodule add, nextbsw.yaml 2 the workspace's own Python environment python nextbsw/tools/setup venv . 3 your board nxconfig board new 4 your project nxconfig new, nxconfig check 5 build cmake --preset main, cmake --build --preset main 6 tests and CI tools/test --workspace ., tools/ci run --workspace . 7 what goes into git .gitignore, the Studio's git page 8 a newer neXtBSW tools/nxupdate

Why a pin and not a copy, which variants were weighed: ../architecture/customer-project.md. This page only says what to do. If you have never built anything with neXtBSW, do Getting started first; everything below assumes that worked.

Term What it is neXtBSW tree one checked-out or unpacked neXtBSW release: the folder with VERSION and tools/ Workspace your repository: the folder with the pin file nextbsw.yaml. One workspace, one tree Pin the reference to exactly one neXtBSW version: nextbsw.yaml plus the submodule's commit

The rule the design rests on: your repository contains only what your ECU decides (projects, boards, components, modules, tests and one pin). Nothing of neXtBSW is copied into it and nothing generated is checked in.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Tool Version used here Notes git any recent one with submodule support Python 3.12 the workspace gets its own .venv; tools/ci/.python-version names the pinned one CMake 4.4.3 (3.28 minimum) preset schema version 6 Ninja 1.13.2 arm-none-eabi-gcc 11.3.1 (xPack, tools/ci/versions.toml) on PATH or NX_ARM_GCC_BIN (workstation setting, never checked in); python -m tools.ci setup fetches it

docs.title: Where the repository may live: the Windows path limit
docs.text:
Windows refuses paths over 260 characters, and the object files of a target build are the longest paths in the system (measured):

Quantity Value longest object path of a workspace target build 247 of 260 characters of that: build directory / below it 55 / 192 characters limit for the build directory 67 characters (about 56 for the workspace root with build/<preset>)

So keep the repository folder short and near a drive root (C:/acme-bcm), keep the preset name short (main), or point the build elsewhere: the Studio setting Build-Wurzel (NX_STUDIO_BUILD_ROOT) or cmake --preset <p> -B <short dir>. The Studio warns when a build directory grows past 67 characters. The submodule folder name does not show up in object paths (CMake hashes them), only in the roomier source paths.

docs.title: Step 1: the repository and the pin
docs.text: A workspace stands on a release tag (v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH> on master; this page uses v0.2.0).

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
mkdir acme && cd acme
git init -b main
git submodule add <url of the neXtBSW repository> nextbsw
git -C nextbsw checkout v0.2.0
git add nextbsw
git submodule update --init --recursive

The order matters. git submodule update puts the submodule back on the staged commit; run it before git add nextbsw and the tag checkout is silently undone. --recursive matters too: OpenBSW is a nested submodule (external/openbsw), and without it the build stops with missing sources. Without access to GitHub, point git at a mirror with git -c url.<mirror>.insteadOf=https://github.com/eclipse-openbsw/openbsw.git …. With a local clone as URL, Git 2.38.1 and newer want -c protocol.file.allow=always.

Then write the pin file nextbsw.yaml in the repository root:

schema_version: 1
nextbsw:
  version: 0.2.0                 # must equal the tree's VERSION file
  source: submodule              # submodule | archive
  path: nextbsw                  # the tree, relative to this file
  profile: open                  # open | licensed | nda
search:                          # your own extensions, searched BEFORE the tree's own folders
  boards: [boards]               # <dir>/<board>/board.yaml
  # mcudb:   [mcudb]             # only if a derivative is missing
  # modules: [libs]              # your own drivers and services

A search path that does not exist is an error, on purpose, so a typo does not silently disable your boards; unknown keys are errors too. Check the pin (this needs the environment of step 2):

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig version .
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig pin --release .

version shows tree, git describe, workspace and pin. pin checks that the pin is a release (annotated tag v<version>, reachable from master, tree clean); --release makes a development pin an error instead of a warning, which is what a customer release uses. If pin and tree disagree you are told which is which (pins neXtBSW 0.1.0, but the tree nextbsw is 0.2.0).

Every tool finds the workspace the way git finds .git: it walks up from the project.yaml you named and stops at the first folder with nextbsw.yaml, at a neXtBSW tree root, or at a git root. No pin means "the tree I am running from".

docs.title: In the Studio
docs.text:
The wizard Neues Projekt, first step Ablage, offers "Eigenes Repository mit fester neXtBSW-Version": folder, version to pin, submodule source or release archive with checksum, CI template, first commit, and the workspace's own .venv. Nothing is written before „Anlegen"; the summary names every file, git step and warning, and the pin is written last and checked at once. The wizard needs an empty or not-yet-existing folder; a further project of an existing workspace follows step 4. The command line equivalent:

python tools/studio new-workspace --releases                                                # which tags exist
python tools/studio new-workspace C:/ECU/acme-bcm acme_main --board acme_ctl_b1 --tag v0.2.0

--development pins a development commit, --copy <project> starts from a copy, --archive <file> [--sha256 <hash>] uses the archive variant.

docs.title: The archive variant
docs.text:
Without access to a git server, use source: archive with url and sha256 and unpack the release to the same path; the tools only read path and version:

nextbsw:
  version: 0.2.0
  source: archive
  path: nextbsw
  url: https://files.example.invalid/nextbsw-0.2.0.zip   # where the delivery is kept
  sha256: e53f4fde7fe3b0c864c9bef0c414de46cdc5c975d5bd8ec921dae335e77f90e1

nextbsw/ is then a plain folder in .gitignore, never a submodule. Another workstation or the CI receives the pin but not the tree and rebuilds it from the same archive, checked against the pinned checksum:

python tools/studio restore-archive <repository> <archive>

A wrong checksum, an archive without a neXtBSW tree, an unsafe member (absolute path, .., link) or a non-empty target are refused before anything is written. A delivered archive has to contain external/openbsw (a plain git archive does not). Without the Studio, compare certutil -hashfile <archive> SHA256 (or sha256sum) with the pin and unpack to nextbsw/.

docs.title: Step 2: the Python environment
docs.text:
The generators, the configuration check and the build run with the workspace's own .venv, built from the requirements of exactly the pinned tree:

python nextbsw/tools/setup venv .

It runs with any Python 3.12 (standard library only; py -3.12 … on Windows) and finds the workspace by walking up. The core list (generators, nxconfig, host tests, CI) is free of Qt; --studio adds PySide6 and the Studio test tools. python nextbsw/tools/setup check . only reports.

A second run changes nothing (Nichts zu tun). The environment carries a marker (.venv/nextbsw-venv.json) with a hash over requirements, constraints and Python version; after you move the pin the hash no longer fits, and setup check (exit 1, with the repair command), tools.ci check and the Studio's Werkzeuge page say so.

docs.title: Step 3: your board
docs.text:
Your boards are ordinary board.yaml files, found through search.boards; same schema, same checks as the boards of the tree.

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig board new acme_ctl_b1 --root . \
    --mcu S32K146 --package LQFP100 --supply-v 5.0 --sosc-hz 8000000 \
    --debug-interface SWD --debug-probe "J-Link" --adc-reference-mv 5000 \
    --can body=FlexCAN0 --can chassis=FlexCAN1 --uart console=LPUART1 \
    --adc vbat=ADC0:SE8:PTC0 --out safe_en=PTD15:high --out fault=PTD16:high \
    --in wake=PTC12:low --no-port --dry-run

--root . puts board (and optional port) into your repository; drop --dry-run to write, the command then also runs the checks (here two warnings: no CAN transceiver phy described, treated as passive). While choosing pins: nxconfig board list --mcu S32K146 --package LQFP100 [--function FlexCAN0_RX]. Channel names are those of the pin multiplexing table (ADC0:SE8, not ADC0:CH8). In the Studio the wizard Neues Board anlegen asks signal by signal and offers only the pins that can carry the function.

Bus, UART, input, output and PWM names are free to choose after the nets of your schematic (body, chassis, console). What goes into a board.yaml is Your first board. If your MCU is not in mcudb/, Adding a derivative applies: put the file under mcudb/<family>/ of your repository and add mcudb: [mcudb] to search.

docs.title: Step 4: your project
docs.text:
A project is a project.yaml plus rte.yaml (and diag.yaml if the ECU answers diagnostics) below projects/<name>/; project.board is relative to project.yaml:

project:
  name: acme_main
  board: ../../boards/acme_ctl_b1
  rte: rte.yaml

Start an empty project on a board or a copy of an example (paths rewritten for you), from the workspace root. nxconfig new offers the boards of search.boards before those of the tree:

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig new --list
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig new acme_main --board acme_ctl_b1
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig new acme_main --copy buildtest_s32k148_min --dir projects/acme_main

A copy still points at the example's board (../../nextbsw/boards/<board>) and keeps its diagnostic addresses, CAN and XCP ids; change project.board to your own board and the ids if both ECUs share a bus. Then let nxconfig check name every reference that does not fit, with file, line and YAML path:

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig check projects/acme_main/project.yaml

project.yaml:135 (safety.locked_pin): error: 'LED2' must be a digital output used by the project
project.yaml:109 (interrupts.ranks[2].name): error: board acme_ctl_b1 has no uart entry UART (available: console)

Work the list from the top: the bus and UART names of the source (CAN0, CAN1, UART) become your names everywhere (bootloader.can, xcp.bus, can:, uart:, interrupts.ranks), and safety.safe_state_output, safety.locked_pin, safety.test_pin name outputs and pins of your board. When the list is empty you get acme_main: ok (board acme_ctl_b1, S32K146, 2 warning(s)). A warning is the tool refusing to pretend something is confirmed. Messages in detail: Your first board.

Connections in rte.yaml that name board signals are checked by rtegen at configure, not by nxconfig check (BUTTON1 is not a dio.in signal used by the project). Connecting a component port to the output that safety.safe_state_output names is a justified safety warning at configure: the pin floats in the safe state and comes back on without an enable (AoU-30). Choose an output the application does not write, or, for a display such as an LED, confirm it with safety.safe_state_output_shared_with_application: "<reason>".

What belongs in the two files: Your first board and The application.

docs.title: Step 5: check, generate, build
docs.text:
A CMake preset is resolved relative to the preset file, so the workspace root needs a CMakeLists.txt next to its CMakePresets.json. Both are templates in the tree, copied once with their placeholders replaced:

Template Copy to Replace nextbsw/cmake/workspace/CMakeLists.txt.in CMakeLists.txt @NX_TREE@ → nextbsw nextbsw/cmake/workspace/CMakePresets.json.in CMakePresets.json @NX_TREE@ → nextbsw, @NX_PRESET@ → main, @NX_PROJECT_DIR@ → acme_main

The root CMakeLists.txt holds no build logic; it sets NX_ROOT to the tree and includes the tree's root file. The preset file includes the tree's base presets and adds one preset per project:

{
    "include": ["nextbsw/cmake/NxPresets.json"],
    "configurePresets": [
        {
            "name": "main",
            "inherits": "nx-arm-gcc",
            "displayName": "acme_main",
            "cacheVariables": { "NX_PROJECT": "${sourceDir}/projects/acme_main/project.yaml" }
        }
    ]
}

Build directory and interpreter come from your workspace, toolchain file and compiler options from the tree; nothing is ever written into the submodule. Write both files without a byte-order mark: tools/ci stops with Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (Windows PowerShell 5.1 Set-Content -Encoding utf8 adds one; CMake itself does not mind).

cmake --preset main
cmake --build --preset main

The configure log names the board, the derived switches and the XCP/bootloader settings and ends with Build files have been written; the build ends with the calseg, romcheck and a2lgen lines and no warning under -Werror (configure 110 s, build 9 min 27 s with -j 2 on a busy machine). The A2L's EPK names project and neXtBSW release. The configure run step by step and the flash targets: Build and flash.

docs.title: No board port needed
docs.text:
A board of your own needs no folder in the tree. The feature switches are derived, and the configure log says where each came from:

Switch Derived from OPENBSW_PLATFORM the family of the derivative IO the project uses an I/O entry of its board (use.dio, use.adc, use.input_capture, a pwm group) CAN the project uses a CAN bus (use.can) TRANSPORT, UDS the project has a diagnostics section ETHERNET build option NX_ETHERNET, checked against the derivative WATCHDOG, MPU the family port, ecu/platforms/<family>/features.yaml

ecu/platforms/<board>/Options.cmake remains the place for a justified exception of one board; write down why.

docs.title: Step 6: your tests and your CI
docs.text:
Both run the tree's tooling against your repository; the tree is only read.

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/ci template --list        # github, gitlab, tests, pipeline
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/ci template tests    --out .
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/ci template pipeline --out .
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/ci template github   --out .

Replace the placeholder MEIN_PROJEKT in ci/tests.yaml with your project folder and the preset name with yours, or your first run is red on purpose.

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/test --workspace . --list
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/test --workspace . --jobs 2 --group python

Six of the eight listed entries are inherited from the tree (they test the workspace mechanics: pin, release strictness, tree resolution, update, environment); the tree never pushes its own project builds into your run. Add your own (host tests of your C components, SIL tests of your models) to ci/tests.yaml in the tree's format; an entry with a cmake_preset per visible preset is expected, otherwise the CI is red with "Profil ohne CI-Entscheidung". --group python leaves out the target build. The test runner reports in German; Ergebnis: OK is the line that counts.

The provider file only checks out (with submodules), provides Python and calls the tree's pipeline:

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/ci run --workspace . --release --jobs 2

The run provides the pinned tools (the compiler of the neXtBSW release CI; --toolchain local uses yours), checks pin and environment, runs your tests and builds, and writes a report with a table of your artefacts under build/ci-out; it ended Ergebnis: OK (8 gruen, 0 rot, …) after 641 s. --release turns the Pin/Release lines into errors for a pin that is not on an annotated release tag reachable from master, or whose tree is dirty.

docs.title: Coverage and static analysis of your own code
docs.text:
From the first release after v0.2.0 on (gap N19 of the architecture page), your workspace keeps its own thresholds and baseline in the tree's formats (with v0.2.0 the workspace CI skips both and says so):

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/ci template coverage         --out .   # ci/coverage.yaml
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/ci template misra-deviations --out .   # ci/misra/deviations.yaml
File What you decide there ci/coverage.yaml statement and branch thresholds per module of your code, each with its reason ci/misra/deviations.yaml justified deviations of your code (starts empty) ci/misra/baseline.yaml the known findings of your first inventory, written by the tool ci/misra/rules.yaml optional: your own rule set; without it the tree's applies

[coverage] and [static_analysis] in ci/pipeline.toml switch the stages on (static_analysis.compile_db = "main/compile_commands.json"). Only files of your workspace count, never the tree, nextbsw/, the build root or .venv. Your first inventory, after one run of the target build:

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/test --workspace . -k target-main
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/misra baseline --workspace .

From then on every finding in neither baseline.yaml nor deviations.yaml turns the run red. A stage switched off is named as not run; a stage switched on without its file is red with the command that writes the starting point. This was checked with synthetic workspaces, not yet with a run against a v0.2.0 workspace.

docs.title: What is checked in
docs.text:
Artefact In git? Why nextbsw.yaml, the submodule's gitlink yes together they are the pin project.yaml, rte.yaml, diag.yaml, DBC, board.yaml yes the sources of the ECU your own mcudb/ derivatives and libs/ modules yes same .slx, <Swc>_data.m, swc.yaml, hand-written src/ yes the sources of the components swc/<Swc>/generated/{src,arxml}, model.sha256 yes firmware and CI build without MATLAB; the hash makes stale code visible at configure root CMakeLists.txt, CMakePresets.json, ci/, the provider file yes written once update reports doc/nextbsw-updates/*.md yes the evidence of an impact analysis per pin move build/, generated/ of the build no determined by your sources plus the pinned tree content of nextbsw/ no referenced, never edited .venv/, CMakeUserPresets.json no workstation

The minimum .gitignore is build/, .venv/, CMakeUserPresets.json, __pycache__/. nextbsw in the tracked files is the gitlink, one line, not a copy of the tree.

docs.title: The git page
docs.text:
The Studio's git page groups the changes of a workspace (neXtBSW-Referenz, Eigene Projekte, Eigene Boards, Eigene Module, Diagnosebeschreibung, Modelle, Komponenten-Code, Generierte Dateien, Sonstiges) and shows the pinned neXtBSW as a row of its own; on the command line:

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/studio git status projects/acme_main/project.yaml
  • The pin moves only through a deliberate commit. The Studio never moves it; it may tell you a newer release exists.
  • A commit of the workspace never touches the tree. Paths inside the submodule are refused, and a submodule with changes of its own blocks the commit.
  • Generated files belong in .gitignore, not in a commit.

The never-commit path rule and the protected branches are read from your repository: git config nextbsw.protectedbranch names yours, otherwise dev, master and main are protected.

docs.title: Step 8: taking a newer neXtBSW
docs.text:
An update is a deliberate change of its own, on a branch, reviewed like any other.

  1. Move the pin. Fetch in the submodule, check out the new tag, git add nextbsw, then git submodule update --init --recursive (the order of step 1), and set nextbsw.version; nxconfig check refuses the mismatch until you do both.
  2. Recreate the environment if requirements changed: python nextbsw/tools/setup venv ..
  3. Migrate the formats the new release raised; nxconfig migrate edits the YAML in place, preserving comments, and shows a diff before it writes anything:
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig migrate --list
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig migrate .          # dry run with diff
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxconfig migrate . --write  # writes a backup of every file it changes
  1. Generate, build, test: cmake --preset …, tools/test --workspace ., tools/ci run --workspace ..
  2. Commit the gitlink, nextbsw.yaml, the migrated files and the update report as one change.

docs.title: The matching Studio
docs.text:
A Studio build bundles the generator modules of the tree it was packed from, so it must match the pin exactly (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Otherwise a NUR LESEND banner blocks generating, building and flashing (configuring, checking, host tests and every view keep working) and offers two ways out: the installed Studio build of the pinned version (<tools>/neXtBSW Studio/neXtBSW_Studio_v_x.y.z), or a deliberate pin move.

tools/nxupdate does the five steps: it generates every project with the old and the new tree, moves the pin only after the target tag has passed the release rule, runs the target tree's migrations, and writes doc/nextbsw-updates/v<old>-v<new>.md (pin findings, skipped releases, changelog excerpt, changed nxconfig check messages, generated-file diff with field-relevant changes flagged):

.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxupdate C:/acme --to 0.3.0                    # dry run, report on stdout
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxupdate C:/acme --to 0.3.0 --write            # moves the pin, writes the report
.venv/Scripts/python nextbsw/tools/nxupdate C:/acme --to 0.3.0 --write --commit   # and commits (never pushes)

--release makes a development target tag an error, --tree <path> points it at an unpacked tree (archive variant). Open: compiling and testing after the move (tools/ci run --workspace does it, but the two are not wired together) and the ELF size change.

Known problem of v0.2.0: a dry run does not get through. A relative workspace path ends in a traceback (pass an absolute path), and with an absolute path the generation "after" fails because the generators refuse to run from the temporary tree. Until fixed, do the five steps by hand and write the update report yourself.

docs.title: What is not there yet
docs.text: Gap What it means for you today Licensed overlays in a workspace (N16) one profile per workspace, no overlay trees neXtBSW version in the image identity (N13) the A2L's EPK names the release; the identity over console and diagnostics does not yet

docs.title: Where to go from here
docs.text:
• Your first board: what belongs in board.yaml and project.yaml, and the messages.
  • The application: components, tasks, connections, CAN.
  • Build and flash: the configure run, flash targets, the console.
  • Adding a derivative: when your MCU is not in mcudb/ yet.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: The way in for someone who wants to use neXtBSW: you have a control unit (or a schematic of one) and want basic software with an application on it. First the whole route at a glance, then you build a project that already exists, so you know your setup works before you describe your own hardware. Why the software is split the way it is: ../architecture/.

docs.title: The route at a glance
docs.text:
A neXtBSW control unit is described in configuration files, not in code. Each fact is written once, in the level it belongs to; the generators derive the rest (clock trees, bit timings, linker values, pin set-up, the RTE).

%%{init: {'theme':'base','flowchart':{'curve':'basis'},'themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif','fontSize':'14px','background':'#ffffff','primaryColor':'#ffffff','primaryBorderColor':'#64748b','primaryTextColor':'#0f172a','lineColor':'#475569','edgeLabelBackground':'#ffffff','tertiaryColor':'#f8fafc','clusterBkg':'#f8fafc','clusterBorder':'#cbd5e1'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    M("1-2 MCU: mcudb") --> B("3 board.yaml") --> P("4 project.yaml") --> R("5 rte.yaml + components")
    R --> C("6 build") --> F("7 flash") --> K("8 console")
Step You decide Where it goes How you know it is right Page 1 Which MCU (derivative and package) the schematic uses nothing yet the derivative exists in mcudb/ Your first board 2 Manufacturer facts of that MCU mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml: check it, or add it nxconfig check finds it and accepts your pins Your first board 3 What is fitted on the board and how it is wired boards/<board>/board.yaml: hardware only nxconfig check Your first board 4 What this software uses, at which clock, bit rate, frequency; memory split; diagnostic addresses projects/<project>/project.yaml nxconfig check Your first board 5 Which components run in which task, and what their ports connect to projects/<project>/rte.yaml, a DBC, components under swc/ the configure run (rtegen) The application 6 Build a CMake preset configure and build pass, without warnings Build and flash 7 Flash bootloader and application flash-bootloader, flash, flash-can the board starts Build and flash 8 Talk to the running ECU serial console the console answers Build and flash

No board is the yardstick. The boards and projects of this tree (a build-test profile for an S32K148, the NXP S32K116 evaluation board) are examples: they show one real set of values, yours will differ, and nothing in neXtBSW assumes the values of an example board.

docs.title: What runs today
docs.text:
The state of the repository, not a promise:

Board profile Derivative (core) Configure and check Target build Running on hardware buildtest_s32k148 (buildtest_s32k148_min) S32K148 (Cortex-M4F) yes yes no: a pure build test with no board behind it

The software has been brought up on one S32K144 board of the maintainers. Its board files exist, but in the maintainers' private repository and not in this public tree, so you will not find them here; for the board profile above there is no recorded bring-up of the application. For your hardware:

  • S32K1 with a Cortex-M4F (S32K142/144/146/148): you can describe your board, check it and build application and bootloader. Expect to be the first to measure the bring-up on a board of your own.
  • S32K116 (Cortex-M0+): the derivative data (mcudb/s32k1xx/S32K116.yaml) and the platform code are in this tree. The maintainers' profile for the NXP evaluation board is not published yet: the levels of its LEDs, buttons and potentiometer are not confirmed by a public source and are measured on the board first. In that profile configuration and compilation work; only a reduced application (no console, no application CAN, no UDS) links, the full application does not fit into 128 KB flash and the small RAM yet.
  • Other families (STM32, S32K3, RM4x): derivative data and parts of the platform exist in the maintainers' tree, but are not published yet; a complete target build does not exist.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Python 3.12, CMake 3.28 or newer, Ninja and an arm-none-eabi-gcc (the pinned xPack GCC 11.3.1 from python -m tools.ci setup; found on PATH or through NX_ARM_GCC_BIN, a setting of your workstation that is never checked in). The one-time set-up (submodule, virtual environment, requirements) is in ../../CONTRIBUTING.md. On Windows use the interpreter from .venv and set PYTHONUTF8=1.

docs.title: Step 0: build something that already works
docs.text:
If this fails, the problem is your set-up, not your board.

.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig check projects/buildtest_s32k148_min/project.yaml
cmake --preset buildtest-s32k148-min
cmake --build --preset buildtest-s32k148-min

The check ends buildtest_s32k148_min: ok (board buildtest_s32k148, S32K148, 0 warning(s)): ok, the board and derivative it resolved to, and the number of warnings. A warning means something is unconfirmed or probably unintended (reading the messages). The configure run ends with -- Build files have been written to: …, the build with the application and bootloader linked; nothing needs a board (Build and flash). Optionally run the checks of the configuration model:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k nxconfig --jobs 4

The test runner reports in German; Ergebnis: OK is the line that counts. When all of this passes, go on to Your first board.

docs.title: Host-Durchlauf ohne Hardware
docs.text:
%%{init: {'theme':'base','flowchart':{'curve':'basis'},'themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif','fontSize':'14px','background':'#ffffff','primaryColor':'#ffffff','primaryBorderColor':'#64748b','primaryTextColor':'#0f172a','lineColor':'#475569','edgeLabelBackground':'#ffffff','tertiaryColor':'#f8fafc','clusterBkg':'#f8fafc','clusterBorder':'#cbd5e1'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    S1("1 new<br/>project.yaml + rte.yaml")
    S2(("2 nxconfig check<br/>0 error, 0 warning"))
    S3("3 Generatoren<br/>bswgen, blgen, rtegen")
    S4("4 Build<br/>app.ecu.elf, bootloader.elf,<br/>blupdater.elf")
    S5("5 Host-Tests<br/>tools/test, no board")
    HW("flash, flash-can, console<br/>needs a board")

    S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> S5
    S4 -.-> HW

    classDef ok fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#15803d,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    classDef no fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#b91c1c,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    class S1,S2,S3,S4,S5 ok
    class HW no

Fünf Schritte von einem leeren Klon bis zu grünen Tests. Kein Board, kein Debugger, kein CAN-Adapter. Grün hinterlegt ist, was dieser Durchlauf wirklich ausführt, rot, was ein Board braucht und hier nicht gelaufen ist (Build and flash). Dies ist der Weg für jeden, der neXtBSW zum ersten Mal ausprobiert; ein Referenzboard, auf dem die Anwendung außerhalb des Maintainer-Aufbaus läuft, gibt es erst nach R1 (Board-Tabelle).

Was geprüft wurde. Jeder Befehl auf dieser Seite wurde am 2026-10-04 in einem Git-Worktree des Repositorys ausgeführt (Windows 10, Python 3.12, CMake 3.28, Ninja, arm-none-eabi-gcc 11.3.1 aus python -m tools.ci setup); die Ausgaben sind echt und gekürzt (…). Zwei Abweichungen vom Klon: Der Worktree hat kein eigenes .venv, deshalb steht beim Konfigurieren -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=… und wegen der Pfadlänge unter Windows ein kurzer -B-Ordner. Im Klon entfallen beide Angaben, wenn das .venv wie in CONTRIBUTING.md angelegt ist. Ein frischer Klon auf einem zweiten Rechner wurde nicht durchlaufen.

Voraussetzungen und die einmalige Einrichtung (Submodul, .venv, Compiler): Getting started. Im Folgenden steht .venv/Scripts/python für den Interpreter dieses .venv; unter Windows PYTHONUTF8=1 setzen.

docs.title: Schritt 1: Projekt anlegen
docs.text:
%%{init: {'theme':'base','flowchart':{'curve':'basis'},'themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif','fontSize':'14px','background':'#ffffff','primaryColor':'#ffffff','primaryBorderColor':'#64748b','primaryTextColor':'#0f172a','lineColor':'#475569','edgeLabelBackground':'#ffffff','tertiaryColor':'#f8fafc','clusterBkg':'#f8fafc','clusterBorder':'#cbd5e1'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    B[("boards/buildtest_s32k148/board.yaml")] --> N(["nxconfig new"])
    C("--safe-state-output<br/>--locked-pin, --test-pin") --> N
    N --> P[("projects/host_demo/project.yaml<br/>projects/host_demo/rte.yaml")]

    classDef gen fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#b45309,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    classDef data fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#94a3b8,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    class N gen
    class B,P data

nxconfig new legt ein leeres Projekt für ein Board an; Takt, Speicheraufteilung, Diagnoseadressen und Interrupt-Ränge werden aus Board und Derivat abgeleitet. Nur der Abschnitt safety wird nie abgeleitet: Welcher Ausgang eine Anzeige ist und welcher Pin unbeschaltet ist, steht nur im Schaltplan. Die Kandidaten nennt nxconfig new --safety-candidates --board <board>.

.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig new host_demo --board buildtest_s32k148 \
    --safe-state-output LED1 --locked-pin LED2 --test-pin PTA0

empty project host_demo in …/projects/host_demo:
  project.yaml
  rte.yaml
note: core clock 80 MHz (highest value of S32K148 the clock model reaches with this board and its buses)
note: safety section as chosen: safe_state_output LED1, locked_pin LED2, test_pin PTA0 - check on the schematic that the indicator drives no actuator and that PTA0 is unconnected. …
…

Beispiel: das Build-Test-Board. LED1, LED2 und PTA0 sind hier beliebig gewählt, weil hinter dem Profil kein Board steht, das man verdrahten könnte. Bei einem echten Board wählt man sie am Schaltplan. Das Projekt liegt in projects/host_demo des eigenen Klons; es gehört nicht zum Lieferumfang.

Ohne eigenes Projekt geht es auch mit dem vorhandenen projects/buildtest_s32k148_min; die Schritte 2 bis 5 sind dieselben. Mehr zum Anlegen: projects/README.md (Abschnitt „Neues Projekt“) und Your first board.

tools/test führt alle Tests aus einer Liste aus. Die Gruppe host übersetzt die C- und C++-Quellen des Treibers mit ziglang für den PC und prüft sie gegen Registermodelle. Eine Auswahl, die in diesem Durchlauf lief:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group host --jobs 4 \
    -k clock-config-s32k-s32k148 -k clock-check-s32k-firc -k safe-watchdog

Ergebnis: OK (3 gruen, 0 rot, 0 uebersprungen, 140 Testfaelle, 35.4s)

(Der Testlauf berichtet noch auf Deutsch; maßgeblich ist die Zeile Ergebnis: OK.) Alles, was fehlt (zum Beispiel ein Compiler), wird als „übersprungen“ gemeldet und nicht rot. --group host --list zeigt alle 110 Einträge dieser Gruppe, ohne sie auszuführen. Der vollständige Lauf, .venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group all --jobs 4, wurde für diese Seite nicht ausgeführt; er dauert lange und ist in CONTRIBUTING.md beschrieben.

docs.text:
How to describe a new MCU derivative of a family neXtBSW already supports, for example one more S32K1 part: which files to write, where each value comes from, how to mark what is not confirmed, how the pin table is made, and how to check the result. Your first board sends you here when your MCU is not in mcudb/ yet.

docs.title: Derivative or family?
docs.text:
New derivative of an existing family New family Example another S32K1 part next to S32K116/142/144/146/148 a first TI RM4x, a first S32K3 that builds What you write data: mcudb/<family>/<DERIVATIVE>.yaml, its pin tables, the vendor pin data under sources/ code: an OpenBSW-style platform platforms/<family>, a family branch in the board generator, the family's clock model, a family port This page yes no

A derivative belongs to an existing family when that family's drivers run it unchanged: same peripheral IP blocks, a device header that describes it (or a superset), a core the toolchain file knows. Everything that differs (memory sizes, instance counts, packages, pins, clock limits) is data. For a new family the rules are in ../architecture/README.md, section 6 (platform rule P1–P6), and ../architecture/plattformen.md.

docs.title: The rule on sources
docs.text:
Every value in mcudb/ is a manufacturer fact and needs public evidence (decision: mcudb values only with a public source):

Allowed as a source Not allowed Data sheet and reference manual as published, including files attached to the PDF; cite document, revision, section or table, page (for s32k1xx the memory map S32K1xx_Memory_Map.xlsx, tag [MAP], cite the sheet) anything from a document the manufacturer has not published, even one number Vendor files in the repository with an open licence, cited by path: Zephyr hal_nxp pin headers (Apache-2.0), STM32 Open Pin Data (BSD-3-Clause), device headers under platforms/*/bsp/bspMcu/include/3rdparty/ vendor files whose licence forbids redistribution or is unclear (device headers and linker scripts of a vendor IDE) Public reference code with an open licence, for a default the documents leave open (the s32k1xx clock defaults cite the OpenBSW reference port) values guessed from a similar part without saying so
  • If no published document answers a question, the value stays out, or goes in as verify: true with a comment that a public source is missing. A clock default without evidence is left out, and a project that uses the instance without choosing a clock gets an error instead of a guessed value.
  • Vendor files whose licence is unclear stay on the workstation. Worked example: the S32K116 SVD file, only a README with download address, licence finding and checksum is checked in (../../mcudb/s32k1xx/sources/keil_s32k116_dfp/README.md (repository: mcudb/s32k1xx/sources/keil_s32k116_dfp/README.md)). A test in ../../mcudb/tools/test_mcudb.py rejects citations of vendor-IDE files.

docs.title: What you need before you start
docs.text: The data sheet (memory sizes, packages, instance counts, clock and oscillator limits), the reference manual (memory map, flash sector and programming sizes, clock distribution, MPU, ADC channel codes) and public pin multiplexing data for every package (The pin tables). Write down document number and revision; you cite them in almost every entry.

docs.title: The derivative file
docs.text:
Create mcudb/<family>/<DERIVATIVE>.yaml (file name = derivative name in capitals, folder = family). nxconfig finds a derivative by the mcu: of a board. Start from the closest existing derivative of the family and change every value you can back; the structure is fixed by the schema, class Derivative (generated reference), and unknown keys are rejected. Put a comment block at the top that lists the documents with a short tag each, and use the tags in the entries (mcudb/s32k1xx/S32K142.yaml, comments there are German):

#   [DS]    S32K1xx Data Sheet Rev. 15 (5 March 2026), Figure 3 "S32K1xx product series comparison"
#   [RM]    S32K1xx Series Reference Manual Rev. 13 (04/2020): 31.3.1 Table 31-2 "On-chip SRAM sizes"

docs.title: Sections and where each value comes from
docs.text:
Section Contents Source derivative name (= file), family (= folder), core, fpu, nvic_priority_bits, features, packages, pin_pattern, sources, optional tool names (jlink_device, pyocd_target, openocd_target) data sheet, reference manual memory per region: name, kind (code_flash, data_flash, ram, eeprom_ram), start, size; flash also sector_size (or sectors) and program_size reference manual memory map and flash chapter; data sheet sizes instances per peripheral instance: class, timer channels, ADC resolution_bits, channel_pattern, internal_channels, clock (sources, divider, max_hz, default) data sheet (counts), reference manual (channels, clock distribution); default from a public reference port mpu regions reference manual, MPU chapter pinmux per package: file of the generated pin table generated (pin tables) device_header file the family code includes, describes (a superset is allowed) a header in the repository with an open licence clock oscillators, pll limits, max_hz per domain, system_source_max_hz, output_max_hz, pcc data sheet, reference manual clock chapter vim Cortex-R only: channel count, fixed channels reference manual

Nothing that depends on a board or project goes in: no crystal, no chosen clock, no pins in use, no memory split.

  • One value, one place. If a family needs a value the schema cannot hold, that is a schema change, not a comment.
  • The largest variant where the ordering code varies the RAM size, said in a comment.
  • Fact and default are separate. The derivative says which clock sources an instance can use; the project chooses. An optional default needs evidence like any other value, otherwise leave it out.
  • The device header must know every instance. nxconfig compares your instances with the derivative named in device_header.describes. If no existing header covers your derivative, providing one is platform work, see ../../platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspMcu/include/3rdparty/nxp/rtd/README.md (repository: platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspMcu/include/3rdparty/nxp/rtd/README.md).

docs.title: source: and verify:
docs.text:
Almost every entry takes a source: string and a verify: flag (instances take verify: only).

  • source: names the document tag, the section or table and the page, enough for a reviewer to find it in a minute: source: "[RM] 36.1.2 256 KB, 36.2.1.1 Sektor 2 KB".
  • verify: true marks a value without public evidence yet (a document you could not get, a sister part, a placeholder). Say in a comment why and what would confirm it.
  • derivative.example: true is for format examples that are not real data; nxconfig warns whenever a project uses one.

nxconfig check warns once per verify: true entry whose values the project actually uses, with file, line and YAML path, naming the fields it read and what they are needed for; entries the project does not touch stay silent. Every such warning has to be cleared, by a source or a measurement on hardware, before the first bring-up.

docs.title: The pin tables
docs.text:
Pin tables say which signal a pin can take with which selector (s32k1xx: the PORT_PCR.MUX value). They are generated from vendor pin data, never typed; each generated file names its source and licence and must not be edited.

Family Vendor data Generator s32k1xx, s32k3xx Zephyr hal_nxp, dts/nxp/s32/pinctrl, one <part>-pinctrl.h per derivative and package (Apache-2.0) ../../mcudb/tools/pinmux_hal_nxp.py stm32 STMicroelectronics STM32_open_pin_data: <RefName>.xml and the GPIO modes file under IP/ (BSD-3-Clause) pinmux_stm32_open_pin_data.py in the maintainers' tree; not published yet, the family is not supported

For an NXP part:

  1. Copy the header of your derivative and package unchanged into mcudb/<family>/sources/hal_nxp/, from the same upstream commit as the others. "Delta headers" #include another part; copy the base header too.
  2. Record the origin in the README.md of that folder: upstream repository, path, commit, date, licence (../../mcudb/s32k1xx/sources/hal_nxp/README.md (repository: mcudb/s32k1xx/sources/hal_nxp/README.md) is the pattern). test_mcudb.py requires a LICENSE file and the word "Commit" in the README of every source folder.
  3. Run the generator (one table per header found; prints nothing when nothing changed):
.venv/Scripts/python mcudb/tools/pinmux_hal_nxp.py
  1. Reference each table from the derivative, keyed by the package name under packages (key and file name may differ, e.g. MAPBGA100: { file: S32K144_BGA100.pinmux.yaml }):
pinmux:
  LQFP100: { file: S32K142_LQFP100.pinmux.yaml }
  LQFP64: { file: S32K142_LQFP64.pinmux.yaml }

--check compares without writing, exits 1 and names every missing or outdated table. Entries the generator cannot map without guessing are left out and listed in the header of the generated file.

No public pin data for a package? Leave it out of pinmux: the configuration loads, but every board on that package gets the warning S32K142 has no pin multiplexing data for package LQFP64: pin functions are not checked. Do not fill the gap with an unmarked copy of another package; the schema has verify: true and complete: false on a pinmux entry for that case.

docs.title: Checking the derivative
docs.text:
The derivative database tests.

.venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k mcudb --jobs 4

The group mcudb loads every derivative file, runs the derivative checks of nxconfig for each package, and checks that every pin table is referenced exactly once and every source folder names origin and licence; mcudb-pinmux-nxp and mcudb-pinmux-stm32 check that the tables are up to date. Two assertions list the database contents on purpose, so a new derivative makes them fail until you update ../../mcudb/tools/test_mcudb.py: the number of derivative/package pairs and, for s32k1xx, the MPU region count per derivative (with its evidence in mpu.source). tools/test -k nxconfig additionally requires every s32k1xx derivative to describe the clock gates the family clock driver writes, each with source (or verify: true) and a default.

nxconfig check with a board on the new derivative. A derivative is only checked completely together with a board and project that use it. Without a board, use a minimal one; the synthetic profile testproject_s32k142_bl is one for the S32K142:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig check tools/nxconfig/test/profiles/projects/testproject_s32k142_bl/project.yaml

Mistakes in the derivative file are reported against that file, with line and YAML path:

S32K142.yaml:17 (derivative.name): error: name S32K143 does not match the file name S32K142.yaml
S32K142.yaml:19 (derivative.core): error: unknown core cortex-m4 (known: cortex-m0plus, cortex-m4f, cortex-m7f, cortex-m33, cortex-r4f)
S32K142.yaml:31 (memory[0].size): error: size 0x40000 of PFLASH is no multiple of sector_size 0x1800

The build test. The last check is a target build of a minimal project on the derivative; it shows that family code, device header and linker template accept the new memory map and instance set, which no configuration check can see. buildtest_s32k148_min is the pattern, a project with no hardware behind it (../../boards/buildtest_s32k148/README.md); give yours a preset in CMakePresets.json (see Build and flash):

cmake --preset buildtest-s32k148-min
cmake --build --preset buildtest-s32k148-min

A derivative with less memory than the application needs configures and compiles but does not link, which is the state of the S32K116 today (Getting started): a real result, not a mistake in the file.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• mcudb/<family>/<DERIVATIVE>.yaml with a document list at the top and source: on every entry that takes one
  • every value without public evidence marked verify: true, with a comment saying why
  • nothing from unpublished documents or from vendor files that may not be redistributed
  • vendor pin data copied unchanged under sources/, origin and licence in its README, tables generated, --check silent
  • tools/test -k mcudb and tools/test -k nxconfig green, test_mcudb.py updated
  • nxconfig check of a board and project on the derivative: ok
  • a build-test project that configures and builds

Next, for your own hardware: Your first board and the board README template.

docs.title: The application
docs.text:
Step 5 of the route: which software components run, in which task, and what their ports are connected to. The result is the ECU description of the project, rte.yaml, from which tools/rtegen generates the RTE during the configure run.

%%{init: {'theme':'base','flowchart':{'curve':'basis'},'themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif','fontSize':'14px','background':'#ffffff','primaryColor':'#ffffff','primaryBorderColor':'#64748b','primaryTextColor':'#0f172a','lineColor':'#475569','edgeLabelBackground':'#ffffff','tertiaryColor':'#f8fafc','clusterBkg':'#f8fafc','clusterBorder':'#cbd5e1'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    SW("component: runnables and ports") -- "connections" --> T[("task: period, priority, runnables")]
    SW --> IO[("dio, adc, pwm, can, ecu")]
    DBC[("DBC")] --> IO
    T --> RTE(["generated RTE"])
    IO --> RTE

    classDef gen fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#b45309,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    classDef data fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#94a3b8,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    classDef app fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#6d28d9,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    class RTE gen
    class T,IO,DBC data
    class SW app

The full rules (model conventions, connection targets, task rules, data consistency, qualifiers) are in ../../swc/README.md (German for now); every key of the file is in the generated rte.yaml reference. This page takes you through the decisions in order.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
File Contents projects/<project>/rte.yaml tasks, components, connections, CAN and diagnostic bus; project.rte points to it. Required: an ECU without components has one task and components: [], as nxconfig new writes it projects/<project>/<Name>.dbc the CAN database, if the application sends or receives CAN signals swc/<Swc>/ or projects/<project>/swc/<Swc>/ a software component: Simulink model (.slx) and its generated code and ARXML, both checked in

Paths inside rte.yaml (components[].path, can.dbc) are relative to the file itself.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Application logic is a Simulink model configured as an AUTOSAR Classic software component. MATLAB with Simulink, Embedded Coder and AUTOSAR Blockset is needed only to change a model; generated C code and ARXML are checked in, so building needs no MATLAB. A new component starts as a swc.yaml copied from swc/template/swc.yaml into a folder of the component's name, checked before the model is created:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/swc/swc_yaml.py check swc/<Swc>

Model creation and code generation run in MATLAB (swc_create, swc_build, see ../../swc/README.md; not run for this guide). A reusable component lives under swc/, one of a single project under projects/<project>/swc/. A component never refers to a pin, a board or a bus, only to its ports.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: tasks lists name, period_ms, priority, stack_bytes and the runnables in call order. priority is an ordering key among the tasks of the basic software (background 10, bsp 20, can 40, sysadmin 50, safety 60); pick one that is not taken. Without tasks, one task swc is created.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
Each port is connected in connections as <Swc>.<Port>.<Element>: <target>. Targets name board entries the project uses (use: in project.yaml), never pins:

Target Meaning dio.in.<NAME>, dio.out.<NAME> digital input or output adc.mv.<NAME>, adc.phys.<NAME>, adc.qlf.<NAME> analog input in mV, in the physical unit of its sensor circuit, and its quality can.rx.<Msg>.<Signal>, can.tx.<Msg>.<Signal>, can.qlf.<Msg> CAN signals from the DBC and the qualifier of a received message pwm.<Pair>, capture.<Channel>.<value>, hall.<Sensor>.<value> PWM duty, measured input signals ecu.state, ecu.wakeup…, ecu.sleep_request ECU state management ecu.mode the ECU states as modes, for mode ports only (Modes) <Swc>.<Port>.<Element> a provided port of another component rte kept in the RTE only (visible on the console)

Where a value has a quality (CAN messages, measured inputs, sensors), connect the qualifier too: a value alone keeps its last content when the source fails; only the qualifier tells the component. rtegen warns when one is missing.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
The ECU states STARTUP, RUN, STANDBY, RUNDOWN, SHUTDOWN, SLEEP are also available as AUTOSAR modes of one mode manager, ecu.mode:

%%{init: {'theme':'base','flowchart':{'curve':'basis'},'themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif','fontSize':'14px','background':'#ffffff','primaryColor':'#ffffff','primaryBorderColor':'#64748b','primaryTextColor':'#0f172a','lineColor':'#475569','edgeLabelBackground':'#ffffff','tertiaryColor':'#f8fafc','clusterBkg':'#f8fafc','clusterBorder':'#cbd5e1'}}}%%
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> STARTUP
    STARTUP --> RUN
    RUN --> STANDBY
    STANDBY --> RUN
    STANDBY --> RUNDOWN
    RUNDOWN --> SHUTDOWN
    SHUTDOWN --> SLEEP

(Main path only; the full state machine with restart paths is ../figures/05-ecu-zustaende.md.)

A component needs a mode port (a required port whose mode switch interface names exactly these six modes; read with Rte_Mode_<Port>_<ModeGroup>()) and may have mode switch runnables (SWC-MODE-SWITCH-EVENT on entry, exit or transition), all described in its ARXML. In rte.yaml the mode port is connected to ecu.mode and every mode switch runnable goes into a task like a periodic one, without offset_ms:

tasks:
  - name: app
    period_ms: 10
    priority: 30
    stack_bytes: 2048
    runnables: [MySwc.Run10ms, MySwc.OnRunEntry, MySwc.OnRunExit]

connections:
  MySwc.EcuMode.EcuMode: ecu.mode        # <Swc>.<Port>.<ModeGroup>

A task sees a change at the start of its next cycle and runs its mode switch runnables once before the periodic ones: on-exit of the old mode, on-transition, on-entry of the new mode. In that time Rte_Mode returns RTE_TRANSITION_<Group>. A port read by runnables of several tasks has no task view and reads the manager directly.

  • A mode that lasts less than one cycle of a task can pass unnoticed (no queue of mode switches).
  • The application tasks stop when the lifecycle goes down: SHUTDOWN is seen for at most one cycle and SLEEP never (rtegen warns about events on them); last actions belong on entry of RUNDOWN.
  • ecu.state stays a sender-receiver port with the state number, for where a number is enough.

rtegen rejects, with the YAML path: a mode port connected to anything but ecu.mode, a mode group with missing or unknown modes, an unassigned mode switch runnable or one with an offset, provided mode ports and mode-disabled events. AUTOSAR correspondence: ../architecture/autosar.md, section 2.3.

docs.title: Explicit and implicit access
docs.text:
Which way a component reads and writes its sender-receiver ports is a property of the component (its port mapping in Simulink, reaching the RTE through its ARXML); rte.yaml has no setting for it.

Model mapping Call in the component code What the runnable sees ExplicitReceive / ExplicitSend Rte_Read_<Port>_<Element>(&v), Rte_Write_…(v) every call reaches the RTE buffer at that moment ImplicitReceive / ImplicitSend, ImplicitSendByRef Rte_IRead_<Runnable>_<Port>_<Element>(), Rte_IWrite_…(v), Rte_IWriteRef_…() its own copy: read values stay the same for its whole run, written values appear when it ends

Implicit access keeps one copy per runnable and data element, loaded before and published after the runnable under one lock at most (for a port used by several tasks). Prefer it for a runnable that reads a value several times and must not see it change in between; the price is RAM and copy time per call (tools/schedana lists both). Both ways may be mixed in one component, even in one runnable. rtegen rejects an implicit read on a provided port, an implicit write on a required port and ExplicitReceiveByVal; it warns when runnables of several tasks write one element implicitly. Not provided: Rte_IStatus, Rte_IInvalidate. The template swc/template/swc.yaml creates explicit ports. Details: ../architecture/autosar.md, section 2.3.

docs.title: CAN and diagnostics
docs.text:
can names the DBC, the node of this ECU in it (BU_), the bus (a board CAN name from use.can) and the task in which signals are packed and unpacked; per received message can.qualifiers sets timeout, debouncing and end-to-end protection. uds.bus selects the bus of the diagnostic stack. The diagnostic IDs are in project.yaml (diagnostics), because the bootloader uses them too. A project without CAN signals leaves out can; the bus is still used for diagnostics and the bootloader.

Example: projects/buildtest_s32k148_min/rte.yaml has two tasks (app10, app100) with freely chosen priority keys, one component DemoSwc (path: ../../swc/DemoSwc) and connections such as DemoSwc.Button1.Button1: dio.in.BUTTON1 and DemoSwc.PcCommandQlf.PcCommandQlf: rte.init (no can section, so the qualifier keeps its init value). The same component runs unchanged in the project of another board, connected to that board's signals. With CAN:

can:
  dbc: MyEcu.dbc
  node: ECU
  bus: CAN0
  task: app10

connections:
  MySwc.CommandQlf.CommandQlf: can.qlf.Command
  MySwc.Led1.Led1: [dio.out.LED1, can.tx.Status.Led1]

docs.title: How you know it is right
docs.text:
rte.yaml is checked by rtegen during the configure run (step 6), not by nxconfig check; messages start with rtegen:. An error stops the run, a warning does not, but read it:

rtegen: rte.yaml:28 (connections.DemoSwc.Button1.Button1): error: connection DemoSwc.Button1.Button1 -> dio.in.BUTTON9: BUTTON9 is not a dio.in signal used by the project
rtegen: rte.yaml:27 (connections.DemoSwc.PcCommandQlf.PcCommandQlf): warning: required port DemoSwc.PcCommandQlf.PcCommandQlf is not connected: it reads QLF_NOT_AVAILABLE (64, no source) from a constant buffer …

The unchanged example project has no warning. The generated RTE lands in <build>/generated/rte/; the generator's own tests run with .venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k rtegen. Next: Build and flash.

docs.title: Your first board
docs.text:
From a schematic to a checked configuration: steps 1 to 4 of the route. At the end you have a derivative, a board and a project that nxconfig check accepts. The application on top follows in The application.

%%{init: {'theme':'base','flowchart':{'curve':'basis'},'themeVariables':{'fontFamily':'Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif','fontSize':'14px','background':'#ffffff','primaryColor':'#ffffff','primaryBorderColor':'#64748b','primaryTextColor':'#0f172a','lineColor':'#475569','edgeLabelBackground':'#ffffff','tertiaryColor':'#f8fafc','clusterBkg':'#f8fafc','clusterBorder':'#cbd5e1'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    D[("derivative.yaml: manufacturer facts")] --> B[("board.yaml: fitted and wired")]
    B --> P[("project.yaml: what this software uses")]
    P --> C(["nxconfig check"])

    classDef gen fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#b45309,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    classDef data fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#94a3b8,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a
    class C gen
    class D,B,P data

Every value has exactly one level it belongs to (binding table: ../architecture/README.md, section 4, "Responsibility per value"):

Level File Contains Changes when Derivative mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml what the manufacturer decided: core, memories, peripheral instances, pin functions, clock limits never for your project Board boards/<board>/board.yaml what is fitted and wired on the PCB the PCB changes Project projects/<project>/project.yaml what this software uses and how: clocks, bit rates, memory split, diagnostics, parameters you change the software

When unsure: would a second piece of software on the same PCB need the same value? Board. Would the same software on a different PCB keep it? Project. Is it in the datasheet of the MCU? Derivative.

docs.title: Step 1: what you have
docs.text: Collect before writing anything: the derivative and package exactly as ordered (pin functions depend on the package), the schematic, and the datasheets of the fitted parts the software drives. Values without a source are allowed, but marked, see Sources and verify.

docs.title: Step 2: the derivative
docs.text: Look in mcudb/ (s32k1xx/, s32k3xx/, stm32/, plus one pin table per package). If it is there, you normally do not touch it; check that your package is listed under packages: and that a pin table <derivative>_<package>.pinmux.yaml exists, because nxconfig uses it to decide whether a pin can take the function you assign. If it is missing, Adding a derivative says how. Some pins exist only in the larger package (the second CAN bus of the S32K148 build-test board sits on PTE24/PTE25, which the LQFP100 does not have); that is why the package matters.

docs.title: Step 3: the board
docs.text:
Create boards/<board>/board.yaml: what is fitted and how it is wired, nothing about how software uses it. A board can carry several projects that use it differently, which only works if the file stays free of usage decisions.

The sections (board, devices, can, uart/spi/i2c, adc, rails, dio, input_capture; pwm with a power stage is after R1) and every key are in the generated Board description; the existing board files are worked examples, for instance boards/buildtest_s32k148/board.yaml (two passive CAN transceivers on two controller instances, an 8 MHz crystal) and the synthetic test boards under tools/nxconfig/test/profiles/boards. What differs from board to board is exactly what belongs in this file.

What does not go in, because the PCB does not decide it:

  • Frequencies, bit rates, baud rates, dead times, which peripherals are used. A board lists everything wired, even if no project uses it yet. Project.
  • Memory split, CAN IDs, diagnostic addresses, tasks. Project.
  • The load behind a sensor input (an NTC in a connector): project (adc_loads); the board describes the circuit up to the pin.
  • Workstation settings (debugger path, serial port, probe serial number): not checked in at all.

A signal name is free: name it after the net in your schematic.

docs.title: Step 4: the project
docs.text:
Create projects/<project>/project.yaml: what this software uses from the board and how. Paths in the project section are relative to the file. The sections (project, clock, use, can/uart, memory, bootloader, diagnostics, interrupts, modules, safety, …) are in the generated Project description. Three rules to know while writing:

  • project.rte is required (an ECU without components has one task and components: []), see The application.
  • clock.system_hz is the core clock; PLL settings, dividers and peripheral clocks are derived, never written.
  • use: lists the board entries the software uses (all or names); every CAN bus and UART in use needs its bit rate or baud rate, and every CAN bus an interrupt rank.

What does not go in: pins, pads and instances (the project refers to board entries by name; the one exception is safety.test_pin), the crystal (board), and derived values such as PLL factors, bit-timing segments, linker addresses or register values (the generator computes them).

Values the flashed bootloader depends on. memory, bootloader.can and diagnostics are also compiled into the bootloader. Once a bootloader is on a board, a project that changes any of them needs a bootloader update as well; choose them carefully and keep them identical across projects that share a board. Example: projects/buildtest_s32k148_min/project.yaml. Using one timer both as PWM and as capture input in one project is rejected by nxconfig check.

docs.title: Checking: nxconfig check
docs.text:
Run it after every change:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig check projects/<project>/project.yaml

It loads project, board and derivative together, resolves every name and checks what can be checked without building: pins and pin functions, resources used twice, clock and timing reachability, memory layout, diagnostic IDs, module parameters, and rules across levels (a CAN bus without interrupt rank). --json gives machine-readable messages; the exit code is 0 without error, otherwise 1. A few rules are applied only by the generators in the configure run and appear as rtegen: messages in step 6.

docs.title: Reading the messages
docs.text:
Every message has file, line, YAML path, severity and a sentence:

project.yaml:45 (memory.bootloader.size): error: bootloader size 0x8800 ends inside a sector of PFLASH (nearest sector boundaries 0x8000, 0x9000)
project.yaml:95 (can.CAN9): error: board buildtest_s32k148 has no can entry CAN9 (available: CAN0, CAN1)
buildtest_s32k148_min: ok (board buildtest_s32k148, S32K148, 0 warning(s))
  • error: the configuration cannot be built as it is; no ok line.
  • warning: it can be built, but something is unconfirmed or probably unintended. Read every warning.

docs.title: Sources and verify
docs.text: Values from a schematic you only have as a picture, from a handbook you could not get, or chosen as a placeholder are welcome, but marked: verify: true on the entry, a comment why, and source: (document and page) for values that are backed. Where a check depends on an unconfirmed fact, nxconfig warns instead of trusting it silently (a PWM group without backed power_stage facts gets a warning that its dead time is not checked). The rules for derivative values are in Adding a derivative.

docs.title: A board port is the exception, not a step
docs.text:
A new board needs no folder in ecu/platforms/: the build switches (OPENBSW_PLATFORM, PLATFORM_SUPPORT_*) are derived from the configuration levels and the family port (table in Your own ECU repository); the configure run prints each with the value it derived. ecu/platforms/<board>/Options.cmake is the place for a justified exception; write down why. The code itself comes from the family template under platforms/<family>/port and is never copied per board (../../ecu/platforms/README.md, German). Copying code from another board's port is an architecture gap to report, not a step of this guide.

Next: The application. With a repository of your own: Your own ECU repository.

docs.title: Beiträge an Eclipse OpenBSW (Kurzseite)
docs.text:
Status: planned (after R1). Vorbereitet sind Fehlermeldungen und Patches für Eclipse OpenBSW; nichts ist eingereicht. Eingereicht wird durch den Maintainer (Entscheidung 2026-09-17, F4): Beitragenden bereiten vor, der Maintainer signiert das Eclipse Contributor Agreement (dieselbe E-Mail-Adresse wie user.email in Git) und öffnet Issue und Pull Request mit seinem GitHub-Konto. Einreichungsreihenfolge je Paket: Issue zuerst, dann Patch mit git am auf upstream/main, Resolves: mit Issue-Nummer, pre-commit run --all-files, Pull Request.

Der Langtext (Issue-Texte, pr.md, tests.md, einreichen.md je Paket, upstream-stand.md mit der Recherche vom 2026-09-17/18) steht in der Git-Historie dieser Ordner (Commit vor dem Kürzungs-Commit zu einer eigenen Aufgabe). Die Patches (fix.patch, Basis OpenBSW 3b6e702) und 12-spi-adc-contracts/issue.md (verlinkt aus libs/bsp/bspSpi) bleiben hier als Arbeitsmaterial. Hintergrund und Auswahl: openbsw-naehe.md, Überblick: openbsw.md Abschnitt 7.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Look-up material: every key of the configuration files, with type, unit, whether it is required, its default, the values it accepts and what it means. The pages are generated from the schema in tools/nxconfig/model.py and checked in; a test fails as soon as schema and pages disagree. For how the levels fit together, read architecture overview, section 3 first.

The driver and service modules have a page of their own, see Modules.

Page Level File Fields Objects Derivative description Derivative mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml, mcudb/<family>/<part>.pinmux.yaml 254 44 Board description Board boards/<board>/board.yaml 230 47 Project description Project projects/<project>/project.yaml 221 46 Diagnostic description (diag.yaml) Project projects/<project>/diag.yaml 241 40 ECU description (rte.yaml) Project projects/<project>/rte.yaml 39 8

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Modules - the catalogue of the 15 modules in libs/bsw (device drivers, services, libraries) and the 6 in libs/bsp (contracts, MCU drivers), plus the 6 with a manifest in the ports (platforms/<family>/port, ecu/platforms/<board>): purpose, the board.yaml and project.yaml keys each one reads, host tests and the stated verification with its note. Generated from the module manifests (module.yaml), the module documentation and tools/test/tests.yaml by the same command and checked by the same --check. All 27 modules have a manifest, 1 of them parked (module.yaml.pending). Verification stated: hardware 13, mock 14; every module states it. What is still missing is listed in the section Gaps and by --gaps.

docs.title: Console
docs.text: Console commands - the 30 command groups (114 commands) the application can register on its text console: syntax, purpose, the build or module each one needs, which groups each project gets and which commands need a person at the board. Generated from the command registration and help texts in the C++ sources, the CMake conditions, the module manifests, the projects and the board READMEs by the same command and checked by the same --check.

docs.title: How to read the tables
docs.text:
Each object of a file has its own table; the heading is the YAML path of the object, [] stands for an entry of a list and <key> for a key of a map. Columns:

  • Field - full YAML path of the key.
  • Type - integer, number, string, boolean, list of …, map of … to …, or a link to the table of a nested object. A type written one of …, selected by kind means the key kind decides which table applies.
  • Unit - from the schema's naming convention <name>_<unit> (system_hz, deadtime_ns, shunt_uohm, t_nominal_ddegc in 0.1 °C) or from an explicit unit in the schema. none marks a number that has no physical unit on purpose (counts, indices, identifiers, addresses, selector and register values); missing marks a numeric field whose unit the schema does not state yet - a gap to be closed in the schema.
  • Required - yes if the key must be present. Optional keys take the default when left out.
  • Default - value that applies when the key is left out, written as YAML. null means not set; what that implies is in the description.
  • Allowed values - enumerations and the limits the schema enforces (ranges, lengths, patterns). item:, key: and value: apply to the entries of a list or map.
  • Description - from the schema: the description or comment of the field, otherwise the first sentence of its object type. missing in schema marks a field the schema does not explain. Nothing is filled in by hand: a gap here is a gap in the schema, and it is closed there.

Two short forms: an object whose table equals an earlier one (routines[].stop next to routines[].start) points to it and keeps its anchor. An object of the power stage or motor control is marked after R1: it stays in the schema and is checked, but is not part of the first release, so its page entry lists only the keys.

Not in these tables: rules that span several keys or files - references between levels, resource conflicts, derivative limits. Those are checked by tools/nxconfig (checks.py and the model validators) and reported with file, line and YAML path.

docs.title: Regenerating
docs.text:
.venv/Scripts/python tools/docgen            # rewrite the pages from the schema, from libs/ and from the console sources
.venv/Scripts/python tools/docgen --check    # exit 1 and name the pages if they are stale
.venv/Scripts/python tools/docgen --gaps     # list schema fields without description or unit, module and console gaps

The output is deterministic (no time stamps, schema order), so the check never fails without a change.

docs.title: Board description
docs.text:
What is fitted and wired on one printed circuit board: derivative and package, crystal, debug interface, fitted parts and how they are connected, buses, ADC channels with the circuit in front of the pin, PWM groups with their power stage, digital inputs and outputs. Hardware only - what the software uses of it is decided by the project.

Configuration level: Board. File: boards/<board>/board.yaml. Schema: Board in tools/nxconfig/model.py.

docs.title: board
docs.text:
Identification of the board: derivative, package, supply, clock and debug connection.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description board.name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Board name; by convention the same as the folder boards/<board>. board.mcu string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Derivative fitted on the board (derivative.name of a file in mcudb/). board.package string yes Package of the fitted derivative, one of its derivative.packages; selects the pin multiplexing table. board.supply_v number V no null Supply voltage of the MCU. The STM32 generator chooses the flash wait states for it. Left out: not stated. board.clock object no {} Fitted crystal or oscillator. board.debug object no null Debug connection. Left out: the build has no flash targets. board.adc_reference_mv integer mV no null > 0 Voltage at the ADC reference input (VREFH): scaling base of all ADC channels. board.description string no null Short description of the board for the reader.

docs.title: Console commands
docs.text: The application has a text console on the UART of the board (how to open it: build and flash, step 8). This page lists every command the neXtBSW application can register, with its syntax, what it does and in which build it exists. It is generated from the sources: the command registration and help texts in the C++ code, the CMake conditions and build options, the module manifests, the projects and the board READMEs. A test fails as soon as page and sources disagree. help on the console shows what the running build really contains.

docs.title: How to read this page
docs.text:
• Syntax - <group> <command> [parameters]. Parameters are shown where the help text states them (param: ... or Usage: ...); a command without them may still take parameters - the purpose column then says so in the words of its help text. help <group> prints the commands of one group.
  • Available - the conditions under which the group is built in: the family port it belongs to, the module a project must use, a PLATFORM_SUPPORT_* switch derived from the project and its board, a CMake build option for test builds. Only in adds conditions of a single command. Always means: in every build of the application.
  • Per-device groups - modules with console: instance in their manifest register one group per board device they serve; its name is the device's console parameter in project.yaml. They are listed as <name>, with the names the projects in this repository use in the project table.
  • Board rule - the command may only be used with a person at the board. The mark comes from the help text, which ends in the marker “(board rule)” (the earlier wordings “only with the maintainer at the board”, “board rules apply” still count, but tools/docgen --gaps reports them), or from the list “Only with a person at the board:” in the README of a board. The marker is what a person at the console sees in help, so every command in a board's list should carry it. Whether a command is dangerous depends on how the board is wired, so the board README is the authority; an unmarked command is not declared safe.

docs.title: Derivative description
docs.text:
Manufacturer facts of one MCU derivative, read-only for boards and projects: memory regions, peripheral instances and their clocks, pin multiplexing per package, clock limits, core, MPU and interrupt controller. One file per derivative under mcudb/<family>/, plus one generated pin multiplexing table per package.

Configuration level: Derivative. File: mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml, mcudb/<family>/<part>.pinmux.yaml. Schema: Derivative, PinmuxTable in tools/nxconfig/model.py.

254 fields in 44 objects. 0 fields have no description in the schema and 0 numeric fields have no unit; they are marked missing in schema and missing. How to read the tables: reference overview.
