docs.title: (top level)
docs.text:
Derivative file mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml: manufacturer facts of one MCU derivative.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description schema_version integer yes 1 Version of the file format; currently 1. derivative object yes Identification, core and packages of the derivative. memory list of object no [] Memory regions (flash, RAM, EEPROM window). instances map of string to object yes Peripheral instances; key: instance name as in the reference manual (e.g. FlexCAN0, LPSPI1), which boards use in instance. pinmux map of string to object no {} Pin multiplexing per package; key: package name from derivative.packages. device_header object no null Vendor device header of the derivative. clock object no null Clock facts: oscillators, PLL and frequency limits. mpu object no null Memory protection unit. Left out: no MPU described; code that needs it stops with an error. uid object no null Unique chip identification. Left out: unknown; a project with a bootloader needs it. vim object no null Vectored interrupt manager, VIM cores only. Left out: not described, no interrupt ranks possible. eeprom_emulation object no null Codes of the one-time partition of the emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx FlexNVM). Left out: the derivative has no partitionable emulated EEPROM; a project with nvm.partition is rejected. pin_interrupts object no null Pins that can raise an interrupt on an edge, their lines and vectors. Left out: not described; a project with pin_events is rejected. comparators list of object no [] After R1. Analogue comparators with reference DAC whose output reaches a fault input of a PWM timer (hardware threshold). Empty: not described; a project with hw_thresholds is rejected. trigger_router object no null After R1. Trigger router between peripherals (PWM timer triggers to sample sequencers and fault inputs). Left out: not described; a project with sample_groups is rejected. sample_sequencers list of object no [] Sample sequencers that convert a list of channels on one ADC after one hardware trigger. Empty: not described; a project with sample_groups is rejected.

docs.title: derivative
docs.text:
Identification and core of the derivative, packages and where its facts come from.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description derivative.name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Derivative name as the manufacturer writes it (e.g. S32K144); boards refer to it in board.mcu. derivative.family string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Family of the derivative (e.g. s32k1xx, stm32): selects the family clock model, the generators and the platform code. derivative.core string yes Processor core, a key of the core table of tools/nxconfig (e.g. cortex-m4f). derivative.fpu string no null none, sp, dp FPU variant: none, single precision (sp) or double precision (dp). Left out: the only variant the core has. derivative.nvic_priority_bits integer bit no null 2 to 8 NVIC cores: number of implemented interrupt priority bits. derivative.features list of string no [] item: lmem_cache Optional core features: lmem_cache is the LMEM processor code cache (S32K14x), switched on at start-up. derivative.packages list of string yes at least 1 item Package names of the derivative (e.g. LQFP100); board.package is one of them. derivative.pin_pattern string yes Regular expression of the pin names; every pin a board names must match it. derivative.sources list of string no [] Documents and repository files the facts of this file come from. derivative.verify boolean no false true: the entry as a whole is not confirmed by a source in the repository. derivative.example boolean no false true: format example only, not for real projects; using it gives a warning. derivative.jlink_device string no null J-Link device name, if it differs from the derivative name. derivative.pyocd_target string no null pyOCD target type, if it differs from the derivative name in lower case. derivative.openocd_target string no null OpenOCD target script, e.g. target/stm32f4x.cfg.

docs.title: memory[]
docs.text:
Memory of the derivative. Partitioning (bootloader, application, NvM) is decided by the project.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description memory[].name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Region name (e.g. PFLASH, SRAM_L); the project refers to it in memory. memory[].kind string yes code_flash, data_flash, ram, eeprom_ram Kind of memory: program flash, data flash, RAM or the RAM window of an emulated EEPROM. memory[].start integer none yes ≥ 0 Start address of the region. memory[].size integer byte yes > 0 Size of the region. memory[].sector_size integer byte no null > 0 Flash: smallest erasable unit. A flash region needs it or sectors. memory[].sectors list of object no null Flash with unequal sectors (e.g. STM32F4): sector table from the start of the region. memory[].program_size integer byte no null > 0 Flash: smallest programmable unit (S32K1 phrase: 8 bytes). memory[].source string no null Document the values of this entry come from (data sheet, reference manual, schematic), with section or page. memory[].verify boolean no false true: the entry is not confirmed by its source; checks that depend on it warn instead of trusting it.

docs.title: memory[].sectors[]
docs.text:
count consecutive flash sectors of size bytes (sector table of a flash with unequal sectors).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description memory[].sectors[].size integer byte yes > 0 Size of each sector of the group. memory[].sectors[].count integer none yes > 0 Number of consecutive sectors of this size.

docs.title: instances.<key>
docs.text:
One peripheral instance of the derivative. class_ is family neutral (timer, not FTM or TIM).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description instances.<key>.class string yes adc, timer, spi, can, uart, i2c, flexio, ethernet, qspi, i2s, gpio Family-neutral kind of the peripheral (timer, not FTM or TIM; gpio for a GPIO port that is an instance of its own, rm4x GIOA). Decides which board and project entries may use the instance. instances.<key>.channels integer none no null > 0 Timer: number of channels of the instance. GPIO port: number of pins of the port (their pin function is GPIO in the pin multiplexing table). instances.<key>.first_channel integer none no 0 ≥ 0 Timer only: number of the first channel, 1 where the manufacturer counts from 1 (TIM1_CH1). instances.<key>.resolution_bits integer bit no null > 0 ADC only: resolution of the converter. instances.<key>.channel_pattern string no null ADC only: regular expression of the external channel names (e.g. SE([0-9]\|1[0-5])), checked against adc[].channel of the board. instances.<key>.internal_channels list of string no [] ADC only: names of the inputs without pin (bandgap, reference, supply monitor) a project may use in adc_internal. instances.<key>.message_buffers integer none no null > 0 CAN only: number of message buffers (mailboxes) of the instance. Left out: unknown. instances.<key>.clock object no null Functional clock of the instance. Left out: unknown; a project that uses the instance gets an error. instances.<key>.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify.

docs.title: instances.<key>.clock
docs.text:
Functional clock of one peripheral instance (s32k1xx: clock gate of the PCC, fields PCCn.PCS/CGC).

Fact and decision are split (doc/architecture/README.md, section 4):

  • the derivative names what the hardware allows - the selectable sources (sources), the asynchronous outputs the instance is wired to (divider) and the limit of the functional clock (max_hz), each with its source like every mcudb value,
  • the project decides which of them is used (project.yaml peripheral_clocks.<instance>),
  • default is the choice that applies to a project which decides nothing. Without it an instance the project uses and does not choose a clock for is an error, so no value has to be invented for a derivative whose data sheet values are missing.

An instance without a clock select (select bus, core or none) has no sources: there is nothing to decide. Neither has an instance that runs on a named clock domain of the global clock module (domain, rm4x: VCLK, VCLK2, VCLKA1): its frequency follows from the domain the family clock model sets up.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description instances.<key>.clock.sources list of string no [] item: SOSC, SIRC, FIRC, SPLL Clock sources the clock select of the instance offers. Empty for an instance without clock select (then select is set). instances.<key>.clock.divider list of integer no [] item: 1, 2 Asynchronous outputs DIVx of the sources the instance is wired to (1: DIV1, 2: DIV2). instances.<key>.clock.default object no null Clock choice that applies when the project names none. Left out: a project that uses the instance must choose its clock in peripheral_clocks. instances.<key>.clock.max_hz integer Hz no null > 0 Maximum functional clock of the instance (limit of the DIVx output) as the reference manual states it. Left out: no limit stated. instances.<key>.clock.select string no null bus, core, none For an instance without clock select: bus or core (runs on that clock), none (the clock is chosen inside the peripheral, e.g. s32k1xx FlexCAN CTRL1.CLKSRC). instances.<key>.clock.domain string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ For an instance without clock select of its own that runs on a named clock domain of the global clock module (rm4x: VCLK, VCLK2, VCLKA1): the name of that domain, a key of clock.max_hz. Given alone, without sources, select, divider, default and max_hz. instances.<key>.clock.source string no null Same as memory[].source. instances.<key>.clock.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify. instances.<key>.clock.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: instances.<key>.clock.default
docs.text:
One clock of a peripheral: source and the asynchronous output of that source it is wired to.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description instances.<key>.clock.default.select string yes SOSC, SIRC, FIRC, SPLL Clock source that feeds the instance (s32k1xx: SOSC, SIRC, FIRC or SPLL, the value of PCCn.PCS). instances.<key>.clock.default.divider integer no null 1, 2 Asynchronous output of the source the clock is taken from: 1 for DIV1, 2 for DIV2. In a project entry it may be left out when the derivative allows only one output.

docs.title: pinmux.<key>
docs.text:
Pin multiplexing of one package: generated table file or (examples, tests) an inline table.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description pinmux.<key>.file string no null Generated table <part>.pinmux.yaml, relative to the derivative file. Exactly one of file and signals. pinmux.<key>.signals map of string to map of string to integer or map of string to integer none no null value: value: ≥ 0; value: value: key: pattern ^[a-z0-9_]+$; value: value: value: ≥ 0 Inline table (format examples, tests): signal -> pin -> function selector, as in the pin multiplexing file. pinmux.<key>.complete boolean no true false: partial data; mismatches with the table are warnings instead of errors. pinmux.<key>.verify boolean no false true: the table is taken from another package or not confirmed. pinmux.<key>.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: device_header
docs.text:
Vendor device header the family code includes for this derivative (mcu.h).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description device_header.file string yes Include path of the header, e.g. 3rdparty/nxp/S32K148.h. device_header.describes string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Derivative the header was written for; may be a superset of this one. device_header.source string no null Where the header comes from or which file adapts it. device_header.generated_by string no null regdesc2header The header is not in the repository but generated at configure time. regdesc2header: from the register description mcudb/<family>/registers/*.yaml, written from the reference manual for a family without SVD, with mcudb/<family>/tools/regdesc2header.py. Left out: the header must be in the include path.

docs.title: clock
docs.text:
Clock facts of the derivative. Which source feeds what is the family clock model (tools/nxconfig/clock.py).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.internal map of string to integer Hz no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$; value: > 0 Frequency of each internal oscillator; key: its name (e.g. FIRC: 48000000). clock.oscillator object no null External oscillator input. Left out: the derivative has none. clock.pll object no null PLL limits. Left out: the derivative has no PLL. clock.lpo object no null Frequency range of the low power oscillator that clocks the MCU watchdog. Left out: not described; a family whose watchdog runs on it (s32k1xx) cannot derive its safety timing then (error at clock.lpo). clock.max_hz map of string to integer Hz no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$; value: > 0 Maximum frequency per clock domain (core, bus, ...) in the run mode the drivers use. clock.system_source_max_hz map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Stricter domain maxima that apply only while a given source feeds the system clock (s32k14x: BUS_CLK 40 MHz with the SPLL as system clock). Key: system clock source of the family clock model. clock.output_max_hz object no null Maximum of every asynchronous clock output in the run mode the drivers use (s32k1xx: SPLLDIV1, FIRCDIV2, ...). The family clock model chooses the output dividers from it (the smallest divider within the limit). Left out: the outputs stay undivided. clock.pcc map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Clock gates of peripherals that are not listed in instances because no generator configures them yet, but whose clock the clock driver switches on (s32k1xx: LPIT, LPTMR0). Key: name of the gate. clock.flash_wait_states object no null Flash read wait states per band of the flash clock. Left out: not described (the flash needs none, or the family code does not configure them). clock.source_numbers object no null Number of every clock source in the source select fields (rm4x GHVSRC). Needed by a family clock model with numbered sources (rm4x). Left out: the family has none. clock.external_max_hz object no null Maximum of every external clock input (rm4x EXTCLKIN1, EXTCLKIN2); keys are names of source_numbers. Left out: no external clock input described. clock.oscillator_monitor object no null Window of the oscillator clock monitor. Left out: no monitor described; the board's oscillator is only checked against oscillator. clock.domain_dividers map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ How each named clock domain is derived (rm4x: VCLK, VCLK2, VCLKA1, RTICLK); key: domain name, which is also its key in max_hz. Peripheral instances name their domain in instances.<x>.clock.domain. clock.source string no null Same as memory[].source. clock.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify.

docs.title: clock.oscillator
docs.text:
External oscillator input (crystal or clock) the derivative accepts.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.oscillator.min_hz integer Hz yes > 0 Lowest crystal or clock frequency the oscillator input accepts. clock.oscillator.max_hz integer Hz yes > 0 Highest crystal or clock frequency the oscillator input accepts. clock.oscillator.source string no null Same as memory[].source. clock.oscillator.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify.

docs.title: clock.pll
docs.text:
PLL fed by the oscillator: output = oscillator / input_divider * multiplier / output_divider.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.pll.input_hz list of integer Hz yes exactly 2 items; item: > 0 [min, max] of the PLL reference after the input divider. clock.pll.vco_hz list of integer Hz yes exactly 2 items; item: > 0 [min, max] of the VCO frequency (reference * multiplier). clock.pll.input_divider list of integer none yes exactly 2 items; item: > 0 [min, max] of the input divider between oscillator and PLL reference. clock.pll.multiplier list of integer none yes exactly 2 items; item: > 0 [min, max] of the feedback multiplier. clock.pll.output_dividers list of integer none yes at least 1 item; item: > 0 Dividers between VCO and PLL output the hardware offers (s32k1xx: fixed 2). With output_divider_stages: every product of the stages, ascending. clock.pll.output_divider_stages list of list of integer none no [] item: exactly 2 items; item: item: > 0 Output divider in stages, in signal order: [min, max] of each stage (rm4x: OD 1..8, then R 1..32). The PLL output is VCO / (product of the stages). Left out: one stage with the dividers of output_dividers. clock.pll.post_divider_input_max_hz integer Hz no null > 0 Maximum of the clock between the first and the second output divider stage (rm4x: post-ODCLK = VCO / OD). Needs output_divider_stages. Left out: no limit stated. clock.pll.source string no null Same as memory[].source. clock.pll.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify.

docs.title: clock.lpo
docs.text:
Low power oscillator (LPO) of the derivative: always-on clock of the MCU watchdog and of other supervision timers (s32k1xx: the 128 kHz LPO of the PMC feeds the WDOG and, as LPO1K_CLK, the LPTMR of the period check). Timing that has to hold at every LPO of the data sheet (watchdog service interval, bounds of the period check) is derived from min_hz and max_hz by tools/nxconfig, never from the nominal value alone.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.lpo.nominal_hz integer Hz yes > 0 Typical frequency of the data sheet, the value the drivers load their counters for (s32k1xx: 128 kHz). clock.lpo.min_hz integer Hz yes > 0 Lowest frequency over process, voltage and temperature (data sheet minimum). clock.lpo.max_hz integer Hz yes > 0 Highest frequency over process, voltage and temperature (data sheet maximum). clock.lpo.source string no null Same as memory[].source. clock.lpo.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify. clock.lpo.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>
docs.text:
Maximum frequencies of named clocks with their evidence (fact of the derivative).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.max_hz map of string to integer Hz yes at least 1 character; key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$; value: > 0 Maximum frequency per clock; key: clock or clock output name of the family clock model. clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.source string no null Same as memory[].source. clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify. clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: clock.output_max_hz
docs.text: Same keys as clock.system_source_max_hz.<key> (table); the paths start with clock.output_max_hz instead of clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.

docs.title: clock.pcc.<key>
docs.text: Same keys as instances.<key>.clock (table); the paths start with clock.pcc.<key> instead of instances.<key>.clock.

docs.title: clock.flash_wait_states
docs.text:
Flash read wait states per band of the flash clock. The family code picks the band of the configured frequency and writes its values; how they are encoded in registers is family knowledge.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.flash_wait_states.clock string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Clock the bands refer to, a key of clock.max_hz (rm4x: HCLK). clock.flash_wait_states.bands list of object yes at least 1 item Bands in strictly ascending max_hz; the last one covers the maximum of clock. clock.flash_wait_states.source string no null Same as memory[].source. clock.flash_wait_states.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify. clock.flash_wait_states.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: clock.flash_wait_states.bands[]
docs.text:
Flash read wait states that apply up to one frequency of the flash clock.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.flash_wait_states.bands[].max_hz integer Hz yes > 0 Highest frequency of the flash clock this band covers; the next band starts above it. clock.flash_wait_states.bands[].data integer none yes ≥ 0 Data (random read) wait states (rm4x: FRDCNTL.RWAIT, for the EEPROM emulation bank EEPROM_CONFIG.EWAIT). clock.flash_wait_states.bands[].address integer none no 0 ≥ 0 Address setup wait states (rm4x: FRDCNTL.ASWSTEN). clock.flash_wait_states.bands[].pipeline boolean no false true: the flash pipeline mode is required in this band (rm4x: FRDCNTL.ENPIPE).

docs.title: clock.source_numbers
docs.text:
Number of every clock source in the source select fields of the clock module (rm4x: the value of GHVSRC, VCLKASRC and RCLKSRC and the bit in CSDISx). The family generator writes these numbers; the clock model uses the names.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.source_numbers.numbers map of string to integer none yes at least 1 character; key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$; value: ≥ 0 Source name -> number (rm4x: OSCIN: 0, PLL1: 1, HFLPO: 5). Numbers the document marks reserved are left out. clock.source_numbers.source string no null Same as memory[].source. clock.source_numbers.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify. clock.source_numbers.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: clock.external_max_hz
docs.text: Same keys as clock.system_source_max_hz.<key> (table); the paths start with clock.external_max_hz instead of clock.system_source_max_hz.<key>.

docs.title: clock.oscillator_monitor
docs.text:
Clock monitor of the oscillator input: the oscillator counts as failed outside the window reference / factor < f < reference * factor (rm4x CLKDET: all domains fed by OSCIN switch to HFLPO).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.oscillator_monitor.reference string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Internal clock the monitor compares with, a key of clock.internal (rm4x: HFLPO). clock.oscillator_monitor.factor integer none yes > 0 Width of the window: the oscillator has to lie above reference / factor and below reference * factor (both limits excluded). clock.oscillator_monitor.source string no null Same as memory[].source. clock.oscillator_monitor.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify. clock.oscillator_monitor.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: clock.domain_dividers.<key>
docs.text:
How a named clock domain is derived from its parent clock (rm4x: VCLK = HCLK / 1..16). The family clock model takes the smallest divider that keeps the domain within clock.max_hz.<domain>.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.domain_dividers.<key>.parent string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Clock the domain is divided from: a system clock of the family model (rm4x HCLK), another key of domain_dividers or a clock source of source_numbers. Where the domain has a source select, the source the family model uses (its reset default). clock.domain_dividers.<key>.dividers list of integer none yes at least 1 item; item: > 0 Dividers between parent and domain, ascending; [1] for a domain that follows its parent undivided. clock.domain_dividers.<key>.multiple_of string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ The frequency of the domain has to be an integer multiple of the frequency of this other domain (rm4x: VCLK2 of VCLK). Left out: no such rule. clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source object no null Dividers and limit that apply only while the domain runs from a source other than parent (rm4x RTICLK: divider 1/2/4/8, at most VCLK/3; from VCLK the divider is bypassed). Left out: no other source described. clock.domain_dividers.<key>.source string no null Same as memory[].source. clock.domain_dividers.<key>.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify. clock.domain_dividers.<key>.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source
docs.text:
Divider and limit of a clock domain while it runs from a source other than its parent.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source.dividers list of integer none yes at least 1 item; item: > 0 Dividers that apply to the other source, ascending (rm4x RTICLK: 1, 2, 4, 8). clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source.max_of string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Clock whose fraction limits the domain from another source (rm4x RTICLK: VCLK). clock.domain_dividers.<key>.other_source.divisor integer none yes > 0 The domain from another source runs at most max_of / divisor (rm4x RTICLK: 3).

docs.title: mpu
docs.text:
Memory protection unit of the derivative: how many region descriptors the hardware implements.

Which unit it is follows from the family (s32k1xx: NXP system MPU at the crossbar, no Arm core MPU), and so does the register encoding of the count (MPU_CESR[NRGD]); that knowledge belongs to the generator.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description mpu.regions integer none yes > 0 Number of region descriptors the hardware implements (RGD[0] to RGD[regions-1]). mpu.source string no null Same as memory[].source. mpu.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify.

docs.title: uid
docs.text:
Unique identification of the chip: the bootloader derives nothing from it itself, it reports it (DID 0xF18C) and the tester derives the device key of the chip from it (HMAC-SHA256 of the project's master key over these bytes). size bytes of memory mapped 32-bit words from address, read in address order, each word most significant byte first (s32k1xx: SIM_UIDH..SIM_UIDL, UID127..UID0; stm32: UID[31:0] first).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description uid.address integer none yes ≥ 0 Address of the first 32-bit word of the UID. uid.size integer byte yes 4 to 32 Length of the UID, whole 32-bit words. uid.source string no null Same as memory[].source. uid.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify.

docs.title: vim
docs.text:
Vectored interrupt manager of the derivative (core with interrupt controller vim).

The priority of a request is its channel number (0 highest). The project gives ranks as with an NVIC; checks.py turns them into a channel order over the channels that are not fixed. How many channels an instance needs and how the requests are moved to their channels is known only to the family generator.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description vim.channels integer none yes ≥ 2 Number of VIM channels (channel 0 to channels-1). vim.fixed list of object no [] Channels the hardware fixes to a request; they are never given to a ranked interrupt. vim.requests map of string to integer none no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$; value: ≥ 0 Default channel of every interrupt request (request name -> channel after reset). The family generator moves a request to the channel of its rank with the channel mapping (rm4x: CHANCTRL) and needs to know where each request starts. Key: request name as the family code uses it (e.g. DCAN1_LEVEL0). vim.source string no null Same as memory[].source. vim.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify.

docs.title: vim.fixed[]
docs.text:
VIM channel whose request the hardware fixes (e.g. an FIQ-only channel); interrupt ranks never get it.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description vim.fixed[].channel integer none yes ≥ 0 VIM channel number. vim.fixed[].request string yes What the channel serves, as the source document names it. vim.fixed[].kind string yes irq, fiq Interrupt kind of the channel; fiq never calls the RTOS. vim.fixed[].note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: eeprom_emulation
docs.text:
Partition of the emulated EEPROM: the codes of the one-time partition command of the derivative.

The emulated EEPROM is read and written through the RAM window of kind eeprom_ram in memory; its backup and the data flash share the region of kind data_flash. data_flash_bytes + backup_bytes of every code is that region's size. What the project chooses is nvm.partition of project.yaml.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description eeprom_emulation.sizes list of object yes at least 1 item EEPROM sizes the command accepts. eeprom_emulation.partitions list of object yes at least 1 item Splits of the partitionable flash the command accepts. eeprom_emulation.timing object no null Write times. Left out: the EEPROM driver keeps its own conservative time limit. eeprom_emulation.keys list of object no [] Key space sizes of the security module the partition command accepts (s32k1xx CSEc: FCCOB1). Empty: the derivative has no key space; the project must not ask for one. eeprom_emulation.endurance list of object no [] Guaranteed writes per ratio of backup to EEPROM in use (data sheet). Empty: not stated. eeprom_emulation.source string no null Same as memory[].source. eeprom_emulation.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify.

docs.title: eeprom_emulation.sizes[]
docs.text:
One EEPROM size the partition command accepts (s32k1xx: EEPROM data set size code, EEESIZE).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description eeprom_emulation.sizes[].code integer none yes 0 to 15 Code of the size in the partition command (s32k1xx: FCCOB4[3:0]). eeprom_emulation.sizes[].eeprom_bytes integer byte yes ≥ 0 Bytes of emulated EEPROM the code gives (0: none).

docs.title: eeprom_emulation.partitions[]
docs.text:
One split of the partitionable flash the partition command accepts (s32k1xx: FlexNVM partition code, DEPART). Several codes may give the same split; the project then names the one it wants.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description eeprom_emulation.partitions[].code integer none yes 0 to 15 Code of the split in the partition command (s32k1xx: FCCOB5[3:0]). eeprom_emulation.partitions[].data_flash_bytes integer byte yes ≥ 0 Bytes that stay data flash. eeprom_emulation.partitions[].backup_bytes integer byte yes ≥ 0 Bytes that back up the emulated EEPROM (EEPROM backup, not addressable any more).

docs.title: eeprom_emulation.timing
docs.text:
Write times of the emulated EEPROM. The generator derives the time limit of one write from them (the limit of the EEPROM driver in time, not in polls).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description eeprom_emulation.timing.backups list of object yes at least 1 item Times per EEPROM backup size; a split without its own entry uses the next larger backup. eeprom_emulation.timing.first_write_factor integer none no 1 > 0 Factor on the longest write for the first writes after a reset (s32k1xx data sheet: up to 2x for EEE clean-up). eeprom_emulation.timing.source string no null Same as memory[].source. eeprom_emulation.timing.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify.

docs.title: eeprom_emulation.timing.backups[]
docs.text:
Longest write to the emulated EEPROM for one backup size (data sheet).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description eeprom_emulation.timing.backups[].backup_bytes integer byte yes > 0 EEPROM backup size the time applies to. eeprom_emulation.timing.backups[].write_max_us integer µs yes > 0 Longest time of one 32-bit write to the emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx data sheet: teewr32b, max). eeprom_emulation.timing.backups[].partition_typ_ms integer ms no null > 0 Typical time of the partition command (s32k1xx data sheet: tpgmpart). Left out: not stated.

docs.title: eeprom_emulation.keys[]
docs.text:
One size of the key space of a hardware security module the partition command reserves in the emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx: CSEc key size, FCCOB1[1:0]). The bytes come off the end of the emulated EEPROM.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description eeprom_emulation.keys[].code integer none yes 0 to 255 Code of the key space in the partition command (s32k1xx: FCCOB1). eeprom_emulation.keys[].slots integer none yes ≥ 0 Key slots reserved (0: none). eeprom_emulation.keys[].system_slots integer none no 0 ≥ 0 Slots of these the module itself occupies once any slot is reserved (s32k1xx: MASTER_ECU_KEY, BOOT_MAC_KEY, BOOT_MAC). eeprom_emulation.keys[].eeprom_bytes integer byte yes ≥ 0 Bytes of emulated EEPROM the key space takes.

docs.title: eeprom_emulation.endurance[]
docs.text:
Guaranteed writes of the emulated EEPROM at one ratio of EEPROM backup to the EEPROM in use (data sheet). Below the smallest ratio the data sheet states nothing.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description eeprom_emulation.endurance[].ratio integer none yes > 0 EEPROM backup bytes per byte of emulated EEPROM in use. eeprom_emulation.endurance[].writes integer none yes > 0 Guaranteed writes at this ratio (data sheet, min).

docs.title: pin_interrupts
docs.text:
Pins that can raise an interrupt on an edge, their lines and vectors.

What the project decides (which input raises events, edge, debounce, rate limit, rank) is pin_events of project.yaml; nxconfig checks it against these facts: the pin must be reachable, pins that share a vector share its priority (same rank), and pins that need the same line exclude each other.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description pin_interrupts.edges list of string no ["rising", "falling", "both"] item: rising, falling, both Edges the edge detectors can react to: rising, falling, both (both edges at once). pin_interrupts.lines list of object no [] Edge detectors that serve one pin at a time. Empty: every interrupt-capable pin has its own detector. pin_interrupts.vectors list of object yes at least 1 item Vectors the edges arrive at. pin_interrupts.source string no null Same as memory[].source. pin_interrupts.verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify. pin_interrupts.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: pin_interrupts.lines[]
docs.text:
Edge detector that serves one pin at a time (stm32 EXTI line, s32k3xx SIUL2 EIRQ).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description pin_interrupts.lines[].name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Line name as the reference manual writes it (e.g. EXTI3, EIRQ5); vectors refer to it in lines. pin_interrupts.lines[].pins string no null Regular expression of the pins the line can be connected to (e.g. P[A-H]3). Exactly one of pins and signal. pin_interrupts.lines[].signal string no null Signal of the pin multiplexing table whose pins the line can be connected to (e.g. EIRQ5); the pins then depend on the package. Exactly one of pins and signal. pin_interrupts.lines[].note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: pin_interrupts.vectors[]
docs.text:
Interrupt vector (NVIC) or request (VIM) that pin edges arrive at.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description pin_interrupts.vectors[].name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Vector name as the family code uses it: the interrupt of the device header without _IRQn on an NVIC core (e.g. PORTC, EXTI9_5), a key of vim.requests on a VIM core (e.g. GIO_A). pin_interrupts.vectors[].pins string no null Regular expression of the pins with an edge detector of their own that end in this vector (e.g. PTC([0-9]\|1[0-7])). Exactly one of pins and lines. pin_interrupts.vectors[].lines list of string no [] item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Lines (lines[].name) that end in this vector. Exactly one of pins and lines. pin_interrupts.vectors[].note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: comparators[] (after R1)
docs.text: After R1: part of the schema and checked by tools/nxconfig, but not of the first release; the table is written when the object is. Keys: name, inputs, dac_bits, supply_reference, bandgap_mv, bandgap_min_mv, bandgap_max_mv, offset_max_mv, dac_inl_max_millilsb, propagation_max_ns, settling_max_us, fault_inputs, source, verify, note.

docs.title: trigger_router (after R1)
docs.text: After R1: part of the schema and checked by tools/nxconfig, but not of the first release; the table is written when the object is. Keys: name, sources, targets, timer_triggers, fault_inputs, register_lock, source, verify, note.

docs.title: sample_sequencers[]
docs.text:
Sample sequencer of one ADC: converts a list of channels after one trigger (s32k1xx: PDB).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description sample_sequencers[].name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Sequencer instance as in the reference manual (e.g. PDB0). sample_sequencers[].adc string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ ADC instance (instances, class adc) whose conversions the sequencer starts. sample_sequencers[].trigger_target string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Router output (trigger_router.targets[].name) that starts the sequencer. sample_sequencers[].slots integer none yes > 0 Conversions one trigger can start on the ADC (s32k1xx: pre-triggers of PDB channel 0, each with its own ADC configuration and result register). sample_sequencers[].back_to_back boolean yes true: the end of one conversion starts the next one (s32k1xx: back-to-back mode), no delay has to be planned between them. sample_sequencers[].counter_bits integer none yes > 0 Width of the delay counter from the trigger to the first conversion. sample_sequencers[].clock string yes core, bus Clock domain the delay counter runs on (s32k1xx: SYS_CLK = core clock). sample_sequencers[].start_clocks integer none yes 0 to 255 Clocks of the sequencer between the trigger (or the end of the previous conversion) and the start of a conversion, on top of the programmed delay. sample_sequencers[].source string no null Same as memory[].source. sample_sequencers[].verify boolean no false Same as memory[].verify. sample_sequencers[].note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: (top level)
docs.text:
Generated pin multiplexing file of one part (mcudb/<family>/<part>.pinmux.yaml).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description schema_version integer yes 1 Version of the file format; currently 1. part string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Part (derivative and package) the table describes. selector string yes Meaning of the numbers in the table, e.g. PORT_PCR.MUX. source string yes Source file the table was generated from, relative to mcudb/. signals map of string to map of string to integer or map of string to integer none yes value: value: ≥ 0; value: value: key: pattern ^[a-z0-9_]+$; value: value: value: ≥ 0 Signal -> pin -> function selector. Signal names are <instance>_<function> (e.g. FlexCAN0_RX, FTM0_CH3) or GPIO; the selector is a register value (s32k1xx PORT_PCR.MUX, stm32 GPIOx_AFR) or, where one number is not enough, named register values.

docs.title: Diagnostic description (diag.yaml)
docs.text:
Data identifiers, routines, sessions, security levels and the diagnostic trouble codes of one ECU software. The file is named by project.diag in project.yaml, checked against its schema and against itself by tools/nxconfig (with file, line and YAML path, before the build) and read by the UDS job generator, the fault memory generator and the ODX/PDX export. The addresses of the diagnostic connection - CAN identifiers, ISO-TP parameters and the security access of the bootloader - are project values and stand in project.yaml.

Configuration level: Project. File: projects/<project>/diag.yaml. Schema: DiagDescription in tools/nxconfig/model.py.

241 fields in 40 objects. 0 fields have no description in the schema and 0 numeric fields have no unit; they are marked missing in schema and missing. How to read the tables: reference overview.

docs.title: (top level)
docs.text:
Diagnostic description of a project (projects/<project>/diag.yaml, named by project.diag).

What one ECU software answers on the diagnostic connection and what its fault memory stores: sessions, security levels, data identifiers, routines, and the DTCs with their events, debouncing, enable conditions, operation cycle, aging, snapshots and extended data. The addresses of the connection (CAN ids, ISO-TP, bootloader security access) are project values and stand in project.yaml diagnostics.

The file is a description only. The UDS jobs and the fault memory are generated from it exports it as ODX/PDX.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description schema_version integer yes 1 Version of the file format; currently 1. sessions list of object no [] Diagnostic sessions of the ECU. Left out: the identifiers and routines name no session and everything is served in every session the UDS stack knows. security list of object no [] Security levels of the application. Left out: none (the security access of the bootloader stands in project.yaml). operation_cycles list of object no [] Operation cycles of the fault memory; required as soon as a DTC is described. enable_conditions list of object no [] Conditions a DTC can wait on before it updates its status. Left out: none. data_identifiers list of object no [] Data identifiers the ECU serves. routines list of object no [] Routines the ECU serves. fault_memory object no null Size and behaviour of the fault memory; required as soon as a DTC is described. bsw_dtc_range object no {} Block of DTC numbers of the basic software (neXtBSW range). Left out: 0x160000..0x16FFFF. dtcs list of object no [] Diagnostic trouble codes of the fault memory. dtc_groups list of object no [] Groups of DTCs the tester can clear with 14 besides all DTCs (0xFFFFFF) and a single DTC (ISO 14229-1, Annex D.1). Left out: none.

docs.title: sessions[]
docs.text:
One diagnostic session of the ECU (DiagnosticSessionControl, 10; ISO 14229-1, clause 9.2).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description sessions[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the session, unique in the file; identifiers and routines refer to it by this name. sessions[].id integer none yes 1 to 126 Session type of the sub-function. 0x01 default, 0x02 programming, 0x03 extended, 0x04 safety system; 0x40..0x5F are left to the manufacturer and 0x60..0x7E to the system supplier. The ranges ISO 14229-1 reserves are an error. sessions[].label string no null Readable name for the tester and for the ODX export (LONG-NAME). Left out: the export uses name. sessions[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC). sessions[].p2_ms integer ms no 50 > 0 P2 of this session: how long the ECU may take to answer before it has to ask the tester to wait. sessions[].p2_star_ms integer ms no 5000 > 0 P2* of this session: how long the tester waits after the ECU asked it to wait.

docs.title: security[]
docs.text:
One security level of the application (SecurityAccess, 27; ISO 14229-1, clause 9.4).

The security access of the bootloader is not described here: it is a project value (project.yaml diagnostics.bootloader.security), because the tester and the provisioning tool have to agree on it before any application exists.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description security[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the level, unique in the file. security[].level integer none yes 1 to 125 requestSeed sub-function of the level; it has to be odd, the matching sendKey is one higher (ISO 14229-1, clause 9.4). security[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. security[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC). security[].method string no "hmac-sha256" hmac-sha256 Method of the key calculation. hmac-sha256: the device key of the bootloader's security access (HMAC-SHA256 of the project master key and the chip UID, provisioned into the key sector) answers the seed; key = the first key_bytes of HMAC-SHA256(device key, "NXAK" + level + seed). The key is bound to the level, so the key of one level unlocks no other level and not the bootloader. seed_bytes and key_bytes at most 32. security[].seed_bytes integer byte no 4 1 to 255 Length of the seed the ECU sends. security[].key_bytes integer byte no 4 1 to 255 Length of the key the tester answers with. security[].attempts integer none no 3 1 to 255 Wrong keys in a row before the ECU refuses further attempts for delay_ms. security[].delay_ms integer ms no 10000 > 0 How long the ECU refuses further attempts after attempts wrong keys. security[].sessions list of string no null item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Sessions the level can be unlocked in. Left out: every session of the file except the default session.

docs.title: operation_cycles[]
docs.text:
One operation cycle of the fault memory (ISO 14229-1, D.2.1): what starts and ends a round of testing.

The status bits of a DTC that speak about "this operation cycle", the confirmation threshold and the aging counter all count in the cycle named here.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description operation_cycles[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the cycle, unique in the file; a DTC refers to it by this name. operation_cycles[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. operation_cycles[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC). operation_cycles[].kind string no "power" power, ignition, operation, other What the cycle follows: power (the ECU is supplied), ignition (terminal 15), operation (a manufacturer defined round of operation) or other. The fault memory treats all of them alike; the name is for the reader and the export. operation_cycles[].autostart boolean no true true: the cycle starts when the ECU starts and ends when it shuts down. false: the application starts and ends it.

docs.title: enable_conditions[]
docs.text:
One condition that has to hold before a DTC may update its status (ISO 14229-1, D.2.1).

While a condition of a DTC is not fulfilled its monitor result is discarded: the debounce counter keeps its value and no status bit changes.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description enable_conditions[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the condition, unique in the file; a DTC refers to it by this name. enable_conditions[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. enable_conditions[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC). enable_conditions[].port string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*){2}$ Provided port element of the ECU description that reports the condition as a boolean, Component.Port.Element. Exactly one of port and bsw. enable_conditions[].bsw string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$ Value of the basic software that reports the condition, e.g. ecu.state. Exactly one of port and bsw. enable_conditions[].initial boolean no false State of the condition before the source has reported for the first time. false: no DTC waiting on it updates until then.

docs.title: data_identifiers[]
docs.text:
One data identifier (DID) the ECU serves with 22 (read) and 2E (write).

The identifier is checked against the ranges of ISO 14229-1 Annex C.1 and against the identifiers the bootloader already answers (diagdesc.py). The length of the response follows from data.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description data_identifiers[].identifier integer none yes 0 to 65535 16-bit data identifier. Must lie in a range Annex C.1 leaves to the manufacturer or the system supplier, must not be one of the identifiers the bootloader answers, and must not appear twice in this file. data_identifiers[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the identifier, unique in the file; snapshots refer to it by this name and the export uses it as the short name. data_identifiers[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. data_identifiers[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC). data_identifiers[].group string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Free group name the tester can sort jobs by (FUNCT-CLASS), e.g. identification or actuator_test. Left out: no group. data_identifiers[].data list of object yes at least 1 item The values of the identifier in the order they stand on the wire; the length of the identifier is their total width. data_identifiers[].read boolean no true true: the identifier answers ReadDataByIdentifier (22). data_identifiers[].write boolean no false true: the identifier accepts WriteDataByIdentifier (2E). A constant source cannot be written. data_identifiers[].read_sessions list of string no null item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Sessions (sessions[].name) the identifier may be read in. Left out: every session of the file. data_identifiers[].write_sessions list of string no null item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Sessions the identifier may be written in; see read_sessions. Only with write. data_identifiers[].read_security string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Security level (security[].name) that has to be unlocked for reading. Left out: no security access needed. data_identifiers[].write_security string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Security level that has to be unlocked for writing; see read_security. Only with write.

docs.title: data_identifiers[].data[]
docs.text:
One value inside the data of a data identifier: a parameter plus where its value comes from.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description data_identifiers[].data[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the element, unique within its list; the export uses it as the short name of the parameter. data_identifiers[].data[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. data_identifiers[].data[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC). data_identifiers[].data[].type string yes uint8, uint16, uint32, int8, int16, int32, float32, ascii, bytes Type on the wire: an integer (uint8, uint16, uint32, int8, int16, int32), float32, a text (ascii) or raw bytes (bytes). ascii and bytes need length_bytes, the others take their width from the type. data_identifiers[].data[].length_bytes integer byte no null > 0 Only for ascii and bytes: width of the element on the wire - always exactly this many bytes: a shorter text is filled up with NUL (0x00), a longer one is cut, so that a tester can split a response by the description alone (e.g. several identifiers in one 22 response). For every other type the width follows from type and stating it is an error. data_identifiers[].data[].byte_order string no "big" big, little Byte order of an element wider than one byte. big is the order UDS uses for its own parameters and the default here; little only where the value is passed on unchanged from a little endian source. data_identifiers[].data[].unit string unit of the described value no null Physical unit of the value as it is shown (e.g. mV, degC, 1/min); the export uses it as the display name of the unit. Left out: the value has no unit (a count, an index, a text, raw bytes). data_identifiers[].data[].factor number none no 1.0 finite Physical value = factor * coded value + offset (the linear conversion of the export). Only for numeric types. data_identifiers[].data[].offset number none no 0.0 finite Added after factor; see there. Only for numeric types. data_identifiers[].data[].min number unit of the described value no null finite Smallest physical value the element takes; the export writes it as the lower limit. Left out: the range of the type. data_identifiers[].data[].max number unit of the described value no null finite Largest physical value the element takes; see min. data_identifiers[].data[].values list of object no null at least 1 item Text table of an integer element: one entry per coded value (the export writes it as a text table conversion). Only for integer types, and not together with factor, offset, min or max; each coded value only once. data_identifiers[].data[].source object yes Where this value comes from: an RTE port, a value of the basic software, or a constant. Every value of an identifier has its own source, so an identifier can mix a fixed byte with a live value (e.g. the number of modules of 0xF180 with the version text).

docs.title: data_identifiers[].data[].values[]
docs.text:
One line of a text table: a coded value and what the tester shows for it.

A list instead of a mapping, because the export writes one entry per line (COMPU-SCALE with its own text) and because the YAML loader of tools/nxconfig reads every mapping key as a string.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description data_identifiers[].data[].values[].value integer none yes Coded value as it stands on the wire. data_identifiers[].data[].values[].text string yes 1 to 64 characters What the tester shows for this value.

docs.title: data_identifiers[].data[].source
docs.text:
Where the data of an identifier comes from: exactly one of the three.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description data_identifiers[].data[].source.port string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*){2}$ Provided port element of the ECU description, Component.Port.Element (rte.yaml components). The value is read through the RTE. data_identifiers[].data[].source.bsw string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$ Value of the basic software in the notation of the rte.yaml connections, e.g. ecu.state or adc.mv.<CHANNEL>. Which names exist is resolved by the RTE generator, not here. data_identifiers[].data[].source.constant integer or string unit of the element it fills no null Fixed value that does not change at runtime (e.g. a hardware number or the number of modules of 0xF180). A text for ascii, a number for a numeric element; it has to fit the element (checked in diagdesc.py).

docs.title: routines[]
docs.text:
One routine the ECU serves with RoutineControl (31).

The identifier is checked against the ranges of ISO 14229-1 Annex F.1 and against the routines of the bootloader (diagdesc.py).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description routines[].identifier integer none yes 0 to 65535 16-bit routine identifier. Must lie in a range Annex F.1 leaves to the manufacturer or the system supplier and must not appear twice in this file. routines[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the routine, unique in the file. routines[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. routines[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC). routines[].group string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Same as data_identifiers[].group. routines[].start object yes startRoutine (sub-function 01); every routine has one. routines[].stop object no null stopRoutine (sub-function 02). Left out: the routine cannot be stopped. routines[].results object no null requestRoutineResults (sub-function 03). Left out: the routine reports no result of its own. routines[].sessions list of string no null item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Sessions (sessions[].name) the routine may run in. Left out: every session of the file. routines[].security string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Security level (security[].name) that has to be unlocked. Left out: none.

docs.title: routines[].start
docs.text:
One of the three steps of RoutineControl (31): start, stop or requestResults.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description routines[].start.call object yes What the step runs: a runnable of a component or a service of the basic software. routines[].start.request list of object no [] Parameters the tester sends with this step, in wire order. Left out: none. routines[].start.response list of object no [] Parameters the ECU answers with, in wire order. Left out: none.

docs.title: routines[].start.call
docs.text:
What one step of a routine runs: exactly one of the two.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description routines[].start.call.runnable string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Runnable of a component of the ECU description, Component.Runnable. routines[].start.call.bsw string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$ Service of the basic software in the notation of the rte.yaml connections, e.g. bsw.reset.request. Which names exist is resolved by the RTE generator, not here.

docs.title: routines[].start.request[]
docs.text:
One value on the wire: a parameter of a routine request or response.

Everything an ODX export needs to describe the value on the wire and in physical units is here: the coded type (type, length_bytes, byte_order), the conversion to the physical value (factor, offset, unit, or values for a text table) and its range (min, max). The byte position follows from the order of the list, the total length from the parameters - neither is configured.

The data of an identifier uses DiagDataElement, which adds where the value comes from.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description routines[].start.request[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Same as data_identifiers[].data[].name. routines[].start.request[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. routines[].start.request[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC). routines[].start.request[].type string yes uint8, uint16, uint32, int8, int16, int32, float32, ascii, bytes Same as data_identifiers[].data[].type. routines[].start.request[].length_bytes integer byte no null > 0 Same as data_identifiers[].data[].length_bytes. routines[].start.request[].byte_order string no "big" big, little Same as data_identifiers[].data[].byte_order. routines[].start.request[].unit string unit of the described value no null Same as data_identifiers[].data[].unit. routines[].start.request[].factor number none no 1.0 finite Same as data_identifiers[].data[].factor. routines[].start.request[].offset number none no 0.0 finite Added after factor; see there. Only for numeric types. routines[].start.request[].min number unit of the described value no null finite Same as data_identifiers[].data[].min. routines[].start.request[].max number unit of the described value no null finite Largest physical value the element takes; see min. routines[].start.request[].values list of object no null at least 1 item Same as data_identifiers[].data[].values.

docs.title: routines[].start.request[].values[]
docs.text:
One line of a text table: a coded value and what the tester shows for it.

A list instead of a mapping, because the export writes one entry per line (COMPU-SCALE with its own text) and because the YAML loader of tools/nxconfig reads every mapping key as a string.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description routines[].start.request[].values[].value integer none yes Coded value as it stands on the wire. routines[].start.request[].values[].text string yes 1 to 64 characters What the tester shows for this value.

docs.title: routines[].start.response[]
docs.text: Same keys as routines[].start.request[] (table); the paths start with routines[].start.response[] instead of routines[].start.request[].

docs.title: routines[].stop
docs.text: Same keys as routines[].start (table); the paths start with routines[].stop instead of routines[].start.

docs.title: routines[].results
docs.text: Same keys as routines[].start (table); the paths start with routines[].results instead of routines[].start.

docs.title: fault_memory
docs.text:
Size and behaviour of the fault memory as a whole (simplified AUTOSAR DEM).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description fault_memory.max_entries integer none yes 1 to 255 DTCs the memory holds at the same time. Fewer than the described DTCs is allowed (not all of them are stored at once) and is reported as a warning. fault_memory.overflow string no "replace_oldest" replace_oldest, keep_oldest What happens when the memory is full and a further DTC matures: replace_oldest displaces the least important, oldest entry (see priority), keep_oldest discards the new one. fault_memory.snapshot_records_max integer none no 1 0 to 254 Snapshot records stored per DTC. 0: no snapshots are stored. fault_memory.extended_records_max integer none no 1 0 to 143 Extended data records stored per DTC. 0: none. fault_memory.aging_cycle string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Operation cycle the aging of a DTC counts in when the DTC names none. Left out: the cycle of the DTC. fault_memory.cycle_ms integer ms no 10 1 to 1000 Cycle of the fault memory: every event is sampled once per cycle, so a counter debouncing of n samples takes n cycles, and time debouncing counts in steps of this. Reported BSW events are taken over once per cycle as well. fault_memory.write_interval_ms integer ms no 1000 0 to 3600000 Shortest distance between two writes of a changed fault memory block to the persistent memory (NvM write policy CHANGE, wear of an EEPROM emulation); the run-down writes what is left. 0: only at the run-down.

docs.title: bsw_dtc_range
docs.text:
The block of DTC numbers the basic software raises its own DTCs in (configurable since an earlier change).

Numbering plan and default: tools/nxconfig/bswdtc.py. A DTC of a BSW event the plan knows leaves number out and gets base + the offset of its source, so moving the base moves every BSW DTC. Project DTCs are numbered outside the range (a project DTC inside it is reported as a warning).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description bsw_dtc_range.base integer none no 1441792 256 to 16776704 First number of the range; it is also the group identifier of the whole range and never a DTC. A multiple of 0x100. Left out: 0x160000 (P16xx-yy, the default of neXtBSW). bsw_dtc_range.size integer none no 65536 256 to 16776704 Numbers in the range, a multiple of 0x100 (one block per source of the plan). Below 0x900 the later sources of the plan have no number. Left out: 0x10000.

docs.title: dtcs[]
docs.text:
One diagnostic trouble code of the fault memory.

The number is a 3-byte DTC in the ISO 14229-1 format (Annex D.4, format identifier 0x01); the ranges Annex D.1 reserves for legislation and for the group identifiers are checked in diagdesc.py. Warning lamp and OBD are deliberately not described (a project decision, 2026-09-21): the status byte has no warningIndicatorRequested source here and the OBD class bits of Annex D.3.3 stay at the unclassified value.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtcs[].number integer none no null 0 to 16777215 3-byte DTC number. 0x000000..0x0000FF is reserved for legislation and 0xFFFF00..0xFFFFFF are the group identifiers (Annex D.1); the number must not appear twice in this file. Left out: only for an event of the basic software that the neXtBSW numbering plan knows (tools/nxconfig/bswdtc.py) - the number is bsw_dtc_range.base plus the offset of the plan, so it follows the range of the project. dtcs[].bsw_instance integer none no null 0 to 255 Low byte of a derived number for a BSW source with instances: index of the used CAN bus for can.busoff.<BUS>, cause for safety.<cause>, NvM block index for nvm.*.<BLOCK>. Only with number left out and only for such a source. dtcs[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the DTC, unique in the file. dtcs[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. dtcs[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC). dtcs[].group string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Same as data_identifiers[].group. dtcs[].display_code string no null 1 to 16 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ Code the tester shows instead of the number (e.g. P061600), for the ODX export (DISPLAY-TROUBLE-CODE). It is not derived: this description uses the ISO 14229-1 DTC format (Annex D.4, 0x01), which fixes no display text. Left out: the export has none and the tester shows the number - except for a derived BSW number (number left out), which gets its SAE J2012 display (0x160100: P160100). dtcs[].severity string no "none" none, maintenance_only, check_at_next_halt, check_immediately Severity of the DTC (Annex D.3.2, bits 7..5 of the severity byte): none, maintenance_only, check_at_next_halt or check_immediately. dtcs[].event object yes The monitor whose result sets and clears the DTC. dtcs[].debounce object yes How the raw monitor result becomes a matured test result. dtcs[].operation_cycle string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Operation cycle (operation_cycles[].name) the status bits, the confirmation and the aging of this DTC count in. dtcs[].enable_conditions list of string no [] item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Conditions (enable_conditions[].name) that all have to hold before the status of this DTC is updated. Left out: none. dtcs[].confirmation_threshold integer none no 1 1 to 255 Operation cycles with a failed test before the confirmed bit is set and the entry is stored (Annex D.2.1). 1: the first failed test confirms. dtcs[].aging object no null When a confirmed DTC is forgotten again. Left out: it is kept until the tester clears it. dtcs[].priority integer none no 1 1 to 255 Which DTC wins when the fault memory is full: 1 is the most important entry, a larger number is displaced first. dtcs[].snapshots list of object no [] Snapshot records of this DTC. Left out: none. dtcs[].extended_data list of object no [] Extended data records of this DTC. Left out: none.

docs.title: dtcs[].event
docs.text:
The monitor whose result sets and clears one DTC: exactly one source.

Every DTC has an event; a DTC nothing can set is a description of nothing and is reported as an error.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtcs[].event.port string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*){2}$ Provided port element of the ECU description that reports the test result, Component.Port.Element. dtcs[].event.bsw string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)+$ Monitor of the basic software that reports the test result, e.g. can.busoff.<BUS>. Which names exist is resolved by the RTE generator, not here. dtcs[].event.description string no null What the monitor tests, for the reader and the export. dtcs[].event.result string no null boolean, qualifier, status, limit How the value of the source becomes a test result, sampled once per fault memory cycle (fault_memory.cycle_ms): boolean (true: failed), qualifier (a signal qualifier of Rte_Qlf.h: QLF_OK passed, QLF_DEBOUNCE no result, every error failed), status (the AUTOSAR event status: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 prepassed, 3 prefailed, other values no result) or limit (failed_above/failed_below). Left out: derived by the RTE generator - limit if a limit is given, qualifier for a qualifier source, boolean for a boolean port. A source the BSW reports itself (a bsw name the RTE does not know) reports AUTOSAR event states through dem::IFaultMemory::report(). dtcs[].event.failed_above integer none no null limit: the sample is failed while the value is above this (in the unit of the source), passed otherwise. dtcs[].event.failed_below integer none no null limit: the sample is failed while the value is below this.

docs.title: dtcs[].debounce
docs.text:
How the raw result of a monitor becomes a matured test result: exactly one of the two ways.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtcs[].debounce.counter object no null Debouncing by counting test samples. dtcs[].debounce.time object no null Debouncing by time.

docs.title: dtcs[].debounce.counter
docs.text:
Debouncing by counting test samples (AUTOSAR DEM counter debouncing).

Every failed sample moves the counter up by increment, every passed sample down by decrement. At failed_threshold the DTC is failed, at passed_threshold it is passed. The counter is the fault detection counter ISO 14229-1 D.6 describes.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtcs[].debounce.counter.failed_threshold integer none no 127 1 to 127 Counter value at which the test counts as failed. dtcs[].debounce.counter.passed_threshold integer none no -128 -128 to -1 Counter value at which the test counts as passed. dtcs[].debounce.counter.increment integer none no 1 1 to 255 Step of one failed sample. dtcs[].debounce.counter.decrement integer none no 1 1 to 255 Step of one passed sample. dtcs[].debounce.counter.jump_up integer none no null -128 to 127 Value a counter below it jumps to on a failed sample, before the sample adds increment. Left out: 0 - the first failed sample after passed ones moves the counter over zero, so the DTC is prefailed at once (ISO 14229-1, D.6). dtcs[].debounce.counter.jump_down integer none no null -128 to 127 Value a counter above it jumps to on a passed sample, before the sample subtracts decrement. Left out: 0 (the first passed sample after failed ones moves it below zero).

docs.title: dtcs[].debounce.time
docs.text:
Debouncing by time: the monitor has to report the same result for this long before it counts.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtcs[].debounce.time.failed_ms integer ms yes > 0 How long the monitor has to report failed without interruption before the test counts as failed. dtcs[].debounce.time.passed_ms integer ms yes > 0 How long the monitor has to report passed without interruption before the test counts as passed.

docs.title: dtcs[].aging
docs.text:
When a confirmed DTC is forgotten again (ISO 14229-1, D.2.1 and D.7).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtcs[].aging.threshold_cycles integer none yes 1 to 255 Operation cycles that have to end without the test failing before the confirmed bit is cleared and the entry is released. dtcs[].aging.cycle string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Operation cycle (operation_cycles[].name) the aging counts in. Left out: the cycle of the DTC.

docs.title: dtcs[].snapshots[]
docs.text:
One snapshot record of a DTC: the data identifiers stored when the DTC is first confirmed.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtcs[].snapshots[].record_number integer none yes 1 to 254 Number of the record, unique per DTC. 0x00 and 0xFF are reserved by ISO 14229-1 (0xFF requests all records). dtcs[].snapshots[].dids list of string yes at least 1 item; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Data identifiers (data_identifiers[].name) stored in the record, in this order; each one once. dtcs[].snapshots[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. dtcs[].snapshots[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC).

docs.title: dtcs[].extended_data[]
docs.text:
One extended data record of a DTC (ISO 14229-1, D.8).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtcs[].extended_data[].record_number integer none yes 1 to 143 Number of the record, unique per DTC. Annex D.8 leaves 0x01..0x8F to the manufacturer; 0x00, 0x90..0xFD are reserved and 0xFE/0xFF request all records. dtcs[].extended_data[].data list of object yes at least 1 item The values of the record in the order they stand on the wire. dtcs[].extended_data[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. dtcs[].extended_data[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC).

docs.title: dtcs[].extended_data[].data[]
docs.text:
One value of an extended data record: a counter of the fault memory or a data identifier.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtcs[].extended_data[].data[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the value inside the record, unique in the record. dtcs[].extended_data[].data[].counter string no null occurrence_counter, aging_counter, fault_detection_counter, failed_cycles, operation_cycles_since_first_failed Counter of the fault memory: occurrence_counter (how often the DTC matured), aging_counter (cycles counted towards aging), fault_detection_counter (the debounce counter, D.6), failed_cycles (operation cycles with a failed test) or operation_cycles_since_first_failed. Each is one byte; exactly one of counter and did. dtcs[].extended_data[].data[].did string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Data identifier (data_identifiers[].name) stored in the record. Exactly one of counter and did. dtcs[].extended_data[].data[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. dtcs[].extended_data[].data[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC).

docs.title: dtc_groups[]
docs.text:
A group of DTCs a tester clears with ClearDiagnosticInformation (14).

group is the 3-byte groupOfDTC value the tester sends, first..last the DTC numbers it stands for. ISO 14229-1, Annex D.1 leaves the groups to the vehicle manufacturer and reserves 0xFFFF00..0xFFFFFE for the functional groups (e.g. 0xFFFF33 emissions, 0xFFFFD0 safety); 0xFFFFFF (all DTCs) and a single DTC number need no entry. Checked in diagdesc.py, generated by tools/diaggen as the table diagDtcGroups() of ecu/uds.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description dtc_groups[].name string yes 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ Name of the group, unique in the file. dtc_groups[].bsw boolean no false true: the group of the whole neXtBSW range - group, first and last are derived from bsw_dtc_range (base, base, base + size - 1) and are left out. dtc_groups[].group integer none no null 0 to 16777215 groupOfDTC value of the group (Annex D.1): a group of the vehicle manufacturer or a functional group 0xFFFF00..0xFFFFFE. Not 0xFFFFFF (all DTCs) and not the number of a described DTC; unique in the file. Required unless bsw is true. dtc_groups[].first integer none no null 0 to 16777215 Lowest DTC number of the group. Required unless bsw is true. dtc_groups[].last integer none no null 0 to 16777215 Highest DTC number of the group (at least first, below the group identifiers 0xFFFF00). Required unless bsw is true. dtc_groups[].label string no null Same as sessions[].label. dtc_groups[].description string no null Sentence for the reader and for the ODX export (DESC).

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Every directory in libs/bsw (device drivers, services, libraries), libs/bsp (contracts and MCU drivers) and every module with a manifest in a port (family port templates platforms/<family>/port, board ports ecu/platforms/<board>), with what it is for, which configuration keys it reads, which host tests cover it and how far it is verified. The page is generated from the module manifests (module.yaml), the module documentation under doc/ and the test list tools/test/tests.yaml; a test fails as soon as page and sources disagree. How drivers are cut into modules: driver granularity (German). What the configuration keys mean: board description and project description.

  • Purpose - the description of the manifest. not stated means there is no manifest or it has no description.
  • Manifest - module.yaml is read by tools/nxconfig and tools/bswgen; a parked module.yaml.pending is not, so such a module cannot be used by a project yet.
  • Host tests - entries of tools/test/tests.yaml that list a file in the module directory under covers or name the module under modules (tests that lie elsewhere, e.g. in a generator's test directory; tools/test refuses a name without a manifest); run one with .venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k <name>.
  • Verification - the manifest field verification: none (not yet), mock (host tests, register models, generator and build tests) or hardware (behaviour confirmed on a real board), with the sentence verification_note on what is confirmed on a board and what is not (linked as note in the table, in full in the module section). Both are set by hand from the changelog; nothing here is inferred from the changelog or the module documentation, a module without the field reads not stated.

All 27 modules have a manifest, 1 of them parked (module.yaml.pending). Verification stated: hardware 13, mock 14; every module states it. What is missing per module: Gaps.
