docs.title: autosarBase
docs.text:
AUTOSAR base types Std_Types.h, Platform_Types.h and Compiler.h for the RTE and the generated component code (32-bit ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-R, little endian)

  • Directory: libs/bsw/autosarBase, manifest: module.yaml, kind: library
  • Verification: mock - Type definitions only; sizes, signedness, limits and CPU macros checked by a host type test and by arm-none-eabi-gcc -fsyntax-only for Cortex-M4F, Cortex-M0+ and Cortex-R4, type identity with <stdint.h>, besides compiling the target builds.
  • Public headers: Compiler.h, Platform_Types.h, Std_Types.h
  • Integration: CMake target autosarBase

docs.title: bccMc33771 (after R1)
docs.text:
NXP MC33771C battery cell controller (7-14 cells) in SPI mode, complex device driver

After R1: not part of the first release. Directory libs/bsw/bccMc33771 (not published, available on request), manifest: pending (module.yaml.pending). Keys, parameters and verification are listed once the module is released.

docs.title: canPhyPassive
docs.text:
CAN transceiver without software control (mode pins strapped by the board), always ready

  • Directory: libs/bsw/canPhyPassive, manifest: module.yaml, kind: device_driver
  • Verification: mock - Covered by generator and target build tests only (build profile S32K148, D-CAN of the eval board); no bus through a passive transceiver has been checked on a board yet.
  • Public headers: can/PassiveCanPhy.h
  • Provides roles: can_phy
  • Integration: CMake target canPhyPassive
  • Board configuration (board.yaml):
    • devices[].part matching SN65HVD1050*, TJA1051* - one instance per board device; devices[].module: canPhyPassive chooses this module where several modules serve the part
    • can[].phy - the CAN buses the device is the transceiver of (role can_phy)
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • use.can - the transceiver role is served for the CAN buses the project uses

docs.title: canSystem
docs.text:
CAN buses of the ECU; hardware independent parts - transmit gate (CanPhyGate, follows the readiness reports of the phy providers through CanPhyReadiness) and bus state with bus off counters (CanBusMonitor), console commands in the console context with a short call into the CAN task (ContextCall), receive log lines that fit one logger entry (CanFrameLog), behaviour after bus off with log series, doubling pause and dropping pending frames (CanBusOffRecovery; project values per bus can.<bus>.bus_off)

  • Directory: libs/bsw/canSystem, manifest: module.yaml, kind: service
  • Verification: hardware - Transmit gate, bus state up to error passive and the console commands with their short call into the CAN task are confirmed on the eval board on CAN0; bus-off and a second bus are covered by host tests only.
  • Public headers: can/CanBusOffRecovery.h, can/CanBusOffReport.h, can/CanBusState.h, can/CanChannelStatus.h, can/CanFrameLog.h, can/CanPhyGate.h, can/CanPhyReadiness.h, can/CanSupervisionCycle.h, can/ContextCall.h
  • Provides roles: can_system
  • Requires: can_phy × 1
  • Integration: lifecycle level 2 in task can, console command group can, CMake target canSystem

docs.text:
Console commands in the console context with a short call into the task that owns the state (ContextCall), and a console input line that shares the terminal with the log output

  • Directory: libs/bsw/consoleContext, manifest: module.yaml, kind: library
  • Verification: hardware - Console commands running in the console context with a short call into the owning task are confirmed on the eval board; the interleaved input line is covered by host tests only.
  • Public headers: console/ConsoleContext.h, console/ContextCall.h, console/IOutputInterleave.h, console/InputLine.h, console/InterleavedConsoleInput.h

docs.title: dem
docs.text:

docs.title: ecuState
docs.text:
ECU state management Startup/Run/Standby/Rundown/Shutdown/Sleep on top of the OpenBSW lifecycle; uses the role power_supply (0..1, without provider the supply is permanent)

  • Directory: libs/bsw/ecuState, manifest: module.yaml, kind: service
  • Verification: hardware - Run, standby with withdrawal, run-down, sleep and the start after a CAN wake-up are confirmed on the eval board; local and cyclic wake-up and the run-down step time-outs are covered by host tests only.
  • Public headers: ecuState/DirectReset.h, ecuState/EcuState.h, ecuState/EcuStateController.h, ecuState/EcuStateIntegration.h, ecuState/EcuStateMachine.h, ecuState/EcuStateRte.h, ecuState/IOutputFlush.h, ecuState/IPowerSupply.h, ecuState/IShutdownStep.h, ecuState/McuStartReasons.h, ecuState/PermanentPowerSupply.h
  • Provides roles: ecu_state
  • Integration: lifecycle level 1 in task bsp, console command group ecu, CMake target ecuState
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.ecuState.<parameter> - one entry per project, parameters below
    • use.can - parameters that name CAN buses accept only buses of use.can
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description min_run_ms int ms 5000 0 .. 3600000 RUN at least this long after the start before a sleep request is served (diagnostic access, reflashing after a wake-up) post_run_ms int ms 2000 0 .. 3600000 STANDBY (post-run) before the run-down, the application runs on and can withdraw the request shutdown_timeout_ms int ms 5000 100 .. 3600000 lifecycle shutdown not finished within this time -> restart. Also the bound of the restart itself: the lifecycle has not reached level 0 within this time after the restart request -> direct reset of the MCU sleep_timeout_ms int ms 2000 101 .. 3600000 MCU still running this long after the power down request -> restart (more than POWER_DOWN_DELAY_MS 100 ms) nvm_timeout_ms int ms 1000 10 .. 3600000 step NvM of the run-down: writing the non-volatile data not finished within this time -> see step_error. Without a NvM provider the step is reported as not present (is blocked) and the limit never applies can_stop_timeout_ms int ms 500 10 .. 3600000 step CAN of the run-down: stopping the transmission and leaving the transceivers ready for a wake-up not finished within this time -> see step_error wakeup_can str all pattern all\|none\|[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(,[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*, names: can_bus CAN buses that may wake the ECU: all (every bus of the project), none, or a comma separated list of bus names of the project (board can[], one wake-up bit per bus) wakeup_local str none pattern all\|none\|LOCAL[0-7](,LOCAL[0-7])*, names: any local wake-up inputs of the power supply that may wake the ECU (SBC UJA113x: WAKE/HVIO pins, bank 0 of register 0x37). Default none, because an input that is not wired on the board wakes the ECU at random wakeup_cyclic_ms int ms 0 0 .. 3600000 cyclic wake-up (wakeup::TIMER): 0 off, otherwise the requested period. The supply rounds it up to its own grid (SBC UJA113x: watchdog periods 8..4096 ms in Sleep) and reports the value it really uses wakeup_during_shutdown str restart pattern restart\|sleep wake-up event during RUNDOWN/SHUTDOWN, restart (evaluate it in a new start) or sleep anyway after_watchdog_reset str run pattern run\|sleep start after a watchdog reset, run (application decides) or sleep without request step_error str restart pattern restart\|continue a run-down step failed or ran into its time limit: restart the ECU (a half prepared ECU must not sleep) or continue and note the step. Never continued: the NvM step (a data flash write must not meet the power down) - tools/rtegen refuses continue for a project with NvM blocks or data flash areas

docs.title: highSideSwitch
docs.text:
Smart high-side switch with input IN, diagnosis enable DEN and current sense IS (PROFET-like)

  • Directory: libs/bsw/highSideSwitch, manifest: module.yaml, kind: device_driver
  • Verification: hardware - Current sense, overcurrent switch-off with latch, open load and the off check are confirmed on the eval board (BTS5030-1EJA, electronic load); the fault current threshold needs a real device fault and is covered by host tests only.
  • Public headers: highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitch.h, highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchBinding.h, highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchChannel.h, highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchConsole.h, highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchIntegration.h, highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchNames.h, highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchSafeOff.h, highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchSense.h, highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchSystem.h, highSideSwitch/IHighSideSwitchIo.h
  • Provides roles: switched_output
  • Integration: lifecycle level 1 in task bsp, console command group per instance (parameter console), CMake target highSideSwitchSystem
  • Board configuration (board.yaml):
    • devices[].part matching BTS5030-1EJA - one instance per board device; devices[].module: highSideSwitch chooses this module where several modules serve the part
    • devices[].connect.in -> an entry of dio.outputs[] (digital_output, switched off first by the fault handlers): input IN (switch on)
    • devices[].connect.den -> an entry of dio.outputs[] (digital_output): diagnosis enable DEN (IS active)
    • devices[].connect.is -> an entry of adc[] (analog_input): current sense IS; the board's adc[].sensor of this channel converts it into the load current in mA (highside_is: k_ILIS, R_IS)
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.<device>.<parameter> - one entry per board device served by this module, parameters below
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description cycle_ms int ms 10 1 .. 1000 supervision period overcurrent_ma int mA required 1 .. 1000000 load current at or above which it is an overcurrent overcurrent_debounce_ms int ms required 1 .. 1000 overcurrent duration before switching off fault_ma int mA required 1 .. 1000000 load current at or above which the fault current of the switch is assumed (IS saturated) fault_debounce_ms int ms required 1 .. 1000 fault level duration before switching off switch_on_blanking_ms int ms required 0 .. 1000 current thresholds ignored after switching on open_load_ma int mA required 0 .. 1000000 load current below this while on is an open load (warning; 0 = off) off_max_ma int mA required 1 .. 1000000 reading above this while off is implausible off_debounce_ms int ms required 1 .. 1000 implausible off reading duration before a fault console str required pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,15}$ console command group of the instance

Rules between the parameters (checked by tools/nxconfig): fault_ma > overcurrent_ma, open_load_ma < overcurrent_ma, off_max_ma < fault_ma, overcurrent_debounce_ms >= cycle_ms, fault_debounce_ms >= cycle_ms, off_debounce_ms >= cycle_ms.

docs.title: sbcUja113x
docs.text:
NXP UJA113x system basis chip (supplies, watchdog, integrated CAN transceiver), complex device driver

  • Directory: libs/bsw/sbcUja113x, manifest: module.yaml, kind: device_driver
  • Verification: hardware - Start-up, register configuration over SPI, the CAN transceiver, battery under-voltage monitoring and Sleep with CAN wake-up are confirmed on the eval board (UJA1131); the SBC watchdog is not active there, and over-voltage and the other UJA113x parts are covered by host tests only.
  • Public headers: sbc/Uja113x.h, sbc/Uja113xCanPhy.h, sbc/Uja113xPowerSupply.h, sbc/Uja113xResetCounter.h, sbc/uja113xRegisters.h
  • Provides roles: can_phy, power_supply, watchdog_trigger, early_init
  • Requires: spi_device × 1
  • Integration: lifecycle level 1 in task bsp, console command group sbc, CMake target sbcUja113x
  • Board configuration (board.yaml):
    • devices[].part matching UJA1131*, UJA1132*, UJA1135*, UJA1136* - one instance per board device; devices[].module: sbcUja113x chooses this module where several modules serve the part
    • devices[].connect.intn1 -> an entry of dio.inputs[] (digital_input, optional): INTN1, interrupt output of the SBC (open drain, active low, all enabled interrupts; data sheet 7.12)
    • spi[].device - the SPI bus the device sits on (the module requires spi_device)
    • can[].phy - the CAN buses the device is the transceiver of (role can_phy)
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.<device>.<parameter> - one entry per board device served by this module, parameters below
    • use.spi - an instance is built when the project uses the SPI bus of its device
    • use.can - the transceiver role is served for the CAN buses the project uses
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description battery_source str bat pattern bat\|batsense pin the under-/overvoltage events are taken from (BMSC): bat = BAT behind the reverse polarity diode, batsense = BATSENSE in front of it undervoltage_mv int mV 9000 0 .. 20000 undervoltage event below this voltage (BMUTC; 0 = never) overvoltage_mv int mV 18000 0 .. 20000 overvoltage event above this voltage (BMOTC; 20000 = never) undervoltage_hysteresis_mv int mV 500 0 .. 4710 release window of the undervoltage event: it ends this much above the threshold (BMHUC, 0..15 x 313.7 mV) overvoltage_hysteresis_mv int mV 500 0 .. 4710 release window of the overvoltage event: it ends this much below the threshold (BMHOC, 0..15 x 313.7 mV) can_shutdown str none pattern none\|undervoltage\|overvoltage\|both CAN transceiver off during these battery events (CSC); none: CAN stays on, the application decides v2_shutdown str none pattern none\|undervoltage\|overvoltage\|both V2/VEXT off during these battery events (V2SC); check what V2 supplies on the board first shutdown_delay_ms int ms 0 0 .. 10000 0: the SBC switches CAN/V2 off by itself within one conversion of its monitor (6 us, tc(ADC)); > 0: the driver switches off only after the event has lasted this long without a break (checked every call of Uja113x::cyclic, 10 ms on the S32K1 port) and on again when it has ended - rides through short dips such as the inrush current of a load

Rules between the parameters (checked by tools/nxconfig): undervoltage_mv < overvoltage_mv.

docs.title: bspAdcAccess
docs.text:
Serialized synchronous ADC access (lock policy per conversion, polling bound derived from the conversion time)

  • Directory: libs/bsp/bspAdcAccess, manifest: module.yaml, kind: mcu_driver
  • Verification: hardware - Policy interrupt_lock with the derived polling bound is confirmed on the eval board (conversion counters, longest exclusive time, no poll time-outs); policy rtos_mutex and converter failures are covered by host tests only.
  • Public headers: adc/AdcAccess.h, adc/AdcAveraging.h, adc/AdcPollLimit.h, adc/FreeRtosAdcLock.h, adc/InterruptLockAdcLock.h
  • Provides roles: adc_access
  • Integration: CMake target bspAdcAccess
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.bspAdcAccess.<parameter> - one entry per project, parameters below
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description lock_policy str interrupt_lock pattern interrupt_lock\|rtos_mutex interrupt_lock: every conversion runs with the interrupts suspended (no RTOS object, no waiting, no priority inversion, interrupt latency = one conversion). rtos_mutex: one RTOS mutex per ADC instance with priority inheritance, the conversion itself runs with the interrupts released; callers that cannot wait (ISR, interrupts suspended, before the scheduler) keep the exclusive path either way. lock_timeout_ms int ms 100 1 .. 60000 longest wait for the lock of an ADC instance; only used with lock_policy rtos_mutex poll_safety_factor int 16 1 .. 4096 the polling bound is this factor times the derived conversion time, counted in iterations of the polling core. A healthy conversion must never reach it, a dead converter must be detected well inside the watchdog window. max_interrupt_suspend_us int us 50 1 .. 1000000 longest interrupt suspension the project accepts for one ADC conversion. Checked against the derived conversion time (tools/nxconfig/adc.py); it does not change any generated value. sample_clocks int ADC clocks 42 1 .. 256 sample (acquisition) phase of one conversion; a high source impedance needs a long one clock_divider int 1 1 .. 8 divider of the converter clock (family values only, s32k1xx CFG1[ADIV]: 1, 2, 4, 8) averages int 1 1 .. 32 conversions per result of the hardware averaging (1: off; family values only, s32k1xx SC3[AVGS]: 4, 8, 16, 32). It multiplies the conversion time and therefore the interrupt suspension.

docs.title: Port modules (platforms/<family>/port, ecu/platforms/<board>)
docs.text: Modules that belong to one MCU family or one board and therefore live in its port. tools/nxconfig reads their manifests only for a project whose derivative is of that family or which runs on that board (port_module_dirs in tools/nxconfig/config.py); a second family brings its own module for the same parameters.

docs.title: capture
docs.text:
Period and duty cycle measurement of a PWM input (FTM dual edge capture), values and quality for the RTE

  • Directory: platforms/s32k1xx/port/bspConfiguration/src/bsp/capture, manifest: module.yaml, kind: mcu_driver
  • Port: family port platforms/s32k1xx/port - loaded by tools/nxconfig for the projects whose derivative belongs to this family
  • Verification: mock - On the eval board only the time-out without an input signal is confirmed; period, duty cycle and the range checks are covered by generator and host tests only.
  • Provides roles: input_capture
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.capture.<parameter> - one entry per project, parameters below
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description min_frequency_hz int Hz 50 1 .. 10000000 lowest frequency the measurement has to cover. The counter prescaler of the timer follows from it: one period of this frequency has to fit into half the counter range, so that a measurement never becomes ambiguous. A lower value means a longer measurable period and a coarser resolution; a measured period outside the range is reported as a quality error, never as a value. How low it can be depends on the counter clock (largest prescaler 128 times the 16-bit counter); the generator says so if it is too low. timeout_ms int ms 200 1 .. 60000 time without a completed measurement after which the quality becomes QLF_ERROR_TIMEOUT (missing signal, constant level, frequency below the range). It has to cover two periods of min_frequency_hz plus one update cycle, otherwise a healthy slow signal would be reported as missing. update_period_ms int ms 10 1 .. 10000 cycle in which the application calls InputCapture::update() (the period of the RTE task that reads the capture values). The counter of the timer must not wrap twice between two calls, otherwise a slow signal could be measured as a fast one; the generator checks this against the derived prescaler and refuses the combination instead of measuring wrongly.

Rules between the parameters (checked by tools/nxconfig): timeout_ms > update_period_ms.

docs.title: hall
docs.text:
Three digital Hall signals of a brushless motor (state, sector, period, speed, direction and quality), measured in the pin interrupt of the port with a time stamp per edge

  • Directory: platforms/s32k1xx/port/bspConfiguration/src/bsp/hall, manifest: module.yaml, kind: device_driver
  • Port: family port platforms/s32k1xx/port - loaded by tools/nxconfig for the projects whose derivative belongs to this family
  • Verification: mock - Host tests only (decoder and pin interrupt access against two profiles); no Hall sensor or signal source has been connected to a board yet.
  • Provides roles: hall_sensor
  • Integration: CMake target bspHall
  • Board configuration (board.yaml):
    • devices[].part matching hall3, hall3_* - one instance per board device; devices[].module: hall chooses this module where several modules serve the part
    • devices[].connect.u -> an entry of dio.inputs[] (digital_input): Hall signal of phase U (H1)
    • devices[].connect.v -> an entry of dio.inputs[] (digital_input): Hall signal of phase V (H2)
    • devices[].connect.w -> an entry of dio.inputs[] (digital_input): Hall signal of phase W (H3)
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.<device>.<parameter> - one entry per board device served by this module, parameters below
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description arrangement str deg120 pattern deg120\|deg60 electrical angle between the Hall sensors. deg120 (the usual brushless arrangement) has the six valid states 100, 110, 010, 011, 001, 101 in that order and reports 000 and 111 as invalid; deg60 has the six valid states 111, 110, 100, 000, 001, 011 in that order and reports 010 and 101 as invalid. The generator turns the choice into the sector table, so no state list is written down twice. pole_pairs int required 1 .. 64 pole pairs of the motor: one mechanical revolution is this many electrical revolutions. The mechanical period and the speed use it, state, sector and the electrical period do not. There is no default - it is a fact of the motor, not a value to guess. forward str sector_up pattern sector_up\|sector_down which way through the sector sequence of arrangement is reported as direction +1. sector_up is the documented order above (U -> V -> W); sector_down mirrors it, for a motor whose phase order or sensor order is the other way round. It only changes the sign of hall.<Sensor>.direction, never the sector numbers, the period or the speed. min_speed_rpm int rpm required 1 .. 200000 lowest mechanical speed that still has to be measured. The generator checks standstill_ms against it: one electrical revolution at this speed has to fit into the standstill time, otherwise a healthy slowly turning motor would be reported as standing still. max_speed_rpm int rpm required 1 .. 200000 highest mechanical speed the motor reaches. The generator derives the shortest sector time from it (60e6 / (rpm * pole_pairs * 6) microseconds) and checks debounce_us against it: debouncing must not swallow real edges at full speed. It refuses the combination with both numbers instead of measuring wrongly. debounce_us int us 20 0 .. 100000 an edge closer than this to the last accepted edge is counted as bouncing and ignored (0 switches the debouncing off). It is done in the driver, not with the input filter of the port: the filter width of the s32k1xx (PORT DFCR/DFWR) is one register per port and would change every other input of that port too. standstill_ms int ms 200 1 .. 60000 time without an accepted edge after which the quality becomes QLF_ERROR_TIMEOUT (standstill): period, speed and direction are not current any more, while state and sector still are - the sensors report the position of a motor that stands still. It also bounds the time base: the driver stamps every edge with the microsecond time of the system timer (32 bit, wraps after about 71.6 minutes), a standstill throws the running revolution away, and the generator checks that six standstill times stay well inside one wrap, so no period can be measured across an ambiguous time.

Rules between the parameters (checked by tools/nxconfig): max_speed_rpm >= min_speed_rpm.

docs.title: safeLifecycle
docs.text:
Safety task of the S32K1 family - cycle of the safety supervision, MCU watchdog service and period check

  • Directory: platforms/s32k1xx/port/safety/safeLifecycle, manifest: module.yaml, kind: service
  • Port: family port platforms/s32k1xx/port - loaded by tools/nxconfig for the projects whose derivative belongs to this family
  • Verification: hardware - The demo values (10 ms, 250 ms time-out, service every 8 cycles until a follow-up task) run on the eval board without watchdog reset; 7 cycles, other values and the period check are covered by host and generator tests.
  • Public headers: safeLifecycle/IsrHooks.h, safeLifecycle/IsrWrapper.h, safeLifecycle/ProgressSupervision.h, safeLifecycle/SafetyManager.h
  • Integration: lifecycle level 1 in task safety, CMake target safeLifecycle
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.safeLifecycle.<parameter> - one entry per project, parameters below
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description task_period_ms int ms 10 1 .. 1000 period of the safety task (SafetySystem schedules it at this fixed rate). Every cycle runs the whole safety supervision, so the period bounds how late a fault the task checks is seen; counters in cycles of other safety modules (e.g. safeSystem.adc_read_error_limit) scale with it. The watchdog is serviced every floor(watchdog_timeout_ms x 1000 / (3 x task_period_ms x lpo_max_per_mille)) cycles, derived by tools/nxconfig at the fastest LPO of the data sheet (mcudb clock.lpo). watchdog_timeout_ms int ms 250 1 .. 65535 time-out of the MCU watchdog. It has to hold three service intervals of the safety task (at least 3 x task_period_ms), so that a single late service does not reset the ECU. The family bounds it by its watchdog counter: S32K1 WDOG at the nominal 128 kHz LPO, at most 511 ms (TOVAL 16 bit). The LPO tolerance of the data sheet shortens the real time-out (at 139 kHz 230 ms for 250 ms); the service interval is derived for that shortest time-out. cycle_lateness_ms int ms 2 0 .. 999 how late a cycle of the safety task may start against its nominal grid point without a period violation (SAFETY_CYCLE_PERIOD_VIOLATION, SM-04): interrupt load, critical sections, one tick of the OS timer. Below task_period_ms. The value is an assumption until the board measurement B4 of doc/safety/fmea.md confirms it.

Rules between the parameters (checked by tools/nxconfig): cycle_lateness_ms < task_period_ms.

docs.title: safeMemory
docs.text:
Safety RAM gate (MPU), ECC supervision and ROM check (CRC of the application image) of the S32K1 family

  • Directory: platforms/s32k1xx/port/safety/safeMemory, manifest: module.yaml, kind: service
  • Port: family port platforms/s32k1xx/port - loaded by tools/nxconfig for the projects whose derivative belongs to this family
  • Verification: hardware - The first ROM-check pass (valid image passes, changed image held in the safe state) is confirmed on the eval board; the re-check period, the CRC-unit self-test and the suspension during flash writes are host tests only.
  • Public headers: safeMemory/EccLatentTest.h, safeMemory/IntegrityEccHandler.h, safeMemory/MemoryLocations.h, safeMemory/MemoryProtection.h, safeMemory/ProtectedRamScopedUnlock.h, safeMemory/RomCheck.h, safeMemory/RomCheckFlashWrites.h, safeMemory/RomCheckList.h, safeMemory/SafeMemory.h, safeMemory/SafetyShell.h, safeMemory/mpu.h
  • Integration: lifecycle level 2 in task idle, CMake target safeMemory
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.safeMemory.<parameter> - one entry per project, parameters below
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description rom_check_period_ms int ms 60000 0 .. 86400000 re-check period of the ROM check (SM-14) from the start of one pass to the start of the next; 0 = once per start only. One pass (known-answer test of the CRC unit, then the CRC over the whole application image) runs in the idle context at the lowest priority without a lock, so the period costs only idle time (about 3 to 6 ms per pass for an image of about 190 KB, computed). The period bounds the latent interval of a flash corruption for ECUs that stay powered for long (AoU-25). It is also the deadline for flash writes: when a due pass could not run for longer than one period because the program or data flash was being written, the check reports ROM_CHECK_FAILURE (safe state S1 held) - a period other than 0 therefore has to be longer than the longest flash write of the ECU (an EEPROM record of the FlexNVM emulation waits at most about a second for its backup sector). The maximum is one day.

docs.title: safeSupervisor
docs.text:
Safe supervisor - reactions to safety events, reset-loop limit and device-bus correlation (safety task)

  • Directory: platforms/s32k1xx/port/safety/safeSupervisor, manifest: module.yaml, kind: service
  • Port: family port platforms/s32k1xx/port - loaded by tools/nxconfig for the projects whose derivative belongs to this family
  • Verification: hardware - The reset-loop limit with 3 resets and 60 s ran on the eval board (hold after three watchdog resets, count cleared after a fault-free minute); the device-bus window and other values are covered by host and generator tests only.
  • Integration: lifecycle level 1 in task safety, CMake target safeSupervisor
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.safeSupervisor.<parameter> - one entry per project, parameters below
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description reset_loop_limit int 3 1 .. 255 consecutive safety resets (a reset the supervisor marked before its reaction S1 + S2, a real watchdog reset, a fault exception or core lockup) after which the start holds the safe state S1 without a reset (RESET_LOOP_LIMIT, SSR-065); only a power cycle ends the hold. 1 holds at the first safety reset. reset_loop_clear_ms int ms 60000 10 .. 86400000 operation without a safety reset that clears the count of the reset-loop limit, counted in cycles of the safety task (rounded up, so a slow task clears later, never earlier). At least one task period. device_bus_window_ms int ms 200 1 .. 60000 window of the per-bus correlation of device reports (F5): communication faults of two different devices on one bus within this time are one event "bus lost", and the verdict ends after a window without one. Counted in cycles of the safety task, ceil(device_bus_window_ms / task_period_ms) (derived by tools/nxconfig, never shorter than the time set). It should span two supervision cycles (cycle_ms) of the slowest device on a bus (warning otherwise).

docs.title: safeSystem
docs.text:
Safety supervision of the ADC reference voltage and the internal supplies of the MCU (safety task)

  • Directory: platforms/s32k1xx/port/safety/safeSystem, manifest: module.yaml, kind: service
  • Port: family port platforms/s32k1xx/port - loaded by tools/nxconfig for the projects whose derivative belongs to this family
  • Verification: hardware - Reference and supply monitoring run on the eval board without false alarms (bandgap readings, safeadc counters at 0, no safety reset); a wrong reference voltage and failed readings up to the limit are covered by host tests only.
  • Public headers: safeSystem/SafeSystem.h
  • Provides roles: adc_reference_monitor, internal_supply_monitor
  • Integration: lifecycle level 1 in task safety, console command group safeadc, CMake target safeSystem
  • Project configuration (project.yaml):
    • modules.safeSystem.<parameter> - one entry per project, parameters below
Parameter Type Unit Default Allowed values Description adc_read_error_limit int 10 1 .. 100000 failed readings in a row before the monitor concerned is triggered, applied separately to the bandgap (reference monitor, context 2) and to the internal supply channel (internal supply monitor, context 2) - in both cases "no measurement possible". A single failed reading is not evidence of a wrong voltage and must not reset the ECU; readings that keep failing mean the voltage can no longer be monitored, which is safety relevant itself. A good reading ends the series; a supply reading skipped for want of a valid reference does not count (that is the reference monitor's case). The limit counts cycles of the safety task, so the time it corresponds to follows from that task's period. adc_reference_tolerance_mv int mV 200 1 .. 1000 allowed deviation of the measured ADC reference voltage (VREFH, computed from the bandgap reading) from its nominal value; outside nominal +- tolerance the reference monitor is triggered (context 1). The nominal value is a board fact (board.yaml board.adc_reference_mv), the tolerance is decided by the project: it has to cover the accuracy of the reference source and the spread of the bandgap (taken as 1000 mV). The maximum of 1000 mV keeps the lower limit above 0 for every real reference.
