docs.title: (top level)
docs.text:
Project file projects/<project>/project.yaml: what one ECU software uses of its board.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description schema_version integer yes 1 Version of the file format; currently 1. project object yes Identification of the project; board and ECU description it is built from. clock object yes System clock of the project. memory object no null Memory partitioning. Left out: no bootloader, no generated memory layout. nvm object no null Non-volatile memory: partition of the emulated EEPROM, fixed block places. Left out: chip as it is, blocks in name order. security object no null Keys of the hardware security module (flags, name of the MASTER_ECU_KEY in the key store of the workstation). Left out: no keys described. bootloader object no null CAN bus and devices of the bootloader. diagnostics object no null UDS addresses of bootloader and application; required together with memory. xcp object no null XCP on CAN. Left out: no XCP slave in the application. use object no {} Board entries the project uses. peripheral_clocks map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Functional clock of a peripheral instance; key: instance of the derivative, or a clock gate of clock.pcc. Only needed where the derivative's default is not wanted or where it has none. can map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Bit timing per CAN bus; key: board CAN bus, required for every used bus. uart map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Baud rate per UART; key: board UART, required for every used UART. i2c map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Rate and time limit per I2C bus; key: board I2C bus. A used bus without an entry runs at 100 kHz (standard mode). pwm map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ After R1. Frequency and dead time per PWM group; key: board PWM group. adc_internal list of object no [] Internal ADC inputs without pin the project reads. adc_loads map of string to one of object (kind: ntc_beta) or object (kind: table), selected by kind no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Load connected to a board ADC channel with a sensor circuit, e.g. the NTC of a motor; key: the channel. adc_sampling map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Sampling of a used board ADC channel other than one conversion per read, e.g. averaged over one PWM period; key: the channel. Left out: one conversion per read. interrupts object no {} Interrupt priorities as ranks. pin_events map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Events on digital inputs (pin interrupt on an edge); key: a used board input (dio.inputs[].name). Each one needs a rank (interrupts.ranks, source dio). Left out: inputs are only read as levels (dio.in.<NAME>). safety object no null Pins of the OpenBSW safety demo. Left out: none. modules map of string to map of string to integer or boolean or string or object unit of the module parameter no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$; value: key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Parameters of the modules; key: board device, or a module with project parameters (project_parameters in its module.yaml) that has no board device. Values are checked against the parameters of that module; verify: true marks the values of an entry as not confirmed. A system basis chip with partial networking (module sbcUja113x) takes can_wakeup_frame in addition. hw_thresholds map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ After R1. Hardware thresholds: a board signal at a comparator input that forces a PWM group to its inactive level without software (latched until reset); key: name of the threshold. Left out: none. sample_groups map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Sample groups: board ADC channels converted after every hardware trigger of a PWM group, with one interrupt at the end of the group; key: name of the group. Each group needs an interrupt rank (interrupts.ranks, source sample_group). Left out: none. bsw_tasks map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Stacks of the BSW tasks (ecu/asyncCoreConfiguration/tasks.yaml: background, bsp, can, sysadmin, safety) and of the OpenBSW tasks idle and timer, or the task a BSW task runs in instead of its own; key: task name. The application tasks take their stack from the ECU description (rte.yaml tasks[].stack_bytes). Left out: the defaults of ecu/configuration/taskStacks.yaml, every BSW task on its own. console object no null Console and logger of the application: selectable, size of the logger ring buffer. Left out: console and logger on, ring buffer 8192 bytes.

docs.title: project
docs.text:
Identification of the project and the files it is built from.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description project.name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Project name; by convention the same as the folder projects/<project>. project.board string yes Board folder or its board.yaml, relative to project.yaml. project.rte string no null ECU description (rte.yaml) for tools/rtegen, relative to project.yaml. Required: the build runs rtegen at every configure, and nxconfig refuses a project that is built without it. An ECU without software components still has one: one task, components: []. project.diag string no null Diagnostic description (diag.yaml): data identifiers, routines, sessions, security levels and DTCs of this ECU software, relative to project.yaml. Left out: the project describes no diagnostic jobs and no fault memory. project.description string no null Short description of the project for the reader. project.integrity string no null qm, asil_a, asil_b, asil_c, asil_d Highest safety integrity the ECU software of this project carries (ASIL of its safety requirements). qm: no safety requirement; the checks that are stricter for ASIL projects then only warn (e.g. a BSW task stack below its default without a proof note, bsw_tasks.<task>.evidence). Not qm while an NvM block has an ASIL integrity. Left out: treated as an ASIL project - the safety part of neXtBSW (safety task, safe supervisor) is in every image.

docs.title: clock
docs.text:
Clock the project runs at; sources, dividers and PLL settings are derived by the family clock model.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description clock.system_hz integer Hz yes > 0 Core clock. Sources, dividers and PLL settings follow from it and from the board crystal.

docs.title: memory
docs.text:
Memory partitioning (doc/architecture/README.md, section 7). The validity record takes the last sector of flash, the application the sectors between bootloader and record. Addresses follow from the derivative.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description memory.flash string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Code flash region of the derivative (memory[].name, kind code_flash). memory.bootloader object yes Flash and RAM of the bootloader. memory.application object yes RAM of the application. memory.calibration object no null Calibration segment. Left out: the parameter values stay in the initialised data of the application.

docs.title: memory.bootloader
docs.text:
Bootloader area at the start of the code flash and the RAM the bootloader (and its updater) runs in.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description memory.bootloader.size integer byte yes > 0 Flash of the bootloader from the start of memory.flash; whole sectors. memory.bootloader.ram string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ RAM region of the derivative the bootloader runs in. memory.bootloader.ram_size integer byte no null > 0 RAM of the bootloader from the start of ram. Left out: the whole region. memory.bootloader.stack_size integer byte no 4096 > 0 Stack of the bootloader.

docs.title: memory.application
docs.text:
RAM of the application. The no-init area (hard fault dump, boot request) ends at the end of the last region.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description memory.application.ram list of string yes at least 1 item; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ RAM regions of the derivative the application uses, in address order and contiguous. memory.application.noinit_size integer byte yes > 0 Size of the no-init area at the end of the last RAM region: it survives a reset and holds the hard fault dump and the boot request. memory.application.ramfunctions_size integer byte no null > 0 RAM for flash routines that run from RAM (.launchFromRAM), at the start of the RAM. Small derivatives (e.g. 14 KB SRAM) need less than the template default. Left out: the default of the linker template (0x1000). memory.application.hot_ram_size integer byte no null > 0 Hot part at the start of the RAM: RAM functions plus hot data and bss. Left out: the default of the linker template (0x2000 with a single RAM region, otherwise the whole first region). memory.application.isr_stack_size integer byte no null > 0 Interrupt stack (main stack: start-up up to the scheduler plus every interrupt level nested). Multiple of 8. Size it with the worst case of tools/stackuse for the image plus a reserve. Left out: the default of the linker template (0x1000). memory.application.isr_stack_guard_size integer byte no null > 0 Guard directly below the interrupt stack that the core may read but not write (MPU): an overflow ends in the hard fault reaction instead of overwriting data. Multiple of 32 (MPU granularity); it must hold the largest frame on the interrupt stack plus the larger of that frame and an exception frame (tools/stackuse checks it). Left out: the default of the linker template (0x400). memory.application.isr_stack_evidence object no null Proof note of the interrupt stack: used_bytes is the worst case on the main stack (start-up plus every interrupt level nested, tools/stackuse --strict for this image) or the high-water mark at the board (inject mspuse). Required for isr_stack_size below the default of the linker template in an ASIL project (project.integrity not qm), otherwise a warning. The interrupt stack must hold used_bytes. Left out: no proof noted. memory.application.isr_stack_guard_evidence object no null Proof note of the guard: used_bytes is the guard tools/stackuse --strict requires for this image (largest frame on the interrupt stack plus the larger of that frame and an exception frame); only method: stackuse, a measurement cannot show it. Required for isr_stack_guard_size below the default in an ASIL project, otherwise a warning. The guard must hold used_bytes. Left out: no proof noted.

docs.title: memory.application.isr_stack_evidence
docs.text:
Proof note of a BSW task stack: what the task uses of its stack and where that is shown.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.method string yes stackuse, high_water_mark stackuse: worst case of the static analysis tools/stackuse for the image of this project. high_water_mark: high-water mark measured at the board (console stats) after the deepest paths of the task have run (covers only what ran). memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.used_bytes integer byte yes > 0 Stack the task uses according to the proof (worst case of tools/stackuse, or the measured high-water mark); the stack of the task must hold it. memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.reference string yes at least 1 character Where the proof is: report file and image (version, commit), or measurement record (date, build, test steps).

docs.title: memory.application.isr_stack_guard_evidence
docs.text:
Proof note of a BSW task stack: what the task uses of its stack and where that is shown.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description memory.application.isr_stack_guard_evidence.method string yes stackuse, high_water_mark Same as memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.method. memory.application.isr_stack_guard_evidence.used_bytes integer byte yes > 0 Same as memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.used_bytes. memory.application.isr_stack_guard_evidence.reference string yes at least 1 character Same as memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.reference.

docs.title: memory.calibration
docs.text:
Calibration segment: the values of all calibration parameters (rte::PARAMETERS) in a flash area of their own, behind a CALV header (magic, format, layout identifier, length, CRC-32). The application checks the header at start-up and reacts as on_invalid says. tools/nxconfig/memory.py places it: in the code flash of memory.flash directly behind the first sector of the application (the vector table stays where the bootloader jumps to), so the download of the application does not grow over the whole flash.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description memory.calibration.region string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Flash region of the derivative the segment lies in: the code flash of memory.flash, or a data flash region (kind data_flash). A data flash can only be written separately, which the bootloader learns with a separate task; until then it is refused with that reason. memory.calibration.size integer byte yes > 0 Size of the segment, whole sectors of the region: 32 bytes of header plus the values of all calibration parameters (the linker checks that they fit). memory.calibration.on_invalid string no "refuse" refuse, defaults, warn Reaction at start-up when the header, the layout identifier or the CRC of the segment does not fit the application. refuse: the application functions (RTE runnables) do not start, the ECU stays reachable over UDS for a new download; required as soon as one parameter is safety relevant (safety of swc.yaml other than qm). defaults: the values built into the application image, development profile only. warn: the values of the segment as they are. Each reaction other than a valid segment is logged and reported to the fault memory (BSW event calibration.segment). memory.calibration.profile string no "development" development, production development: the values are copied into a RAM working page at start-up, XCP calibrates there, the flash segment is the reference page. production: the values are read directly from the flash segment, there is no RAM copy and no write path; the project must not have an xcp section.

docs.title: nvm
docs.text:
Non-volatile memory of the project: partition of the emulated EEPROM, block definitions and places.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description nvm.partition object no null Partition of the emulated EEPROM. Left out: the chip is used as it is, no partition command is built. nvm.blocks map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Definition (type, length, integrity), place and write policy per NvM block; key: block name (nvm.<Block> of rte.yaml, or DemEvents/DemEntries of the fault memory). nvm.data_flash object no null Areas of the data flash (name, size, purpose). Left out: the application does not use the data flash.

docs.title: nvm.partition
docs.text:
Split of the emulated EEPROM, in bytes; the generator derives the codes of the partition command from the derivative (eeprom_emulation).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description nvm.partition.eeprom_bytes integer byte yes ≥ 0 Bytes of emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx: FlexRAM used as EEPROM). One of the sizes of the derivative. nvm.partition.data_flash_bytes integer byte yes ≥ 0 Bytes of the partitionable flash that stay data flash; the rest backs up the emulated EEPROM. nvm.partition.partition_code integer none no null 0 to 15 Code of the split in the partition command (s32k1xx: DEPART). Only needed where the derivative has several codes for the same split; it must be one of them. nvm.partition.load_on_reset boolean no true true: the chip loads the emulated EEPROM during every reset (s32k1xx: PGMPART FCCOB3 = 0, IFR EEERST = 1 - opposite encodings). false: every start would need a flash command (SETRAM), which the start-up never launches; the NvM would run on its defaults. nvm.partition.key_slots integer none no null ≥ 0 Key slots of the security module to reserve in the emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx CSEc: 0, 5, 10 or 20; FCCOB1). One of the key space sizes of the derivative; the bytes come off the usable EEPROM. Left out on a derivative with a key space: the partition command refuses to write - the space is fixed with the partition and cannot be added later. nvm.partition.key_verify_only boolean no false Security flag extension (s32k1xx: SFE, FCCOB2): lets a key be marked verify-only. Not offered yet: the partition command writes it off.

docs.title: nvm.blocks.<key>
docs.text:
Definition of one NvM block (data type, scalar or vector, integrity), its place and write policy.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description nvm.blocks.<key>.type string no null boolean, uint8, sint8, uint16, sint16, uint32, sint32, float32, float64 Platform type of the block's value (of one element of a vector). The ports connected to nvm.<Block> must have this type. Left out: the type comes from the writing port (before a later change; the generator warns and proposes the definition). Not for the blocks of the fault memory (DemEvents, DemEntries), whose layout comes from diag.yaml. nvm.blocks.<key>.length integer none no null > 0 1 = scalar, more = vector (array) of that many elements of type. Left out: 1. Only with type. nvm.blocks.<key>.integrity string no null qm, asil_a, asil_b, asil_c, asil_d qm: one stored value with CRC-16 (as before). asil_a.. asil_d: two copies, each with CRC-32 and write counter; a defective copy is repaired from the other and reported to the fault memory, with both defective the block starts from its default and the application reads the quality 'unsecured' (nvm.qlf.<Block>). All ASIL levels use the same mechanism. Left out: qm. nvm.blocks.<key>.address integer byte no null ≥ 0 Offset of the block's first slot in the emulated EEPROM, a multiple of 4. Left out: laid out after the fixed blocks, in name order. nvm.blocks.<key>.write string no null shutdown, change shutdown: written at the run-down and on request. change: also cyclically after a change, at most once per min_interval_ms. Left out: the default of the block (blocks of components shutdown, blocks of the fault memory from diag.yaml). nvm.blocks.<key>.min_interval_ms integer ms no null > 0 Only with write: change: shortest time between two writes of the block.

docs.title: nvm.data_flash
docs.text:
What the data flash holds. tools/nxconfig checks it against the part the partition leaves as data flash (nvm.partition.data_flash_bytes, or the whole data flash region of a derivative without partition) and lays it out; tools/bswgen generates the table (nvm/nvmDataFlash.h).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description nvm.data_flash.areas map of string to object yes key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Areas of the data flash; key: area name (C identifier, the name in the generated table).

docs.title: nvm.data_flash.areas.<key>
docs.text:
One area of the data flash - whole sectors the application reads like memory and erases and programs at run time (libs/bsw/nvmDataFlash, dataflash::AreaService).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description nvm.data_flash.areas.<key>.size integer byte yes > 0 Size of the area, whole sectors of the data flash region of the derivative (they are erased on their own). nvm.data_flash.areas.<key>.purpose string yes calibration, data calibration: calibration data changed in the device (maps, data sets). data: other data of the application. Not for logs or images (the maintainer's purpose 2026-09-28: calibration data). nvm.data_flash.areas.<key>.offset integer byte no null ≥ 0 Offset of the area in the data flash, a multiple of the sector size. Left out: laid out after the fixed areas, in name order.

docs.title: security
docs.text:
Keys of the hardware security module the project loads (s32k1xx: CSEc; SHE key names). The key space itself is reserved by nvm.partition.key_slots.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description security.stage string no "development" development, production development: development boards; every board of the project gets the same MASTER_ECU_KEY from the key store of the workstation, so the debug authentication can bring any of them back to the factory state. production: per device keys - not offered yet, refused. security.master_ecu_key string no null 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ Name of the MASTER_ECU_KEY in the key store of the workstation (%LOCALAPPDATA%/neXtBSW/keys/csec/<name>.key or NX_CSEC_KEY_DIR; create it with nxconfig csec-key new). A name, never the key: a value that looks like key material is refused. Left out: the board name. security.keys map of string to object no {} key: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Flags per key; key: SHE name (MASTER_ECU_KEY, BOOT_MAC_KEY, BOOT_MAC, KEY_1 ... KEY_<n> up to the free slots of nvm.partition.key_slots). A key left out gets no flags.

docs.title: security.keys.<key>
docs.text:
Attributes of one key of the security module (SHE key flags; s32k1xx: CSEc). Only what the key may be used for - the key value is never part of the project.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description security.keys.<key>.flags list of string no [] item: boot_protection, debugger_protection, key_usage, wildcard, verify_only SHE key flags set when the key is loaded: boot_protection (unusable after a failed secure boot), debugger_protection (unusable while a debugger is attached), key_usage (CMAC instead of encryption), wildcard (may be loaded without the chip UID), verify_only (CMAC verification only; needs nvm.partition.key_verify_only). WRITE_PROTECTION is deliberately not offered and refused in every spelling: one write-protected key makes the debug authentication - the only way back after a partition with key space - impossible for ever.

docs.title: bootloader
docs.text:
CAN bus and devices of the bootloader.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description bootloader.can string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Board CAN bus of bootloader and updater; its bit timing is can.<bus>. bootloader.init list of string no null item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Board devices the bootloader switches on before CAN (drivers in bootloader/devices/<module>). Left out: the transceiver of can, if its module has a bootloader hook. Other used devices with a hook are only read (e.g. SBC watchdog). bootloader.sbc_watchdog string no "leave" leave, serve Watchdog of a system basis chip the bootloader switches on (init). serve: the bootloader sets the watchdog to the fixed period of the device hook (sbcUja113x: autonomous, 1024 ms) in Standby, enters Normal mode and triggers it while it runs; after the jump the application must take the watchdog over within that period (assumption of use). leave: takes effect only while the SBC is in software development mode (UJA113x: SDMS 1) - the bootloader does not touch the watchdog and enters Normal mode. Without development mode (SDMS 0) the watchdog runs from the SBC reset on, in Standby too (UJA113x: timeout, 128 ms), so the bootloader serves it as with serve whatever this value says; the application takes it over the same way. This holds for an SBC that is only read (not in init) as well: with SDMS 0 the bootloader sets up and triggers only the watchdog, the SBC stays in Standby and V2 and CAN are not switched on. serve differs from leave only with development mode: it also sets a watchdog the application left running to the fixed setting. The MTPNV is never changed. Boards without such an SBC: leave.

docs.title: diagnostics
docs.text:
Diagnostic addresses of the ECU (doc/architecture/README.md, section 4: CAN ids and UDS addresses are a decision of the project). Used by the bootloader (bootloader/src/core), the application UDS stack (ecu/uds) and tools/canflash; generated into <build>/generated/board/bootloader/bl_diag.h.

The CAN bus the application answers on is the diagnostic bus of the ECU description (rte.yaml uds.bus); the bootloader listens on bootloader.can.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description diagnostics.request_id integer none yes ≥ 0 CAN identifier of the physically addressed request (11 bit, must not collide with other identifiers of the bus). diagnostics.response_id integer none yes ≥ 0 CAN identifier of the responses of this ECU. diagnostics.functional_id integer none no 2015 ≥ 0 CAN identifier of the functionally addressed request (ISO 14229 "all nodes"). diagnostics.tester_address integer none no 241 0 to 255 Transport address of the tester (1 byte) in the UDS stack. diagnostics.ecu_address integer none no 42 0 to 255 Transport address of this ECU (1 byte) in the UDS stack. diagnostics.isotp object no {} ISO-TP parameters of the diagnostic connection. diagnostics.bootloader object no {} Identification and security access of the bootloader.

docs.title: diagnostics.isotp
docs.text:
ISO 15765-2 parameters of the diagnostic connection (normal addressing, classic CAN).

Bootloader and application answer with the same values, so one tester serves both. Ranges are the ones the protocol can encode; what is plausible for a download is checked in diag.py.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description diagnostics.isotp.padding integer none no 204 0 to 255 Filler byte of frames shorter than 8 bytes. diagnostics.isotp.block_size integer none no 0 0 to 255 Block size BS of the flow control frame: consecutive frames before the next flow control; 0: no further flow control. diagnostics.isotp.stmin_ms integer ms no 0 0 to 255 Minimum separation time STmin of the flow control frame; at most 127. diagnostics.isotp.n_cr_ms integer ms no 1000 > 0 Timeout N_Cr for the next consecutive frame. diagnostics.isotp.n_bs_ms integer ms no 1000 > 0 Timeout N_Bs for the flow control frame.

docs.title: diagnostics.bootloader
docs.text:
How the bootloader identifies itself in its flash (DID 0xF180) and where the application looks for it.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description diagnostics.bootloader.version_prefix string no "nextbsw-bl" 1 to 24 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*$ Prefix of the bootloader version string, without the version number: identifies the bootloader software. The application searches the bootloader area for it, the updater accepts an image with the same prefix and major version. The former name of the software (S32K14x-BL) is accepted as well, so boards flashed before the rename keep working. Compared byte by byte and case-sensitively. diagnostics.bootloader.scan_start integer none no null ≥ 0 First address the application searches for the version string; the end is the start of the application. Left out: behind the flash area the family reserves (s32k1xx: vector table and flash configuration field up to 0x40F). diagnostics.bootloader.security object no {} Security access of the bootloader (seed and key).

docs.title: diagnostics.bootloader.security
docs.text:
Security access of the bootloader. The device answers a seed with HMAC-SHA256(device key, seed); the device key is HMAC-SHA256(master key, chip UID) and is written once per device by the provisioning tool (tools/canflash/provision.py). The master key never enters the repository or the bootloader image: the project names it, the workstation holds it (%LOCALAPPDATA%/neXtBSW/keys/<key>.key or an environment variable).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description diagnostics.bootloader.security.method string no "hmac-sha256" hmac-sha256 Method of the key calculation. diagnostics.bootloader.security.key string no null 1 to 64 characters, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ Name of the master key in the key store of the workstation. Left out: the board name - one key for every project of a board, so that switching between two applications of the same hardware keeps the provisioned device key. diagnostics.bootloader.security.allow_insecure_test_key boolean no false true: the deliberately insecure test key of the repository (nextbsw-insecure-test) may be named in key. Test profiles only.

docs.title: xcp
docs.text:
XCP on CAN: bus and CAN identifiers, a decision of the project like the diagnostic addresses. tools/rtegen generates xcp/xcpCanConfiguration.h from it (ecu/xcp, tools/a2lgen) and adds master_id to the hardware receive filter of the bus. diag.py checks range, bus and collisions with the YAML path (11/29 bit, diagnostics, DBC of the bus).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description xcp.bus string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Board CAN bus from use.can XCP runs on. Left out: the diagnostic bus. xcp.master_id integer none yes 0 to 4294967295 CAN identifier master -> ECU (commands, CTO); bit 31 set: 29-bit identifier (encoding of the DBC). xcp.slave_id integer none yes 0 to 4294967295 CAN identifier ECU -> master (responses and errors), same encoding as master_id.

docs.title: use
docs.text:
Board functions used by the project: 'all' or a list of board names. Omitted: none.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description use.spi string or list of string no [] all; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Used SPI buses (spi[].name of the board): all, or a list of names from the board section of the same name. Left out: none. use.can string or list of string no [] all; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Used CAN buses (can[].name of the board): all, or a list of names from the board section of the same name. Left out: none. use.uart string or list of string no [] all; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Used UARTs (uart[].name of the board): all, or a list of names from the board section of the same name. Left out: none. use.i2c string or list of string no [] all; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Used I2C buses (i2c[].name of the board): all, or a list of names from the board section of the same name. Left out: none. use.adc string or list of string no [] all; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Used ADC channels (adc[].name of the board): all, or a list of names from the board section of the same name. Left out: none. use.input_capture string or list of string no [] all; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Used input capture channels (input_capture[].name of the board): all, or a list of names from the board section of the same name. Left out: none. use.dio string or list of string no [] all; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Used digital inputs and outputs (dio.inputs[].name, dio.outputs[].name of the board): all, or a list of names from the board section of the same name. Left out: none.

docs.title: peripheral_clocks.<key>
docs.text:
The functional clock the project chooses for one peripheral instance.

select must be one of the sources the derivative allows (instances.<x>.clock.sources), divider one of its asynchronous outputs - it may be left out when the derivative allows only one. Without an entry the default of the derivative applies, so a project that decides nothing keeps the values it had.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description peripheral_clocks.<key>.select string yes SOSC, SIRC, FIRC, SPLL Clock source that feeds the instance (s32k1xx: SOSC, SIRC, FIRC or SPLL, the value of PCCn.PCS). peripheral_clocks.<key>.divider integer no null 1, 2 Asynchronous output of the source the clock is taken from: 1 for DIV1, 2 for DIV2. In a project entry it may be left out when the derivative allows only one output. peripheral_clocks.<key>.verify boolean no false true: the choice is not confirmed (e.g. not measured on a board). peripheral_clocks.<key>.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: can.<key>
docs.text:
Bit timing request of a used board CAN bus; prescaler and segments are calculated (clock.py).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description can.<key>.bitrate integer bit/s yes > 0 Nominal bit rate of the bus (e.g. 500000). can.<key>.sample_point_percent number % no 87.5 50 to 95, finite Wanted sample point as a share of the bit time. The calculated bit timing may deviate slightly; nxconfig warns or reports an error when it deviates too far. can.<key>.sjw_tq integer time quanta no null > 0 Synchronization jump width. Left out: as large as the segments allow. can.<key>.prop_seg_tq integer time quanta no null > 0 Propagation segment. Left out: chosen so that phase segment 1 equals phase segment 2 where possible. can.<key>.verify boolean no false true: the bit timing is not confirmed (e.g. not measured on the bus). can.<key>.bus_off object no null Behaviour of the bus after bus off (pause, dropping pending frames, logging). Left out: the defaults of every value.

docs.title: can.<key>.bus_off
docs.text:
What the bus does when a bus off keeps coming back: log series, doubling pause, dropping pending frames.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description can.<key>.bus_off.first_pause_ms integer ms no 10 0 to 65535 Pause before the first release of a series of bus offs: the controller stays in bus off this long before it is let back onto the bus. Default: one supervision cycle (10 ms). can.<key>.bus_off.max_pause_ms integer ms no 1000 0 to 65535 Upper limit of the pause, which doubles with every bus off of a series. 0: the controller is not held and leaves bus off by itself (automatic recovery, as before a later change); logging and dropping stay. can.<key>.bus_off.discard_after integer none no 3 0 to 255 From this bus off of a series on, the frames waiting in the transmit buffers are dropped before the release (a frame that already cost this many bus offs will cost the next one as well). 0: never. can.<key>.bus_off.quiet_ms integer ms no 2000 1 to 65535 A series ends after this long without bus off; its end is logged in one line. Should be longer than max_pause_ms, so a lasting fault stays one series. can.<key>.bus_off.summary_ms integer ms no 10000 1 to 65535 While a series lasts, its further bus offs are counted and summarised in at most one line per this period. can.<key>.bus_off.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: uart.<key>
docs.text:
Settings of a used board UART.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description uart.<key>.baudrate integer bit/s yes > 0 Baud rate (e.g. 115200); the divider of the UART is calculated from its functional clock.

docs.title: i2c.<key>
docs.text:
Settings of a used board I2C bus.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description i2c.<key>.baudrate_hz integer Hz yes > 0 Upper limit of the SCL frequency, e.g. 100000 (standard mode) or 400000 (fast mode); the next slower rate the bus driver can make is used, never a faster one. i2c.<key>.timeout_ms integer ms no 20 1 to 10000 Time limit of one transfer, clock stretching of the device included; at least the longest transfer of the bus driver at the chosen rate. i2c.<key>.verify boolean no false true: the rate is not confirmed (no device datasheet, not measured on the bus).

docs.title: pwm.<key> (after R1)
docs.text: After R1: part of the schema and checked by tools/nxconfig, but not of the first release; the table is written when the object is. Keys: frequency_hz, deadtime_ns, deadtime_margin_ns, alignment, trigger, safe_states, safe_state_test, safe_state_test_us, verify.

docs.title: adc_internal[]
docs.text:
Internal ADC input without pin (bandgap, reference, supply monitor) the project reads as an ADC channel.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description adc_internal[].name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Channel name, unique among all ADC channels of the project. adc_internal[].instance string yes ADC instance of the derivative (e.g. ADC0). adc_internal[].channel string yes Internal channel of the instance, one of its internal_channels.

docs.title: adc_loads.<key> (kind: ntc_beta)
docs.text:
NTC after the beta model, R(T) = R_n * exp(B * (1/T - 1/T_n)); temperature in 0.1 degC.

The generator turns it into a table of points between t_min and t_max (step), the runtime interpolates.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description adc_loads.<key>.source string no null Data sheet or schematic the values come from. adc_loads.<key>.verify boolean no false true: a value is not confirmed by the source. adc_loads.<key>.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. adc_loads.<key>.kind string yes ntc_beta Load type: NTC thermistor described by the beta model; delivers the temperature in 0.1 °C. The board channel must deliver a resistance in ohm. adc_loads.<key>.r_nominal_ohm integer Ω yes > 0, ≤ 2^31-1 Resistance R_n at the nominal temperature. adc_loads.<key>.t_nominal_ddegc integer 0.1 °C no 250 -2731 to 10000 Nominal temperature T_n (usually 25 °C). adc_loads.<key>.beta_k integer K yes > 0, ≤ 100000 Beta value B of the NTC, from its data sheet. adc_loads.<key>.t_min_ddegc integer 0.1 °C no -400 -2731 to 10000 Lowest temperature of the generated table. adc_loads.<key>.t_max_ddegc integer 0.1 °C no 1500 -2731 to 10000 Highest temperature of the generated table. adc_loads.<key>.step_ddegc integer 0.1 °C no 50 > 0, ≤ 10000 Temperature step between the points of the generated table. adc_loads.<key>.max_error_ddegc integer 0.1 °C no 10 > 0, ≤ 10000 Largest interpolation error of the generated table that nxconfig accepts.

docs.title: adc_loads.<key> (kind: table)
docs.text:
Characteristic as points [board value, load value] with ascending board value; linear in between.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description adc_loads.<key>.source string no null Data sheet or schematic the values come from. adc_loads.<key>.verify boolean no false true: a value is not confirmed by the source. adc_loads.<key>.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. adc_loads.<key>.kind string yes table Load type: characteristic given as a table of points. adc_loads.<key>.unit string yes mV, mA, ohm, ddegC, permille Unit of the load value (adc.phys of the channel). adc_loads.<key>.points list of list of integer board unit, unit of unit yes 2 to 255 items; item: exactly 2 items; item: item: -2^31 to 2^31-1 Points [board value, load value] with ascending board value, linear in between; the ends are held. The board value is in the unit the board channel delivers, the load value in unit.

docs.title: adc_sampling.<key>
docs.text:
Reading of a used board ADC channel other than one conversion per read.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description adc_sampling.<key>.kind string yes pwm_period_average Sampling of the channel: pwm_period_average converts samples times at equally spaced instants over exactly one realized period of pwm_group and delivers the rounded mean of the raw values. For channels that carry the ripple of a switching stage, e.g. the DC link current of a motor bridge; the conversion (adc.phys, adc.mv) applies to the mean. adc_sampling.<key>.pwm_group string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ PWM group of the project (pwm.<group>) whose realized period is averaged over. adc_sampling.<key>.samples integer none yes 2 to 64 Conversions per read, equally spaced over one period; they must fit into it (samples times the conversion time of modules.bspAdcAccess). Harmonics of the PWM frequency that are multiples of samples are not cancelled, so a sharper ripple needs more samples. The reading task is busy for one PWM period per read.

docs.title: interrupts
docs.text:
Interrupt priorities of the project (checks.py: against the NVIC priority bits of the derivative, on a VIM core against its channels).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description interrupts.max_syscall_level integer none no null ≥ 0 NVIC cores only: highest NVIC priority level (numerically lowest) that may call the RTOS; the RTOS masks interrupts up to it. Left out: the default of the core architecture (0 on ARMv6-M, which has no BASEPRI). interrupts.ranks list of object no [] Rank of each interrupt source; every used CAN bus needs one.

docs.title: interrupts.ranks[]
docs.text:
Rank of the interrupt of one board entry, e.g. {source: can, name: CAN0, rank: 3}.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description interrupts.ranks[].source string yes can, uart, spi, i2c, adc, input_capture, pwm, dio, sample_group Kind of board entry the interrupt belongs to. interrupts.ranks[].name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Board entry of source (e.g. the CAN bus CAN0); the project must use it. interrupts.ranks[].rank integer none yes ≥ 0 Urgency rank; 0 is the most urgent interrupt that may call the RTOS. The hardware priority follows from the rank. interrupts.ranks[].note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: pin_events.<key>
docs.text:
Events on one digital input of the board (pin interrupt on an edge).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description pin_events.<key>.edge string yes activate, deactivate, both Edge that counts, relative to the active level of the board input (dio.inputs[].active): activate (the input becomes active), deactivate (it becomes inactive) or both. nxconfig derives the physical edge (rising/falling) from the board. pin_events.<key>.debounce_us integer µs yes 0 to 1000000 Software debounce: after an accepted edge, further edges are ignored for this time and the level is confirmed afterwards. 0: no debounce. Must be shorter than the shortest spacing the rate limit allows (window_ms / max_events). More than 0 needs edge detectors that report both edges (pin_interrupts.edges of the derivative). pin_events.<key>.max_events integer none yes 1 to 65535 Rate limit: at most this many candidate edges (edges of the configured direction, including the ones the debounce later drops as glitches) per window_ms. One more disarms the pin, the qualifier becomes QLF_ERROR (interrupt storm: bouncing contact, broken wire, fault on the line). pin_events.<key>.window_ms integer ms yes 1 to 60000 Time window of the rate limit. pin_events.<key>.rearm_ms integer ms yes 1 to 600000 Hold-off after the rate limit tripped: the pin is armed again automatically after this time. pin_events.<key>.wakeup boolean no false Reserved: the input as wake-up source of an MCU low-power mode. true is rejected until neXtBSW has an MCU low-power mode; today the ECU sleeps through the supply (SBC local wake inputs, ecu.wakeup). pin_events.<key>.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: safety
docs.text:
Pins of the OpenBSW safety demo.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description safety.safe_state_output string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Indicator of the safe state, a digital output: disabled (it floats) in the safe state and switched back with the level the application wrote last when the safe state is left. No actuator, and an output the application does not write - otherwise see safe_state_output_shared_with_application. safety.locked_pin string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Digital output whose pin configuration gets locked. safety.test_pin string yes Unconnected pin, checked cyclically as input. safety.safe_state_output_shared_with_application string no null Confirms on purpose that the application writes safe_state_output (an rte.yaml dio.out target), with the reason as text - for example that the output is only a status LED. Entering the safe state disables the indicator's pin (it floats), leaving it switches the pin back with the level the application wrote last, so an actuator there would float in the safe state and come back on without an enable (AoU-30 of the safety concept). With the key, nxconfig does not warn about that case; without the case, the key itself is reported as superfluous. Left out: not confirmed. safety.output_groups list of object no [] After R1. Safe-output groups for the degraded reaction. Left out: none - every reaction switches all outputs, as before. safety.degraded list of object no [] After R1. Events that report and switch only their safe-output groups instead of the fail-safe reaction (safe state for everything, reset). The rest of the ECU keeps running without a reset, the application reads the degraded groups from the RTE signal safety.degraded, and the groups stay degraded until the next power cycle, also across a reset. Left out: none - every event keeps its fail-safe reaction.

docs.title: safety.output_groups[] (after R1)
docs.text: After R1: part of the schema and checked by tools/nxconfig, but not of the first release; the table is written when the object is. Keys: name, pwm, note.

docs.title: safety.degraded[] (after R1)
docs.text: After R1: part of the schema and checked by tools/nxconfig, but not of the first release; the table is written when the object is. Keys: event, device, groups, note.

docs.title: modules.<key>.<key>
docs.text:
Selective CAN wake-up (ISO 11898-2/-6 partial networking) of a system basis chip.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description modules.<key>.<key>.id integer none yes ≥ 0 Identifier of the wake-up frame (11 or 29 bit). modules.<key>.<key>.extended boolean no false true: 29 bit identifier, false: 11 bit. modules.<key>.<key>.compare_mask integer none no null ≥ 0 Identifier bits that must match (bit = 1); bits 0 are don't care. Left out: all bits, the frame must carry exactly id. modules.<key>.<key>.dlc integer none no null 0 to 8 Data length the frame must have; with it the data field is part of the match. Left out: only the identifier is compared. modules.<key>.<key>.data_mask list of integer none no [] item: 0 to 255 Per data byte 0..dlc-1: the frame wakes if one of its bits set here is set in the frame. Exactly dlc entries, at least one not 0 (left out with dlc 0). modules.<key>.<key>.fd_passive boolean no false true: CAN FD frames on the bus are tolerated in Sleep; false: they count as errors and wake the SBC after 32 of them.

docs.title: hw_thresholds.<key> (after R1)
docs.text: After R1: part of the schema and checked by tools/nxconfig, but not of the first release; the table is written when the object is. Keys: input, trip, threshold, reference, pwm, filter_ns, verify, note.

docs.title: sample_groups.<key>
docs.text:
Board ADC channels converted after every hardware trigger of a PWM group (fast control loop).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description sample_groups.<key>.pwm string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ PWM group of the project (pwm.<group>) whose trigger output starts the group; the group needs pwm.<group>.trigger. sample_groups.<key>.channels list of string none yes 1 to 32 items; item: at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Board ADC entries (adc[].name) of the group, in the order of the results. Entries on different ADCs are sampled at the same instant, entries on one ADC one after another in this order (nxconfig warns and names the time offset). sample_groups.<key>.delay_ns integer ns no 0 0 to 1000000 Time from the trigger point of the PWM group to the start of the first sample. The realised value is a whole number of sequencer clocks (nxconfig shows it). sample_groups.<key>.verify boolean no false true: the sampling instant is not confirmed (e.g. not measured on a board). sample_groups.<key>.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: bsw_tasks.<key>
docs.text:
Stack of one BSW task, or the task it runs in instead of a task of its own.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description bsw_tasks.<key>.stack_bytes integer byte no null > 0 Stack of the task. At least min_stack_bytes of ecu/configuration/taskStacks.yaml and a multiple of its multiple_of (8, the safety task 32: MPU region). Below the default nxconfig warns: confirm the value with the high-water mark (console stats) or tools/stackuse. Left out: the default of taskStacks.yaml. bsw_tasks.<key>.run_in string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Merge the task into another BSW task: no FreeRTOS task and no stack of its own, its work runs in the named task at that task's priority (its stack has to hold both). Only the merges taskStacks.yaml lists for the task (run_in); never for or into the safety task. Left out: the task runs on its own. bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence object no null Proof note of the stack (tools/stackuse or high-water mark at the board). Required for a stack below the default in an ASIL project (project.integrity not qm), otherwise a warning. Left out: no proof noted. bsw_tasks.<key>.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence
docs.text:
Proof note of a BSW task stack: what the task uses of its stack and where that is shown.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence.method string yes stackuse, high_water_mark Same as memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.method. bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence.used_bytes integer byte yes > 0 Same as memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.used_bytes. bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence.reference string yes at least 1 character Same as memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.reference.

docs.title: console
docs.text:
Console and logger of the application on the terminal UART.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description console.enabled boolean no true false: no console (no command input, no console commands of the application) and no logger (log calls do nothing, no ring buffer). The UART stays initialised: the safety lines of the safe supervisor (SAFETY RESET, safety::safeConsoleWrite) and the start-up lines are written to it synchronously in every image. Left out: true. console.logger_buffer_bytes integer byte no null 512 to 65536 Size of the logger ring buffer. A full buffer drops the oldest entries (console logger lost counts them); below 8192 bytes the start-up of the eval board lost lines (board 2026-09-18). Left out: 8192. console.note string no null Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it.

docs.title: ECU description (rte.yaml)
docs.text:
Software components, their connections, application tasks and the CAN database of one ECU. The file is named by project.rte in project.yaml, checked against its schema by tools/nxconfig (with file, line and YAML path, before the build) and read by tools/rtegen. What needs the component ARXML, the DBC, the BSW task manifest or the board signals of the project - unknown ports and runnables, the type of a connection, periods and priorities against the BSW tasks, the rules of an E2E profile - is checked by tools/rtegen (--validate, the same messages in neXtBSW Studio).

Configuration level: Project. File: projects/<project>/rte.yaml. Schema: EcuDescription in tools/nxconfig/model.py.

39 fields in 8 objects. 0 fields have no description in the schema and 0 numeric fields have no unit; they are marked missing in schema and missing. How to read the tables: reference overview.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• (top level)
    • tasks[]
      • tasks[].runnables[]
    • components[]
    • can
      • can.qualifiers.<key>
        • can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e
    • uds

docs.title: (top level)
docs.text:
ECU description of a project (projects/<project>/rte.yaml, named by project.rte).

Software components, the connections of their ports, application tasks and the CAN signals of one ECU; read by tools/rtegen. Values of the ECU state management and XCP are project values (project.yaml) and do not stand here.

Format 2 (customer-project.md gap N3): components[].path and can.dbc are relative to this file, like project.board is relative to project.yaml. Before that they were relative to the root of the repository, which only exists in the neXtBSW tree itself - a customer workspace has no such root. A file without the key is format 1 and is raised by nxconfig migrate (migrate.STEPS, step rte:2).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description schema_version integer yes 2 Version of the file format; currently 2. tasks list of object no null at least 1 item Application tasks. Left out: one task with the default name, priority and stack of the BSW task manifest and the period base_period_ms. base_period_ms integer ms no null > 0 Only without tasks: period of the one application task. Left out: the greatest common divisor of the runnable periods. components list of object yes Software components of the ECU; each name once. []: none yet (empty project, only the BSW runs). can object no null CAN signals from a DBC; left out: no CAN signals. uds object no null Bus of the application diagnostic stack. connections map of string to string or list of string no {} value: at least 1 character; value: at least 1 item; value: item: at least 1 character Port connections, key Component.Port.Element. A required port has exactly one source: a provided port Component.Port.Element, a BSW signal (dio.in.<INPUT>, adc.mv.<CHANNEL>, adc.raw.<CHANNEL>, adc.phys.<CHANNEL>, adc.qlf.<CHANNEL>, a value of a module instance <prefix>.<INSTANCE>.<value> as its module.yaml rte describes it (e.g. capture.<CHANNEL>.<value>, hall.<DEVICE>.<value>, gd.<DEVICE>.<value>), ecu.state, ecu.wakeup[.<source>], a BSW service port bsw.power.<value>, bsw.reset.<value>, bsw.time.<value>), a received CAN signal can.rx.<Message>.<Signal> or qualifier can.qlf.<Message>, a non-volatile block nvm.<Block> (reads the stored value, same type as its writer) or its quality nvm.qlf.<Block>, or rte.init (keeps its init value). A provided port feeds one target or a list: dio.out.<OUTPUT>, pwm.<PAIR>, can.tx.<Message>.<Signal>, ecu.sleep_request, a non-volatile block nvm.<Block> (exactly one writer per block, its init value is the default; definition, place and write policy in project.yaml nvm.blocks), or rte (value stays in the RTE). A mode port (required port with a mode switch interface, key Component.Port.ModeGroup) is connected to the ECU mode manager ecu.mode: its mode declaration group names exactly the ECU states STARTUP, RUN, STANDBY, RUNDOWN, SHUTDOWN and SLEEP, and the component reads the mode with Rte_Mode_<Port>_<ModeGroup>(). ecu_state any no null Not allowed: the parameters of the ECU state management are project values in project.yaml modules.ecuState.

docs.title: tasks[]
docs.text:
One application task of the ECU: FreeRTOS task running the runnables assigned to it.

The BSW tasks (bsp, can, ...) are not listed here; they come from ecu/asyncCoreConfiguration/tasks.yaml.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description tasks[].name string yes pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ Task name: lower case letters and digits, starting with a letter (no underscore; idle and timer are reserved). Must not be the name of a BSW task. tasks[].period_ms integer ms yes > 0 Cycle of the task, a multiple of the OS tick of the BSW task manifest. Every runnable of the task has a period that is a multiple of it. tasks[].priority integer none yes > 0 Ordering key between the BSW tasks of the manifest (e.g. between bsp 20 and can 40); unique over all tasks. The FreeRTOS priority follows from the order. tasks[].stack_bytes integer byte yes ≥ 0 Stack of the task; at least min_stack_bytes of the BSW task manifest. tasks[].runnables list of object no null Runnables in call order. Left out in every task and only one task: all periodic and mode switch runnables run in it. Otherwise every periodic and every mode switch runnable has to be listed in exactly one task. Mode switch runnables run at the start of a cycle, before the periodic ones: first every on-exit, then every on-transition, then every on-entry runnable, each group in the order of this list.

docs.title: tasks[].runnables[]
docs.text:
A runnable assigned to an application task, optionally with a start offset.

In the list tasks[].runnables an entry may be written as plain text Component.Runnable (offset 0) or as a mapping {runnable: Component.Runnable, offset_ms: 20}. A mode switch runnable is listed the same way and never has an offset.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description tasks[].runnables[].runnable string yes at least 1 character Runnable as Component.Runnable (name of the component in components[], runnable of its ARXML): a periodic runnable (TIMING-EVENT) or a mode switch runnable (SWC-MODE-SWITCH-EVENT on entry, exit or transition of an ECU mode; the event is part of the component, the task is chosen here). tasks[].runnables[].offset_ms integer ms no 0 ≥ 0 Start offset inside the task: the runnable runs in the task cycles offset_ms, offset_ms + period, ... A multiple of the task period and below the period of the runnable. Not for a mode switch runnable, which runs once at the start of the first task cycle after the mode switch. tasks[].runnables[].enabled boolean no true false: the runnable is disabled - it keeps its place in this list but is not called. Required ports of other components that it feeds read a constant value instead: the init value of the provided port, else components[].disabled_values, else the init value of the reading port; a qualifier port reads QLF_NOT_AVAILABLE. Not allowed for a runnable of a safety-relevant component (swc.yaml safety other than qm).

docs.title: components[]
docs.text:
A software component of the ECU: its name and the folder with generated/arxml and <Name>_data.m.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description components[].name string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ Component name as in its ARXML (Simulink model name, e.g. DemoSwc). components[].path string yes at least 1 character Component folder relative to the repository root (tools/rtegen --repo), e.g. swc/DemoSwc. The RTE reads <path>/generated/arxml/*.arxml and the calibration values of <path>/<name>_data.m. components[].enabled boolean no true false: the component is disabled - its init and its runnables are not called (it stays compiled; the linker drops the code nobody calls). Required ports of other components it feeds read a constant value instead: the init value of its provided port, else disabled_values, else the init value of the reading port; a qualifier port reads QLF_NOT_AVAILABLE. Not allowed for a safety-relevant component (swc.yaml safety other than qm). components[].disabled_values map of string to boolean or integer or number or string or any none no {} Value a provided port (key Port.Element) delivers while the part that writes it is disabled (enabled: false here or at the runnable). Required - and only allowed - for a port without an init value of its own: a C component (swc.yaml has no init values) or an ARXML port without INIT-VALUE (unless every reading port has an init value of its own, or is a qualifier port). A number (physical value of a fixed-point type), true/false, an enumeration literal, or a list for an array or a record. Kept while the part is enabled, so switching it on and off again needs no new entry.

docs.title: can
docs.text:
CAN signals of the ECU (section can:): the DBC, the node of this ECU in it and the bus they run on.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description can.dbc string yes at least 1 character DBC file relative to the repository root. can.node string yes at least 1 character Node of this ECU in the DBC: its messages are sent, the messages it receives are received. can.bus string no null at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ CAN bus of the project (board can[].name, used in use.can) the signals run on. Left out: the first CAN bus of the project. can.monitor list of string no [] DBC messages whose signals the RTE receives for the console and XCP without a connected port. can.task string no null Application task that sends and receives the messages. Left out: the only application task (required with several). can.qualifiers map of string to object no {} Supervision per DBC message (key: message name).

docs.title: can.qualifiers.<key>
docs.text:
Supervision of one CAN message: timeout, debouncing and error values of the signal qualifier.

A received message may use every key, a sent message only e2e. A received message without entry keeps the defaults (DBC timeout, no debouncing, values hold).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description can.qualifiers.<key>.timeout_ms integer ms no null ≥ 0 Received message: time without a message after which the qualifier reports ERROR_TIMEOUT; 0 switches the supervision off. Left out: GenMsgTimeoutTime of the DBC. can.qualifiers.<key>.debounce_ms integer ms no 0 ≥ 0 Received message: an E2E or timeout error must last this long before the qualifier reports it (QLF_DEBOUNCE until then). can.qualifiers.<key>.on_error string no "hold" hold, init Received message: signal values while the qualifier reports an error - hold keeps the last valid values, init falls back to GenSigStartValue. can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e object no null E2E protection of the message; left out: none.

docs.title: can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e
docs.text:
AUTOSAR E2E protection of one CAN message: profile, data id and the DBC signals of CRC and counter.

Receiving, the RTE checks it and reports errors in the signal qualifier; sending, it writes counter and CRC. Which keys a profile takes is checked by tools/rtegen: P01/P11 data_id (16 bit, NIBBLE: 12 bit) and data_id_mode, P02 data_id_list (16 values of 8 bit).

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e.profile string yes P01, P02, P11 E2E profile of libs/bsw/e2e. can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e.data_id integer none no null ≥ 0 Data id of the message (P01, P11). Left out: 0. can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e.data_id_list list of integer none no null item: ≥ 0 P02 only: one 8-bit data id per counter value 0..15 (exactly 16 values). can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e.data_id_mode string no null BOTH, ALT, LOW, NIBBLE How the data id enters the CRC (P01: BOTH, ALT, LOW, NIBBLE; P11: BOTH, NIBBLE; not for P02). Case does not matter. Left out: BOTH. can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e.data_id_nibble string no null Mode NIBBLE only: DBC signal that carries the high nibble of the data id. can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e.crc string yes at least 1 character DBC signal of the CRC. can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e.counter string yes at least 1 character DBC signal of the sequence counter. can.qualifiers.<key>.e2e.max_delta_counter integer counter steps no 1 > 0 Largest accepted counter jump (MaxDeltaCounter), below the counter range of the profile.

docs.title: uds
docs.text:
CAN bus of the application diagnostic stack (ecu/uds). Left out: the bus of the CAN signals.

Field Type Unit Required Default Allowed values Description uds.bus string yes at least 1 character, pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ CAN bus of the project (board can[].name, used in use.can) that DoCAN runs on. The diagnostic addresses are project.yaml diagnostics.

docs.title: neXtBSW v1.0.0-rc1 — release notes
docs.text:
Release date: 2026-10-05 (tag v1.0.0-rc1)

Development release – no safety claim.

neXtBSW targets ASIL B as a software safety element out of context. This release candidate (release R1) does not claim ASIL B capability and is not a safety release.

  • R1 was checked under deviation D-01: the confirmation measures were performed by the safety responsible without independence. No working state and no tag gets an ASIL statement from them.
  • Performed for R1 (all under D-01): CM-01 safety plan, CM-02 safety analyses, CM-04 verification plan and CM-07 safety concept and CM-05 safety case (each closed after a re-check), CM-10 safety manual (accepted with conditions; one finding open until the first public release) and CM-06 release decision (accepted with conditions: the release was decided with the conditions bound CI report, board run on the tagged image and verified export; see the record of the release).
  • Performed after R1, as a documented deviation from their planned timing: CM-03 (dependent failure analysis), CM-08 (tool classification and qualification), CM-09 (component qualification and coexistence) and CM-11 (functional safety audit). The deviation is recorded in safety plan section 5 and as deficit D-22 in the safety case. It is lifted before the first public release or the first release with an ASIL B claim, whichever comes first.
  • R1 is distributed privately. Every recipient receives this statement together with the safety manual.
