docs.title: What is neXtBSW
docs.text:
neXtBSW is a configurable basic software for 32-bit ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-R microcontrollers (little endian), built on Eclipse OpenBSW and FreeRTOS. A control unit is described in configuration files — MCU derivative, board and project — and generators derive clock tree, pins, CAN bit timing, memory layout, bootloader values and the RTE from them. Application software is attached as Simulink models (AUTOSAR Classic software components) through the generated RTE.

Start with the README and the documentation map.

docs.title: Platforms and projects
docs.text:
Board profile / project (CMake preset) Derivative (core) Configure and check Target build On hardware buildtest_s32k148 / buildtest-s32k148-min S32K148 (Cortex-M4F) yes yes no board behind it (build test) same, buildtest-s32k148-ethernet, buildtest-s32k148-threadx S32K148 yes yes no; keep the paths to Ethernet/lwIP and ThreadX open, not the default s32k116evb / s32k116evb-minimal S32K116 (Cortex-M0+) yes partly: the full application does not fit into 128 KB flash yet no nucleo_f446re / nucleo-f446re-demo STM32F446RE (Cortex-M4F) yes no for the application (board generator lacks the stm32 family); the platform build-test image builds partly: flashing, clock, LED, button, console S32K3, TI RM4x — derivative data, nxconfig check no no

The software has been brought up on one S32K144 board of the maintainer, whose board files are not part of this tree. For an S32K1 derivative with a Cortex-M4F you can describe your board, check it and build application and bootloader; expect to be the first to measure the bring-up on your own hardware. Details: Getting started — What runs today.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• Configuration and generators: configuration model and checks (tools/nxconfig), BSW and RTE generators (bswgen, rtegen), CAN database generator (dbcgen), calibration objects in swc.yaml with A2L and datasets, configuration and generator identity in the image (console version/info, UDS DID).
  • ECU application and services: derived from the OpenBSW reference application; ECU state management, CAN with a second bus (diagnostic CAN), UDS in the application, fault memory (simplified DEM), NvM core with integrity classes, data flash, persistent operating hours and reset statistics, E2E profiles P01/P02/P11, XCP.
  • Drivers: 27 driver and service modules with neutral contracts; their verification level is listed per module in the module reference and drawn in the module map.
  • Bootloader: UDS bootloader over CAN (ISO-TP), plain C, hardware-independent core; flashing with tools/canflash; bootloader updater; diagnostic CAN supported (nextbsw-bl 0.3.9).
  • Safety mechanisms (stage 1, s32k1xx family port): safe supervisor, safety task and lifecycle, MPU-protected safety RAM, ECC supervision, ROM check, supply and ADC reference supervision, watchdog and halt deadman, safe outputs table with read-back, degraded reaction per PWM group. The list of mechanisms, what each one covers and what an integrator may rely on is in the safety manual section 5.
  • Tools: test runner (tools/test), CI wrapper (tools/ci), workspace update (tools/nxupdate), distribution check (tools/distcheck).

docs.title: Not part of this release
docs.text:
• neXtBSW Studio (desktop tool) — it has its own release and is not contained in this distribution.
  • The maintainer's own evaluation board, its projects and its board recordings.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Level What State Host (mock) host tests, register models, generator tests with own profiles, mutation checks, static analysis; one command: .venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group all all 27 modules have host tests; 14 modules are verified on the host only (mock in the module reference); release CI on the tagged tree (tools.ci run --strict --slow): 413 of 413 entries green, 539 160 test cases, 50 target builds, static analysis without new findings; report bound to the tag (ci-out-v1.0.0-rc1.zip) Target build application, bootloader and updater for the presets above, warnings as errors see the platform table Board (hardware) one S32K144 board with lab supplies, electronic load, oscilloscope and CAN interface; board sessions per task and suite runs of the board test specification 13 modules verified on hardware (hardware in the module reference): canSystem, consoleContext, e2e, ecuState, gdTmc6200, highSideSwitch, sbcUja113x, bspAdcAccess, bspSpi, safeLifecycle, safeMemory, safeSupervisor, safeSystem; bootloader flashing over CAN including the diagnostic CAN Board regression of the release the demo cases of the board test specification with tools/boardtest suite, the S1 read-back case BT-S1-03 with the pin cases, and the restart-time measurement F4 with the oscilloscope release candidate (code freeze plus version, image SHA-256 93e9796e…730afd, 2026-10-04): no firmware finding; 21 of 25 suite cases passed, the bus-off case included; the remaining cases failed on the test definition, not on the firmware, and passed or were shown by hand after its correction (BT-S1-01: one tool finding left, the board behaviour confirmed by the tester); BT-S1-03: outputs off within 0.71 ms; F4 in six runs: 703 ms (MPU path, limit 858 ms) and 896 … 926 ms (watchdog path, limit 1 077 ms). Tagged image: the automated cases and F4 repeated on 2026-10-05 (image SHA-256 1583be99…c7ba45, the identification v1.0.0-rc1 on the board): 9 of 9 automated cases passed; F4 in six runs 703 ms (MPU path) and 876 … 926 ms (watchdog path) — the cases with a manual step count from the candidate, whose image differs from the tagged one only in the repository identification

Further board results of R1 were taken at integration states between 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-04 (recording folders 2026-10-02_board, 2026-10-02_suite-integ12, 2026-10-03_board, 2026-10-04_rc1-candidate of the development repository). The recordings are not part of this distribution and are available on request. Open board proofs are listed in the safety manual section 10.3 and under Known limitations.

Limits of the release verification compared with a safety release: no coverage gate, no independent review of test authoring, reproduction of the release build on a second machine not shown. They are listed in verification plan section 9.1.

docs.title: Safety documentation
docs.text:
The work products the integrator reads, with their issue at the code freeze. "Accepted" means accepted by the safety responsible; "under D-01" means after a confirmation review without independence.

Work product Issue / status Safety manual (assumptions of use) issue 2, accepted under D-01 (CM-10, accepted with conditions; one finding open until the first public release) Safety concept and the safety requirement catalogues (doc/requirements/safety: safety requirements, goals, assumptions, mechanisms) issue 3, accepted under D-01 (CM-07 closed) Failure analysis (FMEA) issue 2, accepted under D-01 (CM-02 closed) Architecture safety analysis issue 2, accepted under D-01 (CM-02 closed) Verification plan issue 2, accepted under D-01 (CM-04 closed) Safety plan issue 2, accepted under D-01 (CM-01 closed) Safety case issue 2, accepted under D-01 (CM-05 closed); top claim not supported Dependent failure analysis issue 1, accepted; confirmation CM-03 after R1 Tool classification issue 1, accepted; confirmation CM-08 after R1; qualification reports of the TCL 2 tools not written Component qualification, coexistence issue 1, draft / accepted; confirmation CM-09 after R1 Anomaly register issue 1, accepted; public extract below Configuration management plan issue 2, accepted Board test specification issue 1, draft

Not published, available on request. These stay in the development repository: the records of the confirmation reviews and inspections (doc/safety/reviews), the gap analysis, the generated traceability matrix, the RTOS comparison, the requirements other than the safety catalogues, the board recordings, parts B and C of the partner-and-degraded analysis (implementation notes and decisions B/C; section 7, the source of AoU-31 and AoU-33, is published) and the planning files. A Markdown link to such a file reads "not published, available on request" in the distributed tree. Where a document names such a file only as a path in the text, the path is left as it is: the file is not part of this distribution and is likewise available on request. None of these files raises a verdict of the published documents.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
Area Limitation in v1.0.0-rc1 Motor control (FOC) no fast control loop and no motor application in this release; the concept is in fast-control-loop.md (not published, available on request). The center-aligned PWM group with trigger and the hardware trigger chain PWM → TRGMUX → PDB → ADC are in the tree, host-verified, without board proof and not part of the R1 scope Hardware over-current shut-off the comparator threshold with shut-off without the core, its start test and the FTM fault inputs are in the tree, host-verified, without board proof and not part of the R1 scope; the related anomalies are listed below CAN FD only the bit-timing calculation exists (host-tested); no CAN FD driver, schema, DBC/RTE or flashing over CAN FD OTA and multi-MCU ECUs no OTA master, image store or campaign; the inter-MCU link protocol (mcuLink) is host-verified only Secure boot the bootloader checks the application image (CRC, record, compatibility block) but not its own integrity and verifies no signature; CSEc secure boot is planned after R1 Further platforms the safety family port exists for s32k1xx only (safety manual 1.4); STM32, S32K3 and RM4x get the family-neutral part only; S32K116 does not fit the full application yet Board proofs after R1 hold and S1 + S2 with a gated timer, B16 (a), (c), (d), and the low-voltage detect reset (SM-59) at falling supply have no board recording; the LVD reset is switched on and re-checked cyclically, but not credited Partitioning no partitioning of the application; the MPU protects the safety manager's data and stack only; task activation is not supervised Stage-2 mechanisms no plausibility between two measurement paths, no age supervision of device values, no safe state for bus-commanded actuators (G2 … G4) Process no quality management system, no evidence of competence, no independent confirmation review, no functional safety assessment (AoU-35) Tool qualification qualification reports for the TCL 2 tools and the FreeRTOS qualification package are not written Cybersecurity no cybersecurity claim (safety manual section 11) SBC without software development mode an SBC without software development mode (UJA113x SDMS 0) runs its watchdog after an SBC reset already in Standby: use bootloader.sbc_watchdog: serve; the correction follows with a separate task (AN-191). With the default leave a device without a valid application resets in a loop (outputs de-energised, but it cannot be updated), and an application must trigger the watchdog within about 256 ms after the SBC start. The eval board (SDMS 1) is not affected Host tests on Linux several host tests do not build with a 64-bit long; the suite is run on Windows (AN-118)

The complete list, including evidence limits, is in safety manual section 10.

docs.title: Known anomalies
docs.text:
Public extract of the anomaly register at the code freeze: anomalies with status open or accepted that affect how an integrator uses neXtBSW. Anomalies about the documents themselves or about the internal process are not listed; the register has all of them.

ID Anomaly Effect Workaround / assumption of use AN-005 (accepted) a failed SPI master is a common cause for several device diagnostics and is not treated as one event device diagnostics on one SPI bus can fail together; only a per-bus "bus lost" correlation exists no stage-1 mechanism relies on SPI; consider SPI as a shared resource in your own analysis AN-010 (open) RTE task activation (starvation, late start) is not supervised; only run durations are measured a task that is not activated or starts late is not detected by the BSW AoU-17: develop safety-related code at the target ASIL or provide your own partitioning and timing supervision AN-016 (accepted) the tolerance band of the ADC reference supervision allows a silent gain error of up to about 5 % on every analogue value analogue values may be wrong within the band without a reaction AoU-24: check that the reference tolerance is smaller than the accuracy your safety-related values need AN-018, AN-020 (open) no plausibility check of two measurement paths; no safe state for bus-commanded actuators ASG-04 has no stage-1 mechanism; ASG-01 only partly covered AoU-23: provide this detection yourself AN-024 (open) the MCU manufacturer's safety manual is not available to the project; the required software measures are not derived from it hardware coverage statements refer only to neXtBSW's use of a feature AoU-09, AoU-36: obtain it and apply the measures it requires AN-025, AN-067 (open) the MPU does not deny DMA and Ethernet masters access to the protected RAM (descriptor 0 grants them access) a DMA or Ethernet master could overwrite safety data AoU-41: enable no bus master other than the core AN-026 (open) no mechanism checks the integrity of the bootloader itself a corrupted bootloader is not detected (ASG-07 partial) none in this release; consider it in your analysis; CSEc secure boot planned after R1 AN-058 … AN-065 (open) some configuration registers are written but not re-checked at run time: NVIC of the watchdog warning interrupt, system handler enables, ERM and flash fault interrupts, LPIT and system clock, FTM output mask, platform clock gates, ADC supply enable a drift of these registers is not detected by the cyclic register check none in this release; listed so that you can consider them in your hardware analysis AN-069 (open) a stopped LPIT functional clock stops the halt deadman (SM-06) on a lost clock only the MCU watchdog reset de-energises the outputs, after at most about 283 ms on the maintainer's board safety manual 10.2: residual risk; compare the time with your fault tolerant time interval AN-071 (open) the safe outputs walk skips a clock-gated FTM; a gated timer keeps its output level after S1 a PWM group whose timer clock gate is off is not de-energised by the walk give each PWM group a safe_off enable on another peripheral; nxconfig warns for a group without one AN-073 (open) a stopped system time is not detected by the period check SPI and CAN time-outs that count on the system time stop the halt deadman SM-06 (outputs off after about 10 ms) and the watchdog SM-01 (reset after about 160 to 283 ms) react; safety manual section 5 AN-102 … AN-105, AN-119, AN-120 (open) hardware fault path (FTM fault inputs, comparator): polarity and reset behaviour not verified, recovery and start-test strategy undecided, interplay with the safe outputs walk undecided, start with an exceeded threshold and output state with fault control enabled not confirmed on the board the hardware over-current shut-off is not proven do not rely on the hardware threshold in R1 (not part of the R1 scope) AN-130 (accepted) the watchdog is switched off on the way to lifecycle level 0 a level-1 component that hangs in its shutdown is not detected accepted residual; consider it for your shutdown sequence AN-131 (accepted) the interrupt lock around the selection of the active short works only in privileged code in unprivileged thread mode the lock is ignored without a fault AoU-42: run every task privileged AN-164 (open) UDS 10 02 resets the ECU into the bootloader without S1 and without precondition; UDS 11 01/03 run down without precondition a diagnostic request can reset the ECU in any state AoU-ASA-b: protect ECU reset and writing services by security access and a precondition you define AN-165 (accepted) at run-down the outputs keep their last value until the last run-down step actuators stay commanded during run-down AoU-ASA-d: switch the actuators off in the application at RUNDOWN AN-166 (open) timeout_ms: 0 switches the reception time-out off, also for a message with an E2E profile, and no check refuses it a lost safety-related message is not detected AoU-11: configure an E2E profile and a non-zero time-out for every safety-related message AN-167 (open) the age qualifier for ports between tasks is optional a consumer of a stopped producer sees the last value configure the age qualifier on safety-related ports between tasks AN-168 (open) a failed read of dio.in, adc.mv or adc.raw keeps the old value without a qualifier; a failed dio.out write is discarded the application cannot see the failed access none in the BSW in this release; plan your own plausibility for safety-related inputs (AoU-23) AN-169 (open) a UDS DID (2E) or routine (31) may write a required port of a safety-related component; docs.title: Upgrade from v0.2.0
docs.text:
The notes below are taken from the changelog; a compatibility review per interface (RTE, schema, safe supervisor API, assumptions of use) against v0.2.0 was not made.

  • Version. VERSION reads 1.0.0 (the file holds MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH only); the release-candidate state is the tag v1.0.0-rc1, which the image carries in its repository identification. Moving a customer workspace pin: tools/nxupdate <workspace> --to v1.0.0-rc1 (dry run first; see tools/nxupdate).
  • Bootloader 0.3.5 → 0.3.9. Update fielded bootloaders with the updater (canflash blupdate, see tools/canflash) or with the debug probe (flash-bootloader). Since 0.3.7 the bootloader starts only an application whose record carries the compatibility block, and it checks the image again right before the jump; a record written before that block existed is no longer started (DID 0xF1A0 reports why) — flash the application again with the current tools. 0.3.6 adds the low-voltage detect reset from the reset handler and skips the start window after the watchdog fast-test resets; 0.3.9 fixes a reset loop on the 16-buffer FlexCAN instances (diagnostic CAN).
  • NvM layout. The reserved fault memory block DemEvents grows when a project takes the new standard safety-reset DTCs (in the maintainer's demo: 14 → 39 bytes, 2 → 7 DTCs), and the new reserved block EcuStatistics (operating hours and reset statistics, DID 0x0130) lies behind the component and fault memory blocks. Blocks behind a changed one move: after flashing, the fault memory starts empty once and the statistics start at zero once.
  • AUTOSAR base types. uint32/sint32 (and the other integer types) are now the stdint.h types; on the target uint32 is unsigned long. Code that relied on uint32 being unsigned int (format strings, overloads) needs a look.
  • Stricter checks of nxconfig. New project field project.integrity (qm, asil_a … asil_d): without it a project counts as an ASIL project, qm has to be set deliberately. In an ASIL project a BSW task stack, the interrupt stack or its guard below the default without an evidence note is an error (a warning in a QM project); merging the background task into bsp is refused for projects with a power stage; an interrupt stack value on a family where it has no effect is an error. New project values: bsw_tasks.<task>.evidence, memory.application.isr_stack_size, isr_stack_guard_size and their evidence fields.
  • Product image. Service console commands that write registers, frames, outputs or the fault memory are no longer in the product build (NX_PRODUCT_BUILD=ON); out set refuses safe_off outputs in every build, pwm refuses the PWM groups of the safe outputs table. Read commands and nvm write stay.

docs.title: neXtBSW v1.0.0-rc2 — release notes
docs.text:
Release date: 2026-10-XX

Development release – no safety claim.

neXtBSW targets ASIL B as a software safety element out of context. This second release candidate of 1.0.0 does not claim ASIL B capability and is not a safety release.

  • No release decision like the one of rc1. The release decision CM-06 of the safety plan was made for v1.0.0-rc1 only. For v1.0.0-rc2 no such decision has been recorded; rc2 is a candidate for the public state of neXtBSW, not a release confirmed by a review.
  • The confirmation measures that exist were performed by the safety responsible under deviation D-01, without independence. No working state and no tag gets an ASIL statement from them.
  • The deviation recorded for rc1 still applies: CM-03 (dependent failure analysis), CM-08 (tool classification and qualification), CM-09 (component qualification and coexistence) and CM-11 (functional safety audit) are not yet performed (safety plan section 5, deficit D-22 in the safety case). The safety plan ties their completion to the first release with an ASIL B claim; until then a release may be public only as a development release without a safety claim, as this one is (decision of the safety responsible 2026-10-08, safety plan issue 3, released in its confirmation review the same day).
  • Every recipient receives this statement together with the safety manual; it stands in every release note and in the README of the repository (safety plan section 5).

docs.title: Why rc2
docs.text:
v1.0.0-rc1 (2026-10-05) was distributed privately. Before the first public distribution the distributed tree was reviewed for licences and for the public provenance of every value and statement it contains. The review found passages in the rc1 distribution that were taken from a manufacturer document that is not public. v1.0.0-rc2 is the cleaned state: those passages are removed, and every statement they supported now rests on public sources only. The same review led to the other distribution changes listed below (generated code, generator output, supported families). v1.0.0-rc2 is the state from which the public repository is built.

The firmware changes of rc2 are small: the bootloader serves the SBC watchdog of an SBC without software development mode (0.3.10 and 0.3.11), and the SBC driver documents its behaviour from the public data sheet with its code unchanged.

docs.title: Changes since v1.0.0-rc1
docs.text: The changelog of the development repository has the details per task.

docs.title: Sources and distribution
docs.text:
• SBC driver and bootloader SBC hook from public sources only. Every statement of the UJA113x driver, the bootloader's SBC hook, their tests and their module documentation that rested on a non-public manufacturer document now cites the public UJA113x data sheet (Rev. 2); the code of the driver is unchanged. On the way, the host model of the bootloader test was corrected to the data sheet: without software development mode (SDMS 0) the SBC watchdog already runs in Standby after an SBC reset. This finding led to the bootloader changes below.
  • The distribution check guards it. tools/distcheck refuses references to the content of non-public application material in the open export, and it refuses every value in mcudb and in the published board profiles that has no public evidence (verify: true) instead of only warning.
  • Simulink-generated code is not distributed. Code and ARXML generated by Simulink Coder (the demo component and one RTE test model) are left out of the open export. The models, their parameters and the build script stay. The export puts a hand-written C component with the same RTE interface in place of the demo component (swc/DemoSwcSubstitute), so the demo builds without MATLAB; with your own MATLAB licence you can generate the original from the model.
  • Generator output exception. Files written by the neXtBSW generators may be used under terms of your choice. The exception is stated in NOTICE and in LICENSES/AdditionRef-neXtBSW-Generator-Output-Exception.txt; every generated file carries the SPDX line Apache-2.0 WITH AdditionRef-neXtBSW-Generator-Output-Exception. The generators and their templates stay Apache-2.0.
  • Published scope narrowed to the S32K1 family. STM32, S32K3 and TI RM4x (derivative data, platform code and their tests), the Nucleo-F446RE board and project and the S32K116EVB board profile are not part of this distribution until their values have public evidence. The S32K116 derivative data and the build-test profile of the S32K148 stay.
  • Export fixes. The export carries the pinned commit of the Eclipse OpenBSW submodule (rc1 needed it added by hand), and the test suite of the exported tree runs on the published profiles (seven tests moved off the private demo project).

docs.title: Bootloader 0.3.9 → 0.3.11
docs.text:
• 0.3.10: with an SBC without software development mode (UJA113x SDMS 0) the bootloader always serves the SBC watchdog itself, also with bootloader.sbc_watchdog: leave: fixed autonomous setting in Standby, trigger every 256 ms and right before the jump, so that the application has a full period to take over. With development mode (SDMS 1) leave is unchanged. New diagnostic field bl_sbc_watchdog.reason.
  • 0.3.11: the same also when the bootloader only reads the SBC (the SBC not in bootloader.init, for example a bootloader on another CAN bus): only the watchdog is set and triggered, the SBC stays in Standby (no V2, no CAN of the SBC until the application starts).
  • The updater is unchanged; it still refuses an SBC without development mode. The assumption of use AoU-34 in the safety manual states what the board has to meet.

docs.title: neXtBSW safety anomaly register and document register
docs.text:
Title Safety anomaly register and document register Issue 1, 2026-09-28 Author (written on the maintainer's behalf — author side) Approver the safety manager; pending — decision item Status draft for acceptance Change history section 10

Working state: dev at aaa22c86 (after v0.2.0) Readers: the safety manager (decides the closure and acceptance of anomalies, safety plan section 2), the maintainer who keeps the register current at every merge, the contributors whose tasks close anomalies, and later a confirmation reviewer or integrator who wants to see which findings exist and how each was closed. Language: English, like the rest of doc/.

What this document is. Two registers the gap analysis iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) found missing (section 6 no. 24; rows 2-03 and 8-24) and the safety plan safety-plan.md plans as activities P2-03 (management of safety anomalies, 2-5.4.3) and P8-07 (documentation management, 8-10):

  1. the safety anomaly register (sections 2–4): every finding that the safety analyses, reviews and work products of neXtBSW have raised, in one table, with owner, status, the task that closed it, the closure rationale, the evidence and who checked the closure; open anomalies that no task carries are escalated to the safety manager;
  2. the document register (section 6): per safety document the title, author, approver, issue, status and where its change history is kept (8-10.4.5), until a follow-up task carries these elements as document fields.

The consistency test test/test_anomaly_register.py extracts every finding from the finding tables of the safety documents and fails when one is not registered, and it checks each row against the task list.

Licence rule. The standard is cited by part and clause only (for example "2-5.4.3" = ISO 26262-2:2018, clause 5.4.3). No text, table or figure of the standard is reproduced; requirements are restated in our own words.

What it is not. Not the task list (stays the place where work is planned; the register points to it), not the decision log (questions to the safety manager stay there), and not a confirmation review: the column "Reviewer" records a verification by the maintainer or an acceptance by the safety manager, both author side (safety plan section 2). The independent confirmation of closures is part of a separate task.

docs.title: 0. Result in one page

every accepted row names the safety manager's decision Where the documents lag behind 11 places where a safety document still describes a finding as open or unowned although a later task changed it (section 5); none of them is corrected here — the owners are named Documents 34 safety documents: 7 draft, 0 in review, 26 accepted, 1 generated — with author, approver, issue, status and change history each (section 6); released by the safety manager on 2026-09-30: concept, fmea, hsi-s32k1xx, static-analysis, tool-classification, and the safety manual in its review; on 2026-10-02 the 15 documents of the review set (anomaly register, architecture safety analysis, CM plan, coexistence, configuration range, DFA, hardware mechanisms, gap analysis, partner and degraded, SSR, safety case, safety plan, security interplay, SW architecture, unit design); the safety plan issue 2 (corrections after the confirmation review CR-01-1) was checked in the re-check of CM-01 by the safety manager on 2026-10-02 (D-01, without independence) and released; concept issue 3 and its catalogue (goals, assumptions, mechanisms issue 3; SSR with INS-SSR-02) were released in the re-check of CM-07 by the safety manager on 2026-10-04 (D-01, without independence); the verification plan issue 2 (re-check of CM-04) and fmea.md and the architecture safety analysis issue 2 (re-check of CM-02) were released by the safety manager on 2026-10-04 (D-01, without independence); the safety case issue 2 (corrections after the confirmation review CR-05-1) was released in the re-check of CM-05 by the safety manager on 2026-10-04 (D-01, without independence; its increment row of Release R1 is filled at the tag and checked in CM-06); the safety plan issue 3 (2026-10-08, the deviation D-22 for release R1 restated) was released in the delta re-check of CM-01 by the safety manager on 2026-10-08 (D-01, without independence) Formal elements in the documents themselves not added here (paths of parallel tasks); the register is the interim carrier move them into the documents (section 7) Verification mock/host: doc/safety/test/test_anomaly_register.py (completeness against 14 source documents, owners and closers against, reviewer rules, document register against the tree, counts of this section, licence rule, counter-checks with broken copies). No code changed, no hardware

docs.title: 1.1 What counts as a safety anomaly
docs.text:
2-5.4.3 asks that anomalies found during the safety lifecycle are communicated, analysed and either resolved or closed with a rationale that someone has reviewed, and that an anomaly that is not closed is brought to the person responsible for functional safety. neXtBSW has no issue tracker for this; its findings live in the finding tables of the safety documents and in the tasks of the task list. The register takes as a safety anomaly every row of these tables:

Document Rows Kind concept.md F1 … F16 (section 9.1), G1 … G6 (section 9.5) findings in the code; missing base-software mechanisms fmea.md F9 … F14 (section 6, the same findings as concept F9 … F14, registered once), N1 … N7 (section 9) findings of the failure analysis; open points iso26262-gap.md SG1 … SG7 (section 7) findings outside the safety documents tool-classification.md TF1 … TF9 (section 9.1) findings on tools and generated code static-analysis.md BEF-001 … BEF-004 (section 4) defects found by static analysis ssr.sdoc R1 … R7 (review section, INS-SSR-01) findings of the SSR inspection (doc/requirements/safety/ssr.sdoc, was doc/safety/requirements.yaml until a follow-up task step 3) rtos-comparison.md R1 … R5 (section 1.4) safety findings on the kernel hsi-s32k1xx.md H1 … H10 (section 8) configuration relied on but not re-checked dfa.md DFA-1 … DFA-6 (section 8), O1 … O6 (section 10) findings and open points of the DFA sw-architecture.md STK-1 … STK-6 (section 7.4) findings of the stack analysis cm-plan.md G1 … G8 (section 10) gaps of configuration management safety-plan.md O1 … O4 (section 9) open points of the plan safety-case.md S1 … S3, O1, O2 (section 9) proposals and open points of the case hardware-mechanisms.md 1 … 8 (section 5) open points of the hardware mechanisms dev-environment.md DE1 … DE7 (section 8) findings on the development environment component-qualification.md QA-1 (section 5.6), Q-1, Q-3, Q-5, Q-6 (section 6) anomaly of the safeMonitor report and findings of the component qualification; QA-2 … QA-4 are carried by assumptions of use of the report, Q-2/Q-4 are its planned work remark verification-plan.md VF-1 … (section 10.1) findings against the released plan (VF-1 is finding RN of the re-check of CM-04, registered in the plan because an open finding of record CR-04-1 would contradict its verdict accepted) architecture-safety-analysis.md ASA-1 … ASA-12 (section 6) findings of the safety analysis at architecture level, registered by CM-02 decision Z7; ASA-3 is the same gap as fmea.md N5 and registered once (AN-130) reviews/CR-nn-k F-01 … (section 3 of each record under doc/safety/reviews/records), classes major and minor findings of the confirmation reviews (procedure reviews/README.md section 5, step 4); remarks are not registered. First: CR-01-1 (CM-01, 2026-10-02)

A finding keeps the ID of the document that raised it; the register adds a register ID AN-nnn, which is stable (rows are appended, never renumbered or deleted).

docs.title: 1.2 What is deliberately not in the register
docs.text:
Not registered Why Where it is managed Questions to the maintainer (Q1 … of iso26262-gap.md, Q-CM, U and Q-S of rtos-comparison.md, TN1 … TN5) they ask for a decision, they do not report a defect decision log; the answer goes into the task list Board check lists (B1 …, TB1 …, K1 …) they are verification steps, not findings; a failed check becomes a finding of the mechanism fmea.md section 8, the tasks that run them Warnings of tools/trace (traceability.md, "Open trace findings") generated and re-checked in every CI run (safety-trace); each points to an open task (SSR under a separate task) tools/trace, traceability.md Proposals for new work (proposal letters of tool-classification.md section 7, N1 … N9 of safety-plan.md section 8, the task list of iso26262-gap.md section 6) planned work, not anomalies; where a proposal answers a finding, the finding is registered the task list Ordinary defects without a safety argument behind them the register is about the safety claim CHANGELOG.md

A finding table added to a safety document later (for example by an earlier change, of the same wave) is added to SOURCES of the consistency test by the maintainer at the merge; from then on its rows must be here.

docs.title: 2.1 Life cycle
docs.text:
Status Meaning Required in the row open nothing done yet owner = an open task of the task list, or a role; a row with a role only is escalated (section 4) in progress a task changed part of it, the rest has an open task as open, plus "Closed by" the tasks that did the part done review fixed and host-verified, but a board proof, the acceptance of the closing task or a follow-up edit is outstanding "Closed by" and the rationale naming what is outstanding closed fixed, with evidence, nothing outstanding for stage 1 "Closed by", evidence, reviewer other than the author; none of the closing tasks may still be open in the task list accepted deliberately not fixed, with a rationale (usually an assumption of use or a decision that stage 1 does not need it) the safety manager's decision as reviewer: only the safety manager accepts a residual (safety plan section 2)

A row never goes back to "unknown": if a closure turns out wrong, the row returns to open and the rationale says why (the history is in git).

docs.title: 2.2 Who does what
docs.text: Step Who How Raise the author of the analysis or review (contributor) a row in the finding table of the document the contributor works in, with ID, finding, why it matters and a proposed owner Register the maintainer at the merge (or the contributor, if doc/safety/anomaly-register.md is in its paths) a new AN-nnn row; the test fails until it exists Analyse and resolve the task that owns it the change, its tests and a changelog fragment that names the finding ID Close the maintainer at the merge of the closing task status, "Closed by", rationale, evidence; "Reviewer" = maintainer (merge <task>) for a closure checked by re-running the tests at the merge Accept a residual the safety manager "Reviewer" = user (<decision ID>) Escalate the maintainer a row in section 4 and a decision item; the safety manager assigns a task or decides Confirm the confirmation reviewer once named (iso-q1) not yet possible; see section 2.3

docs.title: 2.3 What "reviewer" means here
docs.text:
At ASIL B the closure of an anomaly needs a reviewed rationale, not an independent one. Two reviews are recorded:

  • maintainer (merge <task>) — the maintainer re-ran the tests and the target build of the closing task before the merge and checked that the change answers the finding. The maintainer did not write the change, so this is a review by someone other than the author; it is still the commissioning side (safety plan section 2).
  • user (<decision ID>) — the safety manager accepted the result or the residual.

Neither is a confirmation review at independence I1. When a related task names a reviewer, its protocol template gets a line per closed anomaly of the reviewed work product, and the register records the protocol ID in the reviewer column.

docs.title: 2.4 Link to the release
docs.text: A release that claims ASIL B capability (a safety release, cm-plan.md section 4.2) needs, in addition to the preconditions R1 … R6 of the safety plan: no row with status open or in progress whose source is a stage-1 mechanism without either an owner task planned for a later release or an acceptance by the safety manager. [Proposal] for the next issue of the safety plan (P2-03 objective); not binding before the safety manager accepts it.

docs.title: 3. Register
docs.text:

docs.title: 6. Document register
docs.text:
8-10.4.5 asks that every document of the safety lifecycle carries its formal elements — title, author, approver, a unique identification and version, change history and status — and that the current version can be found. The safety documents carry title, issue and a history in prose, but no author and no approver and not always a status. Until a follow-up task carries them as document fields, this table is their home. Columns:

  • Author — the task(s) whose contributor wrote the document on the maintainer's behalf (the contributor's session and branch are recorded in the task list and in the changelog entry of the task).
  • Approver — the safety manager with the decision that accepted the current issue, pending (<item>) when the acceptance waits for a decision item, — for a generated document.
  • Issue — the issue number and date of the document's own header.
  • Status — draft (written, no acceptance requested yet), in review (merged, acceptance pending), accepted (the safety manager accepted the issue named), generated (derived by a tool, approved through its sources).
  • State line — whether the header carries the line of cm-plan.md section 6 (Baseline: or Working state:).
  • Change history — where the history is kept.

docs.title: 7. How the formal elements get into the documents
docs.text:
Step Who What now this register author, approver, issue, status and change history per document, checked by the test next release (cm-plan.md G5/G6) the state line (Baseline: / Working state:) in every header with the migration to StrictDoc Step 3 document fields in the .sdoc documents; [Proposal] for a separate task: the fields AUTHOR, APPROVER (with the decision ID), ISSUE, STATUS and BASELINE on every safety document node, so the table of section 6 is generated and this register keeps only the anomalies for Markdown documents that stay Markdown the document's next task [Proposal]: the header table of this document (Title, Issue, Author, Approver, Status, Change history) followed by the state line; sw-architecture.md already uses such a table

The test accepts either form; it only requires that a row that claims a state line is right.

docs.title: 8. Maintenance
docs.text:
• At every merge of a task that raises or closes a finding, the maintainer updates the row (status, closed by, rationale, evidence, reviewer) and the counts of section 0; the test anomaly-register fails if a new finding row in a source document has no register row, or if a closing task is still open.
  • At every acceptance, the approver column of section 6 and the reviewer column of the accepted rows are updated.
  • At every release, the register is part of the baseline; a safety release additionally needs section 2.4.
  • The test proposal for tools/test/tests.yaml is in the changelog fragment of a separate task.

docs.title: neXtBSW software architectural safety analysis beyond the mechanisms
docs.text:
Title Safety analysis at architecture level Issue 2, 2026-10-04 (issue 1: 2026-09-28, written against dev at 65f3dc9; changed after it by earlier changes) Author issue 1 (issue 2) — author side Approver the safety manager: issue 1 released with the review set on 2026-10-02; the state at dev aaa22c86 reviewed in the confirmation review CM-02 (record reviews/records/CR-02-1.md (not published, available on request), the safety manager under D-01, 2026-10-04, accepted with conditions); issue 2 released on 2026-10-04 in the re-check of the findings F-01 … F-11 in CR-02-1 (steps 6 and 7 at dev efc474ea: all closed, verdict accepted, CM-02 closed; D-01, without independence) Status issue 2 accepted (released 2026-10-04 in the re-check of CM-02, record CR-02-1); update: section 11 at the NvM core (finding RN, fmea.md N7) Change history section 12

Working state: dev at 898dbcd1 (after v0.2.0) Readers: the architect and safety owner, the maintainer, the contributors of the freedom from interference follow-ups (requirements) and safety manual (StrictDoc migration). Language: English, like the rest of doc/.

What this document is. The gap analysis iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) section 6 no. 16 asks for a safety analysis at the software architectural level that does not stop at the safety mechanisms: the failure modes of the RTE, the ECU state management, the CAN stack, the NvM and the bootloader and their effect on the software safety requirements (SSR, ssr.sdoc) — part 6, clause 7.4.10 and its informative annex on the analysis of the architecture — and, as measure M5 of the gap analysis, a deductive complement: one fault tree each for the assumed safety goals ASG-01, ASG-02 and ASG-06 that ends in mechanisms and shows the single points. fmea.md analyses the mechanisms themselves (how well SM-xx detects its fault); this document analyses the parts the mechanisms are supposed to protect, and asks for each of their failures: does a requirement break, which mechanism notices, and what is left.

Licence rules followed here. ISO 26262 is not in the repository. Issue 1 was written in a contributor session without it; since 2026-09-22 the standard is licensed to the maintainer and compared in iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) (issue 2 corrects the issue-1 statement "not available"). The standard is cited by part and clause only, as the gap analysis does. The guide words of section 1.2 are this project's own wording; whether they match the annex of part 6 completely is open point O1 (section 9), which needs a reader of the licensed standard. No other standard is quoted.

What it is not. Not a quantitative analysis (no failure rates, no probabilities — AoU-09), not the analysis of the application components (the integrator's, AoU-17/AoU-18), not the device packages, not the dependent failure analysis (dfa.md, which this document uses and does not repeat).

docs.title: 0. Result in one page
docs.text: Question Answer Parts analysed RTE (generated by tools/rtegen, run by RteSystem), ECU state management (libs/bsw/ecuState), CAN stack (libs/bsw/canSystem, family CanSystem, the COM part of the RTE, application UDS and XCP), NvM (core libs/bsw/nvm since earlier changes, integration in ecu/application/src/systems/nvm) with the calibration segment and the data flash, bootloader (bootloader/, image check and hand-over) — section 2 Failure modes 43 (RTE 11, ecuState 7, CAN 10, NvM and calibration 8, bootloader 7), each with local effect, effect on the SSR and the assumed goals, the measure that exists today and a verdict — section 3. Issue 2 added FM-NVM-08 (data-flash read during a flash command) Verdicts 21 covered by an existing mechanism or build check, 8 covered with the application (AoU-04/AoU-11/AoU-18, the block quality of the NvM or the receiver carry the other half), 14 open: they break an SSR or are outside every SSR today. The open ones lead to the new findings ASA-1 … ASA-8 or to known ones (F10, N4, the application's own part under AoU-23); ASA-10 and ASA-11 limit two covered rows; ASA-9 is closed by earlier changes and ASA-12 by an earlier change (issue 2: FM-NVM-02 from open to covered with the application) Register and tasks (issue 2) every ASA finding is in the anomaly register (CM-02 decision Z7): ASA-3 is AN-130 (accepted with fmea N5), ASA-9 and ASA-12 closed, ASA-2, ASA-8 and ASA-10 accepted with AoU-ASA-d, AoU-ASA-b and AoU-ASA-a; ASA-1 (a), ASA-4, ASA-5, ASA-6, ASA-7, ASA-11 and the proposals P-SSR-1 … P-SSR-7 are task after Release R1; AoU-ASA-a … d (safety manual 7.4) cover the meantime — section 6 Effect on the SSR section 4: which failure modes can make each SSR's claim fail. Eight failure modes break no existing SSR because none speaks about them — they need new requirements (proposed in section 7.2) Fault trees ASG-01, ASG-02, ASG-06 as text trees with OR/AND gates down to mechanisms, failure modes and assumptions — section 5. Single points at stage 1 (one basic event reaches the top event without any detection in the base software): ASG-01 5, ASG-02 3, ASG-06 4; each is named with the task or assumption that owns it (issue 1: ASG-01 6 - the NvM default is reported since an earlier change) Most important new findings ASA-1 a UDS request to the programming session resets the ECU without S1, without run-down and without a precondition; ASA-2 the RTE's run-down leaves every output at its last value until the lifecycle reaches level 0; ASA-3 the safety part shuts down (watchdog off) while components below it still run down; ASA-4 a received message can be configured without a reception time-out even if it carries an E2E profile — section 6 Changes to existing documents none in issue 1. Proposals for fmea.md, iso26262-gap.md, ssr.sdoc (issue 1: requirements.yaml, moved to StrictDoc by an earlier change), concept.md and doc/architecture/signal-qualifier.md are in section 8 Verification mock/analysis only: issue 1 by code review at 65f3dc9, the host tests named as evidence, and the consistency test doc/safety/test/test_architecture_safety_analysis.py (section 9). Issue 2 brings the NvM, bootloader, run-down and read-back rows to the working state from the code and the records of the tasks named. No board run for this document. external/openbsw was not available in the analysis checkout of issue 1; statements that depend on OpenBSW behaviour are marked (OpenBSW, not checked)

docs.title: 1.1 Steps
docs.text:
1. Parts and their contribution. For every part: where it runs (task, priority, interrupt), which data and control it hands to the safety part or to the application, and which SSR mention it (section 2).
  2. Failure modes per part (inductive). Every interface and every internal function of the part is walked with the guide words of section 1.2. A failure mode is recorded when it is possible in this code — not every combination of guide word and function; combinations that cannot happen are listed once at the end of each part.
  3. Effect. For each failure mode: local effect (inside the part), effect on the SSR (which requirement no longer holds, or "no SSR speaks about it"), effect on the assumed goals (ASG).
  4. Measure and verdict. The mechanism (SM-xx), requirement or assumption that detects or prevents it, with the test that shows it. Verdict words:
  5. covered — a base-software mechanism or a build check detects or prevents it, with evidence;
  6. covered with application — the base software provides the means (qualifier, E2E, mode), the application must use it; the assumption that carries this is named;
  7. open — nothing detects it, or the mechanism that should is itself missing; a finding is named.
  8. Deductive complement. Fault trees for ASG-01, ASG-02 and ASG-06 (section 5), built top-down from the goal, with the failure modes of section 3 and the mechanisms of fmea.md as the lower levels. A basic event that reaches the top through OR gates only, with no mechanism at any level, is a single point at stage 1.
  9. Findings. Every open verdict that is not already a known finding gets an ASA-n (section 6) with a proposed measure and task.

docs.title: 1.2 Guide words (project wording)
docs.text: Guide word Meaning for a software part omission a function is not executed, a value not written, a message not sent or not received commission a function is executed although it should not be, a value written that should not be late / early executed outside its time window (includes "never" as the limit of "late") wrong value a value is produced with the wrong content — calculation, wrong source, wrong configuration stale an old value is presented as current corrupted a stored or transferred value is changed between writer and reader wrong sequence steps are executed in the wrong order, or an operation is interrupted between steps interference the part changes data or timing that belongs to another part (the three kinds of the freedom-from-interference annex of part 6: memory, timing, exchange of information)

docs.title: 1.3 Evidence notation
docs.text: As in fmea.md section 1.4: a test id in backticks names an entry of tools/test/tests.yaml; "review" means code reading at 65f3dc9; "board" names a record in CHANGELOG.md. The consistency test checks that every test id cited in an "Evidence" cell exists.

issue 1: NvmManager.h in the application, removed), integration ecu/application/src/systems/nvm/{NvmRteBlocks.h,NvmEvents.h,FlashWriteBracket.h}, wiring in RteSystem.cpp; blocks defined in project.yaml with type, length and integrity; Two facts shape the whole analysis and are stated once here:

  • None of the five parts raises a safety event except the RTE (RTE_TIMING_VIOLATION, S3) and, through the ROM check, the calibration re-check (ROM_CHECK_FAILURE). Everything else they do wrong is either caught by a mechanism that watches the consequence (watchdog, sequence monitor, E2E) or not caught at all.
  • Every part except the bootloader shares one address space and one set of priorities with the safety part (AoU-17; dfa.md DF-41 … DF-43). A wild write from any of them into the safety data is SM-10's (covered); into another part's data it is not detected (DF-42). This is not repeated per failure mode.

docs.text: Column "SSR / ASG" names the requirement whose claim the failure mode breaks, or "— (none)" when no SSR speaks about it. Column "Measure today" names what detects or prevents it.

outputs stay in the reset state of their pins — ; AoU-04, AoU-07 the bootloader configures only the CAN (and, with SBC, SPI) pins and starts no power output; S3 server time-out 5000 ms returns to the default session bl-s3-host, bl-platform-host covered with application (a silent ECU must be tolerable, AoU-04; the pin rule is not checked by a test → proposed AoU-ASA-c) FM-BL-05 wrong sequence — a flash update is interrupted no valid record → the bootloader stays (FM-BL-04) SSR-051 record sector erased first, written last bootloader-host, bl-update-host covered FM-BL-06 interference — the hand-over leaves hardware in a state the application does not expect (interrupts, SysTick, FlexCAN, clocks, watchdog) the application's start-up runs on a changed peripheral SSR-010(a) (the watchdog must be enabled with the project time-out) hal_jump_to_app disables interrupts, stops SysTick, freezes and gates FlexCAN, clears the NVIC; SOSC and pin mux are left as they are; the application's main() re-configures the watchdog and runs the self-test SM-07 before anything else safe-watchdog, bl-platform-host covered (the watchdog self-test proves the configuration the application sets, not the one it inherits) FM-BL-07 commission — the bootloader updater replaces the bootloader and is interrupted chip without a working bootloader ASG-07 power-loss windows are documented; bl-update-host injects a power loss at every flash operation; the update is only allowed with the maintainer present bl-update-host, bl-update-mutations covered (procedural for the rest)

docs.title: 4. Effect on the software safety requirements
docs.text:
Which failure modes of section 3 make the claim of an SSR fail when they occur, and whether a mechanism catches them. SSR that no failure mode of the five parts touches are left out (they concern the safety part itself and are analysed in fmea.md).

SSR Failure modes that break its claim Caught? SSR-002 de-energise before every safety reset none — but the claim is limited to safety resets; the resets of FM-CAN-06, FM-CAN-07, FM-ECU-03 are not safety resets and do no S1 walk the requirement holds; the gap is outside it → ASA-1, ASA-2, P-SSR-1 SSR-010 MCU watchdog serviced by the safety task FM-ECU-04 (watchdog disabled during the run-down), FM-BL-04 (bootloader runs with the watchdog disabled) no → ASA-3; bootloader: by design (AoU-ASA-c) SSR-015 RTE deadlines reported FM-RTE-01 (a task that is never activated reports nothing), FM-CAN-10 no → F10 SSR-024 / SSR-067 ROM check FM-NVM-04 (prevented), FM-NVM-06 (detected), FM-BL-03 (outside its range) yes, except the bootloader area (N4) SSR-040 qualifier for every analogue value FM-RTE-05 for adc.mv/adc.raw ports without sensor definition: a failed conversion holds the value without a qualifier no → ASA-6 SSR-041 E2E of configured signals FM-CAN-01 (caught), FM-CAN-02 (a time-out switched off is not an E2E fault but empties "stale"), FM-CAN-03 (fail-safe) partly → ASA-4 SSR-042 no transmission into an unhealthy bus FM-CAN-04 on a board whose phy reports no status yes for bus-off; the phy half relies on a provider → ASA-10 (documentation) SSR-050 start reason from two sources FM-ECU-01 yes SSR-051 bootloader starts only a valid, compatible image FM-BL-01 (caught; since an earlier change one CRC per start, the window to the jump is AoU-CFG-7), FM-BL-02 (caught since an earlier change, was ASA-12), FM-BL-03 partly → N4 SSR-052 defined run-down FM-ECU-02, FM-NVM-07 (time caught), FM-RTE-11 and FM-ECU-04 (the run-down is defined in time but not in its effect on outputs and supervision) partly → ASA-2, ASA-3 SSR-065 reset-loop limit FM-ECU-01; the resets of FM-CAN-06/07 are not safety resets and correctly do not count yes SSR-081 / SSR-084 generated files and CAN layout FM-RTE-04 yes (for the generator; the integrator's choice is AoU-10) — (no SSR) FM-RTE-03, FM-RTE-06, FM-RTE-09 (plausibility), FM-CAN-06, FM-CAN-07, FM-CAN-08, FM-CAN-09, FM-NVM-02 these eight need a requirement before a test can show anything → section 7.2

docs.title: 5. Fault trees (deductive complement, measure M5)
docs.text: Notation: [OR] / [AND] gates; a leaf names a failure mode (FM-…), a mechanism (SM-…), an assumption (AoU-…) or a finding. Detection in brackets: ⟨SM-xx⟩ names the base-software mechanism that interrupts the path; ⟨none⟩ marks a path without one. A leaf reached from the top through OR gates only and marked ⟨none⟩ is a single point at stage 1 (bold, listed under each tree). The trees are qualitative; they show the structure, not probabilities (AoU-09).

docs.title: 5.1 FT-ASG-01 — unintended torque not prevented or not terminated within the fault tolerance time
docs.text:
TOP ASG-01  unintended torque of the electric drive, not terminated in time
[OR]
├── G1.1  wrong actuation commanded by the software path            [AND]
│   ├── G1.1a  wrong command reaches the power stage                [OR]
│   │   ├── FM-RTE-03  application computes a wrong output          ⟨none⟩  ** single point (G1/G2, AoU-23) **
│   │   ├── G1.1b  application acts on a wrong input                [OR]
│   │   │   ├── FM-CAN-01  corrupted/repeated frame                 ⟨SM-31⟩ + AoU-11
│   │   │   ├── FM-CAN-02  message stops, time-out switched off      ⟨none⟩  ** single point (ASA-4) **
│   │   │   ├── FM-RTE-05  input read fails, old value held          ⟨none⟩  ** single point (ASA-6) **
│   │   │   ├── FM-RTE-01/08  producer task stops                     ⟨age.qlf if configured⟩ (ASA-5)
│   │   │   ├── FM-NVM-02  block default used                         ⟨nvm.qlf + DEM event⟩ + AoU-12 (ASA-9 closed, NVM-18/NVM-30)
│   │   │   ├── FM-NVM-06  calibration segment corrupted              ⟨SM-14 CALV re-check⟩
│   │   │   └── FM-RTE-04  generator connects the wrong source        ⟨SSR-081/SSR-084 build checks⟩
│   │   ├── G1.1c  a tester writes the command path                 [OR]
│   │   │   ├── FM-CAN-08  UDS 2E/31 on a safety-related port         ⟨session/security only⟩ (ASA-7)
│   │   │   └── FM-CAN-09  XCP parameter write                         ⟨plausibility only⟩ (ASA-8)
│   │   └── FM-RTE-11 / FM-ECU-03  outputs frozen at the last command during run-down  ⟨none⟩  ** single point (ASA-2) **
│   └── G1.1d  the item's own supervision does not stop it           → outside the element (AoU-01, AoU-09)
├── G1.2  a fault the MCU detects, but S1 does not take effect       → transfer to FT-ASG-02
├── G1.3  a control-software failure without a safe state            → transfer to FT-ASG-06
└── G1.4  wrong PWM/pin configuration outside the checked registers  ⟨SM-21/SM-22 generated lists (SYS-24, SYS-153); `SYSTEM_CLOCK` missing⟩ (F4 until SYS-55)
    └── a bridge that keeps conducting, an enable that does not reach the part  ⟨none⟩  ** single point (G1, stage 2 SM-40) **

Single points at stage 1 (5): FM-RTE-03 (application, AoU-23), FM-CAN-02 with timeout_ms: 0 (ASA-4), FM-RTE-05 for DIO inputs (ASA-6), FM-RTE-11 (ASA-2; since an earlier change the table is walked as the last run-down step, AoU-ASA-d for the time before it), and the power-stage path after the pin (G1, stage 2). Issue 1 counted FM-NVM-02 (ASA-9) as a sixth; since earlier changes the block's quality and a DEM event report the default. G1.1d is written as an AND partner on purpose: the item may have a torque plausibility of its own; the element does not rely on it and does not claim it.

docs.title: 5.2 FT-ASG-02 — the switch-off path is not available when it is needed
docs.text:
TOP ASG-02  S1 requested (or needed) but the power stage stays energised
[OR]
├── G2.1  S1 is not requested although a fault is present            [OR]
│   ├── safety task stopped                                           ⟨SM-01 → reset; pins to reset state, AoU-07⟩
│   ├── safety part shut down during run-down (FM-ECU-04)             ⟨none⟩  ** single point (ASA-3) **
│   └── the fault is one no mechanism detects                          → FT-ASG-01 G1.1, FT-ASG-06
├── G2.2  S1 is executed but does not reach an output                [OR]
│   ├── output not declared (no PWM group, no safe_off)                ⟨SM-24 counts adapters; AoU-06⟩
│   ├── wrong inactive level                                           ⟨SSR-080 image check; AoU-07⟩
│   ├── peripheral clock gated, walk skips it                           ⟨SM-22 CLOCK_GATE; DFA-4⟩
│   └── register changed after start (pin mux, direction)               ⟨SM-21/SM-22 generated lists; F4 rest SYS-55⟩
├── G2.3  S1 is left again                                           [OR]
│   ├── leaveSafeState re-energises                                      ⟨SSR-004: indicator only⟩
│   ├── restart after S1 + S2 re-runs the application into the fault     ⟨SM-50 reset-loop limit, SSR-065⟩
│   └── a driver enables its output again                                ⟨SSR-004(b): explicit enable only⟩
├── G2.4  the ECU is reset without S1 (not a safety reset)            [OR]
│   ├── UDS 10 02 → enterBootloader (FM-CAN-06)                          ⟨none before the reset⟩  ** single point (ASA-1) **
│   ├── UDS 11 01/03, ecuState restart (FM-CAN-07, FM-ECU-03)             ⟨none before level 0⟩ (ASA-1, ASA-2)
│   └── in both: after the reset the pins are in their reset state        ⟨AoU-07 external pull⟩
└── G2.5  nothing verifies that S1 took effect                        [OR]
    ├── S1 latched, S1 held, SD, the S1 + S2 sequence                     ⟨SM-23 read-back, SYS-30/SYS-138, host⟩
    └── the fault handlers' and the halt deadman's walk                    ⟨none⟩  ** single point (G1 rest, SSR-060 partial) **

Single points at stage 1 (3): FM-ECU-04 (ASA-3, accepted as fmea.md N5), FM-CAN-06 (ASA-1) and the missing read-back of S1 in the fault handlers' and the halt deadman's path (G1 rest, SSR-060 partial; issue 1: the read-back of S1 as a whole, before later changes; both paths end in or allow a reset into the pin reset state, AoU-07). The frozen outputs of an ordinary run-down (ASA-2) are counted in FT-ASG-01, where they cause the torque. The first two have in common that the power stage is de-energised eventually — by the reset default of the pins under AoU-07 — but not by the element within a bounded time.

docs.title: 5.3 FT-ASG-06 — a control-software failure does not lead to a defined safe state
docs.text:
TOP ASG-06  control-software failure, output behaviour not defined
[OR]
├── G6.1  program flow / timing of the safety part                   ⟨SM-01 … SM-07⟩ (fmea.md 3.1)
├── G6.2  program flow / timing of the application                  [OR]
│   ├── task overruns (FM-RTE-02)                                     ⟨SM-05, S3 only⟩ (AoU-18)
│   ├── task starved / not activated (FM-RTE-01, FM-CAN-10)           ⟨none⟩  ** single point (F10, SYS-21) **
│   └── control flow inside a runnable wrong                           ⟨none⟩  ** single point (AoU-17/18, application) **
├── G6.3  memory                                                    [OR]
│   ├── safety data written                                            ⟨SM-10 … SM-13⟩
│   ├── RTE/application data written by another task (DF-42)           ⟨none⟩  ** single point (SYS-21, AoU-17) **
│   ├── ROM / flash                                                     ⟨SM-14, SM-16⟩
│   └── RAM bit error                                                   ⟨SM-15⟩
├── G6.4  register configuration                                     ⟨SM-21/SM-22 generated lists (SYS-24, SYS-153); F4 rest SYS-55⟩
├── G6.5  BSW service delivers wrong data silently                  [OR]
│   ├── NvM default (FM-NVM-02)                                         ⟨nvm.qlf, DEM event⟩ (ASA-9 closed by NVM-18/NVM-30)
│   ├── DIO/ADC read failure held (FM-RTE-05)                           ⟨none⟩ (ASA-6; counted in FT-ASG-01)
│   ├── calibration invalid                                             ⟨start-up plausibility, SM-14 CALV⟩
│   └── torn shared value (FM-RTE-07)                                   ⟨RTE lock⟩
├── G6.6  start / stop                                              [OR]
│   ├── wrong image (FM-BL-01/02)                                       ⟨SM-51⟩ (absent block: ASA-12, closed by BL-36)
│   ├── bootloader corrupted (FM-BL-03)                                 ⟨none⟩  ** single point (N4) **
│   ├── run-down step hangs (FM-ECU-02)                                 ⟨SM-53 time-outs⟩
│   └── supervision off during run-down (FM-ECU-04)                     ⟨none⟩ (ASA-3; counted in FT-ASG-02)
└── G6.7  the reaction itself fails                                  → FT-ASG-02

Single points at stage 1 (4): application task activation (F10), control flow inside a runnable (application), cross-task memory interference (DF-42) and the bootloader's own integrity (N4). The silent defaults of G6.5 and the supervision gap of G6.6 are counted once, in FT-ASG-01 and FT-ASG-02. G6.2's second and G6.3's second leaf are the known limits of AoU-17 and AoU-18; they stay single points until a follow-up task delivers partitioning.

docs.title: 5.4 What the trees add to fmea.md
docs.text:
fmea.md section 4 confirms the verdicts "partial" (ASG-01), "covered with limits" (ASG-02, ASG-06). The trees keep those verdicts and make two things visible that the per-mechanism view cannot show:

  1. The ordinary stop paths are not safety paths. Diagnostic resets, the ECU state machine's restarts and the lifecycle run-down all end in a reset that de-energises through the pin reset state, not through S1, and the safety part is shut down before that end (G2.4, FM-ECU-04). For ASG-02 this is the largest structural gap outside the mechanisms: ASA-1, ASA-2, ASA-3.
  2. Silent defaults feed the command path. Three services substitute a value without saying so — the NvM default, the held DIO/ADC value and a disabled reception time-out (ASA-4, ASA-6, ASA-9). The qualifier concept exists (SM-30); these three simply do not use it. Issue 2: the NvM uses it since an earlier change (nvm.qlf.<Block>, ASA-9 closed); the other two remain (ASA-4, ASA-6).

docs.text:

docs.title: 7.1 Assumptions of use (numbers to be assigned by the maintainer)
docs.text:
Issue 2: the four are rows of the safety manual section 7.4 since CM-10 (AoU-ASA-b with security access and a precondition for the ECU reset, UDS 11, finding F-03 of CR-10-1); they keep their names there and are not nodes of assumptions.sdoc. The text below is that of issue 1.

ID Assumption AoU-ASA-a On a board whose CAN transceiver reports no status (passive transceiver, canPhyPassive), the transmit gate follows the bus-off state only. The integrator confirms that a transceiver fault that does not lead to bus-off is acceptable for his item or adds his own supervision (ASA-10). AoU-ASA-b In the product, XCP is either not built in or protected by the integrator; UDS services that write component ports or reset the ECU are protected by security access and by a precondition the integrator defines (until ASA-1/ASA-8 provide one). AoU-ASA-c The pins of every power output reach a de-energised level while the MCU is in reset and while the bootloader runs (the bootloader configures only the communication pins and runs with the MCU watchdog disabled). This extends AoU-07 from "reset" to "reset and bootloader" (FM-BL-04, G2.4). AoU-ASA-d Until ASA-2 exists, the application switches its actuators off when the ECU mode view reports RUNDOWN, because the RTE does not drive the outputs to their init value at run-down.

docs.title: 7.2 Software safety requirements (proposed, for ssr.sdoc - issue 1 said requirements.yaml; IDs to be assigned there; carried by an earlier change after Release R1, CM-02 Z7)
docs.text: Proposal Text (in the style of a separate task: element and behaviour, no implementation detail) Derived from Finding P-SSR-1 Every reset that the base software requests for a reason other than a safety event (diagnostic reset, programming request, restart of the ECU state management) shall be preceded by S1. ASG-02 ASA-1 P-SSR-2 At the start of the run-down, before any other run-down step, the RTE shall drive every output port to its configured initial value. ASG-01, ASG-02 ASA-2 P-SSR-3 The build shall refuse a received message that carries an E2E profile or a safety-related signal without a reception time-out. ASG-05 ASA-4 P-SSR-4 (a) Every input port whose value comes from a driver read shall carry a qualifier that becomes "error" when the read fails. (b) A refused output write shall be counted and made visible. ASG-05, ASG-06 ASA-6 P-SSR-5 The NvM shall report per block whether its value was restored or replaced by the default, as a qualifier readable by the application. ASG-06 ASA-9 P-SSR-6 The RTE shall refuse to start the application when a safety-related parameter is implausible, and shall refuse a run-time write of an implausible value. (Describes what exists, so that it becomes traceable.) ASG-06 FM-RTE-09 P-SSR-7 The MCU watchdog shall stay armed until the reset or power-down that ends a run-down. ASG-06 ASA-3

docs.title: 8. Proposals for existing documents (not changed by this task)
docs.text:
To keep the parallel merges of the work step free of conflicts, no existing document was edited. For the maintainer (issue 2: fmea.md section 4 points to the fault trees since its issue 2; the AoU are in the safety manual 7.4; requirements.yaml is ssr.sdoc since an earlier change and the proposals of 7.2 are a separate task; the others stand):

docs.title: 9.2 Consistency test
docs.text:
doc/safety/test/test_architecture_safety_analysis.py checks this document against the concept, the requirements and the test list: every failure-mode id is unique and belongs to one of the five parts, every part has failure modes, every SSR cited exists in ssr.sdoc, every SM cited exists in the catalogue (mechanisms.sdoc), every test id in an "Evidence" cell exists in tools/test/tests.yaml, every open verdict names a finding, every ASA finding of a verdict is defined in section 6 and every defined one is used, the three fault trees exist and list their single points, and no percentage is stated. Counter-checks with a broken copy of the document show that each parser sees the breakage.

The test runs as the entry safety-architecture-analysis of tools/test/tests.yaml (issue 1 proposed it; it exists). It does not check the status line or whether a code path named here still exists (CM-02 G-11, remark).

docs.title: 9.3 Open points
docs.text: ID Point O1 Whether the guide words of section 1.2 cover the informative annex of part 6 on the analysis of the architecture completely needs a reader of the licensed standard O2 OpenBSW behaviour not checked (submodule not available in the analysis checkout): the order of components inside one lifecycle level (ASA-3), what transitionToLevel(0) does before the reset (FM-ECU-03), the lock type of the RTE (FM-RTE-07), the catch-up behaviour of scheduleAtFixedRate (FM-RTE-02), the session transition rules of the diagnostic stack (FM-CAN-06) O3 Whether softwareSystemReset() itself walks the safe-outputs table (implemented in the OpenBSW part of the family, not checked); if it does, ASA-1(a) is already fulfilled and only the precondition remains O4 No board run: the behaviour of the outputs during a run-down (ASA-2) and after 10 02 (ASA-1) can be shown on the eval board with LED1/MOT1 PWM on the oscilloscope — board check for the maintainer, no power stage needed O5 The application part of every tree (FM-RTE-03, control flow inside a runnable) is the integrator's must say that the trees end there

docs.title: 10. Review questions of the architecture (section 11)
docs.text:
This task changed no reusable code, no generator and no bootloader; it added this document and a consistency test under doc/safety/test/. The questions are answered for the analysis and for the measures it proposes.

  1. Board without an SBC? Yes. No failure mode is credited to the SBC; ASA-10 and AoU-ASA-a are exactly about the board with a passive transceiver.
  2. Different crystal and system clock? Yes. No time in this document depends on a clock; the time-outs named are configuration values.
  3. Different derivative, S32K3 / STM32 / Cortex-R? Yes. The parts analysed are family-neutral (RTE, ecuState, CAN core, NvM, bootloader core); the family-specific statements (bootloader hal_init disables the WDOG, FlexNVM READY) are marked as S32K1 and would get their own row per family.
  4. Two or more CAN buses? Yes. The RTE is bound to one bus today (can.bus); the failure modes are per message and per bus, and ASA-4/ASA-7 are rules per message and per port, not per bus.
  5. Several tasks and free priorities? Yes. FM-RTE-01, FM-RTE-07, FM-CAN-10 and ASA-5 are about several tasks.
  6. Every new value in exactly one configuration level? The only new value proposed is bootloader.accept_legacy_image (ASA-12), a project value; ASA-7's confirmation key belongs to rte.yaml at the port, like a separate task's key at its pin. Everything else is derived by the generator.
  7. Host test with its own test profile? The consistency test needs no board profile. The proposed code measures each name a host test (section 6).
  8. Tool core free of Qt, messages with a YAML path? The proposed rtegen/nxconfig checks (ASA-4, ASA-5, ASA-7) are to report with the YAML path of the message or port.
  9. Device driver granularity? Not applicable — no driver analysed.
  10. Placement under platforms/? Not applicable — no new file there.

docs.title: neXtBSW board test specification per SSR with operational use cases
docs.text:
Status: 2026-10-02, issue 1, written against an integration branch at 92edce0b, draft for acceptance by the safety manager. No case of this issue was run at the board; every procedure was run on the host against recorded board captures and against a simulated board (section 6). Working state: dev at 92edce0b (after v0.1.0) Readers: the safety manager, who runs the cases at the board and accepts the specification as safety manager; the maintainer, who keeps the suite current with the firmware and links the records into the verification report of a baseline; the reviewer of confirmation measure CM-04 (integration and test strategy). Language: English, like the rest of doc/.

What this document is. The target test specification that iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) section 6 no. 20 asks for and that the safety plan names as part of P6-20 (testing of the embedded software): for every software safety requirement of ssr.sdoc whose verification includes the board, the board test cases that verify it, ordered by operational use case - start-up, S1, S1 held, S2, sleep and wake-up, flashing, diagnostic session and normal operation - with what each case needs at the bench (oscilloscope, 24 V, a motor, the debugger, a person at the board). The cases are repeatable: each one is a procedure of tools/boardtest that drives the console and the CAN adapter, asks the person at the board for what only a person can do or read, records a transcript and evaluates it with fixed checks; the results of a run are archived as a record next to the board captures (section 7).

What it is not. Not the verification plan: verification-plan.md owns the methods, their ratings, the environments and the regression rings; this document is the specification of the cases at its embedded-software level (its sections 2.3 and 5.2). Not the board regression list of a safety release: which cases run on the tagged image of a safety release, and how a difference analysis may let an earlier record stand (VP-6, task proposal T-VP2), is a separate task; it selects from the cases here and links their records. Not the board checklists of the analyses: fmea.md section 8 (B1 ... B16) stays the place where an analysis says what it needs measured; the cases here take those checks over where they verify an SSR and name them.

Licence rule. The standard is cited by part and clause only; nothing of its text is reproduced.

docs.title: 3. Images and equipment
docs.text:
Image Meaning dev the standard development image of the tag (test console commands safety ..., lc ... present) test the development image built with the CMake option the case names (NX_SAFETY_FAULT_INJECTION_COMMAND, NX_GD_ENABLE_COMMAND, NX_RTE_LOAD_TEST_US, a stall build) special an image or board state the case describes (a corrupted image for the ROM check) product the product image (NX_PRODUCT_BUILD); no case needs it in this issue - it removes the test commands the S1/S2 cases use Equipment Meaning console serial console of the ECU (port and baud from the project or the command line) can CAN adapter (python-can, VN1610 at the workstation); bit timing from the project jlink debugger: halt, register read and write, breakpoint (J-Link rules of the project) scope oscilloscope 24v 24 V supply of the power stage motor a motor at the power stage, at standstill or turned by hand source adjustable source on an analogue input user a person at the board: power cycle, reset button, a cable, or a command the board rules reserve to the maintainer

A case that needs a test or special image says so in the column "Image" of section 5.2 and in its build field; the runner prints both before the case starts.

docs.title: 4. How a case is written, run and evaluated
docs.text:
A case is a procedure in the suite file of the project, tools/boardtest/suites/evalboard_s32k144_demo.yaml (not published, available on request): steps that act (console command, console capture for N seconds, CAN probe, UDS request, wake frame, canflash, an instruction or a question to the person at the board) and checks on the transcript the steps leave behind. The checks are regular expressions matched in order:

  • expect must match after the previous match; its named groups become values of the run (start reason, reset-loop cause, restart gap on CAN, image CRC, ...);
  • absent must not match between the previous and the next matched expect - "no reset while S1 is held", "no event while the ROM check repeats";
  • equals / differs compare captured values (reset-loop cause 0x2 of a fault exception, 0x1 of a watchdog reset, 0x117 of an assertion, wake-up sources not reset);
  • delta compares the difference of two values with a project value (the ROM-check period against modules.safeMemory.rom_check_period_ms, the project's value or the module default) - no time is written into the tool.

A live run writes the console traffic in the capture format of tools/boardtest/captures and adds lines #> ... for the results of CAN steps, the answers of the person at the board and the output of external tools (#| ...). The same evaluator judges a live transcript and a recorded capture: replaying a capture skips only the #> checks. So every case with a reference capture is checked against what the board really printed, without a board, at every run of the host tests, and a firmware change of a console line turns the case red on the host first.

Commands (no hardware for the first four):

.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo suite list [--oc S2] [--ssr SSR-065]
.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo suite check      # against ssr.sdoc
.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo suite matrix     # tables of section 5
.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo suite replay BT-S2-04 [capture ...]
.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo --port COM17 suite run START S2 \
    --out tools/boardtest/captures/evalboard_s32k144_demo/<date>_suite-<tag> --image <app.hex> --baseline <tag> \
    --tester <name>

suite run takes case ids, operating-case codes or all (runnable cases only). A step that cannot run (adapter missing, port busy) ends its case with an error and the run goes on with the next case.

docs.title: 5.1 How to read the tables
docs.text: The first table has one row per SSR that has a board item in ssr.sdoc or a board case: the board items (clauses) of the SSR, the cases that cover them, their operating cases, and whether any of these cases needs the oscilloscope, 24 V, a motor, the debugger or a person at the board; "- (beyond the method)" marks an SSR verified by test or review whose board case adds evidence beyond its method. The second table has one row per case with its image, equipment, the reference capture its checks are tested against on the host, and the earlier board records of the same behaviour. Both tables are generated (suite matrix) and compared with this document by test_suite.py.
