docs.title: 5.4 BT-RUN-08 in detail - bus off and automatic recovery (BTS-6 b)
docs.text:
Equipment: console, CAN adapter, a person at the board (user). Image: dev.

  1. can status before the fault: CAN0 open, phy ..., tx ... (the bus is open and the ECU transmits).
  2. Hand action (operator step of the suite): short CANH and CANL of CAN0 for at least 10 s while the ECU transmits, or pull the terminating resistor and every other node so that no frame is acknowledged. A short of 3 s (2026-09-23) or a wrong bit rate (2026-10-02, com05_busoff) only reaches error passive and does not satisfy the case. Then remove the short (or restore the termination), wait 5 s, press Enter.
  3. can status after the fault must show, in one line: bus off N times (now .. ms, longest .. ms, R recoveries) with N >= 1 and R >= 1, ever bus off yes and recovery automatic. The bus state at that moment is error active (recovered) or error passive, but never stuck in bus off. A status with bus off 0 times fails.
  4. Automatic recovery without a reset or an operator command: canprobe (3 s) must see the ECU's frames on the bus again (#> canprobe: passed).

Reference capture: the existing records stay (2026-09-23_board/10_com35_can_status_after, which shows the error-passive status after the short, no bus off yet, and 2026-09-22_board/90_com26_p9_recovered, which shows bus off 9812 times ... recovery automatic of a separate task); the first run that reaches the bus off on CAN0 replaces them as the reference.

docs.title: 6. Verification of the suite itself (host)
docs.text:
tools/boardtest/test_suite.py (no board, no adapter):

Class Shows SuiteConsistencyTest the suite is consistent with ssr.sdoc (every board item covered or exempted with a reason, no unknown SSR, references and earlier records on disk, vocabulary of operating cases, images and equipment); every operating case has a runnable case; the reader of ssr.sdoc finds clauses, methods and withdrawn clauses; faults in a copy of the suite are found SpecDocumentTest the tables of section 5.2 are the generated ones; scope, 24 V and motor are marked where the cases need them EvaluatorTest order, windows of absent, optional checks, values and constraints, recorder time stamps and colour codes, delta against the project value and against the module default, with a second test profile (a project with its own ROM-check period) ReferenceReplayTest every procedure passes each board capture it names; removing the lines any expect finds turns it red; a forbidden line in any absent window turns it red; counter captures (a watchdog reset against lc assert, a held state against a restart, a software-reset start against the power-on case, ...) fail; the sleep lines are the format strings of the firmware RunnerTest complete runs against a simulated board on a virtual clock: power-on start with the documented start line (pass) and with a software-reset start (fail), safety wdg with the restart gap measured on CAN, the diagnostic session with communication control against UDS answers recorded on the board (pass, and fail when the ECU keeps sending), sleep and wake-up by a CAN frame, a download with the recorded canflash output and a segmented UDS answer; transcript, values and suite-run.json SuiteCommandLineTest suite check/list/matrix/replay, run refusing without --out and for a case of another project

docs.title: 7. Records and archive
docs.text:
A run with --out <folder> leaves, per case, the transcript <case>.console.txt and, for the whole run, suite-run.json and summary.md:

  • what ran on what: project, suite file, baseline (tag or commit given with --baseline), git describe of the repository, the image given with --image with its SHA-256, the tester, start and end time;
  • per case: result (passed, failed, error), the SSRs it covers, the values it captured (start reason, reset-loop cause, restart gap, image CRC from canflash, operator readings such as the walk time on the scope), and every failed check with its step.

The folder goes to tools/boardtest/captures/<project>/<date>_suite-<baseline>/ and is committed like every other board capture; the verification report of the baseline links it (decides which cases a safety release needs). A failed case is a finding: it goes to the anomaly register with the record as evidence, never edited away. A transcript of a passed run can become the reference of its case (references: in the suite file), so the host checks follow the firmware the board really ran.

docs.title: 8. Open points and review points
docs.text:
Open: no case of this issue ran at the board. The next session at the board runs the runnable cases on the current image of dev (order: START, RUN, DIAG, S1, S2, FLASH, SLEEP, S1H, the cases with a test or special image grouped by image), keeps the records as section 7 says and turns the first passed transcript of each case without a reference into its reference. Thirteen cases have no reference capture today (column "Reference capture" = none yet): three are for other projects; BT-START-02, BT-SLEEP-01 and BT-DIAG-01 run on the host against the simulated board (the start line from RcmResetReason.h, the sleep lines from the format strings of EcuStateSystem.cpp, the UDS answers recorded on the board), BT-RUN-03 is a tool step tested by QualifierTest; the others consist mostly of operator readings.

Review points for the safety manager:

ID Title Statement Options Recommendation BTS-1 Operator readings as evidence scope times, J-Link register values and visual checks (LED, current) enter the record as answers of the person at the board, without a file of the instrument (a) accept the answer plus the scope screenshot or CSV stored next to the record (LabControl csv_path); (b) require an automatic measurement for every reading (a) BTS-2 References from earlier firmware decided (a) on 2026-10-02: where the first suite run of 2026-10-02 (2026-10-02_suite-integ12) gives a capture of the current firmware, the case's reference is that capture and its checks accept the current form only: BT-S2-01 WATCHDOG RESET: outputs off, dump saved and cause 0x1, BT-S1-01 the event, KL30B and safe-state lines of a separate task, BT-RUN-01 the log prefix of the project name. Still older references: the leave step of BT-S1-01, the other cases of the earlier sessions; the fault handler cases keep HARD FAULT RESET (a) replace them by the transcripts of the next board run and narrow the checks to the current form; (b) keep both forms (a), decided BTS-3 Restart gap and AoU-05 BT-S2-01 records the CAN gap of a watchdog reset but does not fail on it; the value of AoU-05 (fmea 8.1 B2, 1 077 ms) is the comparison (a) report only, a larger value is a finding for AoU-05; (b) fail above the AoU-05 value (a) BTS-4 Items without a board case SSR-020(b)(c), SSR-024(b), SSR-042(b), SSR-052(c) rest on host tests and review (section 5.3) (a) accept with the reasons given; (b) ask for test builds that make them observable (a) BTS-5 Features the demo does not configure SSR-040, SSR-087, SSR-089, SSR-091, SSR-092 have specified cases that need another project (and a board with a power stage); until such a project exists their board method is not met (a) keep "board" as the method and run them with the first project that configures the feature; (b) change their method to test plus the existing fmea checks (a) BTS-6 Bus off not reached the short of CANH/CANL on 2026-09-23 reached error passive, not bus off; decided (b) on 2026-10-02: BT-RUN-08 requires the bus off (counter and recovery at least 1, ever bus off yes) after a short of at least 10 s or a missing termination, and fails a run that stays in error passive (a) record the counters only; (b) require bus off with a longer short or a missing termination (b), decided

docs.title: 9. Review questions of the architecture (section 11)
docs.text: The tool and the suite file are the only new parts. Board without an SBC, other crystal, other derivative, several CAN buses, several tasks: the tool takes the console baud rate, the CAN bus with its bit timing, the messages of the ECU, the diagnostic addresses and every project value from the project (tools/boardtest/project.py and project_value); the board-specific expectations (console lines of this firmware, signal names, the expected WDOG_CS) live only in the project's suite file, and another project writes its own. Exactly one configuration level: the suite reads project values (ROM-check period) at run time and writes none. Own test profile: the evaluator is tested with a synthetic project whose ROM-check period differs from the eval board's. Core free of Qt, messages with a path: no Qt; suite errors name the file and the YAML path (procedures.BT-X-01.steps[0]...).

docs.title: neXtBSW configuration management plan and baselines
docs.text:
Status: 2026-09-28, issue 2: the safety manager's decisions Q-CM1 … Q-CM4 are worked in, the state line of section 6 is set in every safety document and checked by test/test_cm_plan.py (gaps G5, G6). Issue 1 was written against dev at ae92e89 (after release v0.1.0), draft for acceptance by the safety manager. Update 2026-10-02 (confirmation review CR-01-1 of the safety plan, finding F-07): P9 is binding through the safety plan's precondition R6 (no longer a proposal); section 5.1 names the safety plan's R for each P (the mapping is kept in safety plan section 6 and checked by test_safety_plan.py). Update 2026-10-08: section 4.3 names the next candidate v1.0.0-rc2 and the state of its preconditions before the tag; no rule of this plan changed. Update 2026-10-08: section 4.3 states for v1.0.0-rc2 that a public development release without a safety claim is allowed under the restated deviation D-22 (safety plan issue 3, released in the delta re-check of CM-01 on 2026-10-08) and where the statement "no safety claim" stands; no rule of this plan changed. Working state: dev at c0928380 (after v1.0.0-rc1) Readers: the safety manager as configuration manager and release authority, the maintainer who merges and releases, the contributors of the safety plan, safety case, verification plan, change requests, safety manual (StrictDoc). Language: English, like the rest of doc/.

What this document is. The written configuration management plan that iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) found missing (rows 8-12, 8-13, 8-14, 2-12; section 6 task 10; finding SG7). It states which items are under configuration management, how they are identified, what a baseline is, how a release is made, and how the safety documents name the state they are about. The standard is cited by part and clause only (for example "8-7.4.3" = ISO 26262-8:2018, 7.4.3); no text of it is reproduced.

What it decides and what it only proposes. Binding is the safety manager's decision iso-q3 of 2026-09-22: a release is an annotated tag vX.Y.Z on master; before it there is a green CI run with an archived report, the safety documents refer to the tag, the qualification reports exist and the reviews are closed. Everything else here works that decision out. Issue 1 marked the points where the plan went beyond it as [Proposal] and put four of them to the decision log (section 11); the safety manager decided all four as recommended on 2026-09-28, and issue 2 marks them [Decided Q-CMn]. What is still marked [Proposal] (the release lines of 4.4, the fields of the tag message beyond the status line) was not part of those questions; P9 is binding since 2026-10-02 because it is the safety plan's precondition R6 (accepted with the safety plan).

What it is not. Not the change management process (that is plus), not the verification plan, not the documentation management rules. It names the interfaces to them.

docs.title: 0. Result in one page
docs.text: Question Answer Configuration items 13 classes, from the element's source code to the verification records (section 2); build output, doc/confidential and keys are deliberately not items, with the reason Identification every item in git is identified by the commit; the element as a whole by VERSION (SemVer with the interface meaning of 3.2, Q-CM4) and the release tag; the OpenBSW submodule by its gitlink; external tools by version plus SHA-256 (tools/ci/versions.toml) Baseline an annotated tag vX.Y.Z on master, never moved, never deleted (section 4). It fixes every item in git at once. What lies outside git (CI report, tool archives) is bound to the tag by SHA-256 Safety status of a baseline [Decided Q-CM1] each release tag states in its message whether it is a safety release (all preconditions of section 5.1 met) or a development release (reproducible, but without a safety claim). Only a safety release may be cited as evidence in a safety case Existing baselines one: v0.1.0 → ed48460 (merge commit on master, annotated, not signed, 2026-09-28). By section 5.1 it is a development release: its CI report is not archived beyond 14 days, the safety documents do not cite it, qualification reports and reviews do not exist Release procedure nine steps from the release candidate on dev to the archived report (section 5.2), with the checks that already exist in tools/ci and tools/nxconfig pin Citation rule every safety document carries one line Baseline: vX.Y.Z (or Working state: dev at <commit> (after vX.Y.Z)) in its header; commit hashes in the body are history, not the state the document claims (section 6) Loose commits issue 1 found 11 different hashes in 6 documents (section 6.3); all 10 neXtBSW commits among them are contained in v0.1.0, the eleventh is the OpenBSW submodule commit that v0.1.0 pins. Issue 2: 20 of the 21 safety documents carry the state line (all but the generated traceability.md, see 6.4); the old hashes stay as history Archiving [Decided Q-CM3] the release CI report as a GitHub release asset plus a local copy; for a safety release also the external tool archives (section 7) Signing [Decided Q-CM2] release tags are signed with the safety manager's SSH key from the first safety release on; development releases stay annotated only (4.1 rule 5, G3) Gaps found on the way the CI report does not record commit or tree hash (G1); CI artifacts are kept 14 days (G2); tags are not signed and pincheck checks no signature (G3); master carries its merge commits only, dev does not merge them back (G4, harmless, rule stated); G5 and G6 are closed by an earlier change — section 10 Verification issue 1: analysis (mock), the repository read at ae92e89, pincheck in release mode on a checkout of v0.1.0 returned ok. Issue 2: host test (mock) test/test_cm_plan.py with counter-checks on broken copies; no code changed, no hardware

docs.title: 1. Scope, roles and relation to other plans
1.1 Scope
docs.text:
The plan covers the neXtBSW development repository (private, the repository owner's GitHub account) as the development repository of the SEooC, including the work products needed to reproduce the element and its evidence (8-7.4.3). It covers the open source line (published as github.com/danielsimonreinhardt/neXtBSW, an export of this repository without history) and the licensed lines of lizenz-und-release.md (not published, available on request) only in so far as each of them is derived from one baseline of this repository (section 4.4).

A customer repository (workspace with nextbsw.yaml, customer-project.md) is the integrator's configuration management, not this plan's. The interface is one sentence: the integrator pins a release tag of this repository, and tools/ci run --workspace <dir> --release proves the pin is a clean, annotated, reachable release.

docs.title: 1.2 Roles
docs.text:
neXtBSW has one human. The roles are named so that a second person can take one of them later (iso-q1 is still open; since 2026-09-30 the safety manager reviews himself under deviation D-01, see the row "Reviewer").

Role Held by Responsibility in this plan Configuration manager, release authority the maintainer accepts this plan; approves every merge to master and every release tag; decides the safety status of a release Integrator of dev the maintainer (exactly one at a time) merges checked contributor branches to dev, keeps planning, changelog and tests.yaml, pushes dev, prepares release candidates, creates the tag after approval Contributor contributors (a task branch locally, a session branch in contributor sessions), the maintainer changes only the paths of their task; never commit to dev/master, never tag Reviewer an independent person not yet named (iso-q1); for now the safety manager himself (decision of the safety responsible 2026-09-30 on AN-093; safety plan tailoring T-11; reviews/README.md section 3.1, deviation D-01) confirmation reviews. A review by the safety manager is a confirmation without independence: it does not meet P6, so no release can be a safety release on it, and no working state or tag gets an ASIL statement until an independent person has reviewed it (section 5.1, P6)

Independence: the integrator re-runs tests and builds of every contributor branch, and the safety manager accepts; for the author of code and its tests this is not independence at I1 (gap row 8-23). This plan does not change that.

docs.title: 1.3 Interfaces to other plans
docs.text: Plan / process Task What it takes from this plan What this plan takes from it Safety plan – the release definition and its preconditions (section 5.1) the list of work products per release and who checks them Verification plan – the baseline a report belongs to; the rule that a report is archived per release (section 7) the report format, what "green" means per level Change management the task list the base configuration of a change (section 8) task IDs, safety impact per change Documentation management – the baseline line of a document header (section 6) author, approver, status fields Safety case – "evidence is cited per safety release" — Release lines – "one line = one baseline + one profile" (section 4.4) the export and its check (tools/distcheck) Customer projects – the tag rules (annotated, on master, VERSION) the pin check, which already enforces them

docs.title: 2. Configuration items
docs.text:
A configuration item (CI) is anything whose exact state is needed to rebuild the element, to re-run its verification or to understand a safety claim. The table groups them in classes; each class names how its state is identified.

Class Item Where Identified by Changed by CI-01 Source code of the element libs/, platforms/, ecu/, bootloader/, swc/ (component code), root CMakeLists.txt, CMakePresets.json, cmake/ commit contributors via task, merged by the integrator CI-02 Pre-existing software external/openbsw (submodule, never modified; Python: tools/ci/.python-version; packages: tools/ci/constraints.txt, constraints-docs.txt, tools/misra/requirements.txt version and SHA-256 of each archive, exact package pins, in the commit only by editing the pin file, then a full CI run (versions.toml header) CI-07 Tests, test data and verification settings tools/test/tests.yaml, test folders next to the code, tools/test/coverage.yaml, tools/misra/{rules,baseline,deviations,defects}.yaml, tools/ci/pipeline.toml, doc/safety/test/ commit contributors; CI report of a release (ci-result.json, summary.md, tests.json, tests.log, coverage.*, misra/) board captures: commit; CI report: SHA-256 in the tag message (section 7) captures by the integrator; the CI report is written only by tools.ci run CI-12 Release identity root file VERSION, the release tag VERSION in the commit; Not configuration items, with the reason:

Not an item Why How it is still controlled Build output (build/, %TEMP%/s32k/…, ELF/HEX/MAP) reproducible from a baseline; keeping it would create a second truth the CI report lists the artefacts with sizes; the image CRC is cited in board records doc/confidential/** (ISO 26262, NDA data sheets) licensed or NDA material, gitignored, must not enter the repository cited by title, edition and revision in the documents that use it (source: fields in mcudb/board.yaml) Keys secrets, outside the repository host tests use only the insecure test key; the release names no key Decision log (artifact items) an external working tool, not versioned by git every decision is transcribed into the task list (done_when, "Entscheidung Maintainer ") or CHANGELOG.md, which are CI-10 Workstation state (.venv, tool cache, IDE) derived from CI-06 tools.ci check compares it with the pins

docs.title: 3.1 Branches
docs.text:
Branch Purpose Who writes Rule master released states only integrator, after the safety manager's approval receives only merges from dev (--no-ff); no direct commit, no hotfix on master — a fix goes through dev and a new PATCH release dev integration branch integrator receives only checked task branches; pushed after every merge (after git fsck --full --no-dangling); never force-pushed a task branch one task of a local contributor the contributor stays local; kept after the merge a session branch one task of a contributor session the contributor session pushed to origin, merged by the integrator

The task ID in the branch name is the link to the change request (section 8).

docs.title: 3.2 Versions
docs.text:
• The element has one version: the root file VERSION, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without suffix (read by CMake, nxconfig, Studio and tools/ci).
  • [Decided Q-CM4] SemVer meaning for a base software: MAJOR = an incompatible change of an interface the integrator uses (RTE interface, configuration schema, safe-supervisor API, AoU); MINOR = new function, compatible; PATCH = fix without interface change. As long as MAJOR is 0, a MINOR step may break interfaces, and the changelog says so.
  • The release tag is v + VERSION (tools/nxconfig/version.py: tag_of). No other tag name starts with v<digit>.
  • The Studio has its own version v_x.y.z (tools/studio/version.py); it is not a tag. A release tag records which Studio version belongs to it.

docs.title: 3.3 Commits in records
docs.text:
• In records meant to survive (tag messages, safety case, archived reports) a commit is written in full (40 hex).
  • In prose a short hash of at least 7 characters is fine; it must be unique in the repository at the time of writing.
  • A short hash of the OpenBSW submodule is marked as such ("OpenBSW submodule at 3b6e702"), because it does not resolve in the neXtBSW repository.

docs.title: 4.1 Definition
docs.text:
A baseline is an annotated git tag vX.Y.Z on a commit reachable from master (iso-q3). Because git commits are content-addressed, one tag fixes every configuration item in git at once: source, configuration, generated code, own tools, tool pins, tests, safety documents, board captures and the OpenBSW submodule commit (its gitlink). What lies outside git is bound to the tag through its hash in the tag message (section 5.3): the archived CI report and, through versions.toml, every external tool archive.

Rules:

  1. Annotated, never lightweight: the tag object carries tagger, date and the message of section 5.3. tools/nxconfig/pincheck.py rejects a lightweight release tag (tag-lightweight).
  2. On master: the tagged commit is the merge commit on master (or reachable from it); pincheck rejects tag-unreachable.
  3. VERSION equals the tag: tools/ci is red otherwise (check_release_version).
  4. Immutable: a published tag is never moved or deleted, and never re-created with the same name. A wrong release is corrected by the next PATCH release, whose changelog names what was wrong.
  5. [Decided Q-CM2] Signed from the first safety release on, with the safety manager's SSH signing key (git config gpg.format ssh, git tag -s). Development releases stay annotated only. Signing does not change any other rule; pincheck does not (yet) check a signature (G3): until it does, step 7 of 5.2 includes git tag -v vX.Y.Z for a safety release, run against the safety manager's allowed_signers file.

docs.title: 4.2 Safety status of a baseline [Decided Q-CM1]
docs.text:
The decision binds the preconditions to "release". v0.1.0 already exists and does not meet them — it was made as a reproducible version for customer pins, before this plan. To keep both true, a release tag states its safety status in its message:

Status Meaning May be cited as evidence in a safety case Preconditions development release a reproducible, versioned state; the integrator may pin it for development no P1–P3 and P7–P8 of section 5.1 safety release a state for which the SEooC claim (iso-q2: developed with the methods of part 6 for ASIL B, without the management part) is made yes all of P1–P9

The status never changes after tagging. A development release that later passes the reviews does not become a safety release; the next PATCH release does.

Alternative, not chosen: only a state that meets all preconditions gets a vX.Y.Z tag at all, and development states for customer pins use another tag form (for example vX.Y.Z-dev.N). That conflicts with a separate task (VERSION without suffix, CMake takes numbers only) and with pincheck; the maintainer chose the status line (Q-CM1, 2026-09-28).

docs.title: 4.4 Release lines
docs.text: [Proposal] An open source export or a licensed line is not a baseline of its own; it is one baseline plus one distribution profile (tools/distcheck export --profile <p>). Its identity is "vX.Y.Z, profile open", and the export records the full commit hash of the tag it was made from. A licensed overlay carries the same version (the overlay-version check of pincheck). How the export is published is a separate task's decision, not this plan's.

docs.title: 5.1 Preconditions
docs.text:
P1–P3 and P7–P8 are needed for every release, P4–P6 and P9 additionally for a safety release. The source of each precondition is iso-q3 unless marked otherwise. The safety plan (section 6) states the same preconditions as R1 … R6: P1, P3 and P7 = R1, P2 = R2, P4 = R3, P5 = R4, P6 = R5, P9 = R6; P8 has no safety counterpart.

# Precondition How it is checked Exists today P1 The release candidate on dev is complete: all tasks meant for the release merged, CHANGELOG.md has a section for vX.Y.Z, VERSION is X.Y.Z the integrator; tools/nxconfig version yes P2 A green CI run on the tree that will be tagged, with an archived report python -m tools.ci run --strict --clean (with --slow for a safety release, so the mutation runs count); the tree hash of the run equals the tree of the tag (section 7) the run yes; recording the tree hash no (G1), archiving no (G2) P3 Repository integrity git fsck --full --no-dangling without finding; working tree clean yes P4 The safety documents refer to the tag: every file of CI-08 carries Baseline: vX.Y.Z (section 6) test/test_cm_plan.py (G5): on a tagged checkout every state line must be Baseline: v<VERSION> the test yes; the lines are Working state until the next release P5 The qualification reports exist: tool qualification per tool-classification.md for every tool with TCL > 1 used for the release, and the qualification of pre-existing software per a separate task the safety plan's work-product list no P6 The reviews are closed: confirmation reviews of a separate task and the inspections of a separate task for the documents and units of the release, findings closed review records under doc/safety/reviews/; a record under deviation D-01 (maintainer, without independence) does not count no (no independent reviewer named, iso-q1; the safety manager reviews under D-01 since 2026-09-30, AN-093) P7 The safety manager approves the merge to master and the tag, with the safety status of section 4.2 entry, transcribed into the task list practice yes, entry format no P8 For an export of a release line: tools/distcheck check --profile <p> --references without error tools/distcheck yes P9 The safety case and the safety manual of the release exist and cite the tag (safety plan R6) 's own evidence-link test no

docs.title: 5.2 Steps
docs.text:
Step Action Command / check Who 1 Freeze the candidate on dev: set VERSION, close the changelog section, set every CI-08 header to Baseline: vX.Y.Z (the tag name is known before the tag exists, so no document has to cite a hash of itself) tools/nxconfig version; test G5 integrator 2 Full CI run on the candidate; keep the output folder python -m tools.ci run --strict --clean [--slow] --out build/ci-out-vX.Y.Z integrator (workstation) or GitHub Actions (workflow_dispatch / PR dev → master) 3 Integrity git fsck --full --no-dangling; git status --porcelain empty integrator 4 Approval of merge and tag with safety status decision item maintainer 5 Merge to master without fast-forward git checkout master && git merge --no-ff dev -m "Merge dev in master: neXtBSW X.Y.Z (Studio v_…)"; then git diff dev master must be empty integrator 6 Create the annotated tag on the merge commit with the message of section 5.3 git tag -a vX.Y.Z -F msg-vX.Y.Z.txt master; for a safety release git tag -s with the SSH key (Q-CM2) integrator 7 Prove the tag is a release python -m tools.ci check --release (runs pincheck on the tree: annotated, reachable from master, clean, VERSION equal); python tools/nxconfig pin projects/<p>/project.yaml --release; on the tagged checkout python -m unittest doc/safety/test/test_cm_plan.py (all state lines Baseline: vX.Y.Z); for a safety release git tag -v vX.Y.Z integrator 8 Publish git push origin master vX.Y.Z — the tag explicitly, never --tags, never --force integrator 9 Archive the CI report of step 2 as a GitHub release asset and in the local archive, for a safety release with the tool archives (section 7, Q-CM3); record the release in CHANGELOG.md, on the roadmap page and — integrator

A failure at any step stops the release. A tag that is already pushed is not removed (rule 4 of 4.1); the next PATCH release replaces it.

docs.title: 5.3 Tag message
docs.text:
The tag message is the permanent record of the baseline. The line Status: is decided (Q-CM1): every release tag carries it, development release or safety release. The other lines are [Proposal], the integrator's working template (values as example):

neXtBSW 0.2.0

Status: development release        (or: safety release)
Commit: dev <40-hex commit that was merged>, tree <40-hex tree>
OpenBSW: submodule <40-hex commit>
Studio: v_0.17.0
Compiler: xPack GCC 11.3.1 (tools/ci/versions.toml)
CI: <run id or "local">, verdict pass, <n>/<n> entries, <n> test cases, with/without --slow
CI report: sha256 <hash of the report archive> (ci-out-v0.2.0.zip)
Preconditions: P1 P2 P3 P7 met; P4 P5 P6 P9 not met   (a safety release lists all as met)
Approved: user, decision board <item id>, <date>
git fsck: no finding

v0.1.0 predates this template; its message carries the dev commit, the Studio version, the run result, git fsck and the compiler, and lacks tree hash, report hash, status and preconditions (section 4.3).

docs.title: 6. How safety documents name their baseline
6.1 Rule
docs.text:
Every document of CI-08 carries one line in its header that says which state its statements are about:

  • Baseline: vX.Y.Z — the document was checked against that release and is part of it. This is the only form a safety release accepts (P4).
  • Working state: dev at <commit> (after vX.Y.Z) — the document was written between two releases. At the next release, step 1 of 5.2 replaces the line with Baseline: v<next> after the document has been re-checked against the candidate (or the release says in its message that the document was carried unchecked, which excludes a safety release).

The existing sentences "written against dev at <hash>" and the "Update (task, against dev at <hash>)" blocks stay as history: they say when and against what a part was written. They no longer define the document's state. Commit hashes in the body (a board record at image c9a4f31, an inventory at 19df315) are evidence of a past observation and stay as they are.

docs.title: 6.2 Why the tag and not the commit
docs.text:
• One name for all documents of a release instead of one hash per document (finding SG7).
  • A tag says the state was released (reachable from master, CI green); a dev hash says nothing about that.
  • The tag cannot move; a hash can be unreachable after a history rewrite (the project had one, filter-branch in 2026-09, lizenz-und-release.md (not published, available on request)).

docs.title: 6.3 Inventory of the loose commits and migration
docs.text:
Read at ae92e89 (grep for short hashes in back-quotes). Every neXtBSW commit listed is an ancestor of v0.1.0 (git merge-base --is-ancestor <hash> v0.1.0), so none is lost and every document can take Working state: dev at ae92e89 (after v0.1.0) today and Baseline: v<next> at the next release.

Document Hashes cited Role of the hashes Migration (by the document's next task or the release step 1; not done here) concept.md c0beb4d (issue 1), fa04ed1 (issue 2), c9a4f31 (board image) header: written/checked against; body: evidence add the baseline line; keep both hashes as history fmea.md 63ea900 (issue 1), f2e2c43, 1bbba28 header and "Update" blocks; sources add the baseline line iso26262-gap.md 62a1b53 (analysis), fa04ed1, 63ea900, f8ee573 (quoted in SG7) header and sources; SG7 quotes the others add the baseline line; SG7 is closed by this plan once the lines exist tool-classification.md f8ee573 (issue 1), f2e2c43, 62a1b53 (norm questions) header and "Update" blocks add the baseline line rtos-comparison.md d9d5996; OpenBSW submodule 3b6e702 header add the baseline line; the submodule hash is marked as such already static-analysis.md 19df315 (inventory 2026-09-21) body: date of an inventory add the baseline line hardware-mechanisms.md, traceability.md, requirements.yaml none — add the baseline line (requirements.yaml: a header comment, or the StrictDoc document field after a later change) cm-plan.md (this) ae92e89 header follows the rule from issue 1

The documents of the current work step (safety-plan.md, hsi-s32k1xx.md, dfa.md) should start with the line; the maintainer can add it at the merge if they do not.

docs.title: 6.4 Migration done (issue 2)
docs.text:
Set the line in every safety document, at dev 6f868b5 (2026-09-28). Only the header was touched: the line is inserted as a paragraph of its own (after the title, or after the header table), nothing else in the documents changed, and every hash of 6.3 stays in place as history. The commit named in each line is chosen by one rule:

  • the commit the document says it was written against, when that commit lies after v0.1.0 and no later task changed the document since;
  • otherwise 6f868b5, the dev state at which the line was set: the document was written against a commit before v0.1.0 or names none (concept.md, fmea.md, iso26262-gap.md, tool-classification.md, rtos-comparison.md, static-analysis.md, hardware-mechanisms.md, requirements.yaml), or later tasks changed it after that commit (dfa.md by an earlier change, safety-plan.md by earlier changes, this plan by an earlier change).

Working state claims no re-check (6.1): it says between which release and which dev state the document was written. The re-check against the release candidate happens in step 1 of 5.2.

docs.title: 6.5 Consistency test (G5)
docs.text:
test/test_cm_plan.py checks, on every run:

  1. every file directly under doc/safety (*.md, *.yaml) except the generated ones has exactly one state line, and it lies in the header (before the first ## heading or --- rule; for YAML in the leading comment block);
  2. the line has one of the two forms of 6.1, nothing else on it;
  3. Working state: the commit resolves, is an ancestor of HEAD, and the named release is the newest release whose content the commit contains; Baseline: the tag exists and is not newer than VERSION;
  4. on a checkout that carries the release tag v + VERSION (step 7 of 5.2) every line is Baseline: v<VERSION>;
  5. the table of 4.3 lists exactly the release tags of git for-each-ref refs/tags/v*, each with its full commit;
  6. the exempt generated files are exactly the rows of the document register (anomaly-register.md section 6) with status generated.

The git checks (3 to 5) are skipped with a message when the clone is shallow or has no release tags; the text checks always run. Counter-checks on broken copies show that each rule sees its fault.

docs.title: 7.1 Reproducing a baseline
docs.text:
The procedure the plan promises (8-7.4.4); not executed for this issue:

git clone <origin> neXtBSW && cd neXtBSW
git checkout vX.Y.Z && git submodule update --init
git describe --exact-match   # must print vX.Y.Z
python -m tools.ci setup --python-packages
python -m tools.ci run --strict --clean --release --out build/ci-repro

Expected: verdict pass, the same entries and test cases as the archived report, and the same artefact sizes. Whether the images are byte-identical across machines is not proven: individual tasks recorded a byte-identical demo image before and after their change on the same workstation (for example), not across machines and operating systems. Until it is proven, the image CRC of a board record is valid for the image that was flashed, and a rebuilt image is compared by its CRC before it is used as that evidence.

docs.title: 8. Changes and their base configuration
docs.text:
Change management itself is the task list (task IDs, done_when, owner lines with dates, the decision log) and will get the safety impact field of a separate task. This plan adds only the link to configuration management (8-8.4.2: a change request names its base configuration):

  • The base configuration of a change is the dev commit its branch started from. git records it (git merge-base dev <task branch>); the integrator writes it into the merge commit message or the changelog entry when it matters for a safety document ("against dev at …").
  • A change that touches a CI-08 document sets that document to Working state: dev at <commit> (after vX.Y.Z).
  • A change of CI-06 (tool pins) requires a full CI run (versions.toml header) and is named in the next release message.
  • A submodule update of external/openbsw is a task of its own, never a side effect.

Issue 1, 2026-09-28 Task Gap analysis iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) section 6 no. 2; rows 6-13, 6-14, 9-02 Decision safety manager, decision log iso-q4: show coexistence (variant b) — QM parts keep QM with a freedom-from-interference argument per module; the separating element (RTOS, MPU code) is ASIL B Status draft for review; written by a contributor on the safety manager's behalf (author side, safety plan section 2) Corrections Korrektur nach Safety-Review 2026-10-02 Freigabe unveraendert (the release of 2026-10-02 stands): section 4 and CX-6 say that since an earlier change all 8 MPU descriptors of S32K144 are used, with the consequence for a separate task; AoU-41 added Built against branch dev at 65f3dc9, demo project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo, preset evalboard-s32k144-demo (RelWithDebInfo), xPack GCC 11.3.1, linker map application.map of that build Verification mock/host: consistency test test/test_coexistence.py against this document, the linker map of the demo build, tools/openbswsync/copies.yaml and the tree; nothing on the board

Baseline: v0.2.0

What this document is. The coexistence decision of the safety plan (activity P9-02, P6-06) worked out for every module in the demo image: which software is ASIL B, which stays QM, and for each QM module the argument per kind of interference that it cannot violate an ASIL B requirement — or the finding that says why the argument does not hold yet and which task closes it. It is the work product doc/safety/coexistence.md named by the safety plan (P9-02, CM-09) and the safety case (EW-20).

Licence rule. ISO 26262:2018 is cited by part and clause only (for example "6-7.4.8"), requirements are restated in our own words; no text, table or figure of the standard is reproduced.

What it is not. Not the partitioning design (builds it; section 7 is the hand-over), not the qualification of pre-existing software, not a statement that the image is free from interference today.

docs.title: 1. Reading of the rule and classes
1.1 What the standard asks (own words)
docs.text:
• 6-7.4.8, 9-6. When software elements with different ASILs — or QM and ASIL elements — share one image, either everything is developed to the highest ASIL, or it is shown for each lower-rated element that it cannot interfere with the higher-rated ones. Without that evidence the lower-rated element inherits the highest ASIL.
  • 6-7.4.9. If freedom from interference rests on partitioning, the shared resources are handled so that the separation holds, the partitioning software itself is developed to the highest ASIL of the partitions, and its effectiveness is shown at integration. Hardware support for the partitioning is demanded only at ASIL D; an MPU on one core is admissible at B.
  • 6-Annex D. Interference is considered in three kinds: timing and execution (blocking, deadlock, livelock, wrong allocation of execution time, wrong synchronisation), memory (corruption of content, access to memory allocated to another element), exchange of information (repetition, loss, delay, insertion, masquerade, corruption, wrong sequence of data, blocking of a communication channel).
  • 9-6 is the coexistence clause; 9-5 (decomposition) is not used at stage 1 (safety plan T-08).

Stage 1 has one ASIL (B) and QM. So the question per module is binary: B, or QM with evidence.

docs.title: 1.2 Classes
docs.text: Class Meaning Development B-SM implements a software safety requirement (component of sw-architecture.md section 1) part 6 at ASIL B (allocation, 6-7.4.6) B-SEP provides the separation other arguments rest on: scheduler, task and stack layout, interrupt lock, start-up, vector table, linker script part 6 at ASIL B or qualified per 8-12 (6-7.4.9) B-DEP called by ASIL B code before the safe state is reached, or set up so that an ASIL B mechanism relies on it part 6 at ASIL B or qualified per 8-12 QM-C QM; stays QM only with the coexistence rows of section 3 argued QM process (tests, static analysis as for all code); counts as ASIL B while a row is open

docs.title: 1.3 Direction of calls
docs.text:
Interference from QM to B is what the standard names. In this code base it also enters the other way: when ASIL B code calls QM code, a fault of the QM code runs in the ASIL B context (its stack, its priority, its interrupt lock). The rule used here:

  • a QM function may be called from ASIL B code after the safe state has been reached (the outputs are de-energised by then; a fault of the callee can only delay the reset, which the MCU watchdog bounds) — example: the hard-fault dump uses printf after the safe outputs table was walked;
  • before the safe state, every callee is B-DEP or the call is removed. The linker cross-reference of the safety archives (section 2.3) is the list of such calls.

docs.title: 1.4 When a QM module counts as QM
docs.text: A QM-C module counts as QM for a release claim only when every coexistence row of section 3 that names it has status argued or AoU. A single open row makes it ASIL B for that release. This keeps the claim honest while is not done: today 8 of the 9 QM-C modules with code in the image are ASIL B by this rule (section 0), which is the state the gap analysis described (row 6-13).

Remarks:

  • Why S-OSB holds 22 KB RAM. app.cpp defines the task stacks (2048 B each, section 2.1 of sw-architecture.md) and the task objects. The stacks are the memory the separation argument is about (section 3, CX-8); they belong to the module that lays them out, not to the tasks that use them.
  • M-CAN is larger than the gate. The transmit gate and the bus state are header-only (libs/bsw/canSystem) and compiled into CanSystem.cpp, which also holds the QM integration of the CAN controllers. A translation unit takes the highest ASIL of what it contains (CX-7).
  • The bootloader (C-BLD of sw-architecture.md) is a separate image and not part of this inventory; it contains no QM module that runs together with the application.
  • Q-BLD, Q-BCF, Q-NVM, Q-FIJ, Q-TST and Q-DOC have no part in the demo image; they exist so that every copy of copies.yaml is classified. Q-FIJ is in the image of the development build only when fault injection is on.

docs.title: 4. The separating element at ASIL B
docs.text:
Decision fixes that the software implementing the separation is ASIL B. Concretely, for neXtBSW on S32K1:

Element Module Why it separates Route to ASIL B FreeRTOS scheduler, tick, context switch, configASSERT S-RTOS temporal separation: the safety task preempts every application task; the priorities are the argument of CA-06, CA-11, CA-14, CA-28 pre-existing: qualification per 8-12 or replacement — the route is decided in a separate task (iso-q5, rtos-comparison.md) Task table, priorities, stacks, OS hooks S-OSB the layout the temporal and memory arguments rest on; stack overflow reaction own development per part 6; tasks.yaml checked by nxconfig (above_application) MPU set-up, gate, descriptor check M-MEM (MemoryProtection) spatial separation of the supervisor; basis of every future partition own development per part 6 (already B-SM) ISR hooks and SAFE_ISR wrapper M-LCY (IsrHooks) opens the gate for exactly the safety interrupts own development (already B-SM) Interrupt lock, vector table, start-up, linker script S-INT the lock is the critical section of every monitor; the linker script places .mpu_bss and the safety stack copies of OpenBSW (lock, start-up) and own linker script: own development per part 6 where modified, 8-12 where identical

What the S32K1 MPU can and cannot do for partitions (register facts from mcudb, hsi-s32k1xx.md):

  • The NXP system MPU grants an access if any valid region descriptor grants it. A protected window therefore has to be cut out of the full-access area: since an earlier change all 8 descriptors of S32K144 are used (descriptor 0 for the debugger and, as written by an earlier change, the other bus masters, 1, 3 and 5 for three full-access tiles around the two protected windows 2 and 4: supervisor data and safety stack, 6 for the stack guard, 7 for the tail).
  • One more protected window costs two descriptors (the window and one more tile) — so no further window fits on S32K144, S32K142, S32K146 and S32K116 (8 descriptors, all used) without freeing descriptors, and about four more fit on S32K148 (16). Consequence for a separate task: the partition model has to be designed within the 8 descriptors (or free descriptors first), and the restriction of descriptor 0 for the masters M2/M3 (AoU-41) must not need a descriptor of its own. This bounds to a two-partition model on the small derivatives: one contiguous ASIL B data window (safety-related SWC data and stacks, switched at the context switch) against everything QM (CX-6).
  • FreeRTOS on this family uses the non-MPU Cortex-M4F port: every task runs privileged, and the kernel data (task control blocks, ready lists, queues) lie in general RAM writable by every task (CX-5). The system MPU can discriminate supervisor and user accesses, but only if the kernel runs QM tasks unprivileged — which needs a port with a system-call layer. That is a question for the RTOS route: FreeRTOS has such ports only for the ARM core MPU, which S32K1 does not have (rtos-comparison.md section 2.5).

Consequence for the argument: on S32K1, kernel data corruption by a QM task is detected, not prevented — through the timing mechanisms that the corruption would trip (MCU watchdog SM-01 … SM-03, period check SM-04, halt deadman SM-06) and the kernel asserts. Whether that detection argument is sufficient at ASIL B is decision point Q-CX1 (section 9.3).

Language: English, like the rest of doc/.

What this document is. The work product that the safety plan names for activities P6-07 (pre-existing software) and P8-09 (qualification of software components) and that the safety case lists as evidence EW-07. It gives every pre-existing component in the demo image one route — qualify it per 8-12, treat it as own development per part 6, replace it, or leave it QM under the coexistence argument — together with the plan that carries the route out, and it contains the first qualification report, for OpenBSW's safeMonitor. It also records the two tool changes the gap analysis asked for: the modified OpenBSW copies in the safety path are now analysed as own code by the static analysis (gating) and are counted in the coverage thresholds.

Licence rule. ISO 26262:2018 is cited by part and clause only (for example "8-12" = ISO 26262-8:2018 clause 12); requirements are restated in our own words, and no text, table or figure of the standard is reproduced.

What it is not. Not the FreeRTOS qualification (postponed by an earlier change; its plan is in section 4.3), not the coexistence argument (that is coexistence.md, whose module classes this document uses unchanged), not a tool qualification (compiler and libraries as tools: tool-classification.md).

docs.title: 1. Reading of the rules and the routes
1.1 What the standard asks (own words)
docs.text:
• 6-7.4.7 / 6-12, 8-12. Software that was not developed for this element — a library, an operating system, a component taken over from another project — may be used in a safety-related element when it is qualified: there is a specification of what it must do in this use (requirements, configuration, interfaces, behaviour in abnormal conditions), evidence that it does that (verification suited to the ASIL, including requirements-based tests with a measure of structural coverage), evidence that it is suitable for the intended use (assumptions of use, integration evidence), the exact version and configuration it holds for, and the known anomalies. The qualification holds only for that version and that use; a change of either makes it void.
  • 8-12, 10-9.1. A component that is changed is no longer a qualification case: it is developed (or re-verified) under part 6 like own code, or argued by a change analysis. Hence the gap analysis (row 8-27): a modified OpenBSW copy in the safety path is own development and must pass the same gates as own code.
  • 8-14. Proven in use is not used (safety plan tailoring T-07): no field data exists.
  • 9-6 / 6-7.4.8. A QM component in the same image needs no qualification as long as the coexistence argument shows that it cannot violate an ASIL B requirement (coexistence.md); where the argument is open, the component counts as ASIL B (coexistence rule 1.4) and falls back to one of the routes above.

docs.text: Route Meaning Evidence it produces R-Q (8-12) qualify the unchanged component for its use in neXtBSW a qualification report per component (template: section 5) R-6 (part 6) the component is own development; unit design, unit tests with coverage, static analysis as a gate, code review the part-6 work products of the module (sw-architecture, unit-design, tests, tools/misra, coverage.yaml) R-X (replace) remove the component or replace it by own code developed under part 6 the replacement's part-6 work products R-QM QM under the coexistence argument; no qualification while every coexistence row of its module holds the rows of coexistence.md section 3 n/a not linked into the image (host tests, build files, other families) —

docs.title: 3.1 Static analysis as a gate
docs.text:
Before this task tools/misra analysed every OpenBSW copy, but reported copies separately and not gating (static-analysis.md section 2; gap analysis SG5 / AN-031). Now:

  • tools/misra/rules.yaml has a list scope.gating_copies of 19 path patterns, one comment per module, taken from the module table of coexistence.md. A copy with status: modified that matches is classified own and its findings follow the rules of own code: deviation, baseline, or a new finding that fails the run. Identical copies stay separate even when they match (route R-Q, PC-13), and so do copies of QM modules (R-QM, PC-14).
  • tools/misra/test_misra.py checks the list against the document: the set of modified copies the patterns hit must equal the set of modified copies whose module is B-SM, B-SEP or B-DEP in coexistence.md — 47 at this working state; every pattern must hit a copy. Counter-checks: dropping ecu/safety/safeWatchdog/** or adding ecu/application/src/logger/** (QM) is detected.
  • python -m tools.misra baseline --only <file> (new) rewrites the baseline entries of the named files only. It was used to take the 47 files in without taking in the 57 findings that origin/dev already fails with (Q-1).

docs.title: 4.1 Procedure per component
docs.text:
Every R-Q component gets a report with the sections of QR-01 (section 5), in this order of work:

  1. Identify: path, submodule commit, SHA-256 (16 hex digits) of every file, licence, configuration used.
  2. Intended use: which parts neXtBSW uses, by which ASIL B module, how many instances, with which template arguments or configuration.
  3. Specify: component requirements in our words, from the documentation and the code; where they differ, the code decides and the difference is an anomaly.
  4. Assumptions of use: what the maintainer of the component must ensure (lifetimes, contexts, locks, value ranges).
  5. Verify: requirements-based tests (OpenBSW's own tests where they exist, own tests where they do not), with statement and branch coverage of the component; static analysis with the project rule set; a trace table requirement → test; integration evidence in neXtBSW (host tests with the real ASIL B callers, board records).
  6. Anomalies: every difference and weakness found, with its effect in neXtBSW and how it is handled.
  7. Verdict and validity: for which use the component is suitable; the report is void when a file hash or the use changes.

docs.title: 4.2 Order and effort
docs.text:
Order Component Effort Why this order 1 PC-01 safeMonitor done smallest, decides every safety event 2 PC-02 safeUtils, PC-06 interface headers 1.5 AD trivial, but every ASIL B unit includes them 3 PC-03 safeBspMcuWatchdog 2–3 AD independent watchdog of the MCU; real code has no host test (Q-3) 4 PC-04 bspInterruptsImpl 1–2 AD separating element; needed before a later change can argue partitioning 5 PC-11 CMSIS-Core, PC-05 MCU drivers 1 + 5–10 AD with the HSI review (hsi-s32k1xx.md) 6 PC-10 ETL subset, PC-09 libraries 5–9 AD depend on the usage scans; PC-09 also on the compiler decision TN2 7 PC-08 FreeRTOS with PC-07 async binding 30–50 AD postponed by an earlier change — PC-13 identical copies inside 2–6 qualified with the component they copy

Total without FreeRTOS: about 16–30 AD; with FreeRTOS: about 46–80 AD.

docs.title: 4.3 FreeRTOS package (plan only, not started)
docs.text:
Route R-Q as decided on 2026-09-22 (rtos-u1-anfrage, after the comparison rtos-comparison.md): stay on FreeRTOS and qualify it; the migration to a certified kernel was not chosen. Scope and steps, taken from rtos-comparison.md sections 1 and 4:

  • Scope — the kernel V10.6.2 in the configuration of FreeRtosPlatformConfig.h (static allocation, no MPU port, no timers task unless used), the Cortex-M4F SysTick port with OpenBSW's ManualChanges.diff, and the kernel services the async binding calls, including the kernel internals it relies on (AN-057). Other ports (M0+, R4F) are separate reports when those families enter a safety release.
  • Steps — requirements of the used API subset; the port's interrupt masking and context switch reviewed against the architecture manual; tests of the subset on the host (posix port) and on the target (board test suite, gap task 20); static analysis of the kernel files with the project rule set (reported, not gating, since the code is not ours); anomaly list from the FreeRTOS change history between V10.6.2 and the current release.
  • Effort — 30–50 AD for the first core, redone at every kernel update (rtos-comparison.md section 0).
  • Open — whether a qualified component is accepted as the separating element (6-7.4.9); the coexistence argument needs the answer.

docs.title: 5.1 Identification
docs.text: Item Value Component safeMonitor — generic monitor templates of the OpenBSW safety library Source external/openbsw/libs/safety/safeMonitor, OpenBSW submodule commit 3b6e702 (2026-09-14) Licence Apache-2.0 (header of every file); module.spec: maturity: production, safety: True Files (SHA-256, first 16 hex digits) Register.h 1e3248df946ca148, Sequence.h e7b903d0d7d174be, Trigger.h 69ff3b14b06fc1ad, Value.h 68dd7d4def403c7d, Watchdog.h 2993bb7c545cc64b, common.h 0cc4f65c4ec043ef (581 lines of headers) Build form header-only, CMake INTERFACE library linked by safeSupervisor; uses etl/platform.h (ETL_MAYBE_UNUSED) only Configuration in neXtBSW template arguments of ecu/safety/safeSupervisor/include/safeSupervisor/SafeSupervisor.h: handler SafeSupervisor, event SafeSupervisor::Event; ScopedMutex always the default DefaultMutex (no lock); context DefaultContext for the sequence monitors, uint32_t for trigger and value monitors

docs.title: 5.2 Intended use
docs.text: SafeSupervisor (M-SUP, B-SM) owns every safety monitor and is the handler of all of them: 17 TriggerMonitor (Trigger<…, DefaultMutex, uint32_t>), 3 ValueMonitor (Value<…, bool, DefaultMutex, uint32_t>), 2 sequence monitors (SafetyManagerSequenceMonitor over 7 checkpoints of the safety cycle, SequenceMonitor over ENTER/LEAVE) and one DeferredTriggerMonitor that wraps a Trigger for reporters outside the safety task (SafetyEventMailbox.h). Every event a mechanism reports reaches the reaction of SafeSupervisor::handle() through one of these monitors. Watchdog and Register are not used by neXtBSW.

docs.title: 5.3 Component requirements
docs.text:
Written for this report from the documentation (doc/index.rst, the header comments) and the code; the code decides where they differ (QA-1).

ID Requirement SMON-01 Trigger::trigger(ctx) stores ctx and calls the handler with the configured event exactly once per call. SMON-02 Value::check(v, ctx) stores ctx; it calls the handler with the configured event exactly once if v differs from the expected value, and not at all otherwise. SMON-03 Sequence::hit(cp, ctx) stores ctx; if cp is not the expected checkpoint it calls the handler once and leaves the expectation unchanged; otherwise it advances the expectation by one, and after the last checkpoint back to the first. The first expected checkpoint after construction is the first one. SMON-04 Watchdog::service() counts down from the timeout, saturating at 0, and calls the handler on every call while the counter is 0; kick(ctx) stores ctx and restarts the count at the timeout. SMON-05 Register::check(ctx) stores ctx, compares the masked value at each entry's address with the expected value in order, stops at the first mismatch and then calls the handler once; getLastCheckedEntry() names the last entry compared (the faulty one after a mismatch, nullptr before the first check). SMON-06 Every public operation that changes state holds exactly one ScopedMutex object for its whole duration; the handler is called while it is held (QA-1). SMON-07 The stored context is a copy; getContext() returns the last stored context, and a default-constructed context before the first store. SMON-08 The monitor calls the handler in the caller's context and returns after it; it neither blocks nor defers. SMON-09 No dynamic memory, no recursion, no exceptions thrown, no static state other than the constant default context; run time is constant per call (Register: linear in the number of entries). SMON-10 The monitor keeps a reference to the handler and (Register) to the entry array; it does not copy them. SMON-11 The event and the expected value are copied at construction and cannot change afterwards.

docs.title: 5.4 Assumptions of use
docs.text: ID Assumption How neXtBSW meets it SMON-A1 The handler object (and the Register entry array) outlives the monitor (SMON-10). SafeSupervisor owns the monitors as members and is a static object SMON-A2 A monitor is changed and read from one execution context, or the ScopedMutex makes the operations mutually exclusive. getContext() itself is not guarded. all monitors are driven and read in the safety task; reporters outside it post to SafetyEventMailbox, which hands the report over in the safety context (host test safe-supervisor-mpu) SMON-A3 With a non-default ScopedMutex the handler runs inside the lock (SMON-06); it must not take the same lock or block. only DefaultMutex is used; a compile-time check is proposed (P-6) SMON-A4 The checkpoint type of a Sequence has consecutive values from the first to the last checkpoint, first ≤ last (the monitor advances by +1). both enums in SafeSupervisor.h are consecutive from 0 with first < last; not checked at compile time (QA-3) SMON-A5 Watchdog with timeout 0 reports at the first service() call. Watchdog not used SMON-A6 The monitor state lies in memory the safety part protects; a corrupted monitor can suppress or invent an event. SafeSupervisor and its monitors lie in the MPU-protected safety RAM (sw-architecture.md)

docs.title: 5.5 Verification
docs.text:
Requirements-based tests. OpenBSW ships 42 tests in test/src (gtest/gmock, each with a description of what it checks). They were built unchanged with googletest from the same submodule and run on the host:

g++ -std=c++17 -O0 --coverage -fno-inline -Wall -Wextra \
    -I external/openbsw/libs/safety/safeMonitor/include -I external/openbsw/libs/safety/safeMonitor/test/include \
    -I external/openbsw/libs/3rdparty/etl/include -I ecu/etl_profile \
    -I <googletest>/googletest/include -I <googletest>/googlemock/include \
    external/openbsw/libs/safety/safeMonitor/test/src/*.cpp gtest-all.o gmock-all.o gmock_main.o -lpthread -o smtest
./smtest                                   # [  PASSED  ] 42 tests.
gcovr --filter '.*safeMonitor/include/.*' --exclude-throw-branches .

Result 2026-09-28 (g++ 13.3, gcovr 8.6): 42 of 42 passed; statements 80/80 (100 %), branches 28/28 (100 %) with exception edges excluded (with them 28/40: the 12 missing edges are the exception paths of the lock object and the handler call, which do not exist on the target — it is built with -fno-exceptions).

Requirement Tests (OpenBSW, test/src) SMON-01 TriggerTest.TriggersHandler SMON-02 ValueTest.DetectsTooHighAValue, DetectsTooLowAValue, PassesWithExpectedValue SMON-03 SequenceTest.RunsThroughInCorrectOrder, WrapsBackToFirstCheckpoint, DetectsWrongCheckpointAtTheBeginning, …InTheMiddle, …AtTheEnd, FiresMultipleTimes (three wrong hits, then the first checkpoint is still expected) SMON-04 WatchdogTest.DetectsTimeout, Triggers (reports on every call after the timeout), KickResetsTimeout, KickResetsTimeoutOnlyOnce SMON-05 RegisterTest.DetectsBitFlipToZero, DetectsBitFlipToOne, IgnoresMaskedBits, ChecksAllEntries, LastCheckedEntryIsInitiallyNull, …PointsToLastEntryAfterCheck, …PointsToFaultyEntry SMON-06 UsesScopedMutex of Register, Sequence, Trigger, Value; WatchdogTest.ServiceUsesScopedMutex, KickUsesScopedMutex — count and release of the lock; handler inside the lock: supplementary probe below SMON-07 *Test.UsesDefaultConstructedContext, StoresAndReturnsGivenContext, ContextIsBeingCopied (5 monitors each) SMON-08 every test above: the mock handler is called synchronously inside the tested call SMON-09 analysis of the code (no new, throw, recursion or static mutable data in the six headers); static analysis below SMON-10, SMON-11 analysis of the code (member types Handler&, Entry const* const, Event const, Type const)

Supplementary probe (SMON-06). A short program (26 lines) instantiates all five monitors with a lock type that counts itself and a handler that records whether the lock is held; each monitor is made to report once (the Watchdog also with timeout 0). Result: 6 reports, 6 inside the lock — confirming QA-1 and SMON-A5.

Static analysis. One translation unit instantiating every template as neXtBSW does, analysed with the checks of tools/misra/rules.yaml: clang-tidy 22.1.8 — no finding in the six headers (all findings of the run are in the C++ standard library); cppcheck 2.17.1 with the MISRA add-on — 19 × rule 12.3 on template parameter lists (the C checker reading C++; a tool notice in rules.yaml notices_cpp) and 2 × unusedVariable on the lock object ETL_MAYBE_UNUSED const ScopedMutex m; of Trigger and Value (the object exists for its lifetime, false positive). Nothing that needs a change or a deviation.

Integration evidence in neXtBSW. The real SafeSupervisor with the real safeMonitor headers runs in 12 host test entries (safe-supervisor, safe-supervisor-bare, safe-supervisor-mpu, safe-watchdog, safety-cycle, cycle-timer-off, safe-io, safety-gate, safe-console, safety-reset-console, kernel-fault-reaction, safe-state-hold); they trace to SSR-001…005, 012…018, 020, 021, 033, 034, 064…066 and 070 in tests.yaml. On 2026-09-28 in the Linux container 10 of them passed with the normal flags and all 12 passed in the coverage build; safe-supervisor and safe-supervisor-bare stop there at -Werror on a 64-bit long in the test file (Q-6), not in safeMonitor. The board records of the safety reactions (tools/boardtest/captures) exercise the same code on the target.

docs.title: 5.6 Anomalies
docs.text: ID Anomaly Effect in neXtBSW Handling QA-1 The comments of Register::check, Sequence::hit and Watchdog::service say the handler is called outside the ScopedMutex; the code constructs the lock at the start of the function and calls the handler before it ends, i.e. inside (all five monitors). none: neXtBSW uses DefaultMutex (no lock) everywhere requirement SMON-06 states the real behaviour; assumption SMON-A3; proposed as an upstream documentation fix (P-7) QA-2 getContext() is not guarded by the ScopedMutex; a reader in another context can see a partly written context. none today (SMON-A2) assumption SMON-A2 QA-3 Sequence advances by static_cast<Checkpoint>(expected + 1) and needs consecutive checkpoint values; nothing checks this at compile time. none: both enums are consecutive assumption SMON-A4; a static_assert in SafeSupervisor.h is proposed (P-6) QA-4 Watchdog with timeout 0 reports at the first service(); a timeout of N gives a window of N calls including the one that reports. none: not used assumption SMON-A5

docs.title: 5.7 Verdict and validity
docs.text:
• Trigger, Value, Sequence with DefaultMutex — as used in neXtBSW — are suitable for use in the ASIL B safety part under the assumptions SMON-A1 … A6: the requirements SMON-01 … 03 and 06 … 11 are specified, verified by requirements-based tests with full statement and branch coverage of the component, the static analysis shows no finding that needs action, and the one documentation anomaly (QA-1) has no effect in this configuration.
  • Watchdog and Register are verified to the same depth (SMON-04, 05) but not used; the verdict extends to them only after their intended use is added to 5.2 and checked against the assumptions.
  • Validity. Bound to submodule 3b6e702 and the six file hashes of 5.1, and to the configuration of 5.1. A submodule update that changes one of the hashes, a new template argument (another lock, another context type) or a new user of the component makes the report void until it is re-checked. Proposal P-5 automates the hash check.
  • Status. Complete on the author side; the confirmation review CM-09 (safety plan, I1 independence) is pending, and the acceptance by the safety manager.

Not changed, by a project decision: the coverage grades of the assumed goals (ZC); finding F4 stays open until a follow-up task (ZJ); the re-rating of SM-21/SM-22 in fmea.md (proposal M7 of the gap analysis) and the stale fmea.md places of AN-012 and AN-015 belong to the review of the failure analysis CM-02 (ZJ, ZL).
