docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the core executes no software for longer than 10 ms: debugger halt, interrupt lock, starved BSP task (the retrigger runs in the BSP task's 1 ms poll), later a flash operation that stalls the core Detection LPIT channel 1, 32-bit down counter, MCR[DBG_EN] = 1 (keeps counting while the core is halted), 10 ms, retriggered at every 1 ms poll; second source DFSR Reaction the interrupt walks the safe outputs table (S1 without reset); the guard then inhibits the PWM and takes DRV_EN away until the next explicit enable Times detection 10 ms (hardware counter, independent of the safety task); reaction: exception entry + walk on the first instruction after the halt. Minimum FTTI served: > 10 ms for a stall; for a debugger halt the reaction comes only when the core runs again (concept 6.1) Diagnostic coverage high for stalls and halts ≥ 10 ms. Blind spots accepted by the safety manager: a halt < 10 ms with a probe that clears DFSR. Named blind spot (issue 2, CM-02 decision Z3): the loss of its own clock - SM-06 runs on the SIRC (LPIT functional clock) and stands with it, so a lost SIRC is caught by SM-01's hardware reset only (residual risk DF-05, section 2.1); a gated clock is a bus fault (SM-17) and a slow clock is seen by the progress check since an earlier change (DFA-2). The class stays high for what the mechanism guards - the stall and the halt of the software Latent faults of the mechanism the retrigger re-enables the channel (SETTEN) every millisecond, which heals a cleared enable. Since an earlier change a configuration re-check exists: checkLpitDeadman() compares MCR[M_CEN], MCR[DBG_EN], the channel's MIER bit, TCTRL (32-bit periodic, no trigger; T_EN deliberately excluded because the retrigger and the handler switch it), TVAL, the NVIC enable and the priority of LPIT0_Ch1_IRQn, every safety cycle from the safety task (SafetyManager::checkSupervisionPeripherals, not from the BSP task that retriggers the deadman), and raises DEADMAN_CONFIGURATION_ERROR with the differing fields in the context (S1 + S2); detection nominal 10 ms, guaranteed 17 ms since an earlier change. The expected values belong to the owner of the deadman and come through deadmanExpectedConfiguration(); issue 1 said "host verified, target binding pending" - added the strong definition (out of line in Integration.cpp since an earlier change), and the fault injection of a separate task proved the re-check on the target (falsified TVAL, MIER, NVIC priority and MCR[DBG_EN] each reset with last cause 0x110, 8.1 B6; F12 closed, AN-012). Progress check (DFA-2, issue 2): the safety cycle polls the deadman's counter until it changes, within a budget of two LPIT ticks derived from the clock plan (22 polls on the eval board); a counter that stands still or moves too slowly with the channel enabled is DEADMAN_CONFIGURATION_ERROR field 0x100 (S1 + S2); a channel disabled by the retrigger or an expiry gives no verdict in that cycle. Not seen by either check: the lost SIRC (DF-05, above) Evidence debug-halt-guard (real drivers, PWM inhibited, DRV_EN and KL30B off until next enable), safe-outputs-order (vector of LPIT0_Ch1 walks the table before any call), lpit-deadman-check (the re-check against an LPIT/NVIC register model, every field falsified singly, with and without T_EN), safety-cycle (re-check called in the safety task, event with context; without a deadman no check), lpit-deadman-progress and safety-progress (the progress check, with mutants); board 2026-09-21 (register part: LPIT0_MCR = 0x9, TIF1 set during halt) and 2026-09-21 (fully passed: halts of 30 s and 60 s with running bridge, oscilloscope silent after the J-Link go command, 10 min without false trip); board 2026-09-22 (the re-check on the target, 8.1 B6); board 2026-10-03/04 (SIRCDIV2 /64 gives field 0x100; a stopped system time expires SM-06; a lost SIRC ends in the watchdog reset without a walk - section 2.1) Residual / action the target binding and its board check are done. Residual risk DF-05: a lost SIRC stops SM-06 silently (section 2.1, SM-01); investigation and architecture (for example the deadman on another clock) with a separate task after Release R1. The alternative of DFA-2 (SIRCVLD in the SYSTEM_CLOCK class of SM-22) stays with a separate task

docs.title: SM-07 — Startup watchdog self-test
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the watchdog hardware cannot reset the MCU (latent fault of SM-01) Detection OpenBSW executeFastTest from main(): two deliberate watchdog resets (test low / test high) at every start, before the application Reaction WATCHDOG_STARTUP_CHECK_FAILURE → S1 held Times at start-up (about 6 ms); the latent-fault interval of SM-01 is therefore the time between two starts Diagnostic coverage high for "watchdog cannot reset": both test halves exercise the real reset path Latent faults of the mechanism none needed at this level Evidence safe-supervisor, safe-supervisor-bare (reaction: hold, no reset, outputs walked every round, watchdog serviced); board 2026-09-21 (fifth part): reaction proven with a simulated failure (J-Link breakpoint), console line, no reset for 16 s; the detection of a real hardware failure cannot be provoked Residual / action for ECUs that are rarely restarted, the latent interval equals the operating time → AoU-25 (section 6, F13/F3; issue 1: proposed - binding since concept issue 3, concept 4.2, CM-07 ZG)

docs.title: SM-10 — MPU: protected RAM (fusa gate)
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered code outside the safety context writes the safety manager's data or stack (supervisor state, monitors, counters). Since an earlier change also an overflow of the interrupt stack (MSP), which nested interrupt levels and the start-up share: before, it overwrote .heap and the general .bss (RTE, deferred event box) without any detection Detection MPU region read-only outside the safety shell; any write from elsewhere is a bus fault on the access itself. Static rule and ELF check keep reporters outside the protected RAM. : a guard of 1 KB directly below the MSP (linker .stack_guard, 32-byte aligned) with its own descriptor (core: read, no write), cut out of the full-access region that contains it (the SYSMPU grants an access if any descriptor grants it). The first push or exception frame that crosses __StackLimit writes into the guard. The guard is at least the largest frame on the MSP plus the larger of that frame and an exception frame, so no frame reserved without a write lets a write jump over it (checked by tools/stackuse, isr_stack_guard_bytes) Reaction fault exception → SM-17 (walk, dump, reset) Times on the faulty access (hardware) + exception entry + walk. Minimum FTTI served: exception latency Diagnostic coverage high for writes by the core from outside the shell. Blind spots: while the shell is open all interrupts are suspended, so only the shell's own code can write (by design); accesses by other bus masters are not covered: descriptor 0 (whole address space) grants the DMA (M2) and the ENET (M3, S32K148) rwx, and the SYSMPU grants an access when any valid descriptor grants it, so the "no access" for M2/M3 in the locked gate word and the guard has no effect (finding SFP-F03; open point N3 answered, HSI H10). Caveat of B17: the board reads RGD0_WORD3 = 0 (B17, 2026-10-02) - the valid bit of descriptor 0 is not set after init(), so its M2/M3 rights may not be in effect; until that is settled this analysis keeps the unfavourable reading. No neXtBSW driver enables the DMA or the ENET today (dfa DF-44); the application's data is not protected at all (AoU-17) Latent faults of the mechanism SM-11 (gate state), SM-12 (MPU enabled), SM-13 (descriptors) Evidence safe-supervisor-mpu (write to the protected page trapped by the host MMU; counter-test with the earlier code), safety-context, safety-context-elf, bswgen-mpu; board 2026-09-21 (fifth part): the earlier write from the RTE task into the protected RAM was trapped on the target (bus fault → HardFault → reset) — an unintended but real proof of the detection. safety-gate (guard descriptor on the MPU register model: every word of the guard readable, not writable by the core, heap below and stack above writable), application-linker (guard directly below the stack, size, alignment, rejected sizes), stackuse-demo (guard size against the largest frame, sizes equal to the linker symbols) Residual / action N3 (rights of the DMA/ENET master) →: before the first such user restrict descriptor 0 for M2/M3 and grant the master only the regions it needs; until then a configuration that enables one must be refused. The guard write of the core may be an imprecise bus fault (buffered write); a fault during the exception entry of the hard fault itself can lock the core up, which ends in a reset (RCM_SRS[LOCKUP], counted by the reset-loop limit) without the line - both to be seen on the board (inject mspoverflow, test build). Board (issue 2): 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-03 (suite case BT-S2-07): MSP use 744 of 4 096 B, guard 1 024 B; inject mspoverflow gives HARD FAULT RESET: interrupt stack overflow (guard), outputs off with the dump and reset loop 1 of 3 - the guard write was caught. DMA writes into the guard are not blocked (RGD0 grants the other masters - with the caveat of B17 above)

docs.title: SM-11 — MPU state check on entry and exit
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the gate was left open by a previous cycle or by other code, or is closed when the shell should have opened it Detection mpuStatusCheckOnEnterMonitor / mpuStatusCheckOnLeaveMonitor, every safety cycle Reaction S1 + S2 Times nominal 10 ms, guaranteed 31.25 ms Diagnostic coverage medium: complete for the gate bit, but sampled at the cycle boundaries; a gate opened and closed again between two cycles is not seen (the write it allowed is not undone) Latent faults of the mechanism none Evidence safety-gate: real SafetyManager::cyclic, gate (MemoryProtection.cpp, ProtectedRamScopedUnlock.h) and supervisor on an MPU register model with the descriptors of MemoryProtection::init() — gate left open, lost closing write and every single flipped bit of the gate word reported on entry before the first check, gate closed in the cycle and lost opening write reported on exit; safety-gate-mutations (9 built-in faults, all detected); reaction safe-supervisor Residual / action — (F15 closed for this mechanism by an earlier change); the sampling blind spot stays

docs.title: SM-12 — MPU enabled and complete
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the MPU is switched off, or reports fewer region descriptors than the derivative has Detection mpu::isGlobalEnabled() and hasRegionsOfDerivative() against NX_MPU_REGIONS (mcudb), every safety cycle; context = CESR Reaction MPU_NOT_ENABLED → S1 + S2 Times nominal 10 ms, guaranteed 31.25 ms; while the MPU is off, SM-10 does not protect — the window is this detection time Diagnostic coverage high for the enable and the descriptor count (both read from the hardware every cycle against a derivative fact) Latent faults of the mechanism none needed Evidence bswgen-mpu (MpuHostTest, derivative facts), reaction safe-supervisor Residual / action —

docs.title: SM-13 — MPU region descriptors unchanged
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered a region descriptor overwritten (start, end, access rights, valid bit) Detection areRegionsConfiguredCorrectly() compares every safety cycle: descriptor 0 (WORD2 against REGION0_ACCESS, the constant init() writes), descriptors 1 … 7 (start, end, WORD2, valid bit) and the unused descriptors up to NX_MPU_REGIONS − 1 (not valid); context = failing region, 0 for descriptor 0. WORD2 is compared in every field the S32K1 implements (bus masters 0 … 3 and M0PE/M1PE, 0x007DFFFF); the reserved bits 17/23 and the enables of the masters 4 … 7, which the S32K1 does not implement ([RM13] 15.1.2), are left out. : before, descriptor 0 was never read and WORD2 was compared in the fields of M0 … M2 only (0x0001FFFF, findings SFP-F02/F04) Reaction MPU_CONFIGURATION_ERROR → S1 + S2 Times nominal 10 ms, guaranteed 31.25 ms Diagnostic coverage high: every implemented field of every descriptor in use against the expected value; not covered: RGD0_WORD0/1/3 (fixed whole address space; its valid bit after init() is board check B17). The expected values of descriptors 1 … 7 are computed by init() into the protected RAM (.mpu_bss of the safety library, write-protected outside the shell, ECC SM-15); REGION0_ACCESS, the access words and the masks are constants in flash (SM-14, SM-16) Latent faults of the mechanism none needed Evidence bswgen-mpu; reaction safe-supervisor. safety-gate (guard descriptor with full access written into it or its valid bit cleared → configuration error; a guard no full-access region contains and an empty guard → error naming descriptor 6). safe-memory-mpu-regions and -16 (8 and 16 descriptors; reserved bits read as written and as 0: every one of the 22 field bits of descriptor 0 and of descriptors 1 … 7 detected and named, the write of StaticBsp through RGDAAC0 changes nothing, descriptor 0 reported first), safe-memory-mpu-regions-mutations (15 built-in faults, among them the state before a later change and a comparison of the unimplemented M4 … M7 bits) Residual / action board check B17 passed 2026-10-02 (8.1): no MPU_CONFIGURATION_ERROR in 60 s, RGD0_WORD2 & 0x007DFFFF = 0x007C77D8, the descriptors in use as expected; RGD0_WORD3 reads 0 - the valid bit of descriptor 0 is not set after init(), so the M2/M3 rights of descriptor 0 may not be in effect; HSI H10, N3 and SM-10 carry this caveat since an earlier change (CM-02 re-check BRD a); the restriction of descriptor 0 stays

docs.title: SM-14 — ROM check (CRC-32 over the flash areas)
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the program image in flash is not the one that was linked: multi-bit corruption beyond what the flash ECC detects, a partially erased or partially programmed area, a different image. Since an earlier change also the calibration segment (memory.calibration) during operation, against its own reference: it is not in the list (a dataset may be flashed or generated without a build, and the build reference would hold the ECU before the start-up check of ecu/calibration could apply on_invalid, board 2026-09-28), and every pass runs the owner's check (RomCheck::setOwnAreaCheck, calibration::recheckSegment: header CRC, values CRC, header unchanged since the start-up check accepted it). Not covered: the checksum list and the reference themselves (the bootloader's CRC covers them, SM-51), the bootloader, flash outside the image, the data flash, a calibration segment the start-up check did not accept (refused, replaced by the defaults, or used under on_invalid: warn: not in use or knowingly used) Detection since an earlier change: in the idle context, first after lifecycle level 2 (component romcheck): plausibility of the list, then CRC-32 through the CRC unit over the five areas (demo: 197 044 bytes at a separate task), compared with __checksum_result written by the post-link step. Since an earlier change every pass starts with a known-answer test of the CRC unit (five fixed words, expected 0x498CFAA3, the value of the Python model of the post-link step), and the pass is repeated by the idle handler of the application with the period modules.safeMemory.rom_check_period_ms (start to start; default 60 000 ms; 0 = once per start). No pass starts while a flash write is open (RomCheckFlashWrites, bracketed by every NvM write through nvm::FlashWriteBracket) or a flash command runs (FTFC FSTAT[CCIF] clear); a pass during which one began is discarded without a report and repeated Reaction mismatch, implausible list, failed known-answer test (ROMCHECK_UNIT_FAILED), no pass possible for more than one period because of flash writes (ROMCHECK_OVERDUE) or the calibration segment off its own reference (ROMCHECK_OWN_AREA_FAILED) → ROM_CHECK_FAILURE → S1 held. For the segment this is the run-time reaction only; at start-up the calibration check applies on_invalid (refuse: application functions stopped, UDS and canflash reachable), which is also what the power cycle after a hold leads to Times at start-up, after lifecycle level 2, plus the CRC run: about 3 … 6 ms computed (43 049 words at a few core cycles per word at 80 MHz, flash wait states assumed; the demo image has grown to 49 261 words by an earlier change, about 3.5 … 7 ms by the same estimate), not measured (F3, board checklist B1). Between the start and the end of the check the application already runs. Re-check since an earlier change: a corruption after the first pass is found within one period plus one pass (default 60 s); while flash writes keep the pass off, within two periods plus one pass at most, otherwise ROMCHECK_OVERDUE. Period 0: no re-check, a corruption after the check is found at the next start Diagnostic coverage high for the image content at the time of the check (every flash byte of the image is inside an area or is the list, enforced by the build; a CRC-32 detects every error of up to three bits and every burst of up to 32 bits in these lengths, and misses other patterns with a probability of about 2⁻³²). As a run-time mechanism high with a re-check period (the latent interval is the period), low with period 0 (once per start, F3). The calibration segment gets the same: CRC-32 of zlib over header and values (same detection properties), every single bit flip found (host), same period; with period 0 its start-up check is the once-per-start pass Latent faults of the mechanism since an earlier change the known-answer test before every pass detects a CRC unit that returns a fixed value (e.g. the reference) or computes with a wrong polynomial or configuration. A flash write indicator stuck at "writing" (a writer that never ends its write, or a wild write into the indicator, which lies in ordinary RAM on purpose) postpones the pass; the deadline of one period turns that into ROMCHECK_OVERDUE instead of a silently disabled check — except with period 0, where the first pass waits as long as the write lasts. The CRC unit is reserved for SM-14 (no other user in the repository; a second user would have to be serialised with the pass). A false alarm is excluded by construction (concept 6.2 notes); a flash write during a pass discards the pass instead of reporting it Evidence rom-check (every single-bit flip detected, implausible lists refused without touching the CRC unit; since an earlier change the period with its own test profile, wrap-around, period 0, a corruption found by the re-check, known-answer test against a stuck unit and a lost polynomial bit, postponement and discard during flash writes and commands, the deadline, the pass outside the safety shell), rom-check-mutations (17 mutants of RomCheck.cpp and the indicator, all detected), nvm-flash-write-bracket (every NvM write and no read inside the bracket), rom-check-image (post-link step, synthetic images, the real linker template), safe-supervisor (reaction); board 2026-09-21 (eighth part): valid image passes, an image with one changed character is accepted by the bootloader and held in the safe state by SM-14; finding (console line missing when the hold comes from the idle context). rom-check (own-area check after the list, flip found by the re-check, not asked when the list fails, discarded with a flash write), calibration-segment (every bit flip of header and values, refused segment not armed, other dataset valid, changed segment), rom-check-image and target-calibration (five areas, the segment outside the list, another dataset and a damaged header keep the build reference valid) Residual / action F3 decided in section 5.1; T5 done by an earlier change (host). The software CRC of the segment check has no known-answer test of its own - the start-up check computes the same CRC and must have found the segment valid before the run-time check is armed; board repetition of a separate task point 3 open. Board (issue 2): one pass at most 5 574 µs (B1, 2026-09-22); the re-check ran every period on the target (B9, 2026-09-22/23: 13 passes in 26 s with a 2 s period, 60 s spacing on the demo; suite case BT-RUN-07 2026-10-02). Open: the suspension during a real program-flash write on the target (the NvM writes of B9 wrote nothing; possible after PGMPART); a lower bound for a period other than 0 (longer than the longest flash write) is only documented in the parameter, not checked by tools/nxconfig

docs.title: SM-15 — ECC double-bit error, RAM
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered an uncorrectable (double-bit) error in SRAM Detection ERM->SR0 non-correctable bits (NCE0, NCE1 where present) polled every safety cycle; since an earlier change through safe_memory::takeEccErrors(), which reads ERM_SR0 and FTFC_FERSTAT[DFDIF] once, keeps the address of the RAM error (EARn) and clears exactly the flags it read (write 1 to clear) before the report. The reference manual (S32K1xx RM Rev. 13, 22.4.1/22.4.2) confirms that the ERM records non-correctable and single-bit events in SR0 independently of the enables in ERM->CR0 (which only route them to an interrupt), so the poll detects without neXtBSW setting CR0. What the read itself does differs per core (S32K1xx RM Rev. 13, Table 31-5; corrected the earlier expectation of a bus fault): on the S32K14x the core's read completes without a fault exception (only the ERM interrupt, if enabled), on the S32K11x it ends in a hard fault (→ SM-17) — the poll is the route the concept relies on Reaction INTEGRITY_EVENT_DMA_ECC_ERROR → S1 + S2; since an earlier change with the source in the context word (bit 0 RAM channel 0, bit 1 RAM channel 1, bit 2 flash) and the RAM address in the log. The event is still shared with SM-16 and keeps its name (the documents name it), although it is RAM and flash, not DMA Times nominal 10 ms, guaranteed 31.25 ms after the faulty read; a cell that is not read is not checked at all Diagnostic coverage medium for errors in memory that is read: ECC with single-error correction and double-error detection flags every one- and two-bit error in a word; errors of more bits are not guaranteed. Blind spots: memory that is not read (no scrubbing — latent). Start-up RAM test: decided not in a separate task — the startup writes the whole SRAM (ECC initialisation); a March test would be a task of its own. Single-bit corrections are counted since an earlier change (eccCorrectionCount()) and cleared without a reaction, so a degrading cell is visible in the diagnostics, though not reported as an event Latent faults of the mechanism F11 closed by an earlier change: (a) the flags are cleared before the report, so the reaction (reset) starts clean whatever the reset does with the ERM — no reset loop, and a second error is reported again (no masking); an event between reading and clearing survives, because only the read flags are cleared; (b) SR0 records without CR0 (reference manual, above). A decoder or an ERM record that stopped working would stay latent until the error it should catch — since an earlier change tested at every start by SM-55 Evidence safe-memory-ecc (real IntegrityEccHandler.cpp and safe_memory::cyclic against ERM and FTFC register models with write-1-to-clear; mutants: ERM flags not cleared, all ERM flags cleared, flash flag not cleared, no context); reaction safe-supervisor Residual / action board check B5 (for the record only — the behaviour no longer depends on the reset behaviour of the ERM): run 2026-09-24, ERM registers 0 before and after safety wdg - it shows only that no flag survives a reset; the detection with an injected error is SM-55's

docs.title: SM-16 — ECC double-bit error, flash
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered an uncorrectable error on a program-flash read Detection FTFC->FERSTAT[DFDIF] polled every safety cycle; since an earlier change read and cleared (write 1) by takeEccErrors() before the report, like SM-15 Reaction same event as SM-15 → S1 + S2, context bit 2 (flash) since an earlier change Times as SM-15 Diagnostic coverage medium, same reasoning as SM-15; for the program flash SM-14 adds a complete check at every start and, since an earlier change, once per re-check period Latent faults of the mechanism as SM-15 (flag cleared before the report since an earlier change; F11 closed) Evidence safe-memory-ecc (flash flag with context, cleared, second error reported again); reaction safe-supervisor Residual / action — (F11, F15 closed for this mechanism by an earlier change); the latent faults of the flash ECC itself are not tested (SM-55)

docs.title: SM-55 — Latent-fault test of the RAM ECC
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the SEC-DED decoder of an SRAM array no longer corrects or no longer detects, or the ERM no longer records its events or records a wrong address — a latent fault that disables SM-15 without any symptom Detection since an earlier change once per start in main(), after the watchdog self-test and the reset-loop limit and before the BSP (no DMA, no interrupt, no task): safe_memory::eccLatentTestAtStart(). Per ECC channel of the derivative (ERM/EIM channel = one SRAM array, S32K1xx RM Rev. 13 Tables 21-1, 22-1: S32K14x SRAM_L and SRAM_U, S32K11x SRAM_U) one reserved word of the image in that array (nxEccLatentTestWordFirst in the hot bss, nxEccLatentTestWordLast in the no-init RAM; the address decides the channel, a channel without a word fails). The word gets a pattern (fresh check bits); the EIM inverts bits only on the read path. (1) one data bit inverted: the value read must be the pattern, the ERM must record a single-bit correction of that channel and no non-correctable event, EARn = the word; (2) two data bits: a non-correctable event with the word's address (S32K14x only — the Cortex-M0+ takes such a read as a hard fault). Then the descriptor back to 0, a plain read must return the pattern without a record. Precondition: EIM off and no record of the channel — a real record stays for the SM-15 poll and the test does not pass. The injected read is one register-only sequence with all interrupts and faults masked (Cortex-M4: FAULTMASK plus CCR.BFHFNMIGN; M0+: PRIMASK); read-backs and barriers put the enable before and the disable after the read. ERM_CR0 of the channel is off during the test and restored after the record was cleared, so neither the ERM interrupt nor the cyclic poll ever sees the test's own events Reaction INTEGRITY_EVENT_DMA_ECC_ERROR with context ECC_SOURCE_LATENT_TEST (bit 3), failed checks in bits 17..8, channel in bits 27..24 → S1 + S2; the reset counts for the reset-loop limit, so a permanent fault ends in S1 held after the configured number of starts (SM-50/SSR-065). Pass: console line RAM ECC latent test (EIM) passed, n channel(s) Times at start; about 40 register accesses per channel, estimated below 50 µs for two channels at 80/40 MHz (not measured; the console line of the pass takes longer, about 4 ms at 115200 baud). Latent interval = the time between two starts (AoU-25 applies as for SM-07) Diagnostic coverage high for the decoder and record paths exercised: data-bit correction, double-bit detection and the ERM's flag and address per array. Not exercised: the check-bit inputs of the decoder, every other data-bit position, and the S32K11x double-bit detection (a DMA read would be needed). The flash ECC has no injection module: without erasing or programming only the reporting path could be exercised (FTFC_FERCNFG[FDFD] forces FERSTAT[DFDIF], reference manual 36.4.4.1.12) — not implemented, because it sets the flag on every flash read while active and its side effects on instruction fetch are not confirmed on the board; the decoder itself needs a flash word whose check bits do not match its data, and the flash controller generates the check bits when it programs - such a word can only come from erasing and programming (for example a deliberately interrupted or repeated programming of one phrase), which the start-up test must not do. Flash latent faults stay open (remainder, MCU safety manual) Latent faults of the mechanism the test itself runs once per start; an EIM that does not switch off is checked after every injected read and switched off; an injected read that is not register-only is checked on the linked image Evidence safe-memory-ecc-latent, safe-memory-ecc-latent-s32k11x (real EccLatentTest.cpp against EIM/ERM register models, S32K14x and S32K11x layout; every modelled hardware fault found with its check and channel, EIM off after every run, CR0 masked and restored, precondition, coverage), safe-memory-ecc-latent-mutations (25 mutants), safe-memory-ecc-latent-elf (placement of the words, register-only window) Residual / action board (issue 2): 2026-09-29 the start line RAM ECC latent test (EIM) passed, 2 channel(s) at every start, 16 min without a reset; 2026-09-30 an injected fault gives the reaction (cause 0x107; the missing SAFETY RESET line became, fixed and board-passed the same evening); suite case BT-START-01 2026-10-02 (ecc_channels=2). Open: flash ECC latent faults; the MCU safety manual's software measures (remainder, N2)

docs.title: SM-17 — Fault handlers with dump
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered any fault exception: bus fault (including MPU violations of SM-10 and ECC errors on access), usage fault, hard fault, watchdog warning interrupt Detection the core's exceptions Reaction first the safe outputs walk from assembler (R0–R3 only, no stack, no RAM), then the dump, then the reset. : before the C part, HardFault_Handler_Final (naked) compares the MSP with __StackLimit; below it (overflow into the guard of SM-10) the MSP is recorded and moved back to __StackTop, and nxIsrStackOverflowFinal writes HARD FAULT RESET: interrupt stack overflow (guard), outputs off before the reset - otherwise the first push of the C part would fault again inside the handler. : the watchdog's pre-reset interrupt (vector 38 on S32K1) takes the same path; nxHardFaultFinal reads the exception number of a valid dump and writes WATCHDOG RESET: outputs off, dump saved for it, every other record keeps HARD FAULT RESET: ... Times exception entry + walk (< 1 µs computed). Minimum FTTI served: exception latency Diagnostic coverage high for faults that raise an exception. A fault inside the handler before the walk would lock up the core; the lockup ends in a reset whose pin state is AoU-07's Latent faults of the mechanism the handler code and the table are in flash (SM-14 at start, SM-16) Evidence safe-outputs-order (disassembly of both architectures and of the demo ELF: table walked before dump and output, vectors 3 and 38 and the LPIT vector), hard-fault-dump; board 2026-09-18 (watchdog warning path) and 2026-09-21 (finding: HardFault → reset on the target). kernel-fault-reaction (overflow line with and without transmitter, ordinary line without record), freertos-config-elf (HardFault_Handler_Final without stack use, branches to both C parts, each with two flushes, one line, the reset), hold-console-elf (rule 5 for nxIsrStackOverflowFinal); board 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-03 (the overflow line before the reset, SM-10) Residual / action the read-back of S1 is not called in the fault handlers' path yet (G1 rest, SM-23 below, SSR-060 partial)

docs.title: SM-60 — Lock of the FlexNVM block
docs.text:
(decision of the safety responsible in the safety review of 2026-10-01, point: one lock for the NvM and the readers). Proposed, not credited (as SM-58 and SM-59): it claims nothing until the safety responsible decides. The FlexNVM block does one thing at a time; a data-flash read during an erase, a program, an EEPROM store of the NvM or a CSEc command returns undefined data ([RM13] 36.5.7). The hardware shows a running command (CCIF 0) and a running store (EEERDY 0), but not a reader in the middle of its accesses. The family module platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspFlexNvm (flexnvm/FlexNvmBlockLock.h) makes data-flash readers and EEPROM stores exclude each other.

Field Content Faults considered a data-flash read overlaps a flash command or an EEPROM store started by another task (same priority in its time slice, or higher) and returns undefined bytes the reader takes as valid data (NvM data area, calibration segment, a map read in place). Of the mechanism itself: a reader that bypasses the lock (pointer reads outside the family port), a CSEc command that ignores a hold, a hold that is never released, an unbalanced release Detection not a detector, an exclusion. read() copies in sections of 32 bytes, each with interrupts locked and the block checked idle in the same section, so neither a store nor a command can fall into a section; a store begun between two sections that still runs ends read() with BUSY; while a read() runs no data-flash command starts. A read in place takes a hold (IDataFlash::holdForDirectRead(), RAII dataflash::DirectRead), granted only on an idle block; while a hold exists no EEPROM store and no data-flash command starts. Stores never wait for a read() (no priority inversion through read()). RDCOLERR stays as the second line Reaction read() returns BUSY instead of undefined data (the caller retries); a store under a hold waits as for a running command, at most COMMAND_WAIT_LIMIT_US = 260 ms, then the write fails and the NvM reports it - it never collides; in the run-down the gate of the family port grants no new hold Times interrupt lock per section: 32 bytes from the data flash, a few µs (not measured on a board - the lock times measured on 2026-10-03 are those of a separate task, N6, another lock); a store delayed by a hold: at most 260 ms Diagnostic coverage not claimed. It prevents the collision rather than detecting it, for the readers of the family port (read() and holds through AreaService) Latent faults of the mechanism an unbalanced release is counted (unbalanced()), not under-run; held-off launches, waits for a hold and time-outs are counted and shown in the test build (dflash show) Evidence flexnvm-s32k1xx (register model: a store between two sections ends read() with BUSY, a command start during read() is refused, every section with interrupts locked, a store under a hold waits and fails at the limit or stores once after the release, no hold during a running command or store, limit of 255 holds; 66 mutants), nvm-data-flash (admission and direct read, 26 mutants), data-flash-system (hold through the gate, no new hold in the run-down, 15 mutants); board 2026-10-02 with a separate task (passed; 8 cover, 3 and 6, 4, 5 and 7 are not recorded on their own; captures not in the repository) Residual / action (1) readers by pointer outside the family port do not take the hold yet (the calibration segment in the profile production of memory.calibration, an XCP upload from the data flash) - follow-up task; until then the collision of a separate task remains there; (2) CSEc commands (bspCsec) do not check a hold: they run with interrupts locked and check CCIF, so they never hit a section of read(), but they can hit a hold; (3) a hold taken by a task of lower priority than a task that stores into the EEPROM can make that store fail after 260 ms (reported, never colliding) - assumption of use AoU-40; (4) a hold that exists when the run-down starts ends only at its holder; (5) board proof

docs.title: SM-18 — ADC reference supervision
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered VREFH drifted, so every analogue measurement is wrong by the same factor Detection bandgap channel (nominal 1000 mV) read every safety cycle; VREFH computed from it; compared with board.adc_reference_mv ± modules.safeSystem.adc_reference_tolerance_mv (demo: 4096 ± 200 mV) Reaction ADC_REFERENCE_ERROR, context 1 → S1 + S2 Times nominal 10 ms, guaranteed 31.25 ms Diagnostic coverage medium. A drift beyond the band is found every cycle. Blind spots: (a) the reference of the check is the on-chip bandgap — a bandgap error shifts the computed VREFH and can mask or fake a drift; its accuracy is a data-sheet value that is not in the repository; (b) a drift inside the band is a silent gain error of up to 200 mV in 4096 mV on every analogue value of the ECU (demo values), which may already exceed what a safety-related measurement tolerates (F16) Latent faults of the mechanism read failures: SM-19 Evidence safe-system (decision logic against stubs), bswgen (profile testproject_adc_reference), nxconfig; no board fault injection recorded Residual / action F16 → AoU-24 (section 6; issue 1: proposed - binding since concept issue 3, concept 4.3, CM-07 ZG; F16 accepted, register AN-016)

docs.title: SM-19 — ADC read failure limit
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the bandgap conversion fails permanently, so the reference can no longer be supervised Detection consecutive failed readings counted; the event fires once at adc_read_error_limit (default 10) Reaction ADC_REFERENCE_ERROR, context 2 → S1 + S2 Times nominal 100 ms, guaranteed 312.5 ms Diagnostic coverage high for a permanent failure of the bandgap conversion. Intermittent failures shorter than the limit are tolerated by design Latent faults of the mechanism none needed Evidence safe-system (failed reading) Residual / action —

docs.title: SM-20 — Internal supply supervision
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the MCU's 3.3 V flash, 3.3 V oscillator or 1.2 V core supply out of range Detection SIM supply monitor multiplexed over 6 safety cycles (select, measure), ± 200 mV around the nominal value, scaled with the measured VREFH. Since an earlier change failed readings of the supply channel are counted in a row with the same limit as the bandgap, modules.safeSystem.adc_read_error_limit (demo 10 cycles); a good reading ends the series, a missing reference does not count (that is SM-19) Reaction INTERNAL_SUPPLIES_ERROR → S1 + S2; after adc_read_error_limit failed readings once with context 2 ("no measurement") Times nominal 60 ms per supply, guaranteed 187.5 ms; a permanently failing supply channel: nominal 100 ms, guaranteed 312.5 ms (as SM-19) Diagnostic coverage low to medium. The same ± 200 mV band is narrow for the 3.3 V supplies but one sixth of the nominal value for the 1.2 V core supply, which is wide for a core supply. The value depends on the measured VREFH (common cause with SM-18). A permanently failing supply channel is reported since an earlier change (F14 closed); intermittent failures shorter than the limit are tolerated by design. The MCU's own hardware low-voltage detection is not part of this mechanism; since an earlier change it is switched on by the family port as the separate hardware mechanism SM-59 (not credited), which watches VDD itself Latent faults of the mechanism loss of the measurement: the read-failure limit above (diagnostic value consecutiveSupplyErrors, console safeadc stats) Evidence safe-system (decision logic; since an earlier change the read-failure limit: event at the limit, series reset by a good reading, missing reference not counted — each with a mutant) Residual / action — (F14 closed by an earlier change); a failing supply channel cannot be provoked on the board

docs.title: SM-21 — Safety register lock
docs.text:
Issue 2 (CM-02 decision Z1, gap analysis measure M7): issue 1 analysed the OpenBSW demonstration - one pin locked and read back. Since an earlier change the lock list is generated from the configuration (tools/bswgen, class PIN_FUNCTION), and the block below describes that mechanism; the issue-1 statements are kept where they still hold.

Field Content Faults considered the function of a pin the safe state relies on is changed after start: a PWM pin of a used group, a safe_off output or the role pin remuxed to another function or to GPIO (wild write, a driver that reconfigures it); a lock that did not take (write lost, PCR[LK] stuck at 0). Not considered: registers other than the pin control (that is SM-22), a pin outside the list Detection SafeIo::init() writes the configured function and sets PCR[LK] for every entry of the lock list - the pins of the used PWM groups, every safe_off output and the role pin (safety.locked_pin) - and reads back function (MUX) and lock bit of each once (since an earlier change including LK) Reaction LOCK_REGISTER_ERROR with the pin in the context → S1 + S2 Times start-up only; a locked PCR cannot be changed until the next reset, so the lock prevents the change after the read-back rather than detecting it Diagnostic coverage medium (issue 1: low - one pin, demonstration scope F4). The whole property - the function of every pin the safe outputs table and the PWM groups use - is locked and read back, by comparison with the configuration, and a lock that did not take is reported. Known blind spots: the check runs once per start (a fault of the read-back path itself is not repeated), the lock covers the pin control only (direction, clock gates, timer and clock registers are SM-22's), and the clock of the pins' peripherals (SYSTEM_CLOCK, HSI H5) is in no list yet - F4 stays open until a follow-up task (AN-004). Whether the class can become high is to be checked after a later change Latent faults of the mechanism the lock cannot be undone by software until the next reset; the read-back of every start re-verifies it Evidence safe-io: real SafeIo.cpp, bspIo driver and supervisor on a PORT register model with the PCR lock — every function other than GPIO (set before, locked before, MUX bit stuck) and a lock that did not take are reported with the pin id; safe-io-mutations (built-in faults for SM-21/SM-22, all detected); bswgen-safe-io (the generated lists of every profile against an independent expectation, generator mutants); reaction safe-supervisor. Board: B8 passed 2026-09-22 (role pin LK = 1, MUX = 001, no LOCK_REGISTER_ERROR at the start); the generated list of a separate task on the board 2026-09-22 Residual / action F4 rest → (SYSTEM_CLOCK); re-rating to high after a later change

docs.title: SM-22 — Safety register check
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered a safety-relevant register drifted during operation: pin function (class PIN_FUNCTION), direction of a safe_off GPIO (GPIO_DIRECTION), clock gate of a timer or port in the safe outputs table (CLOCK_GATE), the configuration of a PWM timer (PWM_TIMER: the registers the PWM driver writes once - SC, MOD, CNTIN, COMBINE, POL, INVCTRL, CONF.BDMMODE and the dead times of the used pairs; the software output control word is the read-back of SM-23, not this list), and since an earlier change the low-voltage reset of SM-59 (SUPERVISION, PMC_LVDSC1) Detection SafeIo compares every entry of the generated check list with its expected value under its mask every safety cycle (27 entries on the demo at a separate task, plus PMC_LVDSC1 since an earlier change); issue 1: the direction of one pin Reaction CHECK_REGISTER_ERROR with class and index in the context → S1 without reset, latched until the next init(); for the role pin's indicator the return releases it (AoU-30) Times nominal 10 ms, guaranteed 17 ms since an earlier change (issue 1: 31.25 ms) Diagnostic coverage medium (issue 1: low - one bit of one register, F4). The whole register set the safe state relies on is compared with the configuration at a fixed interval. Known blind spots: the check samples once per safety cycle (a change and its reversal between two cycles is not seen; a changed register acts until the next cycle), and the class SYSTEM_CLOCK (SCG configuration, HSI H5) is missing - a wrong system clock is seen only through its effects (SM-04 against the LPO, SM-01) - F4 stays open until a follow-up task (AN-004). Whether the class can become high is to be checked after a later change Latent faults of the mechanism none of its own; a stopped safety task stops the check (SM-01, SM-04) Evidence safe-io (detection on a GPIO register model — output via PDDR, disabled input via PIDR, reconfiguration through the driver; once per change, the return releases the indicator, neighbouring pins silent; since an earlier change every class of the list; since an earlier change the byte register PMC_LVDSC1), safe-io-mutations, bswgen-safe-io (the generated list per profile against an independent expectation), safe-supervisor, safe-state-hold (S1 held against drivers that want to switch on); board 2026-09-21 (safety dst stops the square wave, DRV_EN and LED; KL30B at 0 A for 6 s, kl30b on refused); board 2026-09-22 (the list in normal operation, no false report); board 2026-10-01 (PMC_LVDSC1 written 0x00/0x30 gives CHECK_REGISTER_ERROR, S1 without reset) Residual / action F4 rest → (SYSTEM_CLOCK; the alternative of DFA-2, SIRCVLD, with it). : the reaction "release the indicator" switches safety.safe_state_output back with the level the application last wrote, and the mechanism relies on a locked_pin no driver reconfigures and a test_pin that is unconnected — assumption of use AoU-30 (concept section 4.2); nxconfig warns when the application writes the indicator

docs.title: SM-59 — Low-voltage detect reset
docs.text:
anomaly AN-066, finding H9 of hsi-s32k1xx.md, decision of the safety responsible 2026-09-30. A hardware mechanism of the MCU that the family port s32k1xx configures: boardInit() writes PMC_LVDSC1 = 0x10 (LVDRE on, LVDIE off, LVDACK not written) in every start (platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/include/pmc/LowVoltageDetectReset.h). Not credited (as SM-58): whether a hardware mechanism counts for stage 1 is the decision of the safety responsible; coverage statements for the MCU's own hardware stay with the integrator and the MCU safety manual (N2, AoU-09, AoU-36).

Field Content Faults considered VDD falls below the specified range (supply, wiring, a load step, a brown-out at switch-off) while the MCU keeps executing: below about 2.7 V the data sheet degrades ADC, comparator, pins and communication, so every analogue check (SM-18 … SM-20) and every output may act on wrong values. Of the mechanism itself: LVDRE not written (port without, a start path that bypasses boardInit()), cleared later (bit flip, a write by other code), the interrupt enabled instead (the shared vector is DefaultISR), the LVD off in a low-power mode Detection the PMC compares VDD with VLVD (2.80 … 3.00 V falling, 50 mV hysteresis; [DS13] table 8) continuously; no instruction involved. Of the mechanism's own faults: since an earlier change PMC_LVDSC1 is in the SafeIo register list (class SUPERVISION, entry PMC_LVDSC1, mask 0x30, expected 0x10, 8-bit read) and compared every safety cycle (SM-22): LVDRE cleared or LVDIE set is CHECK_REGISTER_ERROR, S1 without reset, latched until the next init(); LVDF is not judged Reaction hardware reset with RCM_SRS[LVD]; the MCU is held in reset until VDD is above VLVD plus the hysteresis ([RM13] 25.2.2.2); all pins go to their reset state (AoU-07). The following start counts as power-on: the dump and the reset-loop record are cleared (SM-50) Times the response time of the comparator (hardware, not in the data sheet table); no software time Diagnostic coverage not claimed. Below VLVD the whole MCU is reset, which also ends every software mechanism; between the internal regulators' drop-out and VLVD SM-20 and SM-18 still act (a 5 V board); on a 3.3 V board VLVD lies at most 0.3 V below the nominal supply (AoU-39). Not covered: an over-voltage, a supply in the low-power modes VLPR/VLPS (LVD off, only the LVR), a drop so short that the comparator does not respond Latent faults of the mechanism the reset path is never exercised in normal operation; a lost LVDRE or a set LVDIE is detected within one safety cycle (10 ms nominal, 17 ms guaranteed) by SM-22 Evidence low-voltage-detect-reset (host: the real function on a register model of PMC_LVDSC1 with the supply thresholds at both ends of VLVD - power-on, brown-out to 2.79 V resets and holds, 3.01 V does not, the port without keeps running at 2.71 V, software and watchdog resets without a follow-up reset, 3.3 V board at -5 % and -10 %), low-voltage-detect-reset-mutations (9 mutants of the header), low-voltage-detect-reset-elf (target: boardInit() of the demo stores the byte 0x10 to 0x4007D000 right after the watchdog is disabled, Reset_Handler calls it), safe-io / safe-io-mutations (byte register model, all 256 values against lowVoltageDetectResetOn(), 8 width mutants), bswgen-safe-io (entry in every profile, 7 generator mutants); board: PMC_LVDSC1 reads 0x10 after the start (J-Link 2026-10-02, also halted in the bootloader 2026-10-03), a written 0x00 or 0x30 gives CHECK_REGISTER_ERROR, power-on starts show POR+LVD; the reset at a falling lab supply is not recorded Residual / action (1) board proof with a lab supply (checklist in the changelog of a separate task) - not recorded yet; carried by an earlier change after Release R1, a known gap of Release R1 (CM-02 re-check BRD a, 2026-10-04); (2) closed by an earlier change (cyclic re-check), on the board 2026-10-01; (3) a brown-out loop (the supply sags under load after each start) resets over and over without the reset-loop limit (SM-50) counting it, because a start after LVD clears the record - as before with the LVR, now already below VLVD; (4) the bootloader runs after power-on with LVDRE = 0 until the application starts (the bootloader is not changed by an earlier change); (5) the S32K14xW derivatives specify no VLVD (data sheet table 9); they are not in the derivative database, and adding one needs a decision whether the write stays

docs.title: 3.4 Outputs and the safe state (concept 6.5)
docs.text: SM-23 … SM-25 are reactions. They are judged by whether they take effect, not by coverage. SM-58 is a reaction with a detection half of its own and is not credited.

docs.title: SM-23 — Safe outputs table, one list for three paths
docs.text:
Field Content Faults considered (of the mechanism) an output that should be de-energised is not in the table (AoU-06, SM-24); a table entry corrupted (flash: SM-14, SM-16); a peripheral with gated clock is skipped by design — if a fault gated the clock of an FTM while its outputs were active, the walk leaves those pins at whatever level the module leaves them; the walk wrote but the pin did not follow (G1) Reaction PWM groups to their inactive level via SWOCTRL, safe_off outputs inactive, dsb Times < 1 µs, computed (F8); on the board the walk from the timer to the gate-driver enable is bounded at ≤ 21 µs (B3, oscilloscope 2026-09-22, 8.1), which does not resolve the computed value Effectiveness covered with limits: works for every caller, verified on the board for the demo's two outputs; since an earlier change SafeIo reads back every entry (software output control, pin level of every safe_off output) in every safety cycle while S1 is latched and resets (S1 + S2, LOCK_REGISTER_ERROR, class SAFE_OUTPUT) if S1 did not take effect - host only Evidence safe-state, safe-state-hold, debug-halt-guard, safe-outputs-order, safe-io and safe-io-mutations (read-back, 9 mutants), bswgen-safe-readback; board 2026-09-21 Residual / action Issue 2: S1 held, the groups of SD and the S1 + S2 sequence are read back since an earlier change (the block below); G1 rest: the fault handlers' and the halt deadman's path, board proof B15/B16 (B15 run ad hoc in the board session of 2026-09-30, the task list captures in the repository since an earlier change (8.2) - to be repeated with records as suite case BT-S1-03, which is on the board list of Release R1; B16 not run: (b) with BT-S1-03, (a), (c), (d) after Release R1 with a separate task, a known gap of Release R1, CM-02 re-check BRD a). Issue 1 text: G1 rest (covers S1 only): no read-back in S1 held (no task runs; the hold re-walks every round), for the groups of SD, in the fault handlers' and the halt deadman's path; an entry whose clock is gated is not judged (the pin level of a clock-gated FTM stays unknown); with the input of a pin disabled (reported by SM-22 itself) its level reads 0; board proof B15. F8

The rest of G1 after a later change** (decision of the safety responsible 2026-09-30, review point K6; K5: the reaction stays the reset through LOCK_REGISTER_ERROR). The read-back of a separate task is now one function of the family port (safeSupervisor/SafeStateReadback.h, S32K1: SafeIo.cpp) that the safe supervisor uses as well:

Path Before a later change Since an earlier change (host verified, board open: B16) S1 latched, safety task running read back every safety cycle unchanged, but a clock-gated entry is not confirmed (see below) S1 held (watchdog self-test, ROM check, reset-loop limit, device fault IDENTITY) not read back read back in every round of the hold loop, before its walk (what the previous walk left). Not confirmed: LOCK_REGISTER_ERROR (class SAFE_OUTPUT, entry), S1 + S2. The hold loop is the only code that runs (interrupts suspended), so neither the halt deadman nor the idle context can carry the read-back degraded groups SD not read back (no S1 latch) read back in every safety cycle before their walk, only their entries (holdDegradedGroups()); not confirmed: LOCK_REGISTER_ERROR, S1 + S2. Every group degraded is S1 with its latch: SafeIo S1 + S2 of the supervisor (every resetting event, kernel faults, ETL_ASSERT, ECC error from a fault interrupt) walk, record, console line, reset walk, record, read-back; not confirmed: no console line, the reset at once (the line costs up to two flush time-outs plus its transmission, while an output may stay energised); the cause stays in the reset-loop record hard fault / watchdog handlers (customHardFaultHandler, port isr_sys.cpp), halt deadman (LpitHaltDeadman.h) not read back open - outside the paths of a separate task (platforms/s32k1xx/hardFaultHandler, port/main); the function exists and needs neither stack nor RAM beyond its frame, a call in nxHardFaultFinal() before the line is the follow-up. The hard fault path ends in the reset anyway; the deadman path returns and has no latch

Entries whose clock is gated: up to a separate task not judged. Now not confirmed once SafeIo::init() has run: a timer whose clock is gated keeps its outputs frozen where the walk cannot reach them, and the register list of a separate task expects every such gate on (SafeIoRegisterList.cpp checks at compile time that every gate of the read-back list is a CLOCK_GATE entry of the register list expected on). A gated gate after init() was already a register fault (SM-22, S1 without reset); with S1 latched it now ends in S1 + S2, whose reset puts the pins into their reset state. Before SafeIo::init() (the hold from main() before the BSP start, a fault before the safety task) nothing is judged: the pins are in their reset configuration, pin function disabled, driven by nothing - and an active-low safe_off output would read 0 with its input disabled, a false finding. An active short selected for a group (part C of partner-and-degraded.md) is a safe state in every path, as in a separate task.

Residual after a later change: the hold of S1 before SafeIo::init() and every path before it are not read back (reset configuration of the pins, see above); the fault handlers' and the halt deadman's path (see table); a read-back that follows its walk by only a few bus clocks (S1 + S2 sequence) can see a pin level not yet synchronised - it then costs the console line, never the reset; a reset loop of an S1 that never takes effect ends in the reset-loop limit, whose hold then resets again while the fault persists - the pins are in their reset state for most of that loop. Evidence: safe-io (real SafeIo and SafeSupervisor on the register model), safe-io-mutations (7 new mutants), safe-supervisor-degraded (SD, hold and S1 + S2 against a faked port) and safe-supervisor-degraded-mutations (9 new mutants), hold-console-elf on the demo image. Board check B16 (section 8).

The degraded reaction SD uses a subset of this table** (concept section 3, SSR-087, SSR-088). SD is a reaction, not a mechanism of its own: it walks the entries of the mapped safe-output groups (an entry mask derived by nxconfig, the table unchanged, the walk of nxSafeOutputsSwitchOff() with a mask in SafeState::enterDegradedState()), latches the groups and keeps them until the power cycle. The fault handlers and the halt deadman keep walking the whole table: they never degrade.

Field Content Faults considered a fail-safe event degraded (an MCU-internal fault, a wrong part, a malformed or inconsistent report); a group released before the power cycle (a later event, leaving S1, a driver or the debug halt guard rewriting the timer, a reset); the latch or the record corrupted (wild write); the mapping and the table drifting apart; the last working group degraded while the ECU still claims to run Detection not a detector. Guards: the closed list is a code fact, refused by nxconfig with the YAML path and by a static_assert per generated mapping; the report must be well-formed, not IDENTITY and name the configured bus; latch with inverted copy, record with key and check word Reaction only the mapped groups to their safe state, no reset; walked again every safety cycle; record re-applied at every start without power-on; implausible latch or record = every group; last group = S1 without reset Times the walk as S1 for fewer entries; the report to the application within one period of the reading task Effectiveness covered with limits for the PWM channels of a group; see residual Evidence safe-supervisor-degraded (fault injection: corrupted latch and record, lost bus, wrong bus, IDENTITY, malformed word, escalation, starts with and without power-on), safe-supervisor-degraded-mutations (21 mutants detected, 8 fail-safe configurations refused by the compiler), safe-state-degraded (subset walk against the full walk), nxconfig-degraded, rtegen-safety; no board run Residual / action (1) Closed by an earlier change for a bound enable: the safe_off output of a device bound to the group's PWM group (board pwm[].gate_driver) is an entry of the group (nxconfig derives it in the order of the bswgen table, nxconfig-degraded compares both), SD pulls it low with the channels, and its driver is locked while the group is degraded (gateDriverGroupLock, SafeSupervisor::isEntryDegraded: enable refused, no mismatch fault). An enable of a device bound to no PWM group still goes off with S1 alone (nxconfig warns); a gate driver bound to the PWM group of a project always joins, also with another number of pairs than phases (then only the enable rule of the driver is not applied). (2) Closed by an earlier change: after a safety reset the groups are forced before the BSP starts; the PWM driver's initialisation writes the output control of the timer from its configuration (0) - since an earlier change the driver of a locked group (ComplementaryPwm, NX_PWM_GROUP_LOCK, lock = SafeSupervisor::isEntryDegraded of the group's table entry) forces it again inside init(), before the counter starts and before a pin is muxed to the timer, and main() of the family port walks the degraded groups again right after the BSP start (applyDegradedGroups()). Every duty write of a locked group (RTE pwm.<pair>, console pwm set) is refused and forces the output control again; the fast path (FtmPwmGroup::writeDutiesQ15) writes channel values and the software trigger only and cannot release it. (3) Closed by an earlier change: the debug halt guard's release (FtmPwmInhibit::release) keeps a locked group forced; a gate-driver enable of a degraded group is refused anyway. Remaining, stated: the lock reads the supervisor's latch in protected RAM - a wild write that makes it implausible reads as every group degraded (safe direction); the output control register itself can still be rewritten by a wild write, which the hold of the next safety cycle corrects (at most one safety cycle, as before for any register of the table). Evidence: pwm-group-lock (register model, 6 mutants), safe-supervisor-degraded (applyDegradedGroups, entry lock), demo object code unchanged. (4) The record lies in ordinary no-init RAM like the reset-loop record: a wild write of a valid record with more groups degrades more (safe direction), with fewer is corrected from the latch within one cycle. (5) Independence of the groups beyond timer and bus (supply, sensor, connector) is the integrator's, AoU-32. (6) Board run open

Safety reviews of 2026-09-30 (safety responsible).

  • R1 … R12 as recommended. R2 — a mapping that covers every group gives only a warning (escalation to S1 without reset): the warning is enough. R4 — the window of at most one safety cycle was accepted for the time being with a follow-up task (closed since by an earlier change, residuals (2), (3)). R12 — the residuals (1) … (6) above are accepted.
  • G1 … G7 accepted. G1 "all three phases off" counts as allowed (11 of 12 runs without fault, one outlier 0x0800 caught by the short-circuit shut-off of a separate task). G2 the rule acts at the enable only; a later change of the duties into a mixture is protected only by the device's short detection — whether FOC needs more is decided in a separate task. G3 a number of pairs other than the number of phases stays a warning (the warning is enough). G4 a project with an integrated gate driver that does not use its group gets neither a warning nor a source (behaviour as before a later change). G5 decision C2 (a) in its freewheel form only; the active short is a separate task. G6 the lock reads the supervisor's latch; an implausible latch counts as every group locked, a wild write into SWOCTRL is corrected by the next safety cycle or duty write. G7 one PWM group per project (limit of the family port today): every degradation becomes S1 without reset, the group lock takes real effect only with several groups. Open: G8 — when a read-back from CnV is valid is not checked against the reference manual (documented: the answer leads the output by at most one period), to be clarified on the board or in the manual; G9 — board proof (with the maintainer, 24 V power stage, test build) at the next board session.

docs.title: SM-24 — One adapter per safe_off output, enforced at build time
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered a new power output is declared safe_off, but no driver adapter exists, so the driver keeps believing it is on Detection static_assert over NX_SAFE_OFF_OUTPUT_COUNT (bswgen) against the adapters in Integration.cpp Reaction build error Effectiveness high for declared outputs; nothing for undeclared ones (AoU-06) Evidence bswgen (profile testboard_safe_outputs), the target build target-demo Residual / action —

docs.title: SM-25 — De-energise before the reset
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered a bridge keeps switching in the window between the event and the reset Reaction enterSafeState() before softwareSystemReset() for every resetting event Effectiveness high within handle() Evidence safe-supervisor (every resetting event switches off before the reset) Residual / action —

docs.title: SM-26 — Selectable safe state of a PWM group with fallback to freewheel
docs.text:
Optional per project (pwm.<group>.safe_states), concept and decisions: partner-and-degraded.md part C. Like SM-23 a reaction, not a detector: it changes which values the one table walk writes for the entries of a group, in every path that walks it. Issue 1: refused by nxconfig until two follow-ups exist (the supervisor's bridge-fault rule C4 and the family port's hold of the short C2). Issue 2: both exist since earlier changes (the updates below), nxconfig accepts a short, and the start test is called from the port since earlier changes (SM-27). Not credited for Release R1 (catalogue CREDITED: no, CM-07 decision ZD): no class is claimed; CM-02 checked the marking only (decision Z4). The interrupt locks of a separate task around check and write of the selection and the lock of the short were measured on the board on 2026-10-03, all below 5 µs (N6).

Field Content Faults considered (of the mechanism) selection word corrupted (wild write, bit flip) or stale; the pattern of a short the group does not allow written; timer clock gated while a short is selected (the timer entry is skipped - the enable must not stay on alone); a short applied onto a broken switch (shoot-through through one leg); the short pattern not dead-time protected on its way in; the gate-driver enable of the group switched off by another path (the short turns into freewheel); a reset while a short is selected; the walks with and without selection writing different registers; a project without a short compiled differently than before Detection not a detector. Guards: the word must hold exactly one of two 32-bit patterns (16 bits set, complements of each other; 0 after reset = freewheel); the short slot of a state the group does not allow holds the freewheel value (compile-time check against the allowed mask); the group's timer clock gate is read before the word; the extended table is checked at compile time entry by entry against nxSafeOutputs (same registers, same order, same freewheel values); the service writes only allowed, not withdrawn states Reaction per entry of a group: the selected short's value (timer: all channels forced, CHnOCV of one side; bound enable: a store of 0 to its set/clear register, i.e. left as it is) or the freewheel value; entries of no group as SM-23 Times the walk of SM-23 plus, per entry of a group, one read of the timer's clock gate, one read of the word and up to two compares — computed, not measured. The short lasts until the next reset; then the board's reset state (AoU-33) Effectiveness not claimed: host and disassembly verified only; accepted by nxconfig since earlier changes (head paragraph; issue 1: refused in every project until the follow-ups); board proof open Evidence safe-state-select (C walk, S1, SD, service and start test on a register model with two groups: 149 checks, 16 mutants; both assembler handlers linked with the target-compiled table and executed by an interpreter of their Thumb instructions for 8 scenarios, 8 mutants per architecture; the prologue rules of safe-outputs-order for the extended walk), bswgen-safe-state (generated table against an independent expectation from board.yaml, 5 generator mutants, target layout for Cortex-M4 and M0+), nxconfig-safestate (every check with YAML path, code facts); object code of the demo and its product build unchanged (changelog) Residual / action Issue 2: (1) and (2) below are the state of issue 1 - both follow-ups exist since earlier changes (head paragraph), and nxconfig accepts a short. (1) C4 not in the supervisor yet: a DEVICE_FAULT of the classes OUTPUT, SUPPLY, INTERNAL of the group's gate driver must withdraw the short (nxSafeStateBlockShort) before handle() walks the table; follow-up in ecu/safety/safeSupervisor, which then defines NX_SAFE_BRIDGE_FAULT_CLASSES. (2) C2 not in the family port yet: the safe_off adapter of a shorted group's enable must accept "on" in S1 while the short is selected, the halt deadman's guard must not take the enable away nor release/overwrite the short (FtmPwmInhibit), and the PWM group lock must write the selected value instead of freewheel; follow-up in platforms/s32k1xx/port/main and port/bspConfiguration, which then defines NX_SAFE_STATE_SHORT_HOLD. Until both exist nxconfig refuses the short, so neither gap is reachable. (3) The output mask of the timer (OUTMASK) acts after the software output control: a group whose driver has masked its outputs (before the first duty, disableOutputs) stays in freewheel even with a short selected (safe direction; whether the walk should unmask is a question for the follow-up). (4) The forced pattern's dead-time protection and the complementary-mode behaviour of SWOCTRL for one side on are taken from the reference manual's order of the output logic and are not confirmed on the target (PD-5; board item B12). (5) A wild write of exactly one pattern selects that short where the group allows it - the residual of the same kind as the S1 latch. (6) An uncorrectable ECC error in exactly the selection word faults again inside the handler: lockup, reset, board reset state (freewheel later). (7) The word is read per entry, not once per group: a change between the timer's and the enable's entry gives "timer short, enable off" or "timer freewheel, enable on" - both freewheel at the bridge. (8) The selection's RTE port (C6) and the reaction to a refused request (S3) are follow-ups.

Update (2026-09-30, residual (1) closed in the supervisor, host only). safeSupervisor/Degraded.h defines NX_SAFE_BRIDGE_FAULT_CLASSES(X) X(OUTPUT) X(SUPPLY) X(INTERNAL); in a project with a short SafeSupervisor::handle() withdraws the short (nxSafeStateBlockShort, contract safeSupervisor/SafeStateShort.h) of the groups the device of a DEVICE_FAULT of these classes is bound to - first in the case, under the interrupt lock, before the log line, SD, S1 held and S1 + S2 - and of every group for a malformed word (SSR-091). The bound devices are derived by nxconfig (bridge_fault_device_<n>: instance << 8 | selection groups); nxconfig reads the class list and refuses every short while it lacks one of the three. Evidence: safe-supervisor-bridge-fault (334 checks, own profile with three selection groups, three bound devices and an SD mapping), safe-supervisor-bridge-fault-mutations (14 mutants), nxconfig-safestate. New residuals: (9) C4 acts only for devices whose package raises DEVICE_FAULT; today's TMC6200 driver switches its enable off by itself on its shutdown faults (freewheel at the bridge, the selection stays), so the short stays selectable after such a fault until a DEVICE_FAULT comes; (10) COMMUNICATION, CONFIGURATION, DEVICE_RESET and IDENTITY of the bound gate driver keep the short by the decision's list - a gate driver that cannot be read or was reconfigured is not treated as a bridge fault (question for the safety review); (11) a report only (DEVICE_REPORT, S3) never withdraws the short.

Update (2026-09-30, residual (2) closed in the family port, host only). integration/SafeStateHold.h defines NX_SAFE_STATE_SHORT_HOLD(X) X(gdTmc6200); in a project with a short (ShortHold.h, SSR-092): the lock of a TMC6200 bound to the group reads "not locked" while the walks write the short and the driver is enabled (an enable that was off stays off, enable() refused in S1), its adapter keeps DRV_EN after a debug halt and reports it held to the hold of S1; the PWM inhibit (FtmPwmInhibit, on every entry into S1 and after a halt) and the group lock of a separate task (ComplementaryPwm::lockIfDegraded) write the group's selected output control; HwThresholdWatch withdraws the short on a finding or on the timer's fault latch before it forces the group (review C2: the hardware path has priority). nxconfig refuses a short whose bound enable belongs to another module. Evidence: short-hold (119 checks: 10 s of driver cycles in S1 with DRV_EN and the pattern held and no DRV_EN write; driver off stays off; withdrawal, gated clock, corrupted word give freewheel and DRV_EN off within one poll; halt; leaving S1; group lock), short-hold-mutations (9 mutants); safe-state-hold, debug-halt-guard, pwm-group-lock, hw-threshold-monitor unchanged green; demo object code unchanged. New residuals: (12) after S1 is left, or after a halt, the short stays until the application disables and enables the gate driver again (enable() of an enabled driver is no explicit enable, the guard keeps the PWM inhibited - safe direction, but an application must know it); (13) between the hardware path's latch and the next 1 ms poll a walk of the safety task (HW_SHUTOFF) can still write the short pattern into the output control - the fault input overrides it in hardware ([RM] 47.5.15, review C2) and DRV_EN stays on until the poll (to measure, B13 (c)); (14) the generic safe_off adapter of the generated binding keeps no enable - nxconfig refuses such a group; (15) the Integration.cpp composition (lock per bound instance) is covered by the target build and mirrored in the host test, not executed on the host itself.

docs.title: SM-27 — Start-up test of the active short
docs.text:
Building block of the family's handler library (nxSafeStateShortTestBegin/End). Issue 1: the family port did not call it yet. Issue 2: called from RteSystem::init() since an earlier change, after a power-on reset only since an earlier change (update below). Not credited for Release R1 (CM-07 ZD, CM-02 Z4). Its interrupt lock measured on the board 2026-10-03: begin 2.72 µs, end 2.08 µs at the pin (DWT 2.2 µs and 1.5 µs; N6).

Field Content Faults considered (of the mechanism) the timer's software output control does not take the pattern (register stuck, clock off, write lost); the value before the test not restored; the test run twice or ended without a start; a failed test that leaves the short selectable Detection the pattern read back from the forcing register right after the store; the restored value read back; sequence and clock of the group's timer checked before anything is forced Reaction failure: the short is withdrawn for the power cycle and freewheel forced on the tested entries; the caller raises the event (proposed SAFE_STATE_TEST_FAILURE, degradable) Times at start: the configured pwm.<group>.safe_state_test_us plus a few register accesses Effectiveness not claimed: register level only - it proves the forcing register, not the gate driver, the switches or the phase voltages; issue 1: no call from the port yet - called from RteSystem::init() since earlier changes (head paragraph) Evidence safe-state-select (force, read back, restore; stuck register; sequence, group and clock errors; 4 mutants of the test) Residual / action (1) phase voltages near 0 V before and during the short and the read-back of the gate-driver enable are the caller's (adds the enable read-back to the table); (2) standstill is the application's statement without phase voltages (AoU-33 (d)); (3) issue 1: the call from the family port before the first enable of the group and the event were follow-ups - the call is in place since earlier changes (head paragraph and the update below)

(safety review E2-E4, 2026-09-30, host verified): the caller of a separate task (RteSystem::init(), safeState/SafeStateRte.h startTests) now (E4) builds the shorts only after a power-on reset and keeps the outcome over other resets in a no-init record (passed groups + check word, written before it is read after power-on); after a reset without power-on a group keeps its shorts only with an intact record that says it passed, otherwise freewheel until power-on - this closes a gap of a separate task: the removal after a failed test lay in .bss and a warm reset gave the short back untested. (E3) The gate-driver enable bound to the group must read off through its driver before the short is built and after it is taken back (ENABLE_ON otherwise): the test is register level and does not reach the bridge; residual (1) for the enable is closed for a group with a bound gate driver, the phase voltages stay with a separate task. (E2) The hold ends when the microsecond clock stands still for 100 000 reads (CLOCK_STUCK); tools/rtegen bounds the sum of all holds by a third of the MCU watchdog time-out. Faults considered in addition: a test after a reset at a turning machine, a removal lost by a warm reset, an enable on during the test, a clock that does not run, a hold that delays the lower tasks without bound. Evidence: rtegen-safe-state (the glue on the real service: enable on before and during the hold, stuck clock, power-on then warm reset, failed test kept over a warm reset, corrupted record, low-voltage reset; 11 further mutants of the glue, all detected; generator: reader in the row, budget with YAML path), target-active-short. Residual: (4) a family port whose reset reason cannot tell power-on gives freewheel only (fail-safe, availability); (5) the removal of a short by a bridge fault or by the hardware threshold path lies in .bss of the service and is still lost by a warm reset - the fault itself is seen again only if it persists; (6) AoU-38 (standstill at power-on, enable of a group without bound gate driver, budget of the lower tasks, availability after a reset).

docs.title: SM-58 — Hardware threshold without the core
docs.text:
Optional per project (hw_thresholds), not credited (whether a hardware path counts for stage 1 is a separate task's decision, hardware-mechanisms.md section 3). Unlike SM-23 … SM-25 it has a detection half, and that half is on the MCU: the comparator. Concept and limits: hardware-mechanisms.md 2.4.

Field Content Faults considered (of the mechanism) threshold derived wrongly (characteristic inverted wrongly, rounding to the late side, wrong reference); comparator or DAC switched off or reconfigured by software (a disabled comparator reads its INVT bit: for an above threshold "not exceeded"); route broken (TRGMUX selection, fault source select, fault control, FAULTEN, polarity); comparator output stuck; the FTM not clocked; a threshold already exceeded at start; the fault latched but unknown to the software Detection the comparator against its DAC level, continuous, no instruction involved. Of the mechanism's own faults: derivation checked by nxconfig (inverse of the linear characteristic, rounding to the safe side, range of the reference) and by static_assert of the generat against the FTM configuration; the registers of the path are in the SafeIo list (SM-22, one safety cycle); the TRGMUX selection is locked until reset. Not detected: a stuck comparator output, a stopped FTM clock (outside SM-22's clock-gate entry), a start into an exceeded threshold (not verified, hardware-mechanisms.md 5 point 6) Reaction every channel of the group's pairs to POL (inactive, freewheel), over SWOCTRL as well; latched until reset (FAULTM 10b, manual clearing without a clearing service) Times comparator ≤ 500 ns ([DS13] Table 44) plus 3 FTM clocks, 4 + filter clocks with the glitch filter ([RM13] Table 47-15); profile 64 MHz, 200 ns filter: 766 ns. Computed, not measured Effectiveness not claimed: no board run, the path is never exercised (latent, point 3 of hardware-mechanisms.md 5), and the band of the real threshold includes the supply tolerance only when the bandgap is the reference Evidence nxconfig-hwthreshold (derivation against the hand calculation, every refusal with YAML path), bswgen-hwthreshold (real PWM driver with the generat on a register model: order of the steps, lock, a model of the fault path after the manual switching exactly at the DAC level; mutants in family code, driver, templates, generator and rounding), target-hwthreshold (target build of a demo copy with a synthetic comparator input); byte-identical images of the projects without a threshold (changelog); no board run Residual / action (1) board proof with a signal at a comparator input (the eval board has none; PTA0 through J11 pin 5 is the candidate, a setup change by the safety manager); (2) start into an exceeded threshold and the output buffers under fault control (hardware-mechanisms.md 5 points 6, 7; AN-119, AN-120, to be clarified on the board); (3) a latent-fault test of the path (for example: gate driver disabled, outputs masked, DAC moved across the signal, FAULTF read, cleared) - not built, follow-up; (4) the latched fault is not reported to the supervisor or the application, follow-up; (5) the S32K11x is not described (one fault input of FTM0, which one unknown); (6) a switched-off or stuck comparator (below), follow-up

Safety review (safety responsible, 2026-09-30). H1 manual reset only — the shut-off holds until a reset, no clearing service at run time: agreed. H2 rounding to the safe side — the threshold moves by up to 1 LSB (19.5 mV at VDDA 5 V), the tolerance of the supply reference is named, not included in the band: accepted.
