H3 SM-58 in the catalogue, not credited — effectiveness is not claimed, crediting is a separate task's decision: agreed (the trace check treats the row as not credited). H4 reaction time computed only (766 ns in the profile, tDHSS 500 ns taken conservatively): accepted until measured on the board. H5 a switched-off comparator reads "not exceeded" for above, only the SM-22 register check finds the loss (one safety cycle), and a stuck output is not detected at all: residual accepted, detection as follow-up. H6 latent fault — the path is never exercised, a start test is only proposed: start test as follow-up. H7 a latched fault (FMS[FAULTF]) is not reported: residual with follow-up. H8 start with the threshold already exceeded (AN-119) and H9 the POL values under fault control (SIM_MISCTRL0.FTMx_OBE_CTRL, AN-120): to be clarified on the board. H10 the fault control overrides SWOCTRL — an active short ends in freewheel (as partner-and-degraded.md 5.6): agreed.

(2026-09-30, safety review H5: residual risk accepted, detection as a follow-up). The table above is the state of separate tasks adds a detection half for the mechanism's own faults (hardware-mechanisms.md 2.5). Correction of a fact first: a comparator switched off never trips the timer in either direction - in disabled mode the output to the trigger mux (CMPO) is 0 ([RM13] 45.7.1); only C0[COUT] reads INVT. The text "for an above threshold not exceeded" therefore holds for below thresholds as well (the fault-path model of bswgen-hwthreshold modelled CMPO as INVT and is corrected).

Field Content Faults considered comparator switched off or reconfigured (mode, inversion, filter, window, output select), DAC off or moved, round robin switched on, route or its lock changed, fault source select back on the pin, fault control of the timer changed; comparator output stuck at "above" or at "not above"; output "above" that does not latch the timer (route or fault logic broken after the comparator) Detection (a) start test in ComplementaryPwm::init() before anything of the route exists (trigger mux still 0, timer not configured, pins not muxed): the output is forced both ways by the DAC at VDDA against the input pin (pin against VDDA must read "not above", VDDA against the pin "above"); (b) fast register check of the path in the 1 ms poll of the power stage (integration/HwThresholdWatch.h, DebugHaltGuardSystem::POLL_MS) - the registers of SM-22 plus the fault control of the timer; (c) consistency: output "above" on two polls in a row without FMS[FAULTF]. Every finding is latched (one word in ordinary RAM with its complement, a corrupted word reads as a finding) until reset Reaction the channels of the group forced inactive through the software output control (the halt guard's PWM inhibit), at once in init() for a failed start test and in every poll while anything is latched - the state the tripped hardware path would leave; the decision on the ECU (S1) is the safe supervisor's Times start test: 2 × 30 µs settling once per start; register check and consistency: one poll of 1 ms plus the latency of TASK_BSP (SM-22: 10 ms nominal, 17 ms guaranteed); consistency: two polls. Computed, not measured Diagnostic coverage not claimed (the mechanism itself is not credited). By construction: switching off and reconfiguration of every register of the path high (the same list as SM-22, ten times as often); stuck output once per start (latent-fault interval = drive cycle); a stuck output at "not above" that fails between two starts is not detected at run time - only a second, independent measurement of the signal can tell it from a quiet signal (plausibility G2) Latent faults of the detection the poll stops with TASK_BSP (the halt deadman SM-06 and SM-22 remain); the findings word lies in ordinary RAM - a wild write that clears it to a valid "nothing" word loses a finding, the next poll finds a persisting register fault again (a stuck output found only by the start test is lost until the next start) Evidence hw-threshold-monitor (host: start test with stuck outputs and a signal at the rail, 22 register faults injected one by one and 5 status changes that are no finding, consistency with and without the timer's latch, latch corruption, the real PWM driver and the real poll on register models, 169 checks), hw-threshold-monitor-mutations (23 built-in faults in family code, driver and poll, all detected), bswgen-hwthreshold (the order of a separate task with the start test in front, its 22 mutants still detected), target-hwthreshold (target build with a threshold); object code of the demo unchanged; no board run Residual / action (1) board proof: the start test on a board with a signal at a comparator input (the two forced comparisons read by J-Link or console), a switched-off comparator (J-Link write CMP0_C0[EN] = 0) forcing the group within one poll; (2) assumption of use: at the start the comparator input is further below VDDA than the comparator's offset plus hysteresis (data sheet: offset at most 25 mV) - a signal at the rail fails the start test (fail-safe, "stuck at not above"); (3) run-time detection of a stuck output needs the independent measurement; (4) a window of a few instructions between a release of the guard's inhibit and the next forcing in the same poll

(2026-09-30, safety review H7: report as a follow-up). Residual (4) of the table - the latched fault reported to nobody - is closed towards the supervisor; towards the application the reader exists, the RTE signal and the DTC are open (hardware-mechanisms.md 2.6).

Field Content Faults considered the threshold tripped (FMS[FAULTF] latched) or the path found broken, and nobody but the hardware knows: the drivers keep commanding duties, the other outputs and the gate driver enable stay on, the application does not learn why the bridge does not respond Detection safety task, every cycle, in the family port (SafetyManager::checkSupervisionPeripherals()): FMS[FAULTF], the registers of the path read again (independent of the power stage poll), the findings latch of a separate task; one context word (bit 0 tripped, bits 23..8 findings, bits 31..24 timer) Reaction through the new narrow interface safeSupervisor/HwShutoff.h (safety context only): log line and S1 held until reset, no reset - decided in the supervisor library, not by the reporter; only new bits react; S1 is not left through the register check's return path while reported. No reset because the path latches until reset (H1, manual recovery only) and a reset would re-arm it Times at most one safety cycle after the latch (10 ms nominal, 17 ms guaranteed); the hardware has switched the group off before (≤ 766 ns, SM-58) Effectiveness not claimed with SM-58. The report is kept in the protected RAM with a copy; a mismatch reads as "everything" (fail-safe) Latent faults of the mechanism a stopped safety task (SM-01, SM-04); a wild write that clears both copies loses the report - the next cycle reports again as long as FAULTF or the finding persists, a finding only of the start test is then lost until the next start Evidence safe-supervisor-hw-shutoff (real HwShutoff.cpp and SafeSupervisor.cpp with the switch of an image with a threshold: S1 without reset, new bits only, report without context = everything, corrupted record, the register check does not leave S1; 43 checks), safe-supervisor-hw-shutoff-mutations (9 built-in faults, all detected), hw-threshold-monitor (the context word of the safety cycle, 5 more built-in faults in hw-threshold-monitor-mutations), safe-supervisor, safe-supervisor-degraded, safety-cycle, safety-gate unchanged green; target build with a threshold warning-free, demo object code unchanged; no board run Residual / action (1) the RTE signal safety.hw_shutoff and the DTC safety.hw_shutoff (fixed number in the safety block, e.g. +0x05FE) need tools/rtegen, tools/nxconfig/bswdtc.py and ecu/application - outside 's paths; (2) the reaction is S1 for the whole ECU - a degraded reaction of only the group (SD) would need the report on the closed list of Degraded.h and a mapping in tools/nxconfig/degraded.py (decision); (3) board proof with a signal at a comparator input: threshold crossed → console line Event: HW_SHUTOFF, S1 (indicator, gate driver enable off), no reset, safety console or J-Link reads the record

(2026-09-30, safety review point C1: decision of the safety responsible). Residual (2) of the table is closed as decided: a project may map HW_SHUTOFF to SD, and a trip then degrades only the group of the path (hardware-mechanisms.md 2.6). Residual (2) of the table (the start test needs the input below VDDA by more than offset plus hysteresis) is AoU-37 of the concept (point C3).

Field Content Faults considered as a separate task; in addition: a trip that holds S1 for the whole ECU although only one PWM group is affected (availability), and the wrong group or every group degraded, a finding of the path or an MCU fault degraded instead of held, a degraded report keeping S1 closed, the group released by the reset that re-arms the path Detection unchanged Reaction project with safety.degraded: [{event: HW_SHUTOFF, groups: [<group of the path>]}]: context "tripped and nothing else" of a mapped timer → SD of that group only (outputs, latch, record in no-init RAM with id 0xFE and the context, log), no reset, the last group → S1 without a reset; findings, a report without context, an unmapped timer, an implausible record → S1 held as a separate task. Without the mapping: a related task unchanged Times as a separate task: at most one safety cycle after the latch; the hardware has forced the group before Effectiveness not claimed with SM-58 Latent faults of the mechanism as separate tasks (the degraded latch and record with their checks); new: the record of the S1 hold (held with its copy) - a mismatch reads as held (fail-safe); a wild write that clears both copies of both records of a degraded report is caught by nothing until the next new bit - the group stays degraded through the degraded latch and record, which are independent of it Evidence safe-supervisor-hw-shutoff (own profile: two groups, HW_SHUTOFF of timer 3 → group 0 and DEVICE_FAULT → group 1: SD of group 0 only and inside the interrupt lock, once, record with 0xFE, findings/tripped with findings/trip then finding/undefined bit/unmapped timer/timer 0/no context/implausible record → S1 held, register check leaves S1 after SD and the group is held in the next cycle, last group → S1 without reset, group kept over a reset without power-on; 112 checks), safe-supervisor-hw-shutoff-mutations (18 built-in faults, all detected, and the unmutated test built without the mapping), safe-supervisor-degraded-mutations (26 faults detected, 9 configurations refused, among them a HW_SHUTOFF mapping in an image without the path), nxconfig-degraded (the closed list of reports read from Degraded.h, every refusal with YAML path, the derived word, a demo copy with the synthetic threshold of a separate task); target build of that copy with the mapping warning-free (SD and HW_SHUTOFF compiled in); demo object code unchanged; no board run Residual / action (1) board proof with a signal at a comparator input and the mapping: trip → only the group's channels and its gate-driver enable off, the ECU keeps running (CAN, console), safety.degraded shows the group, no reset; (2) only one timer with thresholds per project while HW_SHUTOFF is mapped (the report record merges the paths; nxconfig refuses more); (3) issue 1: the released texts of concept 2.2/3 and AoU-04/AoU-32 still said "faults of one attached device"; issue 2: concept issue 3 names the trip of a hardware shut-off path as the second degradable case (CM-07 ZA) - done; (4) RTE signal and DTC of the report itself (residual (1)) still open - the degraded group reaches the application through safety.degraded

(2026-10-01, safety review H6: start test as a follow-up). Residual (3) of the table - the path behind the comparator never exercised - is closed for the start: a latent-fault test of the route, the fault input and the fault latch of the timer once per start (hardware-mechanisms.md 2.7).

Field Content Faults considered route not selectable (trigger mux register locked early, wrong register), fault source select back on the pin, fault input disabled or its polarity inverted, fault control off, timer not clocked, fault input stuck asserted or dead, fault logic that does not latch or cannot be cleared, a fault of another enabled input already latched at start Detection hwThreshold::pathTest() in ComplementaryPwm::init(), once per start, after the counter runs and before the route is locked and any pin is muxed (every channel masked): (A) comparator forced "not above", route selected without its lock - no fault may latch; (B) comparator forced "above" through the DAC at VDDA - FAULTF, the flag of the configured input and FAULTIN must be set; (C) forced "not above" again, only the test's flag cleared - nothing may remain; (D) route unselected, comparator configured again. Skipped after a failed start test of a separate task Reaction findings PATH_FAULT_UNFORCED / PATH_NO_TRIP / PATH_NO_CLEAR in the findings latch of a separate task; the group forced inactive through the software output control before any pin is muxed (freewheel, review C2); the route still armed and locked; first power stage poll logs and keeps the group forced; the safety cycle reports the findings (HW_SHUTOFF with findings: S1 held, never SD); a fault that cannot be cleared also keeps FMS[FAULTF] and with it the hardware forcing Times seven waits of settleUs (30 µs) once per start, about 0.21 ms; the filter of the fault input is shorter than one wait (static_assert against the generated FTM clock) Diagnostic coverage not claimed (the mechanism itself is not credited). By construction: every fault of the path from the comparator output to FMS[FAULTF] that is present at the start; latent-fault interval = drive cycle. The forcing of the channels by the fault control (FAULTEN → POL) is not observed (outputs masked during the test) - its configuration is in the register check of a separate task/SM-22 Latent faults of the detection the test runs only at start; a fault of the path that appears later stays with the register check and the consistency check of a separate task; findings latch as a separate task Evidence hw-threshold-monitor (step model of the fault logic after [RM13] 47.4.3.17/47.5.18, test/host/FtmFaultModel.h: healthy test trips and clears with the route left unselected and unlocked and the comparator configured again; stuck and dead input, early-locked route, fault input disabled, fault control off, timer not clocked, source select on the pin, inverted polarity, a latched fault of another input that the test does not clear; the real driver with a failing test: group forced before the pin mux, route locked, context word 0x03280001, first poll; 267 checks), hw-threshold-monitor-mutations (17 new built-in faults in the test and the driver, all detected), bswgen-hwthreshold (the order with the test in between, its 22 mutants still detected), target-hwthreshold (target build with the static_asserts); no board run Residual / action (1) board proof with the safety manager (oscilloscope: no edge on the PWM pins during the start, J-Link read of FMS and the findings latch after the start; fault injection by J-Link before the test); (2) the forcing of the channels is not observed - option for the review: read CnSC[CHOV] with the mask open while the pins are still unmuxed - decided as the follow-up (safety review group A 2026-10-01, P1 a; after the board proof of a separate task, not part of Release R1); (3) AoU-37 covers the start test of a separate task - the path test relies on the same assumption, its text names only the start test; (4) a fault of another enabled fault input latched at start reads as a finding of this test (fail-safe, availability)

docs.title: SM-30 — Signal qualifier of the RTE
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered a value is used although its measurement is invalid: raw value at the converter limits, amplifier outside its range, open pull-up, value outside the breakpoints, failed conversion Detection per channel and task, from the generated conversion: QLF_ERROR_RANGE, QLF_ERROR, else QLF_OK Reaction the application decides (AoU-12) Times one period of the reading task; the reaction time is the application's Diagnostic coverage medium for faults that drive the value out of its valid range (open, short to a rail, conversion failure). None for in-range faults: drift, stuck-at an in-range value, gain error — they need a second source (G2) or age supervision (G3) Latent faults of the mechanism none Evidence adc-access, adc-access-averaging, bswgen, rtegen, demoswc-sil, boardtest (qualifier phases against a simulated ECU) Residual / action G2, G3

docs.title: SM-31 — E2E protection P01 / P02 / P11
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered a CAN message corrupted, repeated, lost, out of sequence, or from the wrong sender Detection CRC-8, data ID and a 4-bit counter per message; status mapped to the qualifier, configured per signal by rtegen Reaction the application decides; the signal is marked Times one reception period; loss is only noticed when the application or the qualifier evaluates the absence (timeout priority in the qualifier) Diagnostic coverage high for corruption (E2E CRC on top of the CAN CRC), repetition and sequence errors within the counter range, and masquerading between configured data IDs — for the signals the integrator configured (AoU-11). Blind spots: loss of more messages than the counter range, and signals without a profile Latent faults of the mechanism none Evidence e2e, e2e-host, e2e-ref (against the specification's examples), e2e-mutations (slow), rtegen, can-bus-state; board 2026-09-16 (seven steps with injected errors give the expected qualifiers) and 2026-09-21 (counter jumps by exactly 1 after a communication pause) Residual / action —

docs.title: SM-32 — CAN bus state and transmit gate
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the ECU keeps sending into, or using data from, a bus that is not healthy Detection CanBusMonitor (fault confinement state, bus-off counters, per bus); CanPhyGate blocks transmission while no phy provider is ready Reaction transmission blocked; bus state feeds the qualifier (priority bus > timeout > CRC > alive) Times one supervision cycle Diagnostic coverage medium: the controller's own error confinement is reported per bus; a transceiver fault that the controller does not see is only visible through a phy provider — on boards with an SBC that is SM-33 (stage 2, not credited); on boards with a passive transceiver there is no transceiver diagnostic at all Latent faults of the mechanism none Evidence can-bus-state (two buses, board without SBC), can-phy-gate, can-console; board 2026-09-16 Residual / action —

docs.title: SM-34 — Device reports to the safe supervisor
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered a fault found by a device package or a base-software service over device values is not attributed or reaches no reaction; a common cause on a device bus (F5) looks like several unrelated device faults; a switching-off reaction triggered by a task without safety context Detection none of its own: it carries what others detect. Context word (bus id, device instance, fault class, detail) checked on delivery, malformed words refused by the box and handled fail-safe; communication faults of two devices on one bus within 20 safety cycles are correlated into one "bus lost" event Reaction DEVICE_REPORT: S3 (log, bus verdict, QLF_ERROR on the device values of a lost bus); DEVICE_FAULT: S1 held for IDENTITY, S1 + S2 for every other class and a malformed word; DEVICE_FAULT only from the safety context (static rule safety-context) Times report: one safety cycle after posting plus the RTE task period for the qualifier; fault: within the safety cycle that detects it Diagnostic coverage reaction - the coverage belongs to the reporting package; credited only once a package reports through it Latent faults of the mechanism a lost box delivery is visible only as a missing report; the box lies in ordinary RAM (decision: only reports without a switching-off reaction use it) Evidence safe-supervisor (9 built-in faults detected), safety-context; no board run yet (no driver reports). (safety review): first user is a base-software mechanism, not a device package - the hold of the safe_off levels of the family port reports every take-back of a foreign active level as DEVICE_REPORT (NO_BUS, NO_DEVICE, class ACTUATOR_STATE, detail = output number) through its own box in ordinary RAM, delivered by SafetyManager::cyclic(); safe-off-command-hold (rate, refusal, counter-check), safe-supervisor (S3 for the word, the same word as DEVICE_FAULT resets), safety-context-elf (box outside the protected RAM, strong safeOffReportBox()), safe-off-hold-mutations; board 2026-10-03 (step 5, demo image 7935d205): a foreign high level on DRV_EN is taken back in 0.815 ms and reported as DEVICE_REPORT detail 3 about 8 ms later, a foreign KL30B switch-on in 0.27 ms (detail 7), no reset, no report for a refused or a commanded write: the take-back is recorded as DTC 0x1605FA (19 02, snapshot DID 0x0140, status after 11 01, power cycle and 14 FFFFFF as expected; two writes 1 … 2 s apart were counted once - open) Residual / action Device packages; port call of deliverDeviceReports() for each further box (done for the safe_off hold); bus id as NX_DEVICE_<D>_BUS_ID from bswgen

docs.title: SM-50 — Start reason from two independent sources
docs.text:
Field Content Faults considered a watchdog reset is not recognised, so the configured reaction to it (after_watchdog_reset) never happens Detection supply role (SBC reset source, where present) and RCM_SRS captured before main(), unified by a rank rule Reaction after_watchdog_reset: sleep also for a reset only the MCU saw Diagnostic coverage high for the recognition of a watchdog reset by the MCU's own register (independent of the SBC) Evidence ecustate (EcuStartReasonHostTest), bsw-providers-sbc, bsw-providers-nosbc, bsw-providers-nosbc-nomcu; board 2026-09-21 (0x2 flash reset, 0x6 after safety wdg, 0x2 reset button, 0x1 power-on); reset-loop limit (below): board B10 and B11 passed 2026-09-22/23 Residual / action this is the recognition only; the limit on repeated safety resets was missing in stage 1 (F13) - since an earlier change see the reset-loop limit below

Reset-loop limit (T4, SSR-065) - an extension of SM-50 on the reaction side, like the period part of SM-04:

Field Content Faults considered a permanent fault that an S1 + S2 mechanism answers with a reset restarts the ECU endlessly; at every restart the safe state is left until the first safety cycle finds the fault again (F13). Board without an SBC: no other limit; with an SBC its reset counter (SM-52) is device-dependent and not credited Detection a record of four words in the application's no-init RAM (safeSupervisor/ResetLoopLimit.h: count, pending mark, last cause, check word), placed by the family port (platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/main.cpp, section .noinit). Whether a start follows a safety reset is decided from independent sources: the supervisor's own mark, written in SafeSupervisor::handle() immediately before the reset of every S1 + S2 reaction (with the event); the MCU's reset status as SM-50 captured it before main() (a real watchdog reset - not the fast test of the start-up - counts, a power-on or low-voltage reset clears); the hard fault dump of SM-17 and a core lockup (RCM_SRS[LOCKUP], a fault while the fault handler runs, so the dump may be missing) count as a fault exception. Debugger case (board finding 2026-09-22): a J-Link reset (VC_CORERESET + AIRCR.SYSRESETREQ) starts with RESET Reaction from reset_loop_limit consecutive safety resets on (default 3, i.e. the third safety reset in a row): RESET_LOOP_LIMIT → S1 held without a reset (holdSafeState, like a separate task), with one console line naming the count and the last cause (SAFE STATE HELD (RESET_LOOP_LIMIT, 3 safety resets, last: event 9): ...). Only a power cycle ends it: a reset from outside finds the count again and holds again. After reset_loop_clear_ms of operation without a safety reset (default 60 000 ms, counted in safety cycles, so a slow safety task clears later, never earlier) the count is cleared Times the limit acts at the start after the N-th safety reset, before anything of the application runs: bootloader, start-up and watchdog fast test only. The N - 1 restarts before it still run the application until the fault is found again Diagnostic coverage high for loops of S1 + S2 reactions of the supervisor, of the MCU watchdog and of fault exceptions. Not counted: a loop through resets the supervisor does not mark (e.g. a run-down step time-out of SM-53, a diagnostic reset request) and, with an SBC, resets of the SBC's watchdog (they reach the MCU as a pin reset; SM-52 counts them) Latent faults of the mechanism the record lies in ordinary RAM outside the MPU region (it must survive the reset and is written from main() and the safety task); a wild write that makes it invalid restarts the count from 0 (the next safety reset counts as the first) - it never leads to a hold by itself. A wild write that sets a plausible count is not detectable; the check word makes a random one unlikely Evidence safe-supervisor (record rules, the mark before every reset of an S1 + S2 reaction and never before a hold or a report, hold without reset from the limit on and again after an outside reset, clearing after the fault-free time, console line; 17 built-in faults all detected, a change-log fragment), safety-context and safety-context-elf (the call only from main() inside its SafetyShell; the record in the NoInit region above the RAM the start-up initializes, outside the MPU region, below the boot request). Board (issue 2): B10 passed 2026-09-22/23 (three J-Link resets count nothing; three safety wdg give 1 of 3, 2 of 3, then SAFE STATE HELD (RESET_LOOP_LIMIT ...), CAN silent; supply interruptions and the reset button do not count, the button in the held state holds again), B11 passed 2026-09-22 (count cleared after more than 60 s, record read by J-Link, safety mpu counts as cause 0x2); suite case BT-S1H-04 2026-10-02 Residual / action the two values are provisional defaults in the family port until the module manifest of the supervisor exists (proposed modules.safeSupervisor.reset_loop_limit / reset_loop_clear_ms, tools/nxconfig/tools/bswgen, see a change-log fragment); the SBC's start reason (second source of SM-50) is not yet an input, because the supply role reports only after the run level is reached; the fault memory entry belongs to a separate task

docs.title: SM-51 — Image check by the bootloader
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the application image is incomplete, from another project, or interrupted mid-flash Detection at every start (app_image_valid() in bootloader/src/core/app_image.c): record CRC, compatibility block, CRC-32 over the whole image, plausibility of the entry. : the start decision is checked again immediately before the jump, not taken from a RAM value of the past. (bootloader 0.3.8): that check before the jump (app_image_confirm()) reads the record, the compatibility block and the entry again from flash, but computes no second CRC-32 over the image - the record's CRC and size must equal the values of the one CRC of this start (bootloader/doc/README.md, "One CRC per start") Reaction the bootloader does not start an invalid image and stays reachable for a download Times at start, before the application runs Diagnostic coverage high for the application image at start (CRC-32 over the complete image including the ROM-check list and reference). Not covered: the bootloader's own code; projects without the neXtBSW bootloader Evidence bootloader-host, bl-update-host (power loss at every flash operation), bl-update-mutations (slow), canflash-tool, bl-platform-host; board 2026-09-21 (power loss at 52 % of a download, bootloader reachable, reflash succeeds); board 2026-10-02/03 (bootloader 0.3.9 with one CRC per start, about 144 ms per start; diagnostic CAN on CAN1, passed - update, flashing and the way back over both channels) Residual / action the integrity of the bootloader itself is not checked by any stage-1 mechanism (open point N4). Since an earlier change (accepted in safety review, 2026-10-03, F5 a): an image byte that changes between the CRC at start and the jump without a flash command (debugger write, bit fault) is no longer detected by the bootloader; with a held extended session that window can last minutes. The residual is left to the flash ECC and SM-14, which runs only after the start (idle context, lifecycle level 2) and whose coverage depends on the project's configuration (config-range CV-11); hence AoU-CFG-7: an image the neXtBSW bootloader starts keeps SM-14 active. Recorded as an assumption of use and not as a configuration check, because the start by the neXtBSW bootloader is a decision of the integrator's delivery and production flow that the configuration of the application image does not describe, and because the part that the configuration does describe - the re-check period - is already the integrator's data-set value (AoU-CFG-4) with the proposed check C2; SM-14 itself cannot be configured away in an image built through the build (AoU-CFG-1). Observation (safety review, F6 b): during the development of the diagnostic CAN a HardFault in the bootloader caused a reset loop inside the bootloader - an observed case of the unsupervised bootloader phase (N4): the outputs stayed in their reset state, and nothing in the bootloader limits such a reset loop (the reset-loop limit SM-50 is a mechanism of the application). The restart time of the CAN1 build was not measured; it is covered by AoU-CFG-2 (the integrator measures his configuration)

docs.title: SM-53 — Defined run-down
docs.text: Field Content Faults considered the run-down before the power down does not finish (a step, the lifecycle shutdown or the power down hangs or fails), so the ECU would stay half shut down; power outputs left at their last value until the supply goes off Reaction state machine with per-step time-outs; a step that does not finish in time is aborted (IShutdownStep::abort()) and leads to a restart; the restart is supervised and, if the lifecycle does not carry it out within shutdown_timeout_ms, ended by a direct reset (safe outputs table, software reset). Last run-down step: the safe outputs table, the outputs locked off until the power down or the reset. step_error: continue never passes the NvM step (state machine and generator) Effectiveness reaction, bounded by the configured time-outs; the restart bounded by shutdown_timeout_ms as long as the ECU state management runs (lifecycle levels above 1) Evidence ecustate (EcuShutdownHostTest, EcuRestartSupervisionHostTest with a lifecycle that never completes, EcuSafeOutputsStepHostTest, EcuOutputFlushHostTest, integration test); data-flash-system (abort keeps the gate locked); rtegen (continue refused with an NvM step); board (b) (Rundown after 2001 ms, MCU unpowered, wake-up by CAN); board 2026-10-02/03 (issue 2): step limits NvM 1 000 ms, CAN 500 ms, outputs 50 ms, lc reboot runs down without a watchdog reset; ecu sleep with the oscilloscope: DRV_EN at 0 V from 3.2 s before the supply is off with a test image that hangs the shutdown: restart requested after 5 000 ms, direct reset 9 995 ms after the hang began (bound 2 × 5 000 ms plus at most 10 ms), restart as software reset, no watchdog Residual / action the static-analysis finding touches this mechanism (concept 8.4). A level-1 component that hangs in its shutdown on the way to level 0 is not covered by the supervision (the ECU state management itself is at level 1), and SafetySystem::shutdown() still disables the watchdog there (WDG-F03). Gap accepted by the safety responsible 2026-10-02 (review, N5): the watchdog is not kept running to level 0 because after its last service about 160 ms remain while the orderly reset comes only after the logger is drained (up to 5.7 s), so every restart would turn into a watchdog reset; a service from the run-down sequence needs a new service point and a bounded logger, which are separate tasks (options b and c, not taken). Residual risk: a level-1 component that hangs in its shutdown during the run-down towards level 0 is not detected by any mechanism; the ECU then stays half shut down with the outputs at the last value of the safe outputs table step or, if that step was not reached, at their last value, until the supply is removed. The risk is bounded by the facts that the situation needs a hang of a level-1 component in a rare event (shutdown or sleep request), that the application is stopped by then, and that the safe outputs table step is the last run-down step. The non-volatile data are not made consistent by SM-53: a cut write is detected by the NvM's own format (two slots and a check sum), not here. The output flush of a separate task drains the diagnostic output only

docs.title: 4. The assumed safety goals, checked
docs.text:
Concept section 2.2 asks to confirm or correct the per-goal verdicts. All seven are confirmed; the analysis adds limits but changes no verdict.

Goal Concept verdict – What the analysis adds ASG-01 unintended torque partial confirmed the termination path is sound for faults the MCU detects (SM-06, SM-10, SM-17 high; the safety-task checks up to 31.25 ms, F9). What is not detected stays not detected: G1, G2, F4. A clock-gated FTM keeps its outputs out of reach of the walk (SM-23) — G1 must read the pin, not the FTM. Issue 2: the safety-task checks are bounded at 17 ms since an earlier change; F4 is narrowed by earlier changes (open until a follow-up task); G1 is closed on the host for S1, S1 held, SD and S1 + S2; the deductive view is the fault tree FT-ASG-01 of architecture-safety-analysis.md section 5.1 ASG-02 switch-off path available covered with limits confirmed further limits: the de-energising before the watchdog reset depends on CS[INT], which nobody checked (F12; checked since an earlier change, SM-02); without an SBC nothing limits a reset loop, and every restart runs the application until the first safety cycle finds the fault again (F13). After a later change: the reset-loop limit holds S1 at the start after the N-th safety reset in a row (host verified; board B10/B11 passed 2026-09-22/23). Issue 2: the residual risk DF-05 (lost SIRC: no walk before the watchdog reset, up to about 283 ms; section 2.1) limits this goal as well; deductive view FT-ASG-02 of the architecture safety analysis section 5.2 ASG-03 cell values outside SOA not covered confirmed the base-software contributions that do exist (SM-18 … SM-20, SM-30, SM-31) protect the MCU's own measurement path and the transport; F16 shows that even the MCU's own path carries a silent gain error inside the SM-18 band ASG-04 unintended balancing not covered confirmed no stage-1 mechanism reaches a bus-commanded actuator (G4) ASG-05 corrupted / stale data covered for CAN data confirmed for signals with an E2E profile (AoU-11); "stale" for device values stays G3 ASG-06 control software failure → safe state covered with limits confirmed further limits: the safety task's own period (F9), task activation (F10), ECC poll gaps (F11), watchdog configuration (F12), supply channel read failures (F14); the evidence for SM-02, SM-03, SM-11, SM-15, SM-16, SM-21 is review only (F15). After a later change: F11, F14 and F12 (watchdog) closed with host tests, SM-02, SM-03, SM-15, SM-16 host-tested; F12 for the deadman host verified, target binding pending; F9, F10 and review-only SM-11, SM-21 remain. After a later change: SM-11, SM-21 and SM-22 host-tested with mutants, F15 closed; F10 remains. The verdict stays "covered with limits". Issue 2: F12 for the deadman closed on the target; the faults of the time bases of section 2.1; deductive view FT-ASG-06 of the architecture safety analysis section 5.3 ASG-07 intended image partial confirmed start: SM-51 high; run: SM-14 high at start, low at run time (F3) — since an earlier change high at run time with a re-check period (host verified, board B9 passed for the re-check); the bootloader's own integrity is not covered (N4)

docs.title: 5. Decisions on the findings handed to a separate task
5.1 F3 — the ROM check in one go
docs.text:
The concept names two problems: an unbounded run in idle, and a once-per-start check that is not a run-time mechanism. Since an earlier change the check exists; the analysis decides:

  1. No slicing while the check runs at idle priority. RomCheck::idle() runs in the idle context of the lifecycle (RomCheckSystem.h), without any lock (the pass, since an earlier change checkPass(), is outside the safety shell; only the report is inside). Every supervised task preempts it. Its only cost is that other work of the idle context (console, log drain) waits for the few milliseconds of the run. Slicing is required only if the check is ever moved into a timed context (a task with a deadline) — that becomes a requirement for a separate task: "The ROM check shall not run with interrupts suspended and shall not run in a context with an RTE deadline unless it is sliced."
  2. Duration: computed about 3 … 6 ms for the demo image (43 049 words; assumption: a few core cycles per word for the flash read and the CRC write at 80 MHz). Not measured — board checklist item B1 (section 8).
  3. A re-check period is needed, because the first intended applications include battery management, where ECUs are often powered for long periods without a restart. Today the run-time protection of the program flash rests on SM-16 (double-bit errors on read) alone. Proposed task T5: periodic re-check with a period as a module parameter of safeMemory (milliseconds; 0 = once per start, today's behaviour), restart of the pass after each full run, a known-answer test of the CRC unit before each pass, the CRC unit reserved for SM-14 (no other user today; a second user must be serialised), and suspension while the program flash is written (a later in-application update must not produce a false ROM_CHECK_FAILURE, which holds the ECU until a power cycle). Until T5 exists, proposed AoU-25: the integrator restarts the ECU at least as often as his latent-fault interval requires, or accepts SM-16 as the only run-time check of the flash.

Implemented by an earlier change (host verified with mutants; board B1 and B9 open in issue 1 - passed since, 8.1 and 8.2): - Period: module parameter modules.safeMemory.rom_check_period_ms (manifest platforms/s32k1xx/port/safety/safeMemory/module.yaml, generated into integration/safeMemoryConfiguration.h), default 60 000 ms, 0 = once per start. Start to start, on the system time of the platform. - Context: RomCheck::idle() is called by the idle handler of the application (ecu/application app.cpp, only in an image with the reference CRC) and, as before, once by the component romcheck; both run in the idle context. The pass itself runs without a lock and outside the safety shell; only the bookkeeping at its end and the report enter the shell (one shell per pass, none per round of the idle loop while it waits). Decision 1 above therefore still holds: no slicing. - Known-answer test of the CRC unit before every pass (ROMCHECK_UNIT_FAILED → ROM_CHECK_FAILURE). - Suspension: every flash writer brackets its write with safety::FlashWriteScope (indicator RomCheckFlashWrites in ordinary RAM, library romCheckFlashWrites, outside the MPU protected sections). The NvM does so for every write of its memory (nvm::FlashWriteBracket around the IEepromDriver of the port: on the S32K1 the FlexRAM stores of the FlexNVM EEPROM emulation). A flash command started elsewhere is seen through FTFC FSTAT[CCIF]. No pass starts while a write is open; a pass during which one began is discarded and repeated, never reported. A due pass kept off for more than one period is reported (ROMCHECK_OVERDUE), so the indicator cannot switch SM-14 off silently. - Not done: slicing (not needed, decision 1); a check in tools/nxconfig that a period other than 0 exceeds the longest flash write (the manifest says so; the tool is outside this task).

docs.title: 5.2 F4 — scope of the register lock and check (input for a separate task)
docs.text:
What must cover to support ASG-01 and ASG-02, by register class. All entries are derived from data the configuration already has (the safe outputs table, the PWM groups, the clock plan), so no new configuration value is needed for the list itself — only a per-project switch for optional classes.

Issue 2: implemented the classes pin function, direction, clock gates and PWM timer as the generated lists PIN_FUNCTION, GPIO_DIRECTION, CLOCK_GATE, PWM_TIMER (board 2026-09-22) added SUPERVISION (PMC_LVDSC1), and the supervision peripherals are checked by earlier changes. The class system clock is open: F4, AN-004. The table below is the scope of issue 1, kept as the input it was.

Class Registers (S32K1) Lock or check Derived from Why Pin function of every safe output and PWM pin PORTx_PCRn (MUX, drive, pull) lock (PCR[LK]) + read-back at start; cyclic check of the value safe outputs table, PWM groups a remuxed pin is out of reach of the walk Direction and level of every safe_off GPIO GPIOx_PDDR, PDOR (for inactive state), PDIR (read-back) check cyclic safe outputs table the check that SM-22 does for one pin today; also the basis of G1 PWM timer configuration FTM CONF, POL, OUTMASK, DEADTIME, COMBINE, FLTCTRL, SWOCTRL (inactive level word), INVCTRL check cyclic; FTM write protection (MODE[WPDIS]/FMS[WPEN]) where usable PWM groups wrong polarity or dead time is a hazard of ASG-01 that no other mechanism sees Clock gates of the peripherals in the table PCC entries of FTM and PORT check cyclic safe outputs table a gated clock makes the walk skip a peripheral (SM-23) System clock SCG clock source control and status (LK bits where the family has them), SCG_CSR lock at start where possible, check cyclic clock plan (mcudb/board) a wrong clock stretches every software time; the watchdog and the deadman run on their own clocks and remain as backstop Supervision peripherals WDOG_CS (full mask, F12), LPIT0 channel 1 (TCTRL, TVAL, MIER, MCR[DBG_EN]) and the NVIC enable/priority of its vector check cyclic fixed by the mechanisms latent faults of SM-01/SM-06 (F12) — done by an earlier change (checkWatchdogControl, checkLpitDeadman; the deadman part runs on the target since an earlier change)

The lock bits and write-protection features named here must be confirmed against the reference manual by an earlier change; this table names the classes, not verified register details. Distribution over several safety cycles is allowed as long as the resulting detection time is stated (the OpenBSW comment in SafeIo.cpp suggests it); each check reports through CHECK_REGISTER_ERROR or a new event with the register class in the context word.

docs.title: 5.3 F5 — SPI as a common cause
docs.text:
Decided: not a stage-1 problem, and no separate SPI supervision in stage 1. Reasoning:

  • No credited stage-1 mechanism uses SPI. The safe outputs walk writes port and FTM registers; the watchdog, the deadman, the MPU, ECC, ROM check and the supply checks are MCU-internal. A failed SPI master therefore removes no stage-1 detection and no stage-1 reaction.
  • What depends on SPI is stage 2: the device diagnostics of the gate driver, the cell controller and the SBC. For them the common cause is real and belongs into the dependent-failure analysis of a separate task.
  • The SBC watchdog, where enabled, is triggered over SPI; a failed SPI therefore ends in an SBC reset — a safe direction (stage 2, SM-42).

What stage 1 contributes is the report path: the device context word proposed in G5 shall carry the bus instance, so that SafeSupervisor::handle() can recognise communication faults of several devices on the same bus within one window as one event ("bus lost") and choose one reaction. That is an addition to the G5 task, not a task of its own. A related task carries the other side: the SPI master is a resource shared between partitions.

Status after a later change (host verified): bus id in bits 31..24 of the context word (kind SPI/I2C/UART/CAN/other, position of the bus among the used buses of that kind in board order - safeSupervisor/DeviceReport.h, the same rule in tools/rtegen device_bus_id). Communication faults (DEVICE_REPORT, class COMMUNICATION) of two different devices on one bus within 20 safety cycles (200 ms nominal) are logged once as "bus lost", further ones in that window are folded into it; the verdict ends after a window without a communication fault. The one reaction is S3 plus QLF_ERROR on the qualifier of every device value on that bus (gd.<device>.qlf today): by the safety manager's decision a verdict built from reports that other tasks posted may not switch off - a package that needs a switching-off reaction to a lost bus detects it in the safety task and raises DEVICE_FAULT. Limits: 8 buses tracked at the same time (a further one is logged without correlation), the window is a code constant (two cycles of the slowest cycle_ms a manifest allows; moves such constants into a configuration level), and the verdict freezes while the safety task stops (safe direction: it stays lost).

docs.text:

Register AN-010 open F11 ECC poll incomplete: status flags never cleared (reset loop or masking, depending on reset behaviour to be confirmed); whether ERM->SR0 records without ERM->CR0 enables is unconfirmed; RAM and flash share one event without context under a DMA name; no start-up RAM test or scrubbing; single-bit corrections invisible SM-15/SM-16 are claimed "medium" only under the assumptions that must be confirmed T2 closed in the code by an earlier change (flags read and cleared before the report, source in the context, SR0 without CR0 confirmed in the reference manual, single-bit corrections counted; start-up RAM test decided not; test safe-memory-ecc); B5 on the board shows only that no flag survives a reset. Register AN-013 closed F14 SM-20 skips a failed reading of the internal supply channel silently; there is no limit like SM-19's a permanently failing channel removes the supply supervision without an event T2 closed in the code by an earlier change (limit adc_read_error_limit, context 2; safe-system); a failing supply channel cannot be provoked on the board. Register AN-014 review F15 Safety code without a host test: safeWatchdog (SM-01 … SM-03), SafetyManager (the order of all cyclic checks, SM-04, SM-11), the ECC part of safeMemory (SM-15, SM-16), SafeIo lock and check (SM-21, SM-22) the evidence for these mechanisms is code review only T3 closed: by an earlier change safeWatchdog (safe-watchdog), SafetyManager::cyclic() (safety-cycle), ECC part of safeMemory (safe-memory-ecc); by an earlier change SafeIo lock and check (safe-io, SM-21/SM-22, with a corrected read-back of SM-21, board B8 passed) and the MPU gate check (safety-gate, SM-11). Register AN-015 closed F16 SM-18 accepts VREFH within ± 200 mV of 4096 mV (demo), i.e. a gain error of up to ± 4.9 % on every analogue value, without any event an integrator whose safety-related analogue value needs better accuracy gets no warning proposed AoU-24 accepted: AoU-24 is binding (safety manual section 7, review D3; a node of concept 4.3 since concept issue 3, CM-07 ZG). Register AN-016 accepted

Proposed assumptions of use (for concept section 4; numbers to be confirmed when carried over): AoU-24 (ADC reference tolerance against the accuracy needed, F16) and AoU-25 (restart or re-check interval against the latent-fault interval of SM-07 and SM-14) - nodes with the status proposed in assumptions.sdoc (moved from this table by an earlier change; text unchanged). docs.text:
Captures in tools/boardtest/captures/evalboard_s32k144_demo/2026-09-22_board/. B1, B3, B4 and B7(b) used a test build with measuring variables in the safety task (not committed, removed after the run).

# Result Captures B1 one ROM-check pass (RomCheck::idle(), idle priority) took at most 5 574 µs without load, inside the computed 3 … 6 ms (F3); safety cycle without load 9 996 … 10 004 µs 112–113 B2 restart time last to first application frame: 1 027 ms through safety wdg (including the 250 ms watchdog timeout), 852 ms through safety mpu (F6, number for AoU-05). docs.title: 9. Open points
docs.text: ID Point N1 Mapping of the coverage classes to the figures the standard expects at ASIL B (issue 1: concept 9.4, point 7 and the diagnostic-coverage question; needs the standard and the MCU safety manual). Closed in issue 2 (CM-02 decision Z2, measure M3): the gap analysis iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) section 3 answers it - no direct mapping; a figure needs each mechanism re-based on the hardware element, the technique and its test interval (M2), which is task after Release R1 and before the first ASIL B release; the classes stay for Release R1 (section 1.3). Register AN-023 N2 The MCU manufacturer's safety manual for the S32K1 family (required hardware measures, coverage of ECC, watchdog, MPU, CRC unit) is not available; every class in section 3 is about neXtBSW's use of the feature. AoU-09 applies N3 Whether the MPU region descriptors restrict the DMA master's write access to the protected RAM (SM-10). Answered by an earlier change: they do not (by the register description; caveat of B17 below) - descriptor 0 (whole address space) grants M2 (DMA) and M3 (ENET) rwx, which overrides the "no access" of the locked words ([RM13] 15.1.2; HSI H10). Remains open as an action: restrict descriptor 0 before the first DMA/ENET user; until then AoU-41 forbids any bus master other than the core (decision 2026-10-02, review); whether descriptor 0 stays valid after init() is board check B17 - issue 2: B17 (2026-10-02) reads RGD0_WORD3 = 0, the valid bit is not set, so the M2/M3 rights of descriptor 0 may not be in effect; H10, this point and SM-10 carry this caveat since an earlier change (CM-02 re-check BRD a) and keep the unfavourable reading until it is settled; the restriction of descriptor 0 stays N4 Integrity of the bootloader itself: no stage-1 mechanism checks it. Observed case of the unsupervised bootloader phase (development of the diagnostic CAN, recorded by safety review F6 b): a HardFault in the bootloader led to a reset loop inside the bootloader with the outputs in their reset state; no bootloader mechanism limits that loop (SM-51 block) N5 Gap accepted: the watchdog is switched off on the way to level 0 (SafetySystem::shutdown()), so a level-1 component that hangs in its shutdown stays undetected; justification and residual risk in the SM-53 block of section 3.6. Decision of the safety responsible 2026-10-02, review (INS-WDG-1 WDG-F03, INS-ECS-1 ECS-F01). The same gap is finding ASA-3 of the architecture safety analysis (registered once, AN-130); confirmed in CM-02 (CR-02-1, Z6) N6 Assumption: all tasks run privileged, because the interrupt lock (cpsid) around check and write in the selection, the lock and the start test of the active short is ignored in the unprivileged thread mode; carried as AoU-42. Decision of the safety responsible 2026-10-02, review P1 (INS-HFH-1 HFH-F06). Issue 2: the lock times are measured on the board (2026-10-03, scope on a pin and DWT, section 8.2): all below 5 µs - start test begin 2.72 µs and end 2.08 µs, selection about 0.5 µs, block 0.93 µs at the pin; the estimate of 2 … 3 µs holds. Accepted gap confirmed in the confirmation review CM-02 (CR-02-1, Z6) N7 Upkeep after the re-check of CM-02 (record reviews/records/CR-02-1.md (not published, available on request), finding RN minor, remarks R2, R3, R4, R11 and Z4; 2026-10-04): stale places of issue 2 - "proposed AoU-24/AoU-25" in SM-18 and SM-07, the residual (3) at the texts before concept issue 3, the residual (2) without the cells of issue 1 in SM-26 (effectiveness, residuals (1)/(2)) and SM-27 (effectiveness, residual (3)) against their head paragraphs, the SM-23 row of 3.7 without the B3 bound, section 0 "Verification" pointing to 8.1 only, the header "update blocks up to 2026-10-02"; outside this document the architecture safety analysis section 11 (NvmManager.h) and the register text of AN-016. Corrected in issue 2; the reviewer's check is open (register AN-177). The failure mode of the diagnostic CAN on CAN1 (R8) follows with a separate task after Release R1

docs.title: 10. Review questions of the architecture (section 11)
docs.text:
This task changed no reusable code, no generator and no bootloader; it added this document, a consistency test under doc/safety/test/, and pointers in concept.md. The questions are answered for the analysis.

  1. Board without an SBC? Yes. Only stage-1 mechanisms are credited; none uses the SBC. F13 names the consequence explicitly: without an SBC nothing limits a reset loop. Since an earlier change the reset-loop limit (T4) does, with the MCU's own reset status and a record in no-init RAM only.
  2. Different crystal and system clock? Yes. All times are stated as times; the one computed duration (ROM check, walk) names the 80 MHz it assumes. F9 and section 5.2 (system clock check) make a wrong clock a detected fault rather than an assumption.
  3. Different derivative, S32K3 / STM32 / Cortex-R? Yes. The analysis follows the concept's split into neutral and family mechanisms; the register list of section 5.2 is by class and names the S32K1 registers as the instance of the family port. Other families get their own entries.
  4. Two or more CAN buses? Yes. SM-31/SM-32 are analysed per bus; F5's correlation is per bus instance.
  5. Several tasks and free priorities? Yes, and F9/F10 are exactly about task timing that is assumed rather than supervised.
  6. Every new value in exactly one configuration level? No new value is introduced. Proposed ones name their level: the re-check period of T5 is a module parameter of safeMemory (project level, since an earlier change modules.safeMemory.rom_check_period_ms); the reset-loop limit of T4 is a module parameter of the supervisor (provisional defaults in the family port until its manifest exists, proposed modules.safeSupervisor.reset_loop_limit / reset_loop_clear_ms); the register list of a separate task is derived, not configured.
  7. Host test with its own test profile? The new test doc/safety/test/test_fmea.py checks the document against the concept and tools/test/tests.yaml (every stage-1 mechanism analysed, every cited test exists, no coverage percentages); it needs no board profile. The code gaps are F15/T3.
  8. Tool core free of Qt, messages with a YAML path? Not applicable.
  9. Device driver granularity? Not applicable — no driver analysed (stage 2).
  10. Placement under platforms/? Not applicable — no new file there.
