What the three tasks change in the reaction model, in one table (section 2 explains each row):

Reaction Outputs Rest of the ECU Reset Ends with S3 report and continue unchanged runs no — SD degraded (new) the event's safe-output groups to their selected safe state runs, informed no power cycle S1 all groups to their selected safe state runs (only CHECK_REGISTER_ERROR) no leave S1 / power cycle S1 held all groups to their selected safe state, every round stopped no power cycle S1 + S2 all groups to their selected safe state, then reset — the board's reset state afterwards restarts yes restart

"Selected safe state" is freewheel unless a related task is used; with a separate task it is freewheel or an active short per group (section 5).

docs.title: 2. Terms
docs.text:
• Partner. The other MCU of a two-MCU (or N-MCU) ECU, reached over a link. Master asks, slave answers; the roles are the ones of a separate task (the master has the diagnostic bus), so a project has exactly one place for them.
  • Shut-off line. A wire from one MCU that disables the power stage of the other MCU without that MCU's software — for example ANDed into the gate driver's enable, or switching the gate-driver supply. It is a board fact of both boards.
  • Safe-output group. A named set of entries of the safe outputs table that can go to its safe state alone: a PWM group plus the safe_off outputs bound to it (its gate-driver enable, its high-side supply switch). Today every project has exactly one implicit group, "all".
  • Selected safe state. For a PWM group, the safe state currently chosen out of those the project allows (freewheel, active short low, active short high).
  • Fault tolerance time (FTT). The time the item tolerates a fault before it becomes hazardous. It is the integrator's (AoU-01); here it becomes a project value only as an input to a check, never as a claim.

docs.title: 3. Part A — supervision of a partner MCU
3.1 Topology
docs.text:
master MCU                                       slave MCU
 ┌────────────────────────────┐   link (SPI, CAN …)   ┌────────────────────────────┐
 │ safety task:               │  question q(k) ─────▶ │ supervision answer:        │
 │  question, window, counter │  ◀───── answer a(k)   │  a = f(q, program-flow sig)│
 │                            │                       │  master-lost timer         │
 │ shut-off line (safe_off) ──┼──────────────────────▶│ AND gate / gate supply ──▶ │ power stage
 └────────────────────────────┘                       └────────────────────────────┘
  • Master supervises slave: question-and-answer, error counter, shut-off line.
  • Slave supervises master: no valid question for master_lost_ms → event on the slave, own safe state.
  • Several slaves: one supervision instance per slaves[] entry, each with its own line. A slave with its own slaves (cascading, section 13) is out of scope, like there.
  • Mixed families: nothing below depends on the family; the family appears only in the link driver and in the safe outputs table of each side.

The role split is deliberate: only the master clocks the SPI link, so only the master can meter time on it; the slave sees time as "questions arriving". On a symmetric link (CAN) the same split is kept, so that one project never has two masters of one question sequence.

docs.title: 3.2 Question and answer
docs.text:
One message class on the link, fixed length, one link frame (so it never waits behind itself):

Field Question (master → slave) Answer (slave → master) class byte a reserved value that is no UDS service identifier (section 3.8) the same value + a fixed offset sequence question number k (8 bit, wraps) k of the question it answers payload the question q(k) the answer a(k) and the slave's state word protection the link's own CRC and session counter; additionally a 16-bit check value over the fields, so that a transport without CRC (or a CRC shared with UDS traffic) does not carry the argument alone same
  • The question sequence is generated by the master from a seed that changes per start (the master's own session value of mcuLink, section 5 of mcuLink.md), so a recorded answer sequence of an earlier run is worth nothing.
  • The answer is a(k) = F(q(k), S(k)), where S(k) is the slave's program-flow signature of the interval since question k−1 (section 3.3) and F is a fixed mixing function (a CRC over both is sufficient: the point is that the answer cannot be produced without S(k) having its expected value, not secrecy). The master knows the expected S because it is a constant of the slave's configuration, generated for both sides from the slave's project (one source, like the link parameters in a separate task section 7.5).
  • The state word carries the slave's reaction state (running, SD degraded with its groups, S1, S1 held is never seen because S1 held stops all tasks) and the slave's view of the master (questions arriving or lost). It is information for the master's reaction and for the error memory, not part of the check.

docs.title: 3.3 What goes into the slave's program-flow signature
docs.text:
The signature is built from checkpoints that only the intended program flow passes, each contributing a fixed value when passed; a missed checkpoint leaves a wrong signature, and the answer is wrong.

Checkpoint Evidence it gives Existing mechanism it reuses every safety cycle since the last question completed its sequence (ENTER … LEAVE) the safety task runs and runs all its checks SM-04 sequence monitor the safety cycle period check passed the safety task runs at its period SM-04 period part the halt/stall deadman is armed and has not expired since the last question the core is not stalled; the deadman's configuration re-check passed SM-06, its re-check the fast loop's liveness counter advanced by the expected amount (only if the project has a fast loop) the PWM-rate loop of a separate task runs fast-control-loop.md (not published, available on request) section 6.4 the answer is computed in the safety context of the slave the evaluation is not done by a runaway QM task static rule safety-context (SM-10)

What the signature does not prove: that the slave computes its function correctly (a core that follows the right program flow and computes wrong values, DF-06 of dfa.md). An answer that additionally requires the slave to compute a small fixed test task (arithmetic over the question) would detect part of that; it is decision A2 (c) and not the recommendation, because what it proves is hard to state without the MCU manufacturer's safety manual.

docs.title: 3.4 Timing on the master
docs.text:
Value (project, physical unit) Meaning question_period_ms (T_Q) one question per T_Q, from the master's safety task or a task the safety task checks answer_window_ms: [min, max] (W_min, W_max) an answer counts only if it arrives after W_min and before W_max, measured from sending the question; W_max ≤ T_Q error_increment, error_threshold (E_inc, E_max) every bad answer (missing, late, early, wrong, wrong sequence) adds E_inc, every good answer subtracts 1 (not below 0); reaching E_max is the partner fault start_answers (N_start) good answers in a row before the master enables the shut-off line at start-up (the line starts cut)

W_min > 0 detects a slave whose answer comes from a path that runs too fast (a loop that answers every question at once); a window of [0, max] turns it off and is allowed.

The counter (rather than "n bad in a row") tolerates a single disturbed exchange without letting a slave that fails every second answer run forever: with E_inc = 2 and a decrement of 1, a 50 % failure rate reaches any threshold. Its worst-case number of failures to detection for a permanent fault is n = ceil(E_max / E_inc).

docs.title: 3.5 The reaction that does not depend on the hanging MCU
docs.text:
Board fact, both sides (decides the names):

  • master board: the output that drives the line (dio.outputs), its active level, and the level the pin has while the master is in reset (pull resistor fitted, or the pin state of the derivative in reset);
  • slave board: what the line acts on — gate_enable (ANDed into the gate driver's enable), gate_supply (switches the gate-driver supply), or pwm_fault_input (a fault input of the slave's PWM timer) — and optionally an input on the slave that reads the line back.

Rules that nxconfig checks (section 3.9):

  1. Fail-safe polarity. The line's reset level on the master must be "cut". A master in reset, in its bootloader or without power must disable the slave's power stage.
  2. The line is a safe_off output of the master. The supervision module's manifest declares it connect.shutoff.safe_off: true, so it lands in the master's safe outputs table (SM-23) and gets its adapter (SM-24). Every switch-off path of the master — S1, S1 held, the fault handlers, the halt deadman — cuts the line. A hanging master therefore also disables the slave's power stage, before its own watchdog reset.
  3. The line is enabled only by the supervision, and only after N_start good answers; it is cut at the partner fault and stays cut until the recovery rule allows otherwise (decision A4).
  4. pwm_fault_input is weaker than the other two, because it relies on the slave's own timer configuration, which is set up by the slave's software — the supervised party. It is allowed with a warning and a reasoned confirmation in the project (decision A6).

Why a line and not a message: a slave that hangs with its PWM running cannot be told anything. Only hardware outside the slave's software can switch its bridge off; the line is the smallest such hardware.

The master's event. At the partner fault the master raises PARTNER_FAULT (context: slave index, cause — missing, late, early, wrong, sequence, peer restart, in bootloader — and the last state word). Its reaction on the master is a project value (decision A3): SD degraded (the master's own function continues; needs), S1, or S1 + S2. The shut-off line is cut before the event is handled, by the supervision itself, so the reaction choice never delays it.

docs.title: 3.6 The slave's side
docs.text:
• Master lost. No valid question (right class, next sequence number, check value correct) for master_lost_ms → event PARTNER_LOST on the slave. Reaction per the slave's project: S1 (recommended default), S1 held, or SD degraded if the slave's function may continue alone (redundant drives: decision B2 lists it as degradable).
  • Line read-back (optional). If the slave board wires the line to an input as well, the slave raises PARTNER_LOST with cause "line cut" when it reads the line cut while its own supervision is fine — the master has decided, and the slave's software should agree with its hardware instead of commanding a bridge that cannot switch.
  • The slave's watchdog. A slave without an external watchdog keeps SM-01 (same clock domain, AoU-13). The master's questions come from another MCU with its own clock, so the partner supervision gives the slave the independent time base that AoU-13 asks the integrator for — but only for the power stage (via the line), not as a reset source. This is worth saying in AoU-13 (section 7.1).

docs.title: 3.7 Proof against the fault tolerance time
docs.text:
Worst case for a permanent fault of the slave that starts right after a good answer:

detection  D = n · T_Q + W_max + T_eval          n = ceil(E_max / E_inc)
                                                 T_eval = period of the master task that evaluates (safety task)
reaction   R = T_line                            T_line = board fact: line change -> power stage off
check      D + R + T_margin  <  FTT_partner      T_margin = project value for jitter the element cannot see

On the slave's side for a master that stops: D_s = master_lost_ms + T_eval_s, and in parallel the hardware path: the master's own switch-off paths cut the line (section 3.5 rule 2) within the master's reaction times of concept section 7.2.

nxconfig computes D + R from the project values and refuses the configuration when it reaches FTT_partner (error with YAML path slaves[<n>].supervision.fault_tolerance_time_ms). T_line is a board value in microseconds; without it the check uses 0 and warns that the board does not state it.

Worked example, hypothetical values only, not a recommendation: T_Q = 10 ms, W_max = 8 ms, E_inc = 2, E_max = 4 → n = 2; T_eval = 10 ms; D = 20 + 8 + 10 = 38 ms. With T_line in the microsecond range the item would need an FTT above about 40 ms plus its margin.

This is the same form as AoU-05 for the single-MCU mechanisms; the difference is that here the element can check it, because the integrator's FTT enters as a value.

docs.title: 3.8 Link neutrality and the SPI bootloader transport
docs.text:
Neutral contract. The supervision needs from the transport: send a message of a few bytes, receive one, and be told of a peer restart. mcuLink gives all three (mcuLink_send, mcuLink_receive, MCULINK_EVT_PEER_RESTART); a CAN link gives the first two with a pair of identifiers and the third through the sequence number of the question. Nothing above the contract names SPI.

Sharing the link with UDS. mcuLink carries whole messages, one at a time per direction. The class byte separates supervision from UDS:

  • The class value is chosen outside the UDS service identifiers. A slave in its bootloader passes the message to its UDS server, which answers every unknown identifier with a negative response "service not supported" (bootloader/src/core/uds.c, default branch). The master recognises exactly that reply as "partner in bootloader": line stays cut, PARTNER_FAULT with cause "in bootloader". No bootloader code is added (requirement R7 stays byte-identical), and a bootloader can never produce a valid answer, because it has no program-flow signature — the rule "only the running application answers" holds by construction.
  • During flashing the forwarding lives in the master's bootloader, so the master application — and with it the supervision — does not run, the line is at its reset level (cut), and the slave is in its bootloader. Nothing to suspend, nothing to arbitrate.
  • If the master application forwards UDS to a running slave (section 6.3, optional), a supervision question may wait behind one UDS message. nxconfig derives the worst-case occupancy from the link values (frameLen, window, retries, ackTimeoutMs, link clock, longest UDS message) and requires W_max ≥ occupancy + slave answer latency; otherwise an error at answer_window_ms (decision A5 (a)).
  • Flow control is no excuse. A BUSY slave that does not answer in the window is a bad answer; the link's own rule ("a slow peer is flow control, not an error") stays true for UDS and does not apply to the supervision.
  • Peer restart (MCULINK_EVT_PEER_RESTART) during supervision is a bad answer with cause "peer restart"; the sequence starts again and needs N_start good answers before the line is enabled again, if the recovery rule allows it at all (A4).

docs.title: 3.9 Configuration sketch and checks
docs.text:
Illustrative only and the implementing task decide names.

# boards/<master board>/board.yaml     - wiring, the line's reset level is a board fact
devices:
  - name: MOT_MCU
    module: mcuLink
    connect: { spi: LINK_SPI, reset: MOT_MCU_RST, shutoff: MOT_MCU_SHUTOFF }
dio:
  outputs:
    - { name: MOT_MCU_SHUTOFF, pin: …, active: high, reset_level: low }   # low = cut (pull-down fitted)

# boards/<slave board>/board.yaml
partner_shutoff: { acts_on: gate_enable, readback: SHUTOFF_IN, switch_off_us: … }   # T_line

# projects/<master project>/project.yaml  - decisions of this ECU
slaves:
  - name: MOT
    supervision:
      question_period_ms: …
      answer_window_ms: [ …, … ]
      error_increment: 2
      error_threshold: …
      start_answers: …
      fault_tolerance_time_ms: …      # the integrator's FTT for this partner (AoU-01), input to the check only
      margin_ms: …
      reaction: degraded              # degraded | safe_state | safe_state_reset   (decision A3)
      recovery: none                  # none | restart_partner (decision A4)

# projects/<slave project>/project.yaml
partner_supervision:
  master_lost_ms: …
  reaction: safe_state                # safe_state | safe_state_held | degraded
Check (nxconfig, error unless marked) Path the shut-off output exists, is a used dio output and has a stated reset_level, and that level means "cut" devices[<n>].connect.shutoff the slave board states partner_shutoff.acts_on; pwm_fault_input only with a reasoned confirmation (warning otherwise) partner_shutoff.acts_on W_min < W_max ≤ T_Q; E_inc ≥ 1; E_max ≥ E_inc; N_start ≥ 1 slaves[<n>].supervision.* D + R + margin < FTT (section 3.7); warning when switch_off_us is missing slaves[<n>].supervision.fault_tolerance_time_ms W_max ≥ worst-case link occupancy + answer latency (section 3.8), when the master application forwards slaves[<n>].supervision.answer_window_ms slave: master_lost_ms > T_Q of the master + W_max (a single late question is no loss) partner_supervision.master_lost_ms reaction: degraded only if the event is degradable (section 4.2) and a group is mapped (section 4.3) slaves[<n>].supervision.reaction both sides generated from one source: the expected signature S and the class values — (generator, like a separate task section 7.5)

docs.title: 3.10 Events, error memory, placement, evidence
docs.text:
• Events (supervisor, safety context only — decision): PARTNER_FAULT (master), PARTNER_LOST (slave). The link driver runs in its own task; question and answer cross into the safety task through a checked mailbox in ordinary RAM (the pattern), and the evaluation, the counter and the line run in the safety task.
  • DTC. New source block in the numbering plan tools/nxconfig/bswdtc.py: +0x09nn partner.<NAME>, nn = index of the slave in slaves[], 0xFF = master lost (on the slave). Proposed, not entered (section 7.4).
  • Code placement (proposal): the neutral protocol (question sequence, F, counter, window) as plain C next to mcuLink in libs/bsw/partnerSupervision, usable by any family; the event wiring in the safety port of each family; the generator part in tools/bswgen (expected signature, table entry of the line).
  • Host test: two simulated partners on the simulated mcuLink bus of a separate task — good sequence, each kind of bad answer, a slave that skips one checkpoint, a slave that replays an old answer, a master that stops, a slave that restarts, a slave in its bootloader (a real uds.c answering "service not supported"), counter and window arithmetic against the formula of 3.7; mutants for every check.
  • Board proof later: eval board as master and Nucleo F446RE as slave (fm-testaufbau), line on a GPIO, measured: D against the formula, T_line with an oscilloscope, line level with the master in reset and in its bootloader.

docs.title: 3.11 What this does not cover
docs.text:
• Common cause of both MCUs — one supply, one clock source if shared, one ground, one connector. The supervision sees a partner that stops; it does not see both drifting the same way. A DFA row is proposed (section 7.5).
  • A master that asks correctly and computes wrongly — the slave checks only that questions arrive in order. Symmetric question-and-answer (decision A1 (b)) would add it at the cost of a second protocol direction.
  • The slave's function — see 3.3; the answer proves program flow, not results.
  • The line itself. A line that is stuck "enabled" is a latent fault. A start-up test (cut the line, see the slave report the read-back, enable again) is possible only with the read-back input; it is part of the implementation task and only with the read-back wired.

docs.title: 6. Decisions for the safety manager
docs.text:
Proposed board keys in brackets; the maintainer enters them. Each item: options, recommendation, reason.

A — Partner supervision

  • A1 Who supervises whom. (a) master asks, slave answers; slave supervises the arrival of the questions · (b) question-and-answer in both directions · (c) master supervises only. Recommendation: (a) — the master owns the time on the link, the slave still reacts to a lost master, and the master's own hang is covered by its safe_off line anyway; (b) is a later extension if a master that computes wrongly must be caught.
  • A2 Content of the answer. (a) CRC over question and the slave's program-flow signature (section 3.3) plus state word · (b) alive counter / echo only · (c) (a) plus a computed test task. Recommendation: (a) — detects stuck, runaway and check-skipping slaves with existing checkpoints; (b) proves only that something answers, (c) claims a coverage we cannot argue without the MCU safety manual.
  • A3 Reaction on the master. (a) project value per slave: degraded | safe state | safe state + reset, default degraded if B is accepted, else safe state · (b) always S1 of the master · (c) line only, report (S3). Recommendation: (a) — the line already secures the slave's power stage; what the master does with its own outputs is an item decision (redundant drives want degraded).
  • A4 Recovery after a partner fault. (a) latched until power cycle · (b) automatic after the partner restarts and gives N_start good answers, at most recovery_limit times per power cycle · (c) master resets the partner over the reset line and then (b). Recommendation: (a) as default, (b) as opt-in with a limit — like every other latch of neXtBSW; availability is a project choice with a stated limit.
  • A5 Sharing the link with UDS. (a) own message class, answer window derived with the worst-case UDS occupancy, "partner in bootloader" from the bootloader's "service not supported" · (b) a separate wire for the supervision (second link or toggle line) · (c) forbid forwarding by the master application while supervision runs. Recommendation: (a) — no bootloader byte, no extra wire, the check makes the cost visible.
  • A6 What the shut-off line may act on. (a) gate_enable, gate_supply freely, pwm_fault_input with warning and reasoned confirmation · (b) all three equally · (c) only gate_enable and gate_supply. Recommendation: (a) — the fault input depends on the supervised MCU's own configuration.

Decisions B1 to B6 (degraded reaction) and C1 to C6 (active short circuit) (not published, available on request)

docs.title: 9. Review questions of the architecture (../architecture/README.md section 11)
docs.text:
For the design proposed here (no code changed):

  1. Board without an SBC. Yes — the partner supervision is designed for exactly that slave; it uses the MCU watchdog and the master's clock, never an SBC. SD and the short need no SBC either.
  2. Other crystal / clock. Yes — every time is a project value in milliseconds or microseconds; the dead-time spin and the link occupancy are derived from the configured clock by the generator.
  3. Other derivative, S32K3/STM32/Cortex-R. Yes — the protocol is plain C over a message contract; the short needs a family fact (can the timer force it with single stores), stated in mcudb, and a family without it simply does not offer the short. The walk's per-group read is architecture-neutral; the assembler handler of each family has to implement it (R0–R3 on Cortex-M; the Cortex-R port has its own register rule).
  4. Two or more CAN buses. Unaffected; on a CAN link the supervision uses its own identifier pair, checked against the DBC like the diagnostic identifiers.
  5. Several tasks, free priorities. The evaluation runs in the safety task; the link task hands over through a mailbox; T_eval is the safety task's period, so another task layout changes only the formula's input.
  6. One configuration level per value. Line wiring, reset level, T_line, bridge reset state and high-side hold: board. Periods, window, counter, FTT, reactions, groups, mappings, allowed states, start test: project. Which events are degradable and which force freewheel: code facts of the supervisor, published in its manifest. The short's feasibility: derivative (mcudb). Derived by the generator: D + R, link occupancy, dead-time spin, the expected signature for both sides.
  7. Host test with its own profile. Planned per step (section 8), with synthetic two-MCU and two-drive profiles, not the eval board.
  8. Tools free of Qt, messages with YAML path. All checks of 3.9, 4.3 and 5.11 name their path.
  9. Device drivers. No driver logic; the gate driver appears only as a safe_off enable bound to a group and as the source of device fault classes.
  10. platforms/ placement. The walk and the start test's register part live in the family's hardFaultHandler and port/safety, as today; nothing in platforms/common.

docs.title: neXtBSW safety case — software SEooC at ASIL B
docs.text:
Title Safety case of neXtBSW - software SEooC at ASIL B: claims, argument, evidence, deficits, increments per release Issue 2, 2026-10-04 (issue 1, 2026-09-28) Author issue 1; contributors writing on the maintainer's behalf - author side, the updates in between by the tasks of section 12; issue 2: Approver the safety manager: issue 1 accepted 2026-10-02 with the review set of 15 safety documents (c7c9398c); issue 2 is the state after the corrections of the CM-05 findings (decision Z4 a of the confirmation review CM-05, record doc/safety/reviews/records/CR-05-1.md, 2026-10-04, the safety manager under D-01, verdict accepted with conditions); issue 2 accepted 2026-10-04 in the re-check of F-01 … F-09 in that record (steps 6 and 7 at dev 9cd81236, verdict accepted, CM-05 closed; D-01, without independence); its increment row of Release R1 (I-1) is checked in CM-06 (record doc/safety/reviews/records/CR-06-1.md, 2026-10-05, the safety manager under D-01, accepted with conditions, decision Z9 a) and filled in the documentation commit after the tag v1.0.0-rc1 Status issue 2 accepted 2026-10-04 (re-check of CR-05-1; D-01, without independence); issue 1 accepted 2026-10-02 Change history section 12

Working state: dev at f4055d8e (after v1.0.0-rc1) Readers: the safety manager (owner of this case, safety plan section 2), the maintainer who keeps it up to date at every merge and release, the safety manager as confirmation reviewer of CM-05 under deviation D-01 (record CR-05-1) and an independent confirmation reviewer once named, and an integrator who wants to see what neXtBSW claims, on which argument, and with which evidence. Language: English, like the rest of doc/.

What this document is. The safety case that the gap analysis iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) found missing (row 2-13, proposed task 6) and that the safety plan safety-plan.md plans as activity P2-13 and release precondition R6. It states the claims (the assumed requirements of the SEooC), the argument that connects each claim with what was done — for the product and for the process — and the evidence the argument rests on: work products, tests, board records, decisions. It is incremental per release: every evidence item says since which baseline it exists, and section 7 adds one increment per release. The consistency test test/test_safety_case.py resolves every evidence link against the repository.

Licence rule. The standard is cited by part and clause only (for example "2-6.4.8" = ISO 26262-2:2018, clause 6.4.8). No text, table or figure of the standard is reproduced; requirements are restated in our own words.

What it is not. Not a statement that neXtBSW complies with anything: section 0 says plainly that the top claim is not supported today. Not the safety plan (who does what), not the safety manual (what the integrator must do), not the traceability matrix (traceability.md, generated) — the case cites them as evidence.

It was developed following the methods of ISO 26262-6 at ASIL B without the management part Release R1 (v1.0.0-rc1) development release, no safety claim; not citable for a safety statement - reasons D-01 (confirmation only by the safety manager, without independence), D-21 (no baseline is a safety release) and D-22 (CM-03, CM-08, CM-09 and CM-11 after R1) Verdict today not supported. The confirmation reviews are performed by the safety manager himself without independence (D-01; row "Confirmation reviews"), so no working state gets an ASIL statement; CM-03, CM-08, CM-09 and CM-11 come after R1 (D-22); the confirmation review of the safety manual is closed, but without independence (D-02); no baseline is a safety release (D-21); C-03 and C-04 stay in the basis for completeness (concept.md 2.2 lists all seven assumed safety goals) and stay not supported on their own, which is what keeps the top verdict at its floor — narrowed wording (AN-101) does not by itself raise it Claims 10 claims: 1 top claim, 7 product claims (the assumed safety goals ASG-01 … ASG-07 of concept.md), 1 context claim (the assumptions of use), 1 process claim (the claim of the safety plan, iso-q2) Product argument per assumed safety goal over the software safety requirements derived from it (ssr.sdoc) to tests and board records. Verdicts: 4 partly supported Evidence 118 items: 59 test, 31 work product, 13 board record, 8 decision, 4 analysis, 3 record. Status: 102 available, 14 partial, 2 missing (each missing item has an open task); review records, the trace matrix, board captures and the task list are not published (section 1.3) Deficits 20 assurance deficits, each with its task or tailoring (section 6) Confirmation reviews performed by the safety manager under D-01, without independence (records under doc/safety/reviews/records, not published, section 1.3): CM-01 safety plan (CR-01-1; issue 3 released in its delta re-check of 2026-10-08), CM-07 concept and requirements (CR-07-1), CM-04 verification plan (CR-04-1), CM-02 failure analysis and architecture safety analysis (CR-02-1) and CM-10 safety manual (CR-10-1; F-02 closed in re-check 3 of 2026-10-08) closed; CM-05 this case (CR-05-1, dev 2c065567) closed, this issue 2 is its correction, accepted in the re-check of 2026-10-04; CM-06 release decision of Release R1 (CR-06-1, tag v1.0.0-rc1, 2026-10-05) performed, accepted with conditions; CM-03, CM-08, CM-09, CM-11 after R1 (D-22) Increments 3: v0.1.0 (development release, no safety case, 84 of today's evidence items already present), Release R1 v1.0.0-rc1 (development release, this issue, 32 further items; tag commit, bound CI report and board run in section 7) and the working state after it (v0.2.0 is a development release without an increment of its own, section 7) Verification mock/host: doc/safety/test/test_safety_case.py resolves every evidence link (paths, test entries with their SSR, text anchors, board captures, decision IDs, task IDs, the tag v0.1.0 when it is present) and runs counter-checks with deliberately broken copies. No hardware, no code change

docs.title: 1.1 Notation
docs.text:
The case is written as tables so that a test can check it; the structure follows the usual claim–argument–evidence pattern:

  • Claim (C-nn, section 2): a statement that the element is meant to meet. For an SEooC the claims are the assumed requirements (2-6.4.5.7, 10-9.2.4): the assumed safety goals of concept.md section 2.2 and the claim of the safety plan section 1.2.
  • Argument (A-nn, A-P<part>, sections 3 and 4): the strategy that says why the claim holds, the basis it decomposes into (requirements, assumptions of use, activities, sub-claims), the evidence it cites, the deficits it admits and a verdict.
  • Evidence (E?-nn, section 5): one row per item, with the reference the test resolves, since which baseline it exists and its status.
  • Deficit (D-nn, section 6): something the argument needs and does not have — the counter-evidence of the case. Every deficit names the task that removes it, or the tailoring of the safety plan that hands it on.

Verdicts, from strong to weak: supported, supported with limits, partly supported, not supported. An argument is supported only without deficits and with all its evidence available; a claim is never stronger than what concept.md section 2.2 says about its coverage; the top claim is never stronger than its weakest sub-claim (all checked).

docs.title: 1.2 How the claims decompose
docs.text:
C-00 top claim ─┬─ C-01 … C-07  product: assumed safety goals ASG-01 … ASG-07  (A-01 … A-07)
                │     └─ SSR-nnn (ssr.sdoc) ─ tests (tools/test/tests.yaml) ─ board records (captures)
                ├─ C-08  context: the assumptions of use are stated for the integrator  (A-08)
                │     └─ AoU-nn cited by the SSR ─ concept.md section 4, safety manual (DOC-19)
                └─ C-09  process: developed following part 6 at ASIL B without management part  (A-P2, A-P6, A-P8, A-P9)
                      └─ activities P2-01 … P9-04 (safety-plan.md section 4) ─ their work products

docs.title: 1.3 Reference forms that the test resolves
docs.text:
Form in the "Reference" column Meaning Resolved by the test `path` a file or folder of the repository the path exists `path::text` a place in a file, named by a text it contains (a heading, a decision ID, a capture line) the file exists and contains the text `test:<name>` an entry of tools/test/tests.yaml the entry exists and names the requirement of the evidence row in its field requirements — no reference yet allowed only for status missing

A test entry is evidence that a test is defined for the requirement; whether it passes is the job of the test run of the baseline (archived CI report, D-12).

Evidence that is not published (decision Z2 b of CM-05, record CR-05-1; export classes of a separate task). Part of the evidence stays in the private repository and is not exported with a release: the review records and code inspections under doc/safety/reviews (EW-11, the records named in section 0 and in D-01, D-02, D-12, D-17, D-20), the generated trace matrix doc/safety/traceability.md (EW-17), the board captures under tools/boardtest/captures (EB-01 … EB-13), the task list the task list (ED-01 … ED-06; exported only in a cleaned form) with its checker tools/todo (EW-32, not published), the requirements under doc/requirements other than the safety requirements (the safety requirements and catalogues under doc/requirements/safety - ssr.sdoc, EW-15, and goals.sdoc, assumptions.sdoc, mechanisms.sdoc - are published since the re-check of CM-05, decision SDOC), and the written project rules (EW-01; exported only in a cleaned form, without the sections on the internal way of working). They are available on request. Their status in section 5 is the status in the repository; that they are not published raises no verdict of this case and lowers none - a reader of the export takes them as named, not as seen. Paths of private files (decision Z10 a): where the published text names the path of a private file, the path stays as a reference; the file itself is not published and is available on request.

docs.title: 3.1 What the integrator supplies himself
docs.text:
An integrator reads his duties in the safety manual (safety-manual.md issue 2): the assumptions of use with how to fulfil them (section 7), the configuration rules (section 8) and the tailoring and process (section 12). Two consequences of this case belong there and are named here as well:

  • The independent confirmation. No confirmation measure of neXtBSW is performed with independence (D-01): the integrator takes over under his own management of functional safety that there is no independent confirmation review yet, as well as no quality management system, no competence evidence and no assessment - AoU-35 (safety manual section 7, safety plan T-03, T-09, T-11).
  • The tailored activities. What the project does not perform - item definition and hazard analysis (T-01), hardware development (T-02), QMS and competence evidence (T-03), the impact analysis at item level (T-04), the development interface agreement (T-05), the evaluation of hardware elements (T-06), proven in use (T-07), ASIL decomposition (T-08), the assessment (T-09), tests on his ECU (T-10) and the independence of the confirmation measures (T-11, a deviation) - is listed with the integrator's side in the safety plan section 3 and in the safety manual section 12; D-14 and D-21 name the consequences that stay with the element.

Board records are evidence of the reference configuration (T-10): the integrator repeats the target tests on his ECU (section 5.2).

docs.title: 5. Evidence
docs.text:
Columns: Kind — work product, analysis, test, board record, decision, record. Requirements — for tests and board records the SSR or AoU the item supports (— otherwise). Since — the first baseline that contains the item: v0.1.0, or next for the working state after it; — for a missing item. Status — available (every reference resolves), partial (references resolve, the item is not complete; the task completes it), missing (not there yet; the task produces it). Task — an open task of the task list for partial and missing, — otherwise.

Not published, available on request (section 1.3, Z2 b and Z10 a of CM-05): the review records and inspections (EW-11), the trace matrix (EW-17), the board captures (EB-01 … EB-13), the task list (ED-01 … ED-06) and its checker (EW-32) are evidence in the private repository, the project rules file (EW-01) is exported only in a cleaned form; the status column gives their status there.   2. The verdicts are re-assessed: a deficit whose task is done is removed together with its citations, the evidence status is raised, and the verdicts follow the rules of section 1.1. The test fails when a task named as the carrier of a partial or missing item or of a deficit is done — that is the signal to update the case, not to relax the test.
  3. The confirmation review CM-05 of the safety plan is performed on the case of that release - until an independent reviewer is named by the safety manager under D-01, without independence (for Release R1 on the candidate state dev 2c065567, record CR-05-1, decision Z1 a). Only when the top claim C-00 is at least supported with limits, D-01 and D-21 are removed and the preconditions R1–R6 are met, may the release be a safety release.

docs.title: 8. Maintaining the case
docs.text:
• Owner: the safety manager. Kept up to date by: the maintainer, in the same merge that changes a task named here (status done) or a requirement of ssr.sdoc.
  • Checked by: doc/safety/test/test_safety_case.py. It fails when an evidence link does not resolve, when a requirement derived from an assumed safety goal is missing in its argument, when a test named here no longer names its requirement, when an activity of the safety plan is not argued, when a claim's text drifts from concept.md or from the safety plan, when a verdict is stronger than the coverage of concept.md 2.2 allows, when a carrier task is done, when the numbers of section 0 do not match the tables, and when the standard is cited beyond part and clause.
  • Change impact: a change that touches a requirement, a mechanism or a work product named here is a change of the case (8-8.4.3) added the optional field safety_impact to the tasks, and until it is filled for the tasks that change the safety part (safety plan N9) the maintainer decides per merge.

docs.title: 10. Review questions of the architecture (section 11)
docs.text: This task changes no code, no generator, no configuration and nothing under platforms/: one document and one consistency test. Board without an SBC, different crystal, derivative, CAN buses, task set: the case contains no board fact of its own; the board records are marked as evidence of the reference configuration (T-10), and the product argument rests on requirements that are written per family and configuration. New values in one configuration level: none. Host test with its own test profile: test_safety_case.py checks the case against the repository and against deliberately broken copies of itself; it needs no board profile. Qt-free core, YAML paths: not affected. Device-driver granularity, platform rule: not applicable.

D-01, without independence); the updates of issue 2 after its release accepted on 2026-10-04 in re-check 2 of that record (dev 2c065567, N6 … N10; D-01, without independence); the update (section 5, column "Clause; neXtBSW rating") accepted on 2026-10-08 in re-check 3 of that record (dev c0928380, C4 … C6, F-02 closed; C7 the class of SM-21/SM-22 as fmea.md issue 2; D-01, without independence) Status issue 2 accepted (released 2026-10-04 in the re-check of CM-10, record reviews/records/CR-10-1.md (not published, available on request): F-01 and F-03 closed; D-01, without independence); the updates after the release - F-04 (AN-143) and F-05 (AN-175) - closed and accepted as updates of issue 2 in re-check 2 of CR-10-1 (2026-10-04); F-02 (the typical classes of the former re-based column, section 5; Z2) corrected by an earlier change (2026-10-08: per mechanism a clause reference and neXtBSW's own rating instead of the typical classes) and closed in re-check 3 of CR-10-1 (2026-10-08), the update accepted; CM-10 closed with the verdict accepted (D-01, without independence) Change history section 16

Working state: dev at c0928380 (after v1.0.0-rc1) Readers: the integrator who builds a safety-related ECU on neXtBSW, his safety manager and assessor; the safety manager as reviewer of CM-10 under deviation D-01 (record CR-10-1), and an independent confirmation reviewer once named (reviews/packages.md (not published, available on request)). Language: English, like the rest of doc/.

What this document is. The integrator-facing safety manual of neXtBSW as a Safety Element out of Context (SEooC), the work product of confirmation measure CM-10 of the safety plan (safety-plan.md section 5). It says what neXtBSW assures and what it does not, which assumptions of use (AoU) the integrator must meet and how, which configuration rules keep the claim valid, which limitations he inherits, and where the evidence is. It adds no new safety statement: every sentence restates an existing statement of the repository and names its source. Where the sources disagree or are out of date, this manual says so (section 15) instead of deciding.

Licence rule. ISO 26262:2018 is cited by part and clause only (for example "10-9.2.4" = ISO 26262-10:2018, clause 9.2.4). No text, table or figure of the standard is reproduced.

What it is not. Not a safety case (safety-case.md), not an assessment, not a statement that an ECU built on neXtBSW is ASIL B capable. neXtBSW is a hobby project; nothing here has been assessed by anyone outside it (concept section 0).

SM-34 a reaction whose coverage belongs to the reporting package - as mechanisms.sdoc and fmea.md issue 2), and the not credited SM-26, SM-27 (selectable safe state and its start test; not credited for release R1, CM-07 ZD), SM-33, SM-52 (device-dependent), SM-58 (optional hardware path), SM-59 (hardware LVD reset), SM-60 (lock of the FlexNVM block, proposed) and SM-40 … SM-43 (stage 2) — each with guaranteed detection, reaction, fault handling time, coverage class, and the clause reference with neXtBSW's own rating of the gap analysis (section 5; AoU-ASA-c covered by existing rows, section 7.7), AoU-CFG-1 … AoU-CFG-7, AoU-SEC-1 … AoU-SEC-8; plus AoU-31 announced for a separate task and not in force (section 7.6); every row added after the acceptance of issue 1 says so in its source column Configuration combined route: relations checked over the whole declared range, behaviour verified per data set; 19 values in config-range.md (section 8) Tools 24 rows of the tool classification; compiler TCL 3, most generators TCL 2 today; the integrator's duties are AoU-26 … AoU-29 (section 9) Known limitations non-qualified FreeRTOS, GCC 11.3.1 (xPack arm-none-eabi-gcc), newlib, ETL; OpenBSW demo skeleton; single channel on one core; no partitioning of the application yet; family port for s32k1xx only; open board proofs (section 10) Verification mock/host: test/test_safety_manual.py checks this document against its sources (every AoU of concept, fmea, tool classification, config range and security interplay present with a source, every stage-1 mechanism of the concept catalogue in section 5, the tool table against tool-classification.md, tailoring T-01 … T-11, links, licence rule; the AoU proposals of dfa.md section 9 and architecture-safety-analysis.md section 7.1 present or marked as covered; in the git repository also the state line against the last tag, an entry of section 16 for every commit that changed this manual since its acceptance, and the note on every AoU row added after it) with counter-checks; tools/trace check sees every AoU here. No code, no hardware

docs.title: 1. What neXtBSW assures, and what it does not
1.1 The element
docs.text: neXtBSW as it is built into an ECU image, plus the tools that produce parts of that image (concept 1.2): safety supervision (ecu/safety/safeSupervisor, ecu/safety/safeWatchdog), the family safety port (platforms/s32k1xx/port/safety/*), the fault handlers, the debug-halt guard, the RTE and its run-time supervision, ECU state and start reasons, E2E and the signal qualifier, the CAN system, the analogue input path, the MCU drivers of the family, the bootloader, the device drivers (stage 1: only their safe_off declaration) and the configuration data with its generators. Out of scope: the application (SWCs), the hardware, the item-level safety concept (concept 1.2, AoU-01, AoU-09, AoU-17).

docs.title: 1.2 The claim
docs.text:
neXtBSW is developed following the methods of ISO 26262-6 at ASIL B, without the management part (safety plan 1.2). For the element this means: parts 6, 8 and 9 applied at ASIL B with the tailoring of section 12; part 2 applied as far as a single-person project can (safety plan, roles, tailoring, safety case, confirmation measures, release procedure). The capability is ASIL B (concept 2.1, confirmed in a separate task), as ASIL capability of an element out of context (10-9.1; gap analysis section 4 point 3).

Stage 1 (concept 1.4): the safety argument is built from mechanisms whose detection runs on the MCU and uses only the MCU, its peripherals and the configuration. Diagnostics of parts outside the MCU (gate driver, cell controller, SBC, high-side switch) are stage 2 and not credited; their safe_off declaration is stage 1.

docs.title: 1.3 What neXtBSW does not assure
docs.text: Not assured Source Consequence for the integrator ASIL C or D concept 2.1, AoU-03 an item with a C or D goal cannot rely on the element failure rates, single-point and latent-fault metrics, hardware measures concept 1.2, AoU-09, safety plan T-02 the integrator provides them; section 5 gives what his metrics need per mechanism detection for ASG-03 (cell values) and ASG-04 (balancing); full coverage of ASG-01 concept 2.2, AoU-23 he provides that detection himself (section 3) the device drivers' diagnostics concept 1.4, 13; AoU-21 he argues them from the manufacturer documents or adds his own measures a function that continues after a fault of the MCU (fail-operational) concept 2.2, AoU-04 only the degraded reaction SD for device faults exists (section 4) freedom from interference for the application concept 6.3, AoU-17 he develops his safety-related code at the target ASIL or partitions it himself qualification of RTOS, compiler, libraries concept 8, AoU-20 section 10 QMS, competence evidence, independent confirmation reviews, functional safety assessment safety plan 1.2, T-03, T-09 AoU-35 any cybersecurity claim security-interplay.md section 0 section 11, AoU-SEC-1 … AoU-SEC-8 the behaviour of the integrator's application or its generated model code concept 1.2, tool classification AoU-29 he verifies his application himself verification of the integration and of the item: the integration test of his ECU with his configuration and the test in the vehicle verification-plan.md sections 1 and 2.3 (vehicle test tailored for the SEooC); AoU-10, AoU-CFG-1, AoU-CFG-2 he runs the same pipeline on his workspace (python -m tools.ci run --workspace), repeats the board checks his values depend on and tests the integrated ECU and the item himself

docs.title: 1.4 Platform status
docs.text: The family safety port exists for s32k1xx only (concept 1.3, 9.2). On stm32, s32k3xx and rm4x an integrator gets the family-neutral part (supervisor, events and reactions, safe outputs table semantics, RTE deadlines, E2E, ecuState) and nothing of sections 6.2 and 6.4 of the concept. That is a gap, not a silence.

docs.title: 2. External interfaces of the element
docs.text:
The interfaces through which the integrator's item, hardware and software meet the element (2-6.4.5.7; gap proposal C3). Each is described in the named document; this list is the index.

Interface What crosses it Where described Integrator's side Safe supervisor events of the mechanisms (trigger(), check(), hit()), context words; event mailboxes in general RAM for events from outside the safety context; the device report word and DeviceReportBox (SM-34) concept 3, 5, 6.2 (SM-10), 6.6 (SM-34) he raises no switching-off event from outside the safety context (concept 6.2 SM-10) RTE values with the quality qualifier (QLF_OK, QLF_ERROR, QLF_ERROR_RANGE), E2E check status, deadlines = configured periods (SM-05), the signal safety.degraded (SD), gd.<device>.qlf concept 3, 6.1, 6.6; ../architecture/signal-qualifier.md AoU-11, AoU-12, AoU-18, AoU-32 Power outputs the safe outputs table (PWM groups, safe_off connections), one IPowerStageOutput adapter per safe_off output, re-enable only through the driver's own enable() concept 3, 6.5 AoU-06, AoU-07, AoU-30 Configuration data mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml, boards/<board>/board.yaml, projects/<project>/{project.yaml,rte.yaml,*.dbc}, module manifests concept 1.2, config-range.md AoU-10, AoU-CFG-1 … AoU-CFG-7 Hardware-software interface peripherals, registers, clocks, interrupts and pins the stage-1 mechanisms use on s32k1xx hsi-s32k1xx.md AoU-07, AoU-09, AoU-13, AoU-30 Bootloader and image validity record, image CRC, memory layout generated from one source, bootloader.sbc_watchdog concept 6.7 (SM-51), doc/reference/project.md AoU-34, AoU-SEC-1 Field interfaces download, bootloader update, UDS, XCP, calibration segment, console, debug port, NvM, received CAN signals (IF-01 … IF-10) security-interplay.md section 2 AoU-SEC-1 … AoU-SEC-8 Tools the build (nxconfig, generators, post-link steps), the Studio, the application's code generator tool-classification.md AoU-26 … AoU-29

docs.title: 3. Assumed safety goals and assumed technical safety requirements
3.1 Assumed safety goals (passed on unchanged from concept 2.2)
docs.text:
These are assumptions about the item, each to be checked off or replaced by the integrator (AoU-02). Only base-software mechanisms are credited; the "later device contribution" of the concept is not part of the argument. The per-goal verdicts were confirmed by the failure analysis (fmea.md section 4). The column "Coverage at stage 1" restates the COVERAGE_NOTE of goals.sdoc issue 3 (concept issue 3, CM-07 decision ZC: grades unchanged, notes at the state of the tree).

ID Assumed safety goal (of the item) ASIL Stage-1 mechanisms credited Coverage at stage 1 ASG-01 Unintended torque of the electric drive shall be prevented, or terminated within the fault tolerance time B SM-23 … SM-25, SM-17, SM-06, sections 6.1/6.2 of the concept as triggers of S1 partial — the termination path works for every fault the MCU detects; nothing compares commanded with actual behaviour (G2); register lock and check from the configuration (SM-21/SM-22), the class SYSTEM_CLOCK open (F4); the read-back of the safe state (G1) closed on the host for S1, S1 held, SD and S1 + S2, open for the fault handlers, the watchdog handler and the halt deadman and on the board (B15/B16) ASG-02 The path that switches the power stage off shall itself be available when needed B SM-23, SM-24, SM-25, SM-21/SM-22, SM-17, SM-06 covered with limits — register lock and check from the configuration, the class SYSTEM_CLOCK open (F4); the walk bounded on the board at ≤ 21 µs (F8, fmea B3); read-back of the safe state on the host (G1), open for the handlers of the family port and on the board (B15/B16); residual risk DF-05: after a loss of the SIRC the outputs are not shown to be de-energised until the watchdog reset after at most about 283 ms (section 5) ASG-03 Cell voltage, cell temperature and pack current outside the safe operating area shall be detected and made known within the fault tolerance time B SM-18 … SM-20 and SM-30 for MCU-measured values, SM-31 on the reporting path not covered (G2, G3, G5; AoU-23) ASG-04 Cell balancing shall not run unintentionally B — not covered (G4; AoU-23) ASG-05 Corrupted, stale or repeated safety-related data shall not be used as if it were valid B SM-31, SM-30, SM-32 covered for CAN data, together with the application (AoU-11, AoU-12); no age supervision of device values (G3) ASG-06 A failure of the control software shall lead to a defined safe state B concept 6.1 … 6.5 covered with limits — SM-05 reports only (S3; the reaction within the FTTI is the application's, AoU-18); task activation unsupervised (F10); register configuration from the configuration, the class SYSTEM_CLOCK open (F4); one ROM pass at most 5 574 µs on the board (fmea B1), the repetition observed (B4), the suspension during flash writes (B9) not recorded on the board ASG-07 The ECU shall not start, or not run, with an image that is not the intended one B SM-51, SM-14 partial — start covered for projects with the neXtBSW bootloader; run time by SM-14 with its period (one pass at most 5 574 µs on the board, the repetition observed); the suspension during flash writes (B9) not recorded on the board; the bootloader's own integrity is not checked (fmea N4)

docs.title: 3.2 Assumed technical safety requirements allocated to the element
docs.text:
The gap analysis (row 10-02, proposal C2) and the safety plan (T-01) ask for the level between the assumed goals and the software safety requirements (SSR): what the element is assumed to do, with ASIL, safe state and maximum fault handling time, in a form the integrator can check against his own technical safety concept. This level is written here for the first time. It invents no requirement: every row groups existing SSRs of ssr.sdoc under the goals they are derived from, and takes the times from section 5. It is a review point (section 15).

ID Assumed technical safety requirement of the element From ASIL Safe state Maximum fault handling time Realised by ATSR-1 On every fault the element detects, it shall de-energise the declared power outputs before any other action, including before a reset ASG-01, ASG-02, ASG-06 B S1 (and S2, S1 held or SD as section 4) per mechanism, section 5; outputs off within the walk after detection SSR-001, SSR-002, SSR-004, SSR-005, SSR-006, SSR-007, SSR-016, SSR-028, SSR-080, SSR-089, SSR-090, SSR-091, SSR-092, SSR-060 ATSR-2 The element shall detect failures of its own control software — program flow, timing, memory, register configuration, supply of the MCU — and react by ATSR-1 ASG-06 B S1 + S2, S1 held from 17 ms (checks in the safety task) to 250 ms (watchdog), section 5 SSR-003, SSR-010, SSR-011, SSR-012, SSR-013, SSR-014, SSR-015, SSR-017, SSR-018, SSR-020, SSR-021, SSR-022, SSR-023, SSR-026, SSR-027, SSR-030, SSR-031, SSR-032, SSR-033, SSR-034, SSR-050, SSR-052, SSR-065, SSR-066, SSR-068, SSR-069, SSR-070, SSR-081, SSR-086 ATSR-3 The element shall not start an image that is not the intended one, and shall detect a change of the running image ASG-07 B image not started; S1 held at start; during operation one period plus one pass SSR-024, SSR-025, SSR-051, SSR-067, SSR-082, SSR-083 ATSR-4 The element shall mark safety-related data that is corrupted, repeated, out of sequence, from the wrong sender or out of its valid range, and shall not transmit into an unhealthy bus; the reaction is the application's ASG-05, ASG-03 (MCU-measured values only) B application's reaction (AoU-11, AoU-12) one reception or task period SSR-040, SSR-041, SSR-042, SSR-062, SSR-084 ATSR-5 On a device fault, or on the trip of a hardware shut-off path (HW_SHUTOFF, never a finding of the path, concept 3, CM-07 ZA), that the project maps to the degraded reaction, the element shall switch only the mapped safe-output groups and keep them off until the power cycle ASG-01, ASG-06, AoU-32 B SD; S1 without reset for the last group as S1 for the mapped groups SSR-087, SSR-088 ATSR-6 The element shall carry device reports to one reaction decision and mark the values of a device on a lost bus ASG-01, ASG-03, ASG-04 B S3 for reports, S1 + S2 or S1 held for device faults one safety cycle plus the RTE task period SSR-064

Not allocated to the element: detection for ASG-03 and ASG-04 (AoU-23), comparison of commanded and actual behaviour (SSR-061 and SSR-063 are open, gaps G2 and G4; SSR-062 (gap G3) is partial since CM-07 ZE - the age qualifier of a value not refreshed within its period, allocated to ATSR-4; the event of its clause (b) is open with a separate task; G1 is closed on the host for S1 by an earlier change and for S1 held, the groups of SD and the S1 + S2 sequence of ecu/safety by an earlier change; SSR-060 stays partial: the hard fault and watchdog handlers and the halt deadman of the family port, and the board proof B15/B16).

docs.title: 4. Safe states and reactions
docs.text:
The reaction to an event is decided in exactly one place, SafeSupervisor::handle(); a mechanism only raises an event (concept 3, SSR-001).

Reaction What happens Leaves it Used for (today) Source S1 de-energised outputs the project's safe outputs table is walked: every PWM group forced inactive through the FTM software output control, every safe_off output driven inactive; no stack, no RAM, callable from task, supervisor and interrupt only through an explicit enable() of each power stage's driver; leaveSafeState() releases the indicator only SM-22 (without reset); first step of every resetting reaction; fault handlers and halt deadman walk it directly concept 3, 5, 6.5 S1 held limp home and S1, then a loop with interrupts suspended that re-walks the table and services the MCU watchdog; one console line; no application runs power cycle or a reset from outside WATCHDOG_STARTUP_CHECK_FAILURE (SM-07), ROM_CHECK_FAILURE (SM-14), the reset-loop limit (SM-50), DEVICE_FAULT class IDENTITY (SM-34) concept 3, 6.6; fmea SM-50 S1 + S2 S1, then limp home and a software reset; what happens after the reset depends on the board (SBC reset counter) and on modules.ecuState.after_watchdog_reset restart; after N safety resets in a row S1 held (reset-loop limit) most events of sections 6.1 … 6.4 of the concept concept 3, 6 S3 report and continue the event is logged — RTE_TIMING_VIOLATION (SM-05), DEVICE_REPORT (SM-34) concept 3 SD degraded (per project) only the mapped safe-output groups go to their safe state (same table, masked walk), latched and recorded in no-init RAM, walked again every safety cycle, reported to the application (safety.degraded) and through a DTC to the error memory; no reset, the rest keeps running power cycle only; a safety reset re-applies the record before the BSP starts; the last working group degraded means S1 without reset DEVICE_FAULT of a well-formed report not of class IDENTITY, and the trip of a hardware shut-off path (HW_SHUTOFF without findings, SM-58; the group the path switches off), if the project maps it (safety.output_groups, safety.degraded); faults of the MCU itself and findings of the shut-off path never concept 3 (both cases since issue 3, CM-07 ZA); partner-and-degraded.md 4

What the integrator must confirm about these states is AoU-04 (and AoU-32 for SD). A reset is not instantaneous: the restart after a safety reset (last to first application frame) was measured on the eval board at up to 1 077 ms through the watchdog path (985 … 1 077 ms, including the 250 ms watchdog time-out) and up to 858 ms through an MPU fault (817 … 858 ms) (fmea.md 8.1, B2, re-measured 2026-09-30 with a bootloader before 0.3.6; 2026-09-22: 1 027 ms and 852 ms). Use the maximum. These two values stay the stated restart times (safety review, 2026-10-03, F2 a): the restart time enters AoU-04, the restart cycle as safe state, not the fault reaction time, because the outputs are switched off before the reset; the fault tolerance times are not changed.

Bootloader 0.3.9 (largest gap of the application frames on CAN, board 2026-10-02/03): safety mpu 699.7 ms in each of three runs, safety wdg 883 … 933 ms in four runs (883.0, 913.2, 923.3, 933.2 ms; the spread is the phase of the 250 ms watchdog time-out against the frame cycle) - within the stated values (fmea 8.1 B2; records tools/boardtest/captures/evalboard_s32k144_demo/2026-10-03_board/bl33/, m1_*_gap.txt and m2_*_gap.txt).

Where the time goes with bootloader 0.3.9 (oscilloscope on RESET_b and on the chip select of the SBC's SPI, board 2026-10-03, same folder, c-20261003-*.csv; F1). The fault reset is followed by the two resets of the MCU watchdog fast test (SM-07): the reset pulses lie at 0, +229.0 and +173.0 ms (after power-on +251.7 and +173.0 ms). Since bootloader 0.3.6 only the first start after the fault reset passes the bootloader's start-up window of 200 ms:

  • start 1 = bootloader initialisation ≈ 20.6 ms + start-up window 200 ms (inside it the CRC over the application image, ≈ 144 ms) + application up to its fast test ≈ 8 ms;
  • start 2 = bootloader initialisation ≈ 20.6 ms + CRC ≈ 144 ms + application up to its fast test ≈ 8 ms;
  • start 3 = bootloader and CRC as start 2, then the application up to its first frame.

Therefore saves ≈ 112 ms (two windows of 200 ms minus the CRC that was computed inside them, 2 × 56 ms), not the 400 ms of two whole windows. The MPU path is 36 ms longer than with bootloader 0.3.6 (664 ms): ≈ 11 ms come from the larger application image (longer CRC in each of the three starts), the rest lies on the application side (fault to reset and start 3 to the first frame); splitting that rest up is task, not part of release R1. For his board, bootloader and start-up the integrator measures the restart time himself (AoU-CFG-2).

The bootloader phase is not supervised. On s32k1xx the bootloader disables the MCU watchdog as its first action (bootloader/platforms/s32k1xx/hal_s32k1xx.c, bl_system_init()) and never enables it; on stm32 the independent watchdog is not running after power-on or software reset and the bootloader does not start it. The application enables its watchdog in its own start-up. From every reset until then, no neXtBSW mechanism supervises the program flow. This is safe under three conditions, which the integrator confirms: (1) every power output is in its reset state while the bootloader runs - the bootloader configures no pin of a power output, only CAN and, on boards with an SBC, its SPI (AoU-07, AoU-SEC-3); (2) the phase is bounded: without a tester it ends after the start-up window with the jump, or the bootloader stays with outputs in reset state; a hang in the bootloader is left only by a reset from outside (power cycle, SBC watchdog served by the bootloader - with bootloader.sbc_watchdog: serve, and since an earlier change always with an SBC without software development mode, since an earlier change also with an SBC that is only read (AoU-34) - or the tester's ECU reset); (3) a bootloader that stays (no valid image, programming session) is a state with de-energised outputs, not a functional state. The start decision itself is not a RAM value of the past: since an earlier change the bootloader checks the start again immediately before the jump, and a record without compatibility block (written before a later change) is never started (SM-51; S11 of the safety review 2026-10-02). Since an earlier change (bootloader 0.3.8) that check reads record, compatibility block and entry again and compares the record's CRC field and size with the one CRC-32 over the image computed at the start, instead of a second CRC over the image; the bootloader has no flash write path between the two checks outside the programming session, which keeps it from jumping, and an image body changed by anything else is the application's ROM check SM-14 at its start.

docs.title: 5. Safety mechanisms the integrator may rely on
docs.text:
How to read the table. Guaranteed detection (nominal) is the time from the fault to the event, as bounded by the failure analysis (fmea.md section 2 and 3.7): checks in the safety task are guaranteed at 17 ms while the task runs (nominal 10 ms, SM-04 since an earlier change); a task that stops is SM-01's. FHTI is the maximum fault handling time interval of the element = guaranteed detection + reaction until the outputs are de-energised (the naming of gap proposals C7/M1); the walk itself is computed below 1 µs at 80 MHz and bounded at ≤ 21 µs by a board measurement (fmea 8.1, B3). The integrator compares the FHTI with the fault tolerant time interval of his goal (AoU-05). Class is the ordinal coverage class of fmea.md 1.3 — a judgement of neXtBSW's use of a feature, no percentage. Clause; neXtBSW rating is the answer of the gap analysis to open point N1 (iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) section 3), since an earlier change in this form: first the clause of the standard against which the integrator rates the mechanism in his hardware metrics (part and clause only; the standard's own ratings are not carried here, the integrator reads them in his copy), then neXtBSW's own rating with what the mechanism sees and what not, in the words of fmea.md section 3; "—" where section 3 has no row (proposal M2 open). Latent faults names how a failure of the mechanism itself is found (fmea section 3).

neXtBSW's rating scale. neXtBSW has no failure rates and no safety manual of the MCU (AoU-09, fmea N2), so it cannot say which share of a hardware element's failures a mechanism detects. What it can show from the repository is how deep the detection of the faults in its own fault model is demonstrated. The rating says that, on a scale of its own that is deliberately not "low / medium / high", so that it cannot be read as the standard's classes:

Rating Meaning Where the evidence is E3 the fault, or its register-level equivalent, was injected on the target and the reaction was recorded, in addition to host tests board run named in fmea.md section 3 or 8, capture or changelog entry E2 the detection is exercised on the host against the fault model, and built-in faults (mutants) of the detecting code are all found; on the target at most the absence of false alarms or the reaction alone host test with a mutation profile (*-mutations, mutants named in fmea.md) E1 host tests without mutation testing, or analysis only host test or review

After the level the cell says what the mechanism sees and what it does not see; "reaction" there means that the hardware detects and neXtBSW contributes the reaction and its time; "not a hardware diagnostic" marks a freedom-from-interference measure. The rating does not replace the class: the class judges how completely the property is checked, the rating how well that is shown. For his metrics the integrator takes neither as a coverage figure without his own rationale against the clause named (AoU-09).

Verified on the host and on the board 2026-10-03 (tools/boardtest/captures/evalboard_s32k144_demo/2026-10-03_board/sys194_196/). Fault What reacts Time to de-energised outputs / reset Evidence OpenBSW system time (DWT CYCCNT) too slow or too fast SM-04 period part (DFA-6): SAFETY_CYCLE_PERIOD_VIOLATION kind 4 (slow) or kind 5 (fast), S1 + S2 at the end of a window of the period check (eval board 7 cycles, 70 ms) + walk host (progress-checks, safety-progress); board B4: no false alarm OpenBSW system time stands still not kind 4: the safety task is scheduled through exactly this time base and does not run any more. The cause of the hang is open (with the core halted the debugger reads the LPIT registers without error, so a blocked bus is not confirmed) outputs in their reset state with the watchdog reset, at most about 283 ms (derived, as left; AoU-07) board 2026-10-03 (B2b), 2026-10-04 (D1); investigation and architecture (for example the deadman on another clock, or an external watchdog on the enable line) with a separate task, after release R1 (dfa.md DF-05)

For his fault tolerant time intervals the integrator takes the last row as the time of a lost SIRC (AoU-05), or provides an independent shut-off path (AoU-13). Derived marks a time computed from the values of section 6 (and the data sheet range of the LPO); the board records in the last column show the reaction, not the bound (since the re-check of CM-10, point N4). The concept carries the same rows in its section 7.2 since issue 3 (CM-07, F-06).

What the integrator does with this table: he takes, per goal he relies on, the mechanisms named in section 3.1, compares their FHTI with his fault tolerant time interval (AoU-05), rates each mechanism against the clause named, with the class and neXtBSW's rating as input and his own rationale, in his hardware metrics with his failure rates (AoU-09), and sets the latent-fault intervals (AoU-25, AoU-CFG-4).

docs.title: 6. Timing: what the element guarantees, and what the integrator compares
docs.text:
The times come from four values (concept 7.1; defaults of the demo project):

Value Where set Default safety task period modules.safeLifecycle.task_period_ms (project) 10 ms watchdog service interval derived by nxconfig: floor(time-out × 1000 / (3 × period × LPO maximum per mille)) cycles 7 cycles = 70 ms MCU watchdog time-out modules.safeLifecycle.watchdog_timeout_ms (project) 250 ms halt deadman time-out / poll code constants of the family port (config-range CV-20, finding G3) 10 ms / 1 ms

The relation three services before the time-out at the fastest LPO of the derivative is checked by nxconfig (safety_timing, test nxconfig-watchdog) and by static_asserts; the S32K1 counter limits the time-out to 511 ms (concept 7.1, config-range CV-02). Other values scale the times of section 5 as formulas of the values (config-range.md section 3); the tables above hold for the defaults.

Two traps the concept calls out (7.3): a reset is not instantaneous (restart times in section 4), and 10 ms is the floor for anything in the safety task, not a guarantee — preemption by higher-priority tasks and interrupts adds to it; tools/schedana is where the integrator shows his schedule (AoU-08, AoU-CFG-3). A later fast control loop at PWM rate (../architecture/fast-control-loop.md (not published, available on request), not implemented) would be an interrupt above the safety task; its credited backstops stay SM-04, SM-06 and SM-01 (section 8.1 there).

docs.title: 7. Assumptions of use and how to fulfil them
docs.text: An integrator who cannot meet an assumption either does not get the corresponding claim, or adds his own measure (concept 4). He validates every assumption against his item before integration and handles a mismatch as a change with an impact analysis (10-9.2.4.5). Status says where the assumption stands: concept (in concept section 4), proposed (proposed in the named analysis and carried into this manual; confirmed with the acceptance of this manual), new here (numbered here from an existing statement that had no number yet). The note added after acceptance at the end of the source column marks a row that was not part of the accepted issue 1 (section 16); these rows were reviewed in CM-10 (record CR-10-1, 2026-10-04, D-01) and are part of issue 2. Since CM-10 (Z4): AoU-37, AoU-38 and AoU-39 read concept and are binding. Since CM-10 (F-03): AoU-33 is in force for every project with an active short, and AoU-ASA-b is a row of its own. Since CM-07 (concept issue 3, decisions ZF and ZG): AoU-33 is a node of concept section 4.3 and AoU-24, AoU-25 and AoU-40 are binding there; all four read concept. Since the re-check of CM-02 (decision Z7I b, 2026-10-04): AoU-ASA-a, AoU-ASA-b and AoU-ASA-d read concept and are binding, because the residual risks accepted in CM-02 (AN-172, AN-170, AN-165) rest on them; they are made binding by that decision, not yet nodes of concept section 4. Since an earlier change (review, D2): AoU-26 … AoU-29 and AoU-34 … AoU-36 are in concept section 4 and read concept; the source column keeps where they came from. With the acceptance of this issue (2026-09-30, D3) every proposed row of that issue is binding; a row added after acceptance is not covered by that acceptance. How to fulfil restates the source; where the source names no method, the column says so.

docs.title: 8. Configuration rules for safe operation
docs.text:
The route in two sentences (config-range.md section 1). The relations the stage-1 mechanisms need are verified for the whole declared range by checks that run on every configuration (tools/nxconfig with the YAML path, static_assert on the generated values, generator refusals), so a configuration outside the admissible range does not build. The behaviour of the built software is verified per data set — for the project's own profiles by the project, for his data set by the integrator (AoU-CFG-1 … AoU-CFG-7).

The value register is config-range.md section 2 (CV-01 … CV-20, 19 values plus the deadman constant): level, declared range, relation checked, what the project verified, route. 11 values are argued for the range, 8 per data set. All target builds of the project use the default safety values (finding G1); on the board only the demo values ran.

Rules, each from its source:

  1. Build the image only through the build; never edit a generated file; tool versions pinned (AoU-26, AoU-CFG-1).
  2. An error of nxconfig stops the configure run; a warning on a safety value is a finding the integrator resolves or justifies in writing (AoU-CFG-1).
  3. Every power output in the safe outputs table: PWM groups in the project, safe_off: true in the manifest (AoU-06); inactive levels right for the circuit (AoU-07).
  4. The three pins of the safety section only in their role (AoU-30).
  5. The safety task stays above every application task (above_application, checked; config-range CV-18); the watchdog service interval is derived, not set (concept 7.1).
  6. rom_check_period_ms between the longest flash write and the latent-fault interval; 0 means once per start (AoU-25, AoU-CFG-4).
  7. A calibration segment with a parameter whose safety is not qm needs on_invalid: refuse; no XCP in the production profile (config-range CV-15; AoU-28, AoU-SEC-5).
  8. One E2E profile and data ID per safety-relevant signal (AoU-11, config-range CV-17).
  9. Degraded mappings only for degradable events, in groups that share no timer; the integrator confirms independence beyond timer and bus (AoU-32; SSR-088).
  10. The product image is built with -DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=ON (no test and fault-injection commands; AoU-SEC-6).
  11. bootloader.sbc_watchdog chosen deliberately (AoU-34).
  12. A hardware threshold (hw_thresholds, SM-58) may be configured but carries no credit (section 5); host verified, board proof not part of release R1; the input stays away from VDDA at start (AoU-37).
  13. On s32k1xx the LVD reset is always on (SM-59, not credited): the supply keeps VDD above 3.05 V (AoU-39).
  14. A PWM group with the start test of the active short (pwm.<group>.safe_state_test) only under the four conditions of AoU-38.
  15. Holds on the FlexNVM block short and never in a task below one that stores into the EEPROM emulation (AoU-40).
  16. No bus master other than the core enabled until a follow-up task (AoU-41); every task runs privileged (AoU-42).
  17. With the neXtBSW bootloader the ROM check SM-14 stays active in the image (AoU-CFG-7).
  18. An active short (pwm.<group>.safe_states, SM-26) only under AoU-33; the ECU reset (UDS 11) and every UDS service that writes a component port protected by security access and a precondition (AoU-ASA-b).

docs.text:
1. The interface description of the RTE: ports, types, runnables and their calling contract (ARXML, rte.yaml).
  2. The Embedded Coder settings neXtBSW applies to every component, which become part of his tool configuration and which he owns from then on — set by tools/swc/swc_prepare.m (and at creation by tools/swc/swc_create.m): SolverType Fixed-step, Solver FixedStepDiscrete, FixedStep = the base period of the runnables, EnableMultiTasking on for several rates without export functions, SystemTargetFile autosar.tlc, GenCodeOnly on, GenerateMakefile off, GenerateReport off, ProdHWDeviceType ARM Compatible → ARM Cortex-M, ProdLongLongMode on, SupportNonFinite off, MatFileLogging off, GenerateComments on, MaxIdLength 63; new components are export-function models (IsExportFunctionModel on). The list is read from the scripts at the working state of this issue; the scripts are the reference.
