docs.title: 10.2 Architectural and product limitations
docs.text:
• Single channel on one core: supervisor and supervised share core, clock domain, RAM, flash and supply; no lockstep, no second MCU voting (concept 2.1, AoU-13; dfa.md).
  • No partitioning of the application: the MPU protects the safety manager's data and stack only is open (concept 6.3, AoU-17). Task activation is not supervised (F10).
  • Register lock and check cover the classes derived by an earlier change; the remaining classes are SSR-070 (partial).
  • Run-time comparisons detect a change, not a wrong design (DFA-5 of dfa.md): the MPU descriptor check, the register check and the safe outputs table take their expected values from the same generated data that configured the hardware; a wrong design value, a generator fault or a wrong derivative fact is configured and expected alike. The design side is covered by tool confidence (section 9), generator tests with own profiles and mutants, and board tests of the generated result per project (AoU-DFA-c).
  • A PWM timer whose clock gate is switched off freezes its pins and does not take the walk of the safe outputs table (DFA-4): the group is de-energised only through a safe_off enable on another peripheral bound to it; nxconfig warns for a used group without one, and whether the walk opens the gate first is open for a separate task.
  • Read-back that S1 took effect (G1) closed on the host since an earlier change (S1) (S1 held, the groups of SD, the S1 + S2 sequence of ecu/safety); SSR-060 partial: the hard fault and watchdog handlers and the halt deadman of the family port, board proof B15/B16 open; no plausibility between two sources (G2), no age supervision of device values (G3), no safe state for bus-commanded actuators (G4) — SSR-061 … SSR-063 open.
  • Family port for s32k1xx only (section 1.4); SM-55 and the hardware threshold are not described for every derivative (fmea SM-55, hardware-mechanisms 2.4: S32K116).
  • The bootloader's own integrity is not checked by any stage-1 mechanism (fmea N4).
  • The bootloader phase runs without MCU watchdog (section 4, HSI 4.13): safe only with all outputs in their reset state while it runs (AoU-07, AoU-SEC-3); a hang there is ended by a reset from outside, not by neXtBSW.
  • A lost SIRC (the clock of the halt deadman's LPIT) is a residual risk (section 5, faults of the time bases; dfa.md DF-05): the halt deadman stops with it, nothing walks the table, and only the hardware reset of the MCU watchdog de-energises the outputs, after at most about 283 ms on the eval board; the cause of the hang is open, investigation and architecture with a separate task after release R1. A stopped system time is not seen by the period check (kind 4/5 see only a slow or fast one); the halt deadman SM-06 and the watchdog SM-01 react (section 5).

docs.title: 10.3 Evidence limitations
docs.text:
• Open board proofs named by the sources: of fmea.md 8, B8 and B10 ran (fmea.md 8.2; safety case EB-11, EB-09), B9 and B11 have records not yet linked on one image and B5 has none (safety case D-15); B16 (a), (c), (d) and the reset at falling supply (LVD, SM-59) are a known gap of Release R1, recorded after R1 with a separate task (safety case D-15); the degraded reaction SD (no board run, fmea SM-23), the gate-driver binding of a separate task, the hardware threshold of a separate task (host verified, board proof not part of release R1), the SBC watchdog serve with SDMS 0 (mock only).
  • Coverage thresholds of the safety modules are proposed, not all met (concept 9.2; component-qualification: modified copies 94.5 % statements, 55.0 % branches, 9 of 23 files without a host test).
  • Host tests use a different compiler from the target; the host/target difference analysis is missing (tool-classification 3.14, proposal I).
  • Tool qualification reports (proposal G) and the qualification of pre-existing software are not written for a release (safety plan R4).

docs.title: 11. Cybersecurity interface
docs.text:
neXtBSW has no cybersecurity management and makes no cybersecurity claim (security-interplay.md section 0). The safety claim covers random hardware and systematic faults; each security gap listed there lets an attacker bypass a mechanism, so the claim stands only together with the integrator's cybersecurity measures. The field interfaces IF-01 … IF-10, the protection that exists and the rules of the interplay are in security-interplay.md sections 2 and 3. The assumptions below keep their identifiers as final numbers.

ID The integrator's obligation Source AoU-SEC-1 Treat every write of program or calibration data as a security-relevant function of his item and protect it with his own measures; neXtBSW verifies integrity and compatibility of an image (SM-51), not its origin security-interplay 4 AoU-SEC-2 Keep the master key of the per-device keys and the provisioning step under his key management; a device key is known once the debug port of that device was open security-interplay 4 AoU-SEC-3 Programming session and ECU reset switch the safety function off for their duration: implement the vehicle-state precondition in the application hook, confirm that the pin reset state of every power output is safe while the bootloader runs security-interplay 4 AoU-SEC-4 Protect every DID and routine that writes a safety-relevant value or drives an output with a security level and an application interlock; decide on preconditions for clearing and suppressing DTCs security-interplay 4 AoU-SEC-5 XCP off in the product, or add resource protection for calibration; the plausibility check limits, it does not authenticate security-interplay 4 AoU-SEC-6 Build the product image without the test and fault-injection console commands (-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=ON); UART not accessible in the vehicle security-interplay 4 AoU-SEC-7 Close the debug port in the product (flash security or physically inaccessible); while open, none of the protections of IF-01 … IF-06 holds security-interplay 4 AoU-SEC-8 Protect data a safety function reads from the bus or NvM against deliberate manipulation where his threat analysis requires it; E2E protects against channel faults only security-interplay 4

docs.title: 12. Tailoring and process
docs.text:
Tailoring of the lifecycle for the SEooC (safety plan section 3; 2-6.4.5.7). Where an activity moves to the integrator, the assumption named in the last column makes the hand-over explicit.

ID Tailoring The integrator's side T-01 item definition, hazard analysis, functional and technical safety concept not performed; replaced by ASG and AoU AoU-01, AoU-02; section 3.2 T-02 hardware development, hardware metrics, random hardware failures, production not performed AoU-09; section 5 T-03 no quality management system, no evidence of competence AoU-35 T-04 no impact analysis at item level AoU-02; the change history per release (CHANGELOG.md) T-05 no development interface agreement negotiated on the basis of this manual T-06 no evaluation of hardware elements AoU-36; he evaluates MCU, SBC and board T-07 proven in use not used pre-existing software per 8-12 or part 6 (section 10.1) T-08 no ASIL decomposition at stage 1 he does not decompose into neXtBSW elements without his own analysis T-09 functional safety assessment deferred AoU-35 T-10 embedded tests on the reference eval board and the host; configuration range argued for the project's configurations AoU-26, AoU-CFG-1 … AoU-CFG-7 T-11 Deviation, not a tailoring: confirmation measures performed for now by the safety manager himself, without the independence I1 (decision 2026-09-30, AN-093); lifted when the safety manager names an independent person (iso-q1), and from then on every measure performed under it is reviewed again at I1 (safety plan issue 2, T-11) AoU-35: no independent confirmation; a working state carries no ASIL statement until an independent review; for release R1 also the deviation of CM-03, CM-08, CM-09 and CM-11 (safety plan section 5, safety case D-22)

Confirmation measures (safety plan section 5): 11 measures CM-01 … CM-11 planned at independence I1; the procedure, checklists and packages exist (reviews/README.md (not published, available on request)). Since 2026-09-30 (decision of the safety responsible, AN-093, tailoring T-11): the safety manager performs them himself for now. That is not independent: a record of such a review is a confirmation without independence, and the working states it looks at keep no ASIL statement until an independent person has reviewed them. This manual is the work product of CM-10. Deviation for release R1 (decision of the safety responsible 2026-10-03, safety-plan.md section 5, deficit D-22 of safety-case.md): CM-10, CM-05, CM-06, CM-04, CM-07 and CM-02 are performed before release R1, CM-03, CM-08, CM-09 and CM-11 after it; the deviation is lifted before the first release with an ASIL B claim (restated 2026-10-08, safety plan issue 3, released in the delta re-check of CM-01 the same day). Until then every release, private or public, is a development release without a safety claim, and every recipient receives that statement together with this manual; it stands in the README.md of the repository and in every release note (safety plan section 5, C2).

Release (safety plan section 6): a safety release is an annotated tag vX.Y.Z on master with a green archived CI run, safety documents citing the tag, qualification reports, closed confirmation reviews, and safety case and safety manual issued for it (preconditions R1 … R6, the same list as P1 … P9 of cm-plan.md section 5.1; mapping in safety plan section 6). No tag meets R1 … R6 today; every tag, v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 alike, is a development release without a safety claim.

docs.title: 13. Work products
docs.text:
The work products an integrator may request, with their state (status words of the document register, anomaly-register.md section 6, read at the working state of this manual). None belongs to a safety release yet; each carries the working state it was checked against in its header (cm-plan.md section 6). "Accepted" names the issue or state the safety manager accepted; several documents were changed after that by later tasks (register section 6, "Accepted, then changed"), and a later change waits for acceptance again. docs.title: 14. Checklist of the safety manual content (11-5.1.11 by analogy)
docs.text:
The gap analysis (section 4, point 1) lists what the safety manual of an element out of context typically contains, for the MCU case of 11-5.1.11, applicable by analogy. Where each item is in this manual:

Item (own words) Section assumed requirements the element fulfils, with ASIL 3.2 assumptions on the design outside the element 2, 7 safe states 4 maximum fault handling times 5, 6 configuration of the element for safe use 8 applicable work products 13 tailoring of the lifecycle 12 confirmation measures and their independence 12 safety mechanisms and their coverage as input for the hardware metrics 5 known limitations, including non-qualified parts 10

docs.title: neXtBSW safety plan — software SEooC at ASIL B
docs.text:
Title Safety plan - software SEooC at ASIL B Issue 3, 2026-10-08 (the deviation for release R1 restated in section 5 after the decision of the safety responsible of 2026-10-08); issue 2: 2026-10-02 (after the confirmation review CR-01-1); issue 1: 2026-09-28 Author issue 1, issue 2 (issue 3) — contributors writing on the maintainer's behalf, author side; the updates in between by the tasks of section 12 Approver the safety manager: issue 1 released 2026-10-02 with the review set of 15 safety documents; issue 2 released 2026-10-02 in the re-check of CM-01 (findings F-01 … F-08 of reviews/records/CR-01-1.md closed by the reviewer, the safety manager under D-01, without independence); issue 3 released 2026-10-08 in the delta re-check of CM-01 (delta review of section 5, reviews/README.md section 4; record reviews/records/CR-01-1.md, points C1 … C3, the safety manager under D-01, without independence) Status issue 3 accepted (released 2026-10-08 in the delta re-check of CM-01, record CR-01-1; D-01, without independence); issue 2 accepted (D-01, without independence) Change history section 12

Working state: dev at c0928380 (after v1.0.0-rc1)

Issue 1 was written against dev at ae92e89; issue 2 checks the statuses against the task list and the tree at dev 3405bf72 (merge of an integration branch); issue 3 changes only the deviation for release R1 in section 5 (the condition that lifts it), written against dev 9bf2d520; the activity statuses of section 4 were not re-checked. The delta re-check of CM-01 on 2026-10-08 added the sentence on README.md and the release notes in section 5 (C2) and released issue 3 (C3), recorded against dev c0928380. Readers: the project manager and safety manager, the maintainer who plans and merges the tasks named here, the contributors of the safety tasks, and later an integrator or reviewer who wants to know how neXtBSW was developed. Language: English, like the rest of doc/.

What this document is. The safety plan that the gap analysis iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) found missing (rows 2-09 and 2-11, proposed task 1). It states the claim neXtBSW makes, names the people responsible, tailors the safety lifecycle for a software Safety Element out of Context (SEooC), lists every activity of parts 2, 6, 8 and 9 of ISO 26262:2018 with objective, responsible role, work product and status, plans the confirmation measures with their independence and defines what a release is. The consistency test test/test_safety_plan.py checks that every work product named here exists or has a task.

Licence rule. The standard is cited by part and clause only (for example "6-9.4.4" = ISO 26262-6:2018, clause 9.4.4). No text, table or figure of the standard is reproduced; requirements are restated in our own words.

What it is not. Not a safety case, not a safety manual, not a statement that neXtBSW complies. The plan says what is done, by whom and with which result; the evidence is in the work products it names.

docs.text: Question Answer Claim neXtBSW is developed following the methods of ISO 26262-6 at ASIL B, without the management part — a software SEooC with ASIL B capability, stage 1 (base-software mechanisms, concept section 1.4) Openly stated limitations no quality management system (2-5.4.5), no evidence of competence (2-5.4.4), no confirmation review by an independent person (2-6.4.9, 2-6.4.10): since 2026-09-30 the safety manager performs the confirmation measures himself (AN-093, T-11), without independence; they go into the safety manual as assumptions of use (AoU-35) Roles (section 2) project manager and safety manager: the repository owner (maintainer, GitHub danielsimonreinhardt), confirmed by the safety manager on 2026-09-28; maintainer plans and merges; contributors author; confirmation reviewer for now the safety manager himself (decision 2026-09-30, AN-093, T-11 — not independent); an independent reviewer is still to be named (iso-q1) Tailoring (section 3) 11 tailoring decisions with rationale (2-6.4.5.7) — ten tailorings of the lifecycle and one deviation (T-11), listed in the same table so that every activity names its ID: item-level work (parts 3, 4, 5, 7, hardware metrics, item impact analysis) goes to the integrator through assumptions; QMS and competence are not provided; the development interface agreement, the evaluation of hardware elements, proven in use and ASIL decomposition are not used; the functional safety assessment is deferred; the confirmation measures are performed by the safety manager himself without independence — a deviation, lifted when an independent person is named (T-11, 2026-09-30) Activities (section 4) 53 activities of parts 2 (16), 6 (22), 8 (11) and 9 (4), covering all 97 gap rows 2-01 … 9-11 of iso26262-gap.md. Status: 15 done, 24 partial, 6 in progress, 1 planned, 7 tailored (issue 1 at the review: 9 done, 21 partial, 9 in progress, 7 planned) Confirmation measures (section 5) 11 measures; 5 of them need independence I1 at ASIL B (safety plan, safety analyses, DFA, integration and test strategy, safety case), the other 6 are planned at I1 by project choice; all 11 prepared by an earlier change; since 2026-09-30 performed by the safety manager himself (T-11) — a confirmation without independence, which gives no working state an ASIL statement; 1 performed: CM-01 on 2026-10-02 (record reviews/records/CR-01-1.md, accepted with conditions, 8 minor findings corrected by an earlier change) Release (section 6) a release is an annotated tag vX.Y.Z on master; before it: green CI run with archived report, safety documents citing the tag, qualification reports, closed confirmation reviews. docs.title: 1.1 The element
docs.text: neXtBSW as described in concept.md section 1: the base software (MCU drivers, safety mechanisms of the base software, RTE, generators) as a software component SEooC (10-9.2.4) with ASIL B capability (10-9.1). Stage 1 argues ASIL B with the mechanisms of the base software only (concept 1.4); the device drivers' own mechanisms are stage 2 and not covered by this issue. The item, its hazard analysis, its safety goals, its hardware and the application software are outside the element (concept 1.2, AoU-01, AoU-09, AoU-17).

docs.title: 1.2 The claim
docs.text:
neXtBSW is developed following the methods of ISO 26262-6 at ASIL B, without the management part.

Decided by the safety manager on 2026-09-22 (iso-q2). What it means:

  • Parts 6, 8 and 9 are applied at ASIL B for the element, with the tailoring of section 3. Where a method is not applied the rationale is given in the work product (6-4.3 reading).
  • Part 2 is applied as far as a single-person open-source project can apply it: a safety plan (this document), roles, tailoring, safety case, confirmation measures and a release procedure. What cannot be provided is stated, not assumed:
  • no quality management system in the sense of 2-5.4.5;
  • no evidence of competence of the persons in the lifecycle in the sense of 2-5.4.4 — most work is written by contributors on the safety manager's behalf and reviewed by the maintainer and the safety manager;
  • no independent confirmation review yet (2-6.4.9, 2-6.4.10): by the decision of the safety responsible of 2026-09-30 (AN-093, tailoring T-11) the safety manager performs the confirmation measures of section 5 himself for now. That is a confirmation without independence: its records find and close findings, but no development state gets an ASIL statement from them, and no release may claim ASIL B capability until an independent person has reviewed it.
  • The integrator who uses neXtBSW in a safety-related item takes over these gaps under his own management of functional safety; the safety manual states them as assumptions of use (gap analysis proposal C8).

docs.title: 2. Roles
docs.text:
Appointment of project manager and safety manager according to 2-6.4.2. The table is the reference for the column "Responsible" of sections 4 and 5; the consistency test rejects any other value there.

Role Held by Responsibility and authority project manager the repository owner (maintainer, GitHub danielsimonreinhardt) scope, priorities and resources of neXtBSW; decides; approves merges to master and every release (section 6) safety manager the repository owner (maintainer, GitHub danielsimonreinhardt) owns this plan and the safety case; decides on tailoring, on the safety claim and on the closure of safety anomalies; confirms the ASIL-B relevance of changes maintainer the maintainer (one at a time, "Nur eine Sitzung schreibt Planung und Merges") turns this plan into tasks in the task list, writes the task briefs, re-runs tests and builds, merges to dev, keeps the status columns of this plan up to date author the contributor or person who writes a work product (a task branch or a session branch) produces the work product with its verification and changelog fragment; never reviews its own work confirmation reviewer for now the safety manager himself (decision of the safety responsible 2026-09-30, AN-093, tailoring T-11); an independent person is still to be named (iso-q1, safety manager: "Reviewer spaeter klaeren") performs the confirmation reviews of section 5; planned at independence I1 (a person other than the author and other than the safety manager as author-side approver), performed by the safety manager without independence until that person is named; eligibility, the deviation D-01 and signature: doc/safety/reviews/README.md section 3 integrator the organisation that builds an item on neXtBSW (outside the project) item-level work handed over by the tailoring of section 3; validates the assumptions of use at integration (2-6.4.5.7, 10-9.2.4.5)

Confirmation of the appointment (N4, done). The safety manager confirmed the appointment of project manager and safety manager, entry (opened by an earlier change on 2026-09-28, answered "bestaetigen" by the maintainer on 2026-09-28). The table above is the maintainer's word, not a proposal of the plan. Issue 2 (finding F-04 of CR-01-1): issue 1 still called the entry open and dated it 2026-09-30.

One person, two roles. Project manager and safety manager are the same person. The standard allows that; it requires that the responsibility is assigned and that the person has the authority (2-6.4.2). The independence that matters at ASIL B is the one of the confirmation reviews (section 5), not the one between these two roles.

The approver is author side. Work products are written by contributors on the safety manager's behalf. The safety manager's acceptance (…) is a real review, but it is a review by the commissioning side, not an independent one. This plan therefore counts it as verification review (part 8-9), not as confirmation review. Whether the safety manager wants to see this differently is part of iso-q1. 2026-09-30 (AN-093): the safety manager decided to perform the confirmation measures himself for now; this plan records it as the deviation T-11, not as independence — his records stay author side (first: CR-01-1, 2026-10-02).

docs.title: 3. Tailoring of the lifecycle for the SEooC
docs.text:
2-6.4.5.1 requires every tailoring to be defined in the safety plan with a rationale; 2-6.4.5.7 says for an SEooC that the requirements are derived from assumptions on intended use and context, including the external interfaces, and that the assumptions are validated at integration. The tailoring below applies these two clauses. A tailoring does not remove the objective: where an activity moves to the integrator, the safety manual carries the assumption that makes the hand-over explicit.

T-01 … T-10 are tailorings of the lifecycle. T-11 is not a tailoring but a deviation from a requirement that applies at ASIL B (the independence of the confirmation measures); it stands in the same table because every activity and every document names it by this ID, and it says what lifts it.

ID Clause(s) Tailoring Rationale Consequence T-01 2-6.4.5.7, 10-9.2.4.2, 10-9.2.4.3 Item definition, hazard analysis and risk assessment, functional and technical safety concept (parts 3 and 4) are not performed; they are replaced by assumed safety goals (ASG-01 … ASG-07) and assumptions of use (AoU-01 …) in concept.md, from which the software safety requirements are derived an SEooC is developed without a known item; the standard's guideline for this case is to assume the higher-level requirements and to validate the assumptions at integration the integrator compares ASG and AoU with his own safety concept (AoU-02); the level of assumed technical safety requirements between ASG and SSR is stated in safety-manual.md section 3.2 (gap proposal C2) T-02 parts 5 and 7, 5-8, 5-9 Hardware development, hardware architectural metrics, evaluation of random hardware failures and production are not performed the element is software; hardware and production belong to the item; the element contributes per mechanism what the integrator's metrics need (gap section 3) AoU-09; the re-based coverage table per mechanism goes into the safety manual (gap proposal M2) T-03 2-5.4.4, 2-5.4.5 No quality management system and no evidence of competence are provided a single-person open-source project has neither; the safety manager decided (iso-q2) to claim the part-6 methods without the management part instead of claiming what cannot be shown stated in the claim (section 1.2) and as assumption of use in the safety manual (gap proposal C8); the integrator's own QMS covers the integration T-04 2-6.4.3 The impact analysis at item level is not performed there is no item; for a changed element version the integrator decides at item level AoU-02; the element supplies a change history per release (CHANGELOG, section 6) T-05 8-5 No development interface agreement no customer during SEooC development; the safety manual carries the interface to the integrator an integrator who wants a development interface agreement negotiates it on the basis of a separate task T-06 8-13 No evaluation of hardware elements hardware is outside the element (AoU-09); MCU, SBC and board are chosen by the integrator, so the element has no hardware element of its own to evaluate the integrator evaluates MCU, SBC and board; the MCU's safety manual (N2 of fmea.md) is his input T-07 8-14 Proven in use is not used as an argument for any component there is no field data; the route would need operating hours we cannot show pre-existing software takes the qualification route of 8-12 or is developed per part 6 T-08 9-5 No ASIL decomposition at stage 1 all stage-1 requirements are ASIL B and implemented on one MCU; decomposition is kept for a later ASIL C/D stage (concept 2.1) the integrator must not decompose into neXtBSW elements without his own analysis T-09 2-6.4.12 The functional safety assessment is deferred: not planned for issue 1 it is only recommended at ASIL B and needs an independent assessor — the same blocker as the confirmation reviews (iso-q1); it adds nothing before those reviews exist reconsidered by the safety manager before the first release that claims ASIL B capability; the integrator may assess the element within his item assessment T-10 6-11.4.1, 6-11.4.4 Tests of the embedded software run on the reference eval board and the host, not on the integrator's ECU; the admissible configuration range is argued for the configurations the project builds, not for all the target ECU is unknown for an SEooC; the element can only be tested on representative hardware and configurations the integrator repeats the target tests on his ECU and verifies his configuration data set (AoU-26, 6-C.4.5); the range argument is config-range.md (proposal N3) T-11 2-6.4.9, 2-6.4.10 Deviation, not a tailoring: the confirmation measures of section 5 are performed for now by the safety manager himself, not by a person independent of the author side — a deviation from the required independence (I1, required at ASIL B for CM-01 … CM-05). Lifted when the safety manager names an independent person (iso-q1); from then on every measure performed under this deviation is reviewed again at I1 (run k+1, full scope) decision of the safety responsible of 2026-09-30 on the escalated anomaly AN-093: "Die Prüfungen (Bestätigungsmaßnahmen) führt vorerst der Maintainer selbst durch"; no independent person is named (iso-q1) and the reviews shall not wait for one the records of these reviews are confirmations without independence: they find and close findings, but they give no development state an ASIL statement and do not meet the release precondition R5 for a safety release; every tag stays a development release until an independent person has reviewed the work products (AoU-35). Who carries it until then: the safety manager, who keeps iso-q1 open, and the integrator, who takes over the missing independent confirmation under his own management of functional safety (AoU-35); no date is set — no release that claims ASIL B capability is planned (R5). Procedure and record rules: doc/safety/reviews/README.md section 3 (deviation D-01)

What is not tailored: part 6 is applied at ASIL B in full; the software safety requirements, the architecture, the unit design and verification, the integration and the target tests stay required activities of the element. Neither are the safety case, the confirmation reviews and the release procedure — they are planned (sections 4–6); the reviews are performed without independence until T-11 is lifted.

Decisions that shape the plan without being tailoring:

  • Coexistence (iso-q4): QM parts stay QM only with a freedom-from-interference argument per module (9-6); the separating element (RTOS, MPU code) must be ASIL B (6-7.4.9). Tasks. Worked out in coexistence.md: 21 of 36 modules are ASIL B (13 mechanisms, 3 separating elements, 5 dependencies); of the 9 QM modules with code in the image only XCP is fully argued today, the other 8 count as ASIL B until a follow-up task and the findings CX-1 … CX-3 close their open rows.
  • FreeRTOS route (iso-q5): decided on 2026-09-22, after the comparison rtos-comparison.md (done) and with the hardening of the OS boundary (done): neXtBSW stays on FreeRTOS and qualifies it. The route is carried out by an earlier change (plan and report QR-01, done) and the FreeRTOS qualification package (rows P6-07 and P8-09); open point O2 is closed (AN-094).
  • Single exit (iso-q6): MISRA C:2012 rule 15.5 is re-enabled for the safety units. Task.

docs.title: 5. Confirmation measures
docs.text:
2-6.4.9 and 2-6.4.10 require confirmation reviews of the key work products, and for ASIL B a set of them by a person other than the author (independence I1). The standard's list is restated in our words: the safety plan, the safety analyses and dependent failure analysis, the integration and test strategy, and the safety case need I1 at ASIL B; the safety validation specification is item level and handed over by T-01. The rest below is planned at I1 as a project choice, because the whole argument leans on those documents.

"Reviewer" is a role of section 2. An earlier change prepared the procedure, the record template and the review packages. Since 2026-09-30 (AN-093, T-11): the safety manager performs the measures himself for now (CM-03 including AN-074 and AN-075). The column "Independence" keeps what is required; a measure performed by the maintainer reaches performed or closed with a record, but without independence — it does not meet R5 and gives no working state an ASIL statement until an independent person has reviewed it.

before the first release closed CM-03 Confirmation review of the dependent failure analysis doc/safety/dfa.md I1 required at B confirmation reviewer after a later change; before the first release prepared CM-04 Confirmation review of the integration and test strategy doc/safety/verification-plan.md I1 required at B confirmation reviewer after a later change; Deviation for release R1 (decision of the safety responsible, 2026-10-03). R1 is a development release without a safety claim (D-01; R5 is not met). Measure Reason for performing it after R1 CM-03 The anomaly AN-074 (completeness of the DFA topic list against part 9 clause 7 and its informative annex) is open and part of this measure; it needs a reader of the licensed standard. The findings DFA-1... DFA-6 are implemented by an earlier change (carried into dev for R1, task in review), so the review can take the DFA as it stands, but it is not done before R1 CM-08 The qualification reports of the tools with TCL 2 do not exist yet (open; K08-05 of the checklist waits for them; D-11, precondition R4) CM-09 The FreeRTOS qualification package and the kernel internals of the async layer (AN-057) are open, and component-qualification.md is not yet released by the safety responsible (issue pending) CM-11 By its definition the audit takes place once, before the first release claiming ASIL B capability, and after the records of CM-01 ... docs.title: 6. Release
docs.text:
The safety manager decided on 2026-09-22 (iso-q3): "Freigabe = annotierter Tag vX.Y.Z auf master, vorher gruener CI-Lauf mit archiviertem Bericht, Sicherheitsdokumente mit Verweis auf den Tag, Qualifizierungsberichte, abgeschlossene Reviews." This section turns the decision into the preconditions of 2-6.4.13 for the element. The details of tag naming, signing and configuration items are a separate task's (cm-plan.md).

ID Precondition before tagging vX.Y.Z on master Evidence R1 The release commit is on master, merged from dev with the safety manager's approval, and gets an annotated tag vX.Y.Z the tag and its message R2 A green CI run on the tree that is tagged (same tree hash, clean, strict), its report bound to that tree and archived with the tool versions archived CI report R3 Every safety document of this plan cites the tag instead of loose commits (gap finding SG7) document headers R4 The qualification reports of the tools (TCL 2) and of the pre-existing components are available for that version qualification reports R5 The confirmation reviews of section 5 and the verification inspections (code inspection of the safety units; inspections of section 4) are performed and closed for that version, the confirmation reviews at I1 — a record under deviation T-11 (D-01) does not count review and inspection records R6 The safety case and the safety manual are issued for that version safety-case.md, safety-manual.md

R and P are one list (issue 2, CR-01-1 F-07). cm-plan.md section 5.1 states the same preconditions as P1 … P9, with how each is checked; a safety release needs all of them. The mapping:

cm-plan Safety plan Note P1 R1 candidate complete on dev, VERSION and changelog section P2 R2 green CI run on the tagged tree, report bound and archived P3 R1 repository integrity before the tag P4 R3 state lines Baseline: vX.Y.Z P5 R4 qualification reports P6 R5 confirmation reviews at I1 and inspections closed P7 R1 the safety manager's approval of merge and tag P8 — export of a release line (tools/distcheck); a configuration-management precondition without a safety counterpart P9 R6 safety case and safety manual of the release — binding through R6 since issue 1 of this plan

A tag that does not meet R1–R6 is a development release (the term of cm-plan.md 4.2 and of the tag message): it may be tagged for reproducibility but carries no safety claim, and its tag message says so. As long as no independent confirmation reviewer is named (R5, T-11), every tag is a development release. Releases of the open-source branch and of licensed branches follow the same rule per branch.

docs.title: 7. Maintaining the plan
docs.text:
• Owner: the safety manager. Kept up to date by: the maintainer.
  • Updates of the current issue: when a task named in section 4 or 5 changes its status to done, the maintainer sets the row's status in the same merge; when a new safety task is created, the maintainer adds it to the row it serves; when a proposal of section 8 becomes a task, the rows name the task instead of the proposal. Each update gets a line in the change history (section 12).
  • New issue (rule sharpened in issue 2 after CR-01-1 F-08): the plan gets a new issue when its argument changes — the claim, a role, a tailoring or deviation of section 3, a confirmation measure, a release precondition — and then CM-01 is repeated for the change (delta review, reviews/README.md section 4). Issue 1 missed this twice: the deviation T-11 came as an update, and the release v0.2.0 carried the plan unchecked as issue 1.
  • At a release: the plan is re-checked against the candidate and its state line becomes Baseline: vX.Y.Z (R3, cm-plan.md P4); if the plan was changed since its last confirmation review, the release is a development release or CM-01 is repeated first. Between releases the state line is Working state: dev at <commit> (after vX.Y.Z) (cm-plan.md 6.1).
  • Checked by: doc/safety/test/test_safety_plan.py. The test fails when a named task disappears from the task list, when a task is done although its work product is still missing, when a done row names a missing work product, or when a gap row of parts 2, 6, 8, 9 is no longer served; since issue 2 also when the plan lags behind: a row still names a proposal whose task is done (or a carried proposal at all), a row is planned although one of its tasks has started and its work products exist, a measure of section 5 is prepared although a record with a verdict exists (or performed/closed without one), or the mapping R ↔ P of section 6 misses a precondition of cm-plan.md 5.1. A red test is the signal to update this plan, not to relax the test.
  • Change impact: added the optional field safety_impact to the tasks; until it is filled for the tasks that change the safety part (N9), the maintainer decides per merge whether a change affects a work product of this plan (8-8.4.3).

docs.title: 10. Review questions of the architecture (section 11)
docs.text: This task changes no code, no generator, no configuration and nothing under platforms/: one document and one consistency test. Board without an SBC, different crystal, derivative, CAN buses, task set: the plan contains no board fact; the one derivative-specific work product (hsi-s32k1xx.md) is named per family, and further families get their own HSI work product through the same row. New values in one configuration level: none. Host test with its own test profile: test_safety_plan.py checks the plan against the repository and against deliberately broken copies of itself; it needs no board profile. Qt-free core, YAML paths: not affected. Device-driver granularity, platform rule: not applicable. Issue 2 changes the same document and its test only; the answers stand.

docs.title: neXtBSW — interplay of functional safety and cybersecurity (N1)
docs.text:
Baseline: v0.2.0

Status: 2026-09-30, issue 1 (proposal N1 of safety-plan.md), written against dev at 65f3dc9. Readers: the safety manager, the author of any change to the bootloader, UDS, XCP or the console, the integrator who runs the cybersecurity engineering of his item, and the author of the safety manual. Language: English, like the rest of doc/.

What this document is. The record of the interplay between functional safety and cybersecurity that the gap analysis found missing (iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) row 2-02, clause 2-5.4.2.3: the safety organisation keeps communication channels to the cybersecurity side where both touch). For an element without a cybersecurity process of its own the channel is this document: it lists every interface through which code, configuration, calibration data or safety-relevant state of a running ECU can be changed in the field, says what a change through it does to the safety argument, which protection exists, and what the integrator must add as an assumption of use for the safety manual.

What it is not. Not a threat analysis and risk assessment and not a cybersecurity concept: neXtBSW has no cybersecurity management and makes no cybersecurity claim. Attack feasibility, risk values and cybersecurity goals belong to the integrator's item-level engineering; this document hands him the interfaces and their safety effect as input. Cryptographic hardware and secure boot are the subject of csec-concept.md; they are cited, not repeated.

Licence rule. ISO 26262 is cited by part and clause only. No other standard is quoted.

docs.title: 0. Result in one page
docs.text: Question Answer Field interfaces (section 2) 10: application download and erase over CAN (IF-01), bootloader self-update (IF-02), entry into the bootloader (IF-03), UDS services of the application (IF-04), XCP calibration (IF-05), calibration segment in flash (IF-06), UART console (IF-07), debug port (IF-08), non-volatile data (IF-09), received CAN signals (IF-10) What an unauthorised change can do to the safety argument replace or corrupt the safety mechanisms themselves (IF-01, IF-02, IF-08), change a safety parameter (IF-05, IF-06), stop the safety function or force the safe state (IF-03, IF-04, IF-07), inject faults on purpose (IF-07), feed wrong values to a safety function (IF-10) Protection that exists security access with a per-device HMAC key in the bootloader and in the application; CRC and compatibility check of every image (SM-51); plausibility of safety-relevant parameters before every XCP write and at start; CALV record with CRC; production profile without XCP; fault-injection and power-stage commands behind build options off by default What does not exist no signature of images, flash security (FSEC) never set — the debug port reads and writes everything, including the device keys; no authentication of the console and of XCP; no precondition on 10 02 / 11 in the application; E2E is not a security mechanism; no SecOC Effect on the safety claim none of these gaps invalidates a stage-1 mechanism against random hardware and systematic faults, which is what the claim covers; each of them lets an attacker bypass a mechanism. The claim therefore stands only together with the integrator's cybersecurity measures, stated as assumptions of use AoU-SEC-1 … AoU-SEC-8 (section 4) Rules for the interplay (section 3) 6 rules: security measures never weaken a safety reaction; safety test paths are security hazards and leave the product; a security finding that reaches a safety function is a safety anomaly; and three more New tasks proposed (section 6) S1 flash security in the product, S2 precondition hook for session change and reset, S3 XCP resource protection or product build without XCP, S4 security section in the safety manual; existing tasks that close gaps: Verification mock/host: doc/safety/test/test_security_interplay.py checks the interface register against the repository (every named path exists, every task exists, every interface has protection, gap and assumption, every AoU and proposal is used) with counter-checks. The facts were read from the code at 65f3dc9; nothing was run on the board for this document

docs.title: 1. Method
docs.text:
Interface. Any path by which, on an ECU in the field and without rebuilding the software, one of the following changes: the program code (application, bootloader), the configuration or calibration data the safety mechanisms use, the non-volatile state they read, or the run-time state of a safety function (running, safe state, reset). An interface that only reads (UDS read services, XCP upload) is not listed; its confidentiality aspect is the integrator's.

Effect on the safety argument. Which assumed safety goal (ASG), software safety requirement (SSR) or mechanism (SM) of concept.md an unauthorised or erroneous use of the interface can defeat, and whether a stage-1 mechanism would still detect it. "Detected" means detected as a fault, not recognised as an attack.

Sources. The code at 65f3dc9 (paths in the table), the project files of the demo (projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo/{project,diag}.yaml), csec-concept.md, tool-classification.md (AoU-26 … AoU-29) and concept.md (AoU-10, AoU-16).

docs.title: 2. Interface register
docs.text:
ID Interface Where Can change Effect on the safety argument Existing protection Gap Assumption Task IF-01 Application download and erase over CAN (bootloader, UDS 10 02, 27, 2E fingerprint, 31 erase/check, 34/36/37) bootloader/src/core/uds.c, bootloader/src/core/seedkey.c, bootloader/src/core/app_image.c, tools/canflash the whole application image, including every safety mechanism of the application and its generated configuration an image without, or with changed, safety mechanisms runs as if it were the released one; SM-51 checks integrity and compatibility, not origin programming session + security access, key = HMAC-SHA256 over a per-device key, 3 tries then 10 s lockout; fingerprint before erase; erase limited to the application area; CRC-32 over the image, compatibility block (target, layout), entry vectors (SM-51, SSR-051) no signature; the device key is readable over the debug port while FSEC is unsecured (IF-08); lockout counter in no-init RAM, cleared by a power cycle AoU-SEC-1, AoU-SEC-2 – IF-02 Bootloader self-update (canflash blupdate, updater image) bootloader/updater, tools/canflash the bootloader, and with it SM-51 a changed bootloader can start any image and removes the image check the updater is loaded like an application (same security access); the SBC driver refuses writes to the MTPNV no authentication; the other commands are always built AoU-SEC-6 – IF-08 Debug port (SWD) bootloader/platforms/s32k1xx/startup.S, bootloader/updater everything: flash, RAM, registers, device keys; the core can be halted every mechanism can be bypassed; a halt stops the safety task and the watchdog (WDOG CS[DBG] = 0) the halt deadman walks the safe outputs table after its time-out (SM-06, AoU-16); nothing else Flash Configuration Field unsecured (FSEC 0xFE), backdoor key disabled, nothing sets FSEC; the updater enforces the unsecured field AoU-SEC-7 S1 IF-09 Non-volatile data (FlexNVM EEPROM emulation: DEM blocks, RTE NvM blocks) ecu/application/src/systems/RteSystem.cpp, platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/CMakeLists.txt stored DTCs and NvM blocks of the application stage-1 mechanisms read no NvM data (AoU-19); a safety function of the application that restores a value from NvM does NvM writes only from the application and the console (nvm write, dem clear); partitioning behind a build option; SBC MTPNV is never written no integrity protection of NvM blocks against deliberate change AoU-SEC-8 – IF-10 Received CAN signals of the RTE libs/bsw/e2e, tools/rtegen the values safety functions of the application compute with wrong commands or measurements reach the application E2E profiles P01/P02/P11 per configured signal (SM-31): counter, data ID and CRC against random and systematic faults of the channel E2E is not a security mechanism: the profile is public, anybody on the bus can form a valid frame; no SecOC AoU-SEC-8 –

Remarks on the register:

  • IF-01 and IF-02 are the ones that matter most. They replace the element itself. The security access with a per-device key is a real barrier against a casual tester, but as long as the debug port is open (IF-08) the key can be read from the key sector, and as long as the image is not signed, anybody who has the key of one device can load any image with a matching CRC into it. For the safety argument this means: the evidence of the safety case is about the released image; which image runs in the field is protected only by the integrator's measures.
  • IF-03 is safety-relevant even when it is authorised. Programming a vehicle while the item is active switches its safety function off. neXtBSW has no information about the vehicle state; the application hook isModeChangePossible() is the place where the integrator's precondition belongs (S2).
  • IF-05 is the interface where safety and security already meet in code. The plausibility check of a separate task is a safety mechanism (it limits a legitimate but wrong calibration); it happens to limit an attacker too, but only to the range of the design. The production profile of a separate task is the actual closure.
  • IF-07: the fault-injection commands are needed for the verification of the safety mechanisms (board tests of fmea.md section 8). They are a security hazard in a product removes them from the product build.
  • IF-10: the safety case must not count E2E as protection against manipulation. The concept states E2E against faults of the communication channel only (SM-31).

docs.title: 2.1 Security mechanisms seen from safety
docs.text:
A security mechanism that reacts at the wrong moment can itself create a hazard or remove a safety reaction. The existing mechanisms were checked for that:

Mechanism Could it weaken a safety reaction? Result lockout after 3 failed security attempts (bootloader 10 s, application 10 s) it blocks programming and the protected diagnostic jobs only; no safety reaction depends on them no effect refusal of an XCP write (ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE) the previous value stays; the design range is kept no effect (it is a safety mechanism) on_invalid: refuse of the calibration segment the application does not start its runnables; the safety task and the supervisor run, outputs stay off safe by design updater refuses a secured Flash Configuration Field prevents an accidental lock, but also prevents securing the chip by update (S1) no safety effect; a security gap session time-out of the bootloader (S3 server 5 s) the bootloader stays in programming; the application does not run availability only

docs.title: 3. Rules for the interplay
docs.text:
These rules apply to every change of neXtBSW that touches one of the interfaces of section 2, and to the review of such a change. They are the communication channel of 2-5.4.2.3 for an element without a security organisation.

ID Rule R-1 A security measure never delays or removes a safety reaction: detection, the safe outputs table walk, the safe state and the reset of the safe supervisor keep precedence over every lockout, authentication or session state. R-2 A path that exists to test a safety mechanism (fault injection, safe state on command, register writes behind a driver) is a security hazard: it stays behind a build option that is off in the product build, or it is removed from the product build. R-3 A security finding that can reach a safety function or change what runs on the ECU is a safety anomaly: it goes into the anomaly register with its effect on the interfaces of section 2, and the safety manager decides. R-4 A change that adds, widens or removes an interface of section 2 updates this register in the same merge; the maintainer treats it as a change with safety impact (8-8.4.3). R-5 No safety requirement relies on a security mechanism: the stage-1 mechanisms are argued against faults; where a safety argument needs protection against deliberate change, it is stated as an assumption of use (section 4), not claimed. R-6 Protection that is configurable (XCP on/off, production profile, security levels in diag.yaml, flash security) is a configuration value in exactly one configuration level and is checked by tools/nxconfig with the YAML path where a combination is unsafe (as for profile: production with xcp).

docs.title: 4. Assumptions of use proposed for the safety manual
docs.text:
Numbered AoU-SEC-n here so that they do not collide with numbers other tasks propose in parallel gives them their final numbers. They refine AoU-10, AoU-16 and AoU-28, which remain valid.

ID Assumption of use Interfaces AoU-SEC-1 The integrator treats every write of program or calibration data (application, bootloader, calibration segment) as a security-relevant function of his item and protects it with his own measures (secured workshop access, signed images once a related task is available, key management of the per-device keys). neXtBSW verifies integrity and compatibility of an image (SM-51), not its origin. IF-01, IF-02, IF-06 AoU-SEC-2 The master key from which the per-device keys are derived, and the provisioning step that writes them (tools/canflash/provision.py), are kept under the integrator's key management; a device key must be assumed known once the debug port of that device was open. IF-01, IF-02 AoU-SEC-3 Entry into the programming session (10 02, lc bootloader) and the ECU reset (11) switch the safety function of the item off for their duration. The integrator implements the vehicle-state precondition (e.g. vehicle stationary, power stage off) in the application hook for session changes, and confirms that the pin reset state of every power output is safe while the bootloader runs. IF-03, IF-04 AoU-SEC-4 Every DID and routine of the integrator's diag.yaml that writes a safety-relevant value or drives an output is protected by a security level and interlocked by the application (refines AoU-28). The integrator decides whether clearing DTCs (14) and suppressing their setting (85) needs a precondition in his item. IF-04 AoU-SEC-5 In the product, XCP is off (memory.calibration.profile: production or no xcp: section / NX_XCP=OFF), or the integrator adds resource protection for calibration; the plausibility check of a separate task limits values to the design range but does not authenticate (refines AoU-28). IF-05, IF-06 AoU-SEC-6 The product image is built without the test and fault-injection console commands: -DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=ON, which also refuses the build options NX_GD_ENABLE_COMMAND, NX_HARDFAULT_TEST_COMMAND, NX_SAFETY_FAULT_INJECTION_COMMAND, NX_FLEXNVM_PARTITION_COMMAND, and the UART is not accessible in the vehicle (the service commands stay in the product console). IF-07 AoU-SEC-7 The debug port is closed in the product (flash security set, or the port physically inaccessible) — refines AoU-16. While it is open, none of the protections of IF-01 … IF-06 holds against a person with access to it. IF-08 AoU-SEC-8 Data a safety function of the application reads from the bus or from NvM is protected against deliberate manipulation by the integrator where his threat analysis requires it (e.g. SecOC); E2E protects against faults of the channel only, and NvM blocks have no protection against deliberate change. IF-09, IF-10

Reference from the safety manual. The safety manual (doc/safety/safety-manual.md) does not exist yet. Proposal S4: it gets a section "Cybersecurity interface" that states that neXtBSW makes no cybersecurity claim, references this document and carries AoU-SEC-1 … AoU-SEC-8 with their final numbers. The consistency test checks the reference as soon as the safety manual exists.

docs.title: 5. Where security measures are planned

docs.title: Static analysis and coding guidelines
docs.text:
Baseline: v0.2.0

Status: 2026-09-21, first issue: deviations approved, rule 15.5 disapplied (section 4a). Part of stage 2 of functional safety: neXtBSW as a Safety Element out of Context, see concept.md sections 9.3 and 10.4. Tool decision: free tools — cppcheck with the MISRA add-on and clang-tidy in the CI; a commercial tool only with a concrete series project.

The tool lives in tools/misra; the CI stage is described in tools/ci/README.md.

MISRA rule texts are copyrighted. This document, the rule set and the reports name rule numbers and short descriptions in our own words only. Whoever needs the text reads it in the licensed standard.

docs.title: 1. Rule set
docs.text:
Code Guideline Checked by Status C (bootloader, E2E library, newlib hooks, C parts of the platform) MISRA C:2012 (with the amendments as far as the add-on implements them) cppcheck MISRA add-on checked, gating C and C++ cppcheck core checks (warning, style, performance, portability) cppcheck checked, gating C and C++ selected clang-tidy checks: bugprone-*, cert-*, clang static analyzer (core, cplusplus, deadcode, array bounds), initialisation, casts, signed bit operations, implicit bool conversion, virtual destructors, definitions in headers clang-tidy checked, gating C++ (application, drivers, platform port) MISRA C++:2023 — not checked: no free tool implements it. The clang-tidy selection covers several of its topics (casts, initialisation, recursion via the add-on, narrowing), but it is not a MISRA C++ compliance statement. Open until a commercial tool is chosen for a series project

Which checks are active, with the reason for each exclusion, is stated in tools/misra/rules.yaml — the single place. Two exclusions are worth naming here: bugprone-throwing-static-initialization/cert-err58-cpp (every C++ unit is compiled with -fno-exceptions, nothing can throw) and bugprone-easily-swappable-parameters (style, not a fault class).

The MISRA add-on is a C checker. On a C++ unit it reads C++ syntax as C — template and base-class lists as comma operators (12.3), using-declarations as typedefs (5.6, 2.3), C++ types as unknown (misra-config). Its findings in C++ units are therefore counted as tool notices and do not gate, except rule 17.2 (recursion), whose meaning is the same in C++. A header seen from a C and a C++ unit is judged in the C view.

docs.title: 2. Scope — what is "our code"
docs.text:
The only source of translation units, include paths and defines is the compile database of the target build (compile_commands.json of the demo project; in CI <build root>/demo). Every file is classified:

Class Meaning Treatment own neXtBSW code analysed, gating copy OpenBSW copy — identical or modified in tools/openbswsync/copies.yaml analysed, reported separately, not gating external the submodule external/openbsw not analysed excluded Simulink output (swc/*/generated), host tests, third-party code under platforms/*/3rdparty read as context, findings dropped outside not in the repository: generated board and RTE code in the build directory read as context, findings dropped

The separation between our code and the OpenBSW copies comes from copies.yaml and nowhere else (finding in concept.md 10.4) — the same list that the OpenBSW qualification path (concept.md 8.1, option a) starts from. Generated code is read as context so that cross-unit rules see the callers (without it the E2E library looks unused, rule 8.7); its own findings belong to the generators, not to this list.

Because the compile database drives the analysis, only code that the demo project compiles is analysed. On 2026-09-21 that is 55 own translation units (19 C, 36 C++) and 38 OpenBSW copies. The report names every own source file that no unit compiles; today 11 files in 6 modules (the STM32 bootloader and BSP, the bootloader's link transport, mcuLink, CellMonitorSystem, HardFaultTestCommand, cacheUnavailable). A second analysed profile is an open point (section 7).

docs.title: 3. Verdicts and what breaks the run
docs.text:
Every finding of our code gets exactly one verdict:

Verdict Source Effect disapplied rule with revised_category: disapplied in rules.yaml (re-categorization plan, section 4a) neither new nor baseline; counted and reported separately notice notices/notices_cpp in rules.yaml (tool limits) counted, reported deviated tools/misra/deviations.yaml counted per deviation, reported baseline tools/misra/baseline.yaml (inventory) counted, reported new none of the above the run fails (python -m tools.misra run exit code 1, CI stage red)

Findings are matched without line numbers: file + rule + the stripped source line, counted as a multiset. Moving code does not create a new finding; a second copy of the same violation does. A baseline entry that is no longer found is reported as resolved; the baseline is then rewritten and only ever shrinks. A deviation matches by rule, file pattern and a source-line pattern or symbol — never by file or line number alone — and may carry a limit.

A missing tool is never green: it is reported as skipped with the place that was searched, and in a strict CI run (python -m tools.ci run --strict) it is red. python -m tools.ci setup installs both tools as pinned pip wheels into the tool cache, without an installer.

docs.title: 4. Handling deviations and findings
docs.text:
1. A new finding is fixed in the code by the task that owns the code. If the code is right and the rule does not fit, a deviation is written.
  2. A deviation (deviations.yaml, MISRA Compliance:2020 "deviation record") names: id (DEV-nnn, never reused), kind (deviation or false-positive for a proven tool error), rule(s), files, pattern/symbol, optional limit, the reason in our own words, who raised it and when, and who approved it (approved_by; empty = open). Approval is the safety manager's; open approvals are listed in every run as a warning and belong. python -m tools.misra check validates the file and reports every error with its YAML path.
  3. A real fault found by the analysis is not deviated away and not repaired by an earlier change. It stays in the baseline (so that the run is green until it is fixed) and is recorded in tools/misra/defects.yaml with a note and a proposed owner; the report lists these separately.
  4. Rule-set changes (a check switched off, an advisory rule disapplied) are changes to rules.yaml with a reason and need the safety manager's decision, like a deviation.

docs.title: 4a. Guideline re-categorization plan
docs.text:
MISRA Compliance:2020 lets a project re-categorize guidelines: any guideline may be made stricter (advisory → required → mandatory), and an advisory guideline may be disapplied — not applied at all. Mandatory and required guidelines can never be disapplied; a deviation record is the only way to depart from them.

The plan lives in tools/misra/rules.yaml, at the rule itself: category stays the category of the standard, revised_category is the one of this project, with reason (own words, no rule text), date and approved_by. python -m tools.misra check (and every run) rejects, each with its YAML path (rules.<rule>.revised_category): disapplying a rule that is not advisory, weakening a rule, re-categorizing a tool check that has no MISRA category, an unknown category, and a missing reason. A missing approval is a warning.

Findings of a disapplied rule get the verdict disapplied: they are not new (the run stays green), not part of the baseline (python -m tools.misra baseline leaves them out; a baseline that still holds them is reported as a warning) and are listed in a section of their own in the report, per module. They stay visible, so the decision can be revisited with numbers.

Rule Category Project Findings 2026-09-21 Approval MISRA C:2012 15.5 (single exit point) advisory disapplied 214 (bootloader/src 113, libs/bsw/e2e 50, bootloader/updater 25, bootloader/platforms 20, bootloader/devices 6) safety manager, decision log

Reason for 15.5, in short (full text in rules.yaml): early return after a failed check is the prevailing pattern of our C code and keeps the good path flat; a forced single exit needs status variables and deep nesting and makes the code harder to read and review without making it safer. What the rule protects — no skipped clean-up, a traceable control flow — is covered by the other control-flow rules, the clang-tidy checks and the review of the function.

docs.title: 6. How this fits the safety concept
docs.text:
Static analysis is a development-process measure, not a safety mechanism: it gets no SM number and has no reaction time. It supports the concept in three ways:

  • Evidence for the code of the mechanisms. The mechanisms of concept.md section 6 are implemented in the analysed modules: SM-05 in the RTE (ecu/application, BEF-001, closed), SM-06 in DebugHaltGuardSystem (BEF-003, BEF-004, closed), SM-23/24 in hardFaultHandler and the port, SM-31 in libs/bsw/e2e, SM-50/51 in the bootloader and the port, SM-53 in ecuState (BEF-002, closed). A finding in one of these modules is weighed against the mechanism it touches.
  • The OpenBSW part of the argument. The copies are reported separately from copies.yaml; this is the "analysis of a separate task" that option (a) of concept.md 8.1 refers to.
  • Assumptions of use. The analysis covers neXtBSW's own code in the configuration of the demo project. It does not cover the integrator's application code, his generated code or other derivatives' code paths. This belongs next to AoU-17 (application code at the target ASIL) and AoU-20 (unqualified compiler and libraries): an integrator who relies on MISRA compliance runs the same (or a qualified) analysis on his own code and his project configuration. Proposal for the concept owner: an AoU of its own for this — concept.md is not changed by an earlier change.
  • Tool classification. cppcheck and clang-tidy are verification tools whose failure can hide a fault; their classification belongs to a separate task. The versions are pinned once, in tools/misra/requirements.txt.

docs.title: 7. Limits and open points
docs.text:
• MISRA C++:2023 is not checked (section 1).
  • Only the demo profile is analysed; derivative- and family-specific code paths of other profiles and the 11 own files outside the demo build are not. A second compile database (for example buildtest-s32k148) is the next step once the run time allows it (today about 2.5 minutes for both tools on the workstation, 6 parallel jobs).
  • Whole-program rules of the add-on (2.5, 8.7) see one image at a time; bootloader, updater and application are in one compile database (DEV-014 exists for that reason).
  • Advisory rule 15.5 (single exit) is disapplied project-wide (section 4a); its 214 findings are reported separately. An integrator whose own process applies 15.5 has to re-enable it (remove revised_category) and rewrite the baseline.
  • The deviations DEV-001 to DEV-014 are approved; a new deviation needs a new approval.

Issue 1, 2026-09-28 Task Gap analysis iso26262-gap.md (not published, available on request) section 6 no. 7; rows 6-07 … 6-19 Status draft for review; written by a contributor on the safety manager's behalf (author side, see section 9) Built against branch dev at 20b2e04, demo project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo, build preset evalboard-s32k144-demo (RelWithDebInfo), xPack GCC 11.3.1 Verification mock/host: stack tool with host tests and against the target build of the baseline; nothing on the board

Baseline: v0.2.0

docs.title: 0. What this document is
docs.text:
The software architecture of neXtBSW as a whole is described in doc/architecture/README.md (layers, roles, module manifests, configuration levels) and in the module manifests. The safety documents describe the mechanisms (concept.md section 6), their analysis (fmea.md, dfa.md), the requirements (ssr.sdoc) and the hardware-software interface (hsi-s32k1xx.md). What the gap analysis found missing (rows 6-10, 6-11, 6-18, 6-19) is one view of the safety part that says which units implement which mechanism, in which task or interrupt, with which data, which requirement is allocated to which component at which ASIL, how much of the resources it needs, and how the design was inspected. This document is that view. It adds no mechanism and changes no requirement.

References to ISO 26262:2018 are given as <part>-<clause> (for example 6-7.4.13), in the project's own words; the standard is not quoted.

Scope: stage 1 of the concept (base-software mechanisms, concept.md section 1.4) on the only family with a safety port, s32k1xx. Numbers are those of the demo image (S32K144, Cortex-M4F). What changes for other families is named where it matters (section 10).

docs.title: 2.2 Start-up and lifecycle levels
docs.text:
1. Reset_Handler → main() of the family port: clocks, watchdog configuration, watchdog self-test (SM-07, SSR-017; failure → S1 held), reset-loop limit (startResetLoopLimit, SSR-065; limit reached → S1 held), MPU init (SM-12), ROM check registration, then the scheduler.
  2. app::startApp() adds the lifecycle components; run level 1: platform, runtime, safety (SafetySystem::init → SafetyManager::init: watchdog, supplies, pin lock (SM-21), cycle timer, period check), ecu; run level 2: platform part two; level 3: UDS, XCP; level 8: sysadmin; level 9: RTE.
  3. SafetySystem::run schedules the safety cycle at a fixed rate of 10 ms in the safety task.
  4. Shutdown (run-down, SM-53): components in reverse order with a time-out per step; SafetySystem::shutdown cancels the cycle and disables the watchdog.

docs.title: 2.3 One safety cycle (SafetyManager::cyclic)
docs.text: ENTER → MPU gate state on entry (SM-11) → period check against LPTMR (SM-04) → PERIOD_CHECKED → every 7th cycle the watchdog service with its own enter/leave sequence and configuration re-check (SM-01 … SM-03) → safe_memory::cyclic (MPU descriptors SM-13, ECC status) → MEMORY_CHECKED → SafeSystem::cyclic (ADC reference SM-18/19, internal supplies SM-20) → SYSTEM_CHECKED → SafeIo::cyclic (register check SM-22) → IO_CHECKED → supervision-peripheral checks (deadman SM-06, watchdog control) → PERIPHERALS_CHECKED → delivery of deferred events (RTE deadlines) → LEAVE → MPU gate state on exit. Every checkpoint is a hit() of the sequence monitor (SM-04): a skipped or reordered check is SAFETY_MANAGER_SEQUENCE_DEVIATION.

docs.title: 2.4 Reaction sequences
docs.text:
Reaction Sequence (all in SafeSupervisor::handle() under the interrupt lock) Events (demo) S3 report and continue log line, return RTE_TIMING_VIOLATION, DEVICE_REPORT, CHECK_REGISTER_ERROR without I/O support S1 enterSafeState(): walk the safe outputs table, indicator on; leaveSafeState() when the register is correct again (indicator only, SSR-004) CHECK_REGISTER_ERROR (with PLATFORM_SUPPORT_IO): its context names the cause - 1 check fine again, 0 the SAFETY_TEST pin, else class (bits 31..24) and entry (bits 15..0) of the register list, in the log line S1 + S2 enterLimpHome() → enterSafeState() → console line → reset-loop record → softwareSystemReset() sequence deviations, watchdog configuration/service, MPU, ECC, ADC reference, supplies, lock register, deadman configuration, period violation, STACK_OVERFLOW, RTOS_ASSERT S1 held holdSafeState(): limp home, S1, one console line, then loop: walk the table again, service the MCU watchdog; interrupts stay locked; ends only with power cycle or external reset WATCHDOG_STARTUP_CHECK_FAILURE, ROM_CHECK_FAILURE, DEVICE_FAULT (well-formed report of a device configured for it; otherwise S1 + S2), RESET_LOOP_LIMIT bypass fault handlers and the halt deadman walk the table before anything else, then dump/report (concept section 5) HardFault, BusFault, UsageFault, WDOG_EWM, deadman time-out

The reaction times per class are in concept.md section 7; they are not repeated here.

docs.title: 3. Freedom from interference — what the architecture provides
docs.text:
Summary of what exists (details: concept 6.3, dfa.md, task for the rest), sorted by the three kinds of interference of 6-Annex D:

Kind Provided Not provided memory MPU region for the safety data and the safety stack, gate open only in the safety context (SM-10 … SM-13); runtime stack check of every task at the context switch (configCHECK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW 2 → STACK_OVERFLOW, S1 + S2); since an earlier change a guard of 1 KB directly below the interrupt stack (MSP) that the core may read but not write (MPU descriptor 6, checked every cycle by SM-13): an overflow ends in the hard fault reaction (SM-17) no partitioning of the application; before a later change the MSP had no guard (section 7.3, finding STK-2) timing and execution safety task above every application task; period check against an independent timer (SM-04); program-flow checkpoints (SM-04); watchdog with window relation (SM-01 … SM-03); halt deadman above the RTOS boundary (SM-06); RTE deadlines (SM-05, report only) the watchdog follows one task (AoU-14) exchange of information E2E for configured signals (SM-31), qualifier for analogue values (SM-30), deferred event box instead of opening the gate no protection of the internal RTE buffers against a faulty writer in the same address space
