docs.title: Board-Ports (ecu/platforms/<board>)
docs.text:
Ein Board-Port ist nur noch das, was dieses Board von anderen Boards seiner Familie unterscheidet - und seit einer früheren Änderung ist das in aller Regel nichts: ein Board braucht überhaupt keinen Board-Port mehr, um gebaut zu werden. Der handgeschriebene Port selbst ist seit einer früheren Änderung eine Familienvorlage unter platforms/<familie>/port (Befund B6, Architektur Abschnitte 5 und 8):

Ort Inhalt platforms/<familie>/port/bspConfiguration L1-Konfiguration der Familie (ADC, CAN, UART, SystemTimer, stdIo, PWM) platforms/<familie>/port/safety safeLifecycle, safeMemory (NXP-MPU), safeSystem, safeIo, adcSafetyConsole platforms/<familie>/port/main startUp.S, bootHeader.S, Linker-Vorlage, ISRs, StaticBsp, BspSystem, Integration platforms/<familie>/port/freeRtosCoreConfiguration FreeRtosPlatformConfig.h der Familie platforms/<familie>/port/port.yaml was die Vorlage vom Projekt, vom Board und vom Derivat braucht platforms/<familie>/bsp/bspMcu mcu/mcu.h der Familie (eine Datei, kein Board-Name im Include-Pfad) ecu/platforms/<familie>/features.yaml was die Vorlage bietet: Funktionsschalter, die nur der Port beantworten kann (Watchdog, MPU) ecu/platforms/<board>/Options.cmake optional: begründete Ausnahme dieses Boards; wird nach den abgeleiteten Schaltern eingebunden und darf einen überschreiben ecu/platforms/<board>/CMakeLists.txt optional: Board-Eigenheiten und begründete Ausnahmen

docs.title: Funktionsschalter (PLATFORM_SUPPORT_*)
docs.text:
Bis zu einer Folgeaufgabe setzte jedes baubare Board die Schalter von Hand in ecu/platforms/<board>/Options.cmake, und die Wurzel-CMakeLists.txt verweigerte ein Board ohne diese Datei. Für ein Kunden-Board war das eine Pflichtdatei an einer Stelle, die dem Kunden nicht gehört, und ihr Inhalt wiederholte, was project.yaml schon sagt (Architektur Abschnitt 9, Zeile 2). Jetzt werden sie abgeleitet - tools/nxconfig/features.py schreibt sie als NX_FEATURE_<NAME> samt Begründung ins Generat, die Wurzel-CMakeLists.txt setzt daraus PLATFORM_SUPPORT_<NAME>:

Schalter Ebene Quelle OPENBSW_PLATFORM Derivat die Familie des Derivats (NX_FAMILY) IO Projekt das Projekt nutzt mindestens einen I/O-Eintrag des Boards (use.dio, use.adc, use.input_capture, eine pwm-Gruppe) oder einen internen ADC-Kanal (adc_internal) CAN Projekt das Projekt nutzt mindestens einen CAN-Bus des Boards (use.can) TRANSPORT Projekt das Projekt hat einen Abschnitt diagnostics (die Transportschicht trägt den Diagnosestapel; DoIP kommt mit Ethernet dazu) UDS Projekt das Projekt hat einen Abschnitt diagnostics ETHERNET Bau-Option NX_ETHERNET, gegen das Derivat geprüft - keine Board-Aussage WATCHDOG, MPU Familien-Port ecu/platforms/<familie>/features.yaml: hat der Port den Treiber überhaupt?

Nicht abgeleitet und deshalb nirgends gesetzt: STORAGE, ROM_CHECK, MIDDLEWARE und die übrigen Schalter der OpenBSW-Referenzanwendung. Sie haben in neXtBSW keinen Leser (nur external/openbsw/executables/referenceApp, das dieser Baum nicht baut) und standen in jedem Board-Port auf OFF.

Kein Board-Port zeigt auf einen anderen Board-Port. Wer für ein neues Board Code aus einem anderen Board-Port braucht, hat einen Architektur-Befund gefunden: melden (Prüffragen, Architektur Abschnitt 11), nicht kopieren und nicht per add_subdirectory einbinden.

docs.title: Was ein Board wirklich unterscheidet
docs.text:
Diese Unterschiede kommen heute ohne Codekopie aus der Konfiguration (Derivat mcudb/<familie>/<derivat>.yaml, Board boards/<board>/board.yaml, Projekt projects/<projekt>/project.yaml) und aus dem Generat von tools/bswgen/tools/blgen. Sie sind die Grundlage für das Board-Profil ohne Codekopie:

Unterschied Quelle Weg in den Code Linkerskript-Werte (Flash-/RAM-Bereiche, Bootloader-/App-Aufteilung, Gültigkeitsrecord, No-Init-Bereich) Derivat (Größen) + Projekt (memory) memory/memoryLayout.h → main/linkerscript/application.dld.in Pins und Pin-Funktionen (Konsole, CAN, LEDs, Taster, ADC-Kanäle, PWM-Ausgänge, SPI/CS/INT) Board (pins, devices, can) + Derivat (Pin-Mux-Tabelle je Gehäuse) bsp/io/io/ioConfiguration.h, bsp/adc/*, bsp/io/outputPwm/ftmPwmConfiguration.h Bestückte Module (SBC ja/nein, passiver Transceiver, High-Side-Schalter, Gate-Treiber) Board (devices mit module) + Projekt (modules) integration/modules.cmake (NX_MODULES), integration/moduleConfiguration.h Takt (Quarz, Oszillator-Bereich, PLL, Kern-/Bus-/Peripherietakte, CAN-Bit-Timing, UART-Teiler) Board (clock.sosc_hz) + Projekt (Systemtakt, Bitraten, Baudrate) bsp/clock/boardClock.h, bsp/can/canBitTimingConfiguration.h, bsp/uart/uartConfiguration.h Debug-Schnittstelle (J-Link-Gerät, SWD/JTAG, Takt) Board (debug) + Derivat (jlink_device) NX_JLINK_* der Wurzel-CMakeLists.txt, Flash-Ziele Derivat-Fakten (MPU-Regionen, NVIC-Prioritätsbits, Peripherie-Instanzen, Gehäuse) Derivat mcu/derivativeFacts.h, mcu/mcuDerivative.h, interrupts/interruptPriorities.h

Bleibt ein Unterschied übrig, der Code braucht (z. B. die Umgehung eines Platinenfehlers), gehört er als eigenes Modul mit Manifest in den Board-Port und wird im Changelog begründet (Architektur Abschnitt 3, Regel 2).

docs.title: Serialized ADC access (bspAdcAccess)
docs.text:
Header-only, MCU- and RTOS-neutral layer that serializes synchronous (polled) ADC conversions from several tasks and from contexts that must not wait (ISR, interrupts or scheduler locked, before the scheduler starts). It also bounds the polling loop of a conversion by a value derived from the conversion time and averages a channel over one PWM period.

The module has no board device. Its parameters are module parameters of the project (modules.bspAdcAccess, project_parameters: true).

State: verification hardware for the policy interrupt_lock; rtos_mutex and converter failures only in host tests (see Tests).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Header Content adc/AdcAccess.h adc::AdcAccess<Lock, Converter, InstanceCount>: convert(instance, input, value), getStatistics(), resetStatistics(); AdcAccessStatistics adc/InterruptLockAdcLock.h lock policy without RTOS objects: every conversion with all interrupts suspended (OpenBSW suspendResumeAllInterrupts) adc/FreeRtosAdcLock.h lock policy with one statically allocated FreeRTOS mutex per converter instance (priority inheritance); needs configUSE_MUTEXES, configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION, INCLUDE_xTaskGetSchedulerState and a platform type InterruptContext::interruptsLockedOrInIsr() adc/AdcPollLimit.h constexpr arithmetic of the polling bound: sarConversionClocks, pollCyclesForClocks, pollLimit, clocksToNs adc/AdcAveraging.h adc::AdcAveraging<Lock>: AveragingSpec (samples, spacingNs), AdcAveragingStatistics

The Lock policy provides canBlock, tryLock, lock (bounded timeout), unlock, enterExclusive, exitExclusive and nowNs; the Converter provides convert(instance, input, value) and restart(instance, input). Both are static types (architecture decision D1). Both converter calls must return after a bounded time even if the converter never signals completion.

CMake target bspAdcAccess (INTERFACE; links OpenBSW bsp and bspInterrupts). A user of FreeRtosAdcLock.h also links FreeRTOS.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Project (project.yaml, modules.bspAdcAccess); the full table with ranges and defaults is in the modules reference:

Parameter Default Meaning in short lock_policy interrupt_lock interrupt_lock or rtos_mutex lock_timeout_ms 100 longest wait for the lock (only rtos_mutex) poll_safety_factor 16 polling bound = factor x derived conversion time max_interrupt_suspend_us 50 interrupt suspension the project accepts for one conversion; checked only, changes nothing generated sample_clocks 42 sample phase in ADC clocks clock_divider 1 converter clock divider (family values only) averages 1 hardware averaging (family values only); multiplies the conversion time

sample_clocks, clock_divider and averages are converter settings; the comment in module.yaml says they belong to the ADC contract and stay here until that contract exists.

tools/nxconfig/adc.py derives the conversion time and the polling bound from these values, the resolution of the derivative (instances.<ADC>.resolution_bits) and the clock plan. It reports an error for a divider or averaging count the family converter does not have, for a missing functional clock and for used ADC instances at different clocks, and a warning if one conversion (with rtos_mutex: two, for a caller that cannot wait) suspends the interrupts longer than max_interrupt_suspend_us. tools/bswgen renders integration/bspAdcAccessConfiguration.h and bsp/adc/adcAccessConfiguration.h.

The averaged channels are configured under adc_sampling.<key> of the project (project reference).

docs.title: Contexts (AdcAccess)
docs.text:
• Task caller (canBlock()): try the lock of the instance, otherwise wait with the bounded timeout (timeout -> BSP_ERROR, counted). Mark the instance busy, convert with the interrupts enabled, clear busy, unlock. The exclusive sections around the busy flag last a few instructions.
  • Caller that cannot wait: convert inside an exclusive section. If a task conversion of the same instance was preempted, restart it afterwards, so the task still gets the value of its own input. Never blocks; added latency one or two conversions.
  • With interrupt_lock every caller takes the exclusive path; there is no waiting and no priority inversion.
  • An instance number out of range returns BSP_ERROR.
  • Single core only: the exclusive section must stop every other caller.

Properties the header adds to the ADC contract: a synchronous read is callable from every context; it returns after a time derived from the conversion time; how long it may suspend the interrupts is a project decision; a failed read is reported, never replaced by a value.

docs.title: Polling bound (AdcPollLimit)
docs.text: The loop count is the only portable bound. cycles assumes one loop iteration per core clock, so limit = cycles x poll_safety_factor is a guaranteed lower bound of factor x conversion time. An unknown converter clock (0 Hz) gives the largest value, so it can never cause a spurious timeout.

docs.title: Averaging (AdcAveraging)
docs.text: samples conversions at equally spaced instants over exactly one PWM period, rounded mean of the raw values. Each conversion goes through AdcAccess on its own, so the interrupt suspension stays that of one conversion. The calling task busy-waits for one PWM period per read; averaged channels are meant for task callers. A failed conversion or a stalled time source ends the read with BSP_ERROR; samples more than a quarter spacing late are counted.

docs.title: Statistics and console
docs.text: AdcAccessStatistics: conversions, contended, lock time-outs, exclusive, nested, errors, longest wait, conversion and exclusive section. On s32k1xx the console group adcaccess stats | reset shows them (console reference).

docs.title: Hardware triggered sample groups
docs.text:
A sample group (bspSampleGroup) converts its channels after every trigger of a PWM group without software. Its ADC instances are exclusive to that chain, and AdcAccess never converts on them - the decision of a separate task, for these reasons:

  • On s32k1xx the trigger mode is one setting per converter (SC2[ADTRG]). With the hardware trigger selected, the software start of convert() (write SC1[0]) starts nothing and the polling bound expires; switching the mode per conversion would drop the triggers of the chain for that time.
  • A software conversion in between would take a result register of the sequence and delay its conversions; the sample instant the fast loop relies on would move by up to one conversion.
  • The lock policies of this module suspend the interrupts for a whole conversion (interrupt_lock); an exclusive instance keeps that suspension out of the latency of the sample group interrupt (fast-control-loop.md 7.2).

tools/nxconfig therefore rejects a project that converts in software (use.adc, adc_internal) on an ADC of a sample group, with the YAML path of the group channel. The converter settings of this module (sample_clocks, clock_divider, averages) still apply: the sample group uses the same CFG1/CFG2/SC3 values and its timing is derived from the same conversion time. Quantities that need slow supervision in software (pwm_period_average, the safety reference channels) stay on an ADC without a group.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• A family model for the conversion time exists only for s32k1xx (MODELS in tools/nxconfig/adc.py); the implementation of the converter and the Cortex-M InterruptContext live in the s32k1xx port (platforms/s32k1xx/port/bspConfiguration/src/bsp/adc).
  • The converter settings will move to the ADC contract; until then they are parameters of this module.
  • rtos_mutex and converter failures have not been run on a board (verification note).

docs.title: I2C master contract (bspI2c)
docs.text:
Hardware-neutral interface bsp::i2c::II2cMaster for one I2C bus as master with 7-bit addresses. Rate, pins, time limit and the resources of the bus are fixed by the configuration of the implementation, so device drivers written against it stay board and family independent. The contract is header only; the implementation is the I2C driver of a family (for s32k1xx: the FlexIO I2C master platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspFlexioI2c, reached through the family port platforms/s32k1xx/port/bspConfiguration, see Implementation on s32k1xx).

It is a catalogue entry (kind: contract): tools/nxconfig and tools/bswgen assign no board device to it. The values of a bus belong to the board I2C bus and the project (i2c[] of the board, use.i2c and i2c.<bus> of the project), not to this contract.

State: verification mock - host tests against a fake bus and, for s32k1xx, a FlexIO register model. Not yet exercised on a board (see Tests).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Header i2c/II2cMaster.h, CMake target bspI2c (INTERFACE).

Method Behaviour I2cResult write(uint8_t address, uint8_t const* data, size_t length, bool sendStop) pure virtual. START (or a repeated START after a call with sendStop false), address byte, length data bytes, STOP if sendStop. length 0 only probes the address I2cResult read(uint8_t address, uint8_t* data, size_t length, bool sendStop) pure virtual. Address byte, then length bytes (1..maxBytesPerTransfer()); the last byte is not acknowledged size_t maxBytesPerTransfer() const pure virtual. Data bytes one call accepts; longer sequences need several calls chained with repeated START

I2cResult: OK, NOT_INITIALIZED, INVALID_ARGUMENT, BUS_BUSY, ADDRESS_NACK, DATA_NACK, TIMEOUT, BUS_ERROR. Values and order are part of the contract - an implementation with an enumeration of its own converts by value and checks the numbering with static_assert. The destructor is protected and non-virtual: objects are not deleted through the interface.

Helpers in i2c/I2cTransfer.h (family neutral, on top of the interface):

Function Behaviour probe(bus, address) address byte with STOP; OK if a device acknowledged writeRead(bus, address, tx, txLength, rx, rxLength) the usual register read: write without STOP, repeated START, read with STOP. A failed write part returns its result and starts no read. txLength 0 reads only scan(bus, first, last) probes first..last, clamped to the device addresses 0x08..0x77 (the I2C bus specification reserves 0x00-0x07 and 0x78-0x7F). ADDRESS_NACK means "no device"; any other failure ends the scan and is returned with its address resultName(result) short text for logs and the console

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The contract itself has no keys (modules reference). The bus comes from the board and the project:

  • board i2c[]: instance, SDA/SCL pins and, on a FlexIO, the data pins flexio_pin (board reference);
  • project use.i2c (which buses) and i2c.<bus> with baudrate_hz (upper limit of SCL, the slowest device on the bus decides it), timeout_ms (default 20) and verify (project reference). A used bus without an entry runs at 100 kHz, the standard mode every I2C device supports; nxconfig check names that default in its info lines.

tools/nxconfig/i2c.py checks the values with their YAML path and derives the rest (divider, resources); tools/bswgen writes bsp/i2c/i2cConfiguration.h (NX_I2C_BUS_COUNT, NX_I2C_BUSES(X)) and NX_USE_I2C in integration/modules.cmake.

docs.title: Implementation on s32k1xx
docs.text:
• Every used bus must be on a FlexIO (the family has no LPI2C driver; nxconfig refuses anything else).
  • nxconfig computes the SCL divider like the driver (flexio::calculateBaud): the fastest rate at or below baudrate_hz, at most f/6 of the FlexIO clock, at least f/512 - a slower request is an error, never rounded up. Above 1 MHz (Fast-mode Plus) is an error as well. The time limit must cover the longest transfer (address, 13 data bytes and the STOP word, 9 SCL periods each).
  • Two shifters and two timers per bus, handed out in board order: bus k gets shifters 2k/2k+1 and SCL timer 2k (the shift timer is SCL timer + 1 and never a multiple of 4). A FlexIO of this family has 4 of each, so two buses fit; a third is an error at use.i2c. A FlexIO data pin used by two buses is an error at the board pin.
  • platforms/s32k1xx/port/bspConfiguration (bsp/i2c/I2cBuses.h) has one II2cMaster per used bus. The FlexIO master is set up (init()) at the first transfer of its bus, in the calling task, and again after a failed setup. Not thread safe: all transfers of a bus must run in one task context.
  • Transitional: FlexioI2cMaster still declares an I2cResult of its own with the same enumerators, so the port keeps the FlexIO masters (FlexioI2cBuses.cpp) and the contract objects (I2cBuses.cpp) in two translation units that meet through FlexioI2cBridge.h. Once the driver implements II2cMaster itself, the bridge goes away.
  • Console group i2c (buses, probe, scan, rd, wr), registered in the console task when the project uses a bus (console reference). wr writes to a device and is a board rule: only to a device whose datasheet allows it.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• 7-bit addresses only; no 10-bit addressing, no general call, no slave operation.
  • No bus sharing or locking in the contract. The s32k1xx buses are used by the console only today; a device driver on a bus needs the same task context or a lock in front of it.
  • No bus recovery (nine SCL clocks with SDA stuck low) and no interrupt or DMA operation in the s32k1xx driver.
  • The only implementation is the s32k1xx FlexIO master.

docs.text: Host-Tests, Testnamen und Verifikationsstand: Modulkatalog.

docs.title: Pin edge contract (bspPinEdge)
docs.text:
Hardware-neutral interfaces between the pin-interrupt dispatcher of a family and the modules that consume pin edges (concept pin-interrupts.md, section 3.1). The dispatcher owns the vectors of the pin interrupts; every pin with a consumer is assigned to exactly one consumer and channel by a static table generated from the project - nothing registers itself at run time.

It is a catalogue entry only (kind: contract): tools/nxconfig and tools/bswgen assign no board device, take no project values and generate nothing for it.

State: verification mock - host tests of the s32k1xx dispatcher and of the Hall access through it; no pin interrupt has been exercised on a board yet (see Tests).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Header pinEdge/IPinEdgeConsumer.h, CMake target bspPinEdge (INTERFACE), namespace bsp::pinedge.

Interface Method Behaviour IPinEdgeConsumer void onEdge(uint16_t channel, uint32_t timestampUs) pure virtual, implemented by a consumer. Called in interrupt context for every flagged pin of the consumer. channel is the consumer's own index (sensor set, event), not a pin number; several pins may share a channel. timestampUs is the 32-bit microsecond system time, taken once per interrupt after the flags were cleared IPinEdgeControl bool setArmed(IPinEdgeConsumer const& consumer, uint16_t channel, bool armed) implemented by the dispatcher. false switches the edge detection of every pin of (consumer, channel) off and clears their pending flags; true clears them and arms the configured edge again. Returns false when the table has no such pin

Both destructors are protected and non-virtual: the objects are static and never deleted through the interface.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The contract itself has no keys. The table behind it (pin, edge, consumer, channel; vectors with their NVIC level) comes from the project: the Hall sensor sets (hall) and the pin events of pin_events, generated by tools/bswgen (bsp/pinIrq/pinIrqConfiguration.h on s32k1xx, vectors from the derivative fact pin_interrupts).

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• onEdge() runs inside the ISR frame of the family (safety hooks), may not call the RTOS and has to be short and bounded. A consumer that needs the level samples it itself.
  • Two flags of one channel in the same interrupt give two calls with the same time.
  • setArmed() may be called from a task or from onEdge() (a rate limit switching its own input off). Calls for one channel belong to one context.

Example (s32k1xx implementation bios::PinIrqDispatcher, platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspPinIrq, not part of the contract): one vector per port on the S32K14x, one for all ports on the S32K11x; the edge is PORT_PCR.IRQC (rising, falling or both - never a level); the interrupt reads PORT_ISFR, clears only the flags of pins with a consumer and walks only the flags that are set. Start-up in two steps (init() arms and clears with the vectors off, enable() sets the NVIC level and enables them) so consumers can start from the levels in between. The table type and its compile-time checks are pinIrq/PinIrqTable.h; the port builds the table in bspConfiguration/src/bsp/pinIrq/PinIrqConfig.cpp.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• The only implementation is the s32k1xx dispatcher. Other families (S32K3 SIUL2, STM32 EXTI, RM4x GIO) bring their own when their port gets pin events; the derivative fact pin_interrupts in mcudb already describes them.
  • An edge chosen at run time (the pin events debounce with both edges, else the configured one) is not part of the contract: the s32k1xx adapter uses PinIrqDispatcher::setEdge() of the family directly. A second family with pin events decides whether that becomes a contract function.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Host-Tests, Testnamen und Verifikationsstand: Modulkatalog.

docs.title: bspPinEvent — events on digital inputs
docs.text:
Status: 2026-09-29. Host tests and target builds; linked into a project with pin_events since an earlier change (generated table, s32k1xx adapter, RTE targets, console); no board test yet. Concept: pin interrupts, variant A with the answers to F2–F4 (logical edge, software debounce, automatic re-arm).

The module counts edges on digital inputs and offers per input what the RTE later maps to pinevent.<NAME>.count, .time_us and .qlf: the number of accepted edges, the time of the last one in microseconds and a signal qualifier. It debounces in software and protects the CPU against interrupt storms with a rate limit. It is family neutral: no register, no pin, no clock, no heap, no RTOS object.

docs.title: Place in the layers
docs.text:
RTE                  PinEvents::read()            per task cycle, consistent copy
 console              PinEventCommand "pinevent"   read only, console context
 owning task          PinEvents::cycle()           re-arm after the hold-off, expiry
 ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 bspPinEvent          PinEvent (one per input), PinEvents (the table)
 ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 family dispatcher    PinEvents::onEdge(input, nowUs, level)      per vector, IO-52
 (platforms/<family>) IPinEventHardware: level(input), arm(input, Detect)

The module sits in libs/bsp because it is the consumer end of the pin interrupt contract: the family dispatcher links it directly, like bspAdcAccess sits on the ADC contract. It is a service, not a device driver: it serves no board part.

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text:
Dispatcher → module (ISR side). For every edge of an armed input the dispatcher calls

bool PinEvents::onEdge(uint8_t input, uint32_t nowUs, bool level);
  • input: index into the generated table (the dispatcher's pin-to-consumer table carries it),
  • nowUs: free-running 32-bit microsecond time of the edge (wraps; the same base as the task side's time source),
  • level: the logical level (true = active, the board inversion applied), sampled after the interrupt flag was cleared, so every later change raises another interrupt,
  • return false: the dispatcher disarms the pin (edge detector off) and calls the module no more for it until the task side arms it again. false also comes for an unknown index or an input that was never started.

The call is constant time: no loop, no call out, only the input's own state. Target size of PinEvent::onEdge with the demo flags (Cortex-M4, -O2): 366 bytes of code.

Module → family (task side only). IPinEventHardware samples the logical level of an input and programs its edge detector (Detect::NONE | ACTIVATE | DEACTIVATE | BOTH, logical like the project). The family turns the logical edge into the physical one (rising/falling from the board's active level) and into its register values. detectorEdges(config) says what to program: both edges whenever debounceUs > 0 (the level confirmation needs every change), otherwise the configured edge.

Time source. PinEvents takes a function returning the same microsecond time as the dispatcher's time stamps. Readers call it inside their copy, so no edge in the copy is younger than the time they compare with.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
Topic What the module does Counter uint32_t, wraps from 0xFFFFFFFF to 0 (defined unsigned arithmetic; a consumer counts differences) Time stamp time of the last accepted edge; with debounce the time of the edge that opened the lock-out, not of the confirmation Qualifier QUALITY_DEBOUNCE (0, QLF_DEBOUNCE: no accepted edge yet, time not valid), QUALITY_OK (1), QUALITY_ERROR (16, QLF_ERROR: disarmed by the rate limit). The values are the RTE's QLF_*; the RTE has no "not available" value, and DEBOUNCE is its meaning of "not valid yet" Debounce an edge outside the lock-out opens it (provisional edge towards the other level); edges within debounceUs are bounces. After the lock-out the last level reported inside it is the level at its end: equal to the new level → confirmed (counted if it is the configured edge), else a glitch, taken back and counted as such. read() shows the confirmation as soon as the lock-out has passed; the next onEdge() commits the same result (no double count) Edge filter activate, deactivate or both, relative to the board's active level. With debounce the other direction is tracked but not counted Rate limit a window opens with the first candidate edge of the configured direction and lasts windowUs; the candidate that makes it maxEvents + 1 disarms the input, QUALITY_ERROR, trips + 1. Candidates count when they open a lock-out, so a storm of spikes that are all taken back as glitches trips too. More than MAX_BOUNCES (32) bounces inside one lock-out trip as well Re-arm PinEvents::cycle() in the owning task: rearmUs after the trip it samples the level, starts a fresh window and lock-out and arms the detector again. The qualifier returns to OK (or DEBOUNCE without any accepted edge); edges while disarmed are lost, which the ERROR phase told the consumer Expiry an input that stays quiet for longer than a wrap of the 32-bit time (71.6 min) must not alias into its old lock-out or window. cycle() marks a history older than EXPIRE_AFTER_US (2^30 µs, 17.9 min) by the sequence value it saw; the next onEdge() finds the mark and closes lock-out and window, read() treats a marked pending edge as settled. cycle() must run at least every ~53 min

Worst-case interrupt load of one input: maxEvents candidate edges per window, plus with debounce at most one edge of the other direction per debounceUs and MAX_BOUNCES + 1 interrupts per lock-out — whatever the line does.

Configuration rules (isValidConfig, the same as tools/nxconfig/pinevent.py): edge 1..3, debounceUs ≤ 1 s, maxEvents 1..65535, windowUs 1 µs..60 s, rearmUs 1 µs..600 s, debounceUs · maxEvents < windowUs.

docs.title: Hand-over between the sides (lock free)
docs.text: Each input has a sequence counter. The ISR side is the only writer while the input is armed: it makes the counter odd, writes, makes it even again. A reader copies the state between two reads of the counter and retries at most READ_ATTEMPTS (4) times; if an interrupt wrote each time (only possible in a storm, which the limit ends) the read fails and leaves its output unchanged — the RTE keeps its last value. The task side writes the state only while the input is disarmed (start, re-arm after a trip), so there is never a second writer; a reader that preempts it sees an odd counter and does not use the copy. The expiry mark is a single word written by the task side only. Single core: compiler barriers (std::atomic_signal_fence) are enough; no exclusive access and no libatomic, which ARMv6-M lacks (checked by the target compile).

docs.title: Console
docs.text:
Group pinevent (PinEventCommand, text in PinEventConsole.h), read only and lock free, so it runs in the console context without a hop into the owning task:

> pinevent show
pin events: 2
DOOR: count 1, last 5000 us, qlf OK (1), trips 0, bounces 0, glitches 0, armed
PULSE: count 2, last 5001 us, qlf ERROR (16), trips 1, bounces 0, glitches 0, off, re-arm in 246 ms
> pinevent config
DOOR: edge activate, debounce 2000 us, limit 10 per 100000 us, re-arm after 100000 us, detector both

docs.title: Safety classification
docs.text: Driver robustness (QM), not a credited base-software safety mechanism (safety concept section 1.4, strict separation). The rate limit protects CPU availability; the credited detection of a delayed safety task stays SM-04 (period check), SM-06 (halt deadman) and SM-01 (watchdog), DF-37. Coexistence row CA-54 in doc/safety/coexistence.md. If an integrator uses a pin event as input of a safety function, the qualifier gives the information; the claim is his (assumption of use).

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
Only a project with pin_events links anything of the module (bsp/pinIrq/pinIrqConfiguration.cmake: NX_PIN_EVENT_COUNT).

  • tools/bswgen writes bsp/pinEvent/pinEventConfiguration.h (family neutral): pinevent::project::CONFIG[] in the order of pin_events (windowUs = window_ms · 1000, rearmUs = rearm_ms · 1000, name = board input), the indices Pe_<NAME>, static_assert(isValidConfig(...)) per entry, and NX_PIN_EVENT_COUNT (0 without events). The family part (pins, inversion, the dispatcher table with the edge of detectorEdges(): both while debouncing, else the physical edge of the configured one) is bsp/pinIrq/pinIrqConfiguration.h.
  • s32k1xx: bios::PinEventAdapter (platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspPinIrq, CMake target bspPinIrqPinEvent) is the consumer of the dispatcher and the IPinEventHardware: it samples GPIO PDIR with the inversion of the board after the flag was cleared, calls PinEvents::onEdge() and switches the detector off on false; arm() maps the logical request to PORT_PCR.IRQC through PinIrqDispatcher::setEdge(). The instances (PinEvent[], PinEvents, adapter, dispatcher) live in bspConfiguration/src/bsp/pinIrq/PinIrqConfig.cpp, all constant initialized.
  • Start and cycle: bsp::startPinInterrupts() (dispatcher init → Hall decoders and PinEvents::start() → enable) once from the RTE init, bsp::cyclePinEvents() every cycle of one task (the first task that reads a pin event, else the first application task) - also when no component reads the events.
  • tools/rtegen: targets pinevent.<NAME>.count (uint32), .time_us (uint32), .qlf (uint8/16/32, QLF_*) from PinEvents::read(); on false the buffers keep the values of the cycle before. test_rtegen.py compares the QUALITY_* values of PinEvent.h with rtegen.QLF; rtegen warns when .qlf of a read input is not connected.
  • Console: BspSystem of the s32k1xx port registers one PinEventCommand in the console context (target bspPinEventCommand).
  • nxconfig: with debounce_us > 0 the derivative must detect both edges (the level confirmation needs every change).

docs.title: Sample group (bspSampleGroup)
docs.text:
L1 contract of a sample group: a named set of analogue channels that is converted after every hardware trigger of a PWM group, without software, with one interrupt at the end of the whole group. It is the event source of the fast control loop (fast-control-loop.md (not published, available on request), section 3). Header only, board and family neutral.

State: host tests only (contract and s32k1xx family part); no image uses a sample group yet, the board port that arms it comes with the fast-loop dispatcher. Board proof open.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
Element Meaning init() converters and sequencers configured (and calibrated), nothing triggers yet arm() / disarm() the chain follows or ignores the triggers of the PWM group; the PWM itself is not touched group complete one interrupt per trigger, after the last conversion of the group; the family entry calls Consumer::complete(Result const&) of a static consumer type (no run-time registration) Result raw values in project order, number of values, error bits of this completion, sequence number since arm(), counter of the PWM group at interrupt entry errors ERROR_SEQUENCE (a conversion was triggered while its converter was busy), ERROR_CONVERSION_MISSING (another converter had not finished at group complete)

sampleGroup/SampleGroup.h also holds the neutral bookkeeping every family implementation shares (Bookkeeping: arms, completions, error counts, recoveries, sequence number that skips 0 on a wrap) and missedBetween(), the number of completions a consumer missed between two sequence numbers. NoConsumer takes nothing.

The contract knows no phases, motors or registers. A raw value is converted by the consumer.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Project (project.yaml), checked by tools/nxconfig/samplegroup.py:

pwm:
  BRIDGE: { frequency_hz: 20000, deadtime_ns: 500, alignment: center, trigger: { point: zero_low } }
sample_groups:
  MOT_SAMPLE: { pwm: BRIDGE, channels: [PHASE_I_U, PHASE_I_V, PHASE_I_W, DC_LINK_U], delay_ns: 500 }
interrupts:
  ranks:
    - { source: sample_group, name: MOT_SAMPLE, rank: 0 }
  • channels are board ADC entries; the board already states on which ADC each one is (adc[].instance). Channels on different ADCs are sampled at the same instant, channels on one ADC one after another in the listed order - nxconfig warns and names the time offset.
  • The instant is the trigger point of the PWM group plus delay_ns; nxconfig check prints the sample instant of every channel and the end of the group, which must lie inside one PWM period.
  • The ADCs of a group are exclusive to it: a software conversion on the same ADC (use.adc, adc_internal) is an error. On s32k1xx the trigger mode is one setting per converter (SC2[ADTRG]); see bspAdcAccess.
  • The derivative describes the trigger router and the sequencers (mcudb trigger_router, sample_sequencers); a derivative without them rejects sample_groups.

docs.title: Family implementations
docs.text: Family Chain Code s32k1xx FTM trigger (INITTRIG or channel match) -> TRGMUX_PDBx -> PDBx channel 0 (delay, back-to-back pre-triggers) -> ADCx slots, AIEN on the last slot of the sequencer that ends last platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspSampleGroup (SampleGroupChain.h), generated bsp/sampleGroup/sampleGroupConfiguration.h stm32, s32k3xx, rm4x not implemented (timer TRGO -> injected group, BCTU, MibADC group; fast-control-loop.md 3.2) -

docs.title: SPI device contract (bspSpi)
docs.text:
Hardware-neutral interface bsp::spi::ISpiDevice for one SPI slave behind a master. Bus instance, chip select, mode and frame size are fixed by the configuration of the implementation, so device drivers written against it stay board and family independent. The contract is a header only; the implementation is the SPI driver of a family (for s32k1xx: platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspLpspi, class bsp::spi::Lpspi).

It is a catalogue entry only (kind: contract): tools/nxconfig and tools/bswgen assign no board device, take no project values and generate nothing for it.

State: verification hardware for 16-bit and 40-bit frames through the s32k1xx LPSPI implementation; other frame sizes only in host tests (see Tests).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Header spi/ISpiDevice.h, CMake target bspSpi (INTERFACE).

Method Behaviour bool transfer(uint32_t tx, uint32_t& rx) pure virtual. Full-duplex transfer of one frame, chip select asserted for its duration. Only the configured number of low-order bits of tx is sent and returned in rx. false on timeout or bus error; rx is then undefined bool transferLong(uint64_t tx, uint64_t& rx) one frame of up to 64 bits, chip select held for the whole frame, most significant configured bit first. Not pure virtual: the default returns false, so implementations limited to 32 bits and test fakes stay unchanged. false also if the implementation does not support the configured frame size

The destructor is protected and non-virtual: objects are not deleted through the interface.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The contract itself has no keys (modules reference). A device driver states its need with requires: { spi_device: 1 } in its manifest (today sbcUja113x and gdTmc6200; the parked bccMc33771 manifest as well). tools/nxconfig then checks that such a device is reached over exactly the required number of used SPI buses (checks.py). The bus, its pins and the chip select come from spi[] of the board and use.spi of the project (board reference, project reference).

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
What the contract promises is stated above; everything else - clock, mode, frame size, timeout, context - is defined by the implementation.

Example (s32k1xx implementation Lpspi, not part of the contract): transfer handles frames of up to 32 bits and returns false for a longer configured frame; transferLong handles 8..64 bits except 33, sending frames above 32 bits as two transmit words in one chip select period. The class is not thread safe: all transfers must run in one task context.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• One slave per ISpiDevice object; there is no bus sharing or locking in the contract. Whether several objects on one bus may be used from different tasks is up to the implementation (the s32k1xx one requires one task context).
  • Only master operation; doc/architecture/README.md lists SPI as "present, master only LPSPI".
  • The only implementation today is the s32k1xx LPSPI driver.
  • A proposal to offer this contract to Eclipse OpenBSW is prepared in doc/openbsw-beitraege/12-spi-adc-contracts (repository: doc/openbsw-beitraege/12-spi-adc-contracts/issue.md).

docs.title: AUTOSAR base types (autosarBase)
docs.text:
Header-only library with the AUTOSAR base types Std_Types.h, Platform_Types.h and Compiler.h. The generated RTE and the component code generated from the Simulink models include them. It is a catalogue entry only (kind: library): tools/nxconfig and tools/bswgen assign no board device to it, take no project values and generate nothing for it.

State: verification mock - host type test and translation probe for the core profiles, nothing on a board (see Tests).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Header Content include/Platform_Types.h CPU_TYPE = CPU_TYPE_32, CPU_BIT_ORDER = LSB_FIRST, CPU_BYTE_ORDER = LOW_BYTE_FIRST; includes <stdint.h>; uint8..uint64 and sint8..sint64 are typedefs of uint8_t..uint64_t and int8_t..int64_t; boolean (uint8_t, not _Bool), the *_least types (all int), float32 (float), float64 (double), VoidPtr, ConstVoidPtr; TRUE/FALSE unless already defined include/Std_Types.h includes the two other headers; Std_ReturnType (uint8), E_OK, E_NOT_OK, STD_HIGH/STD_LOW, STD_ACTIVE/STD_IDLE, STD_ON/STD_OFF; StatusType and E_OK only if STATUSTYPEDEFINED is not set yet include/Compiler.h compiler abstraction for GCC/Clang: FUNC, P2VAR, P2CONST, CONSTP2VAR, CONSTP2CONST, P2FUNC, CONSTP2FUNC, CONST, VAR, FUNC_P2CONST, FUNC_P2VAR, STATIC, INLINE, LOCAL_INLINE, NULL_PTR

Std_Types.h is described in its header as a minimal subset of AUTOSAR_SWS_StandardTypes. Types such as Std_VersionInfoType are not there.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
• CMake: add_library(autosarBase INTERFACE) with include/ as include directory. Users in this repository: ecu/rte/CMakeLists.txt (generated RTE and the component library swcComponents); the generator tests of tools/rtegen and tools/a2lgen put libs/bsw/autosarBase/include on the include path when they compile generated code on the host.
  • Configuration: none - no board.yaml or project.yaml key, no module parameters (see modules reference).

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
Definitions only, no code and no state.

  • Compiler.h ignores all memory and pointer classes: a flat memory model without near/far pointers is assumed, so P2VAR(uint8, AUTOMATIC, RTE_APPL_DATA) becomes uint8*.
  • Platform_Types.h takes the fixed-width integer types from <stdint.h> of the toolchain (a project decision 2026-09-19, option B): uint32 is uint32_t, so pointers to AUTOSAR and <stdint.h> types can be exchanged without cast in C and C++. With the newlib of arm-none-eabi-gcc, uint32/sint32 are therefore unsigned long/long (before a later change: unsigned int/int, same size and range). The host builds of the tests use the same header and get the host's <stdint.h> types.
  • boolean stays the AUTOSAR unsigned 8-bit type (uint8_t) with TRUE/FALSE, deliberately not C99 bool: _Bool converts every non-zero value to 1, which would change the generated component code.
  • The *_least types stay signed int/unsigned int (natural word size of the 32-bit core); option B does not cover them, and uint_least8_t would be 8 bits wide.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• Platform_Types.h is written for the core profiles of decision D11 in doc/architecture/README.md: ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-R, 32 bit, little endian. Its header comment says so since an earlier change (before, it named Cortex-M only); the definitions did not change. The translation probe (see Tests) checks them for Cortex-M4F, Cortex-M0+ and Cortex-R4.
  • Since an earlier change the integer types depend on the toolchain's <stdint.h>: a printf format or a C++ overload written for unsigned int does not fit uint32 on newlib (unsigned long); use PRIu32 or the <stdint.h> name. Until a follow-up task, uint32/sint32 were unsigned int/signed int and distinct from uint32_t/int32_t of newlib (incompatible-pointer warning in C, error in C++). The machine code of the target images did not change with a separate task (SHA-256 comparison in CHANGELOG.md).
  • On the 64-bit host, VoidPtr and ConstVoidPtr are 8 bytes although CPU_TYPE is CPU_TYPE_32; host tests use the target header unchanged. Only the target probe checks the 32-bit pointer width.
  • A target whose int is not 32 bits or which is big endian would need its own Platform_Types.h; there is no selection mechanism for that today.
  • How far the project follows AUTOSAR in general is described in doc/architecture/autosar.md.

docs.title: Passive CAN transceiver (canPhyPassive)
docs.text:
Role provider can_phy for a CAN transceiver that software does not control: its mode pins (STB, S, EN) are strapped to normal operation by the board and there is no status to read. The transceiver always counts as ready, so the transmit gate of canSystem never mutes a bus behind it.

Granularity (treiber-granularitaet.md): a generic module - no protocol and no part facts, only the role; parts: lists the transceivers whose mode pin a board may hard-wire.

State: verification mock - generator and target build tests only, no bus through a passive transceiver has been checked on a board yet (see Tests).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
File Content include/can/PassiveCanPhy.h can::PassiveCanPhy, derived from OpenBSW's bios::CanPhy (header only)

Behaviour of the three overrides:

Method Result init(id) does nothing setMode(mode, id) records mode (read back through getMode() of the base class), returns true getPhyErrorStatus(id) always CAN_PHY_ERROR_NONE

The bus id is ignored everywhere; the object has no state per bus.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Board (board.yaml, see the board reference and the modules reference):

  • a devices[] entry whose part matches SN65HVD1050* or TJA1051*; devices[].module: canPhyPassive selects this module where several modules serve the part;
  • can[].phy names that device as the transceiver of a bus.

Project (project.yaml): the module is only instantiated for buses listed in use.can. It has no module parameters.

The manifest restricts parts: to transceivers whose mode pin a board may strap to normal operation. A board that drives STB, S or EN from a pin needs a transceiver module with that pin instead (comment in module.yaml).

docs.title: Buses without a matching transceiver module
docs.text:
tools/nxconfig (checks.py, constant PASSIVE) also uses this module as the fallback provider of can_phy:

  • a CAN bus without phy gives the warning "CAN bus ... describes no transceiver (phy), treated as passive (always ready)";
  • a phy device whose part no module lists (and which names no module:) gives the warning "no module for part ... treated as passive transceiver (always ready)".

In both cases the bus is served by PassiveCanPhy.

Example: a board with a UJA1169 system basis chip that only serves as CAN transceiver names no module for it and relies on this warning path, because the part is not in the parts: list of this manifest. boards/buildtest_s32k148/board.yaml uses module: canPhyPassive for two TJA1051T/3.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
• tools/bswgen generates NX_CAN_PHY_COUNT_CANPHYPASSIVE, NX_CAN_PHY_BUSES_CANPHYPASSIVE(X) and NX_MODULE_CANPHYPASSIVE_COUNT; the family port links the CMake target canPhyPassive only when a used bus needs it (NX_MODULES, platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/CMakeLists.txt).
  • platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/integration/Integration.cpp creates one PassiveCanPhy object that serves every bus with a passive transceiver.
  • The module has no bootloader hook: listing such a device in bootloader.init is rejected by tools/nxconfig ("device ... (canPhyPassive) has no bootloader hook").

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• A transceiver fault, a missing supply or a wrong strap cannot be detected: the bus is always reported ready. Bus errors are then only visible through the CAN controller (bus state of canSystem).
  • Sleep or standby of the transceiver is not possible; setMode only records the requested mode.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Host-Tests, Testnamen und Verifikationsstand: Modulkatalog.

docs.title: CAN system, hardware independent parts (canSystem)
docs.text:
Header-only service for the CAN buses of the ECU. It holds the parts that do not touch a register and can therefore be tested on the host:

  • the transmit gate of a bus, following the readiness of its transceiver (CanPhyGate, role can_phy);
  • the readiness reports of the transceiver providers (CanPhyReadiness);
  • the supervision cycle that evaluates gate and bus state (CanSupervisionCycle);
  • the bus state with bus-off counters (CanBusMonitor);
  • the behaviour after bus off when bus off keeps coming back: logged in series, doubling pause, dropping the pending frames (CanBusOffRecovery; project values per bus since an earlier change);
  • the text of the console command can status (CanChannelStatus) and the lines of can log (CanFrameLog).

The buses themselves - controller, interrupts, lifecycle component and console command - live in the port (platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/systems/CanSystem.cpp, class systems::CanSystem), which reads the controller and feeds the state into these classes.

State: verification hardware for gate, bus state up to error passive and console commands on one bus; bus-off and a second bus only in host tests (see Tests).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Header Content can/CanPhyGate.h CanPhyGate::isReady(status) / isReady(phy, busId), decide(open, muted, ready) -> Action::NONE/MUTE/UNMUTE, isTransmitAllowed(open, ready) can/CanPhyReadiness.h ICanPhyReadinessListener::phyReadinessChanged(phy); CanPhyReadiness::setListener, removeListener, hasListener, notify(phy) can/CanSupervisionCycle.h GATE_CYCLE_MS = 10, BUS_STATE_CYCLE_MS = 10; run() returns true when the bus state is due can/CanBusState.h enum class CanBusState (UNKNOWN, ERROR_ACTIVE, ERROR_PASSIVE, BUS_OFF); CanBusMonitor with fromFaultConfinement, fromFlags, name, isBusError, update(state, elapsedMs), stop() and the counters can/CanBusOffRecovery.h CanBusOffRecovery::Config (firstPauseMs, maxPauseMs, discardAfter, quietMs, summaryMs), DEFAULT_CONFIG = {10, 1000, 3, 2000, 10000}; feedMonitor(monitor, state, enteredBusOff, elapsedMs, events), wentBusOff(), recovered(), stop(), cycle(busOff, elapsedMs) -> Step (discard, release, logDiscard, logSummary, logSeriesEnd), series and summary counters can/CanChannelStatus.h struct CanChannelStatus (snapshot of one bus), writeChannelStatus(writer, status) can/CanFrameLog.h CanFrameLog::lineCount, formatLine, entryBytes; BYTES_PER_LINE = 16, LINE_CAPACITY = 96 can/ContextCall.h alias can::ContextCall of console::ContextCall from consoleContext

CMake target canSystem (INTERFACE, links bsp and consoleContext).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The module has no board.yaml keys and no module parameters (modules reference). The buses come from can[] of the board and use.can/can.<bus> of the project (see the board and project references). Per used bus the manifest requires one provider of the role can_phy - the module of the bus's transceiver, for example sbcUja113x or canPhyPassive.

Manifest: lifecycle: { level: 2, task: can }, console command group can.

docs.title: Behaviour after bus off (project can.<bus>.bus_off)
docs.text:
Project values per bus, next to the bit timing of the bus. Every key may be left out; a missing entry means the defaults, which are CanBusOffRecovery::DEFAULT_CONFIG (a generator test compares both).

Key Default Range Meaning first_pause_ms 10 0..65535 pause before the first release of a series (one supervision cycle) max_pause_ms 1000 0..65535 limit of the pause, which doubles with every bus off of the series; 0 = the controller is not held and recovers by itself discard_after 3 0..255 from this bus off of a series on the pending transmit frames are dropped before the release; 0 = never quiet_ms 2000 1..65535 a series ends after this long without bus off summary_ms 10000 1..65535 at most one summary line per this period while a series lasts 
can:
  CAN0: { bitrate: 500000 }                         # defaults
  CAN1:
    bitrate: 250000
    bus_off: { max_pause_ms: 200, discard_after: 1, quiet_ms: 500, summary_ms: 1000 }

tools/nxconfig checks the values against each other, with YAML path and line: first_pause_ms 0 or above max_pause_ms while the bus is held is an error; first_pause_ms set with max_pause_ms 0 and quiet_ms not above max_pause_ms are warnings. tools/bswgen generates bsp/can/canBusOffConfiguration.h with ::bsp::can::<bus>_BUS_OFF_CONFIG for every used bus; the family port gives each bus its own CanBusOffRecovery with these values.

docs.title: Transmit gate
docs.text:
• CAN_PHY_ERROR means "not ready"; CAN_PHY_ERROR_NONE and CAN_PHY_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED (no status available) count as ready.
  • Open and not ready -> MUTE: the port stops transmitting on that bus and keeps receiving. Muted and ready again -> UNMUTE. Frames may be written only while the transceiver is open and ready.

docs.title: When the gate is evaluated
docs.text:
• A provider whose readiness can change calls CanPhyReadiness::notify(phy) after every change, in its own task. The registered listener (the CAN system of the port) only schedules its gate evaluation in its own task; several reports may collapse into one evaluation.
  • There is one listener per ECU; setListener refuses a second one. The pointer is held in one std::atomic with plain loads and stores, no compare-and-swap (comment: ARMv6-M has none).
  • As fallback for a provider that does not report, the supervision cycle checks the gate every 10 ms (GATE_CYCLE_MS). A passive transceiver never reports.
  • History recorded in the header: a related task ran the gate every 1 ms (+1.15 % CPU measured on the eval board); went back to 10 ms plus the reports.

docs.title: Bus state
docs.text:
• fromFaultConfinement maps the CAN encoding of FLTCONF (0 error active, 1 error passive, 2 and 3 bus off); fromFlags serves controllers with separate error-passive and bus-off flags.
  • update(state, elapsedMs) returns the edge (STARTED, WENT_BUS_OFF, RECOVERED, WENT_PASSIVE, WENT_ACTIVE) and counts bus-off entries, recoveries, error-passive entries and the current, longest and total bus-off time (saturating). stop() sets the state back to UNKNOWN and keeps the counters.
  • Only BUS_OFF is a bus error (isBusError, used for the signal qualifier, see signal-qualifier.md). Error passive is deliberately not one: a node alone on the bus reaches it regularly.
  • The class triggers no recovery; whether the controller recovers from bus off automatically is reported by the caller.
  • The bus state is evaluated every BUS_STATE_CYCLE_MS = 10 ms.

docs.title: After bus off (CanBusOffRecovery)
docs.text:
• The port reads its controller every supervision cycle, including the latched "went bus off" flag (FlexCAN ESR1[BOFFINT], cleared after reading), and passes both to feedMonitor(). With the flag the monitor sees both edges of a bus off that started and ended between two readings.
  • The first bus off of a series and its recovery are logged; further bus offs of the series are counted and summarised in at most one line per summaryMs; the end of the series (quietMs without bus off) is one line.
  • With maxPauseMs > 0 the port holds the controller in bus off (FlexCAN CTRL1[BOFFREC] = 1) and releases it when cycle() says so, after a pause that doubles with every bus off of the series (firstPauseMs .. maxPauseMs). A controller without a way to hold bus off runs with maxPauseMs 0.
  • From the discardAfter-th bus off of a series on, cycle() asks to drop the pending transmit frames before the release.
  • The class touches no register and needs no clock; one instance per bus. Origin: board finding 2026-09-22 (a frame hanging in a transmit buffer with CANH shorted to CANL: 9812 bus offs in about ten minutes, two log lines each).

docs.title: Console text
docs.text:
• The port fills a CanChannelStatus in the CAN task and prints it with writeChannelStatus in the console context, so the CAN task no longer waits for the UART. The command itself runs through ContextCall (see consoleContext). Commands: see can in the console reference.
  • The status text also shows the state the OpenBSW driver keeps, because that driver misreads FLTCONF; the port answers from the correctly read field instead (explained in CanSystem.h of the port, external/openbsw is not changed).
  • can log: each received frame becomes one or more lines of at most 16 payload bytes; the first line carries the length, further lines the byte offset (+16, +32, +48). Each line is logged as one "%s" argument, so a logger entry has a fixed upper size (entryBytes) that the port checks at compile time. Bus names longer than 16 characters are cut.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• Bus-off has not been forced on a board; bus-off handling and a second bus are covered by host tests only (verification note).
  • Today only the s32k1xx family port uses the module (platforms/s32k1xx/port/main); no other port under platforms/ includes these headers. CanBusOffRecovery knows no controller; the generated bsp/can/canBusOffConfiguration.h comes from the s32k1xx generator only (tools/bswgen/bswgen.py), a port of another family needs the same header from its generator.
  • In the s32k1xx port the recovery state of a bus sits in a table found by bus id, not yet as a member of CanSystem::Channel (the port header was outside; proposal in the changelog of a separate task).
  • The status text (CanChannelStatus) contains FlexCAN register names (CTRL1, ESR1, FLTCONF); what a controller of another family fills in there is not defined yet.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Host-Tests, Testnamen und Verifikationsstand: Modulkatalog.

docs.title: Console context (consoleContext)
docs.text:
Header-only library for the serial console of the ECU. It has two parts:

  1. Commands in the console context (general form of a separate task): a console command parses its arguments, formats and prints in the lowest task (the console context), and only the short access to a system's state runs in the task that owns that state (ContextCall).
  2. An input line that shares the terminal with the log output: typed characters no longer end up inside log lines (InputLine, InterleavedConsoleInput, IOutputInterleave).

It is a catalogue entry only (kind: library): tools/nxconfig and tools/bswgen assign no board device, take no project values and generate nothing for it.

State: verification hardware for the commands in the console context; the input line only in host tests (see Tests).

docs.title: Why
docs.text: Console output goes to the UART synchronously, byte by byte (86.8 us per character at 115200 Bd, header comment of ContextCall.h). A command registered with the context of its system lent that task to the UART: can status held task can for 40-50 ms, rte json held the runnables of an application task for several cycles, sbc dump held the task that triggers the SBC watchdog. Splitting the command removes that: the owner is busy only for the snapshot or change itself, independent of the length of the output.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Header Content console/ContextCall.h console::ContextCall<RunnableBase, ContextT, Execute>: run(owner, work), type-erased run(owner, work, thunk), callerContext(), queuedCalls(). Hardware and OS independent; the runnable type, context type and queue function are template parameters console/ConsoleContext.h binding to OpenBSW ::async: CONSOLE_CONTEXT (= TASK_IDLE), AsyncContextCall, the one instance consoleContextCall, runInOwnerContext(owner, work) console/IOutputInterleave.h beginOutput() / outputIdle(), called by a writer of whole lines (the logger) around its output; consoleOutputInterleave() is defined by the application console/InputLine.h console::InputLine: line editor (onByte, startCommand, prompt, line, isShown), implements IOutputInterleave; CAPACITY = 128 console/InterleavedConsoleInput.h drop-in for OpenBSW console::StdioConsoleInput (same constructor, init, shutdown, run), line editing through InputLine

CMake target consoleContext (INTERFACE). Users in this repository include the systems of the s32k1xx family port (CanSystem, SbcSystem, GateDriverSystem, CellMonitorSystem), the application systems (RteSystem, EcuStateSystem, SysAdminSystem), ecu/application/src/console/console.cpp and ecu/application/src/logger/logger.cpp; canSystem keeps the alias can::ContextCall.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: None - no board.yaml or project.yaml key, no module parameters (modules reference). The console commands themselves are listed in the console reference.

docs.title: ContextCall
docs.text:
• run(owner, work) runs work in the owner's context and returns when it is done. If the owner is the caller's own context, the work runs inline.
  • Otherwise the work is queued in the owner's context (Execute) and the caller spins until it is done. Because the owner has the higher priority, it preempts the caller as soon as the work is queued.
  • A second call while one is in progress returns false without running anything.
  • Preconditions stated in the header: the caller runs below the owner (a caller above the owner would wait for ever); one call at a time; no timeout; the work does not print.

docs.title: ConsoleContext (target binding)
docs.text:
• Every console command of a neXtBSW system is registered with CONSOLE_CONTEXT (TASK_IDLE), where console input and logger output run as well, so command output, prompt and log lines come from one task.
  • runInOwnerContext runs the work inline if the owner is CONTEXT_INVALID, if the caller is not the console context, or if a call is in progress; otherwise through consoleContextCall. It is not inlined (comment: inlining cost 4.3 KB of flash in the demo application).

docs.title: Input line
docs.text:
• Keys as in OpenBSW StdioConsoleInput: printable 0x20..0x7E, backspace 0x08/0x7F, ESC, CR/LF, prompt "> ". Characters beyond 128 are dropped without echo.
  • beginOutput() before a log line: if the line is shown, VT100 erase line (ESC [ 2 K) and CR, 5 characters.
  • outputIdle() when the logger has nothing more: prompt and typed text are drawn again once, if there is typed text. An empty prompt is not redrawn, so without typing the log output is unchanged byte for byte.
  • A key while the line is not shown is stored and drawn only when the log is not busy. Enter always draws the line first, so the command stays readable above its answer.
  • While a command runs the line is inactive and the console does not read; type-ahead stays in the UART receive buffer.
  • Not thread safe: every call comes from the context of the console input.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• ContextCall has no timeout by design; a wrong priority order (caller above owner) would block the caller for ever. runInOwnerContext avoids this only for callers outside the console context.
  • The input line needs a VT100-capable terminal (the log output already uses VT100 colours).
  • The interleaved input line has not been checked on a board (verification note).

docs.title: dem – fault memory (simplified AUTOSAR DEM)
docs.text:
Status: 2026-09-21, verified with host tests (mock); the board check is open.

The fault memory records diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) with their status byte, counters, snapshot and extended data, and keeps them over a power cycle through the NvM. Its scope is the project decision: a simplified AUTOSAR DEM without warning lamp and without OBD. Everything that describes a DTC is configuration – the diagnostic description of the project (projects/<project>/diag.yaml) – and the code only implements the behaviour. Terms and numbers follow ISO 14229-1 (2026), Annex D; the standard is licensed and is only cited by clause number.

docs.title: Parts
docs.text: Part Where What Core libs/bsw/dem/include/dem/Dem.h dem::Manager<Lock>: status byte, debouncing, conditions, cycles, confirmation, aging, entries, persistence image; header only, board and family neutral Types and interfaces dem/DemTypes.h, dem/IFaultMemory.h configuration tables, IFaultMemory (readers, clear, 85, BSW event interface), ISource, IDidReader, dem::registry Reporting side of a BSW monitor dem/EventReporter.h finds the DTC of an event name once a fault memory is registered, reports the level at every call (a report discarded while 85 was off is made good by the next call), a failure seen between two calls (or before the fault memory ran) once; host tests libs/bsw/canSystem/test/test_can_bus_off_report.py, ecu/application/src/systems/dem/test/test_event_reporter_dtc_setting.py Results of the start dem/StartReport.h, dem/SafetyResetReport.h what a start found in a record that survived the reset: FAILED until the fault memory shows testFailedThisOperationCycle (enable conditions, time debouncing and 85 off cannot swallow it), then PASSED once (clearable in the same run); sources without a failure PASSED once; optional fallback source for a failure without a DTC of its own. SafetyResetReport.h: the cause of the safety reset before this start from the reset-loop record - safety.<event> (number of SafeSupervisor::Event), safety.mcu_watchdog (0xFD), safety.fault_exception (0xFC), safety.reset_other (0xFB, fallback), safety.reset_loop (0xFF, two or more in a row); fed by the BSP task of the s32k1xx port (platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/integration/SafetyResetReport.cpp); host test libs/bsw/dem/test/test_start_report.py Occurrences at run time dem/OccurrenceReport.h a monitor whose fault is gone before the fault memory could sample it counts occurrences (occurred()); update() in the monitor's task hands every batch over as one failure: FAILED until the fault memory shows testFailed in this operation cycle (enable conditions, debouncing and 85 off cannot swallow it), then PASSED once - pending/confirmed, the entry with the snapshot of the first confirmation and the occurrence counter stay, 14 clears it for good; occurrences during a hand-over fold into the next one. First user: safety.safe_off_take_back (+0x05FA), the take-backs of foreign safe_off levels of the s32k1xx port (platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/integration/SafeOffTakeBackRecord.h, BSP task); host test libs/bsw/dem/test/test_start_report.py Tables generated RteDem.h (tools/rtegen) rte::demtables::CONFIG: DTC table, snapshots, extended data, cycles, conditions Sources generated rte::demSample/demCondition/demCycleState one sample per event and cycle under the lock of the RTE Persistence NvM blocks DemEvents, DemEntries (tools/rtegen) derived from the description, never written in rte.yaml; write policy CHANGE Integration ecu/application/src/systems/dem/DemRte.h, RteSystem.cpp start after the NvM, cycle in the NvM context, run-down, console dem Data identifiers ecu/uds DiagDidReader snapshot and extended data identifiers through the read functions of service 22

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Sampling. Every fault_memory.cycle_ms (default 10 ms) the fault memory takes one sample of every event. A sampled source is a port of the ECU description (event.port, a provided port or the value a required port reads) or the signal qualifier of a received message (event.bsw: can.qlf.<Message>). How the value becomes a result is event.result: boolean (true: failed), qualifier (QLF_OK passed, QLF_DEBOUNCE no result, every error failed), status (AUTOSAR event status 0..3) or limit (failed_above/failed_below). Left out, the RTE generator derives it (limit given, qualifier source, boolean port).
  • Reported events. Any other event.bsw name is reported by a BSW module through dem::registry.memory->report(findReportedEvent(name), result) – from any task or interrupt, taken over in the next cycle, a failure reported and passed between two cycles is still sampled once. rte.deadline is reported by RteSystem (deadline violations of a separate task) as a level (ecu/application/src/systems/dem/DeadlineReport.h): PREFAILED while a task cycle or periodic runnable missed its deadline at its last check or a violation happened since the last cycle, PREPASSED once the deadlines are met again - the DTC's debouncing decides when it matures, and a clear stays cleared while the deadlines hold (before a later change the level stayed failed until the next start), can.busoff.<BUS> by the CAN system of the board port for every used bus (can/CanBusOffReport.h of libs/bsw/canSystem: FAILED while bus-off, PASSED while on the bus), safety.device_fault by RteSystem while the safe supervisor holds safe-output groups in the degraded reaction (logging only). A monitor uses dem::EventReporter for it.
  • Sampled BSW sources. bsw.power.undervoltage/bsw.power.overvoltage are sampled by the RTE from the BSW service bsw.power (role power_supply): without a limit the state of the provider (its own thresholds, project values of its module, e.g. modules.<sbc>.undervoltage_mv), with failed_below/failed_above (mV) the measured supply voltage; no reading (provider not started, lost, voltage 0) is no result. bsw.power.ok is also an enable condition. The fault memory only records: a safety reaction stays with the safe supervisor; testFailed is not a fail-safe reaction (D.2.1).
  • Debouncing and fault detection counter (D.6). Counter based: increment/decrement per sample between passed_threshold and failed_threshold, with jump_up/jump_down (default 0: the first failed sample after passed ones moves the counter over zero, so the DTC is prefailed at once). Time based: the same raw result for failed_ms/passed_ms. The fault detection counter is scaled to -128..127; 19 14 reports 0 < fdc < 127. FAILED/PASSED of a status source mature at once.
  • Status byte (D.2.2). Matured failure: bits 0, 1, 2, 5 set, 4 and 6 cleared; matured pass: bits 0, 4, 6 cleared. Bit 3 (confirmed) after confirmation_threshold operation cycles with a failure (D.2.1); the DTC is stored then (snapshot records and identifiers of the extended data read at that moment). Bit 7 (warning indicator) is never set; the availability mask is 0x7F.
  • Operation cycles. autostart: true cycles start with the ECU and end at its run-down; autostart: false cycles follow a boolean provided port connected to dem.cycle.<Cycle>. Start: bit 1 cleared, bit 6 set, debouncing restarts. End: a DTC tested without failure loses bit 2 (pending); the confirmation counter restarts.
  • Aging (D.7). A confirmed DTC counts the cycles of its aging cycle that ended tested and without failure; at aging.threshold_cycles it loses bit 3 and its entry. A failure resets the counter.
  • Enable conditions. A DTC samples only while all its conditions hold (port, ecu.state = RUN, ecu.state.<STATE>); otherwise the debouncing stands.
  • ControlDTCSetting (85). Off stops every status change, cycle transitions included, except clearing (D.2.1). ecu/uds hands the service state to the fault memory. A report() of a BSW monitor is discarded while it is off: the level stays the one reported before, so nothing a monitor reports during the preprogramming step of a flash sequence becomes a DTC afterwards. Sampled events are simply not processed while it is off. The reporters of the BSW (dem::EventReporter, rte.deadline) report their level at every call, so after 85 on the fault memory holds the current level again one call later, not the one of before 85 off.
  • Clearing (14). clear(0xFFFFFF) or one DTC number: status 0x50, counters and debouncing zero, entry deleted.
  • Overflow. replace_oldest displaces the least important (largest priority number), oldest entry that is not more important than the new DTC (the displaced DTC loses bit 3); keep_oldest keeps the entries. A DTC that cannot be stored is not confirmed and retries on its next new failure.
  • Persistence. DemEvents (status and counters per DTC) and DemEntries (entries with stored data) are written by the NvM after a change, at most every fault_memory.write_interval_ms (0: only at the run-down), and at the run-down after the cycles ended. The record id of both blocks follows the DTC table and the entry size, so a changed description starts cleared instead of misreading old data. On a memory that is not prepared (FlexNVM not partitioned, the eval board today) both blocks keep their zero defaults and the fault memory works in RAM.

docs.title: Interface for the diagnostic services
docs.text: dem::IFaultMemory (dem::registry.memory): dtcCount, dtcConfig, dtcInfo (number, status, severity, fault detection counter, counters, stored), findDtc, countByStatusMask, readSnapshot/readExtended (record data as stored; the identifiers of a snapshot record are in dtcConfig().snapshots), clear, setDtcSetting. The DTC format is ISO 14229-1 (format identifier 0x01, derived in tools/nxconfig/diagdesc.py). Served by ecu/uds FaultMemoryServices: 19 01/02/03/04/06/0A/14 and 14 for all DTCs, one DTC or a group (groups are not yet part of the description).

Legende

  • Protect schreibt (P11) Data-ID-Nibble, Zähler und CRC in die Daten und erhöht den Zähler modulo 15; Check prüft CRC und Data ID, dann den Zähler. Konfiguration (const) und Zustand liegen je Botschaft vor; die Bibliothek hält keine globalen Variablen. Vorbild ist Profil 11, P01 und P02 folgen derselben Schnittstelle.
  • Ein Zyklus ohne Botschaft heißt Check(NULL, 0) und ergibt NONEWDATA.
  • Abbildung auf den Qualifier: siehe das folgende Bild und Konfiguration.

    ND -- no --> NONEW("NONEWDATA")

    OK1 -- no --> ERR("ERROR")
    OK1 -- yes --> DELTA("delta = received - last counter<br/>wrap-around after 0x0E")
    DELTA --> D1(("delta"))
    D1 -- "> MaxDeltaCounter" --> WS("WRONGSEQUENCE")
    D1 -- "0" --> REP("REPEATED")
    D1 -- "1" --> OKS("OK")
    D1 -- "2 .. MaxDeltaCounter" --> SOME("OKSOMELOST")
    ERR --> QERR("E2E_P_ERROR<br/>QLF_ERROR_CRC")
    WS --> QAL("E2E_P_WRONGSEQUENCE<br/>QLF_ERROR_ALIVE")
    REP --> QAL2("E2E_P_REPEATED<br/>QLF_ERROR_ALIVE")
    OKS --> QOK("E2E_P_OK")
    SOME --> QOK
    NONEW --> QNN("E2E_P_NONEWDATA<br/>timeout supervision of the RTE")

Legende

  • Das ist eine Folge von Entscheidungen je Aufruf, kein Zustandsautomat: die E2E-Zustandsmaschine (E2E_SMCheck) ist nicht umgesetzt, die zeitbasierte Entprellung liegt im Qualifier der RTE (Tabelle „Abweichungen von der AUTOSAR-API“). Der Zustand zwischen zwei Aufrufen ist nur Zähler und letzter Status.
  • Quelle: libs/bsw/e2e/src/e2e/E2E_P11.c (E2E_P11Check, E2E_P11MapStatusToSM), Abbildung auf QLF_* wie im Beispiel unten. Profil 1 und 2 haben zusätzlich SYNC, INITIAL, WRONGCRC (siehe API).

AUTOSAR-E2E-Profile P01, P02 und P11 für den Schutz von CAN-Botschaften: Sender tragen Zähler und CRC ein (Protect), Empfänger prüfen CRC, Data ID und Zählerfolge (Check). Grundlage für den Signal-Qualifier der RTE (doc/architecture/signal-qualifier.md).

Stand: Host-getestet (Mock). Seit einer früheren Änderung (2026-09-16) in der RTE genutzt: rtegen erzeugt die E2E-Prüfung für Signale mit Profil (E2E_PROFILES), ecu/rte/CMakeLists.txt linkt die Bibliothek bei RTE_USES_E2E.

docs.title: Eigenschaften
docs.text:
• C99, nur <stdint.h>/<stdbool.h>, keine OpenBSW-Abhängigkeit, keine dynamische Speicherverwaltung, keine globalen Variablen, reentrant. Läuft damit unverändert auf S32K1/S32K3/STM32 und im Host-Build (Zig, Tester).
  • Zustand je Botschaft: Jede geschützte oder geprüfte Botschaft hat eine eigene Konfigurationsstruktur (E2E_PxxConfigType, kann const im Flash liegen) und eine eigene Zustandsstruktur. Beliebig viele Busse und Botschaften sind möglich; Busse, IDs und Anzahl legt der Generator fest, nicht die Bibliothek.
  • Strukturen enthalten nur uint8_t/uint16_t/bool, Aufzählungen sind uint8_t mit #define-Konstanten. Das Layout ist dadurch unabhängig von -fshort-enums (Target) und aus Python per ctypes nachbildbar.
  • Konstanten- und Funktionsnamen, Werte und Verhalten nach AUTOSAR R22-11 (Quellen unten).

docs.title: API
Konfiguration
docs.text: Offsets sind Bit-Offsets ab Datenbeginn wie in AUTOSAR: Byte = Offset / 8, Offset % 8 == 0 ist das untere Nibble, == 4 das obere. Varianten 1A/1C/11A/11C: CRCOffset 0, CounterOffset 8, DataIDNibbleOffset 12. DataLength in Bit (P01/P11: 16…256, P02: 16…2048). E2E_PxxCheckConfig prüft zusätzlich zu AUTOSAR, dass CRC-Byte, Zähler-Nibble und Data-ID-Nibble in den Daten liegen und sich nicht überschneiden und im Modus NIBBLE die Data ID höchstens 12 Bit hat. rtegen soll die Offsets aus den DBC-Signalen ableiten und dieselben Regeln mit YAML-Pfad melden; die Bibliothek prüft bei jedem Aufruf noch einmal und liefert dann E2E_E_INPUTERR_WRONG.

docs.title: Beispiel für eine eigene Aufgabe (Empfang, P11)
docs.text:
static E2E_P11ConfigType const PcCommandE2e = {8U, 0U, 0x100U, 12U, E2E_P11_DATAID_NIBBLE, 64U, 1U};
static E2E_P11CheckStateType pcCommandE2eState;          /* E2E_P11CheckInit() beim Start */

/* bei Empfang: data/8; im Zyklus ohne Empfang: NULL/0 */
E2E_ReturnType const rc = E2E_P11Check(&PcCommandE2e, &pcCommandE2eState, data, 8U);
switch (E2E_P11MapStatusToSM(rc, pcCommandE2eState.Status))
{
    case E2E_P_OK: /* gültig: Heilung, QLF_OK wenn keine anderen Fehler */ break;
    case E2E_P_ERROR: /* -> QLF_ERROR_CRC (entprellt) */ break;
    case E2E_P_REPEATED:
    case E2E_P_WRONGSEQUENCE: /* -> QLF_ERROR_ALIVE (entprellt) */ break;
    default: /* E2E_P_NONEWDATA: Timeout-Überwachung der RTE */ break;
}

Senden: E2E_P11Protect(&cfg, &state, data, 8U) nach dem Packen der Signale, vor dem Senden.

Abbildung laut Konzept: ERROR → QLF_ERROR_CRC, REPEATED/WRONGSEQUENCE → QLF_ERROR_ALIVE, NONEWDATA → Timeout-Überwachung. E2E_P_NOTAVAILABLE liefert keine Check-Funktion; es ist der Startwert für einen gespeicherten Status, solange noch nichts geprüft wurde.

Für P01/P02 empfiehlt sich profileBehavior = true (R4.2-Verhalten wie P11): die erste Botschaft (INITIAL) zählt als WRONGSEQUENCE, SYNC als OK. Mit der zeitbasierten Entprellung des Qualifiers bleibt die erste Botschaft dadurch QLF_DEBOUNCE, bis die zweite mit passender Folge kommt. P11 verhält sich nach dem Start ähnlich: der Empfänger startet mit Zähler 0x0E; eine erste Botschaft mit Zähler 0 (bis MaxDeltaCounter - 1) ist OK, mit 14 REPEATED, sonst WRONGSEQUENCE. Ab der zweiten Botschaft ist die Folge synchron.

docs.title: Abweichungen von der AUTOSAR-API
docs.text:
AUTOSAR Hier Grund Std_ReturnType, Enum-Typen uint8_t-Typen mit gleichen Werten ohne Std_Types.h, Layout unabhängig von -fshort-enums P01/P02: State->NewDataAvailable, kein Length Parameter length; data == NULL && length == 0 = keine neue Botschaft gleiche Schnittstelle wie P11, Längenprüfung auch bei P01/P02 P02: Konfigurationsfeld Offset (R22-11) nicht vorhanden, Kopf fest in Byte 0/1 die Flussdiagramme von P02 werten Offset nicht aus; Kopfverschiebung bietet P22 Forward-Funktionen nicht umgesetzt für CAN-Botschaften der RTE nicht nötig E2E-Zustandsmaschine (E2E_SMCheck) nicht umgesetzt Konzept: zeitbasierte Entprellung im Qualifier Protect mit Zählerwert > 14 im Zustand (P01/P11) E2E_E_INPUTERR_WRONG Zustand wurde von außen verfälscht

Übernommene Eigenheiten der Spezifikation: P01 meldet einen empfangenen Zähler 15 als E2E_E_INPUTERR_WRONG (nicht als Status); P11 prüft den Zählerwert 15 nicht gesondert (Delta-Berechnung modulo 15 wie im Flussdiagramm). P01 und P02 erhöhen die Zählertoleranz MaxDeltaCounter bei jedem Check-Aufruf um 1 bis zur nächsten gültigen Botschaft.

SyncCounterInit bei P01/P02: Mit SyncCounterInit = 0 bleibt die Referenz LastValidCounter bei WRONGSEQUENCE stehen, während MaxDeltaCounter weiter wächst. Ein stehender Zähler nach einem Sprung passt deshalb nach delta - 1 Botschaften ins Fenster und kommt einmal als OKSOMELOST (E2E_P_OK) zurück, danach REPEATED - spezifikationsgemäß, gedacht für die Zustandsmaschine mit Fenster. Am Board (Mitschnitt 2026-09-16: gültig bis Zähler 4, dann dauerhaft 0) war das die zehnte Botschaft, und der Qualifier der RTE heilte für einen Zyklus. Wer ohne E2E_SMCheck auswertet (Heilung nach einer gültigen Botschaft), setzt SyncCounterInit >= 1: dann wird der Zähler der Botschaft mit falscher Folge neue Referenz, der stehende Zähler bleibt REPEATED, und die nächste Botschaft in Folge ist SYNC (mit profileBehavior = true E2E_P_OK). P11 verhält sich von sich aus so. rtegen erzeugt SyncCounterInit = 1 (tools/rtegen/rtegen.py, E2E_SYNC_COUNTER_INIT). Nachweis: testStalledCounterLegacy im C-Host-Test (Statusfolge mit 0 und 1 für P01 und P02).

Das Python-Referenzmodell tools/e2e/e2e_ref.py ist unabhängig vom C-Code geschrieben (tabellengesteuerte CRC über die ganze Bytefolge mit den effektiven Start-/XOR-Werten statt verketteter Aufrufe) und kann von PC-Werkzeugen importiert werden, z. B. um E2E-geschützte Botschaften im Tester zu erzeugen oder zu prüfen.
