Outputs: integration/hallConfiguration.h, bsp/hall/hallSensorConfiguration.h, bsp/hall/hallDecoderConfiguration.h.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Time base: getSystemTimeUs32Bit() of the OpenBSW system timer (32 bit, wraps after about 71.6 minutes). get() takes the time inside the lock, so an edge between sampling and reading cannot look like a standstill.
  • Debouncing is done in the decoder, not with the digital input filter of the port: that filter is one setting per port and would change every other input of the port (manifest, debounce_us).
  • PinIrqConfig.cpp checks at compile time that the vector table of the family port has a pin-detect vector for every port with a Hall signal; otherwise the handler would never run and the measurement would report standstill for ever. It also checks the dispatcher table (one consumer per pin, every port served by exactly one vector).
  • Several flagged pins of one sensor in one interrupt give several calls with the same time; the decoder does not step on a repeated state, so the result is the same as the single call per port before a later change.
  • Evaluation, qualities and standstill: see hallDecoder.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• Open in todo: a console group hall and the board test with a signal source. The pin-interrupt dispatcher of that item exists since an earlier change; the pin events of the project become its second consumer.
  • Until a follow-up task the dispatcher table is derived from the Hall configuration only, and the generated vector list names one vector per port (PORT<x>_IRQn): a Hall sensor on an S32K11x (one PORT vector) is not supported yet.
  • s32k1xx pin interrupt only; a timer-capture access or another family would bring its own access and manifest (comment in module.yaml).
  • The host tests lie outside this directory (platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspHall/test), so the modules reference shows "Host tests: none" for this module.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
tools/test -k bswgen (entry bswgen, group python), in tools/bswgen/test_bswgen.py:

  • BswGenHallTest - generator on an own profile with two sensor sets (120 degrees, one pole pair, one port; 60 degrees, eight pole pairs, inverted signals, sector_down, two ports) and on the eval board demo profile;
  • BswGenHallHostTest - compiles HallSensors with the decoder and the pin-interrupt dispatcher against the generated configuration and runs platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspHall/test/host/HallSensorsHostTest.cpp against RAM models of GPIO and PORT with a pin-detect model (mutants of the access and of the dispatcher): register picture after init, sampled state with inversion, a revolution forwards and backwards through the pin interrupts of all ports, standstill, no sensor, two independent sensors, foreign interrupt flags, names, state and time under the lock. NoHallSensorHostTest.cpp covers a project without a Hall device;
  • HallDecoderHostTest - the decoder itself.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: From module.yaml: verification: mock - "Host tests only (decoder and pin interrupt access against two profiles); no Hall sensor or signal source has been connected to a board yet."

docs.title: Safety task, s32k1xx (safeLifecycle)
docs.text:
Port module of the s32k1xx family: the safety task. SafetyManager runs one cycle of the safety supervision per period of the task (period check, deadman configuration check, watchdog service, memory, supply and I/O supervision); SafetySystem (ecu/application) schedules the task at a fixed rate. The sources are modified copies of the OpenBSW files of the same name (tracked in tools/openbswsync/copies.yaml).

Since an earlier change its three times are module parameters of the project (modules.safeLifecycle, project_parameters: true), generated into integration/safeLifecycleConfiguration.h. Before, they were code constants in three files, kept equal by tests.

State: verification hardware - the demo values run on the eval board without watchdog reset; other values, the derivation and the period check only in host and generator tests.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Project (project.yaml, modules reference):

Parameter Default Range Used as task_period_ms 10 ms 1..1000 SYSTEM_CYCLE_TIME in SafetySystem.cpp (schedules the task) and SafetyManager::CYCLE_PERIOD_MS (period check) watchdog_timeout_ms 250 ms 1..65535, S32K1: at most 511 SafeWatchdog::WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MS (ecu/safety/safeWatchdog) cycle_lateness_ms 2 ms 0..999, below task_period_ms SafetyManager::CYCLE_LATENESS_MS (period check, SM-04)

Derived by tools/nxconfig (checks.py safety_timing), never set by the project:

  • The LPO limits in per mille of nominal, from the derivative database (mcudb/<family>/<derivative>.yaml clock.lpo, data sheet), rounded outwards: slowest floor(min_hz x 1000 / nominal_hz), fastest ceil(max_hz x 1000 / nominal_hz); S32K1xx 113 ... 139 kHz at 128 kHz: 882 and 1086. Generated as NX_MODULE_SAFELIFECYCLE_DERIVED_LPO_MIN_PER_MILLE / ..._MAX_PER_MILLE; the period check and the watchdog relation of SafetyManager.cpp use them (before constants of safeSupervisionCheck/LptmrCycleTimer.h).
  • SafetyManager::WATCHDOG_CYCLIC_COUNTER = floor(watchdog_timeout_ms x 1000 / (3 x task_period_ms x fastest LPO per mille)), generated as NX_MODULE_SAFELIFECYCLE_DERIVED_WATCHDOG_SERVICE_CYCLES. The WDOG counts the LPO, and its driver loads the counter for the nominal 128 kHz, so at the fastest LPO of the data sheet the time-out expires earlier (250 ms nominal: 230.2 ms at 139 kHz). Three service intervals fit into that shortest time-out by construction (finding F2 of doc/safety/concept.md); demo 3 x 7 x 10 ms = 210 ms <= 230.2 ms (with the nominal derivation before a later change: 8 cycles, 240 ms). It is also the window of the period check (CYCLE_PERIOD_WINDOW).

Checked by tools/nxconfig, each with the YAML path of the value (the configure step stops on an error):

  • time-out shorter than three periods (no service interval possible), and the relation 3 x interval <= time-out at the fastest LPO as counter-check of the derivation (the check of a separate task);
  • a derivative without clock.lpo (error at its clock entry): the S32K1 watchdog counts the LPO;
  • time-out beyond the S32K1 WDOG: TOVAL is 16 bit at the nominal 128 kHz LPO of the OpenBSW driver, so 511 ms;
  • the conditions of the static_asserts of the period check in SafetyManager.cpp (a window of at least one tick, one interval shorter than a window, a window within one wrap-around of the LPTMR), computed with the LPO limits above and the tick and width of safeSupervisionCheck/LptmrCycleTimer.h - e.g. a time-out of 30 ms at 10 ms gives a window of one cycle, which cannot work;
  • the module parameters of the safe supervisor that count safety cycles (modules.safeSupervisor, manifest ../safeSupervisor/module.yaml): the window of the device-bus correlation in cycles is derived from device_bus_window_ms; warnings if it is shorter than two supervision cycles (cycle_ms) of the slowest device on an SPI bus or if there are more device buses than its 8 slots; error if reset_loop_clear_ms is shorter than one period.

SafetyManager.cpp asserts the watchdog relation (at the fastest LPO) once more on the generated values at compile time.

docs.title: Limits and open points
docs.text:
• The LPO range is the column S32K1xx of the data sheet (max 139 kHz). An S32K14xW derivative (max 141 kHz) needs its own mcudb file with max_hz: 141000; the per-mille limits and the service interval follow from it.
  • The OpenBSW watchdog driver still loads TOVAL for the nominal 128 kHz; the fastest LPO is taken into account by servicing more often, not by a longer TOVAL.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• nxconfig-watchdog (tools/nxconfig/test_watchdog_timing.py): derivation and every check with an own test profile (S32K144, two TMC6200 on two SPI buses), own source trees of the constants and own mcudb copies with another LPO range.
  • cycle-period-constants: the code takes all values from the generated macros; bounds recomputed with fractions from the LPO range of mcudb.
  • safety-cycle, safety-gate, cycle-timer-off: SafetyManager with the test profile test/host/stubs/integration (270 ms, 8 cycles).
  • bswgen-reference: integration/safeLifecycleConfiguration.h of every reference profile.

docs.title: Memory safety of the s32k1xx family (safeMemory)
docs.text:
Port module of the s32k1xx family, a modified copy of the OpenBSW module of the same name (tracked in tools/openbswsync/copies.yaml): the MPU gate of the safety RAM (SM-10, SM-11), the ECC supervision of RAM and flash (SM-15, SM-16) with the start-up latent-fault test of the RAM ECC (SM-55) and the ROM check (SM-14). The safety concept describes the mechanisms (doc/safety/concept.md section 6.2), the failure analysis rates them (doc/safety/fmea.md SM-10 … SM-16).

It has no board device. Its one project decision is the re-check period of the ROM check, a module parameter of the project (modules.safeMemory, project_parameters: true).

State: verification hardware for the first ROM-check pass (board 2026-09-21: a valid image passes, an image with one changed character is held in the safe state); the re-check period, the known-answer test of the CRC unit and the suspension during flash writes are host tests only (board checks B1 and B9 of fmea.md section 8).

docs.title: ROM check (SM-14)
docs.text:
Part Where Checksum list (five areas behind the image) linker template platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/linkerscript/application.dld.in, section .checksum Reference CRC, written after the link tools/romCheckImage.py (inject, check), called by cmake/NxRomCheck.cmake Plausibility of the list include/safeMemory/RomCheckList.h (checkList, feedAreas, Image) Pass and re-check include/safeMemory/RomCheck.h, src/safeMemory/RomCheck.cpp Flash write indicator include/safeMemory/RomCheckFlashWrites.h, src/romCheckFlashWrites/RomCheckFlashWrites.cpp (CMake target romCheckFlashWrites)

One pass is: the known-answer test of the CRC unit (five fixed words, expected 0x498CFAA3, the value the Python model of romCheckImage.py gives), then the plausibility of the list, then the CRC-32 through the CRC unit over the areas, compared with __checksum_result. A mismatch, an implausible list, a failed known-answer test and a pass kept off by flash writes for more than one period are all reported as ROM_CHECK_FAILURE (safe state S1 held).

When a pass runs. RomCheck::init() (from SafetyManager::init()) requests the first pass. RomCheck::idle() runs it when it is due; it is called from the idle context only - once by the component romcheck of the board port (lifecycle level 2) and in every round of the idle handler of the application (ecu/application app.cpp). After the first pass the next is due when modules.safeMemory.rom_check_period_ms has passed since the start of the previous one (0 = once per start). The pass runs at the lowest priority without a lock and outside the safety shell; every supervised task preempts it. Only the bookkeeping at the end of a pass and the report enter the safety shell.

Flash writes. Every code that writes a flash module (the NvM through its memory, a later in-application update) brackets the write with safety::FlashWriteScope. While a write is open, no pass starts; a pass during which a write began is discarded without a report and repeated. A running flash command (FTFC FSTAT[CCIF] clear) counts as a write. The indicator lies in ordinary RAM (its own library, whose archive name does not match the protected sections *libsafe* of the linker script), so any task may update it. A due pass that could not run for longer than one period is reported (ROMCHECK_OVERDUE), so a writer that never ends its write cannot switch the check off silently; with period 0 there is no such deadline.

Area with its own reference. Flash content that may be written without a build - the calibration segment of memory.calibration - is not in the list: the build reference would hold the ECU before the calibration start-up check could apply on_invalid. The linker template marks its region (__rom_check_own_area_start/_end), romCheckImage.py accepts image content outside the list only there, and the owner registers its check with RomCheck::setOwnAreaCheck() (the integration in ecu/application app.cpp: calibration::recheckSegment, header and values against the CRCs of the CALV header). Every pass calls it after the list, with the same period and flash write rules; a deviation is ROMCHECK_OWN_AREA_FAILED, reported as ROM_CHECK_FAILURE like the rest.

The CRC unit is reserved for SM-14. No other code of the repository uses it; a second user would have to be serialised with the pass.

The check is only compiled into an image whose reference the build wrote (NX_ROM_CHECK_IMAGE, set by nx_rom_check_image() for its consumers main and app.ecu).

docs.title: Latent-fault test of the RAM ECC (SM-55)
docs.text: safe_memory::eccLatentTestAtStart() (EccLatentTest.h), called once per start by main() of the family port after the reset-loop limit and before the BSP. Per ECC channel of the derivative (S32K14x: SRAM_L and SRAM_U; S32K11x: SRAM_U) the error injection module inverts one data bit, then two, on a read of a reserved word in that array (nxEccLatentTestWordFirst in the hot bss, nxEccLatentTestWordLast in the no-init RAM). Expected: the single-bit read returns the stored pattern and the ERM records a correction at the word's address; the double-bit read is recorded as non-correctable (not on the S32K11x, whose Cortex-M0+ takes it as a hard fault). The EIM is off and the ERM record cleared afterwards, the channel's ERM interrupt enables are masked during the test. A failure is INTEGRITY_EVENT_DMA_ECC_ERROR with context bit 3 (ECC_SOURCE_LATENT_TEST), failed checks in bits 17..8, channel in bits 27..24. The injected read (eimInjectedRead, EccLatentTestTarget.cpp) is register-only with all interrupts and faults masked. The flash ECC has no injection module and is not tested (fmea.md SM-55).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Project (project.yaml, modules reference):

  • modules.safeMemory.rom_check_period_ms, default 60000, range 0..86400000 ms - start to start of two passes; 0 = once per start. A value other than 0 has to be longer than the longest flash write of the ECU (it is the deadline for postponed passes) and at most the latent-fault interval the integrator needs (AoU-25). Generated into integration/safeMemoryConfiguration.h as NX_MODULE_SAFEMEMORY_PARAM_ROM_CHECK_PERIOD_MS.

Duration of one pass: about 3 … 6 ms computed for 43 049 words at 80 MHz (fmea.md 5.1), not measured yet (B1).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Host (tools/test -k <name>): rom-check (the real RomCheck.cpp against a register model of the CRC unit and the FTFC status, own test profile with a period of 2500 ms), rom-check-mutations (21 built-in faults, slow), rom-check-image (post-link step), nvm-flash-write-bracket (the NvM side of the suspension, ecu/application), safe-memory-ecc, bswgen-mpu; ECC latent-fault test: safe-memory-ecc-latent, safe-memory-ecc-latent-s32k11x, safe-memory-ecc-latent-mutations (slow), safe-memory-ecc-latent-elf (demo ELF). Board: first pass 2026-09-21 (eighth part); re-check and suspension open (B9); ECC latent-fault test open.

docs.title: Safe supervisor, project values of the s32k1xx port (safeSupervisor)
docs.text:
The safe supervisor itself is family neutral (ecu/safety/safeSupervisor, CMake target safeSupervisor): it maps every safety event to its reaction (S1 safe state, S2 reset, S3 report), limits reset loops and correlates device reports per bus. This directory only holds its module manifest in the family port, because the family port decides that the supervisor runs in its safety task and counts its times in cycles of that task (modules.safeLifecycle.task_period_ms). Another family port that uses the supervisor brings its own copy.

Since an earlier change the values that were code constants or provisional defaults are module parameters of the project (modules.safeSupervisor, project_parameters: true), generated into integration/safeSupervisorConfiguration.h.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Project (project.yaml, modules reference):

Parameter Default Range Used as reset_loop_limit 3 1..255 limit of SafeSupervisor::startResetLoopLimit() in the family main.cpp (SSR-065) reset_loop_clear_ms 60000 ms 10..86400000, at least one task period fault-free time that clears the count, converted into safety cycles in main.cpp (resetloop::clearCyclesOf, rounded up) device_bus_window_ms 200 ms 1..60000 window of the device-bus correlation, SafeSupervisor::DEVICE_BUS_WINDOW_CYCLES

Derived by tools/nxconfig (checks.py _safe_supervisor), never set by the project:

  • NX_MODULE_SAFESUPERVISOR_DERIVED_DEVICE_BUS_WINDOW_CYCLES = ceil(device_bus_window_ms / safeLifecycle.task_period_ms) - never shorter than the time set; demo 200 ms / 10 ms = 20 cycles.

Checked by tools/nxconfig, with the YAML path of the value:

  • error: reset_loop_clear_ms shorter than one period of the safety task (the static_assert in main.cpp);
  • warning: the window shorter than two supervision cycles (cycle_ms) of the slowest device on an SPI bus;
  • warning: more device buses than the supervisor tracks at the same time (SafeSupervisor::DEVICE_BUS_SLOTS, 8).

State: verification hardware for the reset-loop limit with the default values (board checks B10/B11); the device-bus window has no reporting device yet and is covered by host and generator tests only.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• nxconfig-watchdog (tools/nxconfig/test_watchdog_timing.py): derivation of the window, the checks, the defaults.
  • safe-supervisor, safe-supervisor-bare: the correlation with the test profile ecu/safety/safeSupervisor/test/host/stubs/integration/safeSupervisorConfiguration.h (130 ms, 13 cycles - not the demo values).
  • bswgen-reference: integration/safeSupervisorConfiguration.h of every reference profile.

docs.title: Reference and supply supervision, s32k1xx (safeSystem)
docs.text:
Port module of the s32k1xx family: safety supervision of the ADC reference voltage (bandgap measured against VREFH) and of the internal supplies of the MCU (SIM supply monitor), run in the safety task. It is S32K1 specific and lives in the family port template since an earlier change; before, every board of the family needed its own copy (finding B6). The source is a modified copy of the OpenBSW file of the same name (tracked in tools/openbswsync/copies.yaml).

It has no board device; its parameters are module parameters of the project (modules.safeSystem, project_parameters: true). The nominal reference voltage is a board fact (board.adc_reference_mv).

State: verification hardware - runs on a board without false alarms; a wrong reference voltage and failed readings up to the limit only in host tests (see Verification).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Header safeSystem/SafeSystem.h, source src/safeSystem/SafeSystem.cpp, CMake target safeSystem (links safeSupervisor, safeMemory, bspMcu, bspInterrupts, bspIo).

Item Content init() enables the ADC supply monitor of the SIM (SIM->CHIPCTL) cyclic() one supervision cycle (called by the safety manager) getAdcDiagnostics() -> AdcDiagnostics readErrors, consecutiveRefErrors, skippedRefChecks, skippedSupplyChecks, refVoltageMv, refVoltageValid, consecutiveSupplyErrors resetAdcDiagnostics() clears the counters; the running series of failures, the last reference voltage and its validity stay ADC_REF_ERROR_LIMIT from NX_MODULE_SAFESYSTEM_PARAM_ADC_READ_ERROR_LIMIT (generated integration/safeSystemConfiguration.h) reference band (in SafeSystem.cpp) nominal NX_ADC_REFERENCE_MV (generated bsp/adc/adcReferenceConfiguration.h), tolerance NX_MODULE_SAFESYSTEM_PARAM_ADC_REFERENCE_TOLERANCE_MV (generated integration/safeSystemConfiguration.h) AdcErrorContext context passed to the monitors: ADC_CONTEXT_OUT_OF_RANGE (1), ADC_CONTEXT_READ_FAILURE (2)

Manifest: roles adc_reference_monitor and internal_supply_monitor, lifecycle level 1 in task safety, console group safeadc (stats, reset; implemented in platforms/s32k1xx/port/safety/adcSafetyConsole, see the console reference).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Project (project.yaml, modules reference):

  • modules.safeSystem.adc_read_error_limit, default 10, range 1..100000 - failed bandgap readings in a row before the reference monitor is triggered with context 2. It counts cycles of the safety task, so the time follows from that task's period. Since an earlier change the same limit applies to the internal supply channel (see Behaviour); the description in module.yaml still names the bandgap only.
  • modules.safeSystem.adc_reference_tolerance_mv, default 200, range 1..1000, unit mV - allowed deviation of the measured reference from its nominal value. It has to cover the accuracy of the reference source and the spread of the bandgap.

Board (board.yaml): board.adc_reference_mv - nominal voltage at VREFH, the same value the ADC channels are scaled with. tools/bswgen generates it into bsp/adc/adcReferenceConfiguration.h as NX_ADC_REFERENCE_MV. A board without the key gets no macro, and SafeSystem.cpp stops the build with an #error; a project that reads the bandgap channel is rejected earlier by tools/nxconfig ("defines no board.adc_reference_mv"). A tolerance that is not below the nominal value stops the build with a static_assert.

Example: the eval board S32K144 (LM4132, 4096 mV) with the default tolerance checks 3896..4296 mV; a board whose VREFH is the 5 V supply (buildtest_s32k148, s32k116evb) checks 4800..5200 mV.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
cyclic() reads the bandgap channel and the internal supply channel with all interrupts suspended and the fusa gate of the memory protection closed, then evaluates both:

  • Reference: VREFH = 1000 mV x 4095 / bandgap raw value (12-bit ADC, bandgap taken as 1000 mV). Outside adc_reference_mv +- adc_reference_tolerance_mv (limits inclusive) -> adcReferenceMonitor.trigger(ADC_CONTEXT_OUT_OF_RANGE). Until the first valid reading, refVoltageMv of the diagnostics reports the nominal value (with refVoltageValid false).
  • Failed reading (AnalogInput::get failed, or raw value 0, which the bandgap cannot deliver): counted, the check is left out and the last valid reference is kept. Only when adc_read_error_limit readings in a row failed is the monitor triggered, once, with ADC_CONTEXT_READ_FAILURE. Reason in the header: the safe supervisor answers an ADC reference error with limp home and a software reset, and a single transient of the serialized ADC access is no evidence of a wrong reference.
  • Supplies: a counter 0..5 steps the SIM supply multiplexer - cycle 0 selects 3.3 V flash, 2 selects 3.3 V oscillator, 4 selects 1.2 V core; the cycles in between measure the selected supply. It is compared with its nominal value +- 200 mV using the last measured reference; outside -> internalSuppliesMonitor.trigger(...). The comparison is left out (counted) while the reading failed or no valid reference is known yet.
  • Failed supply reading (finding F14 of doc/safety/fmea.md): failed readings of the supply channel are counted in a row (the channel is read in every cycle); at adc_read_error_limit the supplies monitor is triggered, once, with ADC_CONTEXT_READ_FAILURE, and one good reading ends the series. Before a later change a channel that never delivered ended the supervision of all three supplies without an event. A missing reference is not counted here - that is the bandgap's own limit.

What the monitors do on a trigger is decided by the safe supervisor, not by this module.

docs.title: Limits and known gaps
docs.text:
• Reference band from the configuration (closed): until a follow-up task the nominal reference VREFH_NOMINAL_MV = 4096 (+- 200 mV, the eval board) was a constant in SafeSystem.cpp, and a board with another VREFH (for example 5000 mV) would have triggered the reference monitor. The nominal value now comes from board.adc_reference_mv, the tolerance from modules.safeSystem.adc_reference_tolerance_mv; the eval board binaries are byte-identical to before.
  • Still constants: the supply tolerances (+- 200 mV), the nominal supplies (3.3 V, 1.2 V) and the bandgap value (1000 mV) - facts of the S32K1 derivative rather than of a board, not part of a separate task.
  • s32k1xx only (SIM supply monitor).
  • A wrong reference voltage and the read-failure limits (bandgap and, supply channel) have not been provoked on a board (verification note).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
tools/test -k bswgen (entry bswgen, group python) compiles the production SafeSystem.cpp with test/host/SafeSystemHostTest.cpp against stubs of its dependencies (test/host/stubs: a SIM register struct, a memory protection that records the fusa gate, a safe supervisor that records every trigger with its context instead of resetting, a scriptable AnalogInput::get). Focus: a failed ADC reading must not be taken as a wrong reference (before a later change one transient read error rebooted the ECU). The same test runs as entry safe-system (group host).

The stubs configure the reference band as 5000 mV +- 300 mV on purpose (not the eval board), and the expectations are derived from the macros. BswGenAdcReferenceTest in tools/bswgen/test_bswgen.py checks the generated headers of its own profile (tools/bswgen/test/profiles/projects/testproject_adc_reference: 5000 mV +- 350 mV) and of the repository projects. It runs the host test against the generated headers of that profile and of the eval board demo, and it checks that SafeSystem.cpp with the old constants (4096 mV, 200 mV) or without one of the two limits fails the test.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: From module.yaml: verification: hardware - "Reference and supply monitoring run on the eval board without false alarms (bandgap readings, safeadc counters at 0, no safety reset); a wrong reference voltage and failed readings up to the limit are covered by host tests only."

docs.title: Startup templates per core architecture
docs.text: Architecture File Cores State ARMv6-M armv6m/startUp.S Cortex-M0+ (S32K116/S32K118) template, compiled and linked in the M0+ build test ARMv7-M ../port/main/src/bsp/startUp.S (family port template) Cortex-M4F in the family port since an earlier change, not yet merged with the template here; since an earlier change its external vectors come from the same generated startup/nxIrqVectors.inc

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• Linker symbols (same as the ARMv7-M startup and the S32K1 application linker script): __StackTop, __isr_vector (section .isr_vector), __DATA_RAM/__DATA_RAM_END (RAM cleared before the copy, ECC), __etext + __data_start__/__data_end__, __DATA_ROM_GENERAL + __data_general_start__/__data_general_end__, __DATA_ROM_RX + __LAUNCH_FROM_RAM_START/__LAUNCH_FROM_RAM_END, __bss_start__/__bss_end__, __MPU_BSS_START/__MPU_BSS_END, section .__startUpSection (__start, boot header of the bootloader).
  • Integration functions: boardInit() (before the RAM initialization, no global data), main().
  • Interrupt list startup/nxIrqVectors.inc in the include path: one line per external interrupt number, from 0, NX_IRQ_VECTOR(<handler>) or NX_IRQ_RESERVED(). Handler names unique. The list belongs to the derivative (IRQ names of the device header) and should be generated from mcudb; ARMv6-M allows at most 32 entries (assembler error otherwise). Without NX_STARTUP_SAFE_ISR every handler is weak and defaults to DefaultISR; NMI_Handler, HardFault_Handler, SVC_Handler, PendSV_Handler, SysTick_Handler as well (FreeRTOS maps its handlers to these names in FreeRTOSConfig.h).
  • Interrupt frame of the safety shell: the application assembles the startup with NX_STARTUP_SAFE_ISR (port/main/CMakeLists.txt). Then every external vector points at Safe_<handler> and SysTick at Safe_SysTick_Handler - the SAFE_ISR wrappers of port/safety/safeLifecycle/src/safeLifecycle/IsrWrapper.cpp, which close the MPU gate of the protected RAM around the handler (list interrupts/nxSafeIsrVectors.h, tools/bswgen), and the weak DefaultISR defaults of the handlers live there, not in the startup. The safety handlers keep their own Safe_<handler> (FTFC fault, ERM double fault, naked watchdog path, halt deadman on LPIT0 channel 1 as an alias of its handler). The ARMv7-M startup of the family port does the same unconditionally and fills the numbers behind the derivative's last vector with DefaultISR up to its 255 entries and the TRIM word. tools/elfcheck checks the linked application (isr-unwrapped).
  • VTOR is written with __isr_vector (application behind the bootloader). S32K116/S32K118 have VTOR (__VTOR_PRESENT 1 in the S32DS headers); a Cortex-M0 without VTOR would need the table at address 0.
  • No FPU, no MemManage/BusFault/UsageFault/DebugMon vectors (reserved on ARMv6-M), one NVIC ICER/ICPR register.
  • Not included: the S32K14x "user TRIM" word at the end of the ARMv7-M table, the boot header (bootHeader.S of the family port, data only; since an earlier change without an .arch directive, so it assembles for both architectures).
  • In the application since an earlier change: platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/CMakeLists.txt selects this template for ARMv6-M; startup/nxIrqVectors.inc is generated by tools/bswgen from the IRQ list of the derivative's device header (mcudb/tools/svd2header.py irqvectors is the same function as a command). The list names the handlers; the names a derivative spells differently are unified by FAMILY_IRQ_HANDLERS in bswgen (without the Safe_ prefix, which the startup adds to every vector).
  • DefaultISR loops on a local label: b DefaultISR bound to the strong DefaultISR of OpenBSW's interrupt manager, which a Thumb-1 branch cannot reach in a full application (R_ARM_THM_JUMP11).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: platforms/common/test/test_cortex_m0plus.py: object v6S-M without FP attributes, only Thumb-1 instructions, vector table of the linked test ELF (length 48 words, reserved entries 0, port handlers under the vector names, weak IRQ handlers = DefaultISR), 33 interrupts rejected. Not run on hardware.

docs.title: Projekte
docs.text:
Ein Projekt ist eine ECU-Software auf einem Board (Architektur doc/architecture/README.md, Abschnitte 4 und 8). Beim Bauen ist das Projekt die einzige Auswahl: Board, Derivat, Familie und Kern liest CMake über tools/nxconfig aus der Konfiguration.

projects/<projekt>/
  project.yaml        Nutzung des Boards, Takte, Bitraten, Safety, Verweise auf Board (project.board) und ECU-Beschreibung (project.rte)
  rte.yaml            ECU-Beschreibung für tools/rtegen: Anwendungs-Tasks (Periode, Priorität, Stack, Runnables mit
                      Versatz und Reihenfolge), Komponenten, Verbindungen, CAN (DBC, Knoten, Bus, Task,
                      Signal-Qualifier je Botschaft)
  <Name>.dbc          CAN-Datenbank des Projekts
  swc/<Swc>/          projektspezifische Komponenten (wiederverwendbare liegen unter swc/)
  calibration/        optional: calibration dataset nextbsw-cal 1 (base/, variants/<v>/); when present, the build takes
                      the parameter values from it instead of <Swc>_data.m (TOOL-145, tools/calgen/README.md)

Path rules: every path is relative to the file it stands in. project.board and project.rte are relative to project.yaml, and the paths inside rte.yaml (components[].path, can.dbc) are relative to that rte.yaml. So a project folder can be moved, copied or kept outside the neXtBSW tree without rewriting it: a customer workspace has no repository root the paths could be based on (doc/architecture/customer-project.md, gap N3).

The ECU description carries the format it is written in:

schema_version: 2       # paths relative to this file
components:
  - { name: DemoSwc, path: ../../swc/DemoSwc }
can:
  dbc: MyEcu.dbc        # next to the rte.yaml

A file without the key is format 1, whose paths were relative to the repository root (rtegen --repo). Such a file is refused with the command that raises it; --repo is only that fallback and is ignored for format 2:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig migrate <workspace>            # shows the change
.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig migrate <workspace> --write    # writes it, after a backup

The migration edits the lines it changes and leaves comments, alignment and order as they are.

Tasks: Die Anwendungs-Tasks stehen im Projekt (rte.yaml, tasks:), die BSW-Tasks der ECU-Anwendung mit ihren Prioritätsschlüsseln in ecu/asyncCoreConfiguration/tasks.yaml. rtegen ordnet beide ein und erzeugt async/Config.h und RteTasks.h (Format, Prüfungen und Datenkonsistenz: swc/README.md, Abschnitt „Tasks“).

docs.title: Neues Projekt
docs.text:
Ein neues Projekt entsteht im Studio („Neues Projekt …“ auf der Seite Projekt oder im Menü Projekt, Strg+N) oder auf der Kommandozeile mit demselben Kern (tools/nxconfig/newproject.py, ohne Qt):

.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig new --list                                   # Boards und Projekte zum Starten
.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig new <name> --board <board> [--diag] [--dry-run]   # leer für ein Board
    [--safe-state-output <ausgang> --locked-pin <ausgang> --test-pin <pin>]         # Safety-Pins (TOOL-110)
.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig new --safety-candidates --board <board>      # was das Board dafür anbietet
.venv/Scripts/python tools/nxconfig new <name> --copy <projekt> [--dir <ordner>]      # Kopie eines Projekts

Ablauf im Studio: Ablage → Start (leer oder Kopie) → Name und Ordner → Board bzw. Vorlage → [Sicherheit] → Zusammenfassung → Anlegen → das Projekt öffnet sich. Vor „Anlegen“ wird nichts geschrieben; die Zusammenfassung nennt jede Datei und jeden abgeleiteten Wert.

  • Ablage: heute der Entwicklungsfall im neXtBSW-Repository (doc/architecture/customer-project.md, Abschnitt 6.4): Vorgabe projects/<name>, der Ordner ist frei wählbar (neu oder leer, nicht unter build/, external/, boards/, mcudb/). Das eigene Repository je ECU-Projekt mit fester neXtBSW-Version folgt mit einer eigenen Aufgabe.
  • Name: Buchstabe, dann Buchstaben, Ziffern oder _ (höchstens 48 Zeichen); C-Bezeichner und Ordnername zugleich, keine C-Schlüsselwörter, keine Windows-Gerätenamen, kein Name eines anderen Projekts in projects/.
  • Leer für ein Board (das Derivat folgt aus dem Board): project.yaml und rte.yaml, optional eine leere diag.yaml. Jeder Wert wird aus Board und Derivat abgeleitet und von nxconfig bestätigt, nie aus einem Beispielprojekt übernommen: Kerntakt (höchster Wert, den das Taktmodell mit Quarz und Bitraten erreicht), Speicheraufteilung (32 KB Bootloader ab 256 KB Code-Flash, sonst ein Achtel, mindestens 10 KB, in ganzen Sektoren), Bootloader und Diagnoseadressen (0x7E0/0x7E8) auf dem ersten CAN-Bus, die erste UART als Konsole (115200 Bd, CAN 500 kbit/s), Interrupt-Ränge. Nicht abgeleitet: der Abschnitt safety. Welcher Ausgang eine Anzeige ist und welcher Pin unbeschaltet, steht nur im Schaltplan; der Anwender wählt (Studio-Seite Sicherheit ohne Vorauswahl, Kommandozeile nur mit allen drei Optionen). Ohne Wahl steht der Abschnitt auskommentiert mit Kandidaten in project.yaml, und für eine Familie, deren Port ihn liest (S32K1), meldet nxconfig einen Fehler bei safety. rte.yaml hat schema_version: 2, einen Task mit den Vorgaben von ecu/asyncCoreConfiguration/tasks.yaml (10 ms) und components: [].
  • Kopie eines Projekts: alle Dateien des Projektordners außer Build-Ausgaben (build/, generated/, out/, __pycache__, slprj, *_ert_rtw, *.slxc, …). Neu geschrieben werden project.name, project.board, die Pfade in rte.yaml und Verweise auf den alten Ordner in Kommentaren; Layout und Kommentare bleiben. Projektspezifische Komponenten und die DBC werden mitkopiert, wiederverwendbare (swc/) bleiben referenziert. Diagnose-, CAN- und XCP-IDs sind die der Vorlage; ändern, wenn beide ECUs einen Bus teilen.

Geschrieben wird in einen Hilfsordner neben dem Ziel, der mit einem Schritt an seinen Platz kommt; bricht das Schreiben ab, bleibt nichts zurück. Danach prüft nxconfig check das Projekt; das Projekt bleibt auch mit Fehlern angelegt.

Grenzen: Boards ohne Board-Port (ecu/platforms/<board>) lassen sich prüfen und generieren, aber nicht bauen (N5). Die Familienvorlage s32k1xx liest die internen ADC-Kanäle BANDGAP und ADCINTERNAL0 und braucht safety; das prüft nxconfig noch nicht, der Assistent trägt es ein. Nachweis: der Target-Build-Test target-new-project.

docs.title: neXtBSW version and workspace pin
docs.text:
The version of this tree is the one line in VERSION (SemVer MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH); the root CMake (project(VERSION), reported by the application in DID 0xF181), nxconfig, the Studio and the release check of tools/ci (tag vX.Y.Z must equal it) read that file only. tools/nxconfig version [<project>] prints it with git describe and, for a project, the workspace pin found from there.

The projects in this folder are the development case: they have no nextbsw.yaml, so every tool uses the tree it runs from - nothing changes for them. A project in a customer repository finds the pin nextbsw.yaml by walking up from project.yaml (stopping at a neXtBSW tree or a git repository root); its search.mcudb, search.modules and search.boards are searched before the folders of the tree. Format and rules: doc/architecture/customer-project.md, section 3.1. Building such a workspace outside the tree follows with N4.

docs.title: Ein Board, mehrere Projekte
docs.text:
Ein Board-Profil beschreibt Hardware, ein Projekt ihre Nutzung (Architektur Abschnitt 4). Deshalb tragen mehrere Projekte dasselbe Board, auch wenn sie dieselbe Peripherie unterschiedlich nutzen. Beispiel am FlexTimer FTM0 (schematisch, zwei Projekte auf einem Board mit Motorbrücke und Capture-Eingang):

Projekt A (Motor) Projekt B (Laden) FTM0 PWM-Gruppe (pwm.<Gruppe>) Input Capture (use.input_capture) pwm-Abschnitt die Gruppe keiner → NX_PWM_GROUP_COUNT 0 Modulparameter eigene Werte (modules.capture) eigene Werte Komponente, Task eigene Komponente und Task eigene Komponente und Task Board-Profil identisch – keine Sonderliste, kein exclusive_groups identisch

Beides in einem Projekt (FTM0 als PWM und als Capture) lehnen nxconfig check und bswgen mit Datei, Zeile und YAML-Pfad ab: FTM0 counter is used by input_capture PILOT_DUTY and by pwm MOT1 (use.input_capture). Gleich bleiben müssen zwischen Projekten desselben Boards nur die Werte, die der geflashte Bootloader kennt: memory, bootloader.can und diagnostics (sonst ist ein Bootloader-Update nötig). Alles andere – Tasks, Komponenten, genutzte Peripherie, Modulparameter – entscheidet jedes Projekt für sich.

docs.title: Bauen
docs.text:
Einmalig je Rechner (Arbeitsplatz-Ebene, nicht eingecheckt): arm-none-eabi-gcc in den PATH legen oder die Umgebungsvariable NX_ARM_GCC_BIN auf dessen bin-Ordner setzen. Standard ist der gepinnte xPack GCC 11.3.1 (tools/ci/versions.toml), den tools/ci in den Werkzeug-Cache holt:

.venv/Scripts/python -m tools.ci setup                  # xPack GCC 11.3.1 in den Werkzeug-Cache (NX_CI_CACHE)
setx NX_ARM_GCC_BIN "%LOCALAPPDATA%/NeXtBSW/ci-cache/arm_gcc-11.3.1/xpack-arm-none-eabi-gcc-11.3.1-1.1/bin"   # danach neue Shell

Wechselt der Compiler, hält CMake den alten Pfad fest: einmal mit cmake --preset <name> --fresh neu konfigurieren (tools/test tut das selbst).

Dann mit dem Preset des Projekts:

cmake --preset buildtest-s32k148-min && cmake --build --preset buildtest-s32k148-min

Ein Projekt braucht kein Preset: Das Studio baut jedes Projekt mit dem versteckten Basis-Preset nx-arm-gcc und -DNX_PROJECT=<project.yaml> in <build-root>/<projekt>. Auf der Kommandozeile gleichwertig: ein vorhandenes Preset mit anderem Projekt, z. B. cmake --preset buildtest-s32k148-min -B build/<projekt> -DNX_PROJECT=projects/<projekt>. Ein eigenes Preset in CMakePresets.json ist nur für CI-Bauprofile nötig. Ein Build-Ordner gehört zu einem Kern und einer FPU-Variante; bei anderem Kern einen neuen Ordner verwenden.

Host-Tests, die einen echten Target-Build prüfen, erwarten keinen festen Ordner: NX_BUILD_DIR, sonst der Demo-Build von tools/test ({build}/demo), sonst das binaryDir des Demo-Presets (Regel in tools/test/build_dirs.py, tools/test/README.md, „Build directory“).

Beim Konfigurieren schreibt tools/nxconfig cmake <projekt> <build>/generated/nxconfig/project.cmake die Werte NX_BOARD, NX_DERIVATIVE, NX_FAMILY, NX_CORE, Kern-Optionen, Pfade und Debug-Einstellungen. Daraus folgen:

Wert Quelle Verwendung Board-Port ecu/platforms/<board> board.name handgeschriebene Integration bis zu einer Folgeaufgabe Plattform der Familie derivative.family platforms/<familie>/CMakeLists.txt, wenn vorhanden (bindet die OpenBSW-Module der Familie selbst ein oder bringt alles mit); sonst external/openbsw/platforms/<familie> FreeRTOS-Port, CMSIS-Pfade Architektur NX_CORE_ARCHITECTURE aus derivative.core (Kern-Tabelle unten) platforms/common/3rdparty/freertosPort; CMSIS-Include-Pfade nur für das M-Profil Kern-Optionen NX_FPU, NX_MCPU, NX_MFLOAT_ABI, NX_MFPU derivative.core, derivative.fpu (Kern-Tabelle unten) cmake/toolchains/NxArmNoneEabi-gcc.cmake, eine Datei für alle Kerne Debug-Probe und Flash-Werkzeuge NX_DEBUG_PROBE_KIND, NX_FLASH_TOOLS board.debug.probe (ohne Angabe J-Link) Ziele flash, flash-bootloader, Abschnitt Flash-Ziele je Debug-Probe J-Link-Gerät derivative.jlink_device, sonst derivative.name dito (Probe J-Link) pyOCD-Zieltyp, OpenOCD-Zielskript derivative.pyocd_target (sonst Name klein), derivative.openocd_target (ohne Vorgabe) dito (pyOCD, OpenOCD) Debug-Schnittstelle board.debug.interface (JTAG, SWD, cJTAG) dito, ohne board.debug Ziele mit Fehlermeldung Debug-Takt board.debug.speed_khz, ohne Angabe 1000 kHz dito Configure-Abhängigkeiten NX_CONFIG_FILES Projekt, Board, Derivat, rte.yaml, Pin-Mux-Tabelle des Gehäuses, Derivat des Device-Headers neu konfigurieren bei Änderung

Kern-Tabelle (tools/nxconfig/config.py, CORES). derivative.fpu darf fehlen, wenn der Kern nur eine Variante hat; unbekannte Kerne und unpassende Varianten meldet nxconfig check mit YAML-Pfad.

derivative.core derivative.fpu -mcpu -mfloat-abi -mfpu Architektur FreeRTOS-Port cortex-m0plus none cortex-m0plus soft – armv6m platforms/s32k1xx/3rdparty/freertos_cm0_sysTick cortex-m4f sp cortex-m4 hard fpv4-sp-d16 armv7m OpenBSW CM4F (Ziele der Familienplattform) cortex-m7f sp oder dp (Pflicht) cortex-m7 hard fpv5-sp-d16 bzw. fpv5-d16 armv7m OpenBSW CM4F (ungeprüft) cortex-m33 sp oder none (Pflicht) cortex-m33 hard bzw. soft fpv5-sp-d16 bzw. – armv8m fehlt (Abbruch mit Meldung) cortex-r4f dp cortex-r4f hard vfpv3-d16 armv7r fehlt (Abbruch mit Meldung; geplant ARM_CRx_No_GIC aus FreeRTOS V11.3.1 mit Kern V10.6.2)

Die FreeRTOS-Portauswahl richtet sich nach der Architektur, nicht nach dem Kernnamen; fehlt der Port, bricht das Konfigurieren mit „port missing“ ab. Startup, Fault-Handler und Familienvorlage gibt es für cortex-m0plus (S32K116) und cortex-m4f (S32K14x, STM32F446); für die übrigen Kerne gelingt nur das Konfigurieren der Toolchain.

docs.title: Flash-Ziele je Debug-Probe
docs.text:
Die Ziele flash (Anwendung und Gültigkeitsdatensatz) und flash-bootloader gibt es für jedes Projekt. Das Board nennt seine Probe (board.debug.probe), tools/nxconfig (config.PROBES) leitet daraus die möglichen Implementierungen in Vorzugsreihenfolge ab; welches Werkzeug installiert ist und wo, entscheidet der Arbeitsplatz.

board.debug.probe (Schreibweise frei, Anfang zählt) Art Werkzeuge in Vorzugsreihenfolge Schnittstellen J-Link, J-Link EDU Mini, ohne Angabe jlink jlink (J-Link Commander) JTAG, SWD, cJTAG ST-LINK, ST-LINK/V2-1, STLINK-V3 stlink stm32cubeprogrammer (STM32_Programmer_CLI), openocd SWD, JTAG OpenSDA, CMSIS-DAP, DAPLink cmsis-dap pyocd, openocd SWD, JTAG XDS110 xds110 dslite (UniFlash-Kommandozeile; Debuggen später über OpenOCD) JTAG, cJTAG, SWD

Eine unbekannte Probe oder eine nicht bediente Schnittstelle meldet nxconfig als Warnung. OpenSDA geht nur mit CMSIS-DAP-/DAPLink-Firmware (die PEmicro-Firmware neuer Boards spricht weder pyOCD noch OpenOCD).

Arbeitsplatz-Ebene (nicht eingecheckt), je Werkzeug eine der drei Möglichkeiten: Cache-Variable mit dem Programmpfad, Umgebungsvariable mit dessen Ordner, oder PATH.

Werkzeug Cache-Variable Umgebungsvariable (Ordner) Zusätzlich nötig jlink JLINK_EXE NX_JLINK_BIN (sonst auch C:/Program Files/SEGGER/JLink) – stm32cubeprogrammer NX_STM32_PROGRAMMER_CLI NX_STM32_PROGRAMMER_BIN – openocd NX_OPENOCD_EXE NX_OPENOCD_BIN derivative.openocd_target im Derivat pyocd NX_PYOCD_EXE NX_PYOCD_BIN Zieltyp in pyOCD bekannt (ggf. pyocd pack install <ziel>) dslite NX_DSLITE_EXE NX_UNIFLASH_DIR NX_DSLITE_CCXML: UniFlash-Zielkonfiguration (XDS110 und Baustein)

NX_FLASH_TOOL (Cache) erzwingt eine Implementierung der Probe (z. B. -DNX_FLASH_TOOL=openocd bei einem ST-LINK), NX_DEBUG_PROBE_SERIAL wählt bei mehreren Probes eine aus. Das Konfigurieren nennt das gewählte Werkzeug; fehlt es, entsteht das Ziel trotzdem und bricht beim Aufruf mit der Begründung ab.

Jede Implementierung lässt die MCU am Ende laufen (Befehlsdatei neben den Abbildern, <build>/<modul>/<Konfiguration>/<ziel>.<endung>):

Werkzeug Befehl jlink JLink [-USB <sn>] -ExitOnError 1 -CommandFile flash.jlink openocd openocd -f flash.openocd.cfg (Adapter, Zielskript, je Abbild flash write_image erase und verify_image, reset run) stm32cubeprogrammer STM32_Programmer_CLI -c port=SWD freq=<kHz> [sn=<sn>] -w <abbild> -v ... -rst pyocd pyocd flash -t <ziel> -f <Hz> -O dap_protocol=swd [-u <sn>] <abbilder> dslite dslite --mode flash --config=<ccxml> --flash --verify <abbilder>

Geprüft ist das gegen die erzeugten Befehle (tools/nxconfig/test_flash_targets.py, keine Werkzeuge ausgeführt). Am Board bestätigt sind der J-Link-Weg und der ST-LINK-Weg am Nucleo F446RE; die übrigen Befehlszeilen sind beim ersten Einsatz zu prüfen.

docs.title: Takte und Timings
docs.text:
Jeder Wert steht in genau einer Ebene, alles Abgeleitete berechnet das Taktmodell (tools/nxconfig/clock.py mit den familienneutralen Rechenkernen timing.py); nxconfig check meldet Fehler mit YAML-Pfad, bswgen erzeugt daraus bsp/clock/boardClock.h, bsp/can/canBitTimingConfiguration.h und bsp/uart/uartConfiguration.h.

Ebene Eintrag Beispiel Derivat (mcudb) clock: interne Oszillatoren, Oszillatorbereich, PLL-Grenzen (Referenz, VCO, Teiler, Multiplikator, Ausgangsteiler), Höchstwerte je Taktbereich S32K144: FIRC 48 MHz, VCO 180–320 MHz, Kern 80 / Bus 48 / Flash 26,67 MHz Board board.clock.sosc_hz: bestückter Quarz (fehlt: kein Quarz) 40 MHz Projekt clock.system_hz (Kerntakt); can.<Bus>: bitrate, sample_point_percent (Vorgabe 87,5), optional sjw_tq, prop_seg_tq; uart.<UART>: baudrate – Pflicht für jeden genutzten Bus 80 MHz; CAN0 500 kbit/s, 81,25 %; UART 115200 Bd

Familie s32k1xx: Systemtaktquelle FIRC, SOSC oder SIRC mit DIVCORE, sonst SPLL; FlexCAN am SOSCDIV2 (braucht Quarz), FTM am Kerntakt, LPUART/LPSPI am FIRCDIV2. CAN: exakte Bitrate, nächster Abtastpunkt (Warnung ab 1, Fehler ab 2,5 Prozentpunkten Abweichung). UART: kleinster Baudratenfehler (Warnung über 1 %, Fehler über 2 %). Ohne Taktmodell (andere Familien) prüft nxconfig nur Oszillatorbereich, Kerntakt-Höchstwert und Pflichtangaben.

docs.title: Kommunikationskanäle: CAN-Busse der Anwendung
docs.text:
Die Anwendung bedient jeden CAN-Bus des Boards, den das Projekt nutzt (use.can, höchstens 8). Je Bus entstehen Bus-ID (busid::<Bus>), Transceiver-Objekt mit der Rolle can_phy, Bit-Timing, Interrupt-Anbindung und ein Eintrag der Konsolengruppe can. Der Busname kommt aus board.yaml (can[].name, frei wählbar außer SELFDIAG, ETH_0, ETH_1). Jeder genutzte Bus braucht einen Interrupt-Rang (interrupts.ranks), sonst lehnt nxconfig check das Projekt ab: project.yaml:99 (interrupts.ranks): error: CAN bus CAN0 is used, but has no interrupt rank ... (gilt für Derivate mit Interrupt-Rängen).

Ebene Eintrag Beispiel Board can[]: name, instance, rx/tx, phy (Baustein mit Rolle can_phy) CAN0: { instance: FlexCAN0, rx: PTC2, tx: PTC3, phy: SBC } Projekt use.can: Busse der Anwendung; can.<Bus>: Bitrate und Abtastpunkt (auch für Busse, die nur der Bootloader nutzt) use: { can: [CAN0] } Projekt interrupts.ranks: ein Interrupt-Rang je genutztem Bus - { source: can, name: CAN0, rank: 3 } Projekt (rte.yaml) can.bus: Bus der DBC-Signale (Vorgabe: erster Bus); uds.bus: Bus des Diagnose-Stacks (Vorgabe: can.bus) can: { bus: CAN0 }, uds: { bus: CAN0 } Projekt (rte.yaml) can.qualifiers.<Botschaft>: Überwachung je Botschaft (timeout_ms, debounce_ms, on_error, e2e), Qualifier-Ziel can.qlf.<Botschaft> (doc/architecture/signal-qualifier.md) qualifiers: { PC_Command: { debounce_ms: 200, e2e: { profile: P01, data_id: 0x0210, crc: PcCrc, counter: PcCounter } } }

Generat: busid/busIdConfiguration.h (SELFDIAG 1, CAN-Busse ab 2, danach Ethernet) und bsp/can/canDeviceConfiguration.h (NX_CAN_BUSES(X), je Bus <Bus>_DEVICE_CONFIG), dazu NX_CAN_PHY_BUSES_<MODUL> in integration/moduleConfiguration.h. Konsole: can status [bus], can send [bus] <id> [byte …], can log 0|1 [bus]. Grenzen: Hat ein Bus im Vektor des Board-Ports keinen Vektor, bleiben seine Interrupts aus (Fehlermeldung beim Start); die Nachrichtenpuffer-Aufteilung (14/2/15) setzt 32 Message-Buffer je Instanz voraus.

docs.title: PWM-Gruppen (komplementäre Endstufen-PWM)
docs.text:
Eine PWM-Gruppe ist ein FlexTimer mit komplementären Kanalpaaren (Hoch-/Tiefseite mit Totzeit) für eine Endstufe. Eine PWM-Gruppe ist optional: Ein Board ohne Motorbrücke beschreibt keine, ein Projekt nutzt keine, und Anwendung und Bootloader bauen und linken trotzdem (Nachweis: Bau-Profil buildtest_s32k148_min).

Ebene Eintrag Beispiel Board pwm[]: name, instance (FTM), mode: complementary, active (Pegel je Seite), pairs (Name, high_side, low_side), channels (Name, FTM-Kanal 2k/2k+1, Pin) MOT1 auf FTM0, drei Paare MOT1_U/V/W Projekt pwm.<Gruppe>: frequency_hz, deadtime_ns, optional verify – nur die Gruppen, die das Projekt nutzt (nicht über use:) MOT1: { frequency_hz: 20000, deadtime_ns: 1000 }

Abgeleitet (Taktmodell und tools/bswgen): FTM-Zählertakt, Vorteiler SC.PS, MOD, DEADTIME, COMBINE/COMP/DTEN je Paar, POL aus den aktiven Pegeln, Pin-Funktion je Kanal. nxconfig check meldet mit YAML-Pfad: Paarungsregel 2k/2k+1, Kanal oder Pin doppelt, Pin ohne FTM-Funktion, FTM-Zähler zugleich von input_capture genutzt, Frequenz zu hoch (unter 100 Ticks je Periode) oder zu tief (Vorteiler 128), Totzeit über dem FTM-Maximum (63 x 16 Takte) oder nicht kürzer als eine halbe Periode (pwm.<Gruppe>.frequency_hz, pwm.<Gruppe>.deadtime_ns). Die Mindesttotzeit der Endstufe (power_stage) ist eine eigene Prüfung: sie sagt, wie lang die Totzeit sein muss, diese hier, ob der Zähler sie darstellen kann.

Generat bsp/io/outputPwm/ (outputPwmConfiguration.h, outputPwmConfigurationStrings.h, ftmPwmConfiguration.h); der letzte Header ist immer einbindbar und nennt die Gruppen:

#define NX_PWM_GROUP_COUNT 1
#define NX_PWM_GROUP_INSTANCES(X) X(MOT1)      /* ohne Gruppe: 0 und eine leere Liste */

Ohne Gruppe entsteht kein ComplementaryPwm und keine FTM-Registerwerte; die Konsole pwm bleibt in jedem Projekt. Grenze: Der Treiber bedient eine Gruppe je Projekt; bei zwei Gruppen bricht bswgen mit einer Meldung ab.

docs.title: Speicheraufteilung und Bootloader
docs.text:
Eine Quelle für Bootloader-Linker, Updater-Linker, App-Linker, bl_config.h und canflash (Architektur Abschnitt 7). Rechnung und Prüfung in tools/nxconfig/memory.py, Generat von tools/bswgen/blgen.py.

Ebene Eintrag Beispiel Derivat (mcudb) memory[]: Regionen mit start, size; Flash mit sector_size (oder Sektor-Tabelle sectors: [{size, count}]) und program_size (kleinste programmierbare Einheit) PFLASH 512 KB, Sektor 4 KB, Phrase 8 Byte; SRAM_L, SRAM_U Projekt memory.flash (Code-Flash-Region), memory.bootloader: size (ganze Sektoren ab Flash-Anfang), ram, optional ram_size, stack_size; memory.application: ram (zusammenhängende Regionen in Adressreihenfolge), noinit_size size: 0x8000, ram: SRAM_L; ram: [SRAM_L, SRAM_U], noinit_size: 0x400 Projekt bootloader.can (Board-CAN-Bus, Bit-Timing aus can.<Bus>), optional bootloader.init (Bausteine, die der Bootloader vor dem CAN-Start einschaltet) can: CAN0

Abgeleitet (Konvention der Bootloader-Schnittstelle, hält einen geflashten Bootloader kompatibel): Anwendung ab Bootloader-Ende bis zum letzten Sektor, Gültigkeitsrecord im letzten Sektor, No-Init-Bereich am Ende der letzten App-RAM-Region, Boot-Request 0x10 Byte unter dem RAM-Ende, Plausibilitätsbereich des Stack-Pointers = App-RAM. nxconfig check meldet mit YAML-Pfad unbekannte Regionen, Bootloader-Ende innerhalb eines Sektors, keinen Platz für die Anwendung, fehlendes program_size, ungleiche Sektoren, zu großes oder überlappendes Bootloader-RAM, nicht zusammenhängendes App-RAM, unbekannten Bootloader-Bus, fehlende Bitrate und fehlende Hooks.

Generat unter <build>/generated/board/: bootloader/bl_memory.h (auch BL_TARGET_ID), bootloader/bl_memory.ld, memory/memoryLayout.h und bootloader/bl_diag.h; beim Konfigurieren des Bootloaders zusätzlich bl_board.h und bl_board.cmake (Familie s32k1xx: Reset-Takt, CAN-Instanz, Pins, CTRL1, Baustein-Hooks bootloader/devices/<modul>). Anderer Bus für einen Build: cmake --preset <p> -DBOOTLOADER_CAN_BUS=CAN1.

canflash findet die Speicheraufteilung und die Diagnose-Adressen im Build-Ordner der Hex-Datei, sonst über --layout <build>/generated/board/bootloader/bl_memory.h oder --project projects/<projekt>/project.yaml (auch NX_PROJECT/NX_BL_LAYOUT); das gilt auch für canflash info.

docs.title: Diagnose-Adressen (UDS, ISO-TP, Bootloader-Kennung)
docs.text:
CAN-IDs und UDS-Adressen sind Projektsache (Architektur Abschnitt 4). Bootloader (bootloader/src/core), App-UDS-Stack (ecu/uds) und canflash lesen dieselben generierten Werte, damit ein Tester beide bedient . Prüfung in tools/nxconfig/diag.py, Generat von tools/bswgen/blgen.py.

Ebene Eintrag Beispiel Projekt diagnostics.request_id, response_id (Pflicht), functional_id (Vorgabe 0x7DF) 0x7E0, 0x7E8, 0x7DF Projekt diagnostics.tester_address, ecu_address (1-Byte-Transportadressen) 0xF1, 0x2A Projekt diagnostics.isotp: padding, block_size, stmin_ms, n_cr_ms, n_bs_ms 0xCC, 0, 0, 1000, 1000 Projekt diagnostics.bootloader.version_prefix (Kennung in BL_VERSION_STRING, Vorgabe nextbsw-bl; die Versionsnummer steht in bl_config.h). Zusätzlich angenommen wird die frühere Kennung BL_VERSION_PREFIX_FORMER (S32K14x-BL, bl_config.h) - von Anwendung (DID 0xF180), Updater und canflash. Verglichen wird byteweise, also mit Groß-/Kleinschreibung: NEXTBSW-BL oder s32k14x-bl gelten als fremde Kennung nextbsw-bl → nextbsw-bl 0.1.0 Projekt diagnostics.bootloader.scan_start (optional): erste Adresse, die die Anwendung nach der Kennung durchsucht entfällt Projekt diagnostics.bootloader.security (optional): method (heute nur hmac-sha256), key (Name des Hauptschlüssels am Arbeitsplatz, Vorgabe: Boardname), allow_insecure_test_key (nur Testprofile) entfällt → hmac-sha256, Schlüssel = Boardname Derivat (mcudb) uid: Adresse und Länge der Chip-UID (Geräteschlüssel und DID 0xF18C) S32K1xx 0x40048054, 16 Byte Familie Flash am Anfang der Region, der nicht durchsucht wird (diag.FAMILY_SCAN_OFFSET): s32k1xx 0x410 (Vektortabelle + Flash Configuration Field) 0x410 ECU-Beschreibung (rte.yaml) uds.bus: CAN-Bus des App-Stacks; der Bootloader hört auf bootloader.can CAN0

nxconfig check meldet mit Datei, Zeile und YAML-Pfad: IDs außerhalb des 11-Bit-Bereichs, gleiche IDs, Kollision mit einer Botschaft der DBC auf demselben Bus, Suchbereich außerhalb des Bootloader-Flash, STmin über 127 ms, N_Cr/N_Bs kürzer als STmin; als Warnung: eine ID auf dem Statusrahmen des Updaters (0x7EE), sehr langsames STmin, Bootloader und Anwendung auf verschiedenen Bussen.

Generat <build>/generated/board/bootloader/bl_diag.h: BL_CAN_ID_REQUEST_PHYS/_FUNC/_RESPONSE, BL_ISOTP_PADDING/_BLOCK_SIZE/_STMIN_MS/_N_CR_MS/_N_BS_MS, BL_VERSION_PREFIX, NX_DIAG_TESTER_ADDRESS/_ECU_ADDRESS, NX_DIAG_BL_SCAN_START/_END. Nicht konfigurierbar sind die Data- und Routine-Identifier der UDS-Dienste: Protokollkonstanten, auf die sich Bootloader, Anwendung (ecu/uds/.../AppDataIdentifiers.h) und canflash einigen.

Bootloader security access and identification. blgen writes bootloader/bl_security.h (method, chip UID address and length, name of the master key - never key material) and the key sector BL_KEY_ADDR/BL_KEY_AREA_SIZE into bl_memory.h (the sector below the validity record). The master key is a workstation value (%LOCALAPPDATA%/neXtBSW/keys/<name>.key, or NX_BL_KEY/NX_BL_KEY_FILE for CI); canflash keygen <name> creates one, tools/canflash/provision.py writes the device key of one chip. A project that names the insecure test key without allow_insecure_test_key: true fails in nxconfig check. bl_memory.h also carries BL_HARDWARE_ID and BL_FAMILY; a build directory generated before must be configured again.

docs.title: Module: Bausteine, Anschlüsse, Parameter
docs.text:
Wiederverwendbare Treiber beschreiben sich in libs/bsw/<modul>/module.yaml (Architektur Abschnitt 5). Welche Werte wo stehen:

Ebene Eintrag Beispiel Modul (module.yaml) bediente Teile parts, Anschlüsse connect mit Art (digital_output, digital_input, analog_input), Parameterschema parameters (Typ int/bool/str, min/max Pflicht bei int, pattern, default, unit), Regeln constraints (fault_ma > overcurrent_ma) highSideSwitch Board (board.yaml) devices[].module (optional, sonst über parts) und devices[].connect: Anschluss → Board-Eintrag KL30B_SW: { module: highSideSwitch, connect: { in: EN_SW_KL30B, den: DIAG_EN_SW_KL30B, is: CURRENTSENSE_KL30B } } Projekt (project.yaml) modules.<Baustein>: Parameterwerte, verify: true für unbestätigte Werte modules: { KL30B_SW: { overcurrent_ma: 3633, …, console: kl30b, verify: true } }

Instanziert wird ein Baustein mit Bus (spi[].device, can[].phy), wenn das Projekt einen seiner Busse nutzt; ein Baustein nur mit connect, wenn modules.<Baustein> im Projekt steht. nxconfig check meldet mit Datei, Zeile und YAML-Pfad: unbekanntes oder mehrdeutiges Modul, Teil nicht vom Modul bedient, fehlende/unbekannte Anschlüsse, Anschluss an einen Eintrag falscher Art oder doppelt belegt, unbekannte, fehlende oder falsch getypte Parameter, Bereich, Muster, verletzte constraints, doppelte Konsolennamen, Manifestfehler. Nutzt das Projekt ein angeschlossenes Signal nicht (use:), gibt es eine Warnung und die Instanz entfällt.

Module ohne Baustein (Dienste wie ecuState, bspAdcAccess, safeSystem) setzen project_parameters: true im Manifest; ihre Werte stehen einmal je Projekt unter modules.<modul>, fehlende kommen aus den Standardwerten. Ein str-Parameter mit names: ist eine Namensliste (all, none oder kommagetrennt, kein Name doppelt); bei names: can_bus muss jeder Name ein CAN-Bus aus use.can sein, bei names: any genügt das Muster.

docs.title: ECU-Zustandsverwaltung (modules.ecuState)
docs.text:
Zeiten, Richtlinien und Aufweckquellen der Zustandsverwaltung sind Projektwerte unter modules.ecuState; ohne Eintrag gelten die Standardwerte. Parameter, Standardwerte und Bereiche: ecuState.md, Parameter, alle Felder: Referenz doc/reference/project.md. nxconfig check meldet mit YAML-Pfad, z. B. project.yaml:170 (modules.ecuState.wakeup_can): error: wakeup_can: CAN7 is no CAN bus of the project (use.can: CAN0). Ein Abschnitt ecu_state: in der rte.yaml ist ein Fehler von rtegen. Aus den geprüften Werten entsteht generated/rte/EcuStateConfig.h; die Versorgung wählt die Integration aus den Bausteinen (sbcUja113x: dessen Uja113xPowerSupply, sonst PermanentPowerSupply). Die RTE-Ziele ecu.* beschreibt swc/README.md.

bswgen erzeugt daraus generated/board/integration/: moduleConfiguration.h (Instanzen je Modul, CAN-Rollen), <modul>Configuration.h je Modul mit Anschlüssen oder Parametern (NX_MODULE_<MODUL>_INSTANCES(X), NX_DEVICE_<BAUSTEIN>_IO_<ANSCHLUSS>, _PARAM_<PARAMETER>, _PART, _LABEL) und modules.cmake. Die Integration im Board-Port setzt die Instanzen per X-Makro zusammen; Werte stehen dort keine.

docs.title: Software-Komponenten (Simulink, AUTOSAR Classic)
docs.text:
Anwendungslogik entsteht als Simulink-Modell, das als AUTOSAR-Classic-Softwarekomponente (SWC) mit dem AUTOSAR Blockset konfiguriert ist. Embedded Coder erzeugt C-Code und ARXML. Eine eigene, schlanke RTE (tools/rtegen) verbindet die Ports mit der Basis-Software (OpenBSW) und ruft die Runnables zyklisch auf.

A component can also be written in C by hand, with the same RTE API and without MATLAB: see Hand-written C components.

swc/<Swc>/<Swc>.slx ──(tools/swc/swc_build.m, MATLAB)──► swc/<Swc>/generated/{src,arxml}   (eingecheckt)
                                                                  │
projects/<p>/project.yaml → rte.yaml ─(tools/rtegen, CMake)───────┴─► build/<preset>/generated/rte
ecu/asyncCoreConfiguration/tasks.yaml ─┘                                 Rte_Type.h, Rte_<Swc>.h, Rte.c,
                                                                         RteConfig.h/.cpp, RteTasks.h,
                                                                         tasks/async/Config.h
ecu/application: RteSystem ── init runnables + rte::init(), dann je Anwendungs-Task in seinem Kontext alle period_ms:
                              readInputs(task) → fällige Runnables des Tasks in Reihenfolge → writeOutputs(task)

docs.title: Voraussetzungen
docs.text:
• MATLAB R2024a mit Simulink, Embedded Coder und AUTOSAR Blockset (nur zum Ändern eines Modells).
  • Für den Firmware-Build ist MATLAB nicht nötig: Der erzeugte Code liegt im Repo.
  • The published (open source) tree does not contain the code Simulink Coder generated (MATLAB student licence, decision F9 A): there swc/DemoSwc is built from the hand-written C substitute swc/DemoSwcSubstitute with the same RTE interface; with your own MATLAB licence you generate the original from the model.

docs.title: Modellregeln
docs.text:
Thema Regel Modelltyp Export-Function-Modell, System Target File autosar.tlc Runnables je eine Function-Call-Inport pro Runnable, die Abtastzeit ist die Periode (ganze ms, Vielfaches der RTE-Basisperiode). Der Init-Runnable <Swc>_Init entsteht automatisch. Ports Root-Inports = Required Ports, Root-Outports = Provided Ports, Sender-Receiver, Zugriff ExplicitReceive/ExplicitSend Datentypen AUTOSAR-Plattformtypen (boolean, uint8/16/32, sint8/16/32, float32/64); arrays, records (buses), enumerations and fixed point between components, see "Data types" Hardware keine Hardware-Blöcke (MBDT o. Ä.) im Modell: Ein-/Ausgänge nur über Ports Zielhardware ARM Compatible->ARM Cortex-M

| Kalibrierparameter | Elemente des ParameterReceiver-Ports CalPrm (Abschnitt „Kalibrierparameter“), Werte nur in <Swc>_data.m |

Nicht unterstützt (noch): Client-Server-Ports, Mode-Management, mehrere Instanzen.

docs.title: Arbeitsablauf
docs.text:
1. Neue Komponente: swc/template/swc.yaml nach swc/<Swc>/swc.yaml kopieren, Name, Runnables und Ports eintragen, python tools/swc/swc_yaml.py check swc/<Swc>, dann matlab -batch "addpath tools/swc; swc_create('swc/<Swc>')". Das legt <Swc>.slx mit Subsystemen je Runnable, Ports und AUTOSAR-Zuordnung an; danach ist die .slx die Quelle. Bausteine: Library Browser „neXtBSW Components“ (swc/template/NxSwcLib.slx), z. B. SensorQualifier.
  2. Ports einer bestehenden Komponente ändern: Die .slx wird nie neu erzeugt. Geänderte Ports der swc.yaml schreibt swc_ports gezielt ins bestehende Modell – hinzufügen, umbenennen, entfernen, Datentyp –, jeder andere Block und jede andere Linie bleibt, wo sie ist: 
    swc_ports('swc/<Swc>', 'report', 'ports.json')   % nur lesen: Ports und was im Modell daran hängt
swc_ports('swc/<Swc>', 'apply',  'plan.json')    % schreiben; der Plan muss eine vorhandene Kopie der .slx nennen
    Aus dem Studio mit Vorschau und Sicherung: studio component ports projects/<projekt> <Swc> [--detach] --apply (tools/studio/README.md). Ein Port, an dem Logik hängt, wird abgelehnt, solange das Abtrennen nicht ausdrücklich erlaubt ist – und auch dann wird kein Block gelöscht: an die Stelle des Ports tritt <Port>_Removed (Constant bzw. Terminator). Runnables ändert man weiterhin in Simulink.
  3. Code erzeugen (nach jeder Modelländerung): 
    cd <repo>; addpath tools/swc
swc_build('swc/DemoSwc')
    Schreibt generated/src, generated/arxml und generated/model.sha256 (Hash der .slx). Datumszeilen werden aus dem erzeugten Code entfernt, damit Git nur echte Änderungen zeigt. Passt die .slx nicht mehr zum Hash, warnt der CMake-Konfigurierlauf, dass der eingecheckte Code veraltet ist.
  4. Verbinden in der ECU-Beschreibung des Projekts (projects/<projekt>/rte.yaml, in project.yaml unter project.rte). Paths inside it (path, can.dbc) are relative to that rte.yaml (schema_version: 2), not to the repository root: a reusable component like DemoSwc is reached with ../../swc/<Swc>, a project-specific one with swc/<Swc>, and the project's DBC lies next to the file. That way a project keeps working when it is moved, copied or kept outside the neXtBSW tree. An older description without the key is format 1, whose paths were relative to the repository root (rtegen --repo); nxconfig migrate raises it (projects/README.md). 
    schema_version: 2
components:
  - name: DemoSwc
    path: ../../swc/DemoSwc
connections:
  DemoSwc.Button1.Button1: dio.in.BUTTON1          # Required Port <- digitaler Eingang
  DemoSwc.MotorNtc_mV.MotorNtc_mV: adc.mv.MOTOR_NTC  # Required Port <- ADC in mV
  DemoSwc.Led1.Led1: dio.out.LED1                  # Provided Port -> digitaler Ausgang
  DemoSwc.PcCommandQlf.PcCommandQlf: can.qlf.PC_Command  # Qualifier einer Empfangsbotschaft (uint8)
  DemoSwc.MotorNtcFiltered_mV.MotorNtcFiltered_mV: rte   # bleibt in der RTE
  # OtherSwc.In.Value: DemoSwc.Out.Value           # Komponente zu Komponente
    rtegen prüft: jeder Required Port verbunden, Richtung und Datentyp passen zum Ziel, Signal existiert im Board-Profil und wird vom Projekt genutzt (use:/pwm: in project.yaml), Perioden und Versätze passen zum Task (Abschnitt „Tasks“).
  5. Firmware bauen wie gewohnt (cmake --build --preset buildtest-s32k148-min, projects/README.md), flashen per CAN oder J-Link.
  6. Am Target prüfen: Konsole rte signals (alle Puffer mit Verbindung) und rte runnables (je Task Kontext, Periode, Zyklen, Überläufe, längster Zyklus; je Runnable Periode, Versatz, Aufrufe, Laufzeit), stats cpu und stats stack für die Tasks.

docs.title: Hand-written C components
docs.text:
A component can also be written in C by hand instead of being modelled in Simulink. It is described, connected, scheduled and calibrated exactly like a Simulink component; only the source of the code differs, and no MATLAB is involved at any step.

swc/<Swc>/swc.yaml (implementation: c) ──(tools/swc/swc_skeleton.py create, once)──► swc/<Swc>/src/<Swc>.c  (yours)
        │                                                                                    │
        └──(tools/rtegen reads swc.yaml instead of ARXML)──► Rte_<Swc>.h, Rte.c, RteConfig.cpp ─┴─► ecu/application
Simulink component C component swc.yaml optional; after swc_create only the description the model came from required and the master: implementation: c What rtegen reads generated/arxml/*.arxml swc.yaml (runnables, ports, parameters) Code generated/src (Embedded Coder, swc_build) src/*.c (hand-written) Runnable functions <Runnable> (Embedded Coder), <Swc>_Init <Swc>_<Runnable>, <Swc>_Init Port and parameter API Rte_Read_<Port>_<Port>, Rte_Write_<Port>_<Port>, Rte_Prm_CalPrm_<Name> from Rte_<Swc>.h the same Calibration values <Swc>_data.m the same (read by tools/swc/mdata.py, no MATLAB) Build rules ecu/rte (swcComponents, warnings of the generated code not fatal), outside the MISRA scope ecu/application like the application code: -Wall -Wextra, warnings are errors, in the MISRA scope of tools/misra model.sha256 hint yes no (there is no model)

Workflow

  1. Copy swc/template/swc.yaml to swc/<Swc>/swc.yaml (or projects/<project>/swc/<Swc>/), set the name, runnables, ports, parameters and implementation: c; check with python tools/swc/swc_yaml.py check swc/<Swc>.
  2. Create the code skeleton once: python tools/swc/swc_skeleton.py create swc/<Swc>. It writes src/<Swc>.c with <Swc>_Init and one function per runnable, each with commented example accesses; it never overwrites a C source, the file is yours from then on.
  3. Write the logic. Keep the state static; runnables that share state belong in one task (the RTE protects port buffers, not the component's own variables).
  4. Connect and schedule it in rte.yaml like any component, path relative to that file.
  5. After changing runnables: python tools/swc/swc_skeleton.py check swc/<Swc> lists missing, static or duplicate runnable functions and orphans (warnings, exit code 0, --strict: 1); rtegen and the Studio show the same findings.
# swc/LevelMon/swc.yaml
name: LevelMon
implementation: c
runnables:
  - { name: Run10ms, period_ms: 10 }
ports:
  - { name: Level_mV, direction: in, type: uint32, runnables: [Run10ms] }
  - { name: Above, direction: out, type: boolean, runnables: [Run10ms] }
parameters:
  - { name: OnLevel_mV, type: uint32, runnables: [Run10ms] }      # value in LevelMon_data.m

/* swc/LevelMon/src/LevelMon.c */
#include "Rte_LevelMon.h"

static boolean above;

void LevelMon_Init(void) { above = FALSE; }

void LevelMon_Run10ms(void)
{
    uint32 level_mV = 0U;
    (void)Rte_Read_Level_mV_Level_mV(&level_mV);
    above = (level_mV >= Rte_Prm_CalPrm_OnLevel_mV()) ? TRUE : FALSE;
    (void)Rte_Write_Above_Above(above);
}

rtegen builds the same component model as from the ARXML, so the same checks apply:

  • Ports: sender-receiver, port = interface = data element name, platform types, explicit access by exactly the runnables listed at the port (the task plan uses that list), init value 0.
  • Calibration parameters are supported (scalar, row vector dim, fixed point lsb/offset); values come from <Swc>_data.m without MATLAB.
  • Messages: errors carry the swc.yaml file, YAML path and line; the name in rte.yaml must be the name in swc.yaml; two runnables with the same C function are an error. Array ports are supported, see below.
  • Not (yet) available: records, enumerations and fixed point at ports (types: is refused), implicit access, mode ports, init values other than 0; such a component is built in Simulink.

Example and proof: test profile tools/rtegen/test/c_swc (C component LevelMonSwc next to the Simulink component DemoSwc), tests rtegen-c-swc, swc-skeleton, rtegen-reference and the firmware build target-c-swc.

docs.title: Data types
docs.text:
Besides the platform types, sender-receiver ports carry the composite and scaled types of Embedded Coder R2024a. Test model: tools/rtegen/test/types/TypeSwc (TypeSwc_create.m builds the model, swc_build generates it).

Type in the model ARXML In the RTE vector uint16, dimension 4 IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE ARRAY (rt_Array_uint16_4) typedef uint16 rt_Array_uint16_4[4];, Rte_Read(uint16* data), Rte_Write(const uint16* data), copied with memcpy bus (Simulink.Bus), also nested and with vector elements STRUCTURE + APPLICATION-RECORD-DATA-TYPE typedef struct { ... } Name;, Rte_Read(Name* data), Rte_Write(const Name* data) enumeration (Simulink.IntEnumType or uint8 based) VALUE + TEXTTABLE compu method typedef uint8 Name; and one macro per literal (#define TypeSwc_Mode_Fault ((TypeSwc_Mode)3U)) fixed point fixdt(...) VALUE + LINEAR compu method of the application type typedef uint16 UFIX16_SP1_BN40;, stored values; the scaling is checked, not converted

Model rules, because the RTE defines these types (Rte_Type.h):

Type Rule Bus DataScope = 'Imported', HeaderFile = 'Rte_Type.h', root ports with BusOutputAsStruct on Enumeration getDataScope returns 'Imported', getHeaderFile returns 'Rte_Type.h', addClassNameToEnumNames returns true; a uint8 enumeration in a MATLAB Function block needs SimGenImportedTypeDefs on (simulation only) Fixed point in a bus a named Simulink.NumericType (a bare fixdt(...) bus element loses its scaling in the ARXML of R2024a); at a root port a bare fixdt is fine

Units of Simulink.BusElement.Unit and port Unit do not reach the ARXML of R2024a.

What rtegen checks (message with YAML path, also in rtegen --validate and the Studio): - A connection between two components needs the same layout, element types, scaling and literals; records also the same type name. - One type name has one definition over all components, one literal name one value. - Records, arrays and fixed point connect only to component ports, rte and rte.init; BSW and CAN targets carry unscaled scalars. Enumerations are integers and may use BSW targets of their platform type (e.g. ecu.state). - Init values from the ARXML (numerical, literal, array, record, constant reference); physical values become stored values, rounded to the nearest step and checked against the type. - Refused: variable-size arrays, unions, anonymous nested records, compu methods other than IDENTICAL, LINEAR and TEXTTABLE, records as calibration parameters.

The console (rte signals) lists records and arrays element by element, enumerations as integer, fixed point as its stored value.

docs.title: Named types in swc.yaml
docs.text:
A Simulink component describes its records, enumerations and fixed-point types in the list types: of swc.yaml; a port names one of them as its type. swc_create builds the model with them, so a component with composite ports no longer has to be modelled by hand as TypeSwc_create.m does.

types:
  - name: MySwc_Mode                  # enumeration
    kind: enum
    base: uint8                       # optional: uint8 (default), uint16, sint8, sint16, sint32
    literals: [Off, Run, {Fault: 3}]  # a name, or {name: value}; without a value the previous one + 1, first 0
    default: Off                      # optional, the first literal otherwise
  - name: MySwc_Speed                 # fixed point
    kind: fixed
    base: sint16                      # integer platform type of the stored value
    lsb: 0.0625                       # physical = stored * lsb + offset
    offset: 0                         # optional
    unit: rpm                         # optional
  - name: MySwc_Cmd                   # record (bus)
    kind: record
    elements:
      - { name: Mode, type: MySwc_Mode }
      - { name: Speed, type: MySwc_Speed, unit: rpm }
      - { name: Limits, type: uint8, dimension: 2 }   # array inside the record
      - { name: Enable, type: boolean }
ports:
  - { name: Cmd, direction: in, type: MySwc_Cmd, runnables: [Run10ms] }
  - { name: Speed, direction: out, type: MySwc_Speed, min: -100, max: 100, runnables: [Run10ms] }
Kind In the model (swc_create) In the RTE (tools/rtegen, from the ARXML) enum Simulink.defineIntEnumType with StorageType = base, DataScope Imported, HeaderFile Rte_Type.h, class name in the literal names; model setting SimGenImportedTypeDefs on typedef uint8 MySwc_Mode;, #define MySwc_Mode_Fault ((MySwc_Mode)3U) fixed named Simulink.NumericType (alias, Imported): binary point scaling for a power-of-two lsb without offset, slope and bias otherwise typedef sint16 MySwc_Speed;, stored values, LINEAR compu method record Simulink.Bus (Imported), root port as nonvirtual bus (BusOutputAsStruct) typedef struct { ... } MySwc_Cmd;
  • Where the definitions live: swc_create writes <Swc>_types.m next to the model (generated, do not edit); the model's PreLoadFcn and swc_load_init run it. After a change of types: write it again with python tools/swc/swc_yaml.py types swc/<Swc> (--check only compares). It is an input of generated/model.sha256.
  • Why named fixed point: a bare fixdt(...) inside a bus loses its scaling in the ARXML of R2024a.
  • Checks (YAML path and line): kind and keys per kind; literals are unique identifiers with unique values; default is a literal; fixed point needs an integer base and lsb > 0; record elements are platform or named types, no arrays of records, no recursion; an unused type is a warning. min/max are allowed for fixed point only. The typedef and every literal macro <Type>_<Literal> join the check of generated identifiers.
  • Type names are global in the ECU: prefix them with the component (MySwc_Mode) unless two components share a type.
  • Not (yet) covered: C components refuse types:; arrays of named types at a port (use a record with an array element); the Studio forms and swc_ports know platform types only.

rtegen compares the port types of swc.yaml with the ARXML: enumeration and fixed point by platform type, a record by its name. Proof: tools/swc/test/fixtures/TypeYamlSwc/swc.yaml, test_swc_yaml.py (SwcTypesTest) and the MATLAB test SwcTypesTest.m.

docs.title: Array ports
docs.text:
A port of swc.yaml is an array of fixed size with the key dimension (default 1 = scalar):

ports:
  - { name: CellVoltages, direction: out, type: uint16, runnables: [Run10ms], dimension: 96 }
  - { name: SocByOcv, direction: in, type: uint8, runnables: [Run10ms], dimension: hvscmc.number_cell_voltages }
  - { name: CellTemps, direction: in, type: sint16, runnables: [Run10ms], dimension: 16,
      dimension_source: hvscmc.number_temp_sensors }
Form Meaning dimension: <n> whole number 1..4096; the master of the generated code dimension: <expression> a name of the init data (or arithmetic of names and numbers, a.n * 2), resolved when swc.yaml is loaded (rtegen, swc_yaml.py check, Studio) from <Swc>_init.m and init_data/*.m next to swc.yaml - without MATLAB (tools/swc/initdata.py) dimension: <n> + dimension_source: <expression> the number with the expression it came from, as an import writes it when the expression cannot be resolved without MATLAB; checked again whenever the init data allows it

Decision: the generated code always has a number, the resolution happens in the tool. Init data is evaluated without MATLAB only for plain top-level assignments (name = <number>;, a.b = <arithmetic>;, numeric casts, Simulink.Parameter). Anything else (.mat file, data dictionary, function call, assignment inside if/for) is an error at the port with the next step: write the number MATLAB gives as dimension and keep the expression as dimension_source. A dimension_source that resolves to another number is an error, one that cannot be resolved a warning.

What follows from a dimension > 1: - RTE: type rt_Array_<type>_<n>, Rte_Read_<P>_<P>(<type>* data), Rte_Write_<P>_<P>(const <type>* data), a buffer of the full size copied with memcpy; consistency between tasks as for every signal (section "Datenkonsistenz zwischen Tasks"). - Connections: both ports need the same dimension and element type; a scalar and an array do not connect. - CAN: signals stay scalar; an array port at can.* or another BSW target is refused (one scalar port per element). - A2L: one MEASUREMENT with MATRIX_DIM <n> (tools/a2lgen); the console lists the elements. - Simulink components: swc_create sets PortDimensions; a different number in the ARXML is a warning (the RTE follows the model). C components: the skeleton declares an array per example access.

Proof: test profile tools/rtegen/test/arrays, tests rtegen-c-swc, swc-yaml, swc-skeleton, a2lgen. The Studio import takes the dimension from the model.

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text:
Ports are measurable over XCP anyway. An internal value becomes measurable through the list measurements: of swc.yaml (decision E6 a, doc/architecture/kalibrierung.md section 8.1):

measurements:
  - { name: HvsCellMod_u_CellMax, type: float32, unit: V, min: 0, max: 5, description: highest cell voltage }
  - { name: HvsCellMod_u_Cells, type: float32, dimension: hvscmc.number_cell_voltages }

Keys: name (C identifier of a global variable), type (platform type), dimension and dimension_source as for ports, unit, min/max (engineering limits, A2L LOWER_LIMIT/UPPER_LIMIT, min <= max, inside the type range) and description (all optional).
