  • Simulink component: the model marks the signal: a named Simulink.Signal with storage class ExportedGlobal or ExportToFile (only these make Embedded Coder define a global variable). rtegen checks each entry against generated/src and only declares the variable. With AUTOSAR the signal at a root port must keep Auto (R2024a refuses the build otherwise); the port is measurable anyway.
  • C component: the RTE defines the variable in Rte.c (initial value 0) and declares it in Rte_<Swc>.h.
  • RTE and A2L: rtegen adds the rows <Swc>.<name> to rte::SIGNALS (XCP reads, never writes); tools/a2lgen makes one MEASUREMENT per entry (MATRIX_DIM, PHYS_UNIT). One name is one global symbol per ECU.
  • Limits: rte::SIGNALS has no room for them, so a2lgen reads min/max (and the unit of a port) from the swc.yaml of every component of the project (--project); without them MEASUREMENT keeps the type range.

Ports are measurable this way too: since an earlier change a port may carry unit, min and max. The naming convention (doc/naming/praefix-tabelle.yaml, tools/studio/core/portnaming.py) proposes them from the name's prefix at import (u_ → unit V, pct_ → % and 0..100); a prefix only proposes and warns (decision E6 a). swc_yaml.find_prefix() is the one place that recognizes a prefix. Tests: swc-yaml, rtegen-c-swc, a2lgen, studio-core.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
Runnables laufen in frei konfigurierbaren Anwendungs-Tasks der ECU-Beschreibung (rte.yaml, Abschnitt tasks:):

tasks:
  - name: motor              # Kontext TASK_MOTOR, Name in "stats"; klein, Buchstaben und Ziffern
    period_ms: 1
    priority: 45             # Ordnungsschlüssel zwischen den BSW-Tasks, siehe unten
    stack_bytes: 1536
    runnables: [MotorSwc.Run1ms]
  - name: swc
    period_ms: 10
    priority: 30
    stack_bytes: 2048
    runnables:                                     # Aufrufreihenfolge im Zyklus
      - DemoSwc.Run10ms
      - { runnable: DemoSwc.Run100ms, offset_ms: 20 }   # Aufruf bei 20, 120, 220 ms ...
can:
  task: swc                  # Pflicht bei mehreren Tasks: dort wird CAN gepackt/entpackt
  • Prioritäten: priority ist ein Ordnungsschlüssel: BSW-Tasks aus ecu/asyncCoreConfiguration/tasks.yaml (background 10, bsp 20, can 40, sysadmin 50, safety 60) und Anwendungs-Tasks werden danach sortiert und durchnummeriert (tasks/async/Config.h). Gleiche Schlüssel, Anwendungs-Tasks über safety (above_application) und mehr Tasks als FreeRTOS-Prioritäten sind Fehler mit YAML-Pfad.
  • Prüfungen (YAML-Pfad, z. B. tasks[1].runnables[2].offset_ms: 25 ms is no multiple of the period 10 ms of task app): Runnable-Periode und Versatz sind Vielfache der Task-Periode, der Versatz ist kleiner als die Runnable-Periode, jedes periodische Runnable gehört genau einem Task, Init-Runnables keinem, die Task-Periode ist ein Vielfaches des OS-Ticks, der Stack mindestens min_stack_bytes, der Name nicht idle/timer/BSW-Task, CAN-Zyklen sind Vielfache der Periode von can.task.
  • Ohne tasks: entsteht ein Task swc (Schlüssel 30, 2048 Byte) mit dem ggT der Runnable-Perioden.
  • Erzeugt: tasks/async/Config.h, RteTasks.h, rte::TASKS[] und rte::RUNNABLES[]. Init-Runnables laufen beim Lifecycle-Init im Kontext des ersten Anwendungs-Tasks, danach verteilt rte::init() die Werte an alle Tasks.

docs.title: Kalibrierparameter
docs.text:
Verstellbare Werte einer Komponente (Filterkonstanten, Schwellen, Kennlinien) sind ParameterReceiver-Ports: alle Parameter einer Komponente sind Elemente des Ports CalPrm, das Modell liest sie mit Rte_Prm_CalPrm_<Name>().

Was Wo (genau eine Stelle) Name, Typ, Dimension, Festkomma-Skalierung Modell (.slx); beim Anlegen aus swc.yaml → parameters: Wert swc/<Swc>/<Swc>_data.m neben dem Modell (bei Projektkomponenten projects/<p>/swc/<Swc>/<Swc>_data.m) Ablage zur Laufzeit RAM, von rtegen erzeugt: Rte_Prm_<Swc>_CalPrm_<Name>_data (nicht const) 
% swc/DemoSwc/DemoSwc_data.m
FilterAlpha = 0.125;   % [-] Gewicht des NTC-Tiefpasses
  • Die Datendatei ist gewöhnlicher MATLAB-Code im Stil der alten MBDT-*_data.m (Zahlen, Zeilenvektoren, hex2dec/bin2dec, Verweise wie Gain = cal.gain;). Gelesen wird sie ohne MATLAB von tools/swc/mdata.py, von rtegen und swc_yaml.py; MATLAB liest dieselbe Datei über tools/swc/swc_load_data.m. Ein in der .slx gespeicherter Zahlenwert oder der INIT-VALUE im ARXML zählt nie.
  • Modellseitig ist ein Parameter ein Simulink.Parameter als Modellargument (ParameterArgumentNames), abgebildet als PortParameter (tools/swc/swc_map_parameters.m). Ein Parameter, den das Modell nicht benutzt, bekommt im ARXML keinen Typ; rtegen meldet das.
  • Typen: Plattformtypen als Skalar oder Zeilenvektor (dim), Festkomma über lsb/offset. In der Datendatei steht der physikalische Wert; rtegen rechnet in den gespeicherten Wert um und prüft Länge und Wertebereich.
  • Parameter werden in der rte.yaml nicht verbunden und brauchen keine Kopien am Task-Übergang.
  • Für XCP: rte::PARAMETERS[] nennt Name, Adresse, Typ, Elementanzahl, Einheit und die Umrechnung physikalisch = (numerator[0] + numerator[1] · gespeichert) / denominator (A2L RAT_FUNC).

docs.title: Calibration objects
docs.text:
Stage K1 of the calibration concept (doc/architecture/kalibrierung.md, decision E1 a): swc.yaml parameters: is the one definition of the calibration objects of a component, for C and Simulink components alike. The keys keep their meaning; a parameter without the keys below stays exactly as before (value or array, type range as limits, QM, generated code and A2L unchanged).

Key Meaning kind value, array (dim ≥ 2), curve, map, axis (shared breakpoints, dim ≥ 2); without kind: value (dim 1) or array axis curve: the name of a shared axis, or own breakpoints {dim, type, lsb, offset, unit, min, max, description} axes map: {x: …, y: …}, each as axis; in <Swc>_data.m and the dataset X are the rows, Y the columns (Simulink: the other way round, see below) unit, description physical unit and one line of text (A2L PHYS_UNIT, long identifier) min, max engineering limits, physical, inside the type range (with lsb/offset), min ≤ max safety qm (default), asil_a, asil_b; an ASIL class needs min and max (also on own axes), a shared axis needs at least the class of every curve/map using it; ASIL C/D come later value_table {stored value: text} for an integer or boolean type without lsb (A2L COMPU_VTAB) 
parameters:
  - { name: SpeedAxis_rpm, kind: axis, type: uint16, dim: 5, unit: rpm, min: 0, max: 8000, safety: asil_b,
      runnables: [Run10ms] }
  - name: TorqueLimit_Nm            # map: X shared, Y own (TorqueLimit_Nm_Y)
    kind: map
    type: sint16
    lsb: 0.1
    unit: Nm
    min: 0
    max: 250
    safety: asil_b
    axes:
      x: SpeedAxis_rpm
      y: {dim: 3, type: sint8, unit: degC, min: -40, max: 125}
    runnables: [Run10ms]
  - { name: Mode, type: uint8, value_table: {0: Off, 1: Eco, 2: Sport}, runnables: [Run10ms] }

Values. Until the dataset of the project exists (stage K2) the values stay in <Swc>_data.m as the defaults of the component type. A map is a matrix with one row per X breakpoint ([120 110 90; 150 140 120]); own breakpoints stand under <Name>_X / <Name>_Y. Checked without MATLAB (swc_yaml.py, rtegen): breakpoints strictly ascending, every default inside min/max and the stored limits, a map of the shape its axes give, values of a value table listed in it.

RTE. Own breakpoints are elements <Name>_X / <Name>_Y of CalPrm (access Rte_Prm_CalPrm_<Name>_X()), stored with the values in one record (A2L STD_AXIS); a shared axis is its own object (AXIS_PTS). A map is stored as one block per X breakpoint with the values over Y (Y fastest; in the A2L FNC_VALUES … COLUMN_DIR). rte::PARAMETERS[] gets the limits as stored values, the rows of the axes, the kind and the safety class; texts and the layout identifier go to RteCalibration.json for tools/a2lgen.

Simulink components. The definition in swc.yaml is checked against the ARXML (element type, number of values and scaling must agree); parameters of the model that swc.yaml does not define stay parameters with a warning.

X/Y rule for a map in Simulink. In the model a map (nx X, ny Y breakpoints) is the matrix ny × nx: rows run over Y (1st input of the n-D Lookup Table block), columns over X (2nd input). Because the model keeps column-major layout, the flat order is the same as in <Swc>_data.m (one row per X), the dataset, the RTE and the A2L; nothing is transposed on the way. tools/swc/swc_params.m refuses a matrix of the wrong form or a row-major model; swc_load_data.m fills it with reshape(flat, size(p.Value)). A Simulink.LookupTable is split into <Name> and <Name>_X (set 2) / <Name>_Y (set 1).

Examples: the test profile tools/rtegen/test/calib (C component CalMapSwc) and tools/a2lgen/README.md.

docs.title: ECU-Zustand und Sleep-Anforderung
docs.text:
Die ECU-Zustandsverwaltung (libs/bsw/ecuState) ist über die Verbindungsziele ecu.state, ecu.wakeup, ecu.wakeup.<Quelle> und ecu.sleep_request der ECU-Beschreibung erreichbar; Tabelle der Ziele und Beispiel: RTE-Ports in ecuState.md.

  • Mehrere ecu.sleep_request werden UND-verknüpft: geschlafen wird erst, wenn alle Ports 1 melden; eine Komponente kann Sleep nur zulassen, nie gegen eine andere erzwingen.
  • Zeiten, Richtlinien und Aufweckquellen sind Projektwerte in project.yaml unter modules.ecuState (projects/README.md), nicht in der rte.yaml.

docs.title: Signal-Qualifier empfangener CAN-Botschaften
docs.text:
Timeout-, Prüfsummen- und Zählerprüfung laufen in der RTE, nicht im Modell (doc/architecture/signal-qualifier.md). Jede empfangene Botschaft hat einen Qualifier, den ein Required Port (uint8) über can.qlf.<Botschaft> liest:

Wert Name Bedeutung 0 QLF_DEBOUNCE noch nichts Gültiges empfangen oder ein Fehler wird noch entprellt 1 QLF_OK alle Prüfungen bestanden 2 QLF_ERROR_ALIVE E2E-Zähler wiederholt oder falsche Folge (länger als debounce_ms) 4 QLF_ERROR_CRC E2E-Prüfsumme oder Data ID falsch (länger als debounce_ms) 8 QLF_ERROR_TIMEOUT keine Botschaft seit timeout_ms 16 QLF_ERROR Bus-Fehler (Transceiver nicht bereit, Bus-off) – sofort, für alle Botschaften des Busses 32 QLF_ERROR_RANGE Messwert außerhalb seines gültigen Bereichs, länger als debounce_ms (Bibliotheksblock NxSwcLib/SensorQualifier)

Vorrang bei mehreren Fehlern: QLF_ERROR > QLF_ERROR_TIMEOUT > QLF_ERROR_CRC > QLF_ERROR_ALIVE. Nach einer gültigen Botschaft ist der Qualifier wieder QLF_OK. Signalwerte übernimmt die RTE nur aus gültigen Botschaften; im Fehlerfall bleiben sie stehen (on_error: hold, Vorgabe) oder fallen auf den DBC-Startwert (on_error: init). Konfiguriert wird das je Botschaft in rte.yaml unter can.qualifiers (Profil P01, P02 oder P11 der AUTOSAR-E2E-Bibliothek libs/bsw/e2e, CRC- und Zählerlage über DBC-Signalnamen); Sendebotschaften mit e2e schützt die RTE beim Senden selbst. Beispiel und Prüfungen: projects/README.md und die Referenz doc/reference/rte.md.

Die Konstanten erzeugt rtegen als Rte_Qlf.h (C/C++) und Rte_Qlf.m (MATLAB). Im Modell wird der Qualifier wie jeder uint8-Eingang verwendet (Qlf == QLF_OK); als Zahl gehören die Werte nicht ins Modell. swc_build und swc_mil_test holen sie über tools/swc/swc_load_qlf.m in den Base-Workspace (im MATLAB-Desktop einmal swc_load_qlf). Gesucht wird Rte_Qlf.m unter NX_RTE_GENERATED, <repo>/build/**/generated/rte und %TEMP%/s32k/**/generated/rte; wird nichts gefunden, bricht der Lauf ab. Ein Projekt muss also einmal konfiguriert sein (cmake --preset buildtest-s32k148-min).

Folge für wiederverwendbare Komponenten: Ein Qualifier-Port ist ein Required Port; ein Projekt ohne CAN kann ihn nicht verbinden. Eine „Konstante als Quelle“ (const.QLF_DEBOUNCE) kennt die ECU-Beschreibung nicht.

docs.title: Datenkonsistenz zwischen Tasks
docs.text:
rtegen liest aus dem ARXML, welche Runnables welche Ports lesen oder schreiben (DATA-RECEIVE-POINT-BY-ARGUMENTS, DATA-SEND-POINTS; fehlen alle Zugriffspunkte einer Komponente, gilt jeder Port als von jedem Runnable genutzt). Die BSW-Übergabe eines Puffers (dio, adc, pwm, ecu.*) läuft im Task des Ports, CAN im can.task.

Fall Umsetzung Eigenschaft Puffer nur in einem Task direkter Zugriff wie bisher kein Lock, kein Zusatzspeicher Puffer in mehreren Tasks, jeder Port in einem Task Kopie am Task-Übergang: je Task eine Kopie Rte_Cpy_<task>_…; readInputs(task) übernimmt unter einem Lock alle veröffentlichten Werte, die der Task liest; writeOutputs(task) veröffentlicht unter einem Lock alle Werte, die er geschrieben hat Ein Zyklus sieht einen festen Stand (zweimal lesen ergibt denselben Wert, Wertepaare eines Zyklus bleiben zusammen); Geschriebenes wird erst am Zyklusende sichtbar, Leser sehen es spätestens in ihrem nächsten Zyklus Ein Port wird von Runnables in mehreren Tasks genutzt atomare Übergabe: Rte_Read/Rte_Write greifen unter dem Lock direkt auf den veröffentlichten Wert zu (RteConfig.cpp) jeder Zugriff für sich konsistent (auch 64 Bit), kein fester Stand über den Zyklus

Das Lock ist async::LockType (FreeRTOS: Interrupts gesperrt), gehalten nur für die Kopien. Die Konsole (rte signals) zeigt die veröffentlichten Werte.

docs.text:

docs.title: DemoSwc
docs.text:
Published tree: the generated code is replaced by the hand-written C substitute swc/DemoSwcSubstitute, which implements the behaviour below.

Die frühere Board-Demo als Modell:

Runnable Periode Logik DemoSwc_Init Init – Run10ms 10 ms Led1 = Button1; Led2 wechselt alle 50 Aufrufe (1 Hz blinken), freigegeben durch PcCommandQlf == QLF_OK Run100ms 100 ms MotorNtcFiltered_mV = y + (MotorNtc_mV − y) · FilterAlpha (Tiefpass, FilterAlpha = 0,125 aus DemoSwc_data.m)

Ports: Button1 (boolean), MotorNtc_mV (uint32), PcCommandQlf (uint8, Signal-Qualifier von PC_Command) als Required Ports; Led1, Led2 (boolean) und MotorNtcFiltered_mV (uint32) als Provided Ports.

Freigabe statt Ersatzwert: DemoSwc liest kein Signal von PC_Command, nur dessen Qualifier – ein Ersatzwert hätte also nichts zu ersetzen. Stattdessen gibt der Qualifier Led2 frei: Led2 = Blinken AND (PcCommandQlf == QLF_OK). Der Blinkzähler läuft währenddessen weiter, deshalb blinkt Led2 nach der Heilung phasenrichtig weiter, und die Reaktion ist innerhalb eines Aufrufs in beide Richtungen sichtbar (LED2 am Board und EVB_Status.Led2 auf dem Bus). Led1 bleibt unabhängig, damit der Fehlerfall vom Tasterpfad zu unterscheiden ist.

docs.title: DemoSwc substitute (hand-written C)
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    slx["swc/DemoSwc/DemoSwc.slx<br/>DemoSwc_data.m, build scripts<br/>(published)"]
    gen["swc/DemoSwc/generated<br/>Simulink Coder output<br/>(not published)"]
    sub["swc/DemoSwcSubstitute<br/>swc.yaml + src/DemoSwc.c<br/>(published)"]
    rte["tools/rtegen<br/>Rte_DemoSwc.h, Rte.c"]
    fw["firmware<br/>(buildtest_s32k148_min,<br/>s32k116evb_minimal ...)"]
    slx -- "swc_build, own MATLAB licence" --> gen
    gen -- "ARXML + C (development repository)" --> rte
    sub -- "export.overlay: copied into swc/DemoSwc<br/>(published tree)" --> rte
    rte --> fw

The demo component swc/DemoSwc is a Simulink model. Its C code and ARXML were generated with Simulink Coder R2024a under a MATLAB student licence, which does not allow commercial use - and the Apache-2.0 licence of neXtBSW does. So the generated code is not published (decision F9 A): the model, its calibration data (DemoSwc_data.m) and the build scripts are, and this folder holds a small hand-written C component with the same RTE interface, so the published tree builds the demo without MATLAB.

docs.title: Which one you get
docs.text:
Tree swc/DemoSwc contains The RTE builds DemoSwc from Development repository model, data, scripts, generated/ (ARXML + C) the ARXML, code from generated/src (Simulink) Published (exported) tree model, data, scripts, plus swc.yaml and src/DemoSwc.c from this folder swc.yaml (implementation: c), code from src/

The switch is made by the export, not by the build: tools/distcheck/distribution.yaml classifies swc/*/generated/** as private and its export.overlay entry writes swc.yaml and src/DemoSwc.c of this folder into swc/DemoSwc whenever swc/DemoSwc/generated is not part of the exported profile (rule R13 of tools/distcheck checks that the copy is applicable and was made). No project file changes: the ECU descriptions keep path: ../../swc/DemoSwc.

docs.title: Using the original model instead
docs.text:
With your own MATLAB R2024a licence (Simulink, Embedded Coder, AUTOSAR Blockset) in a published tree:

matlab -batch "addpath('tools/swc'); swc_build('swc/DemoSwc')"   # writes swc/DemoSwc/generated/{src,arxml}
rm swc/DemoSwc/swc.yaml                                           # without swc.yaml the component is Simulink again
rm -r swc/DemoSwc/src

The generated code is then subject to the terms of your MATLAB licence. Nothing else has to change; the runnables are called Run10ms/Run100ms again instead of DemoSwc_Run10ms/DemoSwc_Run100ms.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Identical to the model (checked against its ARXML in the development repository, InterfaceTest):

Port / parameter Direction Type Runnable Button1 in boolean Run10ms PcCommandQlf in uint8 (QLF_* of Rte_Qlf.h) Run10ms MotorNtc_mV in uint32 Run100ms Led1, Led2 out boolean Run10ms MotorNtcFiltered_mV out uint32 Run100ms CalPrm.FilterAlpha calibration float32, value in swc/DemoSwc/DemoSwc_data.m Run100ms

Runnables: DemoSwc_Init, Run10ms (10 ms), Run100ms (100 ms). As for every hand-written component the C functions of the periodic runnables are DemoSwc_Run10ms and DemoSwc_Run100ms.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
Written from the description in swc/README.md, not from the generated code:

  • Run10ms: Led1 = Button1; a blink state toggles every 50 calls (1 Hz), Led2 = blink AND (PcCommandQlf == QLF_OK). The blink counter keeps running while Led2 is blocked, so the blink continues in phase after healing.
  • Run100ms: low-pass y = y + (MotorNtc_mV - y) * FilterAlpha with a float32 state, output rounded to the nearest mV and limited to the uint32 range; FilterAlpha is limited to 0..1.

It is a plausible stand-in for the demo, not a bit-exact copy of the model: no back-to-back equivalence with the Simulink code is claimed.

docs.title: Files and tests
docs.text:
File Purpose swc.yaml description of the C component (name DemoSwc, implementation: c) src/DemoSwc.c the implementation, application code (-Wall -Wextra -Werror, MISRA scope of tools/misra) test/assemble.py builds swc/DemoSwc as the export writes it, from the same export.overlay entry test/test_demoswc_substitute.py test swc-demoswc-substitute: valid C component, interface against the ARXML, host test test/DemoSwcSubstituteHostTest.c the host test proper, compiled against the generated Rte_DemoSwc.h test/target_build.py test target-demoswc-substitute: buildtest_s32k148_min with the substitute, warning-free 
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k swc-demoswc-substitute -k target-demoswc-substitute

This folder is no component folder of its own (its name is not the component name); use it only through the export or test/assemble.py.

docs.title: a2lgen - A2L for XCP on CAN
docs.text:
a2lgen.py writes the A2L of an application built with the neXtBSW RTE. The build runs it after linking (ecu/xcp/CMakeLists.txt, target a2l); the file lands next to the image as app.ecu.a2l.

Input What it provides app.ecu.elf addresses, and the tables rte::SIGNALS / rte::PARAMETERS themselves (name, element type, count, unit, conversion), read from the initialised data of the image generated/rte/RteConfig.h numbering of rte::SignalType xcp/xcpCanConfiguration.h XCP bus and CAN identifiers - the header the target is compiled with generated/board/bsp/can/canBitTimingConfiguration.h bit rate of the XCP bus project.yaml checks only: XCP identifiers against diagnostics and the DBC of the same bus

Output: MEASUREMENT per RTE signal (read only; an array port as one MEASUREMENT with MATRIX_DIM <n> at its first element - the rows Port[0]..Port[n-1] of rte::SIGNALS at consecutive addresses), CHARACTERISTIC VALUE/VAL_BLK per calibration parameter with COMPU_METHOD RAT_FUNC from physical = (n0 + n1 * stored) / d, and IF_DATA XCP (PROTOCOL_LAYER, XCP_ON_CAN). The AML that describes IF_DATA XCP belongs to the calibration tool and is not part of the repository; -DNX_XCP_A2L_AML=<file> adds an /include line for it.

docs.title: Calibration objects
docs.text:
The definitions of swc.yaml (swc/README.md, "Calibration objects") reach the A2L through the image: each row of rte::PARAMETERS carries the stored limits, the rows of its axes, its kind and its safety class; the texts (description, value table) come from RteCalibration.json, which tools/rtegen writes next to RteConfig.h. a2lgen refuses a description file that names other objects or kinds than the image.

Object (swc.yaml) A2L value / array CHARACTERISTIC VALUE / VAL_BLK with NUMBER (unchanged for an parameter) curve, map CHARACTERISTIC CURVE / MAP with one AXIS_DESCR per axis (X first). A map is stored as one block per X breakpoint with the values over Y (Y running fastest, the order of <Swc>_data.m and the RTE); in the A2L view X runs across the columns, so that is FNC_VALUES … COLUMN_DIR in a record layout of its own (RL_MAP_<type>, RL_MAP_<parts>). Up to a separate task a2lgen wrote ROW_DIR there, which a tool reads with X running fastest, i.e. transposed; values, arrays and curves keep ROW_DIR (one dimension, same order) shared axis AXIS_PTS (record layout RL_AXIS_<type>), used through COM_AXIS + AXIS_PTS_REF own breakpoints STD_AXIS: part of the record of the curve/map (RL_STD_… for a curve, RL_MAP_… for a map, with FIX_NO_AXIS_PTS_X/Y, AXIS_PTS_X/Y, FNC_VALUES); a2lgen checks that they lie in front of the values as the record layout says min/max lower/upper limit (from the stored limits in the image), the type range as EXTENDED_LIMITS value_table COMPU_METHOD … TAB_VERB with COMPU_TAB_REF and a COMPU_VTAB description, unit long identifier, PHYS_UNIT component one FUNCTION <Swc> with DEF_CHARACTERISTIC of its calibration objects

EPK. ecu/xcp places the identity of the build in the image (xcp::EPK, src/systems/XcpEpk.cpp); the text comes from epk.py, which the build runs every time (target xcpEpk, the header changes only when the text does): <project> neXtBSW <version> <git describe of the project tree>, with a hash of the uncommitted changes when the tree is dirty. a2lgen writes MOD_PAR with EPK and ADDR_EPK from the image, so the A2L always matches the ELF, and a calibration tool notices an A2L of another build. The application logs it at start (XCP EPK …). The text is readable over XCP at ADDR_EPK and nowhere writable: SHORT_UPLOAD returns it, DOWNLOAD there gets ERR_WRITE_PROTECTED; xcp_master.py … epk [--try-write] does the same comparison a calibration tool does.

No page switching. PROTOCOL_LAYER announces only commands the slave of ecu/xcp implements, and not SET_CAL_PAGE/GET_CAL_PAGE: the ECU uses one page (the RAM values), the slave accepts page 0 only, and the A2L has no SEGMENT/PAGE description. A calibration tool therefore works on the one page instead of expecting a switchable reference/working page. With a calibration segment the flash copy is readable at its flash address.

Formal check. a2lcheck.py checks an A2L of this subset without a tool - tokens, /begin//end, the fixed parameters and keywords of each block, limits against EXTENDED_LIMITS, the axes of CURVE/MAP against their record layouts, and every reference (conversion, record layout, value table, axis points, FUNCTION entries):

python tools/a2lgen/a2lcheck.py <build>/ecu/application/RelWithDebInfo/app.ecu.a2l

xcp_master.py reads the new objects as well: read/write of a curve or map address its values, own breakpoints are <Name>_X / <Name>_Y, a shared axis is its AXIS_PTS name.

The table layout is fixed for 32 bit targets; ecu/xcp/src/systems/XcpSystem.cpp checks it with static_assert, a2lgen.py (SIGNAL_LAYOUT, PARAMETER_LAYOUT) reads it. Little and big endian images are both read.

Fixed point signals. A port whose type has a linear conversion (Simulink fixdt, swc.yaml types: with kind: fixed) gets a row in rte::SIGNAL_SCALINGS next to rte::SIGNALS (SCALING_LAYOUT: signal row, decimals, unit, physical = (n0 + n1 * stored) / d). a2lgen gives its MEASUREMENT the COMPU_METHOD RAT_FUNC of that conversion (the same one a parameter with the same function uses), the unit as PHYS_UNIT and the converted type range as limits; xcp_master.py read/watch then print physical values. The table and the define NX_RTE_HAS_SIGNAL_SCALING in RteConfig.h exist only when the ECU has such signals: header and image must agree, otherwise a2lgen stops (an image without the table would show stored values as physical ones).

docs.title: PC side: xcp_master.py
docs.text:
A small master on python-can for the A2L above - enough for board checks, not a calibration tool:

python tools/a2lgen/xcp_master.py --a2l <build>/ecu/application/RelWithDebInfo/app.ecu.a2l list
python tools/a2lgen/xcp_master.py --a2l app.ecu.a2l --interface vector --channel 0 read DemoSwc.CalPrm.FilterAlpha
python tools/a2lgen/xcp_master.py --a2l app.ecu.a2l write DemoSwc.CalPrm.FilterAlpha 1.0
python tools/a2lgen/xcp_master.py --a2l app.ecu.a2l epk --try-write   # EPK of the ECU = A2L, write refused
python tools/a2lgen/xcp_master.py --a2l app.ecu.a2l watch DemoSwc.MotorNtc_mV.MotorNtc_mV \
    DemoSwc.MotorNtcFiltered_mV.MotorNtcFiltered_mV --period 0.1

Identifiers and bit rate come from the A2L. Measurement is polling (SHORT_UPLOAD); a write is one DOWNLOAD block, which the slave applies as a whole.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• python tools/a2lgen/test_a2lgen.py - images cross-compiled with zig (arm and armeb) from the RTE of the test profile; addresses, types, conversions, byte order and the error messages. The calibration profile tools/rtegen/test/calib with the EPK of ecu/xcp - CURVE/MAP/AXIS_PTS, record layouts, limits, value tables, FUNCTION, EPK; every A2L through a2lcheck.py, the values read back from the image through xcp_master.py, and broken copies of the A2L that the check must refuse.
  • python tools/a2lgen/test_map_index_mode.py: the maps of the Simulink component tools/studio/tests/profiles/MapImpSwc (zig image, a2lgen) read by a small reader of its own under both index modes: only COLUMN_DIR gives the values of MapImpSwc_data.m and the MIL result of a separate task.
  • python ecu/xcp/test/test_xcp_host.py - the slave engine on the host, driven by xcp_master.py over a simulated CAN channel.

docs.title: tools/boardtest – board measurement scripts with host tests
docs.text:
The maintainer's measurement scripts used to live in a private folder; when rte runnables switched from ticks to cycles they silently counted every answer as lost. Here they live next to the firmware, with three rules:

  1. Every value from the console goes through a parser (console.py) that raises FormatError on an unknown format instead of returning nothing.
  2. Every test reads once before anything long begins, so a format error aborts after seconds.
  3. No fixed board values: console baud rate, CAN bus with bit timing, messages and cycles (DBC), E2E configuration, qualifier times, diagnostic addresses and RTE tasks come from the project (project.py); serial port, CAN adapter and channel come from the command line.

test_boardtest.py checks this without hardware against recorded console answers, a CAN capture (captures/) and the format strings of the firmware (ecu/application/src/systems/RteConsole.h, rtegen).

docs.title: Invocation
docs.text:
.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo --port COM9 <test> [options]

Common options: --project (mandatory, the flashed project), --port (console), --baud (default: the only UART of the project), --interface/--channel/--app-name (python-can, default vector, channel 0), --bitrate/--sample-point/--sjw/--quanta (default: project can.<bus> of the bus from rte.yaml can.bus, 16 tq; for Vector this gives SJW 2, TSEG1 12, TSEG2 3 with the demo project), --record <stem> (writes <stem>.console.txt and <stem>.asc in the format of captures/ – this is how a board run becomes a new capture).

Exit code: 0 passed, 1 measurement not passed, 2 format error or missing configuration.

Test Invocation What it proves Resource console console "ecu status" "rte runnables" answers in the capture format (### <command>), replaces console.py console capture capture 20 or capture 5 "rte json" everything that arrives within N seconds (start-up, log), replaces longcmd.py; output as it arrives, Ctrl+C ends early (see below) console echo echo --count 200 N commands rte runnables, every answer fully readable, all tasks from rte.yaml present (characters lost in the UART RX path) console drift drift 540 --limit-ppm 100 system time against the PC: Δcycles × task period against time.monotonic() on arrival of the task line, resolution ≈ one period (10 ms / 9 min ≈ 20 ppm) console canprobe canprobe --seconds 3 the cyclic messages the node sends according to the DBC, with measured cycle (±20 %), and UDS 3E 00 to the diagnostic address of the project with answer 7E 00 CAN qualifier qualifier --observe EVB_Status.Led2 --expect-gated qualifier of an E2E-protected receive message through all states: before the first frame DEBOUNCE or TIMEOUT, valid OK, wrong CRC ERROR_CRC, stuck counter ERROR_ALIVE, sending out of ERROR_TIMEOUT, recovery OK; optionally one signal of a transmit message per phase (DemoSwc: Led2 only blinks on OK) console and CAN wake wake 0x123 --dlc 0 --count 3 sends a candidate wake frame (e.g. a partial-networking probe) with the project's bit timing, reopening the CAN channel before every attempt CAN suite suite run START S2 --out <folder> the board test cases per SSR (below): list, check, matrix, replay without hardware, run at the board per case

qualifier: message --message (default: the first receive message with can.qualifiers.<Msg>.e2e), payload --payload <hex> (default: initial values of the DBC; CRC and counter by tools/e2e/e2e_ref.py), --window seconds per phase after the settling time.

canprobe listens 0.3 s before its window and drops every frame whose adapter time stamp lies before the window's start (right after opening, the VN1610 delivers a burst of older frames that would shorten the measured cycle); the offset between adapter clock and time.monotonic() is learnt from the frames (AdapterTime in checks.py) and the output names both counts. qualifier filters its observed signal the same way.

capture prints every line as it arrives and --record writes every block read into the file immediately. Ctrl+C ends the recording early (capture interrupted after … s, exit code 130); even a killed process leaves everything up to the last read in the file. Without a command the file has no ### line: a plain log, not an answer capture for load_capture.

wake: the partial-networking decoder of the SBC is stricter about the bus bit timing than FlexCAN, so wake takes --sample-point/--sjw/--quanta/--bitrate from the project like every other subcommand and opens the CAN channel again before every attempt (an unacknowledged frame stays in the VN1610's transmit mailbox and would block the next send). --dlc/--data build the payload, --extended a 29-bit id, --count/--gap repeat it. The SBC requirement is in libs/bsw/sbcUja113x/doc/sbcUja113x.md ("Bitzeit des Weckrahmens"); whether the board wakes is read at the board, not by this tool.

docs.title: Board test suite per SSR (suite)
docs.text:
The board test cases of a project live in suites/<project>.yaml; the specification that explains them per software safety requirement and operating case is doc/safety/board-test-spec.md, whose tables suite matrix generates. A case is a procedure: steps that act (console command, console capture, canprobe, CAN silence, UDS request, wake frame, qualifier, an external command such as canflash, an instruction or a question to the person at the board) and checks on the transcript (expect, absent, optional, equals, differs, delta against a project value). The runner (suite.py) records the console in the capture format and adds #> ... lines for CAN results, operator answers and tool output; the same evaluator judges a live transcript and a recorded capture.

.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo suite list [--oc S2] [--ssr SSR-065]
.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo suite check
.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo suite replay BT-S2-04 [capture ...]
.venv/Scripts/python tools/boardtest --project projects/evalboard_s32k144_demo --port COM17 suite run all \
    --out tools/boardtest/captures/evalboard_s32k144_demo/<date>_suite-<tag> --image <app.hex> --baseline <tag>

run writes <case>.console.txt per case and suite-run.json / summary.md (image SHA-256, git describe, baseline, tester, result, values and failed checks per case). Cases marked "not on this project" are refused. The board rules below and in the project rules hold for every case: a case that needs a board-rule command (ecu sleep, MOT1_GD_DRV_EN, a power cycle) lists user in its equipment and is run by the maintainer only.

docs.title: Safety rules
docs.text: The tests only read and only send diagnostic and application messages of the DBC: no flashing, no sbc command. Exception: the suite cases of the operating case FLASH run canflash flash after the operator pressed Enter. console/capture send whatever they are given – for sbc sleep, sbc failstart, kl30b on the rules apply (only with the maintainer on site).

docs.title: Captures (captures/<project>/)
docs.text:
File Origin 2026-09-16_status.console.txt board, demo project after a later change, the maintainer's console.py (ecu/sbc/safeadc/rte runnables/adcaccess); line endings normalised 2026-09-16_measure.console.txt board, same state, measurement commands of the Studio analysis (rte json, rte runnables, stats cpu, stats stack) 2026-09-30_board/tool15_01_rte_signals.console.txt board (remote session "Board tests heute", v0.1.0-262-g1c329e0d): one console session rte signals/stats cpu/rte runnables - replaces the reconstructed rte signals reference of test_boardtest.py 2026-09-30_board/tool15_02_canprobe.asc board (same session): EVB_Status/EVB_Analog at their real cadence with the recorded start-up burst, UDS 3E 00/7E 00 as measured on the board - replaces canprobe.synthetic.asc

rte_signals.reconstructed.console.txt is unused by test_boardtest.py since an earlier change but tools/studio/tests/test_livedata.py (test_several_answers_split_at_ok) needs its three synthetic qualifier states (8, 1, 4) verbatim; change both together. Format of the console captures: comment lines # at the start, then per command ### <command> and the answer.

docs.title: Host tests
docs.text:
.venv/Scripts/python -m unittest tools/boardtest/test_boardtest.py      # about 70 s, no hardware

The classes cover the capture parser (ticks instead of cycles is a FormatError), the firmware format strings against RteConsole.h and rtegen, echo, drift, canprobe, qualifier and capture against recorded answers and simulated boards (each with a counter-check that fails), the project setup (demo and S32K148 profile), and wake against a fake adapter and a mocked canflash.bus_for. test_suite.py (about 60 s) checks the suite: consistency with doc/requirements/safety/ssr.sdoc and the tables of doc/safety/board-test-spec.md, every procedure against the board captures it names (with a mutation per check) and five procedures end to end against a simulated board on a virtual clock.

docs.title: calgen – calibration datasets (stage K2)
docs.text:
calgen manages the values of the calibration parameters of a project: the dataset of stage K2 of the calibration concept (decisions E2 a and E3 a). The definition of each calibration object (kind, type, axes, unit, limits, safety class) stays in the component's swc.yaml (stage K1), and the defaults of a component type stay in <Swc>_data.m. A dataset belongs to the project and wins over the defaults in the build.

No MATLAB and no Qt: calgen loads the components the way tools/rtegen does and judges every value with the same functions as the build.

File Content caldata.py the format nextbsw-cal 1: read (findings with file and line), write, patch keeping comments, resolve a variant, compare calgen.py command line and the functions behind it (migrate, check, rebind, resolve, diff, export, import, values) exchange.py DCM and CDFX, reader and writer nx_cal_load.m MATLAB: loads a dataset into the workspace or into the model arguments of a model test_calgen.py host tests (tools/test -k calgen)

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
PY=.venv/Scripts/python
$PY tools/calgen/calgen.py migrate projects/<p>/project.yaml --author "A. Person"   # dataset from the defaults
# edit projects/<p>/calibration/base/<Swc>.cal.yaml, or import a DCM/CDFX from a calibration tool
$PY tools/calgen/calgen.py check projects/<p>/project.yaml --all                   # what the build will say
cmake --preset <preset>                                                           # re-configure once: rtegen
cmake --build --preset <preset>                                                   # now takes the dataset

Creating the folder calibration/ is not seen by an existing build directory; configure once more (later changes of the dataset files are configure inputs, see below).

docs.title: Layout and format
docs.text:
projects/<p>/calibration/
  dataset.yaml                        format, layout identifier, optional build_variant
  base/<Component>.cal.yaml           every value of the component
  variants/<v>/<Component>.cal.yaml   only the values that differ from base (delta)

dataset.yaml:

format: nextbsw-cal 1
layout: "a5f879e0"          # layout identifier of the software (RteCalibration.json of the build)
build_variant: sport        # optional: the variant the build takes; without it base

A component file (the example of the test profile, shortened):

format: nextbsw-cal 1
component: CalMapSwc
values:
  MaxTorque_Nm:
    value: 250                        # physical, as in <Swc>_data.m
    status: released                  # draft | checked | released
    author: "neXtBSW example"
    reason: "default of the component type (CalMapSwc_data.m)"
  TorqueLimit_Nm:                     # map: one row per X breakpoint, one column per Y breakpoint
    value:
      - [120, 110, 90]     # SpeedAxis_rpm = 0 rpm
      - [150, 140, 120]    # SpeedAxis_rpm = 1000 rpm
    status: released
  Mode:
    value: "Eco"                      # a value table text or its number
    status: checked

Rules:

  • Names are the element names of swc.yaml (as in <Swc>_data.m). Own breakpoints of a curve or map are entries of their own (<Name>_X, <Name>_Y), shared axes too.
  • A scalar is a number, an array, curve or axis a list, a map a list of rows. true/false are 1/0.
  • base must be complete. A missing value is an error; a default is never taken silently (migrate adds missing values as an explicit step).
  • A variant entry replaces the whole base entry (value, status, author, reason). A variant cannot add a value base does not have. check warns about a delta entry equal to base.
  • Status: draft → checked → released. A changed value goes back to draft: a DCM import does that, a CDFX import takes the state the file gives; by hand it is the author's duty, and the Git diff shows it.
  • Files written by calgen are regenerated in a fixed order (parameter order of swc.yaml); the row comments of maps are written by the tool, other comments are not kept. caldata.patch_component (used by the Studio when it takes values calibrated live over XCP into the dataset) changes only the lines of the changed entries and keeps every other line, comments included; a file not in the writer's plain block form is rendered anew.

The layout identifier is a hash over name, kind, type, dimensions, axes, scaling and order of all calibration objects of the software. A dataset fits every build with the same layout; a bug fix does not invalidate it. When the layout changes (a parameter added, a type changed), the build refuses the dataset until calgen check passes and calgen rebind records the new identifier.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
<target> is a project.yaml (dataset calibration/ next to it, ECU description from project.rte) or an ECU description rte.yaml (dataset next to it, for test profiles). --dataset DIR names another folder.

Command Does migrate <target> [--author A] [--status S] [--reason R] creates the dataset from the <Swc>_data.m defaults (structure from swc.yaml), bound to the current layout; on an existing dataset it only adds missing values check <target> [--variant V \| --all] [--release] [--build DIR] the checks of the build (complete, known names, shape, value table, type and grid, engineering limits, strictly ascending axes), layout identifier against the software and, with --build, against a build's RteCalibration.json; --release: every safety-relevant value (safety not qm) must be released, others are warnings. Exit code 1 on an error rebind <target> writes the software's layout identifier into dataset.yaml, only if base and every variant pass the value checks resolve <target> --variant V [-o DIR] base plus delta as one complete dataset (printed, or written to DIR) diff <A>[@V] <B>[@V] differences of values (cell by cell), status, author, reason; A/B are dataset folders, project.yaml or rte.yaml export <target> [--variant V] --format dcm\|cdfx -o FILE [--date D] exchange file for a calibration tool (only a dataset that passes the checks) import <target> FILE [--variant V] [--author A] [--reason R] [--dry-run] takes the values of a .dcm/.cdfx; only changed values are written; into a variant only what differs from base (a value back at base leaves the delta); unknown objects, wrong kinds or sizes and values the build would refuse abort the import without writing values <target> [--variant V] [--json] [-o FILE] the resolved, checked values: physical, shape and stored values per parameter, plus layout and values_id

docs.title: Build connection
docs.text:
tools/rtegen looks for calibration/ next to the project.yaml (only for the project's own ECU description). With the folder:

  1. the values of base, or of build_variant (base + delta), replace the <Swc>_data.m defaults in the generated RTE (Rte.c, record initialisers);
  2. every value passes the same checks as above before anything is written, including the layout identifier; the Studio check (rtegen --validate) reports the same error;
  3. RteCalibration.json gets "dataset": {"name": ..., "values": ...} – values is a hash over the stored values of all parameters, the same as calgen values reports;
  4. rte_components.cmake lists the dataset files as configure inputs, so an edit runs rtegen again.

Without the folder every generated file stays byte for byte as before (tools/test -k rtegen-reference). <Swc>_data.m stays required: it is the default of the component type, the MIL value and the source of migrate.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
A release of a dataset is an annotated Git tag on a commit where calgen check --release passes for what is released:

cal/<project>/<dataset>/v<N>           dataset: base or the variant name, N counting up per dataset
git tag -a cal/evalboard_motor/sport/v3 -m "sport v3: boost curve after bench run 2026-10-02"

The tag message says what changed; the tagged commit holds the dataset files and dataset.yaml with the layout they are bound to. calgen does not create tags. The generated segment HEX and the report of safety-relevant parameters belong to stage K3 and K6.

docs.title: Exchange formats
docs.text:
Both are edges, not the store. The writers put out only what neXtBSW has (value, array, curve, map, shared axis, value table); names are the A2L names <Component>.<Port>.<Element>, own breakpoints are part of their curve or map. The format descriptions in our own words are at the top of exchange.py.

  • DCM 2.0 (text): FESTWERT, FESTWERTEBLOCK, KENNLINIE/GRUPPENKENNLINIE, KENNFELD/GRUPPENKENNFELD (per Y breakpoint the values over X), STUETZSTELLENVERTEILUNG, value table texts as TEXT. No status: the writer puts status, author and reason into a comment, the reader sets draft for a changed value.
  • CDFX (ASAM CDF 2.0, XML): one SW-INSTANCE per object (VALUE, VAL_BLK, CURVE, MAP, COM_AXIS); a map has one VG per X breakpoint; status as STATE (draft → prelimcalibrated, checked → checked, released → completed), author as CSUS, reason as REMARK – they survive a round trip.

Not checked against a third-party calibration tool yet (no CANape/INCA here); the round trips are tested.

docs.title: MATLAB
docs.text:
addpath('tools/calgen');
nx_cal_load('projects/p/project.yaml');                       % base values as variables of the base workspace
nx_cal_load('projects/p/project.yaml', 'Variant', 'sport');   % a variant
nx_cal_load('projects/p/project.yaml', 'Model', 'CalSwc');    % model arguments of a loaded model (like swc_load_data)

Variables are named and shaped as in <Swc>_data.m (a map as matrix, one row per X breakpoint). It calls calgen.py values --json through the Python of the repository. The base-workspace path was run in MATLAB R2024a; the Model option is not verified yet (stage K5).

docs.title: Interfaces for the next stages
docs.text:
• K3 (calibration segment): calgen.values_of(software, name) / calgen values --json give per parameter the A2L name, physical and stored values in memory order, plus layout and values_id; RteCalibration.json of a build names the dataset and the same values_id. A segment HEX needs only these plus the addresses of the ELF. rtegen.use_calibration_dataset() is the one place where the build takes the values.
  • K9 (Studio page): everything is Qt-free Python – caldata.load/resolve/diff/write_part, calgen.open_target/check/migrate/import_file/export, findings with file and line (caldata.Finding).

docs.title: tools/canflash – application and bootloader over CAN (UDS on ISO-TP)
docs.text:
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py flash <app.hex> [--interface vector --channel 0]
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py info    --project projects/<project>/project.yaml
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py compat  <app.hex>
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py scan    [--projects projects/a --projects projects/b]
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py flash   <app.hex> --ecu <project name>
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py fingerprint [--write] [--tester <name>]  # BL-04, DID 0xF184
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py record  <app.hex> <record.hex>          # validity record for J-Link
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py blimage <bootloader.hex> --c-out ...    # in the updater build
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py blupdate <blupdater.hex> [--app <app.hex>]   # only with the user on site

CMake: cmake --build --preset <preset> --target flash-can (adapter via CAN_INTERFACE/CAN_CHANNEL).

Errors of the UDS conversation end with one line, not a traceback: a target that stops answering gives canflash: no response in time (...) and exit code 1. blupdate --app whose application flash fails after the bootloader was replaced says Bootloader updated to <version>, application NOT flashed: <reason> and exits with code 5; the ECU then waits in the new bootloader for canflash flash <app.hex>.

blupdate asks for UPDATE on the terminal; without a terminal and without --yes it stops with needs --yes when not interactive before anything is sent. An updater built for another CAN bus (-DBOOTLOADER_CAN_BUS=CAN1) reports on its own bus: blupdate --channel 0 --follow-channel 1 follows it (--follow-bitrate for another bit rate).

An image that does not belong to the target is refused before the erase, and flash then resets the ECU (11 01) so the installed application starts again if it is valid; --stay-in-bootloader leaves it in the bootloader. --skip-local-compat-check is a test aid (warning on every run): the foreign image is handed to the bootloader's own check (c); an image the local check found different is never flashed.

docs.title: Reaching the bootloader: --wait <s>
docs.text:
Without --wait, flash switches a running application into the bootloader itself (UDS 10 02, repeated until the bootloader answers); this is what the CMake target flash-can uses. --wait <s> is for a tester that resets or power-cycles the board by hand: the tool waits up to <s> seconds for the bootloader after the reset (default 0). The option is also accepted by info, compat, scan, fingerprint and blupdate.

While waiting, 10 02 goes out every 10 ms so the bootloader's startup window (BL_STARTUP_WINDOW_MS, 200 ms on the eval board) gets several requests. Without an acknowledging node the adapter's transmit queue fills and the Vector driver refuses frames (XL_ERR_QUEUE_IS_FULL); since an earlier change canflash empties the queue after a refusal (python-can's Vector backend sends a high-priority frame, ID 0), keeps requesting and reports at the end how many requests were refused.

docs.title: Way back from a held safe state (e.g. ROM_CHECK_FAILURE)
docs.text:
An ECU that holds its safe state until a power cycle (S1 held) does not answer 10 02 and cannot be reset over the bus. The way back is a power cycle while canflash waits:

# by hand: start, then switch the ECU off and on within the 30 s
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py flash <app.hex> --wait 30
# or canflash switches a LabControl power supply itself (TOOL-51, optional)
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py flash <app.hex> --wait 30 --power-cycle psu:COM6 [--power-on-current 0.5]
# or any other switch as shell commands
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py flash <app.hex> --wait 30 --power-off-cmd "<off>" --power-on-cmd "<on>"

The bootloader is caught in its startup window after power-on and the application is flashed in the same run. The preprogramming step before the wait (10 03, 85 02, 28 03) goes unanswered and costs about 3 s; --no-prepare skips it.

Power options (only together with --wait; without them nothing is switched):

Option Meaning --power-cycle <device> LabControl power supply (device id as in LabControl, e.g. psu:COM6): PSU_OUT_OFF, pause, PSU_OUT_ON over LabControl's network interface (LABCONTROL_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:8420, and LABCONTROL_TOKEN, like the LabControl MCP server). Standard library only, no dependency on LabControl. LabControl decides about permission and limits; a refusal is reported with its error code. Without LABCONTROL_TOKEN (or with a wrong one) LabControl refuses with "unauthorized" (HTTP 401); canflash then names the next step (set LABCONTROL_TOKEN) instead of just the code - the token itself comes from LabControl (Settings -> Network, copy button), canflash never prints it and sends it only to LabControl --power-on-current <A> switch on with this current limit (PSU_CURR) instead of PSU_OUT_ON, which raises the limit of an HCS-34xx to only 0.1 A --power-off-cmd <cmd> / --power-on-cmd <cmd> any other switch (relay, other supply) as two shell commands; exit code other than 0 is an error --power-off-time <s> seconds without power (default 1.0)

The switch runs in a thread of its own while the requests go on. A switch that fails is reported and the waiting goes on, so the ECU can still be switched by hand; a Ctrl-C during the pause switches the ECU on again before canflash ends.

docs.title: Where the values come from
docs.text:
No value of the target is a constant of the tool:

Value Source (in this order) memory layout, board/derivative identification --layout <build>/generated/board/bootloader/bl_memory.h, --project, --ecu, NX_BL_LAYOUT/NX_PROJECT, build directory of the hex file name of the master key without bl_security.h next to bl_memory.h --key-name <name>, NX_BL_KEY_NAME; only a bootloader with HMAC security access needs it diagnostic addresses, ISO-TP, bootloader identification bl_diag.h next to bl_memory.h, or project diagnostics bit rate, sample point, SJW --bitrate/--sample-point/--sjw, otherwise project can.<bootloader.can> (also via NX_PROJECT of the build's CMake cache), otherwise 500 kbit/s with the driver default time quanta of the adapter --quanta (default 16; Vector: TSEG2 = quanta × (100 − sample point) %) MCU family, image rule for blimage/blupdate BL_FAMILY in bl_memory.h (host layouts, proposal for blgen), project (--project/--ecu), NX_FAMILY from generated/nxconfig/project.cmake or the project of the build; without any of these, the only family with an updater port (with a notice). Rule per family in IMAGE_RULES (s32k1xx: FCF and vector table, like bootloader/platforms/s32k1xx/upd_family_check_image.inc); a family without a rule is rejected

Every command gets its UDS client from make_client(), which sends each request blocking: the client's P2 (1.0 s; P2* = BL_P2STAR_SERVER_MS + 1 s) starts when the last consecutive frame is out, as ISO 14229-2 counts it (before, P2 ran while the frames went out and a 1026-byte block took more than 1 s with STmin 1 ms). The bootloader's N_Cr (diagnostics.isotp.n_cr_ms) still limits the gap between two frames; a request the stack cannot send ends like a missing response ("not sent completely").

docs.title: Options from a separate task
docs.text:
• --progress auto|line|steps|off (flash, blupdate): auto writes a running line on a terminal and one line per 10 % into a pipe, the CMake log or the Studio output.
  • Version check before erasing: the bootloader identification (DID 0xF180) is shown; a prefix other than diagnostics.bootloader.version_prefix (case-sensitive; the former S32K14x-BL is accepted) or another major version than BL_VERSION_NUMBER is a warning. Board, derivative and memory layout (DID 0xF1A0, routine 0xF1A0) remain hard errors.
  • Compatibility routine: 0xF1A0 from bootloader 0.3.4 on, 0xFF02 below (compat_routine_of(), by the version in DID 0xF180); a target that names no version gets 0xF1A0 first and 0xFF02 after a requestOutOfRange (0x31).
  • scan: TesterPresent (3E 00) to every ECU of the projects (--projects, repeatable, default projects/) and once per functional address; shows who answers, whether bootloader or application runs (DID 0xF181), and answers on IDs of no project. Projects with the same request and response IDs are alternatives for the same device.
  • Fingerprint and identifications: flash writes DID 0xF184 (date in BCD and tester identification) before erasing; without it the bootloader answers 0x22. The tester identification is --tester <name>, else NX_TESTER_ID, else canflash. info shows the software version (DID 0xF189) and hardware number (DID 0xF191) and warns if the target belongs to other hardware than the project. fingerprint [--write] reads (or first writes) it.
  • Who answers: info is read-only and asks DID 0xF181 first, then prints application active: ... or bootloader active: ...; with the application running the bootloader's own DIDs are not readable. info --bootloader switches into the bootloader (10 02), reads and resets back (11 01).
  • --ecu <project name> (flash, info, compat, blupdate) selects the project and with it addresses and memory layout; a hex file whose build has other diagnostic addresses is rejected before the bus is opened.

docs.title: Security access and keys
docs.text:
The bootloader answers a 16-byte seed with HMAC-SHA256(device key, seed) (32-byte key). The device key is HMAC-SHA256(master key, chip UID); it is written once per device into the key sector (the flash sector below the validity record, BL_KEY_ADDR) over the debugger. The bootloader image is the same for every device and holds no key. The project only names the master key (diagnostics.bootloader.security.key, default: the board name); the key itself stays on the workstation:

Where Use NX_BL_KEY (64 hex digits) or NX_BL_KEY_FILE (path) CI, neXtBSW Studio %LOCALAPPDATA%/neXtBSW/keys/<name>.key (or NX_BL_KEY_DIR) workstation tools/canflash/keys/nextbsw-insecure-test.key insecure, host tests and CI only; a project must set allow_insecure_test_key: true, provisioning refuses it otherwise 
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py keygen <name>          # new random master key, never overwrites
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/provision.py --project projects/<p>/project.yaml --uid-from-jlink   # dry run
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/provision.py --project projects/<p>/project.yaml --uid-from-jlink --run

provision.py reads the chip UID (--uid <hex>, --uid-from-can = DID 0xF18C, or --uid-from-jlink = the UID registers of the derivative, mcudb uid), writes the key record as hex file plus a J-Link script (loadfile of the key sector only, verifybin) and runs it only with --run. canflash reads the UID itself (DID 0xF18C), derives the device key and answers the seed; info shows method, key state (DID 0xF1A1) and where the master key was found. Without a provisioned key the bootloader refuses the security access (NRC 0x22) and canflash says why.

Transition: a bootloader before a later change (identification S32K14x-BL, or no DID 0xF1A1) is still answered with the old XOR/rotl13 (4-byte seed and key, blkeys.legacy_key), so the board can be updated with the old bootloader.

docs.title: Security levels of the application
docs.text:
The application's levels (diag.yaml security[], method hmac-sha256, the default) use the same device key from the same key sector - nothing else has to be provisioned. The key of a level is the first key_bytes of HMAC-SHA256(device key, "NXAK" || requestSeed || seed) (blkeys.app_key); label and level keep it from unlocking another level or the bootloader. unlock opens the level's session, reads the chip UID from the application (an identifier with source: {bsw: chip.uid}, usually 0xF18C) or takes --uid, unlocks, then writes and reads:

.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/canflash.py unlock --project projects/<p>/project.yaml \
    --write FD00=12345678 --read FD00            # --level <name|0x01>, --uid <hex> without chip.uid identifier

docs.title: Sector 0, the flash configuration field and CSEc
docs.text:
On s32k1xx the chip reads its security byte FSEC out of reset from the flash configuration field 0x400..0x40F in sector 0; erased (0xFF) it means secured (no debugger access). Once the CSEc has taken a key space (PGMPART with key size != 0, e.g. nvm.partition.key_slots: 20), mass erase is locked, and a reset while the field is erased loses the part. The only way back is a separate task: load the MASTER_ECU_KEY and run DBG_CHAL/DBG_AUTH.

Rules the tools follow:

  • Whoever erases sector 0 writes the field again, unsecured, before any reset can come. The bootloader image carries the field (FSEC 0xFE, FOPT 0x7F; checked by tools/elfcheck); the updater programs the field of its stub right after each erase of sector 0. blupdate refuses an updater image without a field for its stub and an embedded bootloader whose field is not the reference. The application never writes sector 0.
  • No mass erase on a part that may be CSEc-partitioned. flashguard.py checks debugger runs before they start: a mass erase (J-Link erase/unlock, OpenOCD mass_erase, pyOCD --chip, CubeProgrammer -e all) is refused when the project reserves key slots or a partition code says partitioned, and warned about while the state is unknown on a derivative with CSEc; a J-Link range erase of sector 0 and an image for sector 0 without a valid field are always refused. provision.py runs it on its scripts before J-Link.
  • blupdate on such a part shows the risk with the confirmation (and with --yes): keep the supply stable, do not reset.
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/flashguard.py --project projects/<p>/project.yaml \
    --script <build>/bootloader/RelWithDebInfo/flash-bootloader.jlink --image <build>/bootloader/RelWithDebInfo/bootloader.hex
.venv/Scripts/python tools/canflash/flashguard.py --project projects/<p>/project.yaml --depart 0xF --script my.jlink

--depart is the partition code read from the part (flexnvm show, SIM_FCFG1 DEPART); 0xF = not partitioned. The key space cannot be read on s32k1xx, so a partitioned part counts as locked. J-Link's own unlock dialog is refused by a CSEc-partitioned chip; go the way.

docs.title: Host tests
docs.text: File Content test_flashguard.py Configuration field rule with counter-checks, CSEc risk from project/derivative/partition code, mass erase in command texts, flash targets of CMakeLists.txt and provision.py, blupdate stub field and CSEc notice test_canflash_tool.py progress, version warnings, silent DID probe (with counter-check without it), bus timing from the project, ECU selection, scan on a virtual bus – without the DLL, a few seconds test_bootloader_host.py against the bootloader core as a DLL: old bootloader, progress in the log, foreign prefix, two ECUs (demo and S32K148) on one bus test_bl_update_host.py, test_bl_update_mutations.py updater, power loss, meaningfulness test_bl_security_host.py SHA-256/HMAC against NIST and RFC 4231 vectors, security access (wrong key, repetition, lockout also across a reset, missing or damaged key record, other UID) for three layouts, transition to XOR/rotl13, key store, provision.py without hardware

docs.title: tools/ci – provider-neutral CI
docs.text:
All the logic of a CI pipeline lives here, not with the CI provider. A provider (today GitHub Actions, .github/workflows/ci.yml) only checks out, provides Python and calls two commands. The same two commands run locally:

python -m tools.ci setup --python-packages   # pinned tools into the cache, pinned Python packages
python -m tools.ci run --strict              # check tools, tools/test (all groups), artefacts, report

On the workstation with the .venv (the packages are already installed there): .venv/Scripts/python -m tools.ci setup and .venv/Scripts/python -m tools.ci run --jobs 4. Further commands:

Command Purpose check [--toolchain local] tool, Python and package versions against the pinning, coverage of the build profiles run --toolchain local pipeline with the tools of the workstation (for example the GCC of a vendor IDE); deviations as warnings run -k <name> / --group <g> trial run with a selection (not with --strict) run --no-coverage pipeline without the coverage measurement run --no-static-analysis pipeline without the static analysis setup --python-packages --core-only core packages only, without PySide6; the Studio tests are then skipped setup --tool misra only the static analysis tools (pip wheels) into the cache setup --tool strictdoc only StrictDoc into <cache>/strictdoc-venv; run announces it to tools/test as NX_STRICTDOC_VENV, check compares it with constraints-docs.txt lint actionlint (pinned version) over .github/workflows summary <out> print the Markdown report of a run (job summary) preflight [--since v<previous>] pre-flight before the release CI (doc/safety/verification-plan.md 8.2): PF-1 freeze check, PF-2 check --strict, PF-3 increment since the previous release, PF-4 target build + static analysis + coverage, PF-5 safety documents; report preflight.md/json, step timeouts (--timeout-factor), a timed-out test is repeated once alone run --workspace <dir> the pipeline of a customer repository (see below) template <name> [--out <workspace>] the CI files a workspace starts from (github, gitlab, tests, pipeline, coverage, misra-deviations) release [--version X.Y.Z] [--tag vX.Y.Z-rcN] release publication of a tagged baseline (see below); a release candidate by its own tag

docs.title: Pinning – every value exactly once
docs.text:
File Content versions.toml ARM GCC, CMake, Ninja (and actionlint): version, download URL and SHA-256 for Windows/Linux each ../misra/requirements.txt cppcheck and clang-tidy (pip wheels) of the static analysis ../requirements-docs.txt, constraints-docs.txt StrictDoc 0.30.1 and its 88 dependencies, exact pins, own venv (not the .venv, not the Studio build; the workstation .venv pins a different pypdf) .python-version Python interpreter; also read by actions/setup-python constraints.txt exact versions of all Python packages of tools/requirements.txt and tools/requirements-studio.txt pipeline.toml allowed skips, presets deliberately not built, steps outside CI, artefact patterns templates/ the CI files a customer workspace starts from; they call the same commands, they do not repeat their logic

Which tests and target builds exist is stated only in tools/test/tests.yaml.

tools/requirements.txt holds the core packages (generators, checks, host tests, CI); PySide6, pytest, pytest-qt and pyinstaller are only needed by tools/studio and live in tools/requirements-studio.txt . setup --python-packages installs both, because the CI runs the Studio tests as well, and also tools/requirements-site.txt (MkDocs of the documentation website; exact pins in the file itself), also with --core-only - without it docgen-site is skipped, and under run --strict a skipped entry is red. check reports them separately: the core list must fit, the Studio list counts as "skipped" when it is absent and as a finding when it is half installed or wrongly pinned. The environment of a customer workspace is built from the same two files by tools/setup; check names a stale one under "Umgebung".

The tool cache is located under NX_CI_CACHE, otherwise %LOCALAPPDATA%/nextbsw/ci-cache or ~/.cache/nextbsw/ci-cache (ARM GCC unpacked about 1 GB). A tool only counts as installed once the marker file with the checksum has been written after unpacking.

docs.title: What run decides
docs.text:
# Stage Decision 1 Provide the tools pinned versions from the cache (missing ones are downloaded) at the front of the PATH, ARM GCC also as NX_ARM_GCC_BIN 2 Check versions (--strict: every deviation is red); release identity: a commit with tag vX.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z-rcN (release candidate) must equal the root file VERSION, and any other tag starting with v + digit on it (v1.0.0-rc, v1.0.0-beta1) is red; every visible CMake preset is built by a target entry in tests.yaml or listed with a reason under presets.not_built, otherwise red („Profil ohne CI-Entscheidung“). A preset with a cache variable of its own besides NX_PROJECT is a profile of its own (<project> [VAR=value]) 3 Tests and target builds one call python -m tools.test --group all --clean --json …; with --strict every skipped test not listed under allowed_skips is red 4 Coverage tools/test/coverage.py per module (coverage.json, coverage.md, table in the summary); only over the whole list (not with -k/--group/--no-coverage). [coverage] in pipeline.toml: enabled, enforce (below threshold red or warning, today a warning, stage 2), strict (failed measurement red or warning) 5 Static analysis python -m tools.misra run over the compile database of the demo build (tools/misra); [static_analysis]: enforce (a finding in neither baseline nor deviation list is red), strict_tools (missing tool red with --strict, otherwise skipped); only over the whole list, --no-static-analysis skips it 6 Artefacts ELF/HEX/MAP of the target builds with sizes 7 Report ci-result.json, summary.md, tests.json, tests.log in --out (default build/ci-out); what lies outside CI (MATLAB, hardware, doc/confidential, keys) is listed as skipped

Provenance (cm-plan G1): ci-result.json records under provenance the full commit, tree hash, git describe, the OpenBSW gitlink, VERSION and whether the working tree was dirty, before the first stage and at the end (provenance.end); the summary prints the line Stand …. A HEAD that moved during the run is red with --strict.

docs.title: A customer workspace
docs.text:
A customer has his own repository – the workspace, the folder with nextbsw.yaml – with neXtBSW as a submodule on a fixed tag. He gets one run that judges his repository:

python -m tools.ci run --workspace <dir> --strict    # from the tree; <dir> is the customer repository
python -m tools.ci run --workspace <dir> --release   # plus: the pinned tree must be a released baseline
python -m tools.ci check --workspace <dir>           # pin, tools, environment, profile coverage only
python -m tools.ci template gitlab --out <dir>       # the CI file of his provider

What changes against a run in the tree, and nothing else:

tree workspace pipeline tools/ci/pipeline.toml <workspace>/ci/pipeline.toml (missing: the tree's, as a fallback) tests tools/test/tests.yaml tools/test --workspace <dir>: <workspace>/ci/tests.yaml plus the tree entries marked in_workspace (tools/test) profiles CMakePresets.json of the tree CMakePresets.json of the workspace; a profile without a target entry and without a reason under presets.not_built is red, exactly as in the tree build root, report build/… of the tree <workspace>/build/nxtest, <workspace>/build/ci-out; a build root inside the tree is refused first stage versions and profiles the pin on top of it

The pin stage. nextbsw.yaml states which neXtBSW version the workspace is built with; the stage compares it with the VERSION of the tree the run uses and checks that nextbsw.path points at that tree. A deviation is red: an image built with another tree than the pin names cannot be reproduced. The .venv of the workspace is reported against the requirements of the pinned tree as a warning.

--release: the provenance of the pinned tree (gap N10). Version and path say which tree; they do not say whether it is a released one. tools/nxconfig/pincheck.py answers that, and the stage reports it in every run:

finding meaning without --release with --release no-tag the pinned commit carries no release tag – a development pin warning error dirty the pinned tree has local changes (tracked or untracked) warning error tag-lightweight v<version> exists, but as a bare pointer without author, date and message warning error tag-mismatch, tag-elsewhere the commit carries another release tag, or v<version> sits elsewhere in the history warning error tag-unreachable, master-unknown v<version> hangs off a side branch, or there is no master to measure against warning error overlay-version, overlay-missing an overlay (search.overlays) names another version, or is not fetched warning error no-git with source: archive no git checkout, on purpose – the identity is url plus sha256 note note

The findings are printed in every run; the flag decides whether they stop it, because a development pin is the state every customer starts in and a pipeline that is red from day one teaches everybody to ignore it. --release is the point at which an image leaves the house and has to be reproducible from a tag (customer-project.md 4.4 and 5.7). Every message names file, line and YAML path of nextbsw.yaml and the command that fixes it. Without --workspace, --release asks the same question of the tree the run builds. nxconfig pin prints the rule's own severities and exits 1 on an error.

The same rule read on its own, without a pipeline:

python tools/nxconfig pin <project.yaml | folder> [--release] [--json]

Coverage and static analysis measure the customer's own code (gap N19). The thresholds in tools/test/coverage.yaml and the baseline in tools/misra belong to the tree, so a workspace run never uses them; the workspace keeps its own files next to its list:

File in the workspace Content Start from ci/coverage.yaml thresholds per module of the workspace template coverage ci/misra/deviations.yaml justified deviations (required once the stage is on) template misra-deviations ci/misra/baseline.yaml inventory of known findings python -m tools.misra baseline --workspace <dir> ci/misra/defects.yaml, ci/misra/rules.yaml optional; without rules.yaml the tree's rule set applies -

[coverage] and [static_analysis] of ci/pipeline.toml switch the stages on (static_analysis.compile_db names the compile database relative to the build root). Only files of the workspace are own code; the pinned tree, the build root and .venv are context. A stage switched off is named as not run; a stage switched on without its file is red with the command that writes the starting point. The tree is only read: build directory and report lie in the workspace (tools/test/test_workspace.py proves it).

docs.title: CI files for a workspace
docs.text:
python -m tools.ci template <name> [--out <workspace>] prints the file, or writes it where it belongs (never over an existing one without --force):

Name Place in the workspace Content github .github/workflows/ci.yml checkout with the submodule and fetch-depth: 0 (the release tag has to come along), Python from <tree>/tools/ci/.python-version, tools/setup venv ., tools.ci setup, tools.ci run --strict --workspace, job summary, artefacts gitlab .gitlab-ci.yml GIT_SUBMODULE_STRATEGY: recursive, tool cache, the same four commands tests ci/tests.yaml commented starting point of the customer's own test list (format of tools/test/tests.yaml) pipeline ci/pipeline.toml commented starting point of the customer's own pipeline (format of this folder's pipeline.toml), coverage and static analysis of his own code switched on coverage ci/coverage.yaml coverage thresholds for his own code (format of tools/test/coverage.yaml) misra-deviations ci/misra/deviations.yaml empty, commented deviation list of the static analysis of his own code (format of tools/misra)

Both provider files fetch a private neXtBSW repository with a token in the secret NEXTBSW_TOKEN (for a public tree the line is deleted); the templates stay thin hulls around the same two commands anyone runs locally.

docs.title: Release publication (gap N15)
docs.text:
A release is more than the tag: python -m tools.ci release gathers what doc/architecture/customer-project.md gap N15 asks for into one local run - it never pushes and never tags the real tree by itself (tools/ci/release.py has the reasons, tools/ci/test_release.py proves it with temporary repositories):

python -m tools.ci release                                              # VERSION, profile open, build/release/<tag>
python -m tools.ci release --version 0.2.0 --profile open,licensed --archive --report-dir build/ci-out
python -m tools.ci release --tag v1.0.0-rc1 --report-dir build/ci-out   # a release candidate (TOOL-232)

Release candidates. VERSION stays X.Y.Z; a candidate of it is tagged vX.Y.Z-rcN (N = 1, 2,... without leading zero; Release R1 is v1.0.0-rc1). The tag of a release run is --tag, else the release tag of VERSION that HEAD already carries (the release itself before a candidate, the newest candidate otherwise), else v<VERSION>. Tag plan, archive folder, ci-out-<tag>.zip, RELEASE_NOTES-<tag>.md and the default --out are named after it, and the gh release create line marks a candidate --prerelease. A tag of another form (v1.0.0-rc, v1.0.0-beta1) or of another version (v1.0.1-rc1 on VERSION 1.0.0) is refused before anything is written. check --release / run --release judge a candidate on HEAD with the same rule as v<VERSION> (annotated, reachable from master, tree clean); the rule (tools/ci/rctag.py) lives in tools/ci until it moves to tools/nxconfig/version.py after R1, so nxconfig pin --release of a workspace does not know candidates yet.

Piece What it does Tag plan_tag checks the annotated tag v<version> is ready (clean, not already there, VERSION matches, on master) and prints the exact git tag -a command - it never runs it. create_tag runs it for real; run it only against a temporary test repository, never the tree you release, that command is the maintainer's own deliberate step. CI report --report-dir (default build/ci-out) is first checked by report_binding: verdict pass, a --strict run of the tree, clean at the start, HEAD not moved, its tree hash equal to HEAD^{tree} of the checkout to be tagged, same VERSION. Then it is copied under the release tag into the archive - NX_RELEASE_ARCHIVE, else a per-user cache directory (default_archive_root) - and zipped as ci-out-<tag>.zip with a .sha256 file next to it; the plan prints the tag-message line CI report: sha256 … and the gh release create command for the release asset (never run). With --strict an unbound report stops the command and names every reason. Rules and retention: doc/safety/verification-plan.md section 7. A missing report is only noted. Release notes the lines CHANGELOG.md gained since the previous release tag, wherever in the file they landed - this changelog's ## headings name tasks, not versions, so there is no per-release section to cut out instead. The first release takes the whole file. Written to RELEASE_NOTES-v<version>.md in the output folder. Export per profile one tools/distcheck export per requested profile (default open); a profile blocked by findings is reported, not silently forced (--allow-findings is for trial runs, exactly as in tools/distcheck itself). Target repository tools/distcheck/release-targets.yaml names where an exported profile would go, once decided; without an entry the plan carries the profile as undecided (customer-project.md Q2) instead of a guessed address. Archive + SHA-256 (--archive, variant 3) zips each exported profile as nextbsw-<version>-<profile>.zip next to a .sha256 file in sha256sum format.

Everything lands under --out (default build/release/v<version>) as release-plan.json/release-plan.md plus the release notes, the exports and, with --archive, the zips - the plan for what would be pushed where, never the push itself.

docs.title: Another provider
docs.text: Without any change to tools/ci: check out with submodules, Python from tools/ci/.python-version, then python -m tools.ci setup --python-packages and python -m tools.ci run --strict --out ci-out, and keep ci-out as artefact. Linux is pinned in versions.toml, but so far only proven under Windows.

docs.title: Own tests
docs.text:
python -m unittest tools/ci/test_ci.py
python -m unittest tools/ci/test_release.py
python -m unittest tools/ci/test_verification_plan.py   # doc/safety/verification-plan.md against the repository

docs.title: csec – host side of the CSEc way back to the factory state
docs.text:
Task. Computes on the workstation what the CSEc of the S32K1 family needs for the way back after a PGMPART with key space: the SHE key derivation, the messages M1..M5 of the first MASTER_ECU_KEY load, and the authorisation of CMD_DBG_AUTH. The device side is platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspCsec, which explains the procedure and the safety rules. No device access here. Running the lines on a board is part of a separate task, with the maintainer.

python -m tools.csec load-master --key-file <file> [--uid <30 hex>]
python -m tools.csec check-load  --key-file <file> --m4 <64 hex> --m5 <32 hex> [--uid <30 hex>]
python -m tools.csec debug-auth  --key-file <file> --challenge <32 hex> --uid <30 hex>
  • load-master: M1, M2, M3 for CMD_LOAD_KEY of the MASTER_ECU_KEY into its empty slot (authorised by itself, authorising value all ones, counter 1, no key flags), the M4/M5 the device must answer, and the device console lines (staged: csec m1/m2/m3, then csec loadkey LOADKEY-MASTER-ECU-KEY).
  • check-load: the device's M4/M5 against the expectation. With a wildcard M1 (UID 0) the device answers with its own UID in M4 – pass --uid (from csec challenge, which runs CMD_GET_ID).
  • debug-auth: AUTHORIZATION = CMAC_K(CHALLENGE | UID), K = KDF(MASTER_ECU_KEY, DEBUG_KEY_C), and the line csec dbgauth <AUTH> DBGAUTH-<first 4 challenge bytes>.

Exit code 0 ok, 1 the answer does not match, 2 unusable input.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• No key ever gets WRITE_PROTECTION. There is no option and no parameter for key flags; the flag field of M2 is always zero (she.memory_update). The device refuses any other first block of M2 as well.
  • The key file holds the MASTER_ECU_KEY as 32 hex digits and must lie outside the repository (refused otherwise).
