What the method does not see: stack use through alloca/VLA (a register-sized sub sp raises an error; the .su qualifier dynamic is reported), code reached by a path the profile resolves wrongly (the resolutions are a review item), and the stack of a context switch inside a critical section in more detail than context_bytes.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
name: <image>
exception_frame_bytes: 108      # per nested exception, core-specific (Cortex-M4F with lazy FP stacking: 104 + 4)
isr_stack_bytes: 4096           # MSP
isr_stack_guard_bytes: 1024     # SYS-97: no-write guard directly below the MSP
vectors:                        # SYS-97: every handler must be covered
  section: .interrupts
  skip: {0: initial stack pointer}
  default_handlers: [DefaultISR]
  wrapper_hooks: [SafePreIsrHook, SafePostIsrHook]   # SYS-170: wrapper of an unused vector = hooks + default handler
  not_interrupts: {}            # handler -> reason
safety_contexts: [safety]       # marked in the report; DemoImageTest requires them complete and fitting
frames: {asm_function: {bytes: 12, source: "..."}}
indirect: {caller: [target, ...]}                       # valid in every context
bounded_recursion: [{function: f, times: 2}]
contexts:
  - name: safety
    kind: task                  # or isr (then level: <NVIC level>)
    bsw_task: safety            # PLAT-107, optional: stack from BswTasks.h, worst case against the task floor
    stack_bytes: 2048           # with bsw_task: only without BswTasks.h
    context_bytes: 208          # exception frame + saved context on the task stack
    dispatch: [task_function, [alternative_a, alternative_b], ...]
    entries: [runnable, ...]
    indirect: {caller: [target, ...]}                   # valid in this context only
  - name: main-before-scheduler                         # SYS-97
    kind: task
    on_isr_stack: true                                  # stack_bytes defaults to isr_stack_bytes
    entries: [Reset_Handler]
    indirect: {__libc_init_array: ["table:.init_array"]}
    lower_bound_accepted: <reason>                      # optional

--sections-dump <file> gives the objdump -s output for --disassembly runs without a toolchain.

A reference is an exact demangled symbol or a key (it then names every symbol with that key). The profile carries image facts, not board facts in code: the tool knows no board, no derivative and no project. The demo profile is profiles/evalboard_s32k144_demo.yaml, its report for the build of this commit reports/evalboard_s32k144_demo.md (not published, available on request).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: test/test_stackuse.py with its own profile test/profile_test.yaml and a made-up image (tasks, handlers on three levels, dispatch chain, resolved and open indirect calls, recursion, tail call, switch table); deliberate mutations of the tool make tests fail. DemoImageTest runs the demo profile against a real build when one exists (safety contexts complete and fitting, every profile reference names a symbol, every interrupt level complete and every vector covered, MSP and guard sizes equal the linker symbols); IsrStackAnalysisTest and TaskFloorTest cover the additions. The CI step stackuse --strict on the demo image is the entry (group target).

docs.title: tools/test – one command for all host tests
docs.text:
Before this tool, the test commands were spread over five places (README.md, swc/README.md, the file headers of the host tests, CHANGELOG.md) and had to be collected by hand. Whoever forgot a line did not notice: the second build profile buildtest_s32k148_min had been unbuildable unnoticed since the merge.

tools/test runs all host tests from one list and returns one exit code for CI.

.venv/Scripts/python tools/test                          # all groups, without the slow mutation runs
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group host --jobs 6    # only the C/C++ host tests, in parallel
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --group target           # only the target builds (demo + build profile S32K148)
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --list                   # what would run
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k e2e --slow            # a selection, with mutation runs
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --json lauf.json         # result per test, for tools

Prerequisites: the repository's .venv (PYTHONUTF8=1); for the groups build/target also cmake, ninja and arm-none-eabi-gcc from the PATH or NX_ARM_GCC_BIN, and the submodule external/openbsw. If something is missing, the affected group is skipped and named – it does not turn red. No hardware is accessed: no J-Link, no CAN, no serial port, no MATLAB.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
Group Content python Python unit tests: nxconfig, bswgen (including interrupts, blgen and the module host tests), rtegen, dbcgen, todo, schedana, mcudb tools, e2e, canflash and bootloader host tests, board measurement scripts, platforms/common, ecuState, application UDS, linker template, self-test of this runner pytest neXtBSW Studio (pytest tools/studio, offscreen) host C/C++ host tests via ziglang (list from README.md, swc/README.md and the file headers): SBC, high-side switch, CAN gate, hard fault dump, E2E, CAN bit timing, system time in four clock profiles, ADC access, ADC lock, SafeSystem, DemoSwc SIL build host builds: bootloader DLL via tools/canflash/hostbuild.py (demo project and build profile S32K148), STM32 build test target configure and build cmake --preset evalboard-s32k144-demo and buildtest-s32k148-min, expected warning-free. If the second profile fails, board neutrality is broken, not the board to blame. matlab MATLAB/Simulink model tests of tools/swc: SwcCreateTest, SwcPortsTest. slow and requires: [matlab], so an ordinary run does not select them and a machine without MATLAB skips them instead of turning red. parallel: false on both – that is the only thing that keeps at most one MATLAB running (see below).

The two mutation runs (e2e-mutations about 7 min, bl-update-mutations about 4 min) only run with --slow, and so do the two MATLAB entries (swc-matlab-create, swc-matlab-ports, together far over 15 min). The target builds are incremental; --clean builds them from scratch (--clean-first) – only then does "warning-free" say something about the whole tree.

docs.title: Memory report per build profile
docs.text: memory-report-profiles (group target) builds the application of the four build profiles (eval board demo and charge project, S32K148, S32K116), links it once more next to the real image with --noinhibit-exec --print-memory-usage (tools/test/memreport.py, the measuring link of a separate task) and holds the usage of every linker region against its size and the reserve of tools/test/memory_budget.yaml. A profile that overflows therefore still gets a complete report; the entry is red as soon as a region overflows or falls below its reserve. The report lists the biggest items per library/object and symbol (stderr, NX_MEMORY_REPORT_JSON=<file> writes the numbers). memory-report-logic (group python) tests the parsing and the budget logic on synthetic text without a toolchain.

docs.title: At most one MATLAB process
docs.text: MATLAB may not run twice at once on the same tree (shared code generation folder build/swc/<name>, licence). The runner has no resource lock; parallel: false is the only lever (the scheduler runs all non-parallel entries of a wave one after another), so every entry with requires: [matlab] must also set parallel: false. Against a MATLAB started elsewhere it does not protect; the Studio's lock file (nextbsw-studio-matlab.lock) is a Studio mechanism the runner neither takes nor looks at.

docs.title: The list is the truth: tests.yaml
docs.text:
Each entry names group, kind (unittest, pytest, script, command, zig, cmake_preset), the command, a comment and, under covers, the test files it runs. The runner guesses nothing.

To keep the list complete, the runner searches the repository after every run for test_*.py, *HostTest.cpp, *HostTest.c, *_host_test.cpp and *_sil_test.c. A file that is in no covers and in no inventory.ignore line turns the run red ("NICHT IN tools/test/tests.yaml", German for "not in tools/test/tests.yaml"). A new host test therefore has to go into the list – or be excluded deliberately, with a reason.

docs.title: covers must be what really runs
docs.text:
covers feeds the completeness check, but what runs is args (sources for zig). A test file named in covers and missing from args would count as listed and never run – the inventory would confirm itself. So before every run (also with --list) the runner checks, for the kinds that hand files over themselves (pytest, unittest, script: args; zig: sources), that every test file of covers (a name the inventory patterns match) is handed over; otherwise the list is wrong (exit code 2, "Testliste fehlerhaft (covers gegen args)"). A pytest node id (file.py::Case), a root placeholder ({repo}/) and options such as -k Class or -q do not matter: an entry that runs only part of a file with -k still names the file.

args is deliberately not derived from covers: args also carries options (-q, -k, several entries split one file by -k – elfcheck-*, clock-check-*), and covers names more than the runner hands over (see below); tools/docgen and tools/distcheck read covers as it is.

One named exception: a pytest/unittest entry can only hand over Python files. A C/C++ host test in its covers (bswgen, rtegen, ecustate, dem, ...) is compiled and started by the Python test itself; it counts as run only if a Python file of the entry's args names it by its file name. Files in covers that are no test files (the module under test such as pincheck.py, a scenario, a header) are not inventoried and not checked.

Not checked: command (an arbitrary command line; the runner cannot know what it runs – swc-matlab-* name their .m file inside the MATLAB call) and cmake_preset (builds, runs no test file). Also not checked: whether the -k selections of all entries sharing a file together select every test class of it.

Further fields: in_workspace (see below), watch (see --since below), requires (tool missing → skipped), needs_files (precondition from another group), after (order, also applies with --jobs N, but only among entries that are selected anyway), needs (entries that build what this entry uses, e.g. needs: [bl-host-dll] - they are always run first, also with -k or --group, so a single -k canflash-info-host does not use a stale DLL of the build folder; if one of them is not green, the entry is skipped), slow, parallel: false (runs alone), timeout, env, modules (below). Placeholders in paths: {python}, {repo}, {tmp} (a working directory of its own per test), {build}.

docs.title: Field modules: which module an entry tests
docs.text:
modules (optional) is a list of modules with a manifest that the entry demonstrably tests although none of its covers lies in the module directory – for example modules: [capture, hall] on bswgen, which compiles and runs the drivers of those port modules from tools/bswgen/test and platforms/s32k1xx/bsp/bspHall/test. A module is named by its directory name (as in the catalogue); if two manifests share the name, by its directory relative to the repository (platforms/<family>/port/.../capture). Only name a module whose code the test really runs – compiling against a header is not enough.

The runner checks the field before every run (also with --list): a name that is not the directory of a module.yaml or module.yaml.pending under libs/*/, platforms/*/port/ or ecu/platforms/*/, or a name that is not unique, is an error of the list (exit code 2, "Testliste fehlerhaft (Feld modules)"). tools/docgen reads the field for the column Host tests of doc/reference/modules.md: a test belongs to a module if one of its covers lies in the module directory or if it names the module under modules. Without such an entry the module is listed under Gaps.

docs.title: What a change touches: --since
docs.text:
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --since --list                 # which entries the changes since origin/dev touch
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --since --jobs 4               # ... and run them
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --since agent/IO-48 --list     # against another base
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test --since 2950431e^1..2950431e --list   # replay what a past merge touched
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k nxconfig -k rtegen          # -k is repeatable: an entry matching any of them

Why. A mapping file → entry names the group that a change breaks (twice a test group landed red on dev because the selection was made by hand).

Which files. git diff --name-only of the working tree against the merge base of <ref> (default origin/dev) and HEAD - committed, staged, unstaged and untracked files alike, renames as deletion plus addition. A..B compares two commits instead (no working tree).

Which entries. An entry is chosen if a changed file equals a path it names, or lies below one (a directory):

Source What it claims covers, watch always paths (watch also takes glob patterns, * crosses /) args, argv, sources, include only values that name an existing file or directory; -m tools.x becomes tools/x import derived: every repository module the entry's Python files import, transitively (parsed with ast, never run), plus the conftest.py files pytest loads. Resolved against the importing file's folder, the repository root and tools/ list derived: an entry whose own lines in tests.yaml changed (or whose kind's defaults) is triggered by the list

An entry without any claim (today only the cmake_preset target builds - their source is the whole tree) is chosen whenever anything changed at all: nothing proves it unaffected. --group, -k, --slow and --skip still narrow the selection; what they leave out of the triggered entries is named.

Output. Before the run (and with --list): per chosen entry the file that triggered it and why (covers: ..., watch: ..., import ueber <test file>, eigener Eintrag geaendert), then the changed files no entry covers - code and configuration apart from documentation. That list is the actual finding: code without a test, or a test that depends on a file without saying so. It is repeated after the run. With --json the mapping is written under since (in the run result and in the --list file). --since is refused with --workspace.

Field watch. For what a test depends on without running or importing it: a document it checks, test profiles it copies, every CMakeLists.txt it scans (example: watch: ["*CMakeLists.txt", "*.cmake"] on safety-tools, which reads the build files through git ls-files). tools/test/test_run_tests.py (SinceMapping, SinceRealList) covers it.

docs.title: A customer workspace: --workspace
docs.text:
A customer works in his own repository (the workspace: the folder with nextbsw.yaml) with neXtBSW as a submodule on a fixed tag. He checks, builds and tests his projects with the tool of the pinned tree, and his tests never appear in the test list of the neXtBSW tree:

<tree>/.venv/Scripts/python <tree>/tools/test --workspace .            # his list plus the inherited entries
<tree>/.venv/Scripts/python <tree>/tools/test --workspace . --list     # what would run
<tree>/.venv/Scripts/python <tree>/tools/test --workspace . --list --json liste.json   # the same as data
<tree>/.venv/Scripts/python <tree>/tools/test --workspace . --skip target-main          # all but this entry

The step Host-Tests of neXtBSW Studio runs exactly this workspace run: it reads the offer with --list --json (name, group, kind, origin workspace/tree, comment of each entry) and hands the entries its user switched off over as --skip <name> - an exact name, repeatable; an entry another one needs still runs, and a name the list does not know is reported and ignored. Both options work in a tree run as well.

run in the tree run in a workspace list tools/test/tests.yaml <workspace>/ci/tests.yaml plus the tree entries marked in_workspace working directory of an entry the tree the workspace (an inherited entry: the tree) inventory the tree, rules of tests.yaml the workspace, rules of its own ci/tests.yaml build root build/, in a worktree %TEMP%/s32k/… <workspace>/build/nxtest; one inside the tree is refused placeholders {python} {repo} {tree} {workspace} {tmp} {build}, {tree} = {repo} = {workspace} = the tree {tree} = {repo} = the tree, {workspace} = the customer repository

Why ci/tests.yaml. One folder ci/ holds everything the customer's pipeline decides (ci/tests.yaml, ci/pipeline.toml), so the workspace root stays the thin CMakeLists.txt, CMakePresets.json and nextbsw.yaml (gap N12). The format is the tree's format (version 1); python -m tools.ci template tests --out <workspace> writes a commented starting point.

Which entries of the tree carry over. By default none. A tree entry runs in a workspace only with in_workspace: true, and that mark belongs on entries that check a mechanism the workspace itself stands on, run inside the tree and write nothing but their own {tmp}. Today those are nxconfig-workspace (pin, version, search paths) and setup (the environment the customer's .venv is made with). Everything else builds or checks the tree's own projects and boards: re-running it in a customer's pipeline costs half an hour and can only fail for reasons he must not be asked to fix – the release CI of the tree ran it before the tag. A workspace that wants more names it itself, by entry name:

inherit: [rtegen, dbcgen]     # top level of <workspace>/ci/tests.yaml; an unknown name is an error of the list

The inventory never blames the customer: in a workspace run the completeness check walks the workspace with the patterns and ignore lines of ci/tests.yaml; the tree's test files are never reported, and without a ci/tests.yaml the check is named as skipped. The tree is only read: the build root has to lie outside the tree, and tools/test/test_workspace.py compares a snapshot of a synthetic tree before and after a complete run. A run without --workspace is unchanged. What a workspace is and how its pin is checked: workspace.py.

docs.title: Build directory
docs.text:
{build} is build/ in the repository, but in a task worktree under a worktree folder it is a worktree build folder, because the object paths would otherwise exceed the Windows limit of 260 characters . The target builds are located in it under demo and bt148, the bootloader DLL under host. --build-root <path> overrides this.

Host tests that read the demo target build (test_flash_real_application_hex in bootloader-host, the real bootloader.hex in bl-update-host and app-uds-host) have no fixed build folder. The rule lives in tools/test/build_dirs.py: NX_BUILD_DIR (environment) first, then {build}/demo, then the binaryDir of the preset evalboard-s32k144-demo (in a worktree a worktree build folder). The runner passes NX_BUILD_DIR={build}/demo to every test once that directory is configured, also with --build-root; an NX_BUILD_DIR of your own wins. So tools/test -k target-demo followed by -k app-uds-host, -k bl-update-host or -k bootloader-host runs these tests without skips, in the repository and in a worktree. BOOTLOADER_HEX and BL_HEX still override the bootloader image of the two tests.

docs.title: Coverage of the C/C++ host tests
docs.text:
tools/test/coverage.py measures statement and branch coverage of every zig entry and reports it per module. It is a report, not a gate: the thresholds in tools/test/coverage.yaml are a proposal and only turn a run red with --enforce.

.venv/Scripts/python tools/test/coverage.py --jobs 4                      # every zig entry
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test/coverage.py -k e2e --markdown cov.md      # a selection
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test/coverage.py --json cov.json --enforce     # below a threshold = exit code 1

Why not llvm-cov. The host tests are built with the ziglang package, which ships neither the compiler-rt profile runtime nor llvm-cov; the gcov route carries: | Step | Tool | |---|---| | instrument | zig cc --coverage, notes and data file placed with -Xclang -coverage-notes-file/-coverage-data-file | | count at runtime | tools/test/gcov_runtime.c – the missing llvm_gcda_* symbols, writes the .gcda | | read | arm-none-eabi-gcov --json-format, the ARM GCC the CI already pins (gcov reads notes of the host build; the compiler's target does not matter). --gcov or NX_GCOV name another one. |

The coverage build is a second build of the same entry: -O0 (line mapping) and without -Werror (warnings are the job of the normal run). Each run uses a define of its own, because ziglang caches compilations and on a cache hit writes no notes file. Test code (**/test/**), the submodule (external/**) and generated code are not counted – only the code under test.

A module is the directory of its module.yaml (as in doc/reference/modules.md); code without a manifest is reported under its component directory, so nothing measured disappears. tools/test/coverage.yaml carries the threshold per module together with the reason why it is that high – a threshold without a reason is an error of the list. Safety-relevant modules are higher than the default.

A customer workspace (gap N19): coverage.py --workspace <dir> measures the zig entries of <dir>/ci/tests.yaml only (the inherited tree entries test the tree), instruments and counts only files of the workspace (never the pinned tree, also not as a submodule inside it, nor the build root or .venv), takes the modules from the manifests below search.modules of nextbsw.yaml and the thresholds from <dir>/ci/coverage.yaml (same format; starting point python -m tools.ci template coverage). Without that file the run ends with exit code 2 and names the template.

Not measured: the C/C++ host tests that a Python wrapper builds (ecustate, safe-memory and the mutation runs, kind: script/unittest), and MC/DC – see a change-log fragment for the way there.

docs.title: Own tests
docs.text:
.venv/Scripts/python -m unittest tools/test/test_run_tests.py    # runner with invented groups, selection, list checks, --since
.venv/Scripts/python -m unittest tools/test/test_workspace.py    # workspace run against a synthetic tree and customer repository

tools/test/test_coverage.py measures fixtures/coverage_probe.c for real: its never called function and its untaken condition must appear as uncovered.

docs.title: tools/trace — traceability of the safety requirements
docs.text:
Checks and documents the chain assumed safety goal / assumption of use → requirement → mechanism → code → test for the neXtBSW safety requirements. Core without Qt, only PyYAML; every message carries the file and the YAML path (or file and line of a code tag).

.venv/Scripts/python tools/trace check            # messages; exit 1 on an error (--strict: also on a warning)
.venv/Scripts/python tools/trace check --info     # plus the suggested code tags
.venv/Scripts/python tools/trace matrix           # regenerate doc/safety/traceability.md
.venv/Scripts/python tools/trace tags             # suggested tags: file, symbol, comment to insert
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k safety-trace   # the CI entry (check against the repository)
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k trace-tool     # host test of the tool (synthetic repository, faults per rule)

docs.title: Where each link lives
docs.text: Link Source of truth goal / AoU → requirement relation Parent, role DerivedFrom of the SSR node in doc/requirements/safety/ssr.sdoc (step 3; until then derived_from in doc/safety/requirements.yaml); the goals, assumptions and mechanisms are the nodes of goals.sdoc, assumptions.sdoc (with the proposed AoU-24/25) and mechanisms.sdoc; the findings F, G stay in concept.md, F9 …, T, N in fmea.md requirement → mechanism, finding relation Parent, role Specifies (SM), tag field FINDINGS requirement → code field CODE (one file :: symbol per line; file must exist, symbol must occur as a whole word), and nx-req: SSR-nnn comment tags in the code (// nx-req: SSR-001, # nx-req: ... in Python/CMake, {# nx-req: ... #} in Jinja); the @relation markers replace both in step 4 requirement → test field requirements: [SSR-nnn, ...] of a test entry in tools/test/tests.yaml clause → test tag field TESTS of the CLAUSE node SSR-nnn(a): the entries of tests.yaml that name the requirement and verify this clause (a refinement of the link above, checked against it) AoU → safety manual the AoU ID appears in doc/safety/safety-manual.md

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Severity Rule error dead reference (unknown ID, missing file, symbol not found, unknown requirement in tests.yaml or in a tag, evidence test missing from tests.yaml) error schema (required keys, unknown keys, duplicate ID, SSR-nnn format, status, stage, verification methods, implemented requirement without code link) error a stage-1 requirement names a device-dependent (stage-2) mechanism — strict separation, concept section 1.4 error a stage-1 mechanism or an assumed goal without any requirement error an implemented requirement whose verification says test but that no test entry names error a test cited as evidence in fmea.md that names no requirement error an AoU missing from the safety manual once the manual exists error doc/safety/traceability.md not up to date error clauses: clause UID not SSR-nnn(x) of its requirement or out of letter order, not exactly one parent SSR, a requirement with clauses and its own STATEMENT, a clause method that its requirement does not name, a method of the requirement that no clause in force names, a clause test entry that is unknown or does not name the requirement, a withdrawn clause with tests; REVIEW_STATUS not one of proposed, rework, inspected, accepted error RST of the field texts that StrictDoc's HTML export would refuse (check on the command line, rst=True; the interpreter of the StrictDoc venv runs the same docutils components as StrictDoc's HTML writer over all ~1 300 field texts, about 11 s on the loaded workstation instead of the minutes of requirements-html) warning requirement without test (review / board only), mechanism without test, open requirement, goal with open requirements only, AoU without manual while the manual does not exist warning clause whose verification names test without a test entry (clause-without-test, finding R7 of INS-SSR-01), test entry of a requirement that no clause claims (test-not-allocated) info code link without an nx-req tag in that file (suggested tag)

The matrix depends only on the sources, never on the time or on a test run: a test named in the matrix is a test entry that claims the requirement; whether it passes is decided by the test run.

docs.title: StrictDoc model
docs.text:
The requirements are in StrictDoc (doc/requirements, plan in migration-plan.md (not published, available on request)). Since step 3 (2026-10-01) the StrictDoc project doc/requirements is the default and only source of the SSR and the safety catalogue; doc/safety/requirements.yaml was removed (a project decision Q2). --requirements FILE still reads a file in the old format (the synthetic repository of trace-tool and the equivalence check of the migration use it). migrate_sdoc.py is the record of the one-off conversion (--verify --source-rev <commit>: same records, catalogue and messages as before).

.venv/Scripts/python tools/trace check                                         # exports JSON with StrictDoc, then all rules
.venv/Scripts/python tools/trace check --sdoc DIR --sdoc-json index.json       # on an existing export
.venv/Scripts/python tools/trace export --out %TEMP%/sd                        # JSON export only
.venv/Scripts/python tools/trace html --out %TEMP%/sd                          # HTML with the scan of the @relation markers (slow)
.venv/Scripts/python tools/test -k trace-sdoc                                  # host test with the real StrictDoc
  • StrictDoc is a separate program, not imported: sdocmodel.py runs strictdoc export --formats json and reads the documented JSON export. StrictDoc lives in its own venv (python -m tools.ci setup --tool strictdoc, pins in tools/requirements-docs.txt and tools/ci/constraints-docs.txt); it is found through NX_STRICTDOC_VENV, the tool cache, next to the interpreter or on PATH. A missing StrictDoc is an error, never a silent pass.
  • Safety catalogue as nodes (a project decision Q5): ASG, AoU and SM are StrictDoc nodes (ASG, AOU, SM in nextbsw.sgra). An SSR names them with relations: Parent with the role DerivedFrom (ASG, AoU) and Specifies (SM); a plain Parent names the BSR it constrains. Findings (F, G, T, N) stay a tag field checked against concept.md / fmea.md, and the evidence tests stay in fmea.md.
  • Extra rules on the model: every UID: line of the .sdoc files is counted with a regular expression of its own and compared with the export (uid-lost in both directions, duplicate UIDs across documents), the UID format per node type (STK-nnn, BSR-<AREA>-nnn, MOD-<MODULE>-nnn, SSR-nnn, ASG-nn, AoU-nn, SM-nn), and the node type at the end of every parent relation. Withdrawn nodes (status withdrawn) are not checked any more; a reference to one is an error.
  • Rules of step 3: an SM node with CREDITED: no (a stage-1 mechanism described but not credited, SM-58, SM-59) needs no requirement and may not be credited by one; a stage-1 SM node needs its FAULT_MODEL; every #### SM-xx section of fmea.md names an SM node.
  • Step 3b: every lettered clause of an SSR is a CLAUSE node SSR-nnn(a) with STATEMENT, VERIFICATION, TESTS, optional STATUS (withdrawn keeps the UID) and REVIEW_STATUS; its requirement has no STATEMENT and gets its text back from the clauses in force ((a) … (b) …, so the records and the doc/safety tests read the same text as before). REVIEW_STATUS is a required field of every SSR. The matrix shows the review status per requirement and a table of the clauses. migrate_clauses.py is the record of the conversion (--verify --source-rev <commit>).
  • Documents: the consistency tests of doc/safety read the SSR and the catalogue through tracecheck.safety_model() (StrictDoc export, cached in the temp folder per content, sdocmodel.cached_export); the CI check safety-trace exports afresh.
  • Tests: trace-tool runs every rule on the checked-in export fixtures/sdoc/index.json (repository: tools/trace/fixtures/sdoc) without StrictDoc; trace-sdoc (needs StrictDoc) proves that the export of the fixture .sdoc files still equals that JSON, runs the faults StrictDoc refuses and the ones only tools/trace refuses through the real export. After a deliberate change of the grammar or the fixtures: python tools/trace/test_trace_sdoc.py --regenerate.
